en: The Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice is arranged as an Atirātra without the Ṣoḍaśin cup. "Flow on, the foremost of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the bull, pressed. "Sing forth to him, O men; sing well to him who is born, the overcomer of waters. "He shines with flashing luster; the drops have been poured forth. "We [sing] for thee, the purifying one; we [sing] for thee, the purifying one. "Advancing toward the sacrifice... "Sing forth to Mitra; come, O Indra of wondrous luster! "To Indra and Agni, obeisance, great [obeisance]. "Flow on, O seer, in a stream"—thus [are the verses]. [He recites] the Gāyatra, the Āmahīyava, the Eḍa, the Sauparṇa, and the Rohitakūlīya, [beginning with]: "Being purified, O Soma..."

One should maintain [the following]: *samanta* on three verses, *plava* on one, and *dairghaśravasa* on one; or else the *rathaṃtara* on three verses, the *gauṅgava*, the *raurava*, the *triṇidhana*, and the *āyāsya*—these are single-verse hymns. Then: *pra kāvyam uśanāiva bruvāṇaḥ*, the *pārtha* as the final verse, the *bṛhat* and the *vāmadevya*; *mā cid anyad viśaṃsata* is the *abhīvarta*; the *kāleya* on its own verses; *yaste mado vareṇyaḥ* is the *gāyatra*; the *maukṣa*, the *jarābodhīya*, and *pavasvendram accha* are for the *saphasujñāna*.

"Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Gaurīvita; "pro ayāsīt" is the Krauñca; "kāvam antyam" is the Yajñāyajñīya; "agniṣṭomasāma" is the Agniṣṭomasāman; "agniṃ vo vṛdhantam" is the Satrāsāhīya; "saubharam udvaṃśīyam" is the Saubhara; and the Stoma is the Caturviṃśa. 112.

"Sing forth to him, O men"—this is for *pavamāna*. "Of thee, the purifying one, O sage"—this is for *pavamāna*. "O Agni, come hither for the feast"—these are the *ājya* verses. "The wise Soma juices"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *aśva*. "O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—this is the *pajra*, the *yaudhājaya*, and the *auśana* as the final [verse]. The *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, and "that wondrous one of yours, the subduer of enemies"—this is the *abhīvarta*. The *kāleya* is in its own [verses]. "With the sweetest, most intoxicating [draught]"—these are the two *gāyatra-saṃhitā*s. "Flow on, seeking the gods"—he flows.

"Haryato hariḥ" is the Saphasujñāna; "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ" is the Gaurīvita on three verses—the Gaurīvita on one, the Auṣṇiha with the *ekonidhana* on one, and the Audala on one—thus indeed is the Sādhra; the Kava is the final [verse] on three; the Jyotiṣṭoma-stoma has the Yajñāyajñīya as its Agniṣṭoma-sāman. 12.

Flow on as the leader of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. O Soma, you are brilliant; for you are indeed a bull by your radiance. "Of you, the purifying sage, we choose Agni as the messenger"—with these [verses] are the *ājya* offerings. "As a bull, flow on in your stream"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *hāviṣmat*. In the subsequent [sections], there is the *yauktāśva*. That which follows, "Pour out the pressed juice on every side," is the *mādhucchandasa*. And the *pārtha* ending with "Bharga, glory, fame, in Vāyu's mouth, the red bull" is the final [verse]. There are also the *bṛhat* and the *vāmadevya*, and "Forward for you... [is the next].

"Surādhasam" is the Abhīvarta; "Yaste mado vareṇyaḥ," addressed to Kāleya, is the Gāyatra in the Ukṣa-stoma; "Pavasvendramaccha" is the Śaṅku in the Sujñāna-stoma; "Ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ" is the Gaurīvita and the Krauñca; "Vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate" is the Yāma; the final [stotra] is the Yajñāyajñīya, the Agniṣṭoma-sāman; "Sākamaśvam abhrātṛvyo anā tvam" is the Āmahīyava; the Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra is the Goṣṭoma-stoma. 13.

*vidyutatyā rucā*, *ete asṛgram indavaḥ*, *pavamānasya te kave*, *agnināgniḥ samidhyate*—these are the Ājya-stotras. *uccā te jātam andhasaḥ* is the Gāyatra and the Vairūpa; *abhi somāsa āyavaḥ* is the Raurava and the Gautama; *añjaś ca vairūpam* is the Agni-triṇidhana; *tisro vācaḥ* is the Saṃkrośa of the Aṅgirases; the final [stotra] is the Rathantara and the Vāmadevya; *ā tvā sahasram ā śatam* is the Abhīvarta; in its own verses is the Kāleya; and *tisro vāca udīrate*.

The *gāyatram* and the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambham*, "Asitā pari siñcata sakhāya ā niṣīdata," the *vācaḥsāma* and the *sujñānam*, the *daivodāsam*, "sutāsaḥ madhumattamāḥ," the *gaurīvitam* and the *āndhīgavam*, "pavitram te," the *sāmarāja*, the final *yajñāyajñīyam* as the *agniṣṭomasāma*, its own *ukthas*, and the *āyuṣṭoma-stoma*. 14.

"Pavamāna has generated [it]; purifying himself, he has stepped forth. "When, like eager cows, [the drops] have flowed... "O Sage Pavamāna, may Agni strike down the Vṛtras"—this is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ. The subsequent [verses] are: "Purify yourself, O bestower of skill," which is the *gāyatra*; "Adārasṛt"; "Pour out the pressed juice on every side," which is the *pṛśni* and the *ātharvaṇa*; "Abhīśu" and "Yaudhājaya"; "O, indeed, of him," which is the final *vāsiṣṭha*; the *bṛhat* and the *vāmadevya*; "He who is the king of the people," which is the *abhīvarta*; and the *kāleya* among its own [verses].

"Priyā divaḥ kaviḥ" is the Gāyatra; "ūrṇāyavaṃ ca yadīnidhanam," "tvam hyaṅga daivya soma punāna ūrmiṇā," and "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" are the Bṛhat and Kasujñāna; "gaurīvitaṃ ca tvāṣṭrīsāma ca," "yadūrdhvedaṃ pro ayāsīt" is the Lauśa as the final [part]; the Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman; the Saindhukṣita, Saubhara, Vīṅka, Śuddhāśuddhīya, or "yadīḍābhiraiḍam" is the Goṣṭoma-stoma. 15.

"Pavamānasya viśvajit," "yat soma citram ukthyam," "pavamānasya te kave agne stomam manāmahe"—these are the *ājya* chants for the Hotṛ; "svāny uttarāni" are the subsequent *ājya* verses. "Arṣā soma dyumattamaḥ"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *yaṇva*, the *āpatya*, the *santani*, and the *śākvaravarṇa*; these are [to be used] in the subsequent [stotras]. "Abhi somāsa āyavaḥ"—this is the *mānava*, the *ānūpa*, and the *vāra*; and "agneḥ triṇidhanam abhi tripṛṣṭham" are the concluding [verses]. [Then follow] the *rathantara* and the *vāmadevya*; "tvam indra yaśa... [is the next].

The *Asityabhīvarta*, the *Svāsu*, the *Kāleya*, the *Asāvyam̐śu*, the *Madāya*—these are Gāyatra; the *Gauṣūkta* and the *Abhi dyumnam*; the *Bṛhadyaśaḥ*; the *Prāṇāḥ*; the *Śiśurmahīnām*—these are the *Cyāvana*; the *Sujñāna*; the *Daivodāsa*; "Pavasva vājasātaye"—this is the *Gaurīvita*; the *Rayiṣṭha*; "Asāvi somo aruṣo vṛṣā haviḥ"—this is the *Dvyabhyāghāta*; the *Lauśa*; the final one is the *Yajñāyajñīya*, the *Agniṣṭomasāman*; "Yajiṣṭhaṃ tvā vavṛmaha"—this is the *Sādhyam̐*; the *Sāṃvarta*; the *Māruta*; the *Āyuṣṭoma*; the *Stoma*. 16.

"Blood has been shed; the prize-winners have sped forth"—this is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ. "O Sage, these ten fingers [have purified] that very one of yours, O Pavamāna"—these are the subsequent verses belonging to the Hotṛ. "For Indra, O Indu, accompanied by the Maruts"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *aśvasūkta*; one should perform the *iṣovṛdhīya* once. "Being cleansed by the skillful-handed one"—this is the *aiḍa*. One should perform the *aukṣṇorandhra*, the *triṇidhana*, and the *āyāsya* once throughout. "Together with the sprinkling"—this is the final *vāsiṣṭha* containing the word "here. And [one should perform] the *bṛhat* and the *vāmadevya*. "Drink of the pressed, flavorful [Soma]."

Thus [is] the Abhīvarta; "svāsu kāleyam pari svāno giriṣṭhā" is the Gāyatra and the Caidhmavāha; "yadi havat sa sunve yo vasūnām taṃ vaḥ sakhāyo madāya" is the Dīrghasujñāna and the Kāśīta; "somāḥ pavanta indavaḥ" is the Gaurīvita and the Krauñca; "trirasmai sapta dhenavo duduhrire" is the Marutāṃ Dhenvantya; the Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman; "gūrdas traikakubhaṃ nārmedham" are the Ukthas, provided it is an Ukthya; however, if it is an Agniṣṭoma, the Jyotiṣṭoma is indeed the Stoma. 17.

In this manner, the other three *abhiplava* periods should also be performed; however, there is a distinction among them: on the second day of the second *abhiplava*, the *yauktāśva* hymn takes the place of the *hāviṣmat*; on the fifth day of the second *abhiplava*, the *maukṣa* hymn takes the place of the *hāviṣmat*. On the fifth day of the third *abhiplava*, the *apatya* hymn takes the place of the *mānava*. Regarding the fifth day, it is said: "On whichever day the *santani* hymn is to be sung by the village-singers, the *vāmra* hymn should precede the *mānava*. This is for the sake of avoiding monotony (*ājāmya*); in that case, the *vāmra* [is placed] before it.

In the first [Abhiplava], the Mānava [Sāman] is on the third verse; in the fourth Abhiplava, on the fifth day, it is in the place of the Yaṅva, with the Śākvara-varṇa; and on that same sixth day, in the place of the Aśvasūkta, there is the Īṣovṛdhīya for the Triṇidhana, along with the Samanta, Bharga, Yaśas, Vīṅka, Śuddha, and Aśuddhīya—the method of their arrangement has been stated and should not be forgotten. Everything else is just as in the first [Abhiplava]. Having thus completed four Abhiplavas, they enter the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha; he states its arrangement: the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha is combined (samūḍha).

Whether it is arranged (*vyūḍha*) or not, as for that which constitutes the "arrangement" (*vyūḍhatva*) of the *pṛṣṭhya* [ṣaḍaha], if it is prompted by the ten-night sacrifice (*daśarātra*), then this [ṣaḍaha] ought to be "unarranged" (*samūḍha*) because of its continuity; however, if it is prompted by the *pṛṣṭhya* itself, then it is "arranged. Due to this doubt, the prima facie view (*pūrva-pakṣa*) is that there is an option (*vikalpa*). The author states the established conclusion (*siddhānta*): "But it is indeed unarranged (*samūḍha*) when prompted by the ten-night sacrifice; the arrangement is [otherwise]. Thus says the *Nidāna*: "Now, moreover, the six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*) is lost when arranged," and so forth. Furthermore, another scriptural passage (*śruti*) states: "The *pṛṣṭhya* does not exist without the *chandomāna* days."

Regarding the phrase "vyūhamānaśaḥ" (being arranged), he says "tasya kalpaḥ" (the ritual procedure for that) because the arrangement of each of those [days] when combined will be stated. He speaks of the first day: "upāsmai gāyatā nara upoṣu jātamapturam pavamānasya te kavaḥ"—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna* of the first day. "pra soma devavītaye" is the *abhīvarta*; on one verse there is the *pājra*, on one the *yaudhājaya*, and the rest is the same. For the second day: "punānaḥ soma dhārayā" is the *aidamāyāsya*; on one verse there is the *abhīvarta*, on one...

The *kāleya* [stotra] consists of the *vṛṣā śoṇaḥ* for the first [part], the *pārtha* for the last, and the rest is the same as that of the midday [pressing]. For the third day, the *paurumadga* begins with "bhi somāsa āyavaḥ" in the first [turn]; in that same [turn] is the *abhīvarta*, the *kāleya* in the second, and the *gautama* in the third; the rest is the same. 18.

The Pavamāna of the fourth day has been generated; purifying himself, he has stepped forth and become manifest. The *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses are "Agni has struck down the Vṛtras. The *ājya* of the Hotṛ-priest is "O Soma, in thee I have rejoiced. The *aṣṭādaṃṣṭra* is on one verse; the *abhīvarta* is on one verse; the *kāleya* is on one verse; and the final *janitra* of the midday pressing is "Soma flows, the progenitor of thoughts. The final *lauśa* of the third pressing is "O Pavamāna, these milch-cows of thine [are for the Aśvins]. Everything else is the same.

For the *pavamāna* of the fifth day, the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses are "O Soma, [you are] bright, worthy of praise" (*soma citram ukthyam*) and "O Agni, we honor the hymn of Manu" (*agne stomam manūmahaḥ*). The *ājya* of the Hotṛ is "O Soma, you are pressed by the pressers" (*soma u ṣvaṇaḥ sotṛbhiḥ*). For the two *tṛcas* of the Mānavas, there is the *vāmadevya* on one verse, the *abhīvarta* on one verse, and the *kāleya* on one verse. With the concluding verse, "Indu, the prize-winning steed, flows toward the milk-streams" (*indur vājī pavate gonyoghā*), the *tvāṣṭrīsāman* is placed in the middle of the world of Pārtha at midday. The *lauśa* chant, "Flow on, winner of cattle, with double-strikes" (*yad dvyanutodaṃ govitpavasva*), is the final part of the *ārbhava*; everything else is the same.

For the sixth day, the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses are "The strong ones have flowed forth" (*asṛkṣata pra vājinaḥ*) and "This one here, the ten fingers [have pressed]" (*etamu tyaṃ daśa kṣipaḥ*). The *ājya-śastra* of the Hotṛ is "O Agni, the mortal whom [you protect] in battles" (*yam agne pṛtsu martyam*). [The *sāman*] is the *svāra-aukṣṇorandhra*; the *aiḍa-aukṣṇorandhra* is on three verses; the *abhīvarta* is on one verse; the *kāleya* is on one verse; and the final [verse] of the Vasiṣṭha-seer is "Flow with this [purification], bringing these riches" (*ayā pavasva enā vasūni*), which contains the word "here" (*iha*). The light of the midday pressing is "The honey, the dear [juice], of the sacrifice flows" (*yajñasya pavate madhu priyam*). The last [verse] of the Ārbhava-prasthāna belongs to the Maruts' cows. The rest is the same; the rest is the same. (193) This is the *vivṛt* (the expanded form).
The Maśaka-Kalpasūtra,
First Adhyāya: The Gavāmayana Sacrifice.

The twenty-fourth [chapter] treats the *Prāyaṇīya* and the two types of *Jyotiṣṭoma* sacrifices—the *Jyotiṣṭoma* and the *Dvādaśāha*. Now, based on that foundation, the author of the Kalpa-sūtra describes, in two chapters, the arrangement of the stotras for the *Gavāmayana*, which is a year-long sacrificial session (*saṃvatsarasattra*). This sacrifice was taught in the *Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* immediately after the *Daśarātra*, and in the *Brāhmaṇa* it is prescribed over two chapters beginning with "The cows indeed performed this sacrificial session" (*gāvo vā etat satram āsate*), following the enumeration of the *Daśarātra* *viṣṭutis*. The arrangement of the stotras for the *Gavāmayana* is set forth in two chapters starting with "The *Jyotiṣṭoma* has been arranged" (*klṛpto jyotiṣṭomaḥ*).

In this Gavāmayana sacrifice, there are three hundred and sixty-one days of Soma-pressing (*sautya*). These are presented in the section on the sacrificial session (*satra*) within the *Saṃvatsara-brāhmaṇa*, beginning from the section following the *Śatarātra* with the words "The Atirātra, the Caturviṃśa, the Prāyaṇīya day," and ending with the aforementioned portion. It is as follows: "The Atirātra, the Caturviṃśa, the Prāyaṇīya day, four Abhiplava six-day periods, and a Pṛṣṭhya six-day period—this is the first month."

That is the second; that is the third; that is the fourth; that is the fifth—thus [constitute] five months. Then, in the sixth month, there are three *abhiplava* six-day periods (*ṣaḍaha*), a *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period, the *abhijit*, and three *svarasāman* days—making twenty-eight days. Together with the two *caturviṃśa* days and the *atirātra*, this constitutes the sixth month; such is the first half (the prior fortnight). In the middle is the *viṣuvat*, the day of the *divākīrtya*. For the *śruti* states: "This *viṣuvat* is indeed the self (*ātman*) of the year; these two [halves] on either side are its wings."

Now follows the latter fortnight: three Svarasāman days, the Viśvajit, the Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha beginning with the Trayastriṃśa, and three Abhiplava ṣaḍahas—this constitutes twenty-eight days. Together with the Vrata and Atirātra, this is the first month, according to the statement: "The first [month] is with the Vrata and Atirātra, and the next [is] with the [Vrata and Atirātra]. The second month consists of the Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha beginning with the Trayastriṃśa and four Abhiplava ṣaḍahas.

In the same manner the third [month], in the same manner the fourth, and in the same manner the fifth. Three Abhiplava six-day periods, the Āyus and the Gau—these two days—and twelve days of the twelve-day rite; this is the sixth month.

Now follow the Mahāvrata and the Atirātra; it has been stated that these two complete the first month. The performance of this Gavāmayana, which is of the nature of a Satra, is like that of the twelve-day sacrifice (Dvādaśāha). Initiation (dīkṣā) takes place at the prescribed time. The time for initiation and other details have been stated in the passage beginning with "By a Brāhmaṇa [for] the Gavāmayana. Having performed everything up to the Aupasathya day, they enter upon the Prāyaṇīya Atirātra. For that Satra, the rites from the *ṛddhi* offering to the end of the Subrahmaṇyā are like those of the Dvādaśāha. Regarding the arrangement of the Stotras, he says: "The Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra is established as being without the Ṣoḍaśin. (1)

The meaning is that the Gavāmayana sacrifice, characterized by the Caturviṃśa-stoma and an Atirātra of this same nature, has been thus prescribed for the Brāhmaṇa. In that rite, the Subrahmaṇyā litany is to be performed on the day preceding the final day, just as in the Dvādaśāha.
Now it has been stated that this day is the Prāyaṇīya day. Regarding the Caturviṃśa day, [the verses are]: "Flow on, the foremost of speech;

flow on, O Indu, as a bull, pressed. "Sing forth to him, O men; sing to him who is born, the swift one, with flashing luster. "These drops have been poured forth; we [belong] to you, the purifying one; we [belong] to you, the purifying one, O Sage. || 2 ||
Thus concludes the Bahiṣpavamāna.

On the second and subsequent days, the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant in the assembly is performed like that of the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*). The *retasyā* and *rathantaravarṇa* [stotras] apply everywhere; however, the *dhurs* do not.
Approaching the sacrifice, sing forth for you to Mitra and to Indra; O you of wondrous luster, come hither! To Indra and Agni, let there be great homage. 3.
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.

Because of the rule stating that "the injunction for *tṛcas* and *sūktas* is by means of taking the first [verse], unless otherwise directed," even when the four-verse hymn beginning with *upaprayantaḥ* is used for the *upāvaharana*, there is an exclusion of the final verse because it belongs to the *stotra*; the remaining verses constitute the *tṛcas*.

"Flow as a bull, O Soma, in a stream"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *āmahīyava*, the *aiḍa*, the *sauparṇa*, and the *rohitakūlīya*; "being purified, O Soma, in a stream"—this is the *samanta* in three verses, the *samanta* in one verse, the *plava* in one verse, and the *dairghaśravasa* in one verse—or [alternatively]: the *rathantara* in three verses, the *gauṅgava*, the *raurava*, the *triṇidhana*, and the *āyāsya* as single-verse hymns; "proclaiming wisdom like Uśanas"—this is the final *pārtha*. 4.
Thus ends the midday Pavamāna.

Regarding the *samantā* and other single-verse (*ekarcā*) hymns, as well as the *gauṅgava* and other triple-verse (*sāmatṛca*) chants, [the rule is established] because of the statement: "Three [verses] in a single-verse [hymn], [and] various *stotrīyā*s. In this very context, the author of the *Nidāna* has demonstrated such an arrangement of *ṛc*s and *sāmans* with the words: "Now, indeed, that which follows the Jyotiṣṭoma and the Daśāha," and so forth. That, however, is not stated here for fear of prolixity. This word "last" (*antya*) refers to the last [verse] of the Mādhyandina-pavamāna; likewise for the subsequent Ārbhava[-pavamāna]. (4)
The *bṛhat* and the *vāmadevya*, "mā cid anyad viśaṃsata" is the *abhīvarta*, and the *kāleya* is among its own [verses]. 5.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the *gāyatra* [stotra] and the *maukṣa*; "jarābodhīyam pavasvendramaccha"—this is the *saphasujñāna*; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ"—this is the *gaurīvita*, the *gavāmayana*, the *abhiplava* six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*), and the *krauñca*; "pro ayāsīt"—this is the final *kāva*. 6.
Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna;
the Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. || 7 ||
"agnim vo vṛdhantam," "satrāsāhīyam," "saubharam," and "udvaṃśīyam. || 8 ||
These are the *ukthas*.
The *stoma* is the twenty-fourfold (*caturviṃśa*). || 9 ||
On this day, [the procedure] for all the stotras is to be understood; at the end of the Uktha, from the dismissal of the Stoma up to the Apsuṣoma, and also the Subrahmaṇyā [are performed]. || 9 ||

Thus ends the twenty-four-fold Stoma. Regarding the first day: the six-day Abhiplava is described as "Jyotis, Jyotis, Gauḥ, Āyus, Gauḥ, Āyus, Jyotis. This is because of the Śruti passage beginning with "Jyotis, Gauḥ, Āyus... and stating, "He performed this three-day period again. Of that [six-day period], he states that the first day is named Jyotis.
Sing forth to him, O men! We [sing] for you, the purifying one; we [sing] for you, the purifying one, O Sage. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna. "O Agni, come for the feast! (RV 6.16.10).
Thus end the offerings of clarified butter.
"O Agni, come to us; O Mitra; O Indra and Agni"—these are the meanings of the *ājyānī* verses. || 2 ||
"Forward the wise Soma-pressings"—this is the Gāyatra; "Forward, O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—this is the Pajra, the Yaudhājaya, and the final one, the Auśanasa. || 3 ||
Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The Rathantara and the Vāmadevya; "taṃ vo dasmamṛtīṣaham" is the Abhīvarta; the Kāleya is among its own verses.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

“With the sweetest, most intoxicating [song]” (svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā)—this is the Gāyatra-saṃhitā; “Flow on with this, seeking the gods” (ayā pavasva devayuḥ) and “The lovely, tawny one flows” (pavate haryato hariḥ)—these are the Sapha and Sujñāna, or the Kāśīta; “Of the pressed juice” (pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ)—this is the Gaurīvita in three verses: the Gaurīvita in one, the Auṣṇiha with a single Nidhana in one, and the Audala in one; or alternatively, the Sābhra in three verses, with the Kava as the final one. || 5 ||
Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The conceptual construction of "good" and "knowledge" and "space. || 5 ||
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The Jyotiṣṭoma is the Stoma. || 7 ||

By the term *jyotiṣṭoma*, the arrangement of the *stomas* connected with the *jyotiṣṭoma* is here meant. [Namely: the *bahiṣpavamāna* is *trivṛt*; the *ājya* [stotras] are *pañcadaśa*; the *mādhyaṃdina-pavamāna* is *pañcadaśa*; the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] are *saptadaśa*; the *ārbhava* is *saptadaśa*; and the *agniṣṭoma* is *ekaviṃśa*—this is the meaning of *stoma*. At the conclusion of the *agniṣṭoma*, the releasing of the *stomas* and so forth is as before. Thus ends the *jyotiṣṭoma-stoma*. 2.7.2.
The Gavāmayana consists of the Abhiplava six-day period;
regarding the second day of the Abhiplava six-day period,
he says "Gauḥ," meaning the second day of the Abhiplava is designated as "Go."
Flow on as the leader of the voice; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. O Soma, you are brilliant, for you are a bull by your radiance—O Sage, this is of you, the purifying one. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna chant.
"We choose Agni as our messenger. (2)
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.
"agnim dūtam mitram vayam indramitgācaturṛcam"; "indre agnā" are the *ājya* verses. In the four-verse hymn beginning with "indra idgā," there is an omission of the final verse.
"vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā" is the *gāyatra* and the *hāviṣmat*; in the subsequent [sections], the one following "yauktāśvam" is the latter.
The meaning is that in the *abhiplava* periods, specifically in the second, third, and fourth [days], the hymn "yauktāśvam uttaram" takes the place of the "hāviṣmata" hymn.
"Pour out the pressed juice all around"—this [verse] belongs to Mādhucchandas; and Bharga and Yaśas are in the Vāyāsya [Anuvāka].

The *madhucchandas* [is used] in the first [verse]; *bharga* in the triplet (*tṛca*), or *yaśas*; the *aiḍa-āyāsya* in the triplet *ā i parā i iti*. The *triṇidhana āyāsya* [is used] in the middle *adhyāsyā*: "śrīṇanto gobhirūhāu ho va iti. And [it is used] in the *sādhyāsyā*, and one in the *adhyāsyā* itself; finally two in that same [verse], and at the beginning as well—that is the *śaśakarṇaklṛptā*.

Because of the scriptural statement. Thus is the formation of the *tṛca* and *ekarca*. Regarding the fixed allocation of *bhargas* and *yaśas*, the author of the Sūtra states: "On the second day of the *ābhiplavika* [six-day period], *bhargas* and *yaśas* should alternate prior to the *viṣuvat*," beginning with "so says Gautama" and ending with "*yaśas* on the subsequent [day], and the other [on the preceding]" (*aparam*).
The bull, the red one, [protects] the son of Pṛthu as the last. ||3||
Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
Now follow the *pṛṣṭha* stotras:
the *Bṛhat*, the *Vāmadevya*, "Abhi pra vaḥ surādhasam" as the *Abhīvarta*, and the *Kāleya* in its own [tune].
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this *gāyatra* [tune] is for the *aukṣa* [sāman], while the following [verses] are for the *hāviṣmat*. "pavasvendramaccha"—this is for the *śaṅkusujñāna*. "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"—this is for both the *gaurīvita* and the *krauñca*. "vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate"—this is the final *yāma* [sāman]. || 5 ||
Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
Regarding the phrase "the Gavāmayana is the Abhiplava six-day period;
the Hāviṣmatam [is used] in the subsequent ones": this means that in the subsequent Abhiplavas, the Hāviṣmatam is to be used in place of the Maukṣa. || 5 ||
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
"Sākamaśva," "Abhrātṛvya," "Anātvam," "Itthāmahīyava," "Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra," and "Yādauhovada. (7)
Thus end the hymns.
Regarding the phrase "yadau hovaditi": in the verse beginning with "indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan," the word "aiau" means "aṣṭādaṃṣṭram" (the eight-tusked one). || 7 ||
The Goṣṭoma is a Stoma. || 8 ||

The *bahiṣpavamāna* is fifteenfold; the *ājya* chants are threefold; the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina-savana*) is seventeenfold; and the third pressing, consisting of the *ukthas*, is twenty-onefold—this is the meaning of the "stomas of the Goṣṭoma. The rites beginning with the dismissal of the *stomas* are as before. || 8 ||
Thus ends the Goṣṭoma-stoma. || 3 ||

Now, regarding the third day of the *abhiplava* period—the third day of the *abhiplava* known as *āyus*—he recites: "With flashing brilliance... and "The drops have been poured out, O Sage, for thee who art purifying. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
Fire is kindled by fire. || 2 ||
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.
"With Agni I invoke Mitra; with Indra I invoke them"—these are the *ājya* offerings.
"High is the birth of your juice"—this is the Gāyatra and the Vairūpa;

"Toward [us], O Soma, the Āyavas"—this is the Raurava and the Gautama, as well as the Añja and the Vairūpa. The Agni-ṭriṇidhana [is used]. "Three voices"—this is the final Saṃkrośa of the Aṅgirases. || 3 ||
Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The *raurava* [sāman] is on the first [verse]; "prahinvānaḥ" is the *triṇidhana* [sāman] of Agni on the middle [verse]. || 3 ||
The Rathantara and Vāmadevya [Sāmans], and [the hymn] beginning with "A thousand, a hundred"—this is the Abhīvarta; the Kāleya is on its own verses. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"Tisro vāca udīrate" is the Gāyatra and the Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha; "asotā pariṣiñcata sakhāya ā niṣīdate" is the Vācaḥsāman, the Sujñāna, and the Daivodāsa; "sutāso madhumattamā" is the Gaurīvita and the Āndhīgava; "pavitra te" is the Sāmarāja as the final [Sāman]. 5.
Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna; the Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.
One's own hymns of praise. || 7 ||
The hymns for the third day of the six-day period are the Pramahiṣṭhīya, the Hārivarṇa, and the Tairaśca.
The Āyuṣṭoma is the stoma. || 8 ||

The Gavāmayana consists of the Abhiplava six-day period, with the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant in the *trivṛt* stoma; the *ājya* chants in the *pañcadaśa* stoma; the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina-savana*) in the *saptadaśa* stoma; and the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*) in the *ekaviṃśa* stoma, including the *ukthya* rites. Thus ends the Āyuṣṭoma stoma. 4.
The fourth day of the *Abhiplava* is the "Cow";
the fourth day of the *Abhiplava* cycle, known by the name "Cow," Pavamāna has generated.
Purifying himself, he has stepped forth toward us like eager cattle—O Sage, this is for you, Pavamāna. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

The *prayadgā* consists of six verses; for it is stated that "the rule regarding the beginning of the triplets (*tṛca*) and hymns (*sūkta*) applies when there is no specific instruction. The remaining verses form triplets. 1.
"Agni shall strike down the Vṛtras"—this is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ; his own [verses] follow next.
Thus end the *ājya* [laud verses].
"Agni [drives away] the Vṛtras," "This one for you two, O Mitra and Varuṇa," "Indra with the bones of Dadhyañc"—
these Ājya offerings are designated by their own specific names,
because they belong to the fourth day. 2.

"Pavasva dakṣasādhana" is the Gāyatra [Sāman], and "adāra sṛcca"; "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam" is the Pṛśni, the Ātharvaṇa, the Abhīśava, and the Yaudhājaya; and "oho vā asya" is the final Vāsiṣṭha. || 3 ||
Thus is the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
[The verse] "pṛśnim prathamāyām" is used; "śrīṇantaḥ" is used in the Yaudhājaya Adhyāsya.
3. The Bṛhat and Vāmadevya [Sāmans] are used; "yo rājā carṣaṇīnām" is the Abhīvarta; the Kāleya is used in its own [verses]. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"Priyā divaḥ kaviḥ" is the Gāyatra; "caurṇāyavam" is that which has the *yadi* as its *nidhana*. "Tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya somaḥ punāna urmiṇe" is the Bṛhatka; "sujñāne" is the Gaurīvita and the Tvaṣṭrīsāman, which has the *ūrdhveḍa* as its *nidhana*. "Pro ayāsīd" is the Lauśa, which is the final [Sāman]. 5.
Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
[It is] the *saindhukṣita*, the *saubhara*, the *vīṅka*, or the *śuddhāśuddhīya*, if it is the *aiḍa* [sāman] belonging to the *iḍā* verses.
Thus end the hymns.

The determination of the *vīṅka-śuddha* and *aśuddha* [chants] was stated by Bharga and Yaśas. This is expressed by them as follows: "The *vīṅka-śuddha* and *aśuddha* have been stated by these two. (7)
The Goṣṭoma is a Stoma. || 8 ||
"The Bahiṣpavamāna [stotra] consists of fifteen [verses]," and so forth. || 8 ||
Thus ends the fourth day of the Abhiplava, characterized by the Goṣṭoma Stoma. ||5||
The Gavāmayana consists of the Abhiplava six-day period;
he speaks of the fifth day of the Abhiplava as "Life," the fifth day of the Abhiplava so designated.
O Soma, as you are being purified, that which is all-knowing, wondrous, and worthy of praise belongs to you, O Sage, as you flow clear. 1.
Thus concludes the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, we meditate upon the hymn"—this is the *ājya* (offering verse) of the Hotṛ; his own [verses] follow.
Thus end the offerings of clarified butter.

"Even though there is much that is manifold, arise together with vigor"—these are the subsequent *ājya* chants for Indra and Agni. "Flow on, O Soma, most resplendent!"—the *gāyatra*, the *yaṇva*, the *apatya*, the *saṃtani*, and the *śākvaravarṇa*: these occur in the subsequent [sections]. "The living Somas..."—this includes the *mānava*, the *ānūpa*, the *vāmra*, and the *triṇidhana* of Agni. "Toward the three-backed one"—this is the final *sampāntya*.

Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna. "The lineage, the Saṃtani, and the Śākvaravarṇa; these [are] in the subsequent [days]"—the meaning is that the three Sāmans beginning with the *apatya* are applied respectively to the second and following *abhiplava* days at the *yaṇva*-position. The *Mānava* is on the first day; the *Agnestriṇadha* is on the middle day. || 3 ||
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, and "O Indra, you are glorious"—this is the Abhīvarta; the Kāleya is in its own [verses]. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"asāvy aṃśur madāya" is the *gāyatra* and the *goṣūkta*; "abhidyumnaṃ bṛhad yaśaḥ" and "prāṇāḥ śiśur mahīnām" are for the *cyāvana* at the *sujñāna*. Or [the *daivodāsa*]. "pavasva vājasātaye" is the *gaurīvita* and the *rayiṣṭha*; "asāvi somo aruṣo vṛṣā hariḥ" is the *dvyabhyāghāta*, the *lauśa* being the last. 5.
Thus indeed is the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
There is an option regarding *sujñāna* and *daivodāsa*. || 5 ||
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.
"We have chosen you as the best sacrificer"—this is the Sādhya, the Sāṃvarta, and the Māruta [hymn]. || 7 ||
Thus end the *ukthas*.
The *ayustoma* sacrifice:
the *bahiṣpavamāna* stotra is the *trivṛt*; the *ājya* stotras are the *pañcadaśa*; the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina-savana*) is the *saptadaśa*, and so forth.
Thus ends the fifth day of the *ābhiplavika* period, which constitutes a day of life.

The sixth day of the *abhiplava* period—the sixth day of the *abhiplava* series known as "Light" (*jyotis*)—is described by the verses: "They have let loose the prize-winning steeds," "This very one, the ten fingers [have pressed]," and "O Sage, of thee, the purifying one. (1)
Thus concludes the Bahiṣpavamāna.
The Gavāmayana consists of the Abhiplava six-day period; "O Agni, that mortal whom you [protect] in battles," this is the Ājya-stotra of the Hotṛ; his own [verses] follow next.
Thus end the offerings of clarified butter.
"At the rising of the sun, overcome all our enemies for us; for you two are the officiating priests (ṛtvij) of the sacrifice"—these are the subsequent *ājya* offerings. || 2 ||

With the verse "O Indu, for Indra accompanied by the Maruts," he should perform once the Gāyatra and the Aśvasūkta, as well as the iṣovṛdhīya. With the verse "Being cleansed by the skillful-handed one," he should perform once the Aiḍa, the Auksnorandhra, the Triṇidhana, and the Āyāsya, making them all continuous. With the verse "Together with the sprinkling," he should perform the final Vasiṣṭha chant, which contains the word "here."
Thus ends the midday Pavamāna chant.

"One should perform the *iṣovṛdhīya* once. This means that at the end, one should perform the *iṣovṛdhīya* in place of the *āśvasūkta* during the *abhiplava* [period]. Likewise, in place of the *triṇidhana*, one performs the *samanta*. Thus it has been said: "The *iṣovṛdhīya* and *samanta* [are used] when there is immediate succession to the *pṛṣṭhya*, in the sixth [day].
3. The *bṛhat* and the *vāmadevya*; the *abhīvarta* begins with "Drink of the pressed, flavorful [juice]"; the *kāleya* is in its own [verses]. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"Praised as he dwells on the mountain" (*pari stavāno giriṣṭhā*) is the *gāyatram* and the *caidhmavāham*; "if he is pressed for you who are the masters of wealth" (*yadihavat sa sunve yo vasūnām*) is the *madāya* in the *dīrghasujñāna*, or the *kāśītam*. "The Soma drops flow, the juices" (*somāḥ pavanta indavaḥ*) is the *gaurīvitam* and the *krauñcam* in its own source; "for him the three times seven milch-cows have yielded milk" (*trirasmai sapta dhenavo duduhrire*) is the *marutāṃ dhenu* at the end. || 5 ||
Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
"Yadihavat" means "parisūva iha," which refers to the *aidhmavāha* [sāman]. The phrase "yatsvayoni" is for the purpose of excluding the *vāṅnidhana*. || 5 ||
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.
The *gūrdam*, the *traikakubham*, and the *nārmedham* are the *ukthas*, if the rite is an *ukthya*.

"If they should release the Ukthya-stotras, they should release them"—this means that by resorting to this alternative view, one intends to conclude with the Ukthya. Regarding this, it has been stated: "The releases occur month after month; as at the end, so at the beginning of the repeated [cycles]; in the preceding Abhiplava periods, having performed the sixth day as an Ukthya, the last [day] is an Agniṣṭoma. He states the established conclusion: "But it is the Agniṣṭoma. (7)
The intention is that the discarding [of the fire] is not mandatory; likewise, the Brāhmaṇa states, "If they should discard it."
The Jyotiṣṭoma is the Stoma. || 7 ||

The *bahiṣpavamāna* chant is threefold; the *ājya* chants are fifteenfold; the midday *pavamāna* is fifteenfold; the *pṛṣṭha* chants are seventeenfold; the *ārbhava* is seventeenfold; and the *agniṣṭoma* is twenty-onefold. This is the *ukthya*. || 7 ||
Thus [ends the section on] light.
Thus ends the sixth day of the Abhiplava.
The Abhiplava six-day period is complete.
The Gavāmayana consists of a *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period and another *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period;

likewise, three other *abhiplava* periods must be performed. There is a specific distinction regarding these: on the second day, in place of the *hāviṣmata*, the *yauktāśva* follows; in place of the *maukṣa*, the *hāviṣmata*. On the fifth day of the second *abhiplava*, in place of the *yaṇva*, the *apatya* is used. On the fifth day of the third *abhiplava*, the *saṃtani* is used; and prior to the *mānava*, there are the *vāmra*, the *mānava*, and the *ānūpa*.

On the fifth day, on whatever day the *grāmageya* (village-singing) occurs in the sequence, the *vāmra* should precede the *mānava*, according to the injunction. This is for the sake of avoiding monotony (*ajāmi*). Therein, the *vāmra* is in the first [verse], and the *mānava* in the triplet (*ṛc*). In the fourth *abhiplava*, on the fifth day, there is the *śākvaravarṇa* in place of the *yaṇvas*. On that same sixth day, there is the *iṣovṛdhīya* in place of the *āśvasūkta*. The method of arrangement for the *triṇidhana-āsya*, the *bhadra*, the *yaśas*, the *vīṅka*, and the *śuddha-aśuddhīya* has been stated and should not be forgotten. Everything else is as in the first [day].
Having thus performed four *abhiplava* periods, they enter upon the *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period; he states its arrangement:
the *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period is either contracted (*samūḍha*) or expanded (*vyūḍha*).

Regarding the "expanded" (*vyūḍha*) nature of the *pṛṣṭhya* [six-day rite] mentioned by the Brāhmaṇa: if that is applied to the ten-night sacrifice (*daśarātra*), then this [ten-night sacrifice] ought to be "contracted" (*samūḍha*), because it is uninterrupted. On the other hand, if it is applied to the *pṛṣṭhya* itself, then it is "expanded. Because of this doubt, there is an option; such is the prima facie view (*pūrva-pakṣa*). || 1 ||
He states the established conclusion: "But [the soul] is indeed completely deluded. (Sūtra 2)

Thus, the meaning is that the *vyūha* (rearrangement) is enjoined for the ten-night sacrifice (*daśarātra*). Accordingly, the *Nidāna* states: "Now, moreover, the six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*) is rearranged," and so forth. And another scriptural passage says: "There is no rearrangement of the *pṛṣṭhya* days apart from the *chandoma* days. ||2||
He says, "The ritual procedure for that [sacrifice] which has been summarized will now be stated," thus:
"Its ritual manual (kalpa). (3)
Thus [ends the third section].
Regarding the first day, he says:
"Sing forth to him, O men; sing unto the one born, the swift one—O Sage, of you who are being purified. This is the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant for the first day.

Because there is no connection with the "new" (nava) day for this [hymn] characterized by "ancient" (pratna) luster, it is excluded; for starting from the words "with those containing *pratna* and *upa*," there are nine [verses], according to the Śruti statement: "by means of the yoking of the ninth day."
"O Soma, for the banquet of the gods"—this is the *abhīvarta* on one verse; the *pājra* on one verse; the *yaudhājaya* on one verse; the rest is the same. || 5 ||
The meaning is that everything else is the same as on the first day of the ten-night rite.

The *ājya* stotras are: "O Agni, come to us," and "O Mitra, come hither. The *gāyatra* is: "Forward, O wise Soma-stalks. The triplet for the *āśva-somasāman* is: "Forward, O Soma, for the feast of the gods. The triplets for the *sāmans* are: the *abhīvarta*, the *pajra*, and the *audhājaya*. The final [stotra] is the *auśana*: "Run forward indeed. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are: the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *naudhasa*, and the *kāleya*. In this *pṛṣṭha* as well, the *pṛṣṭha*-dharmas, such as the sound of chariots and so forth, must be performed.

Because of the statement, "In all cases, there should be a *pṛṣṭha* [stotra] together with its constituent *dharmas*. In the *gāyatra* [sāman], [the verse] "pra somāso madacyutaḥ" is used in a single [verse]. In that very [verse], the *gavāmayana* sacrifice includes the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha* as a continuous unit. In the two single-verse [sāmans], [the verses] "ayā pavasva devayuḥ" and "pavate haryato hariḥ" are used for the *sapha* and *akṣāra* [stotras]. For the first [stotra], the *gaurīvitagautama* is used with the verse "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ"; the final [sāman] is the *kāva*; the *agniṣṭomasāman* is the *yajñāyajñīya*. Everything is *trivṛt*. Here, this should be kept in mind.

Because it is heard in the section on the *Abhīvarta* that "if they were to release the *Sāman*, they would fall from the heavenly world," and because it is established that the *Abhīvarta* must be performed everywhere during the first fortnight (*pūrva-pakṣas*), yet—due to the fact that the *Pṛṣṭha* [Stotra] has various *Brahmasāmans*—it cannot there be resolved as a *Brahmasāman* in the same manner as the *Abhiplava*. Therefore, it is inserted into the *Vṛhatī* verses of the *Pāvamānī* hymns. And for the sake of fulfilling the *stoma* through constant favor, a single verse (*ekarcam*) is formed by combining the adventitious verses with the permanent ones.

On that occasion, from the second day onwards, the *kāleya* will be prepared as an additional (*āgantuka*) element. Indeed, we prepare that *kāleya* among the *bṛhatī* verses, thinking, "In this [day], there shall be a corresponding [verse] for the *sata*. However, on this [first] day, because the *kāleya* serves as the *sāman* for the *acchāvāka*, the *pajra* has been prepared as an additional element so that the fault of displacement (*saṃcāradoṣa*) may not occur. || 5 || || 8 ||
On the second day, [the stotras are]:

for the *pavamāna*, "soma dhāraya" (Soma, hold fast); the *aiḍam āyāsya* on one verse; the *abhīvarta* on one verse; the *kāleya* on one verse; and the final *pārtha*, "vṛṣā śoṇa. This is for the midday pressing. The rest is the same.

Thus [it is said]. By the word *mādhyaṃdina*, the *mādhyaṃdina-pavamāna* is everywhere referred to in the ritual manual (*kalpa*). Since, according to the Vāsiṣṭha school, it is to be arranged as the final [stotra] of the sixth day, the *pārtha* [sāman] is here arranged for the sake of avoiding displacement (*asaṃcāra*). "This *stoma* is the *kṣatrasāman*; it is appropriate for the *bṛhatī-pṛṣṭha*"—this is the underlying principle (*nidāna*). In that regard, the arrangement is as follows: *pavasva vacaḥ*, *pavasvendo*, *vṛṣā soma vṛṣā hyasi*, and *pavamānasya te vayam* constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna*.

"agnim dūtam mitram vayam indramit gāḥ"—this is the four-verse [stotra]. "indre agnā" and so forth are the Ājya-stotras. In the four-verse [stotra], there is the omission of the final verse. "vṛṣā pavasva dhāraya" is the Gāyatra and the Yauktāśva. "punānaḥ soma dhāraya" is the Aiḍamāyāsya; "abhīvartaḥ" and "kāleyam" are the Sāman-trikas. The Āyāsya has three Nidhanas. In the Trika [stotra], "vṛṣā śoṇa" is the Pārtha and the final [Sāman]. The Bṛhat, Vāmadevya, Śyaita, and Mādhucchandasa are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras.

In the *Bṛhat-stotra*, they should strike the drum. [The verses] "yaste mado vareṇya" (RV 9.11.1) and "pavasvendramaccha" (RV 9.108.1)—these two single-verse hymns are the *gāyatram* and the *hāviṣmatam*. [The verse] "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhaga" (RV 9.67.25) is the *gaurīvitam* on a single verse; the *krauñcam* is on three verses. [The verse] "vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate" (RV 9.86.12) is the final *yāma*. The *yajñāyajñīyam* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *sākamaśvam*, the *gavāmayana*, and the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha* are included. "evā hy asi vīti" is the *āmahīyavam*; "āṣṭādaṃṣṭram" and others are the *ukthas*. Everything is fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*). 6 || 9 || 1 ||

On the third day, the *paurumadga* hymn, beginning with "The Soma-drops, the Āyus... (*abhi somāsa āyavaḥ*), is used for the first [stotra]; on that same [day], the *abhīvarta* is used; the *kāleya* for the second; the *gautama* for the third; the rest is the same.

Thus, according to the rule that "of four [verses], two are used in the first [turn], and the other two in the subsequent turns," the *ekarcakaraṇa* (the performance of single verses) is carried out in this manner. Now, the arrangement (*klṛpti*): The *bahiṣpavamāna* consists of: *davidyutatyā rucā*, *ete asṛgram idavo*, *rājā medhābhir īyate*, *taṃ tvā nṛmṇāni bibhratam*, and *iṣe pavasva dhāraya*. The *ājya* stotras consist of: *agninā mitraṃ huve*, *indreṇa tā huve*, and the *gāyatra* and *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha* chants beginning with *uccā te jātam andhasaḥ*.

"Abhisomāsa āyavaḥ"—this is the *paurumadga* [sāman] on the first verse. The three verses of the *abhīvarta-kāleya* with the *gautama* *sāman* are for the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*) on the three verses. "Pra hinvānaḥ"—on this [verse], the *āṣkāra-nidhana* is used as the final verse. "Tisro vācaḥ"—this is the final *saṃkrośa* of the Aṅgirases. There are also the *vairūpa* and the *vāmadevya*. "Vayaṃ gha tve"—this is the *mahāvaiṣṭambha*. "Taraṇiritsiṣāsati"—[these follow].

The *pṛṣṭha* lauds are the *raurava*. "While fanning [the fire], they should chant with the *vairūpa*" and so forth. The *gāyatra* and the *pāṣṭhauha* are [chanted] to the verses beginning "Three voices arise" (*tisro vāca udīrate*). The *vācaḥsāman* and the *śaukta* are [chanted] to the two single-verse hymns beginning "O friends, pour out [the soma], sprinkle it around" (*ā sotā pariṣiñcata sakhāya ā niṣīdata*). The *gaurīvita* and the *triṇidhana*—the *tvāṣṭrīsāman*—are [chanted] to the verse beginning "The pressed juices, most sweet" (*sutāso madhumattamā*). The *ariṣṭa* is the final [laud] with the verse beginning "Your filter" (*pavitraṃ te*). The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The *pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *tairaśca* are the *ukthas*. Everything is seventeenfold. 1 || 10 ||

For the fourth day, the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses are: "The Pavamāna has brought forth" (*caturthasyāhnaḥ pavamāno ajījanat*) and "Purifying himself, he has stepped forth toward" (*punāno akramīdabhi*). The *ājya* for the Hotṛ is: "May Agni strike down the Vṛtras" (*agnirvṛtrāṇi jaṅghanat*). The *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* chant follows with "O Soma, I have rejoiced in thee" (*tavāhaṃ soma rāraṇa*), performed on a single verse; the *abhīvarta* on a single verse; the *kāleya* on a single verse; and the final *janitra* chant with "Soma flows, the progenitor of thoughts" (*somaḥ pavate janitā matīnām*). The final *lauśa* chant of the midday pressing is "O Pavamāna, these milch-cows of thine, belonging to the Aśvins" (*pra ta āśvinīḥ pavamāna dhenavaḥ*). For the Ārbhava pressing, it is the same as before. 1.

Regarding the Gavāmayana, the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha [is prescribed]. The first triplet of the Bahiṣpavamāna is the *stotrīya*; the second is the *anurūpa*. Here, by means of the mutual displacement of the spheres (*loka*) of the Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh, and Jagatī meters, there is an arrangement similar to the archetype (*prakṛti*), which is called "the collection" (*samūha*). In this three-day period characterized by displacement (*vaiyūhika*), since the Jagatī and Triṣṭubh have been performed at the end of the Ārbhava Pavamāna and the end of the Mādhyandina Pavamāna respectively, the Bahiṣpavamāna remains in its archetypal position. Consequently, the Vaiyūhika sacrificial post (*yūpa*) and the Gāyatrī triplet at the end of the Mādhyandina Pavamāna are desired to remain in their respective positions according to proximity.

And the *ājya* offerings of the Hotṛ priest: having extracted the *vaiyūhika* verses, it should be understood that the *gāyatra* verses, which correspond to their respective divisions, are substituted in their place.

Now follows its arrangement: *pavamāno ajījanat*, *punāno akramīd abhi*, *pra yad gāvo na bhūrṇayaḥ*, *āśur ṛṣab bṛhanmate*, and *hinvanti sūram usrāḥ*—these constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna*. *Agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanat*, *ayaṃ vāṃ mitrāvaruṇā*, *indro dadhīco asthabhiḥ*, and *iyaṃ vāmasya manmanaḥ*—these are the *ājya* hymns. *Pavasva dakṣasādhanaḥ*—this is the *gāyatra*, the *ātharvaṇa*, and the *nidhanakāma*. *Tavāhaṃ soma rāraṇa*, *ābhīvartaḥ*, and *kāleyam*—these are the triple-verse *sāman*s, including the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*. The *ābhīśava* is performed on three verses.

*Svaḥpṛṣṭha* is [performed] in the *triṣṭubh* meters. "Soma flows, the progenitor of hymns" (*somaḥ pavate janitā matīnām*) is the final *janitra*. The *pṛṣṭha* chants are the *vairāja*, the *vāmadevya*, the *traiśoka*, and the *pṛśni*. Regarding the *vairāja*, the procedure begins with "Having commenced the *stotra*," and so forth. "The sage of heaven, beloved on all sides" (*paripriyā divaḥ kaviḥ*) is the *gāyatra* and the *aurṇāyava*. "For you, O Soma, are indeed divine" (*tvaṃ hyaṅga daivyaṃ soma*) and "Purifying yourself with your wave" (*punāna ūrmiṇā*) are the *bṛhat* chants according to the *Kātīṣādīya*. "With your conquest of the front, O juice" (*purojitī vo andhasaḥ*) is the *nānada* and the *āndhīgava*.

The final [laud] is the Lauśa, beginning with *pra ta āśvinīḥ*. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *ukthas* are the Saindhukṣita, the Saubhara, and the Vasiṣṭha-priya. The *ṣoḍaśin-sāman* is the Gaurīvita, beginning with *indra juṣasva*. Everything is in the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*) stoma. || 1 || 11 ||

For the *pavamāna* of the fifth day, the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses are "O Soma, all-knowing one, that which is bright and worthy of praise" (*viśvavit yat soma citramukthyam*). The *ājya* of the Hotṛ is "O Agni, we meditate upon the hymn" (*agne stomaṃ manāmahe*). For the two triplets of the Mānavas and the Ānūpas, [the verses are] "Soma, pressed by the pressers" (*soma uṣvāṇaḥ sotṛbhiḥ*). [The verses] "Vāmraka" are on one [verse], "Abhīvarta" on one, and "Kāleya" on one. "Indu, the racer, flows toward the streams of milk" (*indurvājī pavate gonyoghā*) is the concluding verse of the midday pressing. In the place of the Pārtha [laud], there is the Tvaṣṭṛ-sāman, which is the "Dvyanutoda. "Flow on, finding cattle" (*govit pavasva*) is the Lauśa, the final [sāman] of the third pressing, characterized by a double repetition (*dvyabhyāghāta*). The rest is the same.
"The Gavamayana consists of the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha.

Regarding the world of Pārtha, it is stated for the purpose of the transition that "the Sāman belongs to Tvaṣṭṛ. For the Pavamāna: "O Soma, you who know all," "That wonderful hymn of praise, O Soma," "The Somas have flowed forward," "The sage [has flowed] forward for the feast of the gods," "Like barley, O we who seek barley, with your juice," and "Those streams of yours which drip honey"—these constitute the Bahiṣpavamāna. "O Agni, we meditate upon the hymn," "For even by the wide [space] there is [a way]," "Arising together with vigor," and "O Indra and Agni, you two indeed"—these are the Ājya-stotras.

"O Soma, most brilliant one," beginning with *arṣā soma dyumattamaḥ*, are the Gāyatra, Yaṇva, Śākala, and Vārśa [Sāmans]. For the two triplets beginning with "Soma, pressed by the pressers," there are the Mānava and Ānūpa [Sāmans]. There are the triplets for the Sāmans Vāma, Abhīvarta, and Kāleya. The Agni-triṇidhana is performed on three verses. "The Indu, the prize-winner, flows clear"—this is the final [verse] of the Saṃpāntī. The Pṛṣṭha [Stotras] consist of the Mahānāmnīs, the Vāmadevya, the Bārhadgira, and the Rāyovājīya. Having placed water in the Sāvaka [vessel], they should chant the praise with the Mahānāmnīs, and so forth.

"asāvyaṃśurmadāya" is the *gāyatram* and the *saṃtani*; "abhidyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśaḥ prāṇāśiśurmahīnām" is the *cyāvana* and the *krośa*; "pavasva vājasātaye" is the *gaurīvita*, the *ṛṣabha-śākvara*, the *tvāṣṭrīsāman*, the *dvyanutoda*, the *aṣṭeḍa*, and the *padastobha*; "govitpavasva" is the final *dvyabhyāghāta-lauśa*; the *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*; and the *saṃjaya*, *saumitra*, and *mahāvaiśvāmitra* are the *ukthasthānas*. All [these] are the *triṇava* [stoma]. 12.

For the sixth day, the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses are "The vigorous ones have flowed forth" (*asṛkṣata pra vājinaḥ*) and "This one, the ten fingers [have pressed]" (*etamu tyaṃ daśa kṣipaḥ*). The *ājya* of the Hotṛ is "O Agni, the mortal whom [you protect] in battles" (*yamagne pṛtsu martyam*). [The *stotriya*] beginning with "Being cleansed by the skillful hand" (*mṛjyamānaḥ suhastya*) is the *svāra-sāman*; the *aiḍa-sāman* on three verses of the *aukṣṇorandhra* melody; the *aiḍa-sāman* on one verse of the *aukṣṇorandhra* melody; the *abhīvarta-sāman* on one verse; and the *kāleya-sāman* on one verse. The final [verse] of the midday pressing belongs to Vasiṣṭha and contains the word "here" (*iha*).
"Jyotir yajñasya pavate madhu priyam"—this [verse] belongs to the Maruts; it is the one for the *dhenū* of the Ārbhava [laud]. The rest is the same. The rest is the same. || 1 ||
Thus ends the first chapter in the Ārṣeyakalpasūtra. || 1 ||

The vigorous ones have been let loose; these ten fingers [have sent forth] this one to be raised up. Flow on, O Soma, for the sake of the gods; win and conquer! The exhilarating one runs across the waters. These Somas have been let loose—thus [is the *bahispavamāna*]. "O Agni, [protect] the mortal in battles; against you both at the rising of the sun, shatter all enemies. "For you two are the officiants of the sacrifice"—thus [are] the *ājya* hymns. "For Indra, O Indu, accompanied by the Maruts"—thus [are] the *gāyatra*, *ceṣovṛdhīya*, *gāyatrīkrauñca*, and *vājadāvarya*. And the *gavām ayana*: the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*.

And the *revatī* verses. Regarding the phrase "being cleansed" (*mṛjyamānaḥ*), there are the *svāra*, the *aukṣṇorandhra*, and the *aiḍa* on three verses; the *aukṣṇorandhra*, the *abhīvarta*, and the *kāleya*—these are the *sāman*s on a triplet of verses. The *vājajit* is the *varuṇasāman*. The *aṅgirasāṃ goṣṭha* is also on three verses. The final [verse] is the *vāsiṣṭha* beginning with "Flow with this [stream], bringing these riches" (*ayā pavasvainā vasūni*). On the *revatī* verses is the *vāravantīya*. On its own [verses] is the *vāmadevya*. On the verse "The fair-formed doer for our aid" (*surūpakṛtnumūtaye*) is the *ṛṣabha-raivatam*. And on the verse "When both, O Indra" (*ubhe yadindra*) are the *śyena* and the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

In the *stotra* of the *Vāravantīya*, the characteristics of the *pṛṣṭha* are stated as beginning with "the milch-cow" (*dhenu*). There is the *gāyatra* chant "parisvāno giriṣṭhā," and the three *vaidanvata* chants (the third *vaidanvata*, the first *vaidanvata*, and the fourth *vaidanvata*). Also, "sasunveyo vasūnām" and "taṃ vaḥ sakhāyo madāya" belong to the *dīrgha-kārṇaśravasa*. Furthermore, there is the *gaurīvita* chant "somāḥ pavante," the *madhuścinnidhana*, the *krauñca* with the *vāṅnidhana*, and the *aiḍakrauñca*.

"Jyotir yajñasya" is the final [verse] for the Maruts' *dhenu*. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. "Agne tvam no antamaḥ" is the *gūrda*. "Imā nu kam" is the *bhadra*. "Pra va indrāya" and "Udvaṃśaputra" are the *ukthas*. All [the verses] consist of thirty-three syllables.

"On the sixth day having concluded," and so forth, as before. Regarding this, the Sūtra states: "One should combine the *ābhīvarta* stotriyas with the *ābhiplāvika* [verses] on the *pṛṣṭhya* [day]; by the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the *kāleya* verses; and by the Acchāvāka, [the verses] everywhere, when they might be in the *pavamāna* [laud]. In that regard, for the first and second days, there is the *ābhīvarta* of the *ābhiplāvika*.

Because the *pārṣṭika* [stotras] of the *naudhasa* and *śyaita* have identical *stotrīyās*, there is no separate instruction for them. And so it is for the *kāleya* on the first day. Thus, with four *abhiplava* periods and one *pṛṣṭhya*, one month is completed. That is the second; that is the third; that is the fourth; that is the fifth. In the sixth month as well, three *abhiplavas* are to be performed; there is an omission of the fourth, because of the statement: "In the first fortnight, the fourth *abhiplava* among the three [sets] should be omitted."
In the third *abhiplava* period, on the sixth day, the two *iṣovṛdhīya* chants should be at the end; for it is stated that the sixth [day] follows immediately after the *pṛṣṭhya*.
The *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period should be performed as before. || 1 || 13 ||
Thus ends the first chapter in the commentary on the Ārṣeyakalpasūtra composed by Varadarāja, son of the venerable Vāmanārya. || 1 ||

Flow on as the leader of speech; being purified, he has stepped forth. O Sage, we choose Agni as our messenger for you, the Pavamāna. Come to us, O Mitra and Varuṇa! O Bull, come to the pressed juice, O Indra and Agni! "High is the birth of your plant"—this is the Gāyatra, the Mahīyava, and the Satrāsāhīya. "Being purified, O Soma, in your stream"—this is the Abhīvarta, the Raurava, and the Yaudhājaya. "Flow toward Vāyu, being praised"—this is the final Pārtha. And [the hymns] Bṛhat, Vāmadevya, Śyaita, and Kāleya, with the verse beginning "With the sweetest [honey]."

With the verse *madiṣṭhayā*, the *gāyatra-saṃhita* [is performed]; with *pavasvendram accha*, the *sapha-sujñāna*; with *purojitī vo andhasaḥ*, the *gaurīvita* on three verses; the *gaurīvita* on one verse; the *madhuścunnidhana* on one verse; the *śyāvāśva* on one verse; thus the *vāndhīgava* on three verses; the *yajñāyajñīya* and the *bṛhat*; the *kāva* hymn for Agni as the final part; the *rathaṃtara* as the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* among the verses of the *yajñāyajñīya*; for the *sarvastoma* sacrifice, the stomas are repeated three times and there are four *praṇayas*. 21.

"Sing forth to him, O men; sing well to him who is born, the lord of the waters. To you, who bear manly powers—O Pavamāna, O Sage, O Agni, come hither for the feast. These are the *ājya* verses. "The wise Soma juices flow"—this is the *gāyatra*. "Toward the Soma juices, the Āyus"—this is the *pauruhanmana*, the *dvaigata*, the *gauṅgava*, the *yaudhājaya*, and the *auśana* as the last. "When you were born, O unprecedented one"—this is the *rathaṃtara*. The *antara* is in its own [verses], the *vāmadevya* is in its own [verses]. That of yours...

The *abhīvarta* [stotra] consists of "dasma mṛtīṣaham"; the *kāleya* on its own verses; the *gāyatra* "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" and the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*; the *saphasujñāna* "ā pavasva devayuḥ" and "pavate haryato hariḥ"; the *kāśīta* "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ"; the *gaurīvita* on three verses—or alternatively, the *gaurīvita* on one verse, the *gautama* on one verse, and the *audala* on one verse; the *svara* [stotra] on three verses; and the *aiḍa* "yat payo nidhanam" as well as "abhi priyāṇi"; the *kāva* is the final [stotra], which is *svāra*, if it is so.

One may optionally choose the Yajñāyajñīya as the Agniṣṭoma-sāman, or the Auśana, or the Aupagava, or the Vasiṣṭha-priya, or the Tairaścya; [one may choose] the Ukthas if it is an Ukthya sacrifice, but it is indeed an Agniṣṭoma. 22.

Flow on as the leader of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. O Soma, you are brilliant; your powers surge forth. O Sage, for you who are being purified, we choose Agni as our messenger—these are the *ājya* verses. "Flow on as a bull in your stream" is the *gāyatra* and the *yauktāśva*. "Pour out the pressed juice on all sides" is the *samanta* and the *dairghaśravasa*. "The bull, the ruddy one" is the final *pārtha*. "Great is your draught for the fish" is the *bṛhat*. "Upon your own [waters]" is the *vāmadevya*. "Forward toward you... [is the *abhitvā*].

"Surādhasam" is the Abhīvarta; "svāsu kāleyam" [is the Kāleya]; "yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" is the Gāyatra and the Hāviṣmat; "pavasvendramaccha" is the Śaṅkusujñāna; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ" is the Gaurīvita. [The Gaurīvita] is on three verses, the Krauñca on one verse, and the Āsita on one verse—or rather, the Svara on three verses. In the two Bṛhannidhanas, the former [Gaurīvita] is on the first [verse] and the latter on the repeated [verses]. "vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate" is the Aiḍa; the final Yāma is the Svara, if it is so.

One may optionally perform the Yajñāyajñīya as the Agnistoma-sāman, the Sākamaśva, the Saubhara, and the Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra as the Ukthas, provided it is an Ukthya sacrifice; however, it is indeed an Agniṣṭoma. 23.

*vidyutatyā rucaite*, *asṛgram indavaḥ*, *rājā medhābhir īyate*. "Purify yourself; bring rain for us"—this is the *pavamāna* [laud]. "For you, O Sage, by means of fire, fire is kindled"—these are the *ājya* [stotras]. *uccā te jātam andhasaḥ* is the *gāyatra*; *cāmahīyava* is the *āmahīyava*. *abhi somāsa āyavaḥ* is the *paurumadga*; the *gautama*; the *antarikṣa*; and the *triṇidhana* of Agni. *tisro vācaḥ* is the *saṃkrośa* of the Aṅgirases, being the last [verse]. *pratyasmai pipīṣataḥ* is the *rathantara*; the *vāmadevya* is in its own [verses].

"Vayaṃ gha tvā sutāvantaḥ" is the Abhīvarta; "Svāsu kāleyam" consists of three verses beginning with "tisro vāca udīrate," which are combined in the Gāyatrī meter; "Ā sotā pariṣiñcata sakhāya ā niṣīdata" contains both Vācas and Sāman, as does the Daivodāsa hymn; "sutāso madhumattamāḥ" is the Gaurīvita; on three verses there is the Gaurīvita, on one the Āndhīgava, and on one the Tvāṣṭrīsāman—or alternatively, the Svara-sāman on three verses; "yat prathamaṃ pavitraṃ te" is the Ariṣṭa; the final [hymn] is the Svāra-Sāmarāja.

If he should differentiate them—the Yajñāyajñīya as the Agniṣṭoma-sāman, the Pramahiṣṭhīya, the Hārivarṇa, and the Udvaṃśīya as the Ukthas—if it is an Ukthya; but if it is an Agniṣṭoma, all [the stotras] are seventeen-fold (saptadaśa). 24

"Sing forth to him, O men! To the tawny one, who possesses his own power—let the pressed drops flow forth like chariots. O Sage, may Agni, as you are being purified, strike down the Vṛtras. When the sun has risen today, let him rise up toward the famous wealth. This is the thought of the beautiful one; according to its ancient splendor, this is the Gāyatra, the radiant, ever-conquering song. 'O Soma, I have rejoiced in thee'—this is the *utsedha* [elevation]. In three verses there is the *abhīśava*; in one, the *abhīvarta*; in one, the *pṛśni*; in three, the *rathaṃtara*, [singing] to the newborn infant."

"Haryataṃ mṛjanti" is the Pārtha; "Mahādivākīrtya" and "Vāmadevya"; "Indra kratuṃ na ā bhara" is the Vikarṇa; "Svāsu kāleyaṃ pari svāno giriṣṭhā" is the Gāyatra and the Abhrāja; "Abhi dyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśaḥ prāṇā śiśurmahīnām" are the Sapha and Śrudhya, consisting of single verses each; "Pary ū ṣu" is the Śyāvāśva on a single verse; "Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Bṛhat on three verses; the Gaurīvita on one verse; the Āndhīgava on one verse; and the Niṣedha on one verse.

The *yajñāyajñīya* on three verses, the *kāva* ending with "dhartā divaḥ," the *mūrdhānaṃ divo aratiṃ pṛthivyāḥ*, the *bhāsa* with ten *stobhas*, and the *agniṣṭomasāman* with the twenty-one-fold *stoma*; the *mahāvaiṣṭambha*, the *śyaita*, and the *naudhasa*—these are the *brahmasāmans* for those who have turned back from the *svarasāmans*. In the world of *abhīvarta*, there is the *pauṣkala* for the *rathantara* chants and the *śrudhya* for the *bṛhat* chant, in the world of *sujñāna*.

"May the sisterly songs approach you like women seeking a husband, O Agni; and may that which is dear among our dears be the desirable boon of Savitṛ. "The sounding of the Soma-pressings—O Agni, come hither! "You are being purified as Pavamāna, O Sage; well-kindled, bring [the gods] to us. "That which is capable for us of the earthly [world]. "They yoke the ruddy, bright [horse]; praise him who with his flame follows his ancient radiance. [Then follow] the Gāyatra and the Āmahīyava [sāmans]. "Pour out the pressed [Soma] on all sides"—this is the Kāleya [sāman] on one verse; the Rathantara [sāman] on three verses.

The *Dairghaśravasa* [is used] in three [verses], the *Yaudhājaya* in one; "This Soma" (*ayaṃ soma*) is the final *Pārtha* and the *Vairāja*; the *Mahānāmnīs*, the *Vairūpas*, and the *Revatīs*; "Flowing around, dwelling on the mountain" (*pari svāno giriṣṭhā*) is the *Gāyatra-saṃhitā*; "Flow pure toward Indra" (*pavasvendram accha*) is the *Satrāsāhīya* and the *Śrudhya*; "Around you indeed" (*pary ū ṣu*) is the *Vāmadevya*; "With the conquest of your food" (*purojitī vo andhasaḥ*) is the *Āndhīgava* in one [verse]; the *Gaurīvita* in one; the *Yadvāhiṣṭhīya* in one; the *Yajñāyajñīya* in three; and "Run forward" (*pari pra dhanva*) in the *dvipadās*.

The Vāravantīya is performed on verses containing the word "sūrya"; the Kāvamantya is "O Agni, you are the Hotṛ of sacrifices"; the Bṛhat is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman for the Sarvastoma sacrifice; there are fourfold repetitions of the Stomas, and the Praṇavas are recited three times. 26.

The *paurumīḍha*, the *mānava*, the *janitra*, the *bhāradvāja*, the *vāsiṣṭha*, the *gauṅgava*, and the *śuddhāśuddhīya*—these are the *vaita* single-verse hymns (*ekarcas*) for the *āvṛtta* *pṛṣṭhya* sacrifice in the *abhīvarta* world. "O Indra, bring us wisdom"—this is the *paurumīḍha*, the *mānava*, the *janitra*, the *bhāradvāja*, the *śyaita*, and the *naudhasa*; these are the *brahmasāmans* for the *āvṛtta* *abhiplava* sacrifice in the *abhīvarta* world. The *pauṣkala* is for the *rāthaṃtara* verses, the *śrudhya* is for the *bārhatas*, and [the *sujñāna*] is in the world of good knowledge. 27.

The Jyotiṣṭoma, the Ājyabahiṣpavamāna, the Gāyatrī [chant], and the [verse] "ā soma ā yāhi" with two *hiṃkāras*; the Vārkajambha; the Bṛhannidhana, the Maidhātitha, and either the Raurava or the Yaudhājaya; the Auśana as the final [part]; the Rathantara and the Vāmadevya; the Naudhasa with the verse "indra kratuṃ na ā bhara"; the Kāleya in its own [verses]; the Gāyatra-saṃhita with the verses "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā"; the Sapha and Pauṣkala with the verse "pavasvendram accha"; and [the verse] "purojitī vo andhasaḥ."
The Gaurīvita, the Āndhīgava, the Kāva, the Antya, the Yajñāyajñīya as the Agniṣṭoma-sāman, the Pramahiṣṭhīya, the Hārivarṇa, and the Udvaṃśīya—these are the Ukthas; the Āyuṣṭoma is the Stoma. 28.

Flow on as the leader of speech, with a flashing luster; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. O Soma, you are the brilliant bull. For you, the purifying sage, we choose Agni as the messenger—with the verse "His ancient splendor," the *gāyatram* and the *āmahīyavam*; with "Pour out the pressed juice on every side," the *samantam* and the *vārkajambham*; or the *dainya*, the *dairghaśravasam*, or the *bārhaduktham*, or the *yaudhājayam*; with "This Soma," the *pārtham* as the final [verse], the *bṛhat* and the *vāmadevyam*, and for Indra—

"Bring us the sacrifice"—this is the Śyaita; "In your own [songs] the Kāleya"; "That exhilaration of yours which is most excellent"—this is the Gāyatra on the Auksa verses; "Flow toward Indra"—this is the Saphaśrudhya; "With your food, O you who conquer first"—this is the Gaurīvita on the Andhīgava verses; the final [verse] among those containing *sūryavat* is the Kāva; the Agniṣṭomasāman is the Yajñāyajñīya; the Ukthas are the Sākamaśva, the Saubhara, and the Udvaṃśīya; the Stoma is the Goṣṭoma. 29.

Sing forth to him, O men; sing well to him who is born, the one who crosses the waters. Flow on, O Indu, as the foremost of speech. Flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull; he shines with flashing luster. The drops have been poured forth for us, grain by grain, with their juice. O Sage, may the immortal divine Hotṛ of you, the purifying one, be able to grant us those aids of the earthly realm that create beautiful forms. Pour out the glory upon the pressed juice, according to its ancient splendor—[reciting] the Gāyatra, the Cāmahīyava, the Jarābodhīya, and the Satrāsāhīya: "Pour out the pressed juice all around."

The *samanta*, the *dairghaśravasa*, the *raurava*, and the *yaudhājaya*; "This is Soma" is the final *pārtha* [stotra]; the *vrata* and the *pṛṣṭha* [stotra] consist of thirteen verses; the *brāhmaṇakḷpta* is the *parimāda*; "Indra, him the singers of *gāthās*" and "Indra with the bones of Dadhyañc," "Upward, toward the famous wealth"—these form the threefold *trivṛt* head, which is the *gāyatra*. The fifteen-versed *pañcadaśa* *rathantara* is the right wing; the seventeen-versed *saptadaśa* *bṛhat* is the left wing; the twenty-one-versed *ekaviṃśa* "That indeed was the best among beings" is the tail.

The *pañcaviṃśa* is the *rājana*; the other *pañcaviṃśa* is everything. The *vāmadevya*, the *maitrāvaruṇasāman*, [consists of] "In the *trikadrukas*, the buffalo [drank] the barley-mash"—this is the *vāmadevya* with five *nidhanas* as the *brahmasāman*. On its own verses is the *kāleya*; "Surrounding, dwelling on the mountain"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *svāśira*, the *arka*. "Purify yourself, go toward Indra"—this is the *sapha* and *śrudhya*. "With your first conquest of the soma-juice"—this is the *gaurīvita* and the *madhuścunnidhana*. On the *sūryavatī* verses are the *śyāvāśva* and *āndhīgava*; the *kāva* is the final [part], and the *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. 2101.

The *udayanīya* Atirātra sacrifice is established in the same manner as the *prāyaṇīya*. Now, regarding those one-day (*ekāha*) sacrifices prescribed in the Brāhmaṇa by means of four chapters beginning with the *ṣoḍaśin*, their arrangement is here stated by means of three [chapters]: the commencement time, the initiation (*dīkṣā*), the days of the *upasad* rites, the sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*), and so forth, are declared in the Sūtra by the four chapters beginning with "the northern course of the sun" (*udagayana*) and "the first fortnight" (*pūrvapakṣa*).
This concludes the second chapter of the Vivṛti.
Victorious, you proclaim victory; flow as the foremost of speech. Purifying yourself, you have stepped forth; O Sage, this belongs to you, the Pavamāna.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna. || 1 ||
We choose Agni as our messenger; O Mitra and Varuna, come to us; O Bull Indra-Agni, come to the pressed juice.
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.

"High is the birth of your juice"—this is the Gāyatra, the Āmahīyava, and the Satrāsāhīya; "Being purified, O Soma, in your stream"—this is the Abhīvarta, the Raurava, and the Yaudhājaya; "Toward Vāyu, toward the guest"—this is the Pārtha at the end.
Thus is the Mādhyandina Pavamāna,
as well as the Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita, and the Kāleya.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭhas*. 4.

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" is the *gāyatra-saṃhitā*; "pavasvendram accha" is the *sapha-sujñāna*; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the *gaurīvita* in three verses; or alternatively, the *gaurīvita* in one verse, the *madhuścunnidhana* in one verse, and the *śyāvāśva* in one verse; the *āndhīgava* in three verses, the *yajñāyajñīya*, and the *bṛhat* for Agni; and the *kāva* is the final [stotra]. || 5 ||

Thus, the Ārbhava Pavamāna [stotra] has the Gaurīvita Sāman in the place of the Gaurīvita; the triplet of verses for this Sāman is optional, beginning with the Gaurīvita. Now, there is another Agniṣṭoma Sāman. According to the principle that "the Yajñāyajñīya occurs in Anuṣṭubh verses," the Yajñāyajñīya is arranged upon Anuṣṭubh meters. || 5 ||

In the verses of the *yajñāyajñīya*, the *rathantara* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. (6) Here, the properties (*dharma*) of the *rathantara* are not to be performed. Because of the statement, "Since it is not a *pṛṣṭha-stotra*, its properties shall be set aside," the properties of the *yajñāyajñīya* are instead to be performed. In that regard, the looking at the wife occurs at the point of the *pratihāra*. For there is the statement: "At the time of the *pratihāra* which is without the *hiṃ*-call, the Udgātṛ [should look] at the wife. (6)
He states the arrangement of the *stomas*: for the *sarvastoma* sacrifice, there is a threefold repetition of the *stomas* and four leadings (*praṇayas*).

Thus are the *stomas* of the *sarvapṛṣṭha*. That in which there are the *trivṛt*, *pañcadaśa*, *saptadaśa*, *ekaviṃśa*, *triṇava*, and *trayastriṃśa* is the *sarvastoma*. Of such a [sacrifice] as that, being the *abhijit*, those *stomas* beginning with the *trivṛt* are performed three times over and commence four times each. Three by three [are the days of] the *gavāmayana*; the *svarasāman*s [are mentioned] in section 2, chapter 2.

The meaning is that they lead forth the *stomas* four times. And so says the Śruti: "They lead forth three *trivṛt*s for the *Abhijit*, three *pañcadaśa*s, and three *ekaviṃśa*s. Among these, one leading forth consists of the *trivṛt* *bahiṣpavamāna*, the *pañcadaśa* *hotṛ-ājya*, and the *saptadaśa* *maitrāvaruṇa-ājya*. The *pañcadaśa* [belongs] to the *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin*.

The seventeenth [stoma] for the Acchāvāka and the twenty-first for the Mādhyandina Pavamāna—this is the second [turn]. The seventeenth for the Hotṛ’s Pṛṣṭha, the twenty-first for the Maitrāvaruṇa, and the twenty-sevenfold for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin—this is the third [turn]. The twenty-first for the Acchāvāka, the twenty-sevenfold for the Ārbhava, and the thirty-threefold for the Agniṣṭoma—this is the fourth turn. Thus are the stomas with three turns and four turns of the *praṇayas*. ||7|| 1 ||
Thus [ends] Abhijit. || 1 ||

Regarding the first of the Svarasāmans, which are prescribed by the rule "these are the first Svarasāmans," he states the arrangement for the first: "Sing unto him, O men; sing unto him who is born, the swift one; thee, who bearest manly powers—of thee, the purifying one, O sage, of thee, the purifying one. (1)
Thus ends the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "O Agni, come for the feast!"—thus are the *ājya* [stotras].
"O Soma juices, wise ones..."—this is the Gāyatra; "The Soma juices, the Āyus..."—this is the Pauruhanmana, the Dvaigata, the Gauṅgava, the Yaudhājaya, and the Auśana as the final one. 3.

[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna. The Pauruhanmana [Sāman] is on the first [verse]; the Yaudhājaya is on the middle [verse]. "When you were born, O unprecedented one" (*yaj jāyathā apūrvye*) is the Rathantara; the Vāmadevya is on its own [verses]. "Him, the wondrous subduer of enemies" (*taṃ vo dasma ṛtīṣaham*) is the Abhīvarta; the Kāleya is on its own [verses]. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.
The verse beginning with "yad jāyathā" is an Anuṣṭubh. || 4 ||

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*; "ā pavasva devayuḥ," "pavate haryato hariḥ"—these are for the *saphasujñāna*, or the *kāśīta*. "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ"—in three verses, this is the *gaurīvita*; or alternatively, the *gaurīvita* in one verse, the *gautama* in one verse, and the *audala* in one verse. In three verses, there is the *svara* with the *payonidhana*. "abhipriyāṇi"—this is the *aiḍa-kāva*, the last; it is *svāra* if one should so choose. || 5 ||

[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna. Regarding the two single-verse hymns (*ekarca*) in the *sapha* [section], the *kāśīta* may optionally take the place of the *sujñāna*. "That which has *payas* as its *nidhana*" means that which has "prāsuprāsu" as its *nidhana*. "If one should vary the *svāra*": if one should vary the place of the *gaurīvita* with the three-verse *sāman*—namely, the *gautama* and *audala*—in various ways during the *svarasāman* days of the *gavāmayana*.

Then one should arrange the *svāra* [sāman] with the *sāmans*; the *kāva* [sāman] for the last [verse] of the *ārbhava* [prasthāna], but not the *aiḍa*. This is the meaning. For when the *gaurīvita* is performed on a triplet of verses (*tṛca*), it was feared that the *ārbhava* might thus become devoid of the *iḍā*; therefore, the *kāva* was arranged for the sake of favoring the *iḍā*, according to the logic to be stated later. However, the intention is that by Gautama’s rule alone, the favoring of the *iḍā* is already established in the case of a *sāman* on a triplet of verses. || 5 ||
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.

The *auśana*, *aupagava*, the beloved of Vasiṣṭha, and the *tairaścya*—these are the *ukthas*. If there is an *ukthya* [sacrifice], it is indeed an *agniṣṭoma*. (7) For those performing the twenty-one-day rite (*ekaviṃśatyaha*), the *svarasāman* days are *ukthya*s. Thus says the *Nidāna*: "Now, these *svarasāman*s—those performing the nine-day rite should perform them as *agniṣṭoma*s; those performing the twenty-one-day rite [should perform them] as *ukthya*s. And the *Sūtra* states: "Those performing the twenty-one-day rite proceed to the *pṛṣṭhya* [period] after the *abhijit*."

"And before the Viśvajit, there are the Ukthyas with the Svarasāmans. The meaning is that for us, it is indeed the Agniṣṭoma because it is performed over nine days. According to the scriptural statement, "They are seventeen," the seventeen-fold (saptadaśa) stomas must be performed for the three Svarasāman days. || 7 ||
Thus ends the first Svarasāman. ||2||
The second [stotra] consists of the Svarasāmans; he recites the second Svarasāman:
"Flow on as the leader of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. O Soma, you are a bull, you are brilliant. Your vital powers rise up, O Sage, as you purify yourself. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"Agni we choose as messenger"—with these [verses], the ājya offerings are performed. || 2 ||
One should extract the third verse from the four-verse hymn beginning with "indram id gāthinaḥ," because of the statement: "The third [verse] is for the Sarvasvāra and Svarasāman."

"Flow as a bull for the sake of the *dhārā*," [is] the *gāyatram* and the *yauktāśvam*, which belong to the *pṛṣṭhya*. "Pour out the pressed juice on every side," [is] the *samantam* and the *dairghaśravasam*, belonging to Ayāsya. "The red bull," [is] the final *pārtham*. 3.

[Thus is the Mādhyandina Pavamāna. Regarding the phrase "that which is on the Pṛṣṭhya": this means that which was stated for the six-day period (ṣaḍaha) beginning with the Pṛṣṭhya, namely, "auho-hoi vṛṣa" for the Yauktāśva. Although one should have said "that which is previous," the use of the word "Pṛṣṭhya" is for the purpose of making known that the Svarasāmans have the Pṛṣṭhya as their archetype (prakṛti). [The chant is] all around on the first [day]; it has three Nidhanas on the Adhyāsyā. || 3 ||

*Matsyapāyi te mahaḥ bṛhat* [is the *pṛṣṭha-stotra*] for its own [verses]; *vāmadevyam*. *Abhi pra vaḥ surādhasam gavāmayanaṃ svarasāmāḥ* is the *abhīvarta*; [it is performed] for its own [verses]; *kāleyam*. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].
The first [verse] is a *bṛhatī* of the *matsyapāyī* type; the two following are *anuṣṭubh*s.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *hāviṣmat*. "pavasvendramaccha"—this is the *śaṅkusujñāna*. "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"—the *gaurīvita* is performed on three verses; or alternatively, the *gaurīvita* on one, the *krauñca* on one, and the *āsita* on one. The *svāra* is performed on three verses, using the former of the two *bṛhannidhana*s; the latter is used for the *āvṛtta* verses. "vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate"—this is the *aiḍa-yāma*, which is the final [stotra]; it is the *svāra* if one should so choose. 5.

[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna. Regarding the *śaṅkusujñāna* [chanting], there are two single-verse sections (*ekarcas*). As for "the former of the two *bṛhannidhana*s," this refers to the two *bṛhannidhana*s characterized by the *nidhanas* "has payā" and "has iḍā payā"; "the former" of these two means the one beginning with "ehā vayaṃ pūṣā. Regarding "the latter in the *āvṛtta*s": in the *svarasāman*s that are *āvṛtta*, it is the latter of the two *bṛhannidhana*s; this means the one beginning with "ehāu auho ayaṃ pūṣā. In the view that the *sāman*s consist of triplets (*tṛca*), the final [sāman] of the Ārbhava is a *svāra-yāma*.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The Sākamaśva, Saubhara, and Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra are the Ukthas; however, if it is an Agniṣṭoma, it is indeed [performed] with the Ukthya [stotras].
