"Towards the Lord of Cattle with song"—this is the *ājya* chant of the *Abhijit* sacrifice, provided it is an *Atirātra*.

By the word "brahman," the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is understood, because it is he who must recite that [hymn]. His connection is with the third *ājya* chant. The underlying reason for this is: "The two *atirātra* sacrifices of the Abhijit take place; he draws out the *ājya* for the Brahman priest, lest they should perform the *ārṣabha-stotrīya*. || 1 ||
In the world of the Sāman-triple-verse, [the hymn] of Śyāvāśva.

Thus: "The Gaurīvita on one verse; the Madhucchnidhana on one verse; the Śyāvāśva on one verse. This means that in place of that triplet (*tṛca*) which is constructed by means of Sāmans performed on single verses (*ekarca*) in sequence across three *stotrīyā* verses, the Śyāvāśva is to be used. And here, since the term "if it is an Atirātra" (*yadyatirātra*) is supplied [from the context], the Śyāvāśva applies to both the Agniṣṭoma and the Atirātra; for the Gaurīvita is employed specifically in the *satra* sacrifices. || 2 ||
The most exhilarating [Sāman] belonging to Hāri-varṇa, the Nārmedha. || 3 ||
[Thus end the Ukthas.
"For him who desires to drink" is the Nānada, the *ṣoḍaśin* chant; the night is the *saṃdhi*. (4) The rest is the same as in the *sāṃvatsarika* [rite]. (5)
The *uktha* and other chants should be the *sāman* pertaining to the *atirātra* sacrifice.

In that regard, this is the arrangement for the Agniṣṭoma: "Flow on as the leader of speech; being purified, he has stepped forth" and "Of you, O sage, who are purifying," [are the verses] for the Bahiṣpavamāna.

"We choose Agni as the messenger," "Come to us, O Mitra and Varuṇa," "Toward you, O bull, [we call] with the pressed [juice]," "O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed [juice]"—these are the *ājya* verses.

"Uccā te jātamandhasaḥ" consists of the Gāyatra, the Āmahīyava, and the Satrāsāhīya; "Punānaḥ soma" consists of the Abhīvarta, the Raurava, and the Yaudhājaya; and "Abhi vāyum" consists of the Pārtha and the Māntya.
The Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita, and the Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha stotras.

"svādiṣṭhayā" is for the Gāyatra-saṃhitā; "pavasvendram accha" is for the Saphasujñāna; "purojitī" is for Śyāvāśva and Dhīgava; and the Yajñāyajñīya and Bṛhat are for Agni, with the Kāva hymn as the final one.

In the *ṛc*s of the *yajñāyajñīya*, the *rathantara* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. In the *atirātra* variant, "abhi pra gopatim gira" is the third *ājya-stotra*. The *uktha-stotras* consist of the *pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *nārmedha*. "pratyasmai pipīṣate" is the *nānada*, the *ṣoḍaśin-sāman*. Its metre is the *anuṣṭubh*. The ritual rules for the *ṣoḍaśin* have been stated [in the text] beginning with "one who is about to chant the *ṣoḍaśin-sāman," etc. Then follows the *atirātra* and the *saṃdhi*. For that which possesses all the *stomas*, the *stomas* are repeated and there are four *praṇayas*.

Such is the arrangement of the *stomas* for the *agniṣṭoma*: the *ukthas* are twenty-onefold, together with the *ṣoḍaśin*; the night [session] is fifteenfold, and the *saṃdhi* is threefold; such is the arrangement for the *atirātra*.
Thus ends [the section on] Abhijit. 4.
The Viśvajit [sacrifice] states the ritual arrangement of the Viśvajit. || 1 ||
"Flow on toward Indra," [is the verse] for the Satrāsāhīya; "for the one who hears" (śrudhya) and "for the one who hears with success" (saphaśrudhya), if it is an Atirātra.
The Āndhīgava belongs to the world of the Sāman-triple-verse; it is the Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra sacrifice accompanied by the Ṣoḍaśin cup. || 3 ||

"The rest is the same as in the *sāṃvatsarika* [rite]. Thus it is said. "Flow for Indra" (*pavasvendramaccha*) is the *satrāsāhīya*; "for the one who hears" (*śrudhye*) is a restatement of what is already established. Regarding "for Sapha, for the one who hears" (*saphaśrudhye*), if there is an *atirātra*, this is the intended distinction; herein lies the *nidāna*: "If there is an *atirātra* for Sapha, for the one who hears," then that [rite] becomes complete; it becomes whole (*saphībhavati*). Therefore, regarding those two which become whole, or intending to cause the *sapha* to fall away—therein, this is the arrangement (*klṛpti*) for the *agniṣṭoma*.

"May they bring thee near," "And among our dear and not-dear [things]," "That of Savitṛ is to be chosen," "The sounding of the Soma-juices," "O Agni, thou purifiest our lives," and "Of thee, O Sage, the Pavamāna"—these are the *bahiṣpavamāna* verses. With the exception of the last one, they consist of single verses (*ekarcas*). The distinction of deities has been stated.
Well-kindled, may he be able for us; they yoke the ruddy steed—worship him who is for the flame; these are the offerings of clarified butter.

For this [sāman], there are the Gāyatra and the Āmahīyava set to "asya pratna" (1.8.1). For the Kāleya, the verse "parīto ṣiñcatā suta" (1.2.4) is used for the first [verse]. The Rathantara is used for the three verses of Dairghaśravasa. The Yaudhājaya is used for the middle verse. The final Pārtha is used for the verse "ayaṃ soma" (1.3.1).
The Vairāja, the Mahānāmnyaḥ, the Vairūpa, and the Revatyaḥ are the Pṛṣṭha [stotras]. The duties pertaining to the Pṛṣṭhas have been stated.

"parisvāno giriṣṭhāḥ" is the Gāyatra-saṃhitā; "pavasvendram accha" is the Satrāsāhīya-śrudhya; "pary ū ṣu" is the Vāmadevya; "purojitī" is both the Āndhīgava and the Yajñāyajñīya; and "pari pradhanva" is the Vāravantīya among the Dvipadās. The final [laud] is the Kāva among those containing the word "sūrya."

"O Agni, you of sacrifices..."—this is the *Bṛhat* as the *Agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *Sākamaśva*, *Saubhara*, and *Nārmedha* are the *uktha* chants. The night-chant is the *saṃdhi*. The *uktha* chants are based on the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*) stoma, along with the *ṣoḍaśin* cup. The night-chant is fifteen-fold (*pañcadaśī*). The *saṃdhi* is three-fold (*trivṛt*). Everything else is like the *agniṣṭoma*. There are two alternative views: one may sacrifice with the *Viśvajit* and *Abhijit*, or with the two *Yama* sacrifices. Thus it is said: "The sacrificer [should sacrifice] with the *Viśvajit* and *Abhijit*, or with the two *Yamas," and so forth. (3)
Thus ends the Viśvajit sacrifice. || 5 ||
Now follows the ritual arrangement of the Mahāvrata, which is also known by the name Sarvajit and is described in the Anuvāka as a Pañcaviṃśa Agniṣṭoma.
Of the vow. || 1 ||
"May [the gods] accept our offering among all [peoples]"—this is the Śyaita Brahman-sāman; it belongs to Audala in the place of Gaurīvita.
The rest is the same as in the twelve-year sacrificial session.

Thus, the Mahāvrata is arranged by means of the final section of the second chapter of the *Saṃvatsara*. Having removed the five-chanted (*pañcanidhana*) Vāmadevya from that one-day rite (*ekāhika*), the Śyaita—namely "ā no viśvāsu havya" (RV 7.27.1)—should be made the Brahman-sāman in its place. Regarding this, the *Nidāna* states: "From the one-day vow (*vrata*), he removes the five-chanted Vāmadevya," and so forth. In the place of the Gaurīvita, there is the Audala of that same [verse], "purojitī" (RV 8.69.1). Everything else is the same.

The *pṛṣṭha*-dharmas taught in the two preceding chapters, beginning with "When the *pṛṣṭhya* of the Mahāvrata has been introduced," must also be performed here. This is because of the statement: "In all cases, the *pṛṣṭhya* should be accompanied by its dharmas, except in the tenth vow. Thus ends the Mahāvrata. 6.

The first [section] consists of one thousand [verses], and then there are four sections of a thousand each belonging to the *Nikāyas*. Of these, the first is stated in the section beginning with "Now this light" (*atha eṣa jyotiḥ*). He now describes its ritual arrangement (*klṛpti*).
Flow on as the leader of speech, with a flashing luster; O Sage, this is for you, the purifying one. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, come for the feast"—this is the Rathantara; there are three Bārhata [stotras].
Thus end the offerings of clarified butter.
"O Agni, come for the feast; we invoke Mitra; we invoke Indra with a lofty song"—these are the *ājya* verses beginning with "In Indra and Agni. (2)

For this [laud], there are the Gāyatra and the Āmahīyava, beginning with "His ancient splendor" (*asya pratnāmanudyutam*); and the Samanta, the Rathantara, the Dairghaśravasa, and the Yaudhājaya, beginning with "Pour out the pressed juice" (*parīto ṣiñcatā sutam*); and the Pārtha at the end, beginning with "This Soma" (*ayaṃ soma*). || 3 ||
Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.

The *samanta* [stotra] is in the first [turn]; the *yaudhājaya* is in the middle [turn]. For the *rathantara*, the *kakubh* is the subsequent [verse], and the metre is the *bṛhatī*. The *bṛhat* and the *vāmadevya* are [the stotras for the verses] beginning with "svādoritthā viṣūvataḥ"; the *śyaita* is [the stotra for the verses] beginning with "svāsu. The *kāleya* is [the stotra] for its own [verses].

Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras]. The *śyaita* has the *paṅkti* metre. (4) "With the sweetest, with the most intoxicating" (*svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā*) is the *gāyatra-saṃhitā*. "Flow on toward Indra" (*pavasvendram accha*) is the *sapha-śrudhya*. "For you, with the first conquest of the soma-juice" (*purojitī vo andhasaḥ*) is the *śyāvāśva-andhīgava*. The final [laud] is the *kāva*, consisting of verses containing the word "Sūrya. (5)
Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. || 6 ||

He states the arrangement of the *stomas*: the *bahiṣpavamāna* is *trivṛt*; the *ājya* stotras are *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa*; the midday *pavamāna* and the *pṛṣṭha* of the Hotṛ are *saptadaśa*; that of the Maitrāvaruṇa is *pañcadaśa*; that of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is *pañcaviṃśa*; that of the Acchāvāka is *saptadaśa*; the *ārbhava* is *ekaviṃśa*; and the *agniṣṭoma* is *ekaviṃśa*. || 7 ||

The first *ājya* is fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*), the second is ninefold (*trivṛt*), the third is fifteenfold, and the fourth is ninefold. Thus, the application of the fifteenfold and ninefold stomas in the *ājya* chants is by alternation. And so it is stated in the *Upagrantha*: "For here they recite 'the ninefold and the fifteenfold' [regarding] the *Bṛhat* and *Rathantara*, and the six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*) of the *Pṛṣṭhya*"; thus, in that case, there is indeed an alternating application. The rest is clear. The *viṣṭuti* (recitation method) of the fifteenfold stoma is now described.

Regarding those *stomas* for which the *viṣṭuti* is prescribed in the *Brāhmaṇa*, two methods of combination are stated in the *Sūtra*: "combination by class" (*jātisaṃhāra*) and "combination of even and odd" (*yugmāyuksaṃhāra*), as described in the passage beginning with "tasya yāvabhitaḥ. Among these, in the case of combination by class, the first *paryāya* is to be drawn from the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*); two equal [sets] are taken from the twenty-seven-fold (*triṇava*). Because the twenty-one-fold is the smallest of them, it should be placed in the middle. The first and last *paryāyas* belong to the twenty-seven-fold. For example: "He utters *hiṃ* nine times."

He [performs] with three, he with five, he with one; he utters *hiṃ* for seven: he with one, he with three, he with three. He utters *hiṃ* for nine: he with five, he with one, he with three. Thus. However, in the case of the combination of even and odd [stomas], two rounds (*paryāya*) from the twenty-four-fold [stoma] are to be brought forward. One [is taken] from the twenty-seven-fold [stoma]; and because of their single excellence (*ekajyāyastva*), it should be placed in the middle of the twenty-seven-fold. The first and last rounds belong to the twenty-four-fold. It is as follows:

He utters the *hiṃ* with eight [verses]: three times, four times, and once. He utters the *hiṃ* with nine [verses]: once, three times, and five times. He utters the *hiṃ* with eight [verses]: four times, once, and three times. Regarding this, it has been said: "In the thirteenth, the twenty-third, and the twenty-fifth [stomas], one middle turn is greater; in the greater ones, one is smaller; likewise in the smaller ones, as in the twenty-nine and thirty-one. (7)
Thus ends the first thousand [verses]. ||7||
The second thousand-fold [sacrifice]:
now, by means of the section beginning with "This is all-light" (sarvajyotis), the second thousand-fold is described;
this is the ritual arrangement for the subsequent one as well.

Its *bahiṣpavamāna* stotra is the *trivṛt*; the *ājya* stotras are fifteenfold; the midday *pavamāna* is seventeenfold; there are three *pṛṣṭha* stotras; the *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin*’s stotra is twenty-fivefold; the *ārbhava* is seventeenfold; and the *agniṣṭoma* is twenty-onefold. || 2 ||
Thus, there is a distinction only regarding the arrangement of the hymns (stoma); the rest is as before. || 2 ||
Thus ends the second thousand. ॥८॥
The third thousandfold [offering]:
he arranges the third thousandfold [offering] prescribed by the Anuvāka beginning with "Now this Viśvajyotis.
The Ājya offerings for both [the morning and midday pressings] consist of the verses beginning with "We choose Agni as the messenger."

The Śrāyantīya is the Brahman-sāman. "yaste mado vareṇya" is the Gāyatra [sāman] on the Auksa verses. The Ātharvaṇa follows the Āndhīgava. The Sākamaśva, Saubhara, Traikakubha, and Udvamśīya are the Uktha-sāmans. || 2 ||
The twenty-four-fold Ārbhava-pavamāna and the twenty-one-fold Agniṣṭoma are accompanied by Ukthya-stotras. The rest is the same as the previous [rite], with the same Stomas.

The meaning of the phrase "both *ājyā* [chants]" has been stated by the author of the *Nidāna*: "The former are in the *bārhata* [meter], the latter in the *rāthaṃtara*," says Śaucivṛkṣi; "Those addressed to a single deity are in the *bārhata*, those addressed to two deities are in the *rāthaṃtara*," says Dhānaṃjayya. By the word "former" is meant the second [set] consisting of the *sāman*s. In that regard, this is its arrangement:
the *bahispavamāna* is the threefold (*trivṛt*), beginning with "Flow on, O foremost of speech, with flashing luster" and "Of thee, O sage, who art being purified."

The Ājya offerings are: "Agni, the messenger... (RV 1.12.1), "We have come to Agni... (RV 8.39.1), "O Indra and Agni, come hither... (RV 7.93.1), "Agni, the messenger... (RV 8.44.1), "To us, O Mitra and Varuṇa... (RV 1.151.1), and "Indra, the singer... (RV 8.3.1) and "O Indra and Agni... (RV 7.93.1)—these are the fifteen Ājya hymns. Alternatively, the Ājya offerings consist of these fifteen verses.

For this [stotra], "Asya pratnā dyutir" is in the Gāyatrī and Mahīyu verses; "Parīto ṣiñca samantam" is in the first [verse]; the Rathantara is in three [verses]; the Dairghaśravasa is in three [verses]; the Yaudhājaya is in the Adhyāsya verse; and "Ayaṃ soma pārtham" is the final [verse]. Thus is the seventeen-versed Mādhyandina Pavamāna.

The *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śrāyantīya*, and the *kāleya* are the *pṛṣṭha* stotras. These three *pṛṣṭhas* are based on the seventeen-versed chant (*saptadaśa*). The *brahmasāman* is the twenty-five-versed chant (*pañcaviṃśa*).

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the Gāyatra for Auṣija; "pavasvendramaccha"—this is the Sapha for Śrudhi; "purojitī" is the Śyāvāśva, the Āndhīgava, and the Ātharvaṇa; and the "sūryavatīṣu" verses are the Kāva—this is the Caturviṃśa Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The Sākamaśva, Saubhara, Traikakubha, and Udvamśīya are the twenty-one-fold *uktha* hymns; the meter of the Traikakubha is the *uṣṇih*.
Thus ends the third thousand. ९॥
The fourth [section] consists of a thousand verses; he recites the best of the thousand-verse sections as stated in the *anuvāka* beginning with "yo vā agniṣṭome":
"Sing forth, O men, unto him; sing unto the one born, the swift one. Flow on, the foremost of speech, with a flashing luster—of you, O Sage, the purifying one. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

The two triplets beginning with "vidyutatyāpavamānasya" and "te kava" [are used]; the remaining verses are single-verse units (ekarcas), because of the scriptural injunction: "The last two triplets are used in the Bahiṣpavamāna at the Sāhasra and the final Cāturmāsya sacrifices. (1)
"O Agni, come for the feast; even from afar, indeed, [the gods] are here. To Indra the singers sing aloud; to Indra and Agni, a great homage. These are the *ājya* verses.

"uccā ta" is the Gāyatra and the Cāmahīyava; "pavasva madhumattama" is the *saṃkṣāra* of the *iḍās*, performed on a single verse; "pratnaṃ pīyūṣaṃ pūrvyaṃ yad ukthyam" is the Yaudhājaya, performed on three verses; "punānaḥ soma dhārayā" is the Raurava, performed on a single verse; the Rathantara is performed on three verses; and "śiśuṃ jajñānaṃ haryatam" is the Vāmadevya, which is the final one. || 3 ||
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The *uṣṇih* belongs to the *iḍānāṃ saṃkṣāra*; the *sato bṛhatī* belongs to the *yaudhājaya*; and for the *rathantara*, the subsequent *kakub* is the *bṛhatī*. 3.
The Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha [is performed] on the verses of the Vāmadevya [Sāman], the Svāra [is performed] on the Suparṇa [verses], as are the Śrāyantīya and the Kāleya. || 4 ||
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" and "gāyatrasaṃhite"; "pari pra dhanvendramaccha" for Saphaśrudhya; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" for Śyāvāśva and Andhīgava; and the final [laud] for Kava consists of verses containing the word "sūrya."
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
"Pari pra dhanva" is a two-footed verse; there are single-verse hymns for Sapha and Śr̥dhi. 5.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.

Now, the *stoma* is the threefold (*trivṛt*) for the *bahiṣpavamāna*; the three *ājya* chants are fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*). The *maitrāvaruṇa*’s chant is threefold; the midday *pavamāna* and the *hotṛ*’s *pṛṣṭha* are seventeenfold (*saptadaśa*). The *maitrāvaruṇa*’s chant is fifteenfold; the *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin*’s is twenty-fivefold (*pañcaviṃśa*); the *acchāvāka*’s is seventeenfold. The *ārbhava* is seventeenfold; the *agniṣṭoma* is twenty-onefold (*ekaviṃśa*). Thus ends the fourth thousand-fold [section]. 10.

The first is the *sādyaskra*; then there are four *sādyaskras*. Śaucivṛkṣi says that together with the *śyena* and the two *ekatrikas*, there are six *sādyaskras*. From the initiation (*dīkṣā*) onwards, they should perform everything on the same day. In the case of the first, second, and *śyena* sacrifices among the *sādyaskras*, the *agnīṣomīya-iṣṭi* is prescribed in place of the animal sacrifice to Agni-Soma. In that rite, there is an omission of the *subrahmaṇyā* call at the time of the offering of the omentum (*vapā*). Regarding this, the first *sādyaskra* is prescribed by the section beginning with "The Ādityas and the Aṅgirases. He states its ritual arrangement (*klṛpti*):
Sing forth to him, O men; Pavamāna has brought [the prize] forth. Of you, O Sage, who are Pavamāna—
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
We invoke you as our friend among these people; for I alone have inherited this beautiful thought from my father. 2.
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.

"uccā te jātam andhasaḥ"—this *gāyatram* is on one verse; the *āmahīyavam* on one verse; the *śākvaravarṇam* on one verse; "punānaḥ soma dhārayā"—this *vaiṣṭambham* is on one verse; the *kāleyam* on one verse; the *yaudhājayam* on one verse; and the *auśanam* is the final one. 3.
[Thus concludes the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The Rathantara and the Vāmadevya [are used] in the verses of the Śrāyantīya; the Saubhara in the verses of the Kāleya; and the Vāravantīya [is used] in the verses of the Kāleya.
Thus end the Pṛṣṭhas.

With the verses "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" and "gāyatraṃ ca," the *arka* is with *svāśira*. With "pavasvendram accha," it is for Saphakāyasya. With "purojitī vo andhasaḥ," it is the *śyāvāśva-andhīgava*. The last [laud] is the *kāva*. 5.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.

With the exception of the Kāva verses, all [the others] consist of single verses (*ekarca*). This is because of the rule stating that "in every case, when the *stoma* is possible, the last [verse] occurs in a triplet (*tṛca*).
|| 5 || The *Yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. || 6 ||

All the hymns are *trivṛt* (nine-versed), because it will be stated later that "both are *trivṛt*. Regarding the duties of the *adhvaryu* priest and so forth mentioned in the sūtra beginning with "by means of the *sādyaskra*," none of that has been stated here.
Thus ends the first *sādyaskra*.
Now follows the second *sādyaskra*.
The second Sādyaskra sacrifice has been described by means of this very section beginning with "etasyaivaikaviṃśam. This same procedure applies to the subsequent one as well.
Thus; the meaning is that the determination of the first is exactly the same as that of the second. || 1 ||
He states the distinction:
for that very [sacrifice], the twenty-first [stotra] is the Agniṣṭomasāman. || 2 ||
He states the arrangement of the *stomas* for the first and second [days]: "Both with the *trivṛt*. 3.3.3.
Thus ends the second *sādyaskra*. || 12 ||

The third is the Sādyaskra; and this, called the Anukrī of the Aṅgirases, is the third. The Sūtra states: "The Anukrī is a one-night [rite] and a two-day [rite]. The meaning is that it is accomplished with one night and two days. He now describes its ritual arrangement.
Before the Śākvara syllable is the *svāra* [intonation] of the Suparṇa; in the world of Āyāsya is the Pauṣkala. Before the Śyāvāśva is the Āyāsya of the Eḍa. || 1 ||
The two subsequent Pavamāna lauds consist of twenty-four verses each and are arranged in triplets.
The rest is the same as before, with the same *stoma*. || 3 ||

"Upāsmai pavamāno ajījanat," "Pavamānasya te kava," [and] "Imam ū ṣu tvam asmākam"—these are the *bahiṣpavamāna* stotras of the threefold (*trivṛt*) form. "Mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe," "Aham iddhi pituḥ pari," and "Iyaṃ vāmasya manmanaḥ"—these are the *ājya* stotras of the threefold form. "Uccā te jātam andhasaḥ"—this includes the *gāyatra*, the *cāmahīyava*, the *svāra*, the *sauparṇa*, and the *śākvaravarṇa*. "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā"—this includes the *sauveṣṭambha*, the *kāleya*, the *yaudhājaya*, and the *auśanasantya*.

Thus ends the twenty-fourth [day] of the Mādhyandina [pressing]. All [the stotras] consist of triplets (tṛca). The Pṛṣṭha-stotras are the Trivṛt: the Rathantara and the Vāmadevya in the verses of the Śrāyantīya; the Saubhara in the verses of the Kāleya; and the Vāravantīya.

With the verse *svādiṣṭhayā*, the Gāyatra [stotra] is performed; with *svāśiraḥ* and *arkaḥ*, the Pavamāna; with *pavasva indram accha* and *sapha pauṣkala*, the Āyāsya; with *purojitī vaḥ* and *aiḍa*, the Śyāvāśva; with *andhīgava*, the Kāva; and the last is the Antya. Thus is the Caturviṃśa [Stoma], belonging to the Ārbhava Pavamāna; all [these stotras] consist of triplets (*tṛca*). The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma Sāman, consisting of twenty-one verses. 3.
Thus ends the third Sādyaskra sacrifice. || 13 ||

The fourth is the Sādyaskra, known as the Viśvajit-Śilpa; thus, "this Viśvajit-Śilpa" is the fourth. According to Dhānañjayya, it consists of one night, two nights, or three nights. The first day is the consecration (daikṣa); the second extends from the purchase of the Soma until the end of the Upavasatha; the last is the pressing day (sautya). Its ritual procedure (kalpa) is as follows.

The Rathantara and Dairghaśravasa [stotras] have the Antaraiḍa and Āyāsya [sāmans] on a single verse; the Jarābodhīya follows from the Saṃhitā. The rest is the same as the Viśvajit one-day Agniṣṭoma. || 1 ||
The two subsequent Pavamāna lauds consist of eighteen verses each. The Hotṛ’s Pṛṣṭha stotra consists of twenty-one verses. The Agniṣṭoma consists of twenty-one verses. Everything else is Trivṛt.

Thus: by the term "performed in a single day" (*aikāhika*), there is an exclusion of the annual sacrifice (*sāṃvatsarika*); by the term "Agniṣṭoma," there is an exclusion of the three-night sacrifice (*tirātra*).

The Bahiṣpavamāna stotra, beginning with *upa tvā jāmayo...* and ending with *pavamānasya te kave*, consists of three triplets (*trivṛt*). The Ājya stotras, beginning with *suṣamidde* and ending with *tam īḍiṣva*, likewise consist of three triplets each.

For this [laud], one should chant the *pratna* (ancient) *anudrut*, the *gāyatram*, and the *āmahīyavam*; the *kāleya* with the verse "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam" at the first [verse]; the *rathantaram* over three verses; the *aiḍamāyāsyam* at the first [verse]; the *dairghaśravasam* over three verses; the *yaudhājayam* at the middle *āsya*; and the final *pārtha* with the verse "ayaṃ somaḥ. Thus ends the eighteenth [section] of the midday pressing.

The Vairāja is the Pṛṣṭha-stotra of the Hotṛ, consisting of the twenty-one-fold [stoma]. The Mahānāmnīs, the Vairūpa, and the Revatīs are the subsequent Pṛṣṭha-stotras, consisting of the nine-fold [stoma].

"Pari svāno giriṣṭhā" is the Gāyatra, the Saṃhitā, and the Jarābodhīya; "pavasvendramaccha" is the Satrāsāhīya and the Śrudhya; "paryū ṣu" is the Vāmadevya; "purojitī va" is the Āndhīgava and the Yajñāyajñīya; "pari pra dhanva" is the Vāravantīya among the two-footed verses; and the Kāva is the Mantya among those verses containing the word "sūrya. Thus ends the eighteenth [section], the Ārbhava. The Vāmadevya, Yajñāyajñīya, Vāravantīya, and Kāva are to be performed on triplets (tṛca); the remaining [Sāmans] are to be performed on single verses (ekarca).

For it is stated: "The Vāmadevya [is chanted] on a triplet; the Viśvajit, the Śilpa, and the three beginning with the Yajñāyajñīya [are likewise]. Among these, the Gāyatra, Saṃhita, and Jarābodhīya are Sāman triplets, according to the statement: "Three [Sāmans] on a single triplet, on various stotriya verses."

The Bṛhat Agniṣṭomasāman with the Ekaviṃśa stoma is [performed] with the verse "tvam agne yajñānām. The deities of the meters have already been stated in the context of the Viśvajit sacrifice. And the ritual rules for the Pṛṣṭha-stotras apply to the Pṛṣṭha-lauds.
Thus ends the fourth Sādyaskra sacrifice. || 14 ||
The Śyena sacrifice is mentioned in the *Ṣaḍviṃśa Brāhmaṇa* with the words, "Now this Śyena—one practicing sorcery should sacrifice with it. Regarding its ritual arrangement (*klṛpti*), he says:
"Of the purifying [Soma] who strikes down... the purifying one has stepped forth... and "O Sage, of thee, the purifying one... These are the verses for the *bahiṣpavamāna*.
May Agni strike down the Vṛtras; I invoke Mitra of pure strength. May Soma gladden you; I invoke those two of whom this world is born. 2.
Thus end the offerings of clarified butter.

"Flow on, O Soma, most exhilarating"—this *gāyatra* [sāman] is on one verse; the *vārṣāhara* on one verse; the *śākvaravarṇa* on one verse; "Being purified, O Soma, in thy stream"—this *vaṣaṭkāranidhana* [sāman] is on one verse; the *raurava* on one verse; the *yaudhājaya* on one verse; and the *auśana* as the final [sāman]. || 3 ||
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The two Sāman triplets consist of Gāyatrī and Bṛhatī verses. 3.
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Bṛhat, and the Kāleya. || 4 ||
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

The Rathantara and Bṛhat [sāmans] are to be performed in the successive [verses]. Thus we have studied regarding the one-day sacrifices (ekāha). And there is a scriptural statement (śruti) on this point: "The Rathantara occurs in the successive [verses]."
"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" is for the Gāyatravārṣāhara; "pavasvendramaccha" is for the Saphaupagava; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is for the Nānadāndhīgava; the last [verse] is for the Kāva. || 5 ||
[Thus ends] the Ārbhava Pavamāna;
these are the verses of Kakṣīvān, with the exception of those by Kavi.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the *aniṣṭoma* chant.

He states the arrangement of the *stoma*: "The *pavamāna* chants are threefold, as is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*; the *ājya* and *pṛṣṭha* chants are performed with three [verses] each. (7) Thus: "He utters *hiṃ* for one verse; he does so with the first. He utters *hiṃ* for one verse; he does so with the first. He utters *hiṃ* for one verse; he does so with the first"—this is the *viṣṭuti* of the threefold *stoma*. Or: "He utters *hiṃ* for one verse; he does so with the first. He utters *hiṃ* for one verse; he does so with the middle one. He utters *hiṃ* for one verse; he does so with the last one."

Regarding this, it has been stated: "Śāṇḍilya says that there is a *hiṃkāra* before the three [verses] when they are in the *ekinī* position; and in the *trika*, the completion of the *stoma* is by means of the first [verse]. Dhānaṃjayya says it is by means of a *ṛc*; and there is a *hiṃkāra* once in the *ekinī*. Because of the absence of the *viṣṭāva*, the *kuśā* (grass) is prescribed in place of the portion belonging to the *ṛc*. There is one round (*paryāya*). He utters the *hiṃkāra* for one [verse]; he utters the *hiṃkāra* for three with the middle [verse]; he utters the *hiṃkāra* for five with the last [verse]: such is the *viṣṭuti* of the *trivṛt*.

There is an exchange of arrows with two [other] arrows; of these two, the former belongs to the Śyena because of the statement, "the Agniṣṭoma-sāmans of the Śyena. The sons of Vratīnas and Yaudhas who are learned in the Vedas (*anūcāna*) act as the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) in the rite of malevolent magic (*abhicāra*). According to Dhānaṃjayya, they must be the sons of those who are worthy (*arhat*). They proceed wearing red turbans, red garments, and with their sacred threads suspended around the neck (*nivīta*). Holding arrows and having strung their bows, they should cause the cows intended for the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) to produce blood at the time of the distribution of the fees. The method for this—namely, that they should pierce them with sharp thorns—is stated in another Sūtra.
The Śyena, Iṣu, Vajra, and Saṃdaṃśa [stomas], which serve the purpose of malevolent magic (abhicāra),
have been extracted together with their respective hymns of praise from the Pañcaviṃśa [Stoma].
Those [mantras] studied in the *Ṣaḍviṃśabrāhmaṇa* are understood by men here;
their arrangement according to the rules occurs in those respective sections within the ritual manual (*kalpa*). (7)
Thus ends the Śyena [Sāman]. ||15||
The Ekatrika sacrifice:

this Ekatrika has been described by the Anuvāka beginning with "atha eṣa ekatrikaḥ. Regarding the Ekatrika, they should perform everything on a single day. Gautama says it should have one initiation (dīkṣā) and three Upasad days. He states its arrangement:
the Bahiṣpavamāna chant is performed with the single verse, "upāsmai gāyatā naraḥ. || 1 ||
And that [stotra] should consist of only the *retasyā* verses, because of the statement: "The *bahiṣpavamāna* of the *ekatrika* [sāman] consists of the *retasyā*s."
The *ājya* hymns belong to the *sādyaskra* sacrifices.
"Take this one from among these of ours; for I [have taken] this from my father. These are the *ājya* verses. 2.
"O Indu, for Indra accompanied by the Maruts"—this is the Gāyatra [Sāman]. "Being purified, O Soma, in your stream"—this is the Utsedha. The final [verse] belongs to Auśana. || 3 ||
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
All [the verses] consist of single ṛcs. 3.
The Rathantara and the Vāmadevya; there is a prohibition against [singing] the Śrāyantīya among the ṛks; the Kāleya is [to be sung] in its own verses. || 4 ||
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* stotras.
Now follows the *ārbhava* [stotra]: "With this luster, golden... is the side-chant (*gāyatrapārśva*) in the *gāyatrī* meter.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. 6.
He shows that its *stoma* is indeed established by name:
the *stoma* is the *ekatrika*. || 7 ||
He explains this very point with the verse beginning "ekayātha tisṛbhiḥ" (8).

Thus: the *bahiṣpavamāna* [stotra] consists of one *stotrīyā* verse for the first [turn], three for the second, one for the third, and three for the fourth; this is the meaning of the two *ekatrika* stomas being performed by alternation. For the single-stoma (*ekastoma*) [form], he utters the *hiṃ* call with the first [verse]; that is the *viṣṭuti* (arrangement) of the single-stoma. And that *hiṃ* call is either thrice or only once. The *viṣṭuti* of the triad has been explained. || 8 ||
Thus ends the section on the triad of ones. 16.

First is the Vrātyastoma; then there are four groups of Vrātyastomas. The Vrātyas are those who have been deprived of the purificatory rites beginning with initiation (upanayana). These [sacrifices] are for the purpose of their expiation. Those intending to sacrifice with the Vrātyastomas should, after taking as a wife—without mantras—a woman who has not belonged to another and who is not of the same lineage (gotra), separately establish their sacred fires and procure the implements of sacrifice, and then undergo initiation. According to the opinion of the author of the *Nidāna*, they should do so without having previously performed the Jyotiṣṭoma; according to the author of the Sūtra, they should do so only after having performed it.

That householder who is skilled in studying these [Vedas], who has kinsmen and is wealthy—he is [the one for whom this is prescribed]. They should consume the sacrificial portions following him. With the section beginning "The gods indeed went to the heavenly world," the first Vrātyastoma, known as the Catuṣṣoḍaśin, is described. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is:
the Jyotiṣṭoma with the Bahiṣpavamāna chant. || 1 ||
O Agni, with all the Agnis; O Mitra and Varuna, come hither; O Indra and Agni, sit down here; come to the pressed juice. || 2 ||
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.

"High is the birth of your juice"—this is the Gāyatra and the Cāmahīyava; "Flow on, rich in sweetness"—this is the Kāleya; "In thee, O Soma, the first [priests] who have spread the sacrificial grass"—this is the Yaudhājaya; "Being purified, O Soma, in thy stream"—this is the Raurava and the Auśana as the final [Sāman]. || 3 ||
[Thus ends] the midday Pavamāna.

The *kāleya* consists of a single verse; here at the midday pressing, the *kakubh* consists of a single verse, because of the statement: "In that [verse], except for the last one from the *vrātyastoma*. "Tve soma" is a *sato bṛhatī*.

The *rathantara* and the *vāmadevya*, along with "O Indra, lover of songs, take up the fire" and "Pour the soma-juice for Indra"—these are the *dyautāna* verses in the *māruta* [laud]. Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].
The Kakup is the first, then the Uṣṇih, then the Purauṣṇih, and the Anuṣṭubh—these are the meters. For the Māruta [laud], it is the Uṣṇih. 4.

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" is for the Gāyatra-saṃhitā; "pari pra dhanva nadam va odatīnām" is for the Saphaśrudhya; "pary ū ṣu" is the Marut-saṃstobha; and "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Śyāvāśva, Āndhīgava, and Kava hymns, with the last one being the final.

[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna. "Pari pra dhanva" is an Akṣarapaṅkti; "Nadaṃ vaḥ" is an Uṣṇih; "Pary ū ṣu" is an Anuṣṭubh with a pipīlikā-madhyā (middle-thin) structure. Here, although four single-verse (ekarca) stotras are to be performed, because of the rule stating that from two onwards they follow in immediate succession starting with the Kakubh, when a two-footed verse (*dvipadā*) takes the place of the *kakubh*, one might initially assume the performance of the *sapha* chant. However, since the *saṃstobha* of the Maruts is prescribed for singing in the forest (*araṇya*), it must be performed on a triplet (*tṛca*). And the *gāyatra* chant is performed on a single verse.

"Because there is no reason for skipping the first [verse]," so says one opinion: that the *gāyatra*, *saṃhita*, *sapha*, *śrudhya*, and *aśyāvaśva* [verses] are each single-verse (*ekarca*) hymns. Another opinion holds that because the *gāyatra* is the primary [verse], it should be performed as a triplet (*tṛca*). Furthermore, another view holds that the four beginning with the *sapha* are single-verse hymns in immediate succession. As it has been said: "Dhānañjayya [holds] the *gāyatra* to be a single verse; Śāṇḍilya [holds] the *marutāṃ saṃstobha* to be a triplet, [and] the opposite. (5)
"Devo vo drāvaṇodaḥ" is the *yajñāyajñīya* [chant] for the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. 4.2.6.

Now follows the rule for the *stomas*: the *bahiṣpavamāna* is the *trivṛt*; the three *ājya* [stotras] are the *pañcadaśa*; the *acchāvāka*’s [stotra] is the *ṣoḍaśa*; the midday *pavamāna* is the *ṣoḍaśa*; the three *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] are the *saptadaśa*; the *acchāvāka*’s [stotra] is the *ṣoḍaśa*; the *ārbhava* is the *ṣoḍaśa*; and the *agniṣṭoma* is the *ekaviṃśa*. (7) Thus ends it. Such is the *viṣṭuti* of the *ṣoḍaśa-stoma*: he utters *hiṃ* five times; he [chants] with three [verses], he with one, he with one. He utters *hiṃ* five times; he with one, he with three.
He [sings] with one; he utters *hiṃ* for six [verses]; he [sings] with two; he [sings] with one; he [sings] with three. Or: he utters *hiṃ* for six;

he [sings] with one; he [sings] with two; he [sings] with three. This has been stated by those who follow the *Aśarātrika* [tradition]: "In the longer [stomas], therefore, one should insert [the verses] in the last round (*paryāya*) of the first [stoma]. Regarding these, it is said that they are either *brahmāyatanīyā* or *kṣatrāyatanīyā*; in the performance of the first [round], there are mostly *brahmāyatanīyā* verses, while in the middle [round], there are *kṣatrāyatanīyā* verses. 7.
Thus ends the first Vrātyastoma. || 17 ||

The second [sacrifice] is the Vrātyastoma consisting of sixteen [stotras], or rather, this is the sixteen-fold one; thus he describes the prescribed second Vrātyastoma. For the first *paryāya*, there are three or four verses beginning with "These drops have been poured forth" (*ete asṛgram indavaḥ*) and "O barley, for our sake, for the sake of the soma-juice" (*yavaṃ yavaṃ no andhasaḥ*). These are the hymns of the Āyuṣ. 1.
There are sixteen Pavamāna stotras, the Sāmans for the Acchāvāka, the twenty-one-fold Agniṣṭoma, and two Ukthas.
The rest is the same as before, with the same *stoma*. || 3 ||

Thus: the final triplet of the *bahiṣpavamāna* is the *paryāsa*. "Sing forth to him, O men, with a flashing luster; these drops have been poured out; like barley, [win] for us by means of the soma-juice; O Sage, of you who are being purified"—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. Then, up to the end of the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*, it is as before. The *pramahiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *udvaṃśīya* are the *uktha* chants. The *bahiṣpavamāna* is sixteenfold. The three *ājya* stotras are fifteenfold. The *ṣoḍaśin* belongs to the *acchāvāka*. The *mādhyandina-pavamāna* is sixteenfold.

There are three *pṛṣṭha* chants of seventeen [verses]. The *ṣoḍaśin* belongs to the Acchāvāka. The *ārbhava* is a *ṣoḍaśin*. The *agniṣṭoma* is twenty-one-fold. There are two *uktha* chants. "The *ṣoḍaśin* belongs to the Acchāvāka"—such is the arrangement of the *stomas*.
Thus ends the second Vrātyastoma. || 18 ||

The third is the Vrātyastoma consisting of two sixteen-fold chants; this is called the Vrātyastoma of the Sixteen-fold. For it is said: "For Indra, O Indu, accompanied by the Maruts"—this is the Gāyatra and the Āmahīyava. "Flow on, most honey-sweet"—this is the Kāleya. "O Soma, you first for those who have spread the sacrificial grass"—this is the Dairghaśravasa. "Being purified, O Soma, with your stream"—this is the Raurava and the Yaudhājaya. In the world of Śr̥dhya, there is the *saṃstobha* of the Maruts; from the *saṃstobha* of the Maruts comes the Śyāvāśva. "With the victory of your food"—this is the Āndhīgava. || 1 ||
The two subsequent Pavamāna chants are in the Trivṛt metre.
The rest is the same as the first Vrātyastoma, with the same *stomas*. 3.

Thus: the *bahiṣpavamāna* consists of the *trivṛt* [stoma] with the verses beginning *upa drava*, *vi pājasā*, and *pavasva*. The *ājya* stotras consist of three [verses] each beginning with *agne viśvebhiḥ*, *ā no mitrāvaruṇā*, *ā tvetā niṣīdata*, and *indrāgnī āgatam sutam*; these are of the *pañcadaśa* [stoma]. The final one is of the *ṣoḍaśa* [stoma]. The *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* [sāmans] are for Indra, beginning with *indrāyendo*. The *kāleya* begins with *pavasva madhumattamaḥ*. The *dairghaśravasa* begins with *tve soma*. The *raurava* and *yaudhājaya* are for the one being purified (*punānaḥ*). The *auśana* is the final one for the *svāsu* [verses]. Thus is the *mādhyandina* *trivṛt*. With the exception of the final one, they are single-verse hymns (*ekarcāḥ*).

The *rathantara* and *vāmadevya* [are used] for the *āghāra*; "O Indra, lover of songs" (*endra girvaṇaḥ*) and "to Indra, the drop" (*endum indrāya*) are for the *dyautana* and *māruta*. These are the *pṛṣṭhas*. There are three [sets] of seventeen [verses]; the last is the sixteenfold [stoma]. "Most sweet" (*svādiṣṭhyā*) is accompanied by the *gāyatra*; "around the flowing [Soma]" (*pari pra dhanve*) is the *sapha*; "the roar of you, O Maruts" (*nadaṃ va omarutām*) is the *saṃstobha*; "around us" (*pary ū ṣu*) is the *śyāvāśva*; "with victory in front" (*purojitī*) is the *āndhīgava*; the *kāva* is the final [verse]. Thus the *ārbhava* is the *trivṛt*. With the exception of the final [verse], they consist of single verses. The meters are as in the first [section]. "May the god who bestows wealth upon you" (*devo vo draviṇādāḥ*) is the *yajñāyajñīya*, the *agniṣṭomasāman*. One [verse].
The twentieth [chapter]. 3.
Thus ends the third Vrātyastoma. || 19 ||

The fourth *vrātyastoma* (the *stoma* of the *śaman*, *nicṛt*, and *ameḍhra*). Now follows this *stoma* of the *śaman*, *nicṛt*, and *ameḍhra*. Having thus mentioned the fourth *vrātyastoma*, he says:
the opening hymn (*pratipad*) contains the word "foremost" (*agriya*); this is the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*) of the first [day]. 1.
"Flow on with the flashing word; O Sage, of you who are being purified"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna chant.
"O Agni, with all [the gods], come to us; O Mitra and Varuṇa, come; do you two sit down; O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed [soma]"—these are the *ājya* [verses]. || 1 ||

"High is the birth of your juice"—this is the *gāyatram* and the *cāmahīyavam*. "Flow on, most honey-sweet"—this is the *kāleyam*. "In thee, O Soma, for the first time, for him who has spread the sacrificial grass"—this is the *dairghaśravasam*. "Being purified, O Soma, in thy stream"—this is the *rathantaram*, the *rauravam*, and the *yaudhājayam*. "The bull, the red one"—this is the *pārtham*, the last [of these]. || 2 ||
[Thus ends] the Mādhyandina Pavamāna; all [the verses] consist of triplets (tṛca). || 2 ||
"Bṛhat and Vāmadevya; O Indra, lover of songs, drink the Soma; pour it out for Indra"—this is the *dyautāna* hymn in the *māruta* [śastra]. Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" is the Gāyatra; "jarābodhīya" and "svāśira" are the Ārkas; "pari pra dhanva" and "adaṃ va odatīnām" are the Sapha and Śrudhya; "pary ū ṣu" is the Marutām Saṃstobha; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Śyāvāśva and Āndhīgava; and the final [hymns] are the Atharvaṇa, the Bṛhat, the Āgneya, and the Kāva. || 4 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.]
The *saphaśrudhyā* consists of a single verse (*ekarca*). The remaining [verses] consist of triplets (*tṛca*). The meters have been stated. || 4 ||
"Devo vo draviṇodāḥ" is the Yajñāyajñīya, the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.

Now follows the *Stomakalpa* (the ritual procedure for the *stomas*). There are two *trivṛt* chants; two *pañcadaśa* and *saptadaśa*; two *ekaviṃśa* and *caturviṃśa*; two *catuścatvāriṃśa* and *aṣṭācatvāriṃśa*; two *triṇava* and *trayastrimśa*; and two *dvātrimśa*. Thus [it is said]. Regarding the two *dvātrimśa* chants, Dhānaṃjayya says that one should perform three *viṣṭuti*s (modes of chanting). The application of their arrangement by *paryāya* (turn) is explained by the *catuścatvāriṃśa*, according to the *sūtra*. Among these, the first *viṣṭuti* is as follows: he utters the *hiṃkāra* eleven times.

He utters *hiṃ* with three [verses], with seven, and with one for ten [stomas]. He utters *hiṃ* with one, with three, and with six for eleven [stomas]. He utters *hiṃ* with seven, with one, and with three. The same should be understood for the subsequent [stomas] as well. Regarding these, there are two applications—*samīṣantī* and *stotrasamīṣantī*—just as in the case of the forty-four-fold [stoma]. However, here, for both the thirty-two-fold and the forty-four-fold [stomas], the first *ekaviṣṭuti* (single-verse arrangement) must be performed, but not the *samīṣantī*.
"One should act thus for the one who partakes of the day, elsewhere [one should offer] *pathyā*," according to the scriptural statement. Thus ends the fourth *vrātyastoma*. 20.

The Agniṣṭut is first; then there are four related groups (nikāyins) of Agniṣṭuts. In the section beginning with "Indra indeed [slew] Triśiras," the collective performance of the Agniṣṭuts is described in general terms. The first is stated in the section beginning with "The Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma. The second belongs to this same [rite] when performed with the Revatī verses. The third is for one who has fallen away from a sacrifice, as stated in the passage: "One who has failed in a sacrifice should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma-Agniṣṭut. The fourth is for one desiring food, as stated: "With the Saptadaśa-Agniṣṭut, [one should sacrifice] for the sake of food."

In the Sūtra, however, after presenting two alternative views—that there are either six or five [stotras] for the Agniṣṭut—the position that there are four is established. This is shown by the passage beginning: "The Agniṣṭut has six; the Trivṛt Jyotiṣṭoma has the first two, namely the Svarman and the Vāravantīya," and so forth. In the Agniṣṭuts, regarding the *somāpyayana* mantra, the modification (*ūha*) is: "May the fires swell, O finders of the single wealth; may Agni swell for you; may you, O Agni, swell. In the *subrahmaṇyā*, however, after the threefold utterance of "Subrahmaṇyom," the *āgneya* formula must be recited.

In that regard, the opinion of Gautama is as follows: having said, "Come to the fire, O Rohitābhyas, Bṛhadbhānu, Dhūmaketu, Jātavedas, Vicarṣaṇi, O Aṅgiras, O Brāhmaṇa-Aṅgirasa, you who call yourself so," one should say on the third day before the Soma-pressing, "O fires, O Brahmins, come," and so forth.

According to the opinion of Dhānañjayya, however, one should recite: "O Agni, come! O Rohitāśva, come! Son of Bharadvāja, born of a thousand goats! Leap-over! Lover of the Dawn, descendant of Aṅgiras! You who call yourself a Brahmin of the Aṅgirases! Come to the Soma-pressing on the third day! O Agnis, O Brahmans, come! and so forth. This is because of the statement that Dhānañjayya [teaches] "come" (*āgacchata*) before the invocation of the gods. Thus, in the view of Dhānañjayya, the word "come" (*āgacchata*) must be uttered before the word "O Agnis" (*agnayaḥ*); but not in the view of Gautama.
In that regard, one should pause at the word *vicarṣaṇi* in the former recitation (*nigada*), and at the word *jāra* in the latter; the remainder is as in the archetype (*prakṛti*).
First, he recites the Agniṣṭut: "O Agni, you purify our lives; O Agni, the Purifier, with your flame; Agni is the head of heaven, its summit. (RV 9.66.10–12)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
In the Agniṣṭut sacrifices, Agni is the deity of all the stotras.
O Agni, come hither for the feast; who among men is your kinsman? Agni, worthy of praise and homage, may he strike down the Vṛtras. 2.
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.

"Ut te bṛhanto arciṣaḥ"—this *Gāyatra* is on one verse; the *Āmahīyava* on one verse; the *Jarābodhīya* on one verse; "Pāhi no agna ekayā"—this *Yaudhājaya* is on three verses; "Ino rājann aratiḥ samiddhaḥ"—this *Auśana* is the final one. [Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.

"Enā vo agniṃ namasā," "Kayā te agne aṅgiraḥ"—these are the *Rathantara* and the *Vāmadevya*; "Agnā āyāhy agnibhiḥ," "Acchā naḥ śīraśociṣam"—these are the *Naudhasa* and the *Kāleya*. Thus end the *Pṛṣṭhas*.

*Adābhyaḥ pura etā* is in the *gāyatra-saṃhitā*; *Bhadro no agnir āhutaḥ* and *agne vājasya gomataḥ* are in the *sapha-pauṣkala*; *viśoviśo vo atithim* is in the *śyāvāśva-andhīgava*; and *samiddham agnim* is the final [verse] of the *yajñāyajñīya*.

[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna. The *yajñāyajñīya* is performed on three verses; the remaining [verses] are on the first ones. When the *stoma* is possible, the final [verse] is used everywhere because of the rule "on a triplet. When making it a single verse, one should place it at the beginning of the first [verse]; and when making two, they should be in that same [verse].
In the Vāyavyā verses, "upa tvā jāmayo giraḥ" is the Vāravantīya Agniṣṭoma-sāman.

The mention of "in the Vāyavyā verses" is for the sake of subsequent reference; for it will be stated in the context of the Sattra that "for whom there is an Agniṣṭoma in the Vāyavyās. All the stotras are *trivṛt*, because it will be stated later that "both are *trivṛt*."
[Thus ends the first Agniṣṭut. || 21 ||] The second Agniṣṭut: he extends the arrangement of the first to the second by stating, "This very same is the arrangement for the latter. || 1 ||
Thus [it is said]. He states the specific detail:
"For that [sacrifice], the Vāravantīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman upon the Revatī verses. Its deity is Indra.

Regarding the *stoma* for the first and second [days], he says: "Both are *trivṛt*. From this point onward, in the *subrahmaṇyā* formula, one should say "O gods, O Brahmans" instead of "O Agnis," because of the statement in the *Nidāna*: "Some say that because the *agniṣṭomasāman* belongs to Indra [the term 'Agnis' is not used]. ||3||
Thus ends the second [sacrifice], the Agniṣṭut. 22.

The Agniṣṭut is the third [day]; he speaks of the Agniṣṭut as the third. He draws out the Jarābodhīya; before the Yaudhājaya, the Raurava; in the place of the Pauṣkala, the Śrudhya; the Yajñāyajñīya of Śyāvāśva; and the Kāva for the Yajñāyajñīya. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as before.
The Jyotiṣṭomas are the Stomas. || 3 ||

Thus: *agna āyūṃṣi pavase*, *agne pāvaka rociṣā*, and *agnirmūrdhā divaḥ kakut*—these constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant, which is threefold (*trivṛt*). *agna ā yāhi vītaye*, *kaḥ te jāmir janānām*, *īḍenyo namasyaḥ*, and *agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanat*—these are the fifteen-fold (*pañcadaśa*) *ājya* chants. *utte bṛhanto arcayaḥ* consists of the *gāyatra* and the *cāmahīyava*. *pāhi no agna ekayā* consists of the *raurava* and the *yaudhājaya*. *ino rājann aratiḥ* is the final [verse], belonging to the *auśana* [sāman].

Thus ends the fifteenth [stotra] of the midday pressing. "Enā vo agnim namasā" (With this homage to Agni for you), "Kayā te agne aṅgiraḥ" (By what [way], O Agni Aṅgiras?), these are the Rathantara and Vāmadevya [sāmans]. "Agnā āyāhy agnibhiḥ" (Come hither with the fires, O Agni), "Acchā naḥ śīraśociṣam" (Toward us, the one of sharp brilliance), these are the Naudhasa and Kāleya [sāmans]. Thus are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras consisting of seventeen verses. "Adābhyaḥ pura etu" (May the invincible one go before us) is the Gāyatra-saṃhita; "Bhadro no agne vājasya" (May he be auspicious to us, O Agni, for the sake of booty) is the Sapha-śrudhya. "Viśoviśo vo atithim" (The guest of every clan for you) is the Yajñāyajñīya and Āndhīgava. "Samiddham agnim" (The kindled Agni) is the Kāva. Thus is the Ārbhava-stotra consisting of seventeen verses. The Sapha-śrudhya consists of a single Ṛc.
In the Revatī verses, the Vāravantīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman on the twenty-one-fold stoma. || 3 ||
Thus ends the third [sacrifice], the Agniṣṭut. 23.

The Agniṣṭut is the fourth [day]. Regarding the fourth, the Agniṣṭut: "O Agni, come to us with your aids; let our prayers impel Agni"—these two triplets of five verses are placed before the Paryāsa. "Protect us, O Agni, with one [verse]"—the Raurava [Sāman] is sung on three verses. The Dairghaśravasa [Sāman] is on one verse. The Samanta and Viṣṭārapaṅkti [Sāmans] are [on one each]. The Yaudhājaya [Sāman] is on three verses. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as before.
All [the stomas] are seventeenfold.

"O Agni, you purify the lives; O Agni, the Purifier, with your radiance; protect us, O Agni, with your aids; let our prayers impel Agni; Agni is the head"—with these [verses] is the Bahiṣpavamāna performed. "O Agni, come hither; who is your kinsman? He is worthy of praise and worship"; "Agni shall strike down the Vṛtras"—with these are the Ājya-stotras. "Your lofty [songs], the Gāyatra and the Cāmahīyava"; "Protect us, O Agni"—with these three verses is the Raurava chanted; the Dairghaśravasa on one verse; the Samanta in the Viṣṭārapaṅkti meter.

In the verse beginning with "pāhi viśvasmāt," the *yaudhājaya* is performed over three verses; "ino rājan" is the final [verse] of the *auśana*; "enā vo," "kayā te agne," the *rathantara*, and the *vāmadevya*; and "agna āyāhyagnibhiḥ" and "acchā naḥ śīraśociṣam"—these are the *naudhasa* and *kāleya*, which constitute the *pṛṣṭha* stotras.

"Adābhyaḥ pura etā" is for the *gāyatra-saṃhita*; "Bhadro no agne vājasya" is for the *sapha-śrudhya*; "Viśoviśo vo atithim" is for the *yajñāyajñīya* and *andhīgava*; "Samiddham agniṃ samidhā girā" is the final [verse] of the *kāva*; the *sapha-śrudhya* consists of single-verse hymns (*ekarca*).
In the Revatī verses, the Vāravantīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman; all the stotras consist of seventeen verses. || 3 ||
Thus ends the Agniṣṭut, the fourth [section]. 24.

There are four *trivṛt* *agniṣṭoma*s, beginning with that of Prajāpati. Of these, the first is the *apūrva* (unprecedented) sacrifice of Prajāpati. Regarding the *trivṛt-agniṣṭoma*, its morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*) is "undefined" (*anirukta*), as stated in the section [of the Śrautasūtra] beginning with those words. If someone who is entitled to perform a sacrifice should not obtain [the necessary materials], he should perform the first of the *trivṛt* sacrifices; because its morning pressing is undefined. In the invocation of the *subrahmaṇyā*, the specific modification is: "O Śakra, come! O Viśve Brahmāṇas! He should say "Śakra" for Indra, and "Viśve" for the gods, according to the rule: "In the case of the undefined [deities] and in the case of the two undefined morning pressings."
He speaks of the arrangement of the hymns:
"Flow clear, O Indu, as the pressed bull! These drops have been released, O Sage, of you who are being purified. (1)
Thus concludes the Bahiṣpavamāna.
The *vrātya* offerings are not to be recited with the *ājya* chants.

"uccā te jātamandhasaḥ"—this Gāyatra [Sāman] is on one verse; the Āmahīyava on one; the Jarābodhīya on one; and "punānaḥ soma dhārayā"—this Yaudhājaya [Sāman] is on three verses. The Abhīvarta is the Brahman-sāman among the verses of the Naudhasa. 3.
The rest is the same as the Jyotiṣṭoma. Thus: "Flow on, O Indu, as a bull, being pressed; these drops have been released; of you, O sage, who are being purified"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna.

"The immortal god, the Hotṛ—may he be able to grant us that which is beautiful upon the earth for our protection; pour forth splendor at the pressed juice"—these are the *ājya* verses. Because the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*) is characterized by being "unexpressed" (*anirukta*), the word "god" (*deva*) in the phrase "the god, the Hotṛ" must be replaced by the word "sacrifice" (*yajña*). Accordingly, regarding the *upahavya* sacrifice as being unexpressed, there is a *sūtra*: "The Hotṛ [chants] 'The god, the great [friend]' and 'Of Mitra'"; these are chanted as "The Hotṛ, at the sacrifice, the great [sacrifice]" (*hotā yajñe mahīyajñasya*). The *sāman*-triplets are: "High is thy [flame]" (*uccā te*) for the *gāyatra-āmahīyava*, and "Awakened by praise" (*jarābodhīya*).

The *tiyaudhājaya* on three verses beginning with "punaḥ soma dhārayā," the *auśana* as the final [verse], the *rathantara* and the *vāmadevya*, the *abhīvarta* as the *brahmasāman* on the verses of the *naudhasa*, and the *kāleya* on its own verses—these are the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].

The two verses beginning with *svādiṣṭhayā* are the Gāyatra-saṃhita; those beginning with *pavasva indram accha* are the Sapha and Pauṣkala; those beginning with *purojitī vaḥ* are the Śyāvāśva and Andhīgava; the last [verse] belongs to Kava; and those excluding the [verse] of Kava consist of single stanzas.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. Everything is threefold (*trivṛt*). Thus ends the unprecedented [rite] of Prajāpati. 25.

The Bṛhaspatisava. The Bṛhaspatisava is the second [soma-sacrifice]. It is described in the section beginning with "The Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma; at its morning pressing... and continues with the sūtra: "He whom Brahmins who are self-sovereign kings place at their head should sacrifice with the Bṛhaspatisava," and so forth. By this, the entitlement for this sacrifice belongs only to a Brāhmaṇa, not to a Rājanya or a Vaiśya. Regarding its ritual arrangement, he says: "This very same [arrangement] is for the Mādhyandina pressing of the subsequent [sacrifice]. || 1 ||
Everything else is the same as in the Jyotiṣṭoma. || 2 ||

Thus: that which is this Mādhyandina Pavamāna of Prajāpati’s *apūrva* sacrifice is itself the Bṛhaspatisava; all else is like the Jyotiṣṭoma—this is the meaning. The Bahiṣpavamāna is [performed] with the *upadravi-pava*. The Ājya-stotras are with the verses beginning "O Agni, come to us" and "O Indra and Agni. For the first [Ājya], the Gāyatra-sāman is used with the verse "High is thy birth, O Soma"; for the second, the Āmahīyava; for the third, the Jarābodhīya. The Yaudhājaya-sāman, with the verse "Being purified, O Soma, in thy stream," is used for the three [verses]; the Auśana is the final one.

The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *naudhasa*, and the *kāleya*. The *gāyatra-saṃhita* consists of [the verses] beginning with "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā. The *sapha-pauṣkala* consist of [the verses] beginning with "pavasvendram accha. The *śyāvāśva-andhīgava* consist of [the verses] beginning with "purojitī vo andhasaḥ. The *kāva* is the final [stotra]. The *kāva* is performed on three verses; the remaining [stotras] are performed on the initial [verses].

The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. Everything is *trivṛt*. In this ritual manual (*kalpa*), some—considering the word "mādhyaṃdina" to denote the midday pressing (*mādhyandina-savana*) and accepting that the unprecedented midday pressing of Prajāpati is extended by analogy to the Bṛhaspatisava—state that the *abhīvarta* on the verses of the *naudhasa* is the *brahmasāman*. That is incorrect; because in this ritual manual, the word "mādhyaṃdina" everywhere denotes only the Mādhyandina-pavamāna-stotra, and not the pressing (*savana*).

For instance, in such passages as "Soma purifies himself, the final source of the midday [pressing]," and "The Āśvina [stotra] follows," it is perfectly clear that the term refers specifically to the *pavamāna*. Likewise, regarding the second *ekastoma* sacrifice, he will state: "In the Gaurīvīta-sāman rite, the *bahiṣpavamāna* belongs to the Indra-stoma; the midday [pressing] has 'O Soma, being purified, flow with thy stream' in the *bṛhatī* meter; the *śyaita* [sāman] is performed on its own verses; everything else is the same as the first thousand-fold [sacrifice]."

In this regard, from the statement "on its own [days], the Śyaita," it is understood that this [term] is indeed a designator of the *pavamāna* [laud]. For if it were a designator of the *savana*, then since the prescription of the Śyaita would already be established by the very fact that it is prescribed for the Śyeta [sacrifice] within the *indrastoma* itself, the present statement would be redundant. Furthermore, referring specifically to the Bṛhaspatisava, it will be stated later regarding the middle *pṛṣṭhya*: "It is arranged up to the Bṛhaspatistoma; for that, the *abhīvarta* is the *brahmasāman*."

In that case, if it had already been prescribed as the *brahmasāman* previously, then what would be the purpose of prescribing it again? Therefore, it is established that for the *bṛhaspatisava*, the *brahmasāman* is indeed the *tāndava*. || 2 ||
Thus ends the Bṛhaspatisava. || 26 ||

The *iṣu* is the third *iṣu* prescribed in the *Ṣaḍviṃśabrāhmaṇa*. It is the *trivṛt-agniṣṭoma*. Having performed its *iṣu-viṣṭuti* according to the section beginning with "having made... (*tasyeṣu viṣṭutiṃ kṛtvā*). Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows: the *jarābodhīya* [sāman] is in the place of the *śākvara-varṇa*; the *saptaha* is for the *vaṣaṭkāra-nidhana*; the *bṛhat* [sāman] has the *vaṣaṭkāra-nidhana*. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as for the Śyena sacrifice. || 2 ||
"Purifying himself, he has stepped forth toward us as he strikes down [the enemies]—O Sage, of you, the Pavamāna"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna chant.

"Agni shall strike down the Vṛtras; I invoke Indra of pure strength"—"May the Soma-draughts exhilarate you; I invoke those two for whom this [world exists]"—these are the *ājya* verses. "Flow on, O Soma, most resplendent"—this is the *gāyatra* chant. "Flow on, O Soma, most resplendent"—these are the three-verse *sāman*s of the *vārṣāhara* and *jarābodhīya* types. "Being purified, O Soma, in your stream"—these are the three-verse *sāman*s of the *saptaha*, *raurava*, and *yaudhājaya* types. The *auśana* is the final one. The *pṛṣṭha* chants are the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *vaṣaṭkāraṇidhana*, and the *kāleya*.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" is for the Gāyatra-Vārṣāhara; "pavasvendram accha" is for the Sapha-Upagava; and "purojitī" is for the Nānada-Andhīgava. The last [verse] belongs to Kava; those other than the Kava verses consist of single stanzas (*ekarca*). The *Yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. Everything is *trivṛt*. Two *iṣu*-named *viṣṭutis* (recitation patterns) of the *trivṛt* are prescribed in the *Ṣaḍviṃśa-brāhmaṇa*: "He utters the *hiṃ* for one [verse]," beginning with "he [does so] with the first," and so forth. By means of the first of these two, the *kuśā* (grass-blade) rule is established for the first *ājya* chant.

With the second [verse], [he offers] for the second; again with the first, for the third—and so on. Thus, beginning from the first *ājya* offering, the placement of the *kuśa* grass is performed with the two arrows in reverse order, because of the statement: "with the reversal of the arrow, by means of the two arrows. For the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*), everything such as wearing red turbans (*lohitoṣṇīṣa*) and so forth is like that of the *Śyena* sacrifice. || 2 ||
Thus ends the section on the arrow. 27.

The *sarvasvāra*, or the *śunaskarṇastoma*, is the fourth *sarvasvāra*. It is described in the section beginning with "The threefold *agniṣṭoma* is that *sarvasvāra*"; it is known by the name *śunaskarṇastoma*. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
The Soma juices have flowed forth; like rattling chariots, the drops have been let loose upon their path. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
All [the verses] consist of triplets (tṛca), because of the statement: "All [verses] in the Sarvasvāra."
Approaching the sacrifice, sing forth to Mitra; sing forth a gladdening song to Indra; the chanters of hymns sing forth to you both. 2.
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.

One should extract the third verse of the *upaprayaṃ* four-verse hymn; the second verse of the *pra vām arcaṃ* four-verse hymn; and the third verse of both the *sarvasvāra* and *svarasāman* [sacrifices]. This is because of the statement: "The second verse of *pra vām arcanti*. (2)
"Forward, O wise Soma-stems"—this is the Gāyatra; "Forward, O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—this is the Gauṅgava; "Run forward"—this is the Auśana, which is the final [verse]. || 3 ||
[Thus is the Mādhyandina Pavamāna:
the Vāmadevya, the Maidhātitha, the Hārāyaṇa, and the Kaulmalabarhiṣa. || 4 ||
Thus end the *pṛṣṭhas*. 4.
The Gāyatrī is the metre of the Hotṛ’s Pṛṣṭha-stotra; for the remaining [Pṛṣṭhas], the Bṛhatī is the metre. 4.

"O Soma drops, distilling intoxication"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *āśubhārgava*. "Toward lofty splendor and fame, flow forth, O wakeful Soma"—these are the *saphasatrāsāhīya*. "For the one who presses the juice, [flow] for the food"—this is the *śyāvāśvaudala*. "He has gone forth"—this is the final *kāva*. 5.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna:
with the exception of the last verse, they consist of single-verse stanzas. 5.
The *Yajñāyajñīya* as the *Agniṣṭoma-sāman* is "pra daivodāso agniḥ"; [it is] that of Dīrghaśravas on its own verses, if he should live.

This is the *sarvasvāra*, a sacrifice performed with the desire for death. Its *sūtra* states: "One intending to sacrifice with the *sarvasvāra* should exert himself from the initiation (*dīkṣā*) onwards; [the procedure] from 'on the day of pressing' (*sautye'hani*) until the end of the rite, ending with the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), applies here. In this context, the prolongation of the initiations, the consumption [of the soma], the "breath-consumption" (*prāṇabhakṣaṇa*), and so forth—the means of dying—are prescribed.

While the Ārbhava Pavamāna is being chanted, having gone to the south of the Udumbara post and spread out a black antelope skin, he lies down covered, with his head toward the south; thus the time of death is prescribed. At that time, Śāṇḍilya says that they should depart after casting the deceased into the Āhavanīya fire along with the sacrificial oblations and the Soma dregs. Alternatively, they should complete the rite with the Nediṣṭin ceremony.

Thus says Dhānañjayya. In that regard, based on the view that the remaining rites are to be completed, the author of the Kalpa-sūtra prescribed the Agniṣṭoma-sāman as the Dairghaśravasa on its own verses, provided that [the sacrificer] should live. If he does not die at the stated time, then the Dairghaśravasa Agniṣṭoma-sāman is to be performed on its own verses. If one asks for what purpose this is, it was stated by the author of the Nidāna: "The Dairghaśravasa is on its own verses, provided that he should live; for if he were unable to die, he might yet hear [the news] from afar—this is for the sake of his departure. (6)
The Sarvasvāra sacrifice. || 7 ||

The mention of the designation "Sarvasvāra" is for the purpose of indicating that, by this very designation—namely, "one whose own [possessions] are all"—the *jāmi*-avoidance rule applies here without fault. And thus, according to the statement of the Sūtra, there is no loss of the *tantra* (common ritual framework), just as in the case of the *jāmi*-avoidance rule: "The Sarvasvāra. Beginning with the unprecedented rite of Prajāpati, he states the arrangement of the *stomas* for the four [days]: "All are *trivṛt*. (Sūtra 8)
Thus [ends section] 8.
Peace through the Vāmadevya; peace through the Vāmadevya. [Section] 9.

Regarding the statement "The *śānti* [is] the *vāmadevya*," when the cremation of the deceased has been performed according to the method prescribed in the Sūtra, the *vāmadevya*, which constitutes the *śānti*, is to be sung at the conclusion of the *parisāman*s. And this was stated by the author of the Kalpa for the sake of auspiciousness; thus all is well. 9.
Thus ends the third chapter from the beginning—the first among the one-day sacrifices—in this commentary on the *Ārṣeyakalpa* composed by Varadarāja, son of the venerable Vāmanārya.

"O Agni, you purify our lives; sing to him, O men! Sing forth to him who is born, the one who crosses the waters! We [sing] to you, the purifying one; we [sing] to you, the purifying one, O Sage! May you grant us aid, O Lord of Power! Thus is the *abhīvarta* and the *brahmasāman*; the rest is the same as the *bṛhaspatisava*, with the same *stoma*. 411.

"O Varuṇa, hear this my call!"—"Sing toward him, O men!"—"Toward him who is born, the swift one crossing the waters. These [verses] belong to you, Pavamāna; to you, O Sage, as you are being pressed together, in the world where you are made manifest by birth. There are two *ṛc*s: the *Sapha* and the *Pauṣkala*. The *Śyāvāśva* [verse] and the *Audala* are [included]; the other is the same as that of the *Jyotiṣṭoma*. The *Bahiṣpavamāna* is the *Trivṛt*; the other is the *Pañcadaśa*; everything else is the same. 412.

With what aid will you flow for us, as the leader of the voice? Flow, O Indu, as the pressed bull; O Soma, you are brilliant, for you are indeed a bull by your radiance. "We choose Agni as the messenger"—with these [verses], the *ājyāni* hymns of this [rite]: the *pratnāmanu dyut* and the *gāyatram*, the *hāviṣmatam*, the *samantam*, and the *dairghaśravasam*; the *ayāsye* hymn beginning with "This Soma," the *pārtham* as the final one, the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevyam*, the *traiśokam*, and the *vaikhānasam*; and [the verse] beginning with "That exhilaration of yours which is most excellent."

The *gāyatra-saṃhita* is for the *pavate* verse; the *indramaccha* is for the *satrāsāhīya*; the *ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ* is for the *śyāvāśva*; the *dhartā divaḥ* is for the *krauñca*; the *dīrghatamaso'rkaḥ* is the final [verse]; the *agniṣṭomasāman* is the *yajñāyajñīya*; the *sākamaśva*, the *saubhara*, and the *aṣṭādaṃṣṭra* are used; the *trivṛt* is the *bahiṣpavamāna*; the *pañcadaśa* is the *hotṛ's ājya-stotra*; and all the others are *saptadaśa*. 42.

"May the sister songs approach you; sing to him, O men! Sing well to the one born as the overcomer of waters. "Of you, the purifying one, O Sage; O Agni, come hither for the feast"—these are the *ājya* verses. "The inspired Soma-drops"—this is the *gāyatra* hymn. "The swift horse of Bhṛgu"—the *āśva*. "O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—the *pajra*, the *gauṅgava*, the *yaudhājaya*, and the *auśana* as the final [verse]. The *rathantara* and the *vāmadevya* chants, and "Indra for the service of the gods"—the *yuktasruc*. The *kāleya* hymn in its own [verses], with the verse beginning "With the sweetest [honey]."

The *gāyatra* chant is "madiṣṭhaya," and the *svāśira* is "arkaḥ pavasva indram accha"; the *sapha* and *pauṣkala* are [the same]. The *audala-sādhrī* is "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ," or the *audala-gautama*. The final *kāva* is the *yajñāyajñīya*, which serves as the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *bahiṣpavamāna* is the *trivṛt*; the *hotṛ's ājya-stotra* is the *pañcadaśa*; the *maitrāvaruṇa's* is the *saptadaśa*; and all the others are the *ekaviṃśa*. 43.

"O Indu, flow for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, as the foremost of speech; flow, O Indu, as the pressed bull; O Soma, you are brilliant, for you are indeed a bull by your radiance. With the verses beginning "We choose Agni as the messenger," there are the *ājya* hymns; and with "Flow as a bull, O stream," there are the *gāyatra*, *yauktāśva*, *jiga*, *svāra*, and *sauparṇa* hymns; and with "Being purified, O Soma, in streams," there are the *samanta* and *dairghaśravasa* hymns; and with "The red bull goes forth," there is the *pārtha* as the final one, along with the *bṛhat*, *vāmadevya*, and *śyaita* chants.

The *mādhucchandasa* [is used] with "yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"; the *gāyatra* is the *arkasāman* of Agni with "surūpaṃ tvaṃ hyaṅga pavasva devavītaye"; the *āsita* and *krauñca* are used with "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"; the *yāma* is the final [verse] with "bhargo vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate"; the *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*; the *sākamaśva*, *saubhara*, and *udvaṃśīya* [are used]; the *trivṛt* is the *bahiṣpavamāna*; the *pañcadaśa* is the *hotṛ's ājya-stotra*; the *saptadaśa* is that of the *maitrāvaruṇa*; the *ekaviṃśa* is that of the *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin*; and everything else is the *triṇava*. 44.

O Viśvakarman, strengthened by the oblation, with your flashing radiance the drops have been poured forth; the King approaches with his insights. Flow for nourishment in a stream, you the immortal divine Hotṛ! For even through many [obstacles], he exists; we incite that Indra for strength. With "This [is] for you of the lovely thought," "Upward [your] birth of the soma-juice," the Gāyatra and the Āmahīyava, the Jarābodhīya and the Ṛṣabha, the Pavamāna and the Gauṣūkta, "The Soma-drops [come] hither"—these are the Paurumadga, the Gautama, the Antarikṣa, and the Maidhātitha.

The height [of the altar] is three *vācas*; this is the *saṃkrośa* of the Aṅgirases; the last [stotra] consists of the *rathaṃtara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śrāyantīya*, and the *raurava*. "Pari svano girīsthā" is the *gāyatra-saṃhitā*; the *vāravantīya*; "sa sunve yo vasūnām", "prāṇā śiśurmahīnām"—these are for the *dīrgha-śrudhi*; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the *niṣedha* of Śyāvāśva for the *andhīgava* [sāman]; "pari pra dhanva" is for the *vājadāvaryas*; "yā ruce" is for the *nityavatsa*; and "dhartā divaḥ."

The last *arkas* belong to Dīrghatamas; the *agniṣṭomasāman* is the *yajñāyajñīya*; the *ṣoḍaśisāman* consists of the *pramam̐hiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, the *nārmedha*, and the *gaurīvit*. The night-rite has the *saṃdhi-stotra* with a *trivṛt* *bahiṣpavamāna*, a *pañcadaśa* *hotṛ-ājya*, a *saptadaśa* *maitrāvaruṇa-ājya*, an *ekaviṃśa* *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin-ājya*, and a *triṇava* *acchāvāka-ājya*. The other *agniṣṭomasāman* is the *trayastrim̐śa*; the *ukthas* have *ekaviṃśa* *stotras* together with the *ṣoḍaśin*, and the night-rite has a *pañcadaśa* *stotra*. The *saṃdhi* is *trivṛt*. Thus is the *agniṣṭoma* arranged in the world of the *śunāsīrya*.

Flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull! These drops have been released; and may they [grant] our prayer for the acquisition of cattle, O heroes, for the one who exerts himself. Toward us the sons [of the gods] and the songs rise up, and your vital powers, O Sage, stir themselves. The immortal divine Hotṛ-priest is yours. This great pair, Heaven and Earth, are yours; you meet them together. The cows low toward the one who strikes [the Soma], the Pavamāna. Thus [are sung] the Gāyatra and the Āmahīyava; "Pour out the pressed juice on every side"—thus [are sung] the Dairghaśravasa, the Bārhaduktha, and the Yaudhājaya.

"Sākamukṣa" is the final [verse] for Pārtha; "Mā bhema mā śramiṣma" is the Bṛhat on its own verses; "Imā u tvā purūvaso" and "Yasyāyaṃ viśva āryaḥ" are the Śyaita and Kāleya; "Pavamāno ajījanat" is the Gāyatra; the two Samhitās [beginning with] "Ā sotā pari siñcata" and "Gomanna indro aśvavat" are the Sapha; "Śrudhye abhi no vājasātamam" is the Śyāvāśva; "Dhīgave añjate" is the final [verse] of the Kava; and the Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. 46.

For the second *svarasāman*, the *ājya* and *bahiṣpavamāna* chants are performed in the world of Bṛhaduktha: the *aṣṭādaṃṣṭra* for Maukṣa, the *hāviṣmat* for Śrudhya, and the *sujñāna* is extracted; the *ukthas* are the same as those of the first day of the *gavāmayana*. 471.

"These drops have been poured forth," and "Your vital strengths arise"—these two triplets of five verses in their own meters constitute the *śyaita*; the rest is the same as the first *sahasra-stoma*. 472.

Of the purifying one, the all-knowing, for thy flashing radiance, these drops have been poured forth, O Indu. Thee, who bearest manly powers, [we praise]. Of thee, the purifying sage, O Agni, with all thy fires, we invoke Mitra; we invoke Indra for you from every side—those two whose [power] this [world] is. "Toward thee, O Hero, we cry out"—this is the *Kaṇvarathantara* as the *pṛṣṭha*. "To us, worthy of invocation among all [beings]"—this is the *sadoviśīya* *brahmasāman*, consisting of two verses of the *januṣa* family, with the *sapha* and *pauṣkala* chants. "Around that desirable one... [the *pari tyam haryatam* chant].

The *harimiti* verses are in the *anuṣṭubh* meter; he extracts the final *kāva* verse beginning with "pavitraṃ te"; the *ukthas* are the same as those of the *āyuḥ* sacrifice, except for the one-day (*ekāhika*) [elements]. 473. Before the *paryāsa*, there are two triplets: "ete asṛgram indavas" and "taṃ tvā nṛmṇāni bibhratam. The *śrāyantīya* is the *brahmasāman* of the *saṃhita*; the *maukṣa* is in the place of the *pauṣkala*; the *śrudhya* is that of the *śyāvāśva*; the *yajñāyajñīya* is that of the *yajñāyajñīya*; the *viśoviśīya* is among the verses of the *yajñāyajñīya*; the *agniṣṭomasāman* is the same as that of the *āyuḥ* sacrifice, except for the one-day (*ekāhika*) [elements]. 474.

The Bahiṣpavamāna of the former [sacrifice]; three Ājya-stotras consisting of Vrātya-hymns; the Vaiśvajita as the last [Ājya]; the Rathantara as the Pṛṣṭha-stotra in the place of the Bṛhaduktha; the Abhīvarta as the Brahman-sāman in the place of the Maukṣa; the Śyāvāśva-marka as the Yajñāyajñīya; the Vāravantīya with the verse "tvaṃ naścitra ūtyā" as the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. The rest is the same as that of the Gava-ekāha. The Gau-rīvita is the Ṣoḍaśin-sāman on verses containing the word *śipiviṣṭa* for Viṣṇu; all [the Stomas] are seventeenfold. The Jyotiṣṭoma is prepared for the descent (pratyavarohaṇīya). 475. The [Jyotiṣṭoma] is prepared for the ascent (abhyārohaṇīya). 476.

The triplet beginning with *vāyo śukro ayāmi te* consists of six *saṃbhāryā* verses for the Vaiśvajit rite: *pavasva vāco agriyaḥ*, *davidyutatyā rucā*, *etamu tyaṃ daśa kṣipaḥ*, *pavasvendo vṛṣā sutaḥ*, *utte śuṣmāsa īrate*, and *pavamānasya te kave*. The *ājyāni* (offering-verses) are *dhā kṣapā pariṣkṛtaḥ*, *vaiśvajitāni*, *uccā te jātamandhasaḥ*—which includes the *gāyatram*, the *mahīyavam*, the *jarābodhīyam*, the *svāram*, and the *saindhukṣitam*—and *parīto ṣiñcatā sutam*, which is the *samantam*.

The Rathantara, the Dairghaśravasa, the Devasthāna, the Varuṇasāman, the Raurava, the Yaudhājaya, and "Vṛṣā śoṇa" as the final Pārtha; the Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita, and the Kāleya; "Yaste mado vareṇyaḥ," the Gāyatra, the Maukṣa, the Kākṣīvata, and the Svāśira; "Arkaḥ pavasvendramaccha," the Sapha, the Daivodāsa, the Vādhryaśva, the Vaitahavya, the Somasāman, and the Trāsadasyava.

The *indhīgava* and *kāvamantya* [are the stotras]; the *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*; "O Agni, you are our closest" is the *satrāsāhīya*; the *saubhara*, the *udvam̐śīya*, the thirty-two-versed *pavamāna* chants, fifteen-versed *ājya* chants, seventeen-versed *pṛṣṭha* chants, and the twenty-one-versed *agniṣṭoma* with its *ukthas*. 48.

With the verses, "The king goes forth with wisdom; thee, who bearest manly powers," [they chant] before the *paryāsa*. In the place of the *tṛca* of five verses belonging to Medhātithi, there is the *sado-viśīya*; the *raurava-maidhātitha* and the *śrāyantīya* as the *brahmasāman* in the place of the *pauṣkala*. The *śrudhya*, the *śyāvāśva-yajñāyajñīya*, and the *vāravantīya* as the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* are extracted from their own places. The *ukthas* are the same as those of the *āyuḥ-ekāha*. Everything is seventeenfold. 491.

"Flow on as the leader of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. "With flashing brilliance, the drops have been released for you; O Soma, you are a brilliant bull, for you are indeed a bull by your radiance. "O Sage, for you who are being purified, we choose Agni as our messenger"—these are the *ājya* verses. "Pour out the pressed juice all around"—this is the *samanta*. The *yaśas*, the *abhīśava*, and the *yaudhājaya* follow. "The red bull"—this is the final *pārtha* with the *bṛhat* as the *pṛṣṭha* chant. "O Indra, in the races..."—here the *brahmasāman* is the *abhīvarta*.

The rest is the same as for the *āyuṣ* sacrifice. The morning pressing is the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*), the midday pressing is the seventeen-fold (*saptadaśa*), and the third pressing is the fifteen-fold (*pañcadaśa*) with *ukthas*; it belongs to the night session, has a threefold (*trivṛt*) junction, and its *ājya* and *bahiṣpavamāna* chants follow the *jyotiṣṭoma* pattern.
