Furthermore, the *stomas* are those of the two-day rite, and this [pressing] is the same as the first day of that two-day rite.

Flow on as the leader of speech; this immortal god, he moves with subtle wisdom. We choose Agni, the messenger who brings bliss and skill. With the verse "His ancient splendor," there are the *gāyatra* and the *hāviṣmat*, the *jarābodhīya* and the *ṛṣabha-pavamāna*. With "Pour out the pressed juice on every side," there is the *dairghaśravasa*; "This Soma" is the final *pārtha*. And there are the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *traiśoka*, and the *vaikhānasa*: "The one flowing, dwelling on the mountains."

Thus, the *gāyatra-saṃhitā* is "pavasvendraṃ accha"; the *satrāsāhīya* is "viśoviśīye"; the *niṣedha* is "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"; the *krauñca* is "dhartā divaḥ"; the *dīrghatamaso'rka* is the final [verse]; the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* is the *yajñāyajñīya*. It is a *jyotiṣṭoma-atirātra* with the *ṣoḍaśin* cup; the *pavamāna* stotras are twenty-four-fold (*caturviṃśa*); the three *ājya* stotras are fifteen-fold (*pañcadaśa*); the *acchāvāka*’s [stotra] is seventeen-fold (*saptadaśa*); the three *pṛṣṭha* stotras are twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*); and the *acchāvāka*’s [final stotra] is twenty-nine-fold (*triṇava*).
The Agniṣṭoma has thirty-three [stomas]; the Ukthya-stotras have twenty-one [stomas] together with the Ṣoḍaśin; the night-chant has fifteen [stomas]; the junction (saṃdhi) has nine [stomas].
This is the established Jyotiṣṭoma, the support of the Kṣatra, the expansion.
The Fourth Chapter: The Saumika Cāturmāsya Sacrifices, beginning with the Vaiśvadeva.

By the section of the *anuvāka* stating, "The Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma is the world of the Vaiśvadeva," the seven Soma-pressings (*sutyā*) of the Saumika Cāturmāsya sacrifices are prescribed. Among these, the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice begins on the full moon day of Phālguna; its pressing is ordained for the day of the actual sacrifice (*yajanīya*). The second day of the two-day Varuṇapraghāsa sacrifice begins in such a way that it falls on the day of the sacrifice during the full moon of Āṣāḍha. The second day of the three-night Sākamedha sacrifice begins in such a way that it falls on the full moon day of Kārttika.

Again, on the full moon day of Phālguna, there is the initiation (*dīkṣā*) for the Śunāsīrya sacrifice; its *sutyā* (pressing day) falls on the day of the actual sacrifice, because that too lacks two days [of the preparatory period]. And so says the Sūtra: "One should begin the Cāturmāsya sacrifices on the full moon day of Phālguna," and so forth. Regarding that, he prescribes the threefold Agniṣṭoma which takes the place of the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice: "O Agni, you purify our lives; sing unto him, O men! Sing unto him who is born, the swift one! We [sing] to thee, the purifying one; we [sing] to thee, the purifying one, O Sage! (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

The last two *ṛc*s [of each triplet] are used; the others consist of single verses (*ekarca*). This is because of the rule: "In the *bahiṣpavamāna*, the last two *ṛc*s [of each triplet] are used, as well as the final one in the *Sāhasra* and the *Cāturmāsya* sacrifices. (1) The *Abhīvarta* is the *brahmasāman*, beginning with the words "śagdhyūṣu śacīpate. (2)
The rest is the same as the Bṛhaspatisava, with the same Stoma. || 3 ||

Thus: *agna ā yāhi*, *mitrāyāhi*, and *indrāgnī* are the *ājya* verses. *Uccā te jātam andhasaḥ* is the *gāyatra*; *āmahīyava* and *jarābodhīya* are the three *sāman*-verses. *Punānaḥ soma dhārayā* is the *yaudhājaya* sung over three verses; the *auśana* is the final one. The *rathantara* and *vāmadevya* [are used]. *Śagdhy ū ṣu* is the *abhīvarta*. The *pṛṣṭha* chants are the *kāleya* sung over its own verses. *Svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā* are the *gāyatra-saṃhita*. *Pavasva indram accha* are the *sapha* and *pauṣkala*.

"Purojitī" [is the first verse] for Śyāvāśva; "Andhīgava" is the last [verse] of the Kava [group]. With the exception of the Kava [verses], the others consist of single verses. The *Yajñāyajñīya* is the *Agniṣṭoma-sāman*. Everything is *trivṛt*. Thus ends the Vaiśvadeva [section]. 1.
The first day belongs to the Vāruṇapraghāsa offerings; it is the first day of what is called "the two-day period in the world of the Vāruṇapraghāsas. He recites for this first day:
"O Varuṇa, hear this my call! Sing unto him, O men! To him who is born, the swift one—unto you, O Pavamāna, we [sing], O Sage, unto you, the Pavamāna. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
Here too, as before, the first two are triplets (tṛca); the remaining are single verses (ekarca). The deity of the first verse is Varuṇa. 1.

In the world, that which was composed by Saṃhita has been revealed; the Sapha and Pauṣkala [Sāmans] belong to those who have a single verse for their birth; and the Audala belongs to Śyāvāśva. || 2 ||
The rest is the same as the Jyotiṣṭoma. Thus [it is said].

The *ājya* stotras are "agna ā yāhi," "mitrāya," and "indrāgnī. The *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* are [the stotras] with the verse "uccā te jātam andhasaḥ. For the *pavamāna*, the *dhārā* stotras are the *raurava* and *yaudhājaya*; the *auśana* is the last.
The Rathantara, Vāmadevya, Naudhasa, and Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha chants.

With the two single-verse hymns, "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" (which has its *hāviṣkṛta* [refrain] in the *gāyatrī* meter) and "ayā pavasva devayuḥ pavate haryato hariḥ," there are the *sapha* and *pauṣkala* chants; the *audala* chant, beginning with "purojitī," is used for the first verse, the *āndhīgava* for three verses, and the *kāva* for the final one. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. 3.
He states the arrangement of the *stomas*: the *bahiṣpavamāna* is threefold (*trivṛt*), while all the others are fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*).
Thus [ends section] 4.
Thus concludes the first day of the Vāruṇapraghāsa sacrifice. || 2 ||
The second day of the Vāruṇapraghāsa sacrifice.
Now he recites the second day:
"With what aid will you flow for us, O foremost of speech? Flow, O Indu, as the pressed bull; O Soma, thou art brilliant, for thou art a bull by thy luster. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

As before, the last two [sections] consist of triplets (*tṛca*); the others consist of single verses (*ekarca*). For the first [verse], Agni is the deity. (1) "We choose Agni as the messenger" (*agnim dūtam vṛṇīmahe*)—these are the *ājya* [verses]. (2) "Agni as the messenger," "We [choose] Mitra," and "Indra here"—these four verses constitute the *ājya* verses, meaning they are the *ājya* offerings. In the case of the four-verse section, one should omit the final verse. (2)

The *gāyatra* hymn "asya pratnāmanu dyutam" and the *hāviṣmat* hymn; the *samanta* hymn "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam" and the *dairghaśravasa* hymn for [the deity] Āyāsya; and the final *pārtha* hymn "ayaṃ somaḥ". (3)
[Thus ends] the Mādhyandina Pavamāna. It is performed all around on the first [day], and as a *triṇadhana* on the middle [day]. || 3 ||
The Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Traiśoka, and the Vaikhānasa; these are the Pṛṣṭhas.
The meter of the Traiśoka hymn is Atijagatī. || 4 ||

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the Gāyatra-saṃhitā; "pavasvendram accha"—this is the Satrāsāhīya for Śrudhi; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayir bhagaḥ"—these are the Śyāvāśva and Krauñca hymns; and "dhartā divaḥ"—this is the final Ārka of Dīrghatamas. || 5 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Satrāsāhīya and Śrudhya are each single-verse hymns. 5.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The Sākama-saubhara belongs to Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra. || 7 ||
Thus end the hymns.
Because of the statement in the *Upagrantha* that "previously [it was] once [sung] as a hymn" (*sakṛduktha*).
He states the arrangement of the *stomas*:
the *bahiṣpavamāna* is *trivṛt*; the *hotṛ*'s *ājya* is *pañcadaśa*; all the others are *saptadaśa*.
Thus [ends verse] 8.
Thus ends the second day, pertaining to the Vāruṇapraghāsa offerings.
Now [the author] describes the first day of the Sākamedha,
which is the first day of the three-night period mentioned as "the three nights in the world of the Sākamedhas."
May the sisterly songs approach you; O men, sing forth to him! To him who has been born, the swift one—[we approach] you, O Pavamāna, the sage, [as you flow] pure. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
The last two are triplets (tṛca); the remaining are single verses (ekarca). The deity of the first verse is Agni.

"O Agni, come for the feast"—these are the *ājya* [verses]. "The wise Soma-juices"—this is the *gāyatra* [sāman] belonging to Aśva; [the verses beginning] "O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—this is the *pajra*, the *gauṅgava*, the *yaudhājaya*, and the *auśana* as the final one.

[Thus ends] the Mādhyandina Pavamāna, the Rathantara, and the Vāmadevya; [the verse] "Indram id devatātaye" is for the joined ladle, and the Kāleya [Sāman] is upon its own verses. (4) Thus end the Pṛṣṭhas.

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" is the Gāyatra and the Svāśira; "arkaḥ pavasvendram accha" is the Sapha and the Pauṣkala; "prasunvānāyāndhasaḥ" is the Audala and the Sādhra, or the Audala and the Gautama; the last is the Kāva. 5.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.]
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. 6.
The *bahiṣpavamāna* chant is threefold; the *ājya* chant of the Hotṛ is fifteenfold; that of the Maitrāvaruṇa is seventeenfold; and all the others are twenty-onefold.
Thus ends the first day of the Sākamedha sacrifice. || 4 ||
The second day of the Sākamedha sacrifice:
Flow pure for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, O Indu, as the foremost of speech! Flow pure, O Indu; pressed as a bull, O Soma, thou art resplendent; for thou art indeed a bull by thy radiance. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
The first two are triplets (*tṛca*); the others consist of single verses (*ekarca*). 1.

The *ājya* hymns begin with "We choose Agni as our messenger" (*agnim dūtam vṛṇīmahe*). 2. The *pavamāna* at the midday pressing consists of: the *gāyatra*, the *yauktāśva*, the *ājiga*, the *svāra*, and the *sauparṇa*; the *samanta* and the *dairghaśravasa* beginning with "Being purified, O Soma, in thy stream" (*punānaḥ soma dhārayā*); and the final *pārtha* beginning with "The red bull" (*vṛṣā śoṇaḥ*). 3. [Thus ends the Mādhyamdina Pavamāna.
The *pṛṣṭha* stotras consist of the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *mādhucchandasa*. 4.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the *gāyatra* chant; "agne arkaḥ surūpaḥ"—this is the *surūpa*; "tvaṃ hyaṅga pavasva devavītaye"—this is the *śaṅkusujñāna*; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"—this is the *āsita*; "krauñcaṃ bhargaḥ"; "vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate"—this is the final *yāma*. 5.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. The Sākamaśva, the Saubhara, and the Udvaṃśīya [are the Ukthya-sāmans]. 7.
Thus end the hymns.

The *bahiṣpavamāna* is the *trivṛt*; the *ājya* of the Hotṛ is the *pañcadaśa*; that of the Maitrāvaruṇa is the *saptadaśa*; that of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is the *ekaviṃśa*; all the others are the *triṇava*. Thus it is said.
Thus ends the second day of the Sākamedha. Now he speaks of the third day of the Sākamedha, the third day.

O Viśvakarman, increasing through the oblation, you shine forth with brilliant luster; the drops have been poured out, and the King moves toward the sacrifices with wisdom. Flow for our nourishment in a stream! 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

The first two are triplets (*trcas*); the remaining are single verses (*ekarcas*). The meter of the first verse is *triṣṭubh*, and its deity is Viśvakarman. Regarding this, the underlying principle (*nidāna*) is: "He makes [the hymn] *triṣṭubh* and dedicated to Viśvakarman, for the *gāyatrī* does not exist here. (1)
The immortal god, the Hotṛ-priest, exists indeed even among many distant things; we impel that Indra for the sake of this [sacrificial] strength, [offering] this thought of yours. 2.
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.

"Uccā te jātamandhasaḥ"—this consists of the Gāyatra, the Cāmahīyava, the Jarābodhīya, the Carṣabha, the Pavamāna, and the Gauṣūkta. "Abhi somāsa āyavaḥ"—this consists of the Paurumadga, the Gautama, the Antarikṣa, the Maidhātitha, and the Utsedha. "Tisro vācaḥ"—this is the final Saṃkrośa of the Aṅgirases. [Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna. The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Śrāyantīya, and the Raurava—these are the Pṛṣṭhas.

"Pari svāno giriṣṭhā" is the Gāyatra; "Saṃhitam" and "Vāravantīyam"; "Sa sunve yo vasūnām" and "Prāṇā śiśurbhahīnām" for Dīrghaśrudhi; "Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Śyāvāśva and Āndhīgava; "Niṣedhaḥ" and "Pari pra dhanva"; "Ayā ruce" are the Nityavatsas; and "Dhartā divaḥ" is the final *arka* of Dīrghatamas. || 5 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
"Pari pra dhanva" is the Dvipadā metre; "Ayā ruce" is the Aṣṭi metre. || 5 || The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. || 6 ||
The most bountiful Hārivarṇa Nārmedha. || 7 ||
Thus end the *ukthas*.
The Gaurīvita is the Ṣoḍaśin-sāman;
the night is the junction. || 8 ||

He states the arrangement of the *stomas*: the *bahiṣpavamāna* is *trivṛt*; the *ājya* of the Hotṛ is *pañcadaśa*; that of the Maitrāvaruṇa is *saptadaśa*; that of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is *ekaviṃśa*; that of the Acchāvāka is *triṇava*; and the other is *trayastrimśa*. The *agniṣṭomasāman* is [the *ekaviṃśa*]; the *ukthas* are *ṣoḍaśika-ekaviṃśas*; the night-chant is *pañcadaśī*; and the *saṃdhi* is *trivṛt*. || 9 ||
Thus [ends the ninth].
Thus ends the third day of the Sākamedha sacrifice. || 6 ||

Regarding the Śunāsīrya sacrifice, it is said that in the world of Śunaḥsīra there is a Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma; thus he speaks of the Śunāsīrya: "The Jyotiṣṭoma is prepared for the world of Śunāsīrya. (1)

Thus: the Jyotiṣṭoma is the Agniṣṭoma. The [stomas] Dhur, Jyotis, and Viśvarūpa do not exist here. The remainder is as in the archetype (prakṛti). The section beginning with "When one offers the Agnihotra" is for the purpose of praising the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.
Thus ends the Śunāsīrya sacrifice.
The Cāturmāsya sacrifices are completed. || 7 ||

Now there are six Upahavya sacrifices characterized by the seventeen-fold stoma (*saptadaśa*). Among them, the first Upahavya, a seventeen-fold *agniṣṭoma*, is described in the section beginning with "The gods and the Asuras... (*devāścāsurāśca*). In that context, it is heard: "He brought the undefined (*anirukta*). That state of being undefined is demonstrated by the author of the Sūtras: "In the Upahavya, they should mention the names of the deities indirectly (*parokṣam*) when they are in their proper place; directly (*pratyakṣam*) when they are not in their proper place; and they should avoid the word 'deva' (god) everywhere. Here, the mention of the Upahavya serves as an illustration for the rule regarding the undefined.

In that [rite], they should pronounce the names of the deities residing in their own places (*svasthāna*) indirectly (*parokṣam*), and those not residing in their own places (*asvasthāna*) directly (*pratyakṣam*). They should avoid the word "deva" (god) everywhere, both for those in their own places and those not in their own places. For when a deity is established in a certain place according to the natural order, that is called its "own place"; any other deity there is said to be "not in its own place."

In this regard, when the question arises as to which name of a deity should be used indirectly by which word, it is stated: "Regarding these [verses], 'The divine Hotṛ, the great [friend] of Mitra' and 'The Hotṛ of the sacrifice, the great [lord] of the sacrifice,' they should say [the names] 'Hotṛ' and 'Sacrifice' respectively. Regarding the word "Indu," they should say "Soma. Since Agni is the deity's own station in the *ājya* [offering] of the Hotṛ, they should say "Sacrifice" (*yajña*) in place of the word "Deva" (divine), which denotes Agni, in the verse "The divine, immortal Hotṛ."

In the *ājya* verses dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa, because "Mitra" is its own established position, one should remove the word "of Mitra" from the phrase "accomplish the great [work] of Mitra" and instead say "of the sacrifice. In the *pavamāna* hymns, because "Soma" is its own established position, the word "Indu" should be used in place of the word "Soma" in both the phrases "Soma, who is the highest oblation" and "he has pressed Soma with the stones. The same applies in cases such as "O Soma, apart for our well-being," and so forth.

In the verse *parisvānaś cakṣase devamādanaḥ*, although it is the place for the name of a deity, the word *deva* must be treated as indirect (*pārokṣya*) by means of the word *viśva*, because of the statement: "Viśva [is] the gods. However, for other deities, the names must remain indirect in the verses prescribed by the authors of the Kalpasūtras. In the Yajñāyajñīya, however, the word *agni* must not be treated as indirect.

Because it is stated in the Brāhmaṇa, "He turned toward the gods with the verse *sa uttame stotre devo vo draviṇodāḥ*," the use of the word *deva* (god) in the *stotra* is authorized; based on this indicative mark (*liṅga*), in the *Anirukta-trayastrimśa* at the Bahiṣpavamāna of the *Sattrasāmayana*, one should not employ indirectness (*pārokṣya*) for Indra, Vāyu, and the others, as they are not in their own proper place [in that specific context].

In the Vājapeya sacrifice, regarding the verse "Praise him who [is] with flame" (*tam īḍiṣva yo arciṣā*), when the *ājya* offering belongs to Indra and Agni (*aindrāgna*), the indirectness (*pārokṣya*) of the words "Indra" and "Agni" is established precisely through their singing in an unexpressed form (*aniruktagāna*). However, in the recitation of the *ṛc*, the indirectness that constitutes an auxiliary part of the *stotra* must indeed be performed; for this *stotra* pertains to the *sāman*. For this very reason, it does not occur in the *parisāmans*. Therefore, the intention of the author of the Sūtras is that nothing further remains to be said regarding the subject of indirectness.

However, because the Subrahmaṇyā serves the purpose of invoking the deities, it possesses primacy like a *stotra*; therefore, in that context, indirectness (*pārokṣya*) is indeed appropriate. Thus it has been said: "One should say 'Indra, Śakra'"; and "One should say 'Viśve' for the gods in the case of the unexpressed [deities]."
He speaks the arrangement of the hymns:

"Flow clear, O Indu, as the pressed bull! These drops have been released; and [grant] our prayer that seeks cattle, O heroes, for the one who exerts himself. Or: "Toward us, O sons, [come] with songs; your powers rise upward, O Sage, you who are being purified. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

Furthermore, there are three single-verse hymns beginning with *uta no goṣaṇim dhiyam*. Their deities, in order, are the Maruts, Pūṣan, and the Viśvedevas. Thus, the Nidāna states: "Now indeed it says: 'It belongs to the Maruts, it belongs to Pūṣan, it belongs to the Viśvedevas. By this one should know that these [verses] belong to those deities; they are recited among the hymns dedicated to the gods. "The immortal god is the Hotṛ. "Forward for you two on the great heaven. "This one of yours is at rest. "The cows low toward the watering-place."
Thus end the offerings of clarified butter.
"Pavamānasya jighnataḥ" is the Gāyatra and the Cāmahīyava; "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam" is the Samanta, the Dairghaśravasa, the Bārhaduktha, and the Yaudhājaya; and "sākamukṣa" is the final Pārtha. || 3 ||
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna. It is performed all around on the first [stotra]; the Yaudhājaya [Sāman] is used for the middle [stotra]. 3.

"Let us not fear, let us not grow weary"—this is the *Bṛhat* [Sāman] on its own verses; "O Vāmadevya," "These [songs], O Lord of Many Wealth," and "He whose this [world] is entirely Āryan"—these are the *Śyaita* and the *Kāleya*.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"Pavamāna has generated" is for the Gāyatra-saṃhitā; "Presser, pour out [the juice] rich in cows, Indra rich in horses" is for the Saphaśrudhya; "Toward us, most winning of booty" is for the Śyāvāśva-andhīgava; "They anoint" is the final [verse] of the Kāva. 5.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Saphaśrudhya consists of one verse. 5.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
This entire Upahavya sacrifice consists of seventeen [stomas]; for he will say, "All are seventeen. Thus ends the Upahavya.

The second [sacrifice] is the Ṛtapeya; the Ṛtapeya is a seventeen-fold Agniṣṭoma, as stated in the Anuvāka: "Its twelve [days] consist of initiation and Upasad rites. Regarding this, the Sūtra says: "In the Ṛtapeya, its twelve [days] consist of initiation and Upasad rites," and so forth.
Now follows the ritual rule: for the second Svarasāman, the Ājya-stotra and the Bahiṣpavamāna-stotra [are performed].
The world of Bṛhaduktha is Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra; that of Maukṣa is Hāviṣmanta; that of Śrudhya is Sujñāna. || 2 ||
He recites the *ukthas*. 3. The rest is the same as that of the *gavām-ekāha*. 4.

"Thus: *pavasva vāco agriyaḥ*, *pavasvendo vṛṣā sutaḥ*, *vṛṣā soma dyumāṃ asi*, *utta śuṣmāsa īrate*, *pavamānasya te kave*—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna. *Agniṃ dūtam*, *mitraṃ vayam*, *indramid gāthinaḥ*—these four verses [are used]. For the *tyājyās*, [the verses are] *indre agne*. One should omit the third verse of the group of four, because of the statement: "The third [verse] is omitted for the *sarvasvāra* and *svarasāman*," and because of the mention of the *svarasāman* here. Having performed the worship of the *dhiṣṇya* hearths, they should proceed at the time of entering the *sadas* hall after reciting the *ṛtam*.
Having said, "This is the ground; this is the sun rising in the morning," at the time of consuming the Soma, one should consume it with the prescribed mantra.

For this [sacrifice], there are the *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* hymns beginning with "Asya pratnāmanu dyutam"; the *samanta*, *dairghaśravasa*, *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*, and *yaudhājaya* hymns beginning with "Parīto ṣiñcatā sutam"; and the *pārtha* hymn beginning with "Ayaṃ soma" as the final one. The *samanta* is used in the first [verse] of the *adhyāsya*; the *yaudhājaya* in the middle [verse] of the *adhyāsya*.
The Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita, and the Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" is for both the Gāyatra and the Hāviṣmat; "pavasvendramaccha" is for the Saphasujñāna; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is for the Śyāvāśva and Andhīgava; the final [verse] among those containing "sūryavatīṣu" is for the Kāva; and in the Saphasujñāna, there is one verse.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*; everything is seventeenfold.
Thus ends the Ṛtapeya sacrifice. 9.

The third [day] is difficult to attain; it is the seventeen-fold Agniṣṭoma. Its *dīkṣaṇīyā* offering is stated in the section beginning with "ete asṛgram indavaḥ" and "utte śuṣmāsa īrate. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is:
the two triplets and five verses beginning with "ete asṛgram indavaḥ" and "utte śuṣmāsa īrate" are placed before the *paryāsa*.
The Śyaita [Sāman] is performed on its own verses. || 2 ||
The rest is the same as the first thousand-fold [offering]. || 3 ||
"Thus: 'Flow on, the foremost of speech, with flashing luster! These drops have been poured forth; your vital strengths rise up, O sage Pavamāna! This is the Bahiṣpavamāna."
"O Agni, come for the feast; we invoke Mitra; Indra indeed with a loud song—the singers [invoke]; to Indra and Agni, a great homage"—these are the *ājya* verses.

The *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* [sāmans] are for the verse beginning with "asya pratnā. The *parīto ṣiñcatā sutaṃ*, the *samanta*, the *rathantara*, the *dairghaśravasa*, and the *yaudhājaya* [are used]. "This Soma slays Pārtha" is the final [verse]. The *samanta* is used in the first [turn]; the *yaudhājaya* in the middle turn. The *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *kāleya* are the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].

The *svādiṣṭhayā* verses are for the *gāyatra-saṃhitā*; *pavasvendram accha* is for the *sapha-śrudhya*; *purojitī* is for the *śyāvāśva-andhīgava*; the final [verse] among those containing *sūrya* is for the *kāva*; and the *ekarca* is for the *sapha-śrudhya*.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
All the hymns consist of seventeen verses. || 3 ||
Thus ends the section on the difficult-to-attain. 10.

The Vaiśyastoma is the fourth [Soma sacrifice]. It is a seventeen-fold Agniṣṭoma; its morning-pressing offerings are stated in the Anuvāka beginning with "ete asṛgram indavaḥ. In that regard, the qualification belongs only to a Vaiśya, not to Brāhmaṇas or Kṣatriyas. Its ritual procedure (kalpa) begins: "Of the Pavamāna, the all-knowing, with the flashing luster... "These drops have been poured forth... "Thee, who bearest manly powers... "Of thee, O Sage, the Pavamāna... || 1 ||
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
O Agni, with all your fires we invoke Mitra; we invoke Indra for you from every side—I call upon those two by whom this world exists. 2.
Thus end the offerings of clarified butter.

The *pṛṣṭha* [stotra] is the *Kaṇvarathaṃtara*, beginning with "abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ. The *brahmasāman* for the *sadoviśīya* is "ā no viśvāsu havyam. The *sapha* and *pauṣkala* are based on the single-verse hymns (*ekarca*) beginning with "januṣā. The *anuṣṭubh* is "pari tyaṃ haryataṃ harim. The final [sāman] of the *kāva* group is "pavitram. (3)
He draws forth the hymns. || 4 ||
The rest is the same as that of the one-day fever.

Thus: "uccā te jātam andhasaḥ" is the *gāyatra* and the *āmahīyava*. "abhi somāsa āyavaḥ" is the *mādhyaṃdina* [pavamāna], consisting of the *vāmadevya* with two *hiṅkāras*, the *maidhātitha*, the *raurava*, the *yaudhājaya*, and the *auśana* as the last. The *vāmadevya* has two *hiṅkāras* in the first verse; the *yaudhājaya* is in the middle verse.

The *kaṇvarathantara* is the *pṛṣṭha* [stotra] with the verse "abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ"; the *vāmadevya* is on its own verses; the *brahmasāman*, called *sadoviśīya*, is with the verse "ā no viśvāsu havyam"; the *kāleya* is on its own verses—these are the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras]. The *kaṇvarathantara* is performed on all *bṛhatī* verses. And thus says the *Nidāna*: "On all *bṛhatī* verses, nothing other than the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* is worthy, provided that the subsequent verses are in the *kakubh* meter."
"svādiṣṭhayā" and "ayā pavasva devayuḥ" are the two *gāyatra-saṃhitās*; "pavate haryato hariḥ" is for the two single-verse hymns;
"pari tyam haryatam harim" is for the *sapha* and *pauṣkala*; and "pavitraṃ te" is the final verse of the *kāva*.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. Everything is seventeenfold. 5.

Thus concludes the Vaiśyastoma. The Tīvrasut is the fifth [sacrifice]; it is an Ukthya sacrifice characterized by the *tīvrasut* [offering] and the seventeen-fold chant (*saptadaśa*), as stated in the section beginning with "Indra slew Vṛtra. Its Sūtra begins: "With that fifth [sacrifice], the Tīvrasut, he should cause one who has exceeded the Soma limit to sacrifice," and so forth. Now follows the ritual procedure (*kalpa*).

"ete asṛgram indavas" and "taṃ tvā nṛmṇāni bibhratam"—these two triplets and five verses [are recited] before the *paryāsa*. The *śrāyantīya* is the *brahmasāman*. The *maukṣa* is in the place of the *saṃhita*; the *śrudhya* is in the place of the *pauṣkala*; and the *yajñāyajñīya* of Śyāvāśva [is used]. The *viśoviśīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman* upon the verses of the *yajñāyajñīya*. 1.
The rest is the same as that of the one-day fever (*ekāhika*). || 2 ||
Thus: "Sing for him with a flashing luster; these drops have been poured forth; thee, who art bearing [the Soma] to satiety; O Pavamāna, [thine is] the 'kavi' [hymn]"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, come to us," "O Mitra," and "O Indra and Agni"—these are the *ājya* [offerings].

At this point, at the time of consuming the Soma, they should smell the cups with the *bhakṣavṛt* formula. Those cups which they smell, from those very ones they should pour out [more Soma]. They should consume them during the *stotra* of the Acchāvāka. This should be done in the same manner at all the pressings (*savanas*).

"Uccā te jātam" consists of the Gāyatra and the Āmahīyava. "Abhi somāsa āyavaḥ" consists of the Dvihiṅkāra, the Maidhātitha, the Raurava, the Yaudhājaya, and the Auśana as the last; [the first] has two hiṅkāras, and the Yaudhājaya is [placed] in the middle verse.
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Śrāyantīya, and the Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha chants.

The *svādiṣṭhayā* [verse] is the *gāyatra* for the *aukṣa*; the *pavasvendram accha* [verse] is the *sapha* for the *śrudhya*; the *purojitī* [verse] is the *yajñāyajñīya* for the *andhīgava*. The final [laud] is the *kāva*. At the verses of the *yajñāyajñīya*, the *viśoviśīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. The *pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *ṭhadvaṃśīya* are the *ukthas*.
Every [stotra] consists of seventeen verses. || 2 ||

Thus ends the *Tīvrasut* [section]. The *Vājapeya* is described by two *anuvākas*: "The *Vājapeya* is the sixth; the *Vājapeya* consists of seventeen *ukthyas*, includes the *ṣoḍaśin*, and has seventeen [stotras]" and so forth. Its *sūtra* consists of two sections beginning with: "That king whom the Brahmins place at the head, he should sacrifice with the *Vājapeya*," etc. In the *subrahmaṇyā* formula, the modification is: "O Śakra, come! O Viśve Brahmāṇaḥ! because the morning libation (*prātaḥsavana*) is *anirukta*. Regarding the arrangement of the hymns (*stotra*), he says: the *bahiṣpavamāna* belongs to the former [set]; there are three *vrātya* *ājya* hymns; the *vaiśvajita* is the last.

In the world of Bṛhaduktha is the station of the gods; the Rathantara is the *pṛṣṭha* chant; the Abhīvarta is the *brahmasāman*. In the world of Maukṣa is the Svāśira hymn; the Yajñāyajñīya of Śyāvāśva is the *vāravantīya*, with the verse "tvaṃ naścitra ūtyā," as the *agniṣṭomasāman*. (1) Everything else is the same as that of the *gavāmayana* one-day sacrifice. (2)
The Gaurīvita is the *ṣoḍaśin* chant; the *bṛhat* is performed on the verses containing the word "śipiviṣṭa" addressed to Viṣṇu. || 3 ||
All [the days] consist of seventeen [stomas]. || 4 ||

Thus: "Upāsmai davidyutatyā rucā," "ete asṛgramindavaḥ," "taṃ tvā nṛmṇāni bibhratam," and "pavamānasya te kave" constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna*. The distinction is "ṛdhagindo suvastayoḥ," because of the statement that *indu* refers to Soma. "Hotā devo amartyas," "tā naḥ śaktaṃ pārthivasya," "surūpakṛtnumūtaye," "tamīḍiṣva yo arciṣā"—these are the *ājya* verses. "Hotā yajño amartyo" is the *prastāva*.

Because of the statement, "The Hotṛ should say, 'The sacrifice is great; [the sacrifice] of the sacrifice,'" it has been stated specifically in the context of the *Upahavya* sacrifice that, during the recitation of the *ājya* verses, one should not employ the indirect (parokṣa) form of the words "Indra" and "Agni" when saying "the last."

Now follows the midday [pressing]. "Asya pratnām" (of this ancient one) consists of the Gāyatra and the Āmahīyava [Sāmans]. "Parīto ṣiñcatā sutam" (pour out the pressed juice on all sides) is the Samanta [Sāman] on the first [verse]. The Dairghaśravasa [Sāman] is on three [verses]. The Devasthāna [Sāman] is on three [verses]. The Yaudhājaya [Sāman] is on the Adhyāsya [verse]. "Ayaṃ somaḥ" (this Soma) is the Pārtha [Sāman] as the final one. Regarding the sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇā*), the application of the mantras according to their indicative marks (*liṅga*) should be performed in the manner prescribed in the Sūtra.
The Rathantara, Vāmadevya, Abhīvarta, and Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the Gāyatra hymn; "svāśiraḥ" and "arkaḥ pavasva indram accha"—these two single verses belong to Sapha Śrudhi; "purojitī vaḥ" is the Yajñāyajñīya; "andhīgavaḥ"; and "sūryavatīṣu" is the final Kāva hymn—thus [ends] the Ārbhava Pavamāna.

The *Vāravantīya*—beginning with the verse "tvaṃ naścitra ūtyā"—is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. Regarding this, we have already demonstrated in our commentary on the *pratihāra* in the context of the *Vāravantīya* that there are two alternative views: either it consists entirely of *bṛhatī* verses, or it has *kakubh* verses as the final form. Furthermore, in this case, the ritual rules (*dharmas*) pertaining to the *yajñāyajñīya* when it is situated in the *pavamāna* [stotra] are not to be applied; however, those pertaining to the *Vāravantīya* are to be applied. At the time of the *pratihāra*, the wife is to be looked upon. The *sākamaśva*, the *saubhara*, and the *ṭhadvaṃśīya* are the *uktha* chants.

"O Indra, take pleasure [in this]"—this is the Gaurīvita, the *ṣoḍaśi*-sāman. From the inspection of the *ṣoḍaśi* cup up to the consumption from the cups, it is like the *atirātra*. Having performed the rites from the departure up to the invitation (*upahava*) of the sacrificer, [he chants] the *vājapeya*-sāman. The *vājapeya*-sāman.

With the *bṛhat* Vājapeya-sāman, "kimit te viṣṇo," they should chant the praise. For this [sāman], the *triṣṭubh* verses beginning with "viṣṇu" and so forth belong to Bharadvāja. Among the sixteen *stotrīyā* verses, the reading is "bhāiḥ sādā"; on the seventeenth verse, it is "bhāiḥ sadā. According to the statement in the *Nidāna*, "One should not ascend the last [verse]," [the rule applies]. When the *bhakṣa* (draught) has been brought, one should look at it with the formula: "O Śyena, of thee, drunk by Indra, possessed of power, of the *triṣṭubh* metre, belonging to all the *gaṇas*... and then perform the consumption (*bhakṣaṇa*).

One should consume [the soma] with the *triṣṭubh* metre during the *vājapeya-sāman*, according to the scriptural injunction. Now, the rites beginning with the dismissal of the *stoma* and ending with the *udavasānīyā* are performed as in the archetype (*prakṛti*). However, regarding the conclusion of the *vājapeya*, the author of the Sūtra has stated: "It is either not an *atirātra* or it possesses the *ṣoḍaśin* cup. For that sacrifice, the *stotra* should be the *bṛhat* with the seventeen-fold (*saptadaśa*) chant; on its own verses, it should be the fifteen-fold (*pañcadaśa*) chant.

In that rite, having performed [the ritual] without modification up to the consumption of the *ṣoḍaśin* cup, just like the *Jyotiṣṭoma*, and having completed the rites from the exit until the dismissal (*apahava*) of the sacrificer, there is a chanting with the *bṛhatī* verse and the fifteen-fold hymn-form (*pañcadaśastoma*) upon their own [verses]. Some, however, desire the chanting with the *bṛhatī* verse "kimit te" and the seventeen-fold hymn-form (*saptadaśastoma*); the source for this must be sought. All else, moreover, is to be understood from the Sūtra itself. It has been stated that one should finally perform the sacrifice with the *pratyavarohaṇīya*. He now describes the *pratyavarohaṇīya*:

"The Jyotiṣṭoma to be performed for the descent [from the higher world] is prepared. (5) Thus [it is said]. There is the cessation of the Viśvarūpa, the Jyotis-singing, and the Dhur-singing. The remainder is according to the archetype (prakṛti). (5)
Thus concludes the Vājapeya sacrifice. || 13 ||

The Rājasūya. Now follows the Rājasūya. It is described by four sections beginning with "He performs the Agniṣṭoma first. A king should sacrifice with the Rājasūya. It has seven Soma-pressings: the Abhyārohaṇīya, the Abhiṣecanīya, the Daśapeya, the Keśavapanīya, the Vyuṣṭidvirātra, and the Kṣatrasya Dhṛti. On the first day of the bright fortnight of Phālguna, he should undergo initiation for the Abhyārohaṇīya Jyotiṣṭoma. Regarding its arrangement, it is said: "The Abhyārohaṇīya is already established. || 1 ||

Thus [it is said]. The term "Jyotiṣṭoma" is understood to follow. And that [Jyotiṣṭoma] has the Agniṣṭoma as its concluding form (saṃsthā), because of the Vedic revelation: "He performs the Agniṣṭoma first. || 1 ||
Thus ends the Abhyārohaṇīya [rite]. || 141 ||

The Rājasūya consists of the Abhiṣecanīya [sacrifice]. Having performed the Pratyavarohaṇīya, one should sacrifice with the Abhiṣecanīya after a year has passed. Its Brāhmaṇa begins with "Now this is the Abhiṣecanīya," and so forth. He states the arrangement of the Stotras:

"The triplet 'O Vāyu, the bright [Soma] is offered to thee' constitutes the six Saṃbhāryā verses for the Vaiśvajit. (1) Thus: "Upa tvā jāmayo... (RV 8.91.1), "uta naḥ priyā... (RV 8.91.2), "tat savitur vareṇyam" (RV 3.62.10), "somānām svaraṇam" (RV 8.72.14), and "agna āyūṃṣi" (RV 1.189.1)—these six verses are the Saṃbhāryās. They are so called because they are brought together here, having been collected from various locations within the ten Maṇḍalas. (1)

Flow onward as the leader of speech, with a flashing luster! Flow for this Soma, O Indu, you who are the bull, pressed by the ten fingers; your vital energies rise up. O Sage, you are now adorned by the night as you flow on. Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

The *anuṣṭubh* verses beginning with "vāyo śukra" and "adha kṣapā pariṣkṛta" are used; the last verse, "tamasya marjayāmasi," should be made the final one, according to the statement in the *Nidāna*: "We make the middle one the last among these. For the *saṃbhāryā* verses, the deities in order are Agni, Sarasvant, Sarasvatī, Savitṛ, Brahmaṇaspati, and Agni-Pavamāna; for the remaining verses, Soma alone is the deity. In the *rathantara-varṇā*, one should chant twelve syllables, or indeed only four.

One should chant the *abhiṣṭobha* on twelve syllables within the *anuṣṭubh* metre, because of the statement by Śāṇḍilya that "in all cases there are four. The *ājya* hymns belong to the Vaiśvajit. Thus: "Well-kindled, bring [the gods] to us; make them ours," "The [horses] of the earthly one are yoked," "The ruddy, wandering sun," and "Praise him who with his flame"—these are the *ājya* hymns.

"High is the birth of your juice"—this consists of the Gāyatra, the Cāmahīyava, the Jarābodhīya, the Svāra, and the Saindhukṣita; "Pour out the pressed juice on every side"—this consists of the Samanta, the Rathantara, the Dairghaśravasa, the Devasthāna, the Varuṇasāman, the Raurava, and the Yaudhājaya; "The red bull"—this is the Pārtha as the final [sāman]. || 4 ||
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna. It is performed on all sides in the first [turn], and the Yaudhājaya [Sāman] is used in the middle [turn]. 4.
The Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita, and the Kāleya—these are the Pṛṣṭha [Stotras]. || 5 || Thus end the Pṛṣṭhas.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is for the Auksa [family], with the Gāyatra [meter]; "kākṣīvataṃ ca svāśirāmarkaḥ"; "pavasvendramaccha"—these are for the Sapha-Devodāsa [family]; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ"—this is for the Vadhryaśva [family] and the Vaitahavya; and the Soma-sāman, the Trasadasyava, the Āndhīgava, and the Kāva as the last. Thus is the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The *Sapha-daivodāsa* consists of a single verse. (6) The *Yajñāyajñīya* is the *Agniṣṭoma-sāman*. (7)
"O Agni, you are our closest [relative]," "the Satrāsāhīya," "the Saubhara," and "the Udvaṃśīya"—these are the Ukthas.
The Pavamāna stotras consist of thirty-two verses; the Ājya stotras consist of fifteen verses; the Pṛṣṭha stotras consist of seventeen verses; and the Agniṣṭoma is a twenty-one-fold Ukthya. || 8 ||

The *iṣṭāhotrīya* is the *avabhṛtha-sāman*, or [the verse] "sam asya manyave viśaḥ. Because of the statement "the *iṣṭāhotrīya* at the *abhiṣecanīya*, or 'sam asya'... having performed the *abhiṣecanīya* sacrifice, one should not perform its *avabhṛtha* directly; rather, while still consecrated (*dīkṣita*), one should then sacrifice with the *daśapeya* on the tenth day. Between the *abhiṣecanīya* and the *daśapeya*, there are the *saṃsṛp-iṣṭis*. At the conclusion of these, one should invoke the *subrahmaṇyā* formula including the mention of the name.
This is because of the statement: "Between the *abhiṣecanīya* and the *daśapeya*, the mention of the name always occurs. (9)
Thus concludes the consecration ceremony.

The *rājasūya*, the *daśapeya*, and "of Varuṇa when he has pressed [the Soma]"—these and others constitute the *brāhmaṇa* of the *daśapeya*. The *sūtra*, however, states: "Its *brāhmaṇa* is 'ten by ten they approach the cup'"; and "Including the *subrahmaṇya* as the fourth, they should consume from the *udgātṛ*'s cup; six others [should do so]," and so forth.

He states the arrangement of the hymns: "The King is impelled by wisdoms; thee, who bearest manly powers"—these two *ṛc*s, consisting of three and five verses respectively, are placed before the *paryāsa*. The *sadoviśīya* belongs to the place of the *maidhātitha*. The *raurava* belongs to the place of the *maidhātitha*. The *śrāyantīya* is the *brahmasāman*. The *śrudhya* belongs to the place of the *pauṣkala*. The *yajñāyajñīya* belongs to the place of the *śyāvāśva*. The *vāravantīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman* on its own verses. 1.
He draws forth the hymns. || 2 ||
The rest is the same as the one-day fever (ekāhika). || 3 ||
Every [stotra] consists of seventeen verses. || 4 ||
Thus: "Sing for him with a flashing luster; the King proceeds with wisdoms. You, O Sage, who are being purified and who bear manly powers"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, come to us; O Mitra; O Indra and Agni"—these are the *ājya* verses.

The *uccā te gāyatram* and the *cāmahīyavam*; the *abhi somāsa āyavaḥ*, which has two *hiṃkāras*, the *sadoviśīyam*, the *maidhātitham*, the *yaudhājayam*, and the *auśanam* as the last; [the *yaudhājayam*] with two *hiṃkāras* on the first verse and the *yaudhājayam* on the middle verse. The *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] are the *rathantaram*, the *vāmadevyam*, the *śrāyantīyam*, and the *kāleyam*. [The *gāyatra-saṃhitā* is] "svādiṣṭhayā," and the *sapha-śrudhya* consists of the two single verses beginning with "pavasva indram accha."

The *yajñāyajñīya* stotra consists of the verses beginning with "purojitī vo andhasaḥ"; the *āndhīgava* and the *kāva* are the final [stotras]. The *vāravantīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* among its own [verses]. This entire *daśapeya* sacrifice is characterized by the seventeen-fold chant (*saptadaśa*). || 4 ||
Thus ends the Daśapeya sacrifice. || 143 ||

The Rājasūya sacrifice includes the Keśavapanīya, which has the alternative name Pratīcīnastoma. Now, regarding the Keśavapanīya: its Brāhmaṇa states, "In that this Keśavapanīya is a *stoma* directed hitherward (*arvācīna*)," and so forth. One should undergo initiation for the Keśavapanīya after one year has passed. Regarding this, there is a Sūtra stating, "Its [first day] at full moon is an Atirātra," and so on. The Nidāna states: "The subsequent [portion] is the Pratīcīnastoma."

Now the ritual procedure (kalpa): "Flow on as the leader of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the bull, pressed with a flashing luster. These drops have been poured forth; O Soma, you are the brilliant bull; for you are indeed a bull by your radiance—O Sage, of you, the purifying one... || 1 ||
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
We choose Agni as our messenger. 2.
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.
"Pour out the pressed juice on every side"—this [is the *sāman*] for Samanta, Yaśas, Abhīśu, and Yaudhājaya; "The red bull"—this is the final one for Pārtha. || 3 ||
The *pṛṣṭha* is the *bṛhat*. "O Indra, in the onsets," [this is] the *abhīvarta* *brahmasāman*. (4) The rest is the same as for the *āyus* *atirātra*. (5)

Thus it is said. In that regard, the Mādhyandina [school] prescribes: for the first [verse], "uccā te jātam andhasaḥ," they perform the Gāyatra and the Āmahīyava; for the second, "parītoṣiñcatā sutam," they perform the Samanta, the Yaśas, and the Ābhīśava; and the Yaudhājaya. For the third, "vṛṣā śoṇaḥ," they perform the Pārtha as the final [Sāman]. The Samanta is used in the first [verse], and the Yaudhājaya in the middle verse.

The *Bṛhat* and the *Vāmadevya*; "O Indra, in the onsets" (*tvam indra pratūrtiṣu*) [is the *Abhīvarta*]; and "In our own [songs]" (*svāsu*) [is] the *Kāleya*. These are the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras]. The *Gāyatrasaṃhita* is with "Most sweet" (*svādiṣṭhayā*). The *Sapha* and *Pauṣkala* are with "Flow for Indra" (*pavasva indram accha*). The *Śyāvāśva* and *Āndhīgava* are with "With the conquest of your soma-juice" (*purojitī vo andhasaḥ*). The final [stotra] is the *Kāva*. The *Sapha*, *Pauṣkala*, and *Śyāvāśva* are each single-verse [stotras]. The *Yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *Pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*, *Hārivarṇa*, and *Nārmedha* are the *uktha* [stotras]. There is no *ṣoḍaśin*.

In the Āyur-atirātra sacrifice, because that [procedure] is absent, the night and the *saṃdhi* (concluding ceremony) follow the model of the archetype (*prakṛti*). Although the author will later describe the night of this Āyur-atirātra as belonging to the *ahīna* class, nevertheless, since it has not been specifically prescribed within the context of the one-day (*ekāha*) sacrifices, there is no extension (*atideśa*) of its rules here. || 5 ||
He states the arrangement of the Stomas:

the morning pressing has the twenty-one-fold [Stoma], the midday pressing has the seventeen-fold [Stoma], and the third pressing has the fifteen-fold [Stoma]; it includes the Ukthas and the night; the junction is the threefold [Stoma]. || 6 ||
Thus [ends the sixth].
Thus ends the Keśavapanīya sacrifice. || 144 ||
The *rājasūya* consists of the *vyuṣṭi-dvirātra*;

the first day has been described as the *keśavapanīya*. Having performed the *udavasānīyā* sacrifice for that, or having performed the full-moon sacrifice (*paurṇamāsa*), one should undergo initiation (*dīkṣā*) for the *vyuṣṭi-dvirātra*. Regarding this, there is the Brāhmaṇa passage beginning: "He who is consecrated by the *rājasūya* is indeed unstable," and so forth.

The ritual procedure for the first day consists of the Jyotiṣṭoma with the Ājya-stotras and the Bahiṣpavamāna-stotra, as well as the Stomas; now, this is indeed the same as the first day of the two-day rite. || 1 ||

Thus: the *upadrava* and *viparva* are for the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "O Agni, come to us," "O Mitra," and "O Indra and Agni"—these are the *ājya* chants. "High is thy *gāyatra*," and "The *cāmahīyava*" [are used]. "Being purified, O Soma"—with these, the *raurava* and *yaudhājaya* [are employed]. The *auśana* is the final one. The *rathantara*, *vāmadevya*, *naudhasa*, and *kāleya* are the *pṛṣṭha* chants. "With the sweetest [hymn]" is for the *gāyatrahāviṣkṛta*. "Flow on, seeking the gods" and "The beloved, tawny one flows"—with these two single-verse hymns, the *sapha* and *pauṣkala* [are performed].

The *purojitī vaḥ* is the *audala*; the *andhīgava* is the final [stotra] of the *kāva* group; the *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. This day belongs to the *jyotiṣṭoma-stoma*. This day concludes with the consumption of curds (*dadhi*). At night, at the time of carrying around the *vasatīvarī* waters, the *subrahmaṇyā* invocation is performed with the inclusion of the names [of the sacrificer and his wife]. || 1 ||
Thus ends the first day of the Vyuṣṭi-dvirātra sacrifice. || 145 ||
The second day:
For the second day, flow on as the foremost of speech! This immortal god, he goes along the narrow path of thoughts; [bring] to you skill that brings bliss. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
The rule regarding the *ṛcas* and *sūktas* applies by means of mentioning their initial words.

"Agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe"—these are the *ājya* hymns. (2) "Asya pratnāmanudyutam"—this is the *gāyatram*, the *hāviṣkṛtam*, the *jarābodhīyam*, the *carṣabha*, and the *pavamāna*; "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam" is the *samantam*, the *dairghaśravasam*, the *utsedhaḥ*, and "ayaṃ somaḥ" is the final *pārtham*. (3) [Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
"Bṛhat," "Vāmadevyam," "Traiśokam," and "Vaikhānasam"—these are the *pṛṣṭha* hymns. (4)

"parisvāno giriṣṭhā" is the *gāyatra-saṃhitā*; "pavasvendramaccha" is the *satrāsāhīya* and *viśoviśīya*; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhaga" is the *niṣedha*; the *krauñca* is the *yāvāśva*; and "dhartā divaḥ" is the final *arka* of Dīrghatamas. || 5 ||
Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.
The Jyotiṣṭoma is an Atirātra sacrifice accompanied by the Ṣoḍaśin cup.
The Sākamaśva, Saubhara, and Nārmedha are the Ukthas; the Gaurīvita is the Ṣoḍaśin-sāman; and the Rātri and Sandhi [are the Stotras].

Now follows the rule for the *stomas*: the *pavamāna* chants are twenty-four-fold (*caturviṃśa*); the three *ājya* chants are fifteen-fold (*pañcadaśa*); the *acchāvāka*'s chant is seventeen-fold (*saptadaśa*). The three *pṛṣṭha* chants are twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*); the *acchāvāka*'s chant is twenty-seven-fold (*triṇava*); the *agniṣṭoma* is thirty-three-fold (*trayastrimśa*). The *uktha* chants, including the *ṣoḍaśin*, are twenty-one-fold; the night-chant is fifteen-fold; the *saṃdhi* is nine-fold (*trivṛt*). || 8 ||
Thus ends the day concluding with the Udavasānīyā offering. || 8 ||
Thus concludes the Vyuṣṭi-dvirātra sacrifice. || 146 ||

The Rājasūya is the "Support of the Kṣatriya. Having sacrificed with the Vyuṣṭi-dvirātra, if there is available time, one should sacrifice with the Kṣatrasya Dhṛti in that same first fortnight; if there is no available time, one should sacrifice in the subsequent first fortnight. Its ritual procedure is as follows:
the Jyotiṣṭoma has been explained; [this is] the Kṣatrasya Dhṛti. || 1 ||
Thus: neither the one-day sacrifices (*ekāha*) nor the multi-day sacrifices (*ahīna*); the Cāturmāsya offerings and the Rājasūya; and others as well. This third category was stated by Kātyāyana. (1)
Thus is the support of the Kṣatra. 147.
The Rājasūya sacrifice is completed. || 14 ||
Thus ends the second chapter, being the fourth from the beginning, in the *Vivṛti* commentary on the *Ārṣeyakalpa*, composed by Varadarāja, the son of the venerable Vāmanārya.

"Rājā medhābhir īyate," "utte śuṣmāsa īrate"—these two triplets (ṛcas) consisting of five verses each, beginning with "jyotiṣṭomī gāyatrī," and "vṛṣā śoṇaḥ" as the final Pārtha verse; "yo rājā carṣaṇīnām" is the Abhīvarta Brahmasāman. The rest is the same as the first Sāhasra sacrifice. The Pavamāna stotras have seventeen verses, the Ājya stotras have nine, and the Pṛṣṭha stotras have fifteen; the Agniṣṭoma is twenty-one-fold. "Yavaṃ-yavaṃ no andhasā" is the *anurūpa* verse; following the Āmahīyava, the Ābhīka follows the Āndhīgava; the Arkapuṣpa is the same as in the Jyotiṣṭoma. Everything else is ten-by-ten.

This [verse], "eṣa śuṣmy asiṣyadat," is the single verse for the *paryāsa* from the *āmahīyava*; the following [verse], "pavasva madhumattamaḥ," is the *cyāvana* of the *naudhasa*. Among the verses, the *janitra* is "pari pra dhanva"; the *sapha* is "pary ū ṣu"; the *śyāvāśva* is "purojitī vo andhasaḥ. The *āndhīgava* and the *janitra* are the same; the rest is identical to the *jyotiṣṭoma*, with the same *stomas*, and one additional *stotriyā* verse is added at each stage. 513

Between the Raurava and Yaudhājaya [stotras], the Maidhātitha is performed on the verses of the Naudhasa; the Śuddhāśuddhīya is the Brahman-sāman with the word *pad* as its *nidhana*. In the world of the *saṃhita*, there is the Gauṣūkta; for the Pauṣkala, the Aśvasūkta; the Pramāhiṣṭhīya, the Hārivarṇa, and the Śuddhāśuddhīya are performed on their own verses. That which is *aiḍa* is the same as the other. The midday pressing of the Jyotiṣṭoma has twelve [verses]; it is surrounded on both sides by the Trivṛt. 521.

The midday *ājya* chant of the *Punastoma* consists of three *anuṣṭubh*s beginning with "This Pūṣan is wealth, Bhaga," and four *gāyatrī*s. The *pṛṣṭha* chants are those of the *Tīvrasutas*. In the *Jyotiṣṭoma*, the *yajñāyajñīya* follows the *āndhīgava* in the *ārbhava* [laud]. Regarding the verses of the *yajñāyajñīya*: there are six for the *vāravantīya*, six for the *hārivarṇa*, six for the *tairaśca*, and six for the *anubrāhmaṇa*; these are the *stomas*. 522.

The *bahispavamāna* is performed with the four verses beginning "taratsamandī dhāvati. For Indra, the *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* [are used]. Among the verses of the *yajñāyajñīya*, the *vāravantīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *sākamaśva*, *hārivarṇa*, *tairaścya*, and *gaurīvita* are the *ṣoḍaśi-sāman*. The rest is the same as the previous *anubrāhmaṇa* regarding the *stomas*. 523.

The *anurūpa* [verse] is "upo ṣu jātamapturam"; the *ājya* of the Brahman priest is "yajña indramavardhayat"; the *utsedha* is "pibā sutasya rasinaḥ"; the *brahmasāman* consists of two single-verse hymns (*ekarca*), namely the *sapha* and the *valabhi*; in the place of Śyāvāśva’s [hymn], he removes the final *kāva* hymn, "añjata audalam"; the *ukthas* are the same as those of the *āyuṣa* one-day sacrifice (*aikāhika*); the two seventeen-fold chants (*saptadaśa-stoma*) are reversed. 531.

The *bahiṣpavamāna* of the *pratīcīnastoma* [is performed with the thought]: "The sacrifice has strengthened Indra. The *ājya* for the Brahman priest is [performed with] "Drink of the pressed, flavorful [Soma]"; the *niṣedha* is the *brahmasāman*; in the world of the ox is the *valabhit-sapha*; [the *stotra*] is the *satrāsāhīya*. With "This Pūṣan, wealth, Bhaga," [are performed] the *śyāvāśva* and *krauñca* [sāmans]; with "The king, the leader, has been praised," is the final *kāva*. He extracts the *ukthas*; the rest is the same as that of the one-day *gavām-ayana*. The *bahiṣpavamāna* is the twenty-one-fold; the *ājya* of the Hotṛ is performed with three [verses]; the other is the seventeen-fold *saptisaptadaśa*; everything else is the same. 532.

The *bahiṣpavamāna* chant has the *valabhid* [stotra]; both *paryāsa* chants belong to the *abhijit*; the *gāyatrī* [stotra] begins with "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā"; the *bṛhat* [sāman] is used in the Jyotiṣṭoma; the *brahmasāman* is the *yaśas*, beginning with "Tvam indra yaśā asi" from the *saṃhitā*; the *jarābodhīya* follows the *āndhīgava*; the *bharga* is the same as in the first *sahasra-stoma* sacrifice; the *bahiṣpavamāna* is twenty-four-fold (*caturviṃśa*); the *ājya* stotras are threefold (*trivṛt*) and fifteen-fold (*pañcadaśa*); the midday *pavamāna* is twenty-four-fold; the *pṛṣṭha* stotras are seventeen-fold (*saptadaśa*) and twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*); the *ārbhava* is twenty-nine-fold (*triṇava*); and the *agniṣṭoma* is twenty-one-fold. 533.

The *bahiṣpavamāna* is a thousand [verses]. As for the first [day]: after the *mahīyava*, the *uttaramaiḍa* and *sauparṇa* follow; after the *jarābodhīya*, the *svāśira*; after the *ārka*, the *ānuṣṭubha* verses; after these, the *pari pra dhanva*. Among the *dvipadā* verses, the *vāravantīya*; among those containing the word "sūrya," the *kāva* is the last. The rest is the same as before. The *trivṛt* *bahiṣpavamāna*, the *pañcadaśa* *hotṛājya*, two *saptadaśa* [ājyas], the *ekaviṃśa* [ājya] of Acchākāva, the *triṇava* *mādhyaṃdina-pavamāna*, the *chandomas*, the *pṛṣṭhas*, and the *trayastrim̐śa* *ārbhava-pavamāna*; the *agniṣṭoma* is the *ekaviṃśa*. 541.

"High is the birth of thy juice"—this consists of the Gāyatra, the Cāmahīyava, the Jarābodhīya, the Svāra, and the Sauparṇa; the Vrata of Agni; that which precedes the Yaudhājaya; the Raurava in the world of glory; the Śyaita; "With the sweetest, with the most intoxicating"—this consists of the Gāyatra, the Svāśira, and the Ārka; the rest is the same as before. From this point upward, there are six [verses] ascending and six descending. 542.

He extracts the *jyotiṣṭoma* with the *ājya-bahiṣpavamāna* [stotras] beginning with the *jarābodhīya*. For the Vājapeya, the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] consist of the *rathaṃtara* and *raurava* [sāmans]. [The verses] "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" are used: the *audala* on one verse, the *āndhīgava* on one verse, and the *śyāvāśva* on one verse; the *bṛhat* on three verses. The rest is the same as the previous [rite]. The *bahiṣpavamāna* is the *trivṛt*; the three *ājya* [stotras] are *pañcadaśa*; the *maitrāvaruṇa* is *trivṛt*; the midday *pavamāna* is *caturviṃśa*; the three *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] are *saptadaśa*; the *maitrāvaruṇa* is *pañcadaśa*; the *ārbhava* is *saptadaśa*; and the *agniṣṭoma* is *ekaviṃśa*. 543.

With the verse *punaṇaḥ soma dhārayā*, the Raurava is [the Brahman’s chant] on three verses; the Sadoviśīya on one verse; the Viṣṭārapaṅkti on all [verses]; the Yaudhājaya on three verses; the Abhīvarta is the Brahman’s chant; with the verse *purojitī vo andhasaḥ*, the Gaurīvitam is on one verse; the Āndhīgavam on one verse; the Śyāvāśvam on one verse; and the Bṛhat on three verses. The Mādhyandina Pavamāna is the seventeen-fold (saptadaśa); the rest is the same as in the Jyotiṣṭoma, with the same Stomas. 551.

"Sing forth to him, O men"—this triplet is the *ṣaṭsaṃbhāryā* for the *vaiśvajit*. "Flow on, the foremost of speech"; "Flow on, O Indu, as a bull, pressed"; "With flashing luster"; "The drops have been poured out for thee"; "O Soma, thou art a bull, thou art resplendent; for thou art indeed a bull by thy radiance"; "Him, the ten fingers [prepare]"; "Of thee, the purifying one"; "We [worship] thee, the purifying one, O sage"; "Being purified, O Soma, in thy stream"—these are the *bṛhatī*s; the rest is the same as for the *abhiṣecanīya*. The entire [rite] consists of thirty-six [verses]. That which belongs to the *jyotiṣṭoma* also belongs to the *marutstoma*.
The *anubrāhmaṇa* for the *bṛhaspatisava* and the *kulāya* sacrifice dedicated to Indra and Agni, as well as the *stomas*, [are described here]. 554

"O Indu, flow for Indra accompanied by the Maruts; O Indu, you are the pressed bull; O Soma, you are brilliant, for you are indeed a bull by your radiance. Who is worthy of praise and homage for you, O Pavamāna, when the sun has risen? To Indra alone the singers sing loudly. To Indra and Agni be great homage! 'High is the birth of your juice'—this is the Gāyatra and the Āmahīyava. 'For you, O Soma, I have rejoiced'—this is the Samanta and the Yaudhājaya. 'The red bull'—this is the final Pārtha. And upon the Revatī verses are the Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, and the Śyaita."

The *kāleya* is with the verses "svādiṣṭhayā" and "madiṣṭhayā"; the *gāyatramaukṣa* is with "pavasva indram accha"; the *sapha* is with "śrudhye"; the *parityam haryatam hari* is the *śyāvāśvāndhīgava*; the final [laud] is on verses containing the word "sūrya," belonging to Kava; the *yajñāyajñīya*, the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*, is with the verse "pra daivodāso agniḥ" on its own [verses]; the *satrāsāhīya* is [on its own verses]; the *saubhara* is with the verse "tava tyad indriyaṃ bṛhat" on its own [verses]; the *udvaṃśīya* is [on its own verses]. The entire [stoma] is the fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*). 56.

"Flow on as the leader of speech; sing for him, O men! For you, O sage, who are being purified—'We choose Agni as our messenger'—these are the two *ājya* hymns. 'O Soma, purifying yourself with your stream,' [is the *sāman*]: the *raurava* on one verse, the *yaudhājaya* on one, the *dairghaśravasa* on one, the *rathantara* on three verses, and the *bṛhat* as the *pṛṣṭha*. The *śyaita* is the *ṛk* for the *abhīvarta*, which is the *brahmasāman*; the rest is the same as in the *jyotiṣṭoma*. The *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* *stomas* alternate. (571)

In his own [laudatory verses], the Śyaita follows the Saṃhitā; the Jarābodhīya follows the Śrudhya in its world; the Viśoviśīya follows the Āndhīgava; the Soma-sāman is the Tharvaṇa; and the other is the Vāsamāna. With the first thousand [verses], there are two Trivṛt lauds, two Dvādaśas, two Pañcadaśa and Saptadaśas, two Ekaviṃśa and Navadaśas, two Caturviṃśas, and two Triṇavas. 572.

Flow on as the leader of speech; sing to him, O men! To you, O Sage, who are being purified—homage to you, O Agni, for your power! We invoke Mitra; we call upon the clans for his wrath. I call those two for whom this ancient, primordial, and praiseworthy nectar exists. In these two *satobṛhatī* verses, there is the *gāyatra* melody in three [verses], the *āmahīyava* in one, the *aiḍa-sauparṇa* in one, and the *satrāsāhīya* in one. In whichever single verse remains, there is the *sadoviśīya* melody. [The verse begins: "O Soma, being purified, flow with your stream..."

The *raurava* on one [verse], the *yaudhājaya* on one, the *samanta* on one, and the *rathantara* on three; then the *utsedha* with "These two worlds, O Pavamāna"; the *pārtha* as the final [verse] with "This Soma"; the *bṛhat* and the *vāmadevya*; the *śyaita* with "That indeed was the eldest among beings"; the *kāleya* on its own verses; the *gāyatra* with "With the sweetest, most intoxicating [juice]" on three [verses]; the *saṃhita* on one; the *surūpa* on one; the *svāśira* and the *arka* on one; and [the verse] "Flow for Indra."

In the *saphaviśoviśīya*, [one should chant] "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" as the *gaurīvita* on one verse, the *śyāvāśva* on one verse, and the *āndhīgava* on one verse; the *madhuścunnidhana* on three verses; the *sumanmā vasvī rantī sunarī* as the *vāravantīya* on three verses; and the *kāvamantya* as the *yajñāyajñīya* *agniṣṭoma-sāman* on three verses. There are two *trivṛt* stotras, two *dvādaśa* stotras, two *pañcadaśa* and *saptadaśa* stotras, two *navadaśa* and *caturviṃśa* stotras, two *caturviṃśa* and *ekaviṃśa* stotras, and two *triṇava* stotras. (58)

The *śyena* [sāman] has the *ājyabahiṣpavamāna* as its *ṛc*: "O Soma, most brilliant... (Soma 9.64.1). The *gāyatra* [sāman] belongs to Vārṣāhara; "Being purified, O Soma, in your stream... (Soma 9.101.1) is the *vaiyaśva*. There is a *vaṣaṭkāranidhana* on one verse, the *raurava* on one verse, the *yaudhājaya* on three verses, and the *auśana* as the final one. Then there are the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *saptaha*, and the *kāleya*. "That exhilaration of yours which is most excellent" (Soma 9.101.3) is the *gāyatra* belonging to Vārṣāhara. The *satrāsāhīya* is "Flow for Indra... (Soma 9.101.1). For Pagu it is "By your power, O juice... (Soma 8.91.2).

The *nānadā* [is used] for the *dhīgava*; of the three *sāmans*, the first is the *kāva*, the last is the *yajñāyajñīya* as the *agniṣṭomasāman*; there are two *trivṛt* stotras, two *dvādaśa*, two *pañcadaśa*, two *ekaviṃśa*, two *caturviṃśa*, and two *triṇava*. 591.

"Flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull; driving away the adversaries, he flows"—from this triplet at the beginning of the *paryāsa*, he extracts the *satrāsāhīya*. [He places] the *purojitī vaḥ andhasaḥ* on one verse; on that same [verse], the *nānada*; on that same [verse], the *andhīgava*; on one [verse], the *śyāvāśva*; on one [verse], the *sāman* for three [verses]: the *pramāhiṣṭhīya*, the *aupagava*, and the *udvaṃśīya*. The *mahānāmnīs* and the *ṣoḍaśisāman* are the same as in the previous [rite]. The entire Jyotiṣṭoma is arranged with fifteen [stotras]; it is for the sake of peace, for the sake of peace. 592 Vivṛti. Fifth Chapter.

Now, the one-day sacrifices (*ekāha*) to be described hereafter are generally designated as *dvandva* (paired) because they consist mostly of pairs. Now, this *rāṭ* sacrifice: that which was called *rāṭ* by the section beginning with "yo rājā" (The king...), its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows: "The king approaches with prayers; your powers rise up"—these three verses and five [additional] verses are placed before the *paryāsa*. The *gāyatrī* verses belong to the *jyotiṣṭoma*; "vṛṣā śoṇaḥ" is the final verse of the *pārtha* hymn. (1) "yo rājā carṣaṇīnām" is the *abhīvarta*, the *brahmasāman*. (2)
The rest is the same as with the first thousand-fold [offering]. ||3||
Thus: "Flow on as the leader of speech, with flashing luster; the King is approached with sacred hymns. "Your vital strengths rise up, O Pavamāna, you the wise one"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, come hither; we [invoke] Mitra; Indra indeed, O singers; in Indra, O Agni"—these are the *ājya* verses.

"Uccā te jātamandhasaḥ" is the Gāyatra and the Āmahīyava; "parītoṣiṣam" is for the first [verse]; the Rathantara is for three [verses]; and the Dairghaśravasa as well; the Yaudhājaya is for the middle [verse]; and "vṛṣā śoṇaḥ" is the final Pārtha.
The Bṛhat and the Vāmadevya; "He who is the king of the peoples" is the Abhīvarta; "In one's own [songs], the Kāleya"—these are the Pṛṣṭhas.

The *gāyatra-saṃhitā* is [performed] with the verse beginning "svādiṣṭhayā"; the *sapha-śrudhya* consists of the two single verses beginning "pavasvendramacchā"; the *śyāvāśva-andhīgava* consists of the verse beginning "purojitī"; the final [laud] is the *kāva* among those containing the word "sūrya"; and the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* is the *yajñāyajñīya*. || 3 ||
Now follows the arrangement of the Stomas: the Pavamāna lauds are seventeenfold; the Ājya lauds are threefold; the Pṛṣṭha lauds are fifteenfold;
the Agniṣṭoma is twenty-onefold. || 4 ||
Thus [ends the fourth section].
Thus [ends] the king. ||1||
Now, this Virāj is declared by the Anuvāka beginning with "virāṭ. Its ritual application (kalpa) is as follows:
"yavaṃ-yavaṃ no andhasaḥ" is the *anurūpa* [verse]. Following the *āmahīyava*, there is the *ābhīka*; following the *āndhīgava*, there is the *arkapuṣpa*. ||1||
The rest is the same as the Jyotiṣṭoma; everyone is entitled to perform it. ||2||
Thus: "Upāsmai yavam-yavam naḥ andhasaḥ pavamānasya te kave" is the Bahiṣpavamāna [Stotra].
"O Agni, come hither for the sake of Mitra," and "O Indra and Agni"—these are the *ājya* verses.

The *gāyatra*, *cāmahīyava*, and *abhīka* [are to be used] for the verse "uccā te"; the *raurava* and *yaudhājaya* for the purifying Soma; the *auśana* as the final [verse]; and the *auśanayaudhājaya* for the two triplets (*tṛca*). The others consist of single verses (*ekarca*). In every case, the final [verse] occurs when the *stoma* is possible. If the second [verse] is in a triplet, it is to be sung in the forest (*araṇyegeya*), according to the rule: "In its absence, that which is prior to the final [verse]. The *gāyatra*, *cāmahīyava*, and *abhīka* are *sāman*-triplets; for there is the rule: "Three [verses] in a single triplet, on different *stotrīyā* verses."
The Rathantara, Vāmadevya, Naudhasa, and Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha [stotras].

The *gāyatra-saṃhitā* consists of the verse beginning with "svādiṣṭhayā. The *sapha-pauṣkala* consists of the verse beginning with "pavasvendramacchā. The *śyāvāśva*, *āndhīgava*, *arkapuṣpa*, and *kāva* consist of the verses beginning with "purojitī," with the *kāva* being the last. With the exception of the last, these are single-verse hymns (*ekarcāḥ*). In the *anuṣṭubh* meters, there are triplets for the *sāman*. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. All the *stotras* consist of ten verses. He utters the *hiṃ* call over three verses. He utters the *hiṃ* call over four verses in succession. He utters it over one, then two, then one; he utters the *hiṃ* call over three verses.

"Sa parācībhiḥ" is the *viṣṭuti* consisting of ten verses. Regarding this, it has been stated: "In the ten-verse [stoma], there is a fourfold [repetition] in the middle, with the [verses] revolving around it on both sides. (2)
Thus ends the Virāj. 2.

The *Aupaśada* [stotra]: now, this *Aupaśada* is described by the section beginning with "This *Aupaśada*. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows: before the *Paryāsa*, there is one verse beginning with "Thou art the swiftest, thou hast flowed" (*eṣa śuṣmyasiṣyadat*). After the *Āmahīyava*, there is the *Cyāvana* hymn beginning with "Flow on, most rich in honey" (*pavasva madhumattama*). Among the verses of the *Naudhasa*, there is the *Janitra*. The *Sapha* hymn begins with "He runs around" (*pari pradhanva*). The *Śyāvāśva* hymn begins with "Around indeed" (*paryūṣu*). And the *Āndhīgava* hymn, which is also a *Janitra*, begins with "For the sake of victory over you through the soma-juice" (*purojitī vo andhasaḥ*). ||1||
The rest is the same as the Jyotiṣṭoma with respect to the *stomas*; one additional *stotrīyā* verse is added at each stage. ||2||
Thus: "Upāsmai davidyutatyā rucā," "eṣa śuṣmyasiṣyadat," and "pavamānasya te kave"—these are for the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, come to us for Mitra," and "Indra and Agni"—these are the *ājya* [offering verses].

"High is thy Gāyatra and the Cāmahīyava; flow, O most honey-sweet"—this is the Cyāvāna [stotra]. "Being purified, O Soma, hold fast thy stream"—this is the Raurava and Yaudhājaya [stotras]. The Auśana is the last. The Cyāvāna is in one verse. Here, at the midday pressing, there is a single-verse Kakubh; this is because of the statement "in that [verse]."
The Rathantara, Vāmadevya, and Naudhasa are the sources among the Ṛks; the Kāleya is [the source] among its own [verses]. These are the Pṛṣṭha [stotras].

The *svādiṣṭhayā* [verse] belongs to the *gāyatra-saṃhitā*; the *pari pra dhanva indramaccha* [verse] belongs to the *sapha-pauṣkala*; the *paryūṣu* [verse] belongs to the *śyāvāśva*; and the *purojitī* [verse] belongs to both the *āndhīgava* and the *janitra*. The final [verse] belongs to the *kāva*. The *sapha*, *pauṣkala*, and *śyāvāśva* verses consist of single stanzas (*ekarca*); the *pari pra dhanva* [verse] consists of two feet (*dvipadā*). The *paryūṣu* [verse] is an *anuṣṭubh* with a "middle like an ant" (*pipīlikāmadhyā*). Among the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras], the *janitra* comes first; however, in the *ārbhava* [pavamāna], it is the last. This has been stated in the *Upagrantha*: "In the case of the nine-versed and seventeen-versed [stomas], the *janitra* comes first; elsewhere than this, it follows the sequence."

The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The meaning of the statement "each *stotrīyā* verse increases by one" is as follows: in the stotras beginning with the *bahiṣpavamāna* and ending with the *yajñāyajñīya*, the stomas of the Jyotiṣṭoma are to be performed with an increase of one *stotrīyā* verse at each stage. Consequently, this is the arrangement of the stomas: the *bahiṣpavamāna* has ten verses; the *ājya* stotras have sixteen; the Mādhyandina-pavamāna has sixteen; the *pṛṣṭha* stotras have eighteen; the Ārbhava-pavamāna has eighteen; and the *agniṣṭoma* [sāman] has twenty-two.

In that regard, the *viṣṭuti* of the sixteenth [day] is as follows: he utters the *hiṃ* for five verses—three times, once, and once; then he utters the *hiṃ* for six verses—twice, once, and three times. Because [the verses] are greater by one than those of the ten-night rite (*daśarātra*), one should therefore insert [the additional verses] in the final round (*paryāya*) of the preceding [day], because of the statement: "But they are the abodes of the Brahman. Gautama says that one should insert the eighteenth [verse] into the seventeenth. Dhānaṃjayya says it should be done according to the established rule.

In that regard, according to the *āvāpa* (insertion) method, by means of the *garbhiṇī* praise, one should perform the *hiṅkāra* chant eight times in the final round (*paryāya*), arranging it thus: "He chants with two, he chants with three, he chants with three. This constitutes the state of having equal rounds, which is prescribed by rule. According to the other method, one chants six times: "He chants with three, he chants with two, he chants with one"; he chants six times: "He chants with one, he chants with three, he chants with two"; he chants six times: "He chants with two, he chants with one, he chants with three"—this is the *viṣṭuti* (specific arrangement of chanting) in that alternative method.

In the last *paryāya* of the twenty-second *saptinī*, one should insert the following *viṣṭuti*: "He chants the *hiṃkāra* over eight verses: three of them with three verses, one with one verse, and [the remaining] three with three verses. (2)
Thus ends the section on the Aupaśada [oblation]. ||3||

Furthermore, Āpastamba has described the *Sarvatomukha* sacrifice immediately after the *Aupaśada*: "One who desires, 'May I become this entire world,' should sacrifice with the *Sarvatomukha*. The Gārhapatya fire is in the center; the sacrificial enclosures (*vihāra*) pertaining to Soma are in every direction. A *Trivṛt* [stoma] is in the eastern direction; a *Pañcadaśa* to the south; a *Saptadaśa* to the west; and a *Ekaviṃśa* to the north."

And those four forms, beginning with the *trivṛt*, are to be performed over four days of the six-day rite (*ṣaḍaha*) which has the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* as its *pṛṣṭha* chants, because of the connection with the *stomas*. For it is only where there is the completion of the six-day rite that the *vairūpa* and other chants are employed; however, in the case of deficiency, only the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* are used alternately. Thus says the author of the *Kalpa*: "In the *caturvīra* and other rites, he arranges [the ritual] by means of the *pṛṣṭha* consisting solely of the *bṛhat* and *rathantara*, but not the *vairūpa* and others, according to possibility. And the author of the *Nidāna* says:

Now, this [sacrifice] has four heroes and the Bṛhat and Rathantara as its Pṛṣṭha-stotras; for they do not experience the [stotras] belonging to the six-day period (ṣaḍaha), nor has anyone else deprived them. And regarding the Chandomas, he says: "The Bṛhat and Rathantara are the Pṛṣṭhas; for they do not experience the ṣaḍaha-stotras, nor has anyone deprived them. Furthermore, he will later prescribe the six-day period with the Bṛhat and Rathantara as its Pṛṣṭhas, known by the name *pṛṣṭhya-stoma*. Consequently, the four faces of this [sacrifice] are to be performed by means of the four days of the *pṛṣṭhya-stoma*.

Therein, the arrangement of the first face is as follows: "Sing unto him, O men; sing unto him who is born, the swift one"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna chant, beginning with "O Sage, of you, the purifying one."
The *ājya* offerings are: "O Agni, come to us," and "O Indra and Agni."

"O Soma juices, wise ones..."—this Gāyatra [Sāman] is for the first [verse]; "The brown ones toward the wooden vats..."—this Āśva [Sāman] is for the second; "Pressed for Indra, for Vāyu..."—this Somasāman is for the third; "O Soma, forth for the feast of the gods..."—this Yaudhājaya [Sāman] is for all three; "Run forth indeed..."—this Auśana is the final one.
The Rathantara, Vāmadevya, Naudhasa, and Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha [stotras].

"pra somāso madacyutaḥ"—this Gāyatra hymn is for the first [verse]; the Saṃhita is on that same verse. "ayā pavasva devayuḥ" and "pavate haryato hariḥ"—these two single-verse hymns are with the Sapha and Kṣāra chants. "pra sunvanāya"—this Audala hymn is for the first [verse]; the Gautama and Kava hymns are on that same verse, the latter being for the final three verses.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*; all the *stotras* are *trivṛt*.

"Flow on as the leader of speech; flow on, O Indu, as a bull, for you, O Soma, are indeed a bull"—with these words [they perform] the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant. For even the subsequent sections (*mukha*), the *bahiṣpavamāna* praise takes place outside [the sacrificial ground], because it is prescribed in the context of the one-day sacrifice (*ekāha*) and because there is no difference in the time [of performance].

"agnir dūtam," "mitram vayam," and "indram id gāthinaḥ"—these four verses [are used]. The Ājya offerings consist of the verses beginning with "indre agnā. From the four-verse hymn, the last verse is omitted.

"Flow as a bull, O stream"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *yauktāśva*. "Being purified, O Soma, flow with a stream"—this is the *aiḍa* with three *nidhanas* belonging to Āyāsya. "The red bull"—this is the final hymn of the Vasiṣṭhas; some, however, desire the *pārtha*.
And the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *mādhucchandasa* are the *pṛṣṭha* stotras.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *hāviṣmat*. "pavasvendramaccha"—these two single verses belong to the *śaṅkusujñāna*. "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"—this is the first of the *āsitāt*. The *krauñca* occurs in three verses. "vṛṣā matīnām"—this is the final *yāma*.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.

"Sākamaśvam" (with the horse); "evā hi" (even so indeed) is the Āmahīyava; "indraṃ viśvā" (Indra with all [powers]) is the Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra; and "pūrvam" (the first) are the Ukthas. The entire [stotra] is the Pañcadaśa. Now, for the third [day]:

"davidyutatyā rucā" (with flashing brilliance), "ete asṛgramindavaḥ" (these drops have been poured forth), "rājā medhābhirīyate" (the King goes with the songs of wisdom), and "taṃ tvā nṛmṇāni bibhratam iṣe pavasva dhāraya" (you, bearing manly powers, flow for nourishment, O stream)—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"With Agni as Agni, I invoke Mitra; with Indra, I invoke them"—these are the *ājya* verses.

"uccā te jātamandhasaḥ"—this is the Gāyatra and the Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha. "abhi somāsa āyavaḥ"—in the first [verse], the Paurumadga; in the [next] three, the Gautama; in the [next] three, the Antarikṣa; in the Adhyāsyā, the Āṣkāraṇidhana. "tisro vācaḥ"—the last is the Krośa of the Aṅgirases.
The Rathantara and the Vāmadevya; "vayaṃ gha tvā" is the Mahāvaiṣṭambha; "taraṇiritsiṣāsati" is the Raurava—these are the Pṛṣṭhas.

"Tisro vāca udīrate" contains both the Gāyatra and the Pāṣṭhauha [Sāmans]. "Ā sotā pari ṣiñcatasakhāya ā niṣīdata" contains the Vācaḥ Sāman, the Śaukta, and the Ekarca. "Sutāso madhumattama" contains the two Tvaṣṭrī Sāmans, beginning with the Svāra and ending with the Atriṇidhana. "Pavitraṃ te" is the final [Sāman], the Ariṣṭa.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.
The *pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *tairaścya* are the *ukthas*. Every [stoma] is seventeenfold (*saptadaśa*).

Now, for the fourth [stotra], [the verse] "The purifying Pavamāna has brought them forth; purifying himself, he has stepped forward, hastening like eager cows; flow swiftly, O thou of lofty thought; the rays impel the Sun"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"May Agni strike down the Vṛtras; this Indra [is] for you two, O Mitra and Varuṇa, with the bones of Dadhyañc; this [is] for you two from my own mind"—these are the *ājya* verses.

"Pavasva dakṣasādhanaḥ"—this is the Gāyatra, the Ātharvaṇa, and the Nidhanakāma. "Tavāhaṃ soma rāraṇa"—this is the Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra, the Ābhīśava, the Svarpṛṣṭha, and the Aṅgirasa. "Somaḥ pavate janitram" is the final [hymn].
The *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *traiśoka*, and the *pṛśni* are the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].

"Pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ" is the Gāyatra and the Aurṇāyava; "tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya somaḥ punānaḥ ūrmiṇā" is the Bṛhat and the Kātīṣādīya; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Nānada and the Āndhīgava; and "pra ta aśvinīḥ" is the Lauśa as the final [verse].
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
"O Agni, for you who increase"—this is the Saindhukṣita; "We indeed [choose] you"—this is the Saubhara;
"This one, O Indra"—and "The beloved of Vasiṣṭha"—these are the Ukthas.

"Pratyasmai pipīṣate" is the Gaurīvita, the *ṣoḍaśin* *sāman*. For the author of the ritual manual (*kalpakāra*) will state regarding the *pṛṣṭhya* sacrifice: "For the fourth day, 'pratyasmai pipīṣate' is the Gaurīvita, the *ṣoḍaśin* *sāman*. And the author of the *Sūtra* says: "And it departs at the departure of the *virāj*, and [it departs] in other cases as well. The learned say that the first [day] is like the *catuṣṭoma*; he states that its four faces should be performed by means of the *jyotiṣṭoma* itself, with the *rathantara-pṛṣṭha* and according to the arrangement of the *stomas*. The arrangement of the *stomas* beginning with the *trivṛt* will be explained in the context of the *viśvasṛjām ayana*.

Now, the *punastoma* has been described by the section beginning with "athaiṣa punastomaḥ. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows: between the *raurava* and the *yaudhājaya*, there is the *maidhātitha*. Among the verses of the *naudhasa*, the *śuddhāśuddhīya* is the *brahmasāman* which has its *nidhana* on the word *pad*. In the *loka* of the *saṃhita*, there is the *gauṣūkta*. There is the *aśvasūkta* of the *pauṣkala*.
