The *pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *śuddhāśuddhīya* are performed on their own verses (*svasu*), while the *yadaiḍa* is performed on its own verses. ||1||
The rest is the same as the Jyotiṣṭoma. ||2||

Thus [it is said]. The *bahis-pavamāna* consists of the verses beginning with "upāsmai gāyatā naraḥ" and "punānaḥ somadhārayā. The *ājya* hymns consist of "agna ā yāhi," "no mitrāvaruṇā," and "indrāgnī. For the *gāyatra*, "uccā te jātamandhasaḥ"; for the *cāmahīyava*, "punānaḥ soma dhārayā. In the first [turn], the *raurava*; in the second, the *maidhātitha*; in the third, the *yaudhājaya*; and at the end, the *auśana*. According to the statement that "three [sāmans] may occur in either [turn] when possible," the *bṛhatī* is treated as a single verse. The *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, and the *śuddhāśuddhīya*—the latter having its *nidhana* on the word "pada" within the verses of the *naudhasa*—[are likewise applied].

The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are: "svāsu kāleyam" for the Gāyatra-Goṣūkta; "pavasvendramaccha" for the Sapha-Pauṣkala; and "purojitī vaḥ" for the Śyāvāśva-Āndhīgava. The last [stotra] belongs to Kava; with the exception of the Kava, they consist of single verses.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The *Pramahiṣṭhīya*, the *Hārivarṇa*, the *Śuddhāśuddhīya*, and [the hymn] beginning with "svāsu yadaiḍam"—these are the *ukthas*. 3.
Now follows the arrangement of the Stomas:
the midday pressing consists of twelve [verses]; it is surrounded on both sides by the Trivṛt.

Thus: the entire morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*) is *trivṛt*; the meaning is that the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina-savana*) and the third pressing (*tṛtīya-savana*) are also *trivṛt*. This is the *viṣṭuti* (mode of chanting) for the twelve-fold hymn (*dvādaśa-stoma*). He utters *hiṃ* four times: he [chants] with two [verses], he with one, he with one; he utters *hiṃ* four times: he with one, he with two, he with one; he utters *hiṃ* four times: he with one, he with one, he with two. At the places of insertion (*āvāpa-sthāna*), there are double repetitions of the *iṣṭāva* (recitation). As it has been said: "In the twelve-fold [stoma], at the places where the triplets (*ṛca-bhāga*) stand, there are double repetitions of the *iṣṭāva*; or else, at the places of insertion. (4)
Thus ends the *punastoma*. 4.

The first is the Catuṣṭoma; the former Catuṣṭoma has been described by the section beginning with "Now this is the Catuṣṭoma," while the latter is described by the section beginning with "Now that which has four stotras. These two are known as the Gautama Catuṣṭomas in other sūtras. The ritual procedure for the former of these two is as follows:

He makes three *anuṣṭubh*s—"This Pūṣan, wealth, Bhaga"—and four *gāyatrī*s. The *ājya* [laud] of the *punastoma* is the midday [service]. The *pṛṣṭha* [lauds] are for the *tīvrasut*. The *ārbhava* [laud] is the *jyotiṣṭoma*. The *uttara-yajñāyajñīya* is the *āndhīgava*. For the verses of the *yajñāyajñīya*, there are six [verses] with the *vāravantīya*, six with the *sākamaśva*, six with the *hārivarṇa*, and six with the *tairaścya*; these are the *brāhmaṇastomas*. 1.

Thus: "This is Pūṣan," etc.—these are three *anuṣṭubh* verses. With these three, using three feet [from each], one should form four *gāyatrī* verses. They are as follows: "This is Pūṣan, wealth, fortune" (*ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ*); "He has looked upon both heaven and earth" (*vi yakhyad rodasī ubhe*); "The Soma-drops create a path" (*somāsaḥ kṛṇvate pathaḥ*); "O Pavamāna, for the sake of glory" (*pavamāna śravasyave*). The first verse is the *retasyā*; the last is characterized by the *rathantara*. This is the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant.
"O Agni, come to us for Mitra," and "O Indra and Agni"—these are the *ājya* [offerings].
"uccā te gāyatram" and "cāmahīyavam"; while being purified, [he recites] "so rauravam", "maidhātitham", and "yaudhājayam"—these are the triplets of Sāmans; "auśanam" is the final one.
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Śrāyantīya, and the Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha [stotras].

*svādiṣṭhayā* is the *gāyatra-saṃhitā*; *pavasvendramacchā* consists of two single-verse hymns, the *sapha* and the *pauṣkala*; *purojitī vaḥ* is the *śyāvāśva* and the *āndhīgava*; the last [hymn] belongs to Kava.

With the four triplets beginning with *yajñāyajñā vo agnaye* and *taṃ te śrudhi*, the Agniṣṭoma-sāman is performed with six stotrīyā verses using the Vāravantīya chant. In the first two *yajñāyajñīya* [verses], Agni is the deity; in the latter two, Indra. The arrangement of the Stomas is according to the Anubrāhmaṇa: the Bahiṣpavamāna is performed with four verses; the Ājya-stotras with eight each; the Mādhyandina-pavamāna consists of twelve verses; the Pṛṣṭha-stotras consist of sixteen verses each; and the Ārbhava-pavamāna consists of twenty verses.

"The Agniṣṭoma is twenty-fourfold. In the two Catuṣṭomas, four rounds (paryāyas) are to be performed. Therein is the *viṣṭuti* of the Aṣṭi-stoma: "He utters *hiṃ* with two [verses]. He utters *hiṃ* with the first; he utters *hiṃ* with two; he utters *hiṃ* with the middle one; he utters *hiṃ* with the last—this is according to the *brahmāyatana* view. However, according to the *kṣatrāyatana* view, there are two rounds in the middle.

As it has been said: "If there are two turns (*paryāya*) in the first [set] of four, one should perform the *brahmāyatanīyā* [chanting]; if they are in the middle [set], the *kṣatrāyatanīyā*, and likewise the eight [syllables]. But its turns are in pairs. In that case, having placed the first and second turns in the positions belonging to those respective *ṛc*-portions, one should place the third turn to the north of the second turn with two *kuśa* blades whose tips point westward. Regarding the final turn...

In the very place where the *tṛca* division stands, there is the final *paryāya*. Thus, in all four *paryāyas*, it is the place for the arrangement of the *kuśā* verses. Now, regarding the sixteenth [laud]: he utters the *hiṃ* over four [verses]; he [chants] with two, with one, and with one. He utters the *hiṃ* over four; he [chants] with one, with two, and with one. He utters the *hiṃ* over four; he [chants] with one, with two, and with one. He utters the *hiṃ* over four; he [chants] with one, with one, and with two.

In the *ṣoḍaśin* there are four [stotras], each consisting of twelve verses; among these, the two middle ones are similar. Now, regarding the *caturviṃśa*: he chants the *hiṃ* syllable six times—twice for one verse and twice for another—this is the first round (*paryāya*). The other three are likewise. In that regard, in the *yajñātṛca*, the first round consists of each individual *stotrīyā* verse being repeated twice. The other rounds are formed in the same manner with the other *tṛcas*. As it has been said: "In the *caturviṃśa*, there are four rounds of six, with the *dvikaviṣṭāva* chant."

Regarding the phrase "four *ṛc*s in separate *ṛc*s": here, the alternative methods for the *viṣṭuti* of the *aṣṭin* and *caturviṃśa* [stomas], as stated in the Sūtra, have not been written down here for fear of prolixity. ||1||
Thus ends the first Catuṣṭoma. || 5 ||
The second [section] states the subsequent fourfold stoma:

the *bahiṣpavamāna* is performed with the four verses beginning "tarat sa mandī dhāvati"; the *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* [sāmans] are for Indra accompanied by the Maruts; the *vāravantīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* among the verses of the *yajñāyajñīya*; the *sākamaśva*, *hārivarṇa*, and *tairaśca* [are used]; and the *gaurīvita* is the *ṣoḍaśi-sāman*. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as before; the Stomas are according to the Anubrāhmaṇa. || 2 ||

Thus: "The *taratsamandī* rushes on"—this four-verse hymn is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. The *ājya* stotras are "O Agni, come to us," "O Mitra," and "Indra and Agni. The *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* are for Indra accompanied by the Maruts; "being purified, he... is the *raurava* and the *maidhātitha*; the *yaudhājaya* and the *auśana* are the last. The *auśana* alone is for a triplet; the remaining verses are single-verse hymns.
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Śrāyantīya, and the Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras.

The *svādiṣṭhayā* verses are for the *gāyatra-saṃhitā*; the *pavasvendramacchā* verses are for the *sapha-pauṣkala*; the *purojitī vaḥ* verses are for the *śyāvāśva-andhīgava*. These are the *yajñāyajñīya* verses. The final [verse] belongs to Kava; the two triplets (*tṛca*) belong to Kava and the *yajñāyajñīya*; the others consist of single verses (*ekarca*). When the *stoma* is possible, the entire final [section] is in triplets. If the second [section] is to be sung in the forest (*araṇyegeya*), then in its absence, that which precedes the final [verse] is used, according to the scriptural injunction. Regarding the *ṛks* of the *yajñāyajñīya*, the *vāravantīya*, the *agniṣṭomasāman*, the *sākamaśva*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *tairaśca* are the *ukthas*. The *gaurīvita* is the *ṣoḍaśisāman*.

Now, there are four hymns (*stotra*), which are the *stoma*s prescribed in the Brāhmaṇa beginning with "by means of four," as follows: the *bahiṣpavamāna*; the three *ājya* [stotras], which have the fourfold *stoma*; the final *ājya*; the *mādhyaṃdina-pavamāna*; the *rathantara* and *vāmadevya*, which have the eightfold *stoma*; the two final *pṛṣṭha* [stotras]; the *ārbhava* and the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*, which have the twelvefold *stoma*; the *uktha* [stotras] and the *ṣoḍaśī*, which have the sixteenfold *stoma*. Among these, the *viṣṭuti* (mode of chanting) for the fourfold [stoma] is as follows:

He utters *hiṃ* for one [verse], that is with the first; he utters *hiṃ* for one, that is with the first; he utters *hiṃ* for one, that is with the middle; he utters *hiṃ* for one, that is with the last. In the case of the *kṣatrāyatanīya*, there are two rounds (*paryāya*) in the middle [verse]. The *viṣṭuti* for the eightfold hymn (*aṣṭistoma*) has been stated previously. Now, for the twelvefold hymn: he utters *hiṃ* for four [verses]—that is, two, one, and one. He utters *hiṃ* for two [verses], that is, for the two preceding ones in succession; he utters *hiṃ* for two [verses].

He performs the *hiṃ* with the last two of the four [verses] following [the first]. He does so with one, then with one, then with two. And it has been stated in the twelfth [chapter] that the first and the last [stomas] are explained; the middle ones consist of two [verses] each for the first two [sections], and the first [stoma] consists of two [verses] for the latter two—thus it was already stated regarding the sixteenfold [stoma] in the former [section].
Thus ends the second Catuṣṭoma. ||6||

The two [sacrifices] Udbhid and Balabhid are mentioned in the section beginning with "Udbhid is indeed the strength of the Asuras. There is a sūtra stating, "One should sacrifice with Udbhid and Balabhid without separation," and so forth. Regarding that, he states the ritual preparation for the Udbhid:
the *anurūpa* verse is "upo ṣu jātam apturam" (RV 8.69.1).

"Indram avardhayat" (He strengthened Indra) is the *ājya* chant of the Brahman priest; "Pibā sutasya rasinaḥ" (Drink of the pressed juice) is the *utsedha*; the *brahmasāman* consists of two single-verse hymns (*ekarca*), namely the *sapha* and the *udbhic*; the *lokaudala* belongs to Śyāvāśva; "Añjate" (They anoint) is the final *kāva*. ||1||
He draws up the hymns. ||2||
The rest is the same as that of the one-day fever (ekāhika). ||3||
Thus: "Upāsmai," "Upoṣu pavamānasya te kave"—these are for the Bahiṣpavamāna. Śāṇḍilya says that the *anurūpa* consists of a single verse; Gautama and Dhānañjayya say it consists of the *stotrīya*.
"O Agni, come for the feast; [come] to us, O Mitra and Varuṇa"; "The sacrifice has strengthened Indra"; "O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed juice"—these are the *ājya* verses.

The *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* [sāmans] are chanted loudly. In the first [verse], "abhi somāsaḥ," there are two *hiṃkāras*. In the three verses of the *maidhātitha-raurava*, [there are two *hiṃkāras*]. The *yaudhājaya* is in the middle verse; the *auśana* is in the final verse.
The Rathantara and the Vāmadevya; "Drink of the pressed, flavorful [juice]" is the *utsedha*; "In one's own [verses], the Kāleya" are the *pṛṣṭhas*.
The two verses beginning with *svādiṣṭhayā* are the Gāyatra-saṃhitā; *ayā pavasva devayuḥ* and *pavate haryato hariḥ* are the Sapha and Udbhid respectively;

*purojitī vo andhasaḥ* is the Audala-andhīgava; and *añjate* is the final [verse] of the Kava group. All [these] consist of single verses (*ekarca*). When a Stoma is possible, the final [verse] is used everywhere; this is because of the statement "it is possible" (*saṃbhavati*) in the rule regarding the triplet (*tṛca*). The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. || 3 ||
The two stomas, the sevenfold and the seventeenfold, are to be exchanged.

Thus concludes the *bahis-pavamāna*. The first *ājya* chant has the *sapti-stoma*, and the second has the *saptadaśa-stoma*; in this manner, the *stomas* alternate between the *sapti* and the *saptadaśa*. Regarding that, the *viṣṭuti* (recitation method) for the *sapti-stoma* follows the "grouping by birth" (*jāti-saṃhāra*) principle: "He utters the *hiṃ* call for one [verse], he utters the *hiṃ* call for three [verses] with the first [verse repeated], he utters the *hiṃ* call for three [verses] with the [verses] proceeding in succession."

But in the case of the even-odd withdrawal (yugmāyuk-saṃhāra-pakṣa), he utters "hiṃ" with two [verses], namely the first; he utters "hiṃ" with two, namely the first; he utters "hiṃ" with two, namely the middle one; he utters "hiṃ" with three, namely those directed forward (parācībhiḥ). || 4 ||
Thus [ends the section on] the Udbhid sacrifice. 7.

The breaker of strength (Indra) prescribed the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant for the *pratīcīnastoma*. The *ājya* [stotra] belongs to the Brahman priest, beginning with "The sacrifice strengthened Indra. The *niṣedha* [stotra] is the *brahmasāman*, beginning with "Drink of the pressed juice. In the world of the Maukṣa, there is the *balabhit*; for the Sapha, the *satrāsāhīya*. For the Śyāvāśva and Krauñca, [the stotras begin] with "This Pūṣan is wealth, he is Bhaga. The final *kāva* [stotra] begins with "The king, the leader, has been praised. || 1 ||
He draws up the hymns. || 2 ||
The rest is the same as that of the one-day *gavām ayana*.

Thus [it is said]. The *keśavapanīya* sacrifice has its *stomas* arranged in reverse order. The *bahiṣpavamāna* chant consists of the verses: "Purify yourself for speech," "O Indu, purify yourself with flashing luster," "These drops have been poured forth," "O Soma, you are a bull, you are brilliant," "For you are a bull by your radiance," and "Of you, O Sage, who are being purified."
"We choose Agni as the messenger," "We invoke Mitra," "The sacrifice strengthened Indra," and "To Indra and Agni be great homage"—these are the *ājya* verses.

For this [sacrifice], there are the *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* chants to the verse "asya pratnāmanudyutam. The *parītoṣi samantam* is used in the first [verse]; the *dairghaśravasa* in three [verses]; the *yaudhājaya* in the middle [verse]; and the final *pārtha* chant is for the verse "ayaṃ somaḥ."
The Bṛhat and Vāmadevya [Sāmans] are used; "pibā sutasya" is the Niṣkevalya Śastra; and the Pṛṣṭha Stotras are performed with their own respective Kāleya Sāmans.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the *gāyatram* and the *balabhit*; "pavasvendramaccha"—this is the *satrāsāhīyam* for the *śrudhya*; "ayaṃ pūṣā"—these are the *śyāvāśva* and *krauñca*; "agrego rājāpyastaviṣyataḥ"—this is the final *kāvam*. All [of these] consist of single verses (*ekarcāḥ*). The *yajñāyajñīyam* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. 3.
The *bahiṣpavamāna* consists of twenty-one verses; the *ājya* of the Hotṛ consists of three verses; all the others consist of seventeen verses each. 4.

Thus [ends the section on] the prescription of the *stoma*s. The method of chanting (*viṣṭuti*) for the threefold *stoma* has been stated in connection with the *śyena* sacrifice, and that for the sevenfold *stoma* in connection with the *udbhid*.
Thus ends [the section on] Balabhid.

The first *apaciti* sacrifice is described by the section beginning with "Now this is the *apaciti*. The second is described by the section beginning with "Now this *sarvastoma* is the *apaciti*. According to Dhānaṃjayya, one who desires honor (*apaciti*) should perform these two sacrifices. According to Śāṇḍilya, anyone at all who desires honor may do so. Of these two, here is the ritual procedure for the first.

The *bahiṣpavamāna* chant belongs to Balabhid; both *paryāsa* chants belong to Abhijit. The *gāyatrī* verse "Punānaḥ soma dhāraya" is a *bṛhatī*; it is used at the end of the *jyotiṣṭoma*. The *brahmasāman* called *yaśas* is based on the verse "Tvam indra yaśā asi. Following the *saṃhitā*, the *jarābodhīya* is used; following the *āndhīgava*, the *bharga* is used. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as the first [rite] involving a thousand [cows]. || 2 ||

Thus: "Of thee, the purifying one; of thee, the purifying one, O sage"—both the Bārhata and Rathantara [stotras] serve here as the *paryāsa* (concluding stotras). Among them, because of the predominance of the *bṛhat* [sāman], the Bārhata is performed first. In the Jyotiṣṭoma, at the end—meaning at the conclusion of the Mādhyandina and Ārbhava [pavamānas]—the Auśana and Kāva [stotras] are used. In this regard, the arrangement is as follows: "Flow on, the foremost of speech"; "Flow on, O Indu, with flashing luster"; "These drops have been poured forth"; "O Soma, thou art a bull, thou art resplendent"; "For thou art a bull by thy radiance."
"Pavamānasya te vayam" and "pavamānasya te kave" are for the Bahiṣpavamāna;
"agna āyāhi," "mitraṃ vayaṃ," "indramid gāthinaḥ," and "indre agne" are the Ājya hymns.

The *gāyatra*, *cāmahīyava*, and *satrāsāhīya* [sāmans] are for the verse "uccā te" (*RV* 9.61.12). While being purified, they are used in the first [stotra]. The *rathantara*, *dairghaśravasa*, and [the third] in the three [verses beginning with] "punānaḥ". The *yaudhājaya* is for the middle [stotra], and the *auśana* is the last.

The *bṛhat* and *vāmadevya* [are used] in the third [stotra]. The *yaśas* [sāman] is for the verse "tvam indra yaśā asi" (*RV* 8.6.39). The *kāleya* is for its own [verse]; these are the *pṛṣṭha* [sāmans].
"svādiṣṭhayā" is the Gāyatra, the Saṃhitā, and the Jarābodhīya; "pavasvendramacchā" is the Sapha and Śrudhya; "purojitī vo" is the Śyāvāśva and Āndhīgava; and "bhargaśca" is the final Kāva.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.

The Bahiṣpavamāna is twenty-four-fold; the Ājya-stotras are threefold and fifteenfold; the Mādhyandina-pavamāna is twenty-four-fold; the Pṛṣṭha-stotras are seventeenfold and twenty-one-fold; the Ārbhava-pavamāna is twenty-seven-fold; and the Agniṣṭoma is twenty-one-fold. || 3 ||

Thus: there is an exchange in the performance of the *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* [stomas] in the *ājya* [stotras], and likewise for the *saptadaśa* and *ekaviṃśa* [stomas] in the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras]. ||3||
Thus ends the section on honor. 6.

The *sarvastoma* is the second form of the *apaciti*. Its *bahiṣpavamāna* consists of one thousand verses, just as for the first. After the *āmahīyava*, the *uttaramaiḍa* is the *sauparṇa*. After the *jarābodhīya*, the *svāśira* is the *arka*. After the *ānuṣṭubha* verses, the *vāravantīya* is placed after the two-footed verses beginning with "pari pra dhanva. The *kāva* hymn, containing the word "sūrya," is the last. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as before. ||2||
Thus: "Flow on as the leader of speech, with flashing luster; O Sage, for you, the Pavamāna..."—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna chant.
"O Agni, come hither; we [invoke] Mitra; Indra indeed, O singers; in Indra, O Agni"—these are the Ājya offerings.

"High is your Gāyatra, the Āmahīyava, the Aiḍa, the Sauparṇa, and the Satrāsāhīya; O Soma, being purified, flow with your stream"—thus [are] the Samanta, the Rathantara, the Dairghaśravasa, the Yaudhājaya, and the Auśana as the last.
The Bṛhat and the Vāmadevya; "O Indra, you who are glorious"—this is the Yaśas; "In your own [songs] the Kāleya"—these are the Pṛṣṭhas.

The *gāyatra*, the *saṃhitā*, the *jarābodhīya*, and the *svāśira* hymn of *Arka* are [to be recited] with the verse "svādiṣṭhayā. The *sapha* and *śrudhya* [are recited] with the verse "pavasvendramacchā. The *śyāvāśva*, *āndhīgava*, and *bharga* [are recited] with the verse "purojitī va. The *vāravantīya* [is recited] with the two-footed verses beginning "pari pradhanva. The *kāva* is the final [hymn] among those containing the word "sūrya."
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.

He states the rule for the *stomas*: the *bahiṣpavamāna* is the *trivṛt*; the *hotṛ*s Ājya-stotra is the *pañcadaśa*; the two [Ājya-stotras] of the Maitrāvaruṇa and Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin are the *saptadaśa*; the Acchāvāka’s is the *ekaviṃśa*; the midday *pavamāna* is the *triṇava*; the *pṛṣṭhas* are the *chandomas*; the Ārbhava[-pavamāna] is the *trayastrimśa*; and the Agniṣṭoma is the *ekaviṃśa*. ||3||
Thus: "The Chandomas are the Pṛṣṭhas. This means that the Pṛṣṭhas are, respectively, those having the twenty-four-fold, the forty-four-fold, and the forty-eight-fold Stomas. || 3 ||
Thus ends the *sarvastoma* propitiation. 10.

The first *stoma* of Agni is called *pakṣin* (the winged one). This *stoma* is prescribed as a bird by the section beginning with "For this *stoma* is indeed a bird" (*atha eṣa pakṣī*). Then, by the section beginning with "Now this is the *jyotis*," the *jyotis* is prescribed. These two are referred to as the *agni-stomas*. As it has been said: "The means for the two *stomas* of Agni is stated by means of the vow belonging to the *aikāhika* (one-day rite). The *jyotis* also has the designation "bird. As Āpastamba has stated: "The two [rites] involving the piling of the fire-altar are performed with the two birds. First, he describes the *stoma* of Agni.

The *gāyatra*, the *cāmahīyava*, the *jarābodhīya*, the *svāra*, the *sauparṇa*, and the vow (*vrata*) of Agni; before the *yaudhājaya* is the *raurava*; in the world of glory is the *śyaita*; and with the verse "svādiṣṭhayā" are the *gāyatra* and the *svāśirā-marka*. (1)
The rest is the same as before; from this point forward, it is the Jyotiṣṭoma. || 2 ||

Thus [it is said]. The meaning of the passage beginning with "The rest is the same as the preceding" is as follows: that which was not stated prior to the Ārbhava [stotra] is the same as the preceding; however, from the *svāśira* after the *arka* onwards, it is the same as the *jyotiṣṭoma* beginning with the *kakub*. The *bahiṣpavamāna* [stotra] is performed with the verses: "Flow on with the flashing luster of speech," and "O Sage, of thee, the purifying one..."
"O Agni, come hither; we [invoke] Mitra; Indra indeed, O singers; in Indra, O Agni"—these are the *ājya* verses.

The *uccā te gāyatram*, the *cāmahīyavam*, the *jarābodhīyam*, the *svāra*, the *sauparṇa*, and the *vratam* of Agni; [the hymns] "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā," the *samantam*, the *rathantaram*, the *dairghaśravasam*, the *raurava-yaudhājaye*, and the *auśanam* as the final one.
The Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita, and the Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras.

"Stomāsvādiṣṭhayā" is the Gāyatra; "Svāśirāmarkaḥ" is the Sapha-Pauṣkala; "Pavasvendramaccha" is the Śyāvāśva-Āndhīgava; and the final [verse] is the Kāva. The Sapha-Pauṣkala, Śyāvāśva, and Āndhīgava [stotras] are performed with single verses.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. || 2 ||
Six stomas are directed upwards; six are directed downwards. || 3 ||

The *pārṣṭhika* stomas are sixfold, with the first [set] directed upwards; thereafter, those same [stomas] are directed downwards—this is the meaning. For example: the *bahiṣpavamāna* is the *trivṛt*; the *ājya* stotras are the *pañcadaśa*, *saptadaśa*, *ekaviṃśa*, and *triṇava* respectively; the *mādhyandina-pavamāna* is the *trayastriṃśa*; the *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *trayastriṃśa*, *triṇava*, *ekaviṃśa*, and *saptadaśa* respectively; the *ārbhava-pavamāna* is the *pañcadaśa*; and the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* is the *trivṛt*. Thus [it is said]. 3.
Thus ends the first hymn of praise to Agni.
The second hymn of praise to Agni is known by the alternative name "Jyotis" (The Light).

He states the second *stoma* of Agni: the *Jyotiṣṭoma* with the *Ājya* and *Bahiṣpavamāna* chants; he extracts the *Jarābodhīya*, the *Rathantara*, and the *Raurava*; the *Pṛṣṭha* chants of the *Vājapeya*; the *Audala* on one verse with "purojitī vo andhasaḥ"; the *Āndhīgava* on one verse; the *Śyāvāśva* on one verse; and the *Bṛhat* on three verses. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as before. ||2||
Thus: "Upāsmai davidyutatyā," "Pavamānasya te kave"—these are for the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, come to us for Mitra," and "O Indra and Agni"—these are the *ājya* offerings.

"Uccā te jātamandhasaḥ"—this consists of the Gāyatra, the Cāmahīyava, the Svāra, and the Sauparṇa; and the Vrata of Agni, "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā"—this consists of the Samanta, the Dairghaśravasa, the Yaudhājaya, and the Auśana as the final [Sāman]. This is the extraction of the Jarābodhīya, Rathantara, and Raurava.
The Rathantara, Vāmadevya, Abhīvarta, and Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha [stotras].

The *gāyatra* [sāman] is "svādiṣṭhayā"; the *arka* is "svāśiraḥ"; the *sapha* and *pauṣkala* are the single-verse [sāmans] "pavasva indram accha"; the *audala*, *āndhīgava*, and *śyāvāśva* are the three-verse *sāmans* beginning with "purojitī vo andhasaḥ"; and the final *kāva* is on three verses.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. || 2 ||
Now follows the arrangement of the Stomas: the Bahiṣpavamāna is Trivṛt; the three Ājya-stotras are Pañcadaśa; the Maitrāvaruṇa-stotra is Trivṛt;
the Mādhyandina Pavamāna is Caturviṃśa; and the three Pṛṣṭha-stotras are Saptadaśa.
The Maitrāvaruṇa [stotra] consists of fifteen [verses]; the Ārbhava [stotra] consists of seventeen; the Agniṣṭoma [sāman] consists of twenty-one. || 3 ||
Thus [ends the third section].
Thus ends the second hymn of praise to Agni. 12.
The *Ṛṣabha*. Now, as for the *Ṛṣabha* sacrifice for a Kṣatriya: this *Ṛṣabha* has been described in the section beginning with "Now this *Ṛṣabha*. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:

the *Raurava* chant is performed on three verses with the verse "Punānaḥ soma dhāraya"; the *Sadoviśīya* on one verse; the *Samanta* in the *Viṣṭārapaṅkti* meter; the *Yaudhājaya* on three verses; the *Abhīvarta* is the *Brahmasāman*; the *Gaurīvit* on one verse with the verse "Purojitī vo andhasaḥ"; the *Āndhīgava* on one verse; the *Śyāvāśva* on one verse; and the *Bṛhat* on three verses. ||1||
The Mādhyandina Pavamāna consists of seventeen [verses]. The rest is the same as in the Jyotiṣṭoma, with the same stomas.
Thus [it is said]; "upadavipava" refers to the bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, come to us for Mitra," and "O Indra and Agni"—these are the *ājya* offerings.

The *gāyatra* and the *cāmahīyava* are in the high [pitch]; while being purified, he sings the *raurava* in three verses; the *sadoviśīya* in one; "milking the udder" (*duhāna ūdhaḥ*) is in the *viṣṭārapaṅkti* meter throughout; the *yaudhājaya* in three verses, and the *auśana* at the end.

The *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *abhīvarta*, and the *kāleya* are the *pṛṣṭha* chants. The *gāyatrasaṃhita* is [performed] with the verse "svādiṣṭhayā" (RV 9.1.1). The *sapha* and *pauṣkala* are single-verse hymns [respectively] with the verses "pavasvendram accha" (RV 9.46.1) and "indurindrāya pavate" (RV 9.86.12). The *sāman*-triplets are the *gaurīvitam* with "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" (RV 8.91.1), the *āndhīgavam* with "abhi dyumnam" (RV 8.3.1), and the *śyāvāśvam* with "pra mandine" (RV 8.91.3). The *kāva* is performed on three verses; the *bṛhat* is the final one. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *bahiṣpavamāna* is the *trivṛt*. The *ājya* stotras are the *pañcadaśa*. The midday (*mādhyaṃdina*) pressing is the *saptadaśa*.
There are seventeen *pṛṣṭha* chants; the *ārbhava* [laud] has the twenty-one-fold hymn as its *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. Such is the arrangement of the *stomas*. || 2 ||
Thus ends the section on Ṛṣabha. 13.

The Gosava sacrifice has been described by the section beginning with "That which is indeed the Vājapeya. A Vaiśya whom the people, together with the king, should place at their head, he should sacrifice with the Gosava.

Its *bahiṣpavamāna* chant consists of the triplet beginning with "Sing forth to him, O men" (*upāsmai gāyata naraḥ*), followed by the six *saṃbhāryā* verses of the Vaiśvajit: "Flow on, the foremost of speech" (*pavasva vāco agriyaḥ*), "Flow on, O Indu, as a bull, pressed with a flashing luster" (*pavasvendo vṛṣā suto davidyutatyā rucā*), "These drops have been released" (*ete asṛgramindavaḥ*), "O Soma, you are a brilliant bull" (*vṛṣā soma dyumāṃ asi*), "For you are a bull by your radiance" (*vṛṣā hyasi bhānunā*), and "Him, that one, the ten fingers [purify]" (*etamu tyaṃ daśa kṣipaḥ*). [And further: "Of thee, the purifying one" (*pavamānasya te vayam*), "Of thee, the purifying one, O Sage" (*pavamānasya te kave*).
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
The six verses beginning with "upa tvā jāmayo giraḥ" and ending with "agna āyūṃṣi pavase" are the *saṃbhāryā* hymns for the Vaiśvajit sacrifice.
"Purifying yourself, O Soma, with your stream"—this is a Bṛhatī verse; the rest is the same as for the Abhiṣecanīya sacrifice. || 2 ||

Thus: "Suṣamiddha na āvaha" (O well-kindled one, bring us hither); "tā naḥ śaktaṃ pārthivasya" (those [powers] of ours, of the earthly realm); "yuñjanti bradhnamaruṣaṃ carantam" (they yoke the ruddy, moving sun); "tamīḍiṣva yo arciṣā" (praise him who with his flame)—these are the *ājya* hymns. In the *suṣamidh* four-verse hymn, the *uddhāra* (extraction) is according to the lineage (*gotra*). "Uccā te jātamandhasaḥ" (High is the birth of thy juice): this consists of the *gāyatra*, the *cāmahīyava*, the *jarābodhīya*, the *svāra*, and the *saindhukṣita*. "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā" (Being purified, O Soma, with your stream): this consists of the *samanta*, the *rathantara*, the *dairghaśravasa*, the *devasthāna*, the *varuṇasāma*, the *raurava*, and the *yaudhājaya*. "Vṛṣā śoṇaḥ" (The red bull): this is the final *pārtha* hymn.
The *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *kāleya*, and the *śyaita* are the *pṛṣṭha* stotras.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is for the Aukṣa [family] in the Gāyatra [meter]; "kākṣīvataṃ ca svāśiraḥ" is for the Arka; "pavasvendramaccha"—these are the Sapha and Daivodāsa [Sāmans]; "purojitī" is the Vādhryaśva, the Vaitahavya, the Somasāman, the Trāsadasyava, the Āndhīgava, and the Kāva as the final one.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*; the *satrāsāhīya*, the *saubhara*, and the *udvaṃśīya*—beginning with "O Agni, you are our closest"—are the *uktha* chants. ||2||
Now follows the arrangement of the Stomas;
all [of them] consist of thirty-six. || 3 ||

Thus: "He utters *hiṃ* for twelve [verses]: three times with three, once with eight, and once with one; he utters *hiṃ* for twelve: once with one, three times with three, and once with eight; he utters *hiṃ* for twelve: three times with eight, once with one, and once with three. This is the *viṣṭuti* (arrangement) of the thirty-six-fold hymn (*ṣaṭtriṃśastoma*). Regarding the phrase "as the first of the twenty-seven-fold" (*triṇavādya*), the meaning is that the stomas should be performed in the same manner as the first *viṣṭuti* of the twenty-seven-fold hymn, because of the statement "they are equal" (*samāḥ*). || 3 ||
Thus ends the Gosava sacrifice. || 14 ||
The Marutstoma and the Kulāya of Indra and Agni.

Now, this Marutstoma is described by the section beginning with "This is the Marutstoma," and this Kulāya of Indra and Agni is described by the section beginning with "This is the Kulāya of Indra and Agni. The ritual procedure for these two is the same as that of the Jyotiṣṭoma.
That which belongs to the Bṛhaspatisava and the Kulāya sacrifice dedicated to Indra and Agni. ||2||
Thus; the word "yeti" refers to the arrangement (*klṛpti*) as the qualificand. He states the arrangement of the *stomas* for both:
"The *stomas* are according to the *Anubrāhmaṇa*. (3)

Thus it is said. In that context, the Marutstoma involves many sacrificers, according to the Vedic injunction: "By this very [rite], one should cause three [persons] to sacrifice," and from the statement: "Friends or brothers who would perform [the rite together] should sacrifice with the Marutstoma. Everything regarding it is like the Jyotiṣṭoma, except for the cessation of the *dhūr*, *jyotis*, and *viśvarūpa* [sacrifices]. There are three *trivṛt* stotras, three *pañcadaśa* stotras, three *saptadaśa* stotras, and three *ekaviṃśa* stotras. In the *ārbhava* [pavamāna], all the *sāmans* are based on triplets (*tṛca*). Everything regarding the *kulāya* of Indra and Agni is like the Bṛhaspatisava. Six.

The *stotras* are threefold: two *stotras* are fifteen-fold (*pañcadaśa*), two are seventeen-fold (*saptadaśa*), and [one] is twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*); these are the *stomas*. In the *ārbhava-pavamāna*, all [verses] consist of triplets (*tṛca*). According to the scriptural injunction: "By this very [rite], one should cause two [persons] to sacrifice. (3)
Thus ends the Marutstoma and the Kulāya sacrifice for Indra and Agni. || 15 ||
The Indra-stoma:
Now this fifteen-fold Indra-stoma Ukthya is described by the Anuvāka beginning with "Indra-stoma. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
"O Indu, flow for Indra accompanied by the Maruts; O Indu, you are the pressed bull; O Soma, you are brilliant; for you are a bull by your luster; [this is] of you, the purifying sage. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
Worthy of praise and worthy of homage, when the sun has risen today, sing forth a great song to Indra; offer great reverence to Indra and Agni. 2.
Thus end the offerings of clarified butter.
The *uccā te gāyatram* and the *cāmahīyavam*; the *samantam* and the *yaudhājayam* with the words "O Soma, I have rejoiced in thee"; and the *pārtha* ending with "vṛṣā śoṇaḥ. || 3 ||
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The Bṛhat and the Vāmadevya are upon the Revatī verses; the Śyaita and the Kāleya as well. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" is the Gāyatra [stoma] at the Auksa; "pavasvendramaccha" is the Sapha at the Śrudhya; "pari tyaṃ haryataṃ harim" is the Śyāvāśva at the Āndhīgava; and the final [stotra] is the Kāva upon verses containing the word "sūrya."
The three beginning with "sapha" each consist of a single verse. || 5 ||
"pra daivodāso agniḥ"—this is the Yajñāyajñīya Agniṣṭoma-sāman.
The *Satrāsāhīya* is in the *svāsu* verses; the *Saubhara* is "That great power of yours, O Indra"; the *Udvaṃśīya* is in the *svāsu* verses. || 7 ||
Thus end the hymns.
Every [stotra] consists of fifteen [verses]. || 8 ||
Thus ends the Indra-stoma. || 16 ||
The Stoma of Indra and Agni:

Now, this Stoma of Indra and Agni has been declared by the Anuvāka beginning with "indrāgnyoḥ stomaḥ. A king and his domestic priest (purohita) should sacrifice together with the Stoma of Indra and Agni, either separately or jointly. Its ritual procedure (kalpa) is as follows:
"Flow on, the foremost of speech! Sing to him, O men! Of you, the purifying sage... (RV IX.1.1).
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"Agni we choose as messenger"—with these words, both types of *ājya* offerings are performed.
"Agni as the messenger," "Come to us, O Mitra and Varuṇa," "Indra, the singer [sings] loudly," and "O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed [juice]"—these are the Ājya offerings.

"O Soma, being purified, flow in a stream"—with this [verse], the Raurava is performed on one [verse], the Yaudhājaya on one, the Dairghaśravasa on one, and the Rathantara on three; the Bṛhat is the Pṛṣṭha-stotra, and the Abhīvarta is the Brahmasāman for the verses of the Śyaita. || 3 ||
The rest is the same as the Jyotiṣṭoma. ||4||

Thus: "uccā te gāyatram" and "cāmahīyavam"; "punānaḥ soma" [with] "rauravam," "yaudhājayam," and "dairghaśravasam"—these are the *sāman*-verses (*sāmatṛcaḥ*). The *rathantaram* is on three verses; the *auśanam* is the last. The *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevyam*, and the *abhīvarta* as the *brahmasāman* on the verses of the *śyaitam*; the *kāleyam* on its own verses—these are the *pṛṣṭha* chants. "svādiṣṭhayā" is the *gāyatrasaṃhitā*. "pavasva indram accha" is the *sapha-pauṣkala*. "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the *śyāvāśva-andhīgava*.
The *kāva* is the final [stotra]. The *kāva* consists of a triplet; the others consist of single verses. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* *stomas* are to be performed in alternation.
Thus ends the rule for the Stomas. ||5||
Thus ends the hymn to Indra and Agni. 17.

The *vighana* is the first; this *vighana* is described by the section beginning with "atha eṣa vighanaḥ. The second is [the hymn] beginning with "indram adevyo māyā asacanta. One desiring cattle or practicing exorcism should sacrifice with these two *vighanas*. Regarding the first *vighana*: the *śyaita* is on its own [verses]; the *jarābodhīya* follows the *saṃhitā*; the *viśoviśīya* is in the world of *śrudhya*; and the *somasāman* is either the *āndhīgava* or the *ātharvaṇa* following that. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as with the first thousand-fold [offering]. ||2||

Thus, the rule for the alternative between the *somasāman* and the *ātharvaṇa* as stated in the Sūtra is as follows: one should employ the *ātharvaṇa* at a sacrifice performed with the desire for cattle, and the *somasāman* for one practicing sorcery (*abhicaran*). For the *bahiṣpavamāna*, [the verses are] "Flow on, O Pavamāna, with the flashing of speech" and "Of you, O Sage, who purify yourself."
"O Agni, come hither; we [invoke] Mitra; Indra indeed, O singers; in Indra and Agni"—these are the Ājya offerings.

For this [stotra], there are the *gāyatra* and *āmahīyava* chants to the verse "asya pratnāmanudyutam. In the first [turn], the *samanta* chant is used for the verse "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam. The *rathantara* and *dairghaśravasa* are used for two triplets; the *yaudhājaya* is used for the middle *asyā*. The final [verse] is the *pārtha*, beginning with "ayaṃ soma. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras consist of the *bṛhat*, *vāmadevya*, *śyaita*, and *kāleya*. The *gāyatrasaṃhita* and *jarābodhīya* chants are used for the verse "svādiṣṭhayā. The *sapha* and *viśoviśīya* chants are used for the verse "pavasvendramaccha."

The *purojitī* [verse] belongs to Śyāvāśva and Andhīgava; or it is the *soma-sāman* of Atharvan. The *kāva* [sāman] is the final one among those containing the word "sūrya. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. ||2||
He states the arrangement of the *stomas*:
two *stotras* are *trivṛt*; two are *dvādaśa*; two are *pañcadaśa* and *saptadaśa*; two are *ekaviṃśa* and *navadaśa*; two are *caturviṃśa*; and two are *triṇava*. ||3||

Thus [ends the section on] the twelve-fold stoma; its *viṣṭuti* has been shown again in the context of the *stoma*. Now, for the nineteen-fold stoma: "He utters *hiṃ* three times with [the verses] in their natural order (*parācībhiḥ*). He utters *hiṃ* thirteen times: three times with three [verses], seven times with seven [verses], and three times with three [verses]. He utters *hiṃ* three times with [the verses] in their natural order. This has been stated: "In the nineteen-fold stoma which revolves, there are two turns (*paryāya*) on either side; in this [turn] which has thirteen [verses] in the middle, there is a triple recitation of the first [verse] and likewise of the last. (3)
Thus ends the first obstacle. ||18||
The second [section] is Vighana;
he states the second Vighana:
"Flow on as the leader of speech; sing to him, O men, for you, O sage, who are being purified. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
Salutations to you, O Agni, for your vital power! We invoke Mitra; I call upon the subjects of this assembly, those two by whom this world exists. 2.

Thus are the *ājya* stotras. For two [verses] beginning with *pratnaṃ pīyūṣaṃ pūrvyaṃ yadukthyam*, there is the *gāyatra*; for three [verses], the *āmahīyava*; for one [verse], the *aiḍa sauparṇa*; for one [verse], the *satrāsāhīya*; and for whichever one remains, the *sadoviśīya*. For the verse *punaḥ soma dhāraya*, there is the *raurava* on one [verse]; the *yaudhājaya* on one; the *samanta* on one; and the *rathantara* on three. For the verse *adha yadime pavamāna rodasī*, there is the *utsedha* on one;
and the final one is the *pārtha* on the verse *ayaṃ somaḥ*. 3.

[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna. There are two *bṛhatī* verses consisting of seventy-two syllables each. In that regard, having formed three *gāyatrī* verses by means of four twenty-four-syllable [pādas] each, the *gāyatra* sāman should be performed upon them. For example: "The ancient nectar, the primordial... (*pratnaṃ pīyūṣaṃ pūrvyom*); "Indra, being born... (*indramabhijāyamānom*); and "The divine, wealth-shining ones, toward heaven... (*vasuruco divyā abhyom*). As follows: "The ancient nectar, the primordial... is the *āmahīyava*; "Indra, toward heaven... is the *sauparṇa aiḍa*; and "The wealth-shining ones" is the *satrāsāhīya*.
As for the remaining *satobṛhatī* verse in the *tṛca* beginning with "atha yad imāḥ," the *sado-viśīya* [chant] is performed upon it; the rest is clear.

Now follows the Taittirīyaka: "They chant on *satobṛhatī* verses; they chant with intermingled [verses]. The intermingling (*vyatiṣaṅga*) of the *satobṛhatīs* consists in their being separated by *bṛhatīs*. Consequently, for the purpose of effecting this intermingling, the repetition of the verse beginning with *atha yadimāḥ* constitutes a transposition (*saṃcāra*), and this does not constitute a fault. And it is stated in the *Upagrantha*: "There is no transposition of the *stotriya* verses on the same day, except in the case of the *vighana*. (3)
"The *Bṛhat* and the *Vāmadevya*, that indeed was the eldest among the worlds"—with these [verses], the *Śyaita* and the *Kāleya* [are performed] on their own [verses]. || 4 ||
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā": the Gāyatra [Sāman] is chanted on three verses joined together, on one verse [the *surūpa*], and on one verse [the *svāśira*]. "arka" is on one verse; "pavasvendramaccha" is the *sapha-viśoviśīya*. "purojitī vo andhasaḥ": the *gaurīvita* is on one verse; the *niṣedha* is on one verse; the *śyāvāśva* is on one verse;

the *āndhīgava* is on three verses; the *madhuścunnidhana* is on three verses. "sumanmā vasvīrantī sūnarī": the *vāravantīya* is on three verses. The final [Sāman] is the *kāva*. Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
Now, the *stomas*: two *trivṛt* chants; two *dvādaśa*; two *pañcadaśa* and *saptadaśa*; two *navadaśa* and *caturviṃśa*; two *caturviṃśa* and *ekaviṃśa*; and two *triṇava*. 7.
Thus ends the second [chapter], Vighana. ||18||

The *saṃdaṃśa*: Now, this *saṃdaṃśa* sacrifice—one seeking to practice sorcery should perform it—is mentioned in the *Ṣaḍviṃśa-Brāhmaṇa*. "Now, this *vajra* sacrifice—one seeking to practice sorcery should perform it" refers to the *vajra*. One should practice sorcery against a king with the *saṃdaṃśa*, and against a country with the *vajra*. Regarding that, he speaks of the *saṃdaṃśa*:
"The *śyena* [sāman] as the *ājya* and the *bahiṣpavamāna*. (1)
Thus: "Of the purifying one who strikes down," "Purifying, he has stepped forth toward [the worlds]," and "O Sage, of you, the purifying one"—[these are] for the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"Agni, the slayer of Vṛtras; Mitra, I invoke you. "May the Soma-draughts exhilarate you. "I invoke those two of whom this [world] exists"—these are the *ājya* verses. ||1||

"Flow on, O Soma, most resplendent"—this is the Gāyatra for the Vārṣāhara; "Being purified, O Soma, with thy stream"—this is the Vaiyaśva on one verse; the *vaṣaṭ*-call and the *nidhana* on one verse; the Raurava on one verse; the Yaudhājaya on three verses; and the Auśana is the final one. || 2 ||
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna:
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Saptaha, and the Kāleya. 3.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" is the Gāyatra [Sāman] belonging to Vārṣāhara; "satrāsāhīyam" is the [Sāman] for the Pavamāna; "pavasvendramacchā" is the Kāśītaupagava; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Nānada for the Andhīgava. Of these three Sāmans, that which is first is the Kāva, and it is the last.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
Regarding the first of the three Sāmans: *hāu hāu hāu as phaṭ*, and so forth. 4.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
He states the *stomas*: two *trivṛt* chants; two *dvādaśa*; two *pañcadaśa*; two *ekaviṃśa*; two *caturviṃśa*; two *triṇava*. ||6||

Thus, the *viṣṭuti*s for the *trivṛt*, *pañcadaśa*, *ekaviṃśa*, and *triṇava* stomas intended for malevolent rites have been taught in the section on the *ṣaḍviṃśa*. Among them, there is an option between the two *trivṛt* *viṣṭuti*s.
Thus ends the section on the pincers (saṃdaṃśa). ||19||

Vajra said regarding the Vajra: "Flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull; driving away the adversaries, he flows"—this is for the triplet before the *paryāsa*. He omits the *satrāsāhīya*. "With your food, victorious from of old"—this *nānada* is on a single verse. On that same verse is the *āndhīgava*. The *śyāvāśva* is on a single verse. The *sāman* is on a single verse for three [verses], namely the second one. The *pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*, the *aupagava*, and the *udvaṃśīya* [are likewise]. || 1 ||
The Mahānāmnī verses are the Sāman for the Ṣoḍaśin; the rest is the same as before.

Thus: "Of Pavamāna as he strikes down," "Purifying, he has stepped forth," "Flow on, O Indu, as a bull when pressed," "Striking away the adversaries, he flows," and "Of you, O sage Pavamāna"—these are for the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"I invoke Agni against the Vṛtras; I invoke Mitra of purified will. "May the Soma-draughts exhilarate you. "I invoke those two of whom this [world] exists"—these are the Ājya verses.

"Flow on, O Soma, most brilliant!"—this is for the Gāyatra-Vārṣāhara. "Being purified, he..."—this is the Vaiyaśva, with the *vaṣaṭ* as its finale. "The Raurava"—these are two *sāman*-verses. The Yaudhājaya is performed over three verses; the Auśana is the final one.
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Saptaha, and the Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha chants.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" is for the Gāyatra-Vārṣāhara; "pavasvendram accha" is for the two single-verse hymns of the Kāśīta and Aupagava; "purojitī vaḥ" is for the Nānada-Andhīgava on the first [verse]; the Śyāvāśva is for the second; the Mahāsāman beginning with "abhyābhūḥ" is for the third; the Kāva is the final one; the Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman;
and the Pramaṃhiṣṭhīya, "tvaṃ na indra," the Aupagava, and the Udvaṃśīya are the Uktha-sāmans.
The Mahānāmnī verses constitute the *ṣoḍaśi-sāman*. At the time of their chanting, a loud shout (*udaghoṣa*) must be made; however, the *nidhana* should not be performed with a *yajus* formula.
He states the rule for the *stoma*:
"Every [stotra] is fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*). (3)
Thus ends the *viṣṭuti* for the purpose of malevolent magic. 3.
He says that for the sake of pacification at the end of the *saṃdaṃśa* and *vajra* [sections], one should sacrifice with the *jyotiṣṭoma*:
"The *jyotiṣṭoma* is prescribed for the sake of pacification; it is for the sake of pacification. (4)
Thus [ends section] 4.
Thus ends the Vajra [section], number twenty.
Thus Varadarāja, the son of Vāmanārya and born of the lineage of Kuśika,
has explained the *Kalpa* for the one-day rites according to tradition and according to his own understanding.
Thus ends [the section] in the commentary on the *Ārṣeyakalpa* composed by Varadarāja, the son of the venerable Vāmanārya.
The Fifth Chapter ||5||
The one-day rite is completed.

The Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra is established either as one without the Ṣoḍaśin cup or as one with the Ṣoḍaśin cup. According to another Brāhmaṇa, the Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra is established as being without the Ṣoḍaśin in the four chapters beginning with the sixth, or alternatively, it is stated to be with the Ṣoḍaśin in accordance with other Brāhmaṇas. The procedure for this Atirātra has already been shown by us at the very beginning. He states the distinction of the Rātri [Sāman] among those to be described: "In the Ahīnika Rātri, 'paṇyaṃ-paṇyam it sotāraḥ' is the Śrautakakṣa Daivodāsa, the Hotṛṣāman of Kautsa."
"May the drops enter you, O world with eight tusks"—in these verses, everything else is the same as in the *sattrika* [rite].

For the *sarvastoma*, the introductory verse (*pratipad*) is the *upavatī*; the *śyaita* [sāman] is performed on its own verses; the *parisvān* is the *ārbhavīya*; the *jarābodhīya* follows the *samhitā*; the *ātharvaṇa* follows the *āndhīgava*; everything else is the same as the first *sāhasra*. Its *jyotiṣṭoma* is an *atirātra* accompanied by the *ṣoḍaśin* cup.

For the third *aptoryāman*, which consists of a thousand verses, one omits the *surūpa* [verse] from the *ājya-bahiṣpavamāna* in the place of the *jarābodhīya*; the *sauhaviṣa* has the *svarvat* finale, while the rest is the same as the preceding [rite]. The *vaiśvajita* *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the embryos of the *pṛṣṭhas*; the *anubrāhmaṇa* [section] contains the additional stotras. 613

For the *navasaptadaśa* day, after [the verse] "O great one, from the barley," follows "Flow on, most honey-sweet"; for the *sākamaśva*, [the verse] "O Soma, the Āyus"; for the *janitra*, the verses of Raurava and Yaudhājaya; for the *naudhasa*, the verses of Ṛkṣa; for the *janitra*, [the verse] "Run forth toward the prize"; for the *sapha*, [the verse] "Together. The rest is the same as the *jyotiṣṭoma* performed as an *atirātra* without the *ṣoḍaśin*.

Whatever belongs to the *jyotiṣṭoma* applies to the *viṣuvat*; its *ukthas* consist of seventeen-fold stotras, and the *atirātra* is without the *ṣoḍaśin*. The *go* and *āyus* [stomas] are established.

In the *kḷpti* [section], the Viśvajit and Abhijit [are mentioned]. That which belongs to the Bṛhaspatisava is the first of those with a single *stoma*; its Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra includes the *ṣoḍaśin*. (617–618) The *gorāj* [sāman] is the *bahiṣpavamāna* of the Indrastoma; the midday [pavamāna] is [performed] with the *bṛhatī* verse beginning "punānaḥ soma dhārayā. The *śyaita* [sāman] is performed on its own verses; the rest is the same as the first *sāhasra*. Its Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra includes the *ṣoḍaśin*. (621)
The *ājya* and *bahiṣpavamāna* chants of the Tīvrasutas are the same as those of the midday pressing; the rest is the same as the first *ekastoma*.

For the *pratīcīnastoma*, the *bahiṣpavamāna* is the *gāyatrī* of the Abhijit; for the subsequent *jyotis*, it is the *bṛhatī*; the rest is the same as the second *ekastoma*. There are *ṣoḍaśin* cups, or the *anubrāhmaṇa* of the *ṣoḍaśins*.

Those two days which belong to the *vyuṣṭi*-dvirātra, he extracts them for the second day of the Āṅgirasa-dvirātra: the *ṛṣabha* and the *jarābodhīya*. From the *samanta* [he extracts] the *dairghaśravasa*; between [these], the *ātharvaṇa*; after the *saṃhitā*, the *jarābodhīya*; and in the place of the *viśoviśīya*, the *śrudhya*.

The first day of the *dvirātra* of Aṅgirasa belongs to Caitraratha; its *ukthas* are those of Āyu. [The verses for] the first day are: "Flow on as the foremost of speech," "Flow on, O Indu, as the bull, pressed," "May thy skill, which brings bliss, [be ours]," and "In the world of him who hears [the call], be thou wakeful at dawn. Then they proceed to the night of Nārmedha. Now, that which is the final day of the two-day rite, this is the same [as the first]; thus [is] the second day. 625. Those two days of Caitraratha belong to Kāpivana: the first day is an *agniṣṭoma* with the *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* stomas, and the second day is an *atirātra* of Āyu. 626.

For the first day of the *ābhiplava* [six-day period], the *ājya* and *bahiṣpavamāna* chants are the *rathantara*; the midday [stotra] is the *svāra-sauparṇa*; the *abhīvarta* is "śagdhy ū ṣu śacīpate" with its own verses; the *kāleya* is "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā"; the *gāyatra* is "ayā pavasva devayuḥ pavate haryato hariḥ"; the *audala* is "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ" with the *cartanidhana*; the *ājyadoha* is "abhi priyāṇi"; the *vaikhānasa* is the final [stotra]; and the *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. 63.

"Upa su jātamapturam," "Davidyutatyā rucā," "Pavasvendro vṛṣā sutaḥ," "Rājā medhābhirīyate," "Iṣe pavasva dhārayā. "Kayā te agne aṅgiraḥ," "Purūruṇā cid dhyasti," "Tam indraṃ vājayāmasi," "Iyaṃ vāmasya manmānaḥ," "Asya pratnāmanu dyutim"—these are the Gāyatra and the Āmahīyava. "Abhi somāsa āyavaḥ"—this is the Gautama and the Dairghaśravasa, along with the Dvihiṃkāra. "Ayaṃ somaḥ"—this is the Īnidhana, and the Ājyadoha is the final [verse].

The *vāmadevya* is in its own [verses]; "mo ṣu tvā vāghataś cana" is the side of the *gāyatra*; "astāvi manma pūrvyam" is the *saṃtani*. They chant the *saṃkṛti* among the *ṛc*s; "yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" is the *gāyatra*; the *arka* of Agni is "abhi dyumnaṃ bṛhad yaśaḥ"; "sakhāya ā niṣīdata" is the *sāman* of Vāc and the *śaukta*. "pary ū ṣu" is the *āndhīgava*; "indrāya soma pātave" is the *yajñāyajñīya*; "pavitraṃ te" is the final, unharmed (*ariṣṭa*) *viśoviśīya*, the *agniṣṭomasāman*; the *ukthas* are in their own [verses] for the sake of long life. 64.

Flow on as the leader of speech; this immortal god, this one, goes with the subtle *dhī*. We invoke the immortal god Mitra, the great Indra for his might. "Homage, vast and high, to Indra and Agni! Your birth from the soma-juice..."—thus the *Gāyatra*, the *Gauṣūkta*, the *Jarābodhīya*, and the *Ṛṣabha*; the *Pāvamāna* hymn, the ancient nectar, the primordial, which is worthy of praise—this is the *Utsedha*. "Pour out the pressed juice on every side"—this is the *Ābhīśava*; the *Atharvaṇa* hymn, "The speckled one, the three voices..."—thus [it ends].

The *triṇidhana* [sāman], the *ājyadoha*, the final [sāman], the *bṛhat*, the *satrāsāhīya*, the *śyaita*, the *raurava*, the *pari svāno giriṣṭhāḥ*, the *gāyatram*, and the *hāviṣmatam*; [the verses] "sa sunve yo vasūnām," "prāṇā śiśurmahīnām" for the *dīrghaśrudhi*; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ" for the *niṣedha*; the *śyāvāśvam*, the *krauñcam*, and the *yajñāyajñīyam*; "pari pra dhanva" for the *vājadāvaryas*; "ayā ruce" for the *nityavatsa*; and the *arka* of Dīrghatamas beginning with "dhartā divaḥ" as the final [sāman].
The Vāravantīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman; the Jyotiṣṭoma is an Atirātra with the Ṣoḍaśin cup.

He performs three Anuṣṭubhs and four Gāyatrīs beginning with "pavasva vājasātaye" for the Pajra and Audhāja families; between these, the Gauṅgava and Audala Ājyadohas; the Gautama [Sāman] is the same as the first day of the Garga-trirātra. 661.

"Sing forth to him, O men; sing well to him who is born, the overcomer of waters, for his splendor with flashing brilliance. These drops have been poured out for you; the King is approached with sacred hymns. O Soma, you are the bull, the radiant one; flow with your stream, O Soma, for the sake of the Āyus. These are the verses of Gautama, Antarikṣa, Dairghaśravasa, Paurumadga, Gāyatrapārśva, and Maidhātithi—each consisting of a single verse (*ekarca*)—to be chanted continuously (*santani*) across three verses, accompanied by two *hiṅkāras*. Furthermore, there are the *Mahānāmnīs*, the *Vāmadevya*, the *Pārthuraśma*, and the verses of the *Śrāyantīya* hymn.

The *saṃkṛti* [stotra] is the same as the other [of the Garga-trirātra] by means of the middle day. 662. "Flow on, the foremost of speech; flow on, O Indu, the bull, being pressed. Of you, O sage Pavamāna, there are four single-verse hymns following the *gāyatrī*; the last one is in the *bṛhatī* metre. There are three single-verse hymns in the *anuṣṭubh* metre, and the last one is in a triplet (*tṛca*). The rest is the same as the other [of the Garga-trirātra] by means of the final day. 663.

"Forward, O wise Soma-stems"—on one verse the Gāyatra, on one the Āśva, on one the Jarābodhīya; "Forward, O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—on one verse the Gauṅgava, on one the Pājra, on one the Yaudhājaya; the Auśana, Aupagava, and Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra; "To him who desires to drink"—the Nānada, the Ṣoḍaśin-sāman, the night, and the junction (sandhi); the rest is the same as the first day of the Garga-trirātra. 671.

"Upa su jātamapturam," "Davidyutatyā ruce," "Pavasva dhārayā," "Pary ū ṣu śyāvāśvam indrāya somapātave"—these are the Āndhīgava stotras; "Pavitraṃ te" is the Yajñāyajñīya; the final [stotra] is in the place of the Udvaṃśīya, namely the Tairaścya; the Udvaṃśīya is the Ṣoḍaśin-sāman; the night is the *sandhi*; the rest is the same as on the second day of the Garga-trirātra. 672.

Flow on as the leader of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. From thee it draws forth skill that brings bliss—the *jarābodhīya*, the *satobṛhatī*, the *dvipadā*, and the *aticchandas* in reverse order; the *bārhata* verses beginning with "This Pūṣan, wealth, Bhaga," and the hymn of Dīrghatamas; the *krauñca* chant beginning with "The upholder of heaven"; and the *yajñāyajñīya* as the finale—all this is the same as the final day of the Garga-trirātra sacrifice.

For the Viṣuvat day of the year-long sacrifice, both Paryāsa stotras are [performed]: the Aśva and the Soma-sāman; the Rohitakūlīya and the "Pavasva indram accha" are with the Sapha-kṣāra; the rest is the same as the first [day] of the Aśvatrirātra. 681.

"O Soma, you are a bull, you are brilliant; for you are indeed a bull. "The Soma drops flow toward the beloved [goal]; the Soma, being purified, flows on; your powers rise up. With these verses he takes up the *paryāsa* from the *āmahīyava*. Following it are the six [verses] beginning with the *āśubhārgava*, each preceded by two *hiṃkāras*. Then the *acchidra*, the *maidhātitha*, and the *pauruhanmana*; those following the *arkam* of Agni; the four beginning with the *surūpa*; those preceding the *yajñāyajñīya*; and the *āsita*, the *kautsa*, the *śuddhāśuddhīya*, and the *krauñca*.

The *rayiṣṭha* [sāman] is the same; the rest is identical to that of the middle day of the Garga-trirātra. From the ninth day, following the eight-verse [hymn], he brings down four six-verse [hymns]: "ā te dakṣam mayobhuvam" is the final verse (*paryāsa*). Following the *ṛṣabha-pavamāna*, there are the *surūpa-kṛt-sūkta* and the *dārasṛk*. There is a combination (*saṃkṣāra*) of the *ḍāna*s and the *svāra*. The *saindhukṣita* follows the *pṛśni*; the *arkapuṣpa*, *kaulmalabarhiṣa*, and *devasthāna* follow the *hāviṣmat*. The four beginning with the *śāṃmada* follow the *yajñāyajñīya*. The *yadvāhiṣṭhīya* is the same as the one for the last day. The rest is identical to that of the highest day.
Of the Garga-trirātra:
those which are the first and last days of the Garga-trirātra belong to the Antarvasus.

"Upa ṣu jātam apturam," "Davidyutatyā rucā," "Pavasvendro vṛṣā sutaḥ," "Rājā medhābhir īyate," "Ete asṛgram indavaḥ," "Vṛṣā soma dyumāṃ asi," "Vṛṣā hy asi bhānunā," and "Iṣe pavasva dhārayā. Now, that which is the middle day of the Chandoma-pavamāna, for that [day] the Ārbhava [Śastra] is arranged according to the *tṛca* (triplet) structure.

That which is the first *antarvasu* belongs to the *parāka*. 693. "O Soma, you are a bull, you are brilliant; for you are indeed a bull with your light"—with these words, he takes [the draught] from the *paryāsa* before the *āmahīyava*, and from the *āśu* and *bhārgava* after the *mārgīyava*, and from the *surūpa-bhāsa* after the *agni-arka*, and from the two preceding the *yajñāyajñīya*; the rest is the same as the middle day of the Garga-trirātra. 694.

The *bahiṣpavamāna* of the second day follows that of the *vyuṣṭi*. Now, that which is the last day of the *chandomapavamāna*, that is its [day]: it is arranged like the hare's ear (*śaśakarṇaka*), consisting of a *vivṛt* with *bṛhatī* verses; it is a *jyotiṣṭoma* *atirātra*.
Now, by means of three Brāhmaṇa chapters beginning with the twentieth,
the ritual arrangement (*klṛpti*) for those *ahīna* sacrifices that have been prescribed is set forth in the three [chapters] beginning with the sixth.

The three chapters beginning with "The Ahīnas have the full-moon day as their initiation and conclude with the month," and so forth, contain their sūtra: "All Atirātras are Ahīnas; and the multi-day sacrifices (ahargaṇas) beginning with the Dvirātra [are Ahīnas]. However, the Cāturmāsya and Rājasūya are not Ahīnas, because they are recited specifically within the section on one-day sacrifices (ekāha), and because there is no accumulation of days in them. For that very reason, the distinction of the Ahīna-night sacrifice which will be mentioned later does not apply to those two.
Here, he describes the arrangement of the Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra sacrifice, which was mentioned in the first Anuvāka beginning with "The Bahiṣpavamāna is Trivṛt":
"The Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra is arranged [as follows]: either without the Ṣoḍaśin cup, or with the Ṣoḍaśin. (1)

Thus, in the Brāhmaṇa, the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice in the form of an Atirātra without the *ṣoḍaśin* cup is established through the four chapters beginning with the sixth. Alternatively, the phrase "if [there is] the *ṣoḍaśin*" is stated in accordance with another Brāhmaṇa. The performance (*prayoga*) of this Atirātra has already been shown by us at the very beginning. He states the specific feature of the night among those to be described, regarding the night of the *āhīnika* (daily) sacrifice: "At every pressing, O pressers... (*panyaṃ-panyam it sotāraḥ*). [The verses used are] the *Śrautakakṣa*, the *Daivodāsa*, the *Hotṛṣāman* of Kautsa, the *Loka*, the *Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*, and the verse beginning "May the drops enter thee" (*ā tvā viśantvindavaḥ*). (2)
The rest is the same as that of the Sātrikī.

Thus it is said: "The *daivodāsa* is the *hotṛṣāman*. Here, indeed, there are the *ājya*, *pṛṣṭha*, and *agniṣṭoma* chants, as well as the *uktha* chants. For each of the nocturnal rounds (*rātriparyāya*), four *sāmans* are to be chanted in sequence by the *hotṛ*, *maitrāvaruṇa*, *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin*, and *acchāvāka*; thus they are designated according to their respective associations. Consequently, following the *śrautakakṣa*, that which is the first *sāman* of the middle nocturnal round—the *hotṛṣāman*—is invariably the *daivodāsa*.

The meaning is that it is not optional with respect to the *aurvasadmana*. The use of the dative case in the word *sātrikyāḥ* is a Vedic usage (*chāndasa*) employed in connection with a term of similar meaning; the sense is that "everything else is the same as [the ritual] of the *sātrikī* night. The *sātrikī* is that night which occurs in the *satras*, such as the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*) and others. Thus, although it should have been stated that "it is the same as the *jyotiṣṭoma*," the use of the term *sātrikī* indicates that even though the *āhinika* [daily] rites—such as the *atirātra* with all the *stomas*—are extended to the *satras*, the night remains essentially archetypal (*prākṛtī*).

This is for the purpose of illustration. Furthermore, in the Brāhmaṇa, the Jyotir Atirātra prescribed in the sixth chapter and subsequent chapters is indeed independent. Now, an objection may be raised: "But it is part of the Dvādaśāha; and in that context, it has been established that there is no Ahīna-night," as stated in the Sūtra beginning with "The injunction for the Jyotiṣṭoma [applies] because of its immediate sequence," and so forth. || 2 ||
Thus concludes the Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra sacrifice. || 1 ||

The *sarvastoma* *atirātra*. Now, regarding the *sarvastoma* *atirātra*: the *bahiṣpavamāna* is the *trivṛt*; the *ājya* stotras are the *pañcadaśa*; the midday *pavamāna* is the *saptadaśa*; the *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *ekaviṃśa*; the *ārbhava* is the *triṇava*; the *agniṣṭoma* is the *trayastriṃśa*; the *uktha* stotras follow in descending order, with the *triṇava* first; two [stotras] are *ekaviṃśa* along with the *ṣoḍaśin*; the night-stotra is the *pañcadaśa*; the *saṃdhi* is the *trivṛt*. "One desiring prosperity should sacrifice with the *sarvastoma* *atirātra*"—this is stated in the [relevant] section. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:

The *upavasathīya* introductory day belongs to the *sarvastoma*. On its own verses, the *śyaita* [sāman] is the *parisvān* for the *ārbhavapavamāna*; the *jarābodhīya* follows the *saṃhitā*; and the *ātharvaṇa* follows the *āndhīgava*. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as the first thousand-fold [offering]. || 2 ||
For him, there is the Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra with the Ṣoḍaśin cup.

Thus: "belonging to the Ārbhava" means the *gāyatrī* verse beginning with "Ārbhava"; "the *upadrava*" refers to the *bahiṣpavamāna*; "agna ā no mitrāmitraṃ vayam aindram id gāthina indre agne"—these are the *ājya* verses.

The *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* [stotras] are performed with the hymn beginning "Asya pratna" (*RV 9.1.1*). In the first [verse], the *samanta* is used with "Parīto ṣiñcatā sutam" (*RV 9.1.6*). The *rathantara* and *dairghaśravasa* are for the two triplets. The *yaudhājaya* is for the *adhyāsya*; "Ayaṃ soma" (*RV 9.1.60*) is the final *pārtha*. The *bṛhat*, *vāmadevya*, *śyaita*, and *kāleya* are the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras]. The *jarābodhīya* is the *gāyatrasaṃhita* with "Parisvāno giriṣṭhā" (*RV 9.86.25*). The *saphaśrudhya* is with "Pavasvendramaccha" (*RV 9.97.27*).
The *śyāvāśvāndhīgava* is with "Purojitī va" (*RV 9.41.1*). There is also the *ātharvaṇa*. The final *kāva* is with verses containing the word "sūrya."

The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *sākamaśva*, *saubhara*, and *nārmedha* are the *uktha*s. The *gaurīvita* is the *ṣoḍaśi-sāman*. The night is of the *āhīnika* type. The *sandhi* is archetypal (*prākṛta*). From this point onward, because the stomas are prescribed by the Brāhmaṇa itself, they are not mentioned in the *ārṣeya-kalpa*. 3.
Thus ends the Sarvastoma Atiratra. ||2||

The Aptoryāma sacrifice: Now follows the Aptoryāma. The *bahiṣpavamāna* stotra consists of the *trivṛt* (nine-versed) hymn; the *ājya* stotras consist of the *pañcadaśa* (fifteen-versed) hymns; the *mādhyandina-pavamāna* consists of the *saptadaśa* (seventeen-versed) hymn; the *pṛṣṭha* stotra of the Hotṛ consists of the *ekaviṃśa* (twenty-one-versed) hymn; the other *pṛṣṭha* stotras consist of the *chandomas*; the *ārbhava-pavamāna* consists of the *triṇava* (twenty-seven-versed) hymn; and the *agniṣṭoma* consists of the *trayastriṃśa* (thirty-three-versed) hymn. The *uktha* stotras follow in descending order: first the *triṇava*, then the *ekaviṃśa*, and then the *saptadaśa*.

The twenty-first [stoma], the sixteenfold, and the fifteenfold night with a threefold *saṃdhi*, having a threefold first *atirikta-stotra*, then a fifteenfold, then a seventeenfold, and then a twenty-onefold—this is stated in the Anuvāka. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:

for the third thousand [of verses] of the Aptoryāman, the *ājya-bahiṣpavamāna* belongs to the *jarābodhīya*; in the place of the *surūpa*, one extracts the *ātharvaṇa*. "Pari pra dhanva" is the *svarnidhana* belonging to the *sauhaviṣa*. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as before.
The Vaiśvajita days are the embryos of the Pṛṣṭha days. || 3 ||
The *anubrāhmaṇa* [contains] the supplementary stotras. 4.

Thus, the method for the *garbha* (intercalary day) has been explained by the author of the *Nidāna-sūtra*. Regarding that, they say the rule for the *garbha* is: one should make the middle *paryāya* the *garbha*, including the *sāman* for the singers; the first and last [paryāyas] belong to the principal [day]. In this way, the occurrence of the *garbha* comes about. This very *aptoryāma* with the *bṛhat* as the *pṛṣṭha-stotra* was stated by the author of the *Kalpa-sūtra*. However, the author of the *Sūtra* has shown many variations of the *aptoryāma*. The *garbhas* performed in the *aptoryāma* are according to the *kalpa*; or the *rathantara* may be the *pṛṣṭha-stotra*.

In its place is the *bārhata* [sāman] *vājajit*. The *bṛhat* and *vāravantīya* are the two subsequent *pṛṣṭha* [stotras]. The *vāravantīya* is upon the verses (*ṛk*) of the *kāleya*; in its place is the former [the *kāleya*]. And the *kāleya* is for *samanta*. The *auśana* is for *pārtha*. These same [sāmans] are the embryos within the *pṛṣṭhas*: such is one view.

Now he states what is common to both this [present] position and that which was declared in the Kalpa: "Dhānaṃjayya says one should place the *garbhas* within the *ājya* chants other than the *vaiśvajita*; the *ukthas* belonging to the sixth day within the *ukthas*. Even in this position, there is no *garbha* for the *yajñāyajñīya*. According to the opinion of Śāṇḍilya, in both positions, the *garbhas* belong only to the *pṛṣṭhas*. Thus he says:

"Śāṇḍilya says it should be performed exactly according to the *Arṣeyakalpa*. According to his opinion, he states another ritual procedure: "In the Jyotiṣṭoma or the Atirātra, one should add the *atirikta-stotras* [extra chants] as being possessed of the *ṣoḍaśin*. These very [chants] are the *garbhas* (intercalary elements) within the *pṛṣṭhas*, and the *yajñāyajñīya* is the *bṛhat-garbha*. This is called the Jyotis-Aptoryāma. However, the author of the *Nidāna* says: "Alternatively, one should make all the *āvartins* possess *garbhas* by means of the *vaiśvajita-āvartins*."

"In that [rite], the Bṛhat [Sāman] moves about; for him, the Vairūpa [is used] by way of support. Here, first of all, the performance of the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha is described, relying on the opinion of Nidānakāra. In that regard, everything is like the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha Atirātra. However, the distinction is as follows: the Bahiṣpavamāna [stotra] consists of [the verses] "O Savitṛ, [impel] our speech," "Shining with light," and "Of you, O Sage, who purifies. The Ājya [stotras] consist of "Agni, the messenger," "To us, O Mitra," "Indra, the singers [praise]," and "O Indra and Agni, come hither. In the four-verse [Ājya], the last verse is omitted.

"Suṣamiddho na āvaha... (VS 15.48), "tā naḥ śaktam... (VS 15.49), "pārthivasya... (VS 15.50), "yuñjanti bradhnam... (VS 15.51), and "tam īḍiṣva yo arciṣā... (VS 15.52) are the *garbhas* (intermediate verses) of the *ājya* offerings. Regarding the verse "suṣamiddha," one should omit the second *ṛc* for the lineages of Śunaka, Kaṇva, Saṃkṛti, and Vādhryaśva, while for others, the third *ṛc* is omitted. During the time of the silent recitation (*japa*) of the *ṛcs*, the recitation of the *ṛcs* for those who have *garbhas* and for those who do not follows this sequence.

In that regard, having praised the first round (*paryāya*) of the first *ājya* chant with the fifteen-fold hymn (*pañcadaśastoma*) using the triplet beginning with "Agni as the messenger" (*agnim dūtam*), they should praise the second round with the triplet beginning with "Well-kindled" (*suṣamiddha*). Again, they should praise the third round with "Agni as the messenger. This should be understood to apply likewise to the subsequent *ājya* chants as well.

Now follows the Mādhyandina Pavamāna. "Asya pratnāmanudyutim" is the Gāyatra and the Cāmahīyava; "parīto ṣi" is the Samanta in the first verse; the Rathantara in three verses; the Dairghaśravasa in three verses; the Yaudhājaya in the Adhyāsya verse; and "ayaṃ soma" is the final Pārtha—thus it is the Saptadaśa Stoma. The *kakubh* of the Rathantara has the Bṛhatī as its meter.

The sounds of chariots and so forth, which were mentioned in the passage beginning with "they should drive the chariot over the *pṛṣṭhya*," are the duties (*dharma*) pertaining to the *pṛṣṭha* that must be performed here. Regarding how these duties are to be performed, some say: "They are to be performed as being like a fetus (*garbha*), not yet fully developed. This is because of the statement in the *Nidāna*: "The *pṛṣṭha* becomes a fetus; it becomes a non-duty (*adharma*). Here, during the chanting of the *rathantara* at the *pavamāna*, they should drive the chariot, which is situated behind outside the sacrificial ground (*vedī*), toward the east. The *bṛhat* is its *pṛṣṭha*, and the *vairāja* is its fetus.

The *stoma* is the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*). The specific feature for the *pṛṣṭha-homa* is: "May they drink the Soma-mead; may the Adhvaryu bestow it upon the lord of the sacrifice. The *virāṭ* is the metre of the *vairāja*. The prescriptive *brāhmaṇa* begins with: "Drink the Soma, O Indra; let them exhilarate thee," and so forth. "Spring is the *hiṃkāra*" refers to the meditation on the constituent parts (*bhakti*). Prior to the application of the *stoma*, there is the meditation on the ten *vyāhṛtis*, beginning with: "The *bṛhat* is indeed the *aira*," and so on.

When the *stotra* has been introduced with the two fire-drills and the two blades of *darbha* grass, the Udgātṛ priest takes those two fire-drills and the two blades of *darbha* grass; he places a piece of wood and the two blades of *darbha* grass upon his own right thigh, lays the lower fire-drill (*araṇī*) crosswise upon the piece of wood, and places the upper fire-drill upon that; then he should churn it three times clockwise, [reciting]: "Be born following the Gāyatrī metre! Be born following the Triṣṭubh metre!"

The joining of the two kindling woods is performed with the mantra: "O Jāgata meter, be born after me. Having touched them with both hands, he should smell them with his hands while reciting: "Thou art splendor; bestow splendor upon me. Then, while the fire is being churned by another, having yoked the Stoma and caused the sound of drums to be made, they should chant the first round of the twenty-one-fold Stoma with the Bṛhat Sāman. While lighting the churned fire with another, they should chant the middle round with the Vairāja Sāman.
Again, causing the sound of drums to be made, they should complete the final round with the Bṛhat Sāman.

Having caused the sacrificer to recite the formula ending with *punarūrjā* and *spārhā*, he should consecrate the churned fire with that mantra. When it has been cast into the Āhavanīya by the Adhvaryu, he should offer an oblation with the Virāj verse *preddho agne*, ending with *svāhā*. Then [he should chant] the *Svāhā* and the Vāmadevya, the Sāman of Mitrāvaruṇa. Its embryo consists of the Mahānāmnīs; its Stoma is the Caturviṃśa; the metre of the Mahānāmnīs is the Śakvarī. "Indra approached Prajāpati"—this is the prescriptive Brāhmaṇa.

"Earth is the *hiṃkāra*"—this is a meditative worship (*bhakty-upāsana*) based on a figurative identification. Prior to the application of the *stoma*, there is the meditation: "Cows are horses. When the hymn has been commenced with water mixed with *śaivāla* moss and two blades of *darbha* grass, one should take those two blades of *darbha*, place the water nearby, and complete the first round (*paryāya*) with the *Vāmadevya* chant. Then they should chant the middle round with the *Śakvarī* verses. In that regard, whoever recites a constituent part of the *sāman* should produce a loud sound toward the north. The rule for the *kuśā* grass applies specifically to the first *prastāva*.

In the second and subsequent recitations, the *udgītha* is not commenced with the syllable *oṃ*. Immediately after the final repetition, there is praise with the *purīṣa* verses beginning with "āivā. Having thus completed the middle round (*paryāya*), they should perform the third round with the *Vāmadevya* chant. After performing the address to the sacrificer (*yajamānavācana*), he should pour that water onto the *āstāva* with the formula ending in "anādhṛṣṭāsi videya" (you are unassailable; may I find [the world]). He should place moss upon his knees. Then follows the recitation (*japa*). The *Śyaita* is the *Brahmasāman*; its embryo is the *Vairūpa*.

The forty-fourfold hymn-form (*stoma*). "O Indra, if [there were] a hundred [of you]"—thus they consist of verses containing the word "hundred," and so forth; this is the *brāhmaṇa* of the *vairūpa* chant. "The clouds gather together"—this is the meditative visualization (*abhidhyāna*). "I take refuge in the two *sāmans*, Śyaita and Vairūpa. "I take refuge in the two verses, 'Abhipravas' and 'Yadyāva'. "I take refuge in the seers Prajāpati and Viśvarūpa. "I take refuge in the forty-fourfold *stoma*"; such is the specific procedure for the ritual approach (*upasaraṇa*).

When the *stotra* has been introduced with two *darbha* blades as fans, one of those fans should be placed in the hands of the attendants of the sacrificer. Having completed one round (*paryāya*) with the *śyaita* [Sāman], they should chant the middle round with the *vairūpa* [Sāman] while being fanned with the fan. Again, having caused the sacrificer to recite the final round with the *śyaita*, one should produce wind for him with the fan and consecrate that wind with the three-verse hymn beginning with "May that wind blow" (*taṃ vāta āvātu*). The *kāleya* is the *acchāvāka*-sāman; its womb is the *revatī* verses.

The *stoma* is the forty-eight-fold. He utters the *hiṃ* for sixteen verses; this is the *pathyā* *viṣṭuti*. The *gāyatrī* is the metre of the *revatī* verses. "The other metres have their strength exhausted," and so forth, says the Brāhmaṇa. Having completed one round (*paryāya*) with the *kāleya* [sāman], they should chant the middle round with the *revatī* verses. At the chanting of those verses, having placed the cows to the south and the calves to the north, they should mutter the lowing of the cows.

Again, at the time of the excellent recitation (*paryāya*), having praised [the cows], and having swept the *sadas* with the cowherds and calves as before, they should throw these [cows] toward the west and the *āgnīdhrīya* fire toward the north. Having caused the sacrificer to recite, he should consecrate them with the names of cows, beginning with "O Havyā, O Kāmyā" and ending with "vośīya. If they have been marked with water, then he should pour that water into the *āstāva* with the three verses beginning with "āpo hi ṣṭhā. Now follows the *ārbhava-pavamāna* stotra consisting of the *triṇava* stoma: "pari svāno giriṣṭhā," the *gāyatra-saṃhitā*, and the *surūpa* verses.

"Pavasva indram accha" is for Saphaśrudhya; "purojitī" is for Śyāvāśva Āndhīgava; "pari pra dhanva" is for the Akṣarapaṅktis, with the *svar* finale and the *sauhaviṣa* [chant]. Among the verses containing the word "sūrya," the last is the *kāva*. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. Its *bṛhadgarbha* [interlude] is "tvam agne yajñānām. The *stoma* is the thirty-three-fold (*trayastriṃśa*). It is performed with the *viṣṭutis* beginning with "he utters *hiṃ* for eleven [verses]," etc. The *chandas* is the Gāyatrī of the *Bṛhat*. This is the meditation on the ten *vyāhṛtis*.

And the sound of the drum is as before. Regarding the phrase "nājāigyūṣā," it should be stated here that [the root] *ṣūṣ* belongs to the *krā* class. In the final verse of the hymn (*stotrottamā*), [one should recite] *pratya*...

Because of the prescription of the *avaroha* (descent). Here, although the defect of monotony (*jāmitva*) would have resulted from both the prescription of the *pṛṣṭha* and the *agniṣṭoma* being praised with the *bṛhat* immediately following the *rathantara*, it is avoided by means of the *śyeta* [sāman] which flows toward [the former]. And thus, concerning the causes of monotony, the *Nidāna* states: "The *kaṇvarathantara* carries [the chant] across; the *rathantara*-finale [sāmans] are used in conjunction with the *bṛhat*.
