Now, the *uktha* [stotras]: the *sākamaśva* is "ehyū ṣu"; the *saubhara* is "vayamu tve".

"Adhāhīndra" is the Nārmedha hymn; these [three] have, respectively, the Triṇava, Ekaviṃśa, and Saptadaśa stomas. They have no *garbhas* (intercalary verses), because they themselves function as *ukthas* in the Viśvajit sacrifice. Others, however, manifest the *garbhas* here—those mentioned in the alternative view regarding the *ukthas* of the sixth day—as follows: for the Sākamaśva, the *gūrda*; for the Saubhara, the *bhadra*; and for the Nārmedha, the "son of Udvamśa. The meter of the *garbhas* is the *dvipadā*. Thus the rule for the *garbhas* has been stated.

This confusion of the two positions is not pleasing to us. Now, [the sequence] begins with the *ṣoḍaśin* and ends with the *saṃdhi-stotra*. Therein, at night, one should recite the *panya* hymn for each respective occasion; the *hotṛṣāman* of Daivodāsa is constant. In the section belonging to Kautsa, the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* hymn is used; the specific rule is that it is applied to the verses beginning with "ā tvā viśantvindavaḥ."

Four additional *stotras* have been prescribed by the Brāhmaṇa. In that context, after the drinking from the *saṃdhi-camasa*, and having performed the rites beginning with the exit (*niṣkramaṇa*) and ending with the invitation of the sacrificer (*yajamānopahava*), they should chant their own [stotras] with the *jarābodhīya* *trivṛt* stoma. The seers and other details are "Agni is the Gāyatrī, Agni... and so forth. The *viṣṭuti* is the *parivartinī*. The consumption [of the soma] is with the formula "having the Gāyatrī metre," because of the statement: "In the additional *stotras*, [the consumption is] with the Gāyatrī metre," according to Gautama.

Then, having performed the rites from the exit (*niṣkramaṇa*) up to the invitation (*upahava*), they should chant their own *sāman*s with the *satrāsāhīya*, a fifteen-versed hymn; Indra is the deity, the Gāyatrī the metre. Having consumed [the soma] as before, and having again performed the rites from the exit up to the invitation, they should chant their own *sāman*s with the *mārgīyava*, a seventeen-versed hymn; Indra is the deity, the Gāyatrī the metre, and the Viśve Devāḥ [are also present]. The consumption is as before. Having again performed the rites up to the invitation, they should chant with the *vāravantīya*, a twenty-one-versed hymn, using the verse "idaṃ viṣṇuḥ"; Indra is the deity, the Gāyatrī the metre, and Viṣṇu [is the deity]. The consumption is as before. Then follows the sequence from the dismissal of the *stoma* up to the *uvadasanīya*.
Thus concludes the Aptoryāma sacrifice with the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha stotra.

In the Rathantara-pṛṣṭha sacrifice, however, the Kāleya [Sāman] is placed in the position of the Samanta upon that same ṛc; in the position of the Rathantara, it is on those very same verses. The Vājijit [Sāman], beginning with "mṛjyamānaḥ suhastya," is at the end. In the position of the Pārtha, the Auśana is on its own verses. The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, and the Bṛhat are on their own verses; and the Vāravantīya is on the verses of the Kāleya—these are the pṛṣṭhas. The Vāravantīya is in the position of the [Sāman] beginning with "idaṃ viṣṇuḥ" on that same triplet of verses.

One should transpose the *vāravantīya* chant at the beginning; everything else is like the *bṛhat-pṛṣṭha* *aptoryāma*. However, in the *jyotis-aptoryāma*, the *vairāja* and other chants of the *jyotiṣṭoma* are the embryos (*garbha*), as before. For the *yajñāyajñīya*, however, "O Agni, of sacrifices... is the *bṛhat*-embryo. After the *saṃdhi* [stotra], there are the *atirikta* stotras. Everything else is like the *jyotis-atirātra*. Some, moreover, desire that in the *jyotis-atirātra* which is devoid of embryos, the *atirikta* stotras should follow immediately after the *saṃdhi* stotras.
That [measure] must be investigated. The other options for the Aptoryāma, however, are clear. Thus ends the Aptoryāma. 3.

The Seventeenth [Chapter] on the *Navasaptadaśa*. Now begins the seventeenth [chapter]. The *Bahiṣpavamāna* chant is threefold (*trivṛt*). The *Ājya* chant of the Hotṛ is fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*). The *Stotras* are seventeenfold (*saptadaśa*). The *Agniṣṭoma* is twenty-onefold (*ekaviṃśa*). It includes the *Ukthas*. The night [chant] is fifteenfold. The *Sandhi* is threefold. This is stated in the section beginning with "by means of the *Atirātra* consisting of nine seventeenfold [stotras]. The meaning of "the *Stotras* are nine seventeenfold" is that the nine *Stotras*, beginning from the *Ājya* of the Maitrāvaruṇa up to the end of the *Ārbhava*, are seventeenfold. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows.

The *sākamaśva* [stotra] follows the *āmahīyava* in the ninth seventeen-versed [laud]: "Flow on, most honey-sweet" (*pavasva madhumattama*). The *janitra* [stotra] consists of the *raurava* and *yaudhājaya* chants: "The Soma-drops, the Āyus... (*abhi somāsa āyavaḥ*). The *janitra* for the *naudhasa* is found among its verses. The *sapha* [stotra] is: "He runs forth all around" (*pari pra dhanve*). (1) Everything else is the same as the *jyotiṣṭoma* performed as an *atirātra* without the *ṣoḍaśin* cup. (2)

Thus: the *bahiṣpavamāna* consists of the *upāṃśu* and *vipruṣ* [verses]. The *ājya* hymns are "O Agni, come to us" and "O Indra and Agni. The *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* chants are "High is thy birth, O Soma, the juice. The *sākamaśva* is in one [verse], "Flow on, most rich in honey," because of the statement: "The *kakubh* here at the midday [pressing] is in that single verse. The *janitra* is in one [verse], "The Soma-drops, the living ones..."

When forming single-verse stanzas (*ekarca*), one should place them at the beginning of the first [round]; this is because of the statement: "If there is one or two [verses] at the midday pressing, they should be placed in the *bṛhatī* [metre] itself. This is the former *janitra*. The *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, and the latter *janitra* among the verses of the *naudhasa*; the *kāleya* in its own [verses]—these are the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras]. The *gāyatrasaṃhita* is "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā. The *sapha* and *pauṣkala* are the single-verse stanzas "pari pra dhanva indram accha" and "purojitī vo andhasaḥ. The *śyāvāśva* and *āndhīgava* are "purojitī vaḥ."

The Kāvamantya [is the stotra]. The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. The Sākamaśva, Saubhara, and Nārmedha are the Ukthas. The Ṣoḍaśin is not to be performed. The junction (saṃdhi) is the night of the Ahīna sacrifice. || 2 ||
Thus ends the nineteenth [chapter] of the ninth [section]. 4.

The Viṣuvat Atirātra sacrifice: now follows the Viṣuvat. The Bahiṣpavamāna is the Trivṛt; the Ājya-stotras are Pañcadaśa; the Mādhyandina Pavamāna is Pañcadaśa; the Pṛṣṭha-stotras are Saptadaśa; the Ārbhava is Saptadaśa; the Agniṣṭoma is Ekaviṃśa; the Uktha-stotras are Saptadaśa; the night [stotras] are Pañcadaśa; the *saṃdhi* is Trivṛt. This is declared by the section beginning with "By means of the Viṣuvat Atirātra. Its ritual arrangement (*klṛpti*) is as follows:
That which belongs to the Jyotiṣṭoma belongs to the Viṣuvat; its Ukthya-stotras consist of seventeen verses, and it is an Atirātra without a Ṣoḍaśin. || 1 ||
Thus: for that [sacrifice], everything is like the Atirātra; the Ukthas are seventeen-fold; the Viśeṣa is that there is no Ṣoḍaśī cup. || 1 ||
Thus ends the Viṣuvant Atirātra.

Regarding the Go and Āyus [sacrifices], the Bahiṣpavamāna stotra is fifteen-fold; thus, by means of these two sections, the Go and Āyus are prepared and prescribed. Their ritual procedure is the "preparation" (kalpa) of the Go and Āyus. 1.
Thus, by the [verses] beginning with "The world of Vārkajaṃbha" and "The world of Āyu," the day and night of those two are established; their night is equal to a single day. (1)
Thus [are performed] the Go and Āyus [Sāmans] at the Atirātra [sacrifice].

The *viśvajit* and *abhijit* sacrifices have the *trivṛt* *bahiṣpavamāna* and the *pañcadaśa* *hotṛ-ājya*. Thus, the *abhijit* *atirātra* is described in the eighth section (*anuvāka*), and the *viśvajit* in the ninth. Their ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
the *viśvajit* and *abhijit* are fully established. (1)

Thus, the *klṛpti* (preparation) for the Abhijit is by means of the verses beginning with "abhi pra gopatiṃ girā," and that for the Viśvajit is by means of those beginning with "pavasvendramaccha. For these two, the night is that of the *āhīnika* (daily performance). || 1 ||
Thus [are explained] the Viśvajit and Abhijit sacrifices. || 7 ||

There are four sacrifices with a single *stoma*, and then another four with a single *stoma*. The first is declared by the section beginning, "With the *atirātra* of the *trivṛt*"; the second is "with the *atirātra* of the *pañcadaśa*"; the third is "with the *atirātra* of the *saptadaśa*"; and the fourth is "with the *atirātra* of the *ekaviṃśa*."
Thus end the four sacrifices consisting of a single stoma.
The Trivṛt Atirātra:
therein, the rule for the first [day] is that which belongs to the first of the Ekastomas of the Bṛhaspatisava; its Jyotiṣṭoma is an Atirātra accompanied by the Ṣoḍaśin cup. || 1 ||

Thus: up to the Agniṣṭoma, it is like the Bṛhaspatisava; from the Sākamaśva onwards, it is like the Jyotiṣṭoma. All the stotras are *trivṛt*; however, the *ṣoḍaśin* is either *ṣoḍaśa* or *trivṛt*. Regarding this, he will say: "The *ṣoḍaśins* are [performed] with the *anubrāhmaṇa* of the *ṣoḍaśins*. ||1||
Thus ends the Trivṛd-atirātra sacrifice. || 8 ||
The fifteenth day is an Atirātra.
He prescribes a second [set of] one-stoma [laud-s].

The Bahiṣpavamāna has the Gaurīvita Sāman. The Mādhyandina [Pavamāna] belongs to the Indra-stoma. "O Soma, being purified, flow with thy stream"—this is a Bṛhatī verse. The Śyaita [Sāman] is performed on its own [verses]. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as the first thousand. || 2 ||
For him, the Jyotiṣṭoma is an Atirātra sacrifice accompanied by the Ṣoḍaśin cup.
"Thus: 'Flow on as the leader of speech, with flashing luster; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull; O Soma, you are a bull, you are brilliant.
'Of you, the purifying sage,' [with these verses] is the Bahiṣpavamāna."
The *ājya* hymns begin with "We choose Agni as the messenger. The *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* chants follow with "High is thy [flame]," and the *samanta* with "Being purified, he..."

And [the *stotras*] are the Yaudhājaya and the Vṛṣaśoṇa; the Pārtha is the last. And the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] are the Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita, and the Kāleya. The Gāyatra-saṃhita is with the verse beginning "svādiṣṭhayā"; the Saphaśrudhya is with the verse beginning "pavasvendram accha. The Śyāvāśvāndhīgava is with the verse beginning "purojitī vaḥ. The Kāva is the last, [performed] on verses containing the word "sūrya. The Saphaśrudhya, the Śyāvāśva, and the others are performed on single-verse [hymns]. The Agniṣṭoma-sāman is the Yajñāyajñīya. Starting from the Sākamaśva, it is like the Jyotiṣṭoma. The night is of the *āhīnika* type.

Every [stotra] is fifteen-fold; the sixteenth is either the sixteenth [verse] or the fifteenth. However, for the sake of completing the fifteenth at the juncture (*saṃdhi*), an insertion (*āvāpa*) or a repetition (*abhyāsa*) must be performed. As it has been said: "Now, regarding the juncture, there is insertion or repetition. In that regard, according to the position favoring repetition, the *viṣṭuti* (method of chanting) is: "He utters the *hiṃkāra* five times. || 13 ||
Thus ends the fifteenth Atirātra.

The seventeenth day is an Atirātra; he prescribes the third [pressing] as having a single-stoma, with the Ājya and Bahiṣpavamāna chants of the Tīvrasut [Soma] for both the morning and the midday pressings. ||1||
The rest is the same as the first [rite] with a single-stoma.

Thus: "Upāsmai," "avidyutatyā rucā," "ete asṛgramindavaḥ," "taṃ tvā nṛmṇāni bibhratam," and "pavamānasya te kave"—these constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna*. The *ājya* hymns are: "agna ā yāhi," "mitrāya," and "indrāgnī. The *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* chants are performed with the verse "uccā te. In the first [verse], there is a double *hiṅkāra* for the hymn beginning "abhi somāsa āyavaḥ. The *maidhātitha* chant is performed over three verses; the *yaudhājaya* on the middle verse; and the *auśana* on the final verse.

From the *pṛṣṭha* chants up to the conclusion of the *saṃdhi-stotra*, it is like the Jyotiṣṭoma; the distinction is that everything has the seventeenfold (*saptadaśa*) *stoma*. Or else, there is the *ṣoḍaśin*; the night belongs to the *āhīnika-ṣoḍaśin*. 1.2.2.
Thus ends the seventeenth *atirātra*.
The twenty-first [day] is an Atirātra.
He states the first Stoma for the fourth [day]:
the Bahiṣpavamāna of the Pratīcīnastoma; on both sides is the Gāyatrī; for the subsequent Jyotis [stoma], the Bṛhatī. ||1||
The rest is the same as the second [rite] with a single-stoma. ||2||

Thus: "Of the Jyotis, the latter" means "of the bird [stoma], the latter. Here, by the qualification "the latter," there is an exclusion of the first of the thousand-fold stomas. The *bahiṣpavamāna* consists of: *pavasva vāco pavasvendro davidyutatyā rucā*, *ete asṛgramindavo*, *vṛṣā soma dyumānasi*, *vṛṣā hyasi bhānunā*, and *pavamānasya te kave*. The four-verse hymn consists of: *agniṃ dūtam*, *mitraṃ vayaṃ*, *indramidgāthinaḥ*, and *indraṃ vo viśvataspari*. The *ājya* hymns consist of: *indre agne*.

"Uccā te gāyatram," "cāmahīyavam," and "satrāsāhīyam"; "punaḥ soma dhāraya"—these are the [stotras] for the entire [sacrifice], as well as the yaudhājaya and auśana at the end. The *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] consist of the bṛhat, vāmadevya, śyaita, and kāleya. The two verses beginning with "svādiṣṭhayā" constitute the gāyatra-saṃhita; "pavasva indram accha" constitutes the sapha-śrudhya; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" constitutes the śyāvāśva-andhīgava; and those containing the word "sūrya" constitute the kāva at the end. From the yajñāyajñīya onwards, up to the conclusion of the *saṃdhi-stotra*, it is like the jyotiṣṭoma.

The night belongs to the Āhīna sacrifice. Everything is twenty-one-fold; the distinction is that it is either a *ṣoḍaśa* or a *ṣoḍaśin*. (12) Regarding the arrangement of the *stomas* for the *ṣoḍaśins* among those sacrifices having a single *stoma*, he says:
"The *ṣoḍaśa* [is used] for the *ṣoḍaśins*, or according to the *Anubrāhmaṇa*. (3)

Thus [it is said]. On this point, the Sūtra states: "Or according to the *Anubrāhmaṇa*. Because of its connection with the archetype (*prakṛti*), the Stoma is twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*). The prima facie view (*pūrva-pakṣa*) is that because of the connection with the archetypal Stomas such as the *Sandhi-kāra*, the *Ṣoḍaśin* is twenty-one-fold. The established conclusion (*siddhānta*), however, is that it is the Stoma of the day (*aha-stoma*). Consequently, this is the meaning of the ritual manual (*kalpa*): either the Stomas of the *Ṣoḍaśin* for the single-day rites should be sixteen-fold; or else, whatever Stoma is prescribed by that Brāhmaṇa passage beginning with "for each respective day, by means of the *Trivṛt* Atirātra," that Stoma should be used. And so it has been illustrated; thus the thirteen-night *Atirātra* has been described. ||3||
Thus ends the twenty-first Atirātra. || 11 ||
The Ekastomas are completed.
There are three *dvirātra* sacrifices;
first, the *Aṅgirasadvirātra*.
Then there are three more *dvirātra*s. The *Aṅgirasadvirātra* is described in the section beginning with "The first day is the *Jyotiṣṭoma-agniṣṭoma*. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:

Those two days which belong to the *vyuṣṭi*-dvirātra are extracted for the later day of the *āṅgirasa*-dvirātra as the *ṛṣabha* and *jarābodhīya*. The *antarātharvaṇa* is for the *samanta-dairghaśravas*. The *jarābodhīya* follows the *saṃhitā*. The *śrudhya* is in the place of the *viśoviśīya*. || 1 ||

Thus: for the first day, the *bahiṣpavamāna* is "upāsmai gāyatā naraḥ. The *ājya* hymns are "agna ā yāhi," "mitrāya," and "indrāgnī. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* with "uccā te jātam andhasaḥ"; the *raurava* and *yaudhājaya* with "punānaḥ soma dhārayā"; and the *auśana* as the final one. The *pṛṣṭha* chants are the *rathantara*, *vāmadevya*, *naudhasa*, and *kāleya*. The *ārbhava-pavamāna* consists of the *gāyatra* and *hāviṣkṛta* with "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā"; and the *sapha* and *pauṣkala* on the single-verse sections "ayā pavasva devayuḥ" and "pavate haryato hariḥ. The *audala* and *āndhīgava* are on "purojitī vo andhasaḥ"; and the *kāva* is the final one.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *jyotiṣṭoma* consists of the *stomas*. The day concludes with the consumption of curd.

For the second day: "Flow on as the leader of speech; this immortal god... he goes with subtle wisdom; [grant] your skill that brings bliss"—with these verses is the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant performed. By means of that, the chanting takes place in the *sadas*. According to the injunction, "They should chant in the *sadas* with the *bahiṣpavamānas* of the *ahīna* sacrifices, except for the first day," they should depart before the distribution of the *dhiṣṇya* hearths and complete the rite starting from the scattering of grass. The *ājya* offerings are with the verse, "We choose Agni as the messenger."

For this [hymn], the *gāyatra* and *hāviṣmat* [verses] begin with "asya pratna-"; the verse beginning with "parīto ṣi" is for the first [day] on all sides; the two triplets are for the Ātharvaṇa and Dairghaśravasa [sāmans]; the *utsedha* is for the *adhyāsya*; and the final [verse] beginning with "ayaṃ soma" is the *pārtha*.

The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *traiśoka*, and the *vaikhānasa*. The *gāyatrasaṃhitā*, *jarābodhīya*, and [stotras] beginning with "parisvāno giriṣṭhā" [are used]. The *satrāsāhīya* and *śrudhya* [stotras] are those beginning with "pavasvendramaccha. The *niṣedha* is "ayaṃ pūṣā," and the *krauñca* is the *śyāvāśva*. The final *arka* is that of Dīrghatamas, beginning with "dhartā divaḥ. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *sākamaśva*, *saubhara*, and *nārmedha* are the *uktha* stotras. The *ṣoḍaśin-sāman* is the *gaurīvita*. The *sandhi* is the night of the *āhīnika* [rite].

Now, the Stomas: the Bahiṣpavamāna is twenty-four-fold; the Ājyastotras are fifteen-fold; the Mādhyandina Pavamāna is seventeen-fold; the Pṛṣṭhas are twenty-one-fold; the Ārbhava is twenty-seven-fold; the Agniṣṭoma is thirty-three-fold. The Ukthas descend: the first is twenty-seven-fold, then twenty-one-fold, then seventeen-fold. The Ṣoḍaśī is twenty-one-fold; the Night-stotra is fifteen-fold; the Saṃdhi is nine-fold. Thus [ends section 1].
Thus ends the two-night rite of the Aṅgirases. 12.
Regarding Caitraratha: now, by means of the section beginning with "jyotirukthyaḥ," the Caitraratha sacrifice has been described. Its ritual procedure (kalpa) is as follows:
that which is the first day of the Aṅgirasa Dvirātra belongs to the Caitraratha; its Ukthas are those of the Āyuṣ.
"Of the former" means the arrangement of the preceding day. The *pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *udvaṃśīya* are the *uktha* chants of the twenty-one-fold stoma. ||1||
[Thus ends the first day. He speaks the second day:
"Flow on, the foremost of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. May thy skill bring us bliss. (RV 9.101.2)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
In this world, the *jarābodhīya* chant belongs to Śrudhya; they approach the night from the *nārmedha*. Now, that which is the final day of the two-day rite is this very [day]. || 3 ||

"Thus: *Pavasva vāco agriyaḥ*, *pavasvendo vṛṣā sutaḥ*, *ā te dakṣaṃ mayo bhuvam*—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna. *Agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe*—these are the Ājya [stotras]. *Asya pratnāmanu dyutam*—this is both the Gāyatra and the Hāviṣmat. *Parīto ṣiñcatā madhu* is for the first [verse]; the Dairghaśravasa [Sāman] is for three [verses]; the Aiḍa-Āyāsya is for three [verses]; the Triṇidhana-Āyāsya is for the middle [verse]. *Ayaṃ somaḥ*—this is the final Pārtha."

The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *traiśoka*, and the *vaikhānasa*. The *gāyatrasaṃhita* consists of the verses beginning with "yaste madaḥ. The *satrāsāhīya* and *jarābodhīya* consist of the verses beginning with "pavasvendram accha. The *śyāvāśva* and *krauñca* consist of the verses beginning with "ayaṃ pūṣā. The final *arka* of Dīrghatamas consists of the verses beginning with "dhartā divaḥ. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *uktha* stotras are the *sākamaśva*, the *saubhara*, and the *nārmedha*. There is no *ṣoḍaśin* chant, because of the scriptural injunction: "They enter the night [rite] after the *nārmedha*."
The night of the *āhīnika* is the junction (*saṃdhi*). According to the Brāhmaṇa, "The *āyuḥ* [stoma] is the *atirātra* as the subsequent [part]"; thus, these are the stomas of the *āyurātra*.
Thus ends [the section on] Caitraratha. 13.
The Kāpivana [rite]: Now, by the section beginning with "He whose Agniṣṭoma has fifteen [stotras]," the Kāpivana Dvirātra is described. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
those two days which belong to the Caitraratha [Dvirātra] are [the same for] the Kāpivana; [it consists of] an Agniṣṭoma with the Trivṛt and Pañcadaśa [stomas].
The *mahar* [stoma] is first, the *atirātra* is last. ||1||

Thus: everything for the first day is like that of Caitraratha; however, the *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* *stomas* are reversed, and in the *ārbhava-pavamāna*, the verses are single-verse units with the exception of the last one; the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* is the *pañcadaśa*: this is the distinction. Everything for the second day is exactly like that of Caitraratha. || 1 ||
Thus ends [the section on] Kāpivana. 14.
The three two-night sacrifices have been completed.
There are six three-night sacrifices;

first is the Garga-trirātra. Regarding the six three-night sacrifices, the Garga-trirātra is described by means of five sections beginning with "The morning pressing is the Trivṛt. He states its first day as follows:

The *ājya* and *bahiṣpavamāna* chants for the first day of the *ābhiplavika* [six-day period], as well as the midday [service], are as follows: "Upāsmai gāyata naraḥ" and "Pavamānasya te vayam," [along with] "Pavamānasya te kave," constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "Agnā ā naḥ mitrāya" and "Indrāgnī" are the *ājya* stotras. "Pra somāso vipaścitaḥ" constitutes both the *gāyatra* and the *āśva*. "Pra soma devavītaye" constitutes the *pajra*, the *yaudhājaya*, and the *auśana* as the final one.
The *yaudhājaya* with the *ekākṣaranidhana* is recited in the *ahīnakāṇḍa*. 1.

The Gargatrirātra [sacrifice] consists of the Rathantara and the Sāman called Sauparṇa with the *svāra* accentuation; the Abhīvarta [Sāman] is performed on the verses beginning with "śagdhy ū ṣu śacīpate"; and the Kāleya [Sāman] is performed on its own verses.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" is the Gāyatra; "svāśiraṃ ca arkaḥ ayā pavasva devayuḥ pavate haryato hariḥ" is the Saphākṣāra; "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ" is the Audala with the *cartanidhana* and the *ājyadoha*; and "abhi priyāṇi" is the Vaikhānasa, which is the final [stotra]. || 3 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.

At the midday pressing, having maintained the fire on the Hotṛ’s hearth (*dhiṣṇiya*) which has been spread out, they should kindle it at the time of the *ājyadoha* hymns. This is stated in the Brāhmaṇa: "They chant the *ājyadoha* hymns after placing the fire nearby," and so forth. [The following applies] to the *saphākṣara* and the single-verse hymns. || 3 ||
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.
The morning pressing consists of the *trivṛt* stoma; the midday pressing consists of the *pañcadaśa* stoma; the third pressing consists of the *saptadaśa* stoma. ||4||
Thus ends the first day. || 16 ||
The second day:

regarding the second day, he says— "Near the born one, the swift, with flashing luster, flow clear, O Indu; as a bull, pressed, the King goes forth with songs of wisdom. Flow for nourishment, O stream! (RV 9.87.1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
By what [means], O Agni Aṅgiras, do you exist even among many and far-reaching things? We incite that Indra for the sake of booty; this [is] the thought of your beautiful mind. 2.
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.

The Gāyatra [Sāman] "asya pratnāmanudyutam" and the Āmahīyava; the Gautama [Sāman] "abhisomāsa āyavaḥ," the Antarikṣa, the Dairghaśravasa, and the Dvihiṅkāra; and the Nidhana "ayaṃ soma" is the final Ājyadoha. 3.
Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.

The *Gautama* [Sāman] is for the first [turn]. The *Pra hinvānaḥ* [Sāman], with two *hiṃkāras*, is for the second turn. At the morning pressing, there is the maintenance of the Hotṛ’s hearth (*dhiṣṇya*) which has been spread out; its kindling takes place at the time of the chanting of the *Ājyadoha*. || 3 ||
The Vāmadevya [Sāman] is on its own verses; "mo ṣu tvā vāghataś ca naḥ" is the Gāyatrapārśva; "astāvi manma pūrvyam" is the Saṃtani; and the *saṃkṛti* is among the verses of the Śrayantīya. ||4||
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].

In the case of the two subsequent *stotriya* verses of the *santani*, the placement of the *kuśa* grass occurs at the very beginning; this is because of the statement: "At the beginning of those [verses] that lack a *prastāva*."

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the Gāyatra of Agni; "abhi dyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśaḥ sakhāya ā niṣīdata"—this is the Sāman of Vāk and the Śaukta. "paryū ṣu"—this is the Āndhīgava. "indrāya soma pavate"—this is the Yajñāyajñīya. "pavitraṃ te"—this is the Ariṣṭa, the final [Sāman]. || 5 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Viśoviśīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. 6.
Each according to his own lifespan, [they offer] their hymns of praise. || 7 ||

The *pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *udvaṃśīya* are the *uktha* chants. The morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*) consists of the fifteenfold stoma; the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina savana*) consists of the seventeenfold stoma; and the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*), together with its *ukthas*, consists of the twenty-onefold stoma. || 7 ||
Thus ends the second day. || 17 ||
The third day:
He speaks of the third day— "Flow on, the foremost of speech! This immortal god, this one, goes with subtle wisdom. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna. || 1 ||
We invoke the immortal divine Hotṛ, Mitra; we invoke the great Indra who [rules] by his might. To Indra and Agni be great homage. 2.
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.

"High is the birth of your juice" (*uccā te jātamandhasaḥ*)—this consists of the *gāyatra*, the *gauṣūkta*, the *jarābodhīya*, the *carṣabha*, and the *pāvamāna*. "The ancient, primordial nectar which is worthy of praise" (*pratnaṃ pīyūṣaṃ pūrvyaṃ yadukthyam*) is the *utsedha*. "Pour out the pressed [juice] on every side" (*parīto ṣiñcatā sutam*) is the *ābhīṣava* and the *pṛśni* of the Atharvans. "Three voices" (*tisro vācaḥ*) is the *triṇidhana* and the final *ājyadoha*. (3)
Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
Having placed the fire as before, there follows the recitation of the Ājyadoha hymns. 3.
The Bṛhat, the Satrāsāhīya, the Śyaita, and the Raurava. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"Pari svāno giriṣṭhā" consists of both the Gāyatra and the Hāviṣmat. "Sa sunve yo vasūnām prāṇā śiśurmahīnām" is for Dīrghaśrudhi. "Ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhaga" includes the Niṣedha, the Śyāvāśva, the Krauñca, and the Yajñāyajñīya. "Pari pra dhanva" belongs to the Vājadāvarīs; "ayā rucā" consists of the Nityavatsas. "Dhartā divaḥ" is the final hymn of Dīrghatamas. 4.
Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Vāravantīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman, [to be sung] on its own verses.
The Jyotiṣṭoma is an Atirātra sacrifice accompanied by the Ṣoḍaśin cup.

The night has twenty-one [verses]. The morning pressing has twenty-one; the midday pressing has twenty-seven; the third pressing has thirty-three; the Agniṣṭoma has thirty-four. The Uktha-stotras, including the Ṣoḍaśin, have twenty-one verses each. The first night-chant is the Ṣoḍaśin; the night has fifteen [verses]; the junction (saṃdhi) has nine. These are the Stomas for the thirty-four-fold [Agniṣṭoma], the method of chanting (viṣṭuti) for which is as follows: he utters *hiṃ* eleven times—three times, seven times, and once.

"He chants the *hiṃkāra* for eleven [verses]: he with one, he with three, he with seven. He chants the *hiṃkāra* for twelve [verses]: he with eight, he with one, he with three. And it is said: "From those of the ten-night rite, [the difference is] by one [verse] more," and so forth. The first two days end with the consumption of curd; the final day ends with the *udavasānīyā* offering.

The Śabalī-homa has been described in the Anuvāka beginning with "Speech indeed is Śabalī," and it is explained in the Sūtra starting with, "One desiring nourishment for a thousand [years] should perform the Śabalī-homa. (6)
Thus ends the third day. 18.
The Garga-trirātra is completed.

The three-night Aśvamedha sacrifice is described by this section [of the text]: the first day is a *catuṣṭoma* *agniṣṭoma* with the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*) stoma; the second is an *ukthya* with all the stomas; and the third is an *atirātra* with all the stomas. The king, having made the formal pledge, shall perform the Aśvamedha. At the time of eating the *brahmodana* (the Brahmin’s rice-porridge), the *udgātṛ* priest shall eat the *brahmodana*, and he shall receive a thousand [cows] from the sacrificer. During the concluding rites of the Sāvitra offerings, while the *hotṛ* recites the *pāriplava* narrative day after day for a year, the sacrificer shall sit upon a golden cushion.

After a year has passed, having bound the horse, he should take possession of that seat while the sacrificer is consecrated (*dīkṣita*). On all days, they should chant the *bahiṣpavamāna* at the *cātvāla* pit. Regarding this, he states for the first day:
"Pavasva vājasātaye"—he thus makes three *anuṣṭubh*s into four *gāyatrī*s. Between the *pajra* and *audhājaya*, there is the *gauṅgava*.
In the *audala-ājyadoha*, there is the *gautama*.
The rest of the Garga-trirātra is the same as the first day.

"Thus: *Pavasva vājasātaye, devebhyo madhumattaraḥ, vatsaṃ jātaṃ na mātaraḥ, pṛthivīṃ cāti jabhriṣaḥ*—this is the *Bahiṣpavamāna*. *Agnā ā yāhi*, *mitrāya*, *indrāgnī*—these are the *Ājya* hymns. *Pra somāso vipaścitaḥ*—this is the *Gāyatra* and the *Aśva*. *Pra soma devavītaye*—these are the *Sāman*-verses of the *Pajra*, *Gauṅgava*, and *Yaudhājaya*. The *Auśana* is the last. Three [of these] may optionally [be used] for either [the *Gāyatra* or the *Aśva*]."

Because of the statement "they may occur," there is the performance of a single verse (*ekarca*) in the *Bṛhatī* meter; the *Rathantara*, the *Svāra*, and the *Sauparṇa*; the *Abhīvarta* beginning with "śagdhyūṣu śacīpate"; the *Kāleya* on its own verses—these are the *Pṛṣṭha* chants. The *Gāyatra* beginning with "svādiṣṭhayā" and the *Marka* beginning with "svāśiraḥ"; the two single-verse hymns beginning with "ayā pavasva devayuḥ" and "pavate haryato hariḥ" [are used] for the *Saphākṣāra*; and the *Audala*, the *Gautama*, and the *Artanidhana Ājyadoha* are [used] for the pressing of the soma-juice (*andhas*).

The *Vaikhānasa* [Sāman] begins with "abhi priyāṇi"; the *Yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The arrangement of the *stomas* is like that of the first *catuṣṭoma*. Regarding the *viṣṭutis*, however, there are four groups of six verses (*ṣaṭkas*) within a single *ṛc* of the twenty-four-fold (*caturviṃśa*) [stoma]; the distinction is that there are two *viṣṭāvas* for each turn (*paryāya*). Alternatively, the *viṣṭuti* is as follows: he utters *hiṃ* for six [verses]—three times, twice, and once; he utters *hiṃ* for six [verses]—once, three times, and twice.

He utters *hiṃ* for six verses: two, two, and two. He utters *hiṃ* for six verses: two, one, and three. Regarding this it is said: "In the Aśvamedha, the penultimate [stotra] has the *dvikaviṣṭāva*, while the others have eighteen [verses]. Alternatively, the arrangement of the rounds (*paryāya*) is such that the first two are fifteen-versed, and the latter two are twenty-one-versed. Some Adhvaryus maintain that the days [of the Aśvamedha] have the nature of the *avabhṛtha* (concluding bath). On this point, the Sūtra states: "In the Aśvatrirātra, the days have distinct *avabhṛthas*."

For them, the *avabhṛtha-sāman* of the first [day] is "sanād agne"; for the second, it is either "yad vā u viśpatiḥ" or "ty agnāiḥ. Otherwise, the two [days] conclude with the consumption of curd. In that case, the chanting of the *bahiṣpavamāna* follows the rule of the *ahīna* sacrifices.
Thus ends the first day. || 16 ||
The second day: He recites the second day's [laud]:

"Sing forth, O men, unto him; sing unto the one born of the waters, who flashes with brilliant luster. These drops have been poured forth; the King goes with the songs of praise. O Soma, you are a bull, full of splendor; flow for our nourishment, O stream! (RV 9.11.1–3).
Thus concludes the Bahiṣpavamāna.

"Abhi somāsa āyavaḥ"—this is for Gautama; "Antarikṣam" is for Dairghaśravasa. These are single-verse [stotras]. The Santani is performed over three verses. "Paurumadgam," "Gāyatrapārśvam," and "Maidhātitham"—these are single-verse [stotras]. The Dvihiṅkāra is performed over three verses. The Mahānāmnīs, the Vāmadevya, and the Pārthuraśma are performed with the verses of the Śrāvantīya, along with the Saṃkṛti. 2.
The rest of the Garga-trirātra is the same as the middle day.
Thus it is said. On this day, having touched the tail of the horse, they should proceed for the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant;

or alternatively, the *adhvaryu* alone touches the tail, while the others may touch it as they please. While they are proceeding, the sacrificer should say to the *udgātṛ*: "O *udgātṛ*, I choose you with a hundred cows and a gold necklace;
my horse will sing the *udgītha*. The meaning of this is: "O *udgātṛ*, you..."

"Leaving aside the horse, I choose the Udgātṛ for a hundred cows, a gold necklace, and ornaments; the horse itself shall chant for me. Having made the horse step onto the place of chanting (āstāva), they should show him a mare. When the horse neighs at her, then the sacrificer should say to the Udgātṛ: "O Udgātṛ, I choose you with a hundred cows and a gold necklace; you alone shall chant for me. He should then give a hundred cows and a gold necklace to the Udgātṛ.

Having made the horse step northward, immediately after the Udgātṛ has sat down with the mantra "yo me ātmā," he should chant the *aśvavrata* using the triplet beginning with "abhi vājī viśvarūpaḥ. For the two subsequent *stotrīya* verses as well, he should introduce the chant at each step with "hau hau" and so forth. The seer (*ṛṣi*) and other details for these are "aśvaḥ" and "triṣṭubh. The purpose is the distribution according to the respective parts (*bhaktivibhāga*), because they share a single performer.

Then they should chant the *bahiṣpavamāna* laud. The *bahiṣpavamāna* begins with "Sing to him, O men" (*upāsmai gāyata naraḥ*) and ends with "Flow for our desire, O stream" (*iṣe pavasva dhārayā*). Having chanted the *bahiṣpavamāna*, the *udgātṛ* priest, seated upon a golden cushion (*hiraṇyakaśipu*), shall take that deerskin himself, because there is a single agent [for both actions].

Then follows the *abhimedhana*. That which is prescribed by the passage beginning with "She who is the most beloved of the wives of the sacrificer," and the recitation of the *brahmodya* (theological riddle) by the formula beginning with "Having performed [the rite] with the *svāhākṛti*s. Thereafter, the duties such as the worship of the *dhiṣṇya* hearths are to be performed. The *ājya* stotras are: "O Agni Aṅgiras, with what [help]? and "Even though it is very far, O Indra, we incite that [strength] for the sake of booty"; and "This [hymn] of yours, from my mind. The *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* chants are performed with the verse "Of this [sacrifice], the ancient... and so forth.

The triplet of Sāmans beginning with "abhi somāsa āyavaḥ" is for Gautama; the triplet of Sāmans beginning with "antarikṣam" is for Dairghaśravasa. The Saṃtani is performed over three verses. The triplet of Sāmans beginning with "paurumadga", "gāyatrapārśva", and "aidhātitha" is for [the respective sages]; it is performed over three verses with two *hiṃkāras*.

The *ājyadoha* chant ending with the *nidhana* "ayaṃ soma" is the final one; likewise the *mahānāmnīs*. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras consist of the *vāmadevya*, the *pārthuraśma*, and the verses of the *śrāyantīya* beginning with "saṃkṛti. The meter for the *mahānāmnīs* is the *śakvarī*; for the *pārthuraśma*, it is the *paṅkti*. The *gāyatra* chant is "yaste mada," and the *arka* of Agni is "abhi dyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśaḥ sakhāya ā niṣīdata. The *vācaḥ sāma* is the *śaukta*, and the *āndhīgava* is "paryū ṣu."

"O Soma, for Indra to drink"—this is the *yajñāyajñīya*. "A purifier for thee"—this is the final *ariṣṭa* [stotra]. The *viśoviśīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman* on its own verses. The *pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *udvaṃśīya* are the *uktha* [stotras]. Everything is in the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*) stoma. || 3 ||
Thus ends the second day. || 20 ||
The third day:
He recites the third day [hymn]:
"Flow on as the leader of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. Of thee, the purifying sage... (RV 9.26.1).
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
After the Gāyatra [hymn], there are four single-verse hymns; the last one is in the Bṛhatī metre. In the Anuṣṭubh [section], there are three single-verse hymns; the last one is in a triplet (tṛca).
The rest is the same as the highest day of the Garga-trirātra sacrifice.
Thus: "The immortal god, the Hotṛ, we invoke as Mitra; for the great Indra with his power; to Indra and Agni be great homage"—these are the Ājya offerings.

The *gāyatra* chant, beginning with "uccā te," is performed on three verses. The *sāman*-triplets are the *goṣūkta*, the *jarābodhīya*, and [the triplet] beginning with "ṛṣabhaḥ pavamānaḥ. The *utsedha* chant, beginning with "pratnaṃ pīyūṣam," is on one verse. The *ābhīśava* chant, beginning with "parīto ṣiñcata," is on three verses. The *ātharvaṇa* chant is on three verses. The *pṛśni* chant is on one verse. The final *ājyadoha* chant, consisting of the *triṇidhana* chant beginning with "tisro vācaḥ," is used. The *pṛṣṭha* chants are the *bṛhat*, the *satrāsāhīya*, the *śyaita*, and the *raurava*. The *gāyatra* and the *hāviṣmata* chants are [performed] on the verse beginning with "parisvāno giriṣṭhāḥ."

"sa sunve yo vasūnām... prāṇā śiśumahīnām" is for the Dīrghaśrudhi; "ayaṃ pūṣā" is the Niṣedha; "śyāvāśvaṃ krauñcam" are the Sāman-trikas; the Yajñāyajñīya is performed upon three verses; "pari pra dhanva" is the Vājadāvarya; "ayā rucā" are the Nityavatsas; "dhartā divaḥ" is the final verse of Dīrghatamas; the Vāravantīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman; the Sākamaśva, Saubhara, and Nārmedha are the Ukthas; and the Gaurīvita is the Ṣoḍaśin-sāman.

The *āhinīkī* night is the *saṃdhi*. All the *stomas* are like those of the *atirātra*. The *bahiṣpavamāna* is *trivṛt*; the *ājya* chants are *pañcadaśa*; the *mādhyaṃdina-pavamāna* is *saptadaśa*; the *pṛṣṭha* chants are *ekaviṃśa*; the *ārbhava* is *triṇava*; the *agniṣṭoma* is *trayastriṃśa*. The *uktha* chants descend in order: the first is *triṇava*, followed by two *ekaviṃśa* chants including the *ṣoḍaśin*. The night chant is *pañcadaśa*; the *saṃdhi* is *trivṛt*. The *avabhṛtha-sāman* is "ahāvo hāvā. The variations for the *aśvamedha* are to be understood from the Sūtra itself. 3.
Thus ends the third day. || 21 ||
The Aśvatrirātra sacrifice is completed.

The Baida-trirātra is described by the following *anuvāka*: "Three *trivṛt* *atirātras*, all provided with the *ṣoḍaśin*. The *bahiṣpavamāna* chant for the middle day takes place at the *cātvāla* pit; alternatively, for the first day it is at the *cātvāla*, and for the two subsequent days it is in the *sadas*. Regarding this, it is said: "In the Baida-trirātra, Gautama maintains it is a *satra* according to the rule, while Dhānañjayya maintains it is an *ahīna* according to the rule."
The first day: therein is the ritual procedure for the first day.

"pra somāso vipaścitaḥ" (O wise ones, forth [flow] the Soma juices)—the Gāyatra [Sāman] on one verse; the Āśva on one verse; the Jarābodhīya on one verse; "pra soma devavītaye" (Forth, O Soma, for the feast of the gods)—the Gauṅgava on one verse; the Pājra on one verse; the Yaudhājaya on one verse; the Auśana, the Aupagava, and the Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra; and "pratyasmai pipīṣate" (To him who desires to drink)—this is the Nānada, the Ṣoḍaśin-Sāman. ||1||
The night is the junction. The rest is the same as the first day of the Garga-trirātra sacrifice.
Thus: "Sing forth for him, O men; we [sing] for you, the purifying one; for you, the purifying one, O sage"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna.

The *ājya* [stotras] are: "O Agni, come to us," and "O Indra and Agni. The *sāman*-triplets are: the *gāyatram* "O Soma, [streams] of the wise," the *āśvam* "O Jarābodhi," and the *gauṅgavam* "O Soma, for the feast of the gods," as well as the *pajram* and *yaudhājayam*. The *auśanam* is the final [sāman]. The *rathantaram*, the *svāram*, and the *sauparṇam* are the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras]; the *abhīvarta* is "Be gracious among these, O Lord of Power," and the *kāleyam* is among its own [verses]. The *gāyatram* is "With the sweetest [hymn]," and the *arka* is "With the milk-mixture."

With the verses "Flow on, seeking the gods" (*ayā pavasva devayuḥ*) and "The beloved, golden-hued one flows" (*pavate haryato hariḥ*), [the *saphākṣāra* chant is performed]. With the verse "For the pressed juice" (*pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ*), the *audala*, the *cartanidhana*, and the *ājyadoha* are performed. With the verse "Toward the dear things" (*abhi priyāṇi*), the *vaikhānasa* is performed on the last three verses. On the other [verses], the *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* on the first three verses. With the verse "Most beloved of you" (*preṣṭhaṃ vaḥ*), the *auśana* is performed. With the verse "Thou for us, O Indra" (*tvaṃ na indra*), the *aupagava* is performed. With the verse "Indra, all... (*indraṃ viśvā...*), the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* chants are performed, the latter of which constitutes the *uktha* hymns.

It is called "uttara" (the latter) because of the statement in the *Upagrantha*: "The *abhiplava* and the *trirātra* [are] the latter. Regarding the verse "pratyasmai pipīṣate," the *ṣoḍaśin* chant is the *nānada*; the night is the *āhīnika*; everything is *trivṛt*. ||2||
Thus ends the first day. || 22 ||
The second day:
for the second day—
[chant] "upo ṣu jātam apturam davidyutatyā rucā iṣe pavasva dhārayā" (Hither, indeed, the swift one born, with flashing brilliance, flow for our nourishment in a stream).
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

"Paryū ṣu" belongs to Śyāvāśva; "indrāya somapātave" belongs to Āndhīgava; "pavitraṃ te" is the final Yajñāyajñīya; the Tairaścaya is in the place of the Udvamśīya; the Udvamśīya is the Ṣoḍaśin-sāman, the night, and the junction. || 1 ||
The rest of the Garga-trirātra is the same as the middle day.

"Thus: *upo ṣu jātam apturam* (VS 9.1), *davidyutatyā rucā iṣe pavasva dhārayā*—this is the *barhiṣpavamāna*. *kayā te agne aṅgiraḥ*, *purūruṇā cid dhy asti*, *tam indraṃ vājayāmasi*, *iyaṃ vāmasya manmanaḥ*—these are the *ājya* stotras. *asya pratnām*—this is the *gāyatram* and the *cāmahīyavam*. *abhi somāsa āyavaḥ*—this is the *gautamam*, the *antarikṣam*, the *dairghaśravasam*, and the *dvihiṃkāram*. *ayaṃ somaḥ*—this is the *ainidhanam*; the final one is the *ājyadoha*."

With the exception of the last [verse], they consist of single *ṛc*s. Among them, the *sāman*-triplets belonging to Gautama, Antarikṣa, and Dairghaśravasa are those with two *hiṃkāra*s in the middle. Regarding the *adhyāsyā* [verses], it is because of the statement: "four [verses] in different *stotrīyā*s. The Vāmadevya [sāman] is on its own [verses]. "Mo ṣu tvā vāghataś cana" is the Gāyatra-pārśva. "Astāvi manma pūrvam" is the Saṃtani. The Pṛṣṭha [sāmans] are on the verses of the Śrāyantīya, according to the rule "in the *saṃkṛti*s. "Yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" is the Gāyatra and the *arka* of Agni.

"Come, O friends, to the splendor"—this is the *Sāman* of the *Vācas*. And the *Śaukta* is likewise. "Around [thee], O Soma"—this is the *Āndhīgava*. "For Indra, for drinking the Soma"—this is the *Yajñāyajñīya*. "Thy purifier"—this is the *Ariṣṭa*, which is the final [verse]. With the exception of the final [verse], the others consist of single verses (*ekarcas*). The *Viśoviśīya* is the *Agniṣṭoma-sāman* on its own verses. The *Pramahiṣṭhīya*, the *Hārivarṇa*, and the *Tairaścya* are the *Uktha* chants. The *Udvaṃśīya* is the *Ṣoḍaśi-sāman*. The night [rite] follows the daily [pattern]; this is the *Sandhi* [stotra]. Everything is in the *Trivṛt* [stoma]. (2)
Thus ends the second day. || 23 ||
The third day:
For the third day, flow on as the foremost of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. May thy skill, which brings bliss, [come] to us. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
It rescues one from the ocean of old age; it consists of the Satobṛhatī, the Dvipadā, and the Aticchandas meters. ||2||
The Bārhata verses are in reverse order. 3.
"May this Pūṣan be wealth and fortune"—this is the *arka* hymn of Dīrghatamas; and the *krauñca* chant as well. "The upholder of heaven"—this is the final *yajñāyajñīya*.
The rest of the Garga-trirātra is the same as the last day.

Thus: "Flow on as the leader of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. "May your skill, which brings bliss," thus [is] the *Bahispavamāna*. "The immortal god, the Hotṛ; we invoke Mitra; the great Indra who [rules] by his might; obeisance, vast, to Indra and Agni"—thus [are] the *Ājya* verses. "High is the birth of your juice," thus [is] the *Gāyatra* and the *Goṣūkta*, [beginning with] "The bellowing bull, the purifying one. "Pour out the pressed [juice] all around"—thus [is] the *Pṛśni*.

The *ātharvaṇa* [stotra] belongs to the *ābhīśava* [tune]. "Three voices" (*tisro vācaḥ*) is the *triṇidhana* [stotra]; the *ājyadoha* is the final [part]. The verses other than the final one consist of single *ṛc*s. Among them, the *gāyatrī* and *bṛhatī* are the *sāman*-triplets. The *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] are the *bṛhat*, the *satrāsāhīya*, the *śyaita*, and the *raurava*. "Flowing around, dwelling on the mountain" (*parisvāno giriṣṭhāḥ*) is for the *gāyatrahāviṣmat*. "He is pressed, he who is the breath of the Vasus, the child of the great ones" (*sa sunve yo vasūnām prāṇā śiśurmahīnām*) is for the *dīrghaśrudhi*. "This Pūṣan is wealth, fortune" (*ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ*) is the *arka* of Dīrghatamas, as well as the *krauñca*.

The *Yajñāyajñīya* chant, beginning with "Dhartā divaḥ," is the final one; it is indeed the final [verse] in the triplet (*ṛca*). The *Vāravantīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *Sākamaśva*, *Saubhara*, and *Nārmedha* are the *uktha* chants. The *Gaurīvita* is the *ṣoḍaśin-sāman*. The night-chant (*rātri*) is the *saṃdhi*. Everything is in the *trivṛt* stoma. The first is the *rātri-sāman*, or the *ṣoḍaśin*; for there is the statement of the teachers: "That [is performed] even at the end of the *vaidas*. (5)
Thus ends the third day. 24.
The Baidatrirātra is completed.

The Chandomapavamāna Trirātra has its first day consisting of Pavamāna stotras in the Caturviṃśa Stoma; this is stated in the Anuvāka beginning with "the Pavamānas are Caturviṃśas. The ritual procedure (kalpa) for that first day is as follows:

The *bahiṣpavamāna* chant of the annual *viṣuvat* day consists of both *paryāsa* verses; the latter two follow the *aśva* verse. There are also the *somasāman* and the *rohitakūlīya*. "Flow for Indra" (*pavasvendramaccha*) is performed with the *saphākṣāra* melody.
The rest of the Aśvatrirātra is the same as the first day.

Thus: "Of the one-year-old" (*sāṃvatsarikasya*) is for the purpose of excluding the *viṣuvat* and *atirātra* sacrifices. "Sing forth to him, O men, for the tawny one who is self-strong; like chariots they have been let loose"—"We [sing] to thee, the purifying one, O sage"—these constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "O Agni, come hither for the feast"—these are the *ājya* hymns. "The wise Soma-drops"—this includes the *gāyatra*, the *aśva*, the *somasāman*, and the *rohitakūlīya*.

"O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—this is the *pajra*, the *gauṅgava*, the *yaudhājaya*, and the *auśana* as the final [stotra]. The *rathantara*, the *svāra*, and the *sauparṇa*; "be gracious, O waters"—this is the *abhīvarta*. "In our own [songs], the *kāleya*"—these are the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras]. "With the sweetest [hymn]"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *svāśira-arka*. "Flow on toward Indra"—this is the *sapha* and the *akṣāra*. "For the one who presses the juice"—this is the *audala*, the *gautama*, the *ṛtanidhana*, and the *ājyadoha*. "Toward the dear [hymns]"—this is the *vaikhānasa* as the final [stotra].

The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. The *pavamāna* chants are twenty-four-versed (*caturviṃśa*). The *ājya* stotras are three-versed (*trivṛt*). The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are fifteen-versed (*pañcadaśa*). The *agniṣṭoma* is seventeen-versed (*saptadaśa*). In this case, there is no fourfold repetition (*catuṣparyāyatva*) of the *stomas*. || 2 ||
Thus ends the first day. ||25||

The second day: for the second day—“O Soma, you are a bull, brilliant; for you are indeed a bull with your light”; “These Somas flow toward the beloved [place]”; “Soma, being purified, flows on”; “Your vital powers rise up”—with these [verses], he brings forward the verses prior to the *paryāsa*. After the *āmahīyava*, there are six subsequent [verses] beginning with the *āśu* and the *bhārgava*. After the two *hiṃkāras*, there are the subsequent [verses]: the *acchidra*, the *maidhātitha*, and the *pauruhanmana*. After the *arka* of Agni, there are four subsequent [verses] beginning with the *surūpa*.
The verses preceding the Yajñāyajñīya are the Āsita, the Kautsa, the Śuddhāśuddhīya, the Krauñca, and the Rayiṣṭha. || 1 ||
The rest of the Garga-trirātra is the same as the middle day.

Thus: "Upon the newborn, the swift one, with flashing luster, flow clear, O Indu; pressed as a bull, the King is led by the songs of wisdom. O Soma, you are a bull, resplendent; indeed, you are a bull by your radiance. These Somas [flow] toward the beloved; the Soma, being purified, flows on. Your vital energies rise upward; flow for nourishment, O stream!"—this is the *Bahiṣpavamāna*. "With what [song], O Agni Aṅgiras? Even through the wide [space], he truly exists. We incite that Indra for vigor. This [is] from your mind"—these are the *Ājya* hymns.

For this [sāman], there are the *gāyatram*, the *cāmahīyavam*, the *āśubhārgavam*, the *mārgīyavam*, the *saumitram*, the *aiṭatam*, the *sākamaśvam*, and the *vilambasauparṇam*. For "abhi somāsa āyavaḥ," there are the *gautamam*, the *antarikṣam*, and the *dairghaśravasam*. There are also the *dvihiṅkāram*, the *ācchidram*, the *maidhātitham*, and the *pauruhanmanam*. For "ayaṃ somaḥ," there is the *īnidhana* as the final *ājyadoha*. The *gautamam* is for the first verse; the *pauruhanmanam* is for the middle verse.

The *vāmadevya* is on its own [verses]. "Do not steal thee, even the priests" (*mo ṣu tvā vāghataś cana*) is the *gāyatrapārśva*. "The ancient hymn has been praised" (*astāvi manma pūrvyam*) is the *santani*. Regarding the verses of the *śrāyantīya*, "the two who have prepared" (*saṃkṛtī*) are the *pṛṣṭhas*. "That exhilaration of thine which is most excellent" (*yaste mado vareṇyaḥ*) is the *gāyatra*, as well as the *arka* of Agni, the *surūpa*, the *bhāsa*, the *kākṣīvata*, the *gāyatrīsāman*, and the *asitam*. "Splendor, lofty fame—O friends, sit down" (*abhidyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśaḥ sakhāya ā niṣīdata*) is the *vācaḥsāman*, as well as the *śaukta* on two verses. "Around thee" (*pary ū ṣu*) is the *āndhīgava*.

"O Soma, for Indra to drink"—thus [are the stotras]: the Āsita, the Kautsa, the Śuddhāśuddhīya, the Krauñca, the Rayiṣṭha, and the Yajñāyajñīya. "A purifier for thee"—this is the Ariṣṭa as the final [stotra]. The Agniṣṭoma-sāman is the Viśoviśīya upon its own verses. The Pramaṃhiṣṭhīya, the Hārivarṇa, and the Udvaṃśīya are the Ukthas. The Pavamānas have forty [verses]; the Ājyas have fifteen; the Pṛṣṭhas have seventeen; and the Agniṣṭoma, together with the Ukthas, has twenty-one—such are the Stomas. 2.
Thus ends the second day. 26.

The third day: the ritual procedure for the third day. From the eighth hymn, he brings forward four six-verse sections from the ninth day. "ā te dakṣaṃ mayobhuvam" is the concluding verse (paryāsa). Following the *Ṛṣabha* and *Pavamāna* [hymns], there is the *Surūpa*, the *Ādārasṛt*, and the *Iḍā-saṃkṣāra*. There is also the *Svāra* and the *Saindhukṣita*. Following the *Pṛśni* [hymn], there are the *Arkapuṣpa*, the *Kaulmalabarhiṣa*, and the *Devasthāna*. Following the *Hāviṣmata*, there are the four beginning with the *Śāmmada*. Following the *Yajñāyajñīya*, there is the *Yadvāhiṣṭhīya*. ||1||
The rest of the Garga-trirātra is the same as the highest day.

Thus: "Flow on as the leader of speech; this immortal god, he goes with subtle wisdom. He indeed is that bull-like chariot; he is the steed urged by men. He is the seer praised aloud; he, the bull, has been pressed for drinking. [With the words] 'May thy skill, which brings bliss,' [they perform] the Bahiṣpavamāna."
"The immortal god, the Hotṛ; we invoke Mitra; the great Indra who [rules] by his might; homage, vast, to Indra and Agni"—these are the Ājya offerings.

"Uccā te jātamandhasaḥ"—this is the Gāyatra, the Gauṣūkta, the Jarābodhīya, the Ṛṣabha, the Pavamāna, the Surūpa, the Adārasṛt, the Saṃkṣāra of the Iḍās, the Saindhukṣita, and the Utsedha beginning with "Pratnaṃ pīyūṣam. "Parīto ṣiñcatā sutam"—this is the Ābhīśava, the Atharvaṇa, the Pṛśni, the Arkapuṣpa, the Kaulmalabarhiṣa, and the Devasthāna. "Tisro vācaḥ"—this is the Triṇidhana, with the Ājyadoha as the final [Sāman].
The *bṛhat*, the *satrāsāhīya*, the *śyaita*, and the *raurava* are the *pṛṣṭha* chants.
"Pari svāno giriṣṭhā" consists of the Gāyatram, the Hāviṣmatam, the Śāmmadam, the Dāvasunidhanam, the Pratīcīneḍam, the Kāśītam, and the Hāviṣkṛtam.

"Sa sunve yo vasūnām prāṇā śiśurmahīnām" is for the Dīrghaśrudhya. "Ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhaga" consists of the Niṣedha, the Śyāvāśvam, the Krauñcam, and the Yajñāyajñīyam. "Pari pra dhanva" is the Vājadāvarya. "Ayā ruce" consists of the Nityavatsas. "Dhartā divaḥ" is the final Ṛk of Dīrghatamas.

The *vāravantīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. It is a *jyotiṣṭoma* *atirātra* sacrifice accompanied by the *ṣoḍaśin* cup. The *pavamāna* stotras consist of forty-eight verses; the *ājya* stotras consist of twenty-one verses; the *pṛṣṭha* stotras consist of twenty-seven verses. The *agniṣṭoma* consists of thirty-three verses; the *uktha* stotras, including the *ṣoḍaśin*, consist of twenty-one verses. The night-chant consists of fifteen verses, and the *saṃdhi* consists of nine verses. || 2 ||
Thus ends the third day. || 27 ||
The Chandoma Pavamāna three-night rite is completed.
The Antarvasu three-night sacrifice is described by the section beginning with "The first and last days have the *trivṛt* morning pressing. Regarding that, the ritual manual (*kalpa*) states:
Those which are the first and last days of the Garga-trirātra are [the days] of the Antarvāsas.
Thus: on the final day, the first *rātrisāman* is performed; it is stated that for two days, it is indeed the *pañcadaśa* [stoma]. ||1||
Thus [are the rites] on the first and the last days. || 28 ||
The second day:

he speaks of the middle day— "Nearby, the water-crossing one born [of the waters], with flashing brilliance, flow on, O Indu! As the pressed bull, the King, he goes forth with songs of praise. These drops have been let loose; O Soma, thou art the brilliant bull, for thou art indeed a bull by thy luster. Flow for nourishment in a stream! (RV 9.101.1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
Now, that which is the middle day of the Chandomapavamāna is this very one; its Ārbhava [Pavamāna] stotra is arranged according to the *tṛca* (three-verse) pattern.

Thus: at the Ārbhava [laud], there are the *vācasāman* and the *śaukta*. In that case, they consist of single verses (*ekarcāu*); here, however, the meaning is that they consist of triplets (*tṛcāu*). The *bahiṣpavamāna* begins with "upo ṣu jātam apturam" and ends with "iṣe pavasva dhārayā. The *ājya* hymns are: "kayā te agne aṅgiraḥ," "purūruṇā ciddhi asti," "tam indraṃ vājayāmasi," and "iyaṃ vāmasya manmanaḥ."

For this [sāman], there are the *gāyatram*, the *cāmahīyavam*, the *āśubhārgavam*, the *mārgīyavam*, the *saumitram*, the *aiṭatam*, the *sākamaśvam*, and the *vilambasauparṇam*—to the verse "asya pratnāmanudyutam. Then there are the *gautamam*, the *antarikṣam*, the *dairdhaśravasam*, the *dvihiṅkāram*, the *acchidram*, the *maidhātitham*, and the *pauruhanmanam*—to the verse "abhi somāsa āyavaḥ. The *īnidhana* [sāman] "ayaṃ soma" is the final *ājyadoha*. The *gautama* is used for the first verse; the *pauruhanmana* is used for the middle verse.

The Vāmadevya [Sāman] is on its own verses; "mo ṣu tvā" is the Gāyatrapārśva; "astāvi manma pūrvyam" is the Saṃtani; and the Pṛṣṭha [Stotras] are based on the verses of the Śrayantīya, beginning with "saṃkṛti."

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the Gāyatra, the *arka* of Agni, the *surūpa*, the *bhāsa*, the *kākṣīvata*, the Gāyatrī *sāman*, and the *āsita*. "abhi dyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśaḥ sakhāya ā niṣīdata"—this is the *vācaḥsāma* and the *śaukta*. "paryū ṣvi tyān"—this is the *āndhīgava*. "indrāya soma pātave"—this is the *āsita*, the *kautsa*, the *śuddhāśuddhīya*, the *krauñca*, the *rayiṣṭha*, and the *yajñāyajñīya*. "pavitraṃ te"—this is the *ariṣṭa*, the final one.

The *svāsu viśoviśīyam* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*; the *pramam̐hiṣṭhīyam*, the *hārivarṇam*, and the *udvaṃśīyam* are the *ukthas*. The morning pressing has the twenty-four-fold hymn-form (*stoma*); the midday pressing has the forty-four-fold; the third pressing has the forty-eight-fold. Thus are the *stomas* for the [rite] with *ukthas*. 2.
Thus ends the middle day. || 26 ||
The third day has been described.
The Antarvasu Trirātra sacrifice is completed.
The *parāka-trirātra* sacrifice is described by the section beginning with "The first day has a *trivṛt* morning pressing. He now states the ritual arrangement for that first day.
That which is the first of the two inner garments belongs to Parāka. ||1||
Thus [ends the first section]. ||1||
Thus ends the first day. || 30 ||
The second day:

Now, regarding the second day—[the priest] takes up [the verses] before the *paryāsa* with the words, "O Soma, you are a bull, you are brilliant; for you are indeed a bull by your radiance. After the *āmahīyava*, [he takes] the two following: the *āśu* and the *bhārgava-mārgīyava*. After the *arkāgni*, [he takes] the two following: the *surūpabhāsa*. Before the *yajñāyajñīya*, [he takes] the *āsita* and the *kautsa*.
The rest of the Garga-trirātra is the same as the middle day.

Thus: "Nearby, the swift one, born [of waters], with flashing luster, flow clear, O Indu; pressed as a bull, the King is led forth with songs of wisdom. O Soma, you are a bull, resplendent; for you are a bull by your radiance. Flow for nourishment, for the sake of the stream"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna chant.
"By what [means], O Agni, is there even for you that which is very far away? We incite that Indra for strength. These are the *ājya* verses of this hymn.

The *gāyatra* [stotra] consists of "asya pratnām anu dyutam," the *cāmahīyava*, the *āśubhārgava*, and the *mārgīyava*. The [stotra] consisting of "abhi somāsa āyavaḥ" includes the *gautama*, the *antarikṣa*, the *dairghaśravasa*, and the *dvihiṃkāra*. The final [stotra] is the *īnidhana* "ayaṃ somaḥ," which is the *ājyadoha*.

The Vāmadevya is on its own verses; "mo ṣu vāghataś cana" is the Gāyatra-pārśva; "astāvi manma pūrvyam" is the Santani; for the Śrāyantīya, "saṃkṛti" among the verses constitutes the Pṛṣṭhas; "yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" is the Gāyatra and the *arka* of Agni, as well as the Surūpa; "abhi dyumnaṃ sakhāya ā niṣīdata" is the Vācaś-casāma and the Śaukta; "pary ū ṣu" is the Āndhīgava; "indrāya soma pātave" is the Āsita, the Kautsa, and the Yajñāyajñīya; "pavitraṃ te" is the Ariṣṭa, which is the final [stotra]. ||2||
The *viśoviśīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*; the *pramam̐hiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *udvaṃśīya* are the *uktha* chants in their own [respective] verses.
Thus ends the second day. || 31 ||
The third day:
for the third day—the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant of the subsequent day, which is the *vyuṣṭi*—this is indeed the final day of the *chandomapavamāna*. Its *bṛhatī* [verse] is arranged like a hare's ear. 1.

Thus: if there is one [syllable] in the *sādhyā* [verse], or two at the end in that same *adhyāsyā*, and [one] at the beginning of that same [verse], it is called *śaśakarṇaklṛpti*; thus the *śaśakarṇaklṛpti* has been explained.
Flow on as the leader of speech; this immortal god, with his subtle wisdom, moves along. "May thy skill, which brings bliss," thus [is] the Bahiṣpavamāna.
Everything else is the same as the final day of the Chandoma Pavamāna. The Ābhīśava [stotra] is on the first [verse]; "śrīṇanta" is on the Adhyāsyā; "devasthānam" is the distinction. ||1||
Thus ends the third day. || 32 ||
The three-night rite performed outside the village is completed.
Thus ends the first chapter, which is the sixth from the beginning, in the commentary on the Ārṣeyakalpa composed by Varadarāja, the son of the venerable Vāmanārya. 6.

"Sing forth for him, O men, for the tawny one who is self-strong, as the restless cows [low]—flow swiftly, O thou of lofty mind! O Sage Agni, come hither to the feast!"—these are the *ājya* verses. "The inspired Soma-drops"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *aśva*, the *jarābodhīya*, and the *āśubhārgava*. "O Soma, flow for the feast of the gods"—this is the *pajra*, the *gauṅgava*, the *yaudhājaya*, the *auśana*, and finally the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *naudhasa*, and the *kāleya*, with the verse beginning "with the sweetest [honey]."

"madiṣṭhayā" is the Gāyatra; "saṃhitaḥ pavasva indram accha" is the Sapha and Pauṣkala; "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ" is the Audala-Gautama; "ākūpāram abhi priyāṇi" is the Dvīḍa; the final [verse] is the Padastobha; the Agniṣṭoma-sāman is the Yajñāyajñīya. 71.

Flow on as the leader of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. O Soma, you are brilliant; for you are indeed a bull by your luster. Being purified, Soma flows. We choose Agni as our messenger, the purifying one—these are the *ājya* verses. "Flow on as a bull, O stream"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *hāviṣmat*, the *ājiga*, the *svāra*, and the *sauparṇa*. "Being purified, O Soma, with your stream"—within this *āyasya* [hymn], there is the *dairghaśravasa*. "The red bull"—this is the final *pārtha*. And there are the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, and the *śyaita*.

The *mādhucchandasa* [is] "yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"; the *gāyatra* and the *svāśira* [are] "arkastvaṃ hyaṅga daivya pavasva devavītaye"; the two *śaṅkusujñāna* [verses are] "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"; the two *krauñca* [are] "vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate"; the *caturiḍa* has the *padastobha* as its final part; the *yajñāyajñīya* and the *agniṣṭomasāman* [are used]; the *śana*, the *saubhara*, and the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*. 72.

"By the shining one, for thy splendor, the drops have been poured forth; the King goes with the sacrificial offerings. "These vigorous Soma-drops have been poured forth; flow for the sake of the beloved food with a stream. "Agni is kindled by Agni"—these are the *ājya* verses. "High is the birth of thy plant"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*, the *aiḍa*, and the *sauparṇa*. "The Soma-drops, the Āyus"—this is the *gautama*, the *antarikṣa*, and the *maidhātitha*, together with the *dvihiṃkāra* and the *tisro vācaḥ*, which is the *saṃkrośa* of the Aṅgirases. "Towards thee, O Bull... [the final verse].

"Suta" is the Rathantara; "Ka stam indra tvāvase" is the Vāmadevya, the Śrāyantīya, and the Raurava; "Tisro vāca udīrate" is the Gāyatra; "Agnec carke," "Ā sotā pari siñcata," "Sakhāya ā niṣīdata" are the Vācaḥsāma and the Śaukta; "Sutāso madhumattamā" are the two Tvaṣṭrī-sāmans; the Svāra is between them; the Andhīgava is the Pavitra; "Iti ṣaḍiḍaḥ" is the Padastobha; the final [chant] is the Yajñāyajñīya, which is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman; the Ukthas are for long life. 73.

Pavamāna has generated this immortal god; he goes with the subtle *dhī*. That immortal Hotṛ god [bestows] skill that brings bliss. "When today at the rising of the sun, for great Indra, for his power..."—"This [is] the thought of Vāma, according to its ancient splendor"—[these are] the Gāyatra, the Āmahīyava, and the Satrāsāhīya. "Pour out the pressed [juice] on all sides"—[this is] the Pṛśni, the Atharvaṇa, and the Abhīśava, as well as the Utsedha. "This Soma..."—[this is] the Vāsiṣṭha ending with "Since you were born unprecedented. "The Bṛhat and the Edu... [are the concluding verses].

The *madhu* [laud] has the *madiṃtara*, the *vāmadevya*, and the *traiśoka*; the *samanta* [laud] has "pari svāno giriṣṭhā," the *gāyatra*, and the *gauṣūkta*. The *dīrghavāravantīya* [laud] has "sa sunve yo vasūnām" and "prāṇā śiśurmahīnām. The *niṣedha* [laud] has "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" and the *śyāvāśva*. The *arka* [laud] of Dīrghatamas has "pari pra dhanva. The *aṣṭeḍa* [laud] has "dhartā divaḥ"; its final part is the *padastobha*. The *agniṣṭomasāman* is the *yajñāyajñīya*. The *sākamaśva*, *traikakubha*, *nārmedha*, and *gaurīvitam* are the *ṣoḍaśisāman*. The night is the *sandhi*. 74.

"Upa ṣu jātam apturam" is the *anurūpa*; the *brahmasāman* is the Naudhasa; in the world of Sujñāna, the Pauṣkala; "Pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ" is the Audala in the Gautama [tune]. The rest is the same as on the first day of the *abhiplava*.

He removes the Ajigarta and Krauñca [stotras] and places the *uṣṇih* and *kakubh* verses in their own [verses]; the *yāma* [sāman] is the same as on the second day of the fourfold [day], the Caturvīra.

With the verse *asṛkṣata pra vājinaḥ*, he draws out the *aiḍa* from the *arka* of Agni, which is higher than [the norm] and kindled by Sindhukṣita; in the place of the *tvāṣṭrīsāman*, there is the *triṇidhana* *tvāṣṭrīsāman*; the rest is the same as on the third day. In the place of the *caturvīra* *vāravantīya*, he exchanges the *śrudhya* [verse]; in the *anuṣṭubh* *dvipadās*, there is the *vāravantīya*; the last *arka* belongs to Dīrghatamas; the rest is the same as on the final day. That which is the first [verse] of the *jāmadagnya* belongs to the *saṃsarpa*.

He extracts the *suparṇa* hymn consisting of nine verses beginning with "Pour out the pressed juice on every side" (*parīto ṣiñcatā sutam*), as well as the *bārhaduktha* and *dairghaśravasa* hymns; the rest is the same as on the second day of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*) of the Jamadagni lineage. 762. The *ājya* and *bahis-pavamāna* chants of the third day are in the *gāyatrī* meter; the rest is the same as on the third day of the Jamadagni lineage. 763.

The *vrātya*-gāyatrī, "He lifts up the overturned," [is used]; the *bṛhatī* "O Soma, purifying yourself with your stream" follows the *gauṣūkta*; the *niṣedha* "With your conquering power, O juice," [is used]; he takes the *tvāṣṭrīsāman*, the *vāravantīya*, from the two-footed *aticchandas* verses; the rest is the same as on the final day of the *jāmadagnya*. "The Soma juices, the wise ones"—the *gāyatra* [is sung] on one verse, the *āśva* on one, the *jarābodhīya* on one; "O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—the *yaudhājaya* on three verses; the rest is the same as on the first day of the *saṃsarpa*.
"Purifying yourself, O Soma, with your stream..."—this is the *āyāsya*; the rest is the same as on the second day of the *saṃsarpa*.
(772) He extracts the *saindhukṣita* and *andhīgava*; the rest is the same as on the third day of the *saṃsarpa*.

(773) He extracts the *jarābodhīya* and *vāravantīya*, the *dvipadā* and *aticchandas* verses, and [the hymn] beginning "Pour out the pressed juice all around," the *pṛśni*, the *ābhīśava*, and the *ātharvaṇa*; the *jyotiṣṭoma* and the *anuṣṭubh* [verses]; the rest is the same as on the final day of the *saṃsarpa*. (774)

The Vaiśvāmitra [stoma] consists of two days: the *jarābodhīya* is in the *loka* of Soma; the *svāśira* is the *maukṣa* of the *arka* of Saubhara; the *aupagava* is the twelve-day third day of the Vairūpa; the *rathaṃtara* is in the *loka* of Pāṣṭhauha; the *arka* of Agni is the *tvāṣṭrīsāman* of Gaurīviti. The connection (*abhyāsaṅga*) of this three-day period is with the verses "svadiṣṭhayā" and "madiṣṭhayā"; the *Gāyatra* is on two *ṛc*s of the *Sāṃhitā*; the *Gautama* is on a triplet (*ṛc*); the *āsita* is on a triplet; the *Vācaḥ-sāman* and the *Śaukta* are each on two triplets.

Pavamāna has brought them forth; purifying himself, he has stepped forward. When they rush like eager cattle, flow swiftly, O thou of lofty mind! The ruddy cows urge the Sun on. May Agni utterly destroy the Vṛtras—this is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ. His subsequent [stotras] are: "Flow on, accomplishing strength"—this is the *gāyatra*; "The unassailable, the conqueror in battle"—this is the *adārasṛt-satrāsāhīya*; "In thee, O Soma, I have rejoiced"—this is the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra-ābhīśava*; "The heaven-backed"—this is the *āṅgirasa*; "Truly, indeed"—this is the final *vāsiṣṭha*; and the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *traiśoka*, and the *pṛśni*.

"pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ" is the Gāyatra; "svāśiraḥ" is the Ārka; "bṛhad bhāradvājam"; "tvam hy aṅga daivya somaḥ punāna ūrmiṇā" is the Bṛhat; "krośe"; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Nānada; the Tvaṣṭrīsāman is the Tharvaṇa; "pro ayāsīt" is the Lauśa; the final [verse] is the Yajñāyajñīya Agniṣṭomasāman; the Saindhukṣita, the Saubhara, and the Udvaṃśīya. 79.

The all-knowing Pavamāna has been let loose; the prize-winning ones have sped forth. This immortal god, this one, goes with the subtle intellect (*dhi*), bringing strength and bliss. The immortal god, the Hotṛ, indeed exists even through many wide spaces. Arising together with vigor, for you two are the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) of the sacrifice, according to its ancient splendor—thus [are] the Gāyatra, the Āmahīyava, the Jarābodhīya, and the Ṛṣabha, as well as the Pavamāna hymn. "Pour out the pressed juice on every side"—"pour out the pressed juice on every side"—thus [are] the Vāmra, the Mānava, and the Nūpa.

*tsedhaś cāyam̐ somaḥ*—this is the *havadvāsiṣṭha*; the final [stotras] are the *rathaṃtara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śrāyantīya*, and the *vaiyaśva*; *pari svāno giristhāḥ*—this is the *gāyatra*, the *gauṣūkta*, and the *vāravantīya*; *sa sunve yo vasūnām*, *prāṇāḥ śiśur mahīnām*—these are for the *dīrghaśrudhya*; *somāḥ pavanta indavaḥ*—these are the *śyāvāśva*, the *ndhigava*, and the *niṣedha*; *pari pra dhanva*—these are the *vājadāvaryas*; *ayā ruce*—this is the *nityavatsa*; *dhartā divaḥ*.
The *arka* is the final [stotra] of Dīrghatamas; the *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*; and there is a four-hero *atirātra* with the *ṣoḍaśin*.

This very [rite] is the four-day sacrifice (*caturaha*) which is not attached to the five-night rite of the gods. From the fourth day, one extracts the following six verses: the *punarjarābodhīya*, "he goes to his own world," the *satrāsāhīya*, the *ābhīśava*, the *bṛhat*, the *bhāradvāja*, and the *ātharvaṇa*. 710–711.1.

When they have poured out for Pavamāna Soma that all-knowing, wonderful, and praiseworthy [draught], let your swift powers surge forth; O Indra and Agni, you two who are our protectors, [bring] your skill that brings bliss—thus he draws the Aindrāgna [cup] at the Jarābodhīya [stotra]. In the place of the swelling [of the Soma], he draws the Agni cup with three nidhanas, not pressed [with a stone], with the verse "The stalk is intoxicating. He draws the Śyāvāśva [cup] and the Dhīgava [cup] with the Gāyatra and Gauṣūkta [sāmans], beginning with "Flow for the winning of booty. [He draws] the two-footed and the Atichandas [verses]; the rest is the same as on the final day of the five-night rite of the Gods. 7112.

The Jyotiṣṭoma, the Agniṣṭoma, the Gaur-ukthya, the Mahāvrata, the Gaur-ukthya, the Āyu-atirātra—these are the arrangements for the one-day sacrifices (ekāhas). 7113. The Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha is either in the combined (samūḍha) or the expanded (vyūḍha) form; however, it is indeed the combined form that is used here. For its Bahiṣpavamāna chant on the first day, [the verses] "Upāsmai gāyatā naraḥ," "Upa su jātam apturam," and "Pavamānasya te kava" are employed. The Audala is the Sāman for the Āsita, the Tvaṣṭrīsāman is for the fourth day, and the Krauñca is the Tvaṣṭrīsāman. These are the Svaras of the Pṛṣṭhya. Regarding the Gaurīvita, the Lokat, and the Udvaṃśaputra, they say: "They enter the night from the son of the Udvaṃśa," provided it is the expanded form. 7121.

Now, if it is the *samūḍha* [arrangement], this very [stotra] is the *bahiṣpavamāna* of the first day; these *svaras* are for the second day; "vṛṣā śoṇa" is the final [stotra] of the fifth day, which belongs to the *pārtha*; in the sphere of the *pārtha* is the *ākūpāra*; that which occurs on the ninth day is the *sāṃvatsarika* *samūḍha*; for the subsequent three-day period, there are unmodified *bṛhatīs* for the entire six-day rite.

This is the very same three-day period as that of the *ṛtus* when expanded: on the third day, the *rathaṃtara* is in the place of the *vairūpa*; there are three *tvāṣṭra-sūma* verses; the *aiḍa* is in the middle, with the *bṛhat* on both sides; in the three [verses] are the *jyotis*, *go*, and *āyus*; and the *atirātra* is arranged according to the one-day (*ekāha*) ritual. 7123.

This very five-day rite (*pañcāha*) is the *samūḍha* [form] of the seasons (*ṛtu*), characterized by the *bṛhat* and *rathaṃtara* as the *pṛṣṭha* chants. For the first day, there is the *svādiṣṭhā* hymn for the *ārbhava* laud; for the second day, the *vāsiṣṭha*; for the third day, its own place; for the fourth day, the *pārtha* hymn; and after the *aurṇāyava*, the *bṛhat* and *bhāradvāja*. He extracts the *śuddhāśuddhīya* from the *āndhīgava* for the fifth day, followed by the *ṣoḍaśin*. Above the *saṃtanina* chants, he places the *aiḍa*, the *saindhukṣita*, and the *gausūkta*. The *viśvajit* is the final *atirātra*.

This very six-day period is that which is either condensed or expanded; however, when it is condensed, its vow is that of a one-day sacrifice, and its Jyotiṣṭoma is an Atirātra accompanied by the Ṣoḍaśin cup.

This very six-day period is that which is either condensed (*samūḍha*) or expanded (*vyūḍha*). It is indeed condensed; its vow is the seventeen-fold [stoma]. For it: "Sing forth for him, O men! Flow on, the foremost of speech! Flashing with light, your powers rise up—of you, the purifying one, O Kavi! From the *bahispavamāna*, he removes two *gāyatrī* verses from the latter [set] and [inserts] two *anuṣṭubh* verses from the former. The rest is the same as the previous vow. Its *uktha* hymns follow the sequence of stomas, and the *ṣoḍaśin* is twenty-one-fold. 7132.

This is indeed the same six-day period, whether it is arranged in its natural order (*samūḍha*) or expanded (*vyūḍha*). However, when it is in its natural order, the *chandoma* *pavamāna* is its observance. In the place of the four-verse hymn beginning "Of that *pavamāna*, we [are]," he transposes a triplet; [he places] the *satrāsāhīya* and the *jarābodhīya* there. [He places] the *āśu*, the *bhārgava*, the *mārgīyava*, and the *saumitra*—these being the verses following the *aiṭata*—and those following the *yaudhājaya*: the *bārhaduktha*, the *dvaigata*, and the *pauruhanmana*. [He places] the *śāṃmada* and the others following the *svāśira* and the *ārka*.

The four [stotras] following the Āndhīgava, as well as the Ākūpāra and the Sādhra, have the same *dharma* as their respective [original] first [stotra], namely, the seven-night vow (saptarātrika). 7133.

This is indeed the same six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*), whether it is arranged in a condensed form (*samūḍha*) or an expanded form (*vyūḍha*). However, when it is in the condensed form, a five-day period (*pañcāha*) is attached to it, as follows: on the fourth day, there is the twenty-one-fold *ṣoḍaśī* chant; on the fifth day, the *pārtha* chant, the *ākūpāra*, or the *vātreya*. This applies if it is in the condensed form. Now, if it is in the expanded form, on the fourth day, at the *śuddhāśuddhīya* chant, there is the *ākūpāra*; on the fifth day, the *pārtha* or the *ātreyam*. Or rather, for one who possesses the *chandomas*, the *vratam* has the *bahiṣpavamāna* of seventeen-fold verses; the rest is the same. 7134.

The Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma, the Gauḥ Ukthya, the Āyuḥ Ukthya, the Abhijit Agniṣṭoma, the Viśvajit Agniṣṭoma, the Sarvajit Agniṣṭoma, and the Sarvastoma Atirātra—these are the arrangements for the one-day sacrifices (ekāha). 7135.
That which is the first [day] of the five-night sacrifice of the gods is the unattached [first day] of the Janaka seven-night sacrifice. 7141.

The *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* [verses] are "Pavasva dhārābhir" and "Vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā"; the *paryāsa* is the Gāyatra, the Hāviṣmat, and the Ājiga; these are single-verse [hymns]. "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā" is the Triṇidhana Āyāsya on three verses; the Maukṣya is in the world of the Moon; the Saubhara of Aupagava is with the Svāśira; the rest is the same as that of the second day of the five-night rite of the Gods. 7142.

The *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* [verses] are as follows: "High is your birth from the soma-juice" (*uccā te jātam andhasaḥ*) is a *gāyatra* hymn; the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha* is *svāra*; the *sauparṇa* consists of those single verses (*ekarcā*); "Toward us, O Āyus, flow the Soma-drops" (*abhi somāsa āyavaḥ*) is the *antarikṣa* [hymn]. On three verses, the *śrāyantīya* belongs to the world of the *mahāvaiṣṭambha*. The rest is the same as on the third day of the five-night rite of the Gods. 7143.

The *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* [verses] are [the same]; the *paryāsa* is "Pavasva dakṣasādhana" (Purify yourself, O achiever of skill); the *gāyatra*, *adārasṛt*, and *satrāsāhīya*; the *ekarca* "tavāham soma rāraṇa" (O Soma, with thee I have rejoiced); the *svaḥpṛṣṭha*, the *āṅgirasa*; on three [verses], the *svāśira*; in the world of Arka, the *gauṣūkta*; the *arka* of Lauśa Dīrghatamas; the *traikakubha* of Saubhara; the rest is the same as the fourth day of the Pañcaśāradīya. The Viśvajit, Mahāvrata, Jyotiṣṭoma, Atirātra, and Ṣoḍaśin are arranged as one-day sacrifices.

This is indeed the same six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*) which is condensed according to the seasons (*ṛtu*), not joined by repetition, with the *Bṛhat* and *Rathantara* as the *pṛṣṭha* chants on the fourth day; for the sixth day, he transposes the *Gaurīvita*—the *ṣoḍaśin* *sāman* sung on the verse "pratyasmai pipīṣate"—from its place among the *Revatī* verses to the *Dārḍhacyuta*; [then follows] the *Aukṣṇorandhra* and the *Viśvajit Atirātra*.

This is indeed the same six-day period, whether condensed or expanded; however, when condensed, the vow is that of a one-day rite (*ekāhika*), ending with a *Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra* without the *ṣoḍaśin*.

This very six-day period is that which is either condensed (*samūḍha*) or expanded (*vyūḍha*). When condensed, it consists of the *jyotis*, *go*, and *āyus* [Soma-sacrifices], followed by an *atirātra*; these are arranged as one-day sacrifices (*ekāha*).
