There is a *jyotiṣṭoma-agniṣṭoma*, a *gau-ukthya*, and an *āyur-ukthya*. For that *āyus*, there is the *Śyāvāśva* [sāman] on one verse, the *Āndhīgava* on one verse, and the *Ākūpāra* on one verse; the *Bṛhat* [sāman] with the *bṛhat-nidhana* Vārka-jambha [sāman] is used on three verses. This is the five-day period of the *Pṛṣṭhya-avalamba*. Then there is the *viśvajit-atirātra*. The *viśvajit-atirātra* is the seventh chapter.
The *caturrātras* (four-night sacrifices) are as follows:
there is the *atricatūrātra* (the four-night sacrifice of Atri), also known as the *caturvīra*.

Now, regarding the four *caturrātras*: the *atricatūrātra* is described by the subsequent section beginning with "The *pavamāna* [stotras] consist of twenty-four verses"; its designation is *caturvīra*.
The arrangement of the first day of the first day:
"Sing forth to him, O men, for the tawny one who possesses his own power! Like restless bulls, flow swiftly toward us, O thou of lofty thought; flow on, O Pavamāna, thou sage! (RV 9.1.1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

"O Agni, come for the feast"—these are the *ājya* verses. "The wise Soma juices"—this consists of the *gāyatra*, the *āśva*, the *jarābodhīya*, and the *āśubhārgava*. "O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—these five consist of the *gauṅgava*, the *yaudhājaya*, the *auśana*, and the final one.
Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The Pṛṣṭha stotras are the Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Naudhasa, and the Kāleya. 4.

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" is in the Gāyatra-Saṃhitā; "pavasvendramaccha" is the Sapha-Pauṣkala; "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ" is the Audala-Gautama-Ākūpāra; and "abhi priyāṇi" is the second Dvir-iḍa-pada-stobha. || 5 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.]
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.
The Pavamāna stotras consist of twenty-four-fold hymns; the Ājya stotras are threefold; the Pṛṣṭha stotras are fifteenfold; and the Agniṣṭoma is seventeenfold. || 6 ||
Thus ends the first day. || 1 ||
The second day:

for the second day, [the chant is] "Flow on, the foremost of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. "O Soma, you are brilliant; for you are a bull by your radiance. "Being purified, Soma flows; we [worship] you, the purifying Pavamāna. (1) Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

"Let us choose Agni as the messenger"—with these words, the *ājya* offerings [are performed]. "Flow on, O bull, in your stream"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *hāviṣmat*, the *ājiga*, the *svāra*, and the *sauparṇa*. "O Soma, being purified, flow in your stream"—this is the *āyāsya*; within it is the *dairghaśravasa*. "The red bull"—this is the final *pārtha*.
[Thus ends] the Mādhyamdina Pavamāna.

The *pṛṣṭha* chants are the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *mādhucchandasa*. "The exhilaration which is most excellent" (*yaste mado vareṇyaḥ*) is the *gāyatra*; the *svāśira* hymn is the *arka*. "O member of the gods, flow for the feast of the gods" (*tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya pavasva devavītaye*) is the *ṣaḍkusujñāna*.

"This Pūṣan is wealth, he is Bhaga" (*ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ*) is the *āsita*; there are two *krauñca* chants. "The bull of prayers flows" (*vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate*) is the *caturiḍa*, with the *padastobha* at the end.

[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna. Regarding the two *krauñca* [melodies]: "This Pūṣan, ho! is one; "This Pūṣan, ho! Wealth, Bhaga, e! is the other. These two should be employed in reverse order for the sake of avoiding monotony (*ajāmi*). Otherwise, there would be monotony due to the collision of those two *krauñcas*, which possess the same accentuation (*svarita*). || 3 ||
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*; the *auśana*, *saubhara*, and *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* are the *uktha*s.

The *preṣṭhaṃ vaḥ* hymn belongs to Auśana; the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* is first, because of the statement: "First, once, in the *anukthya*, in the *ahīna*, and in the *rātri*. The *pavamāna* stotras consist of twenty-four-fold verses; the *ājya* stotras are fifteen-fold; the *pṛṣṭha* stotras are seventeen-fold; and the *agniṣṭoma* is twenty-one-fold, including the *uktha* stotras. || 4 ||
Thus ends the second day. || 2 ||
The third day:

For the third day—“With flashing luster, these drops have been poured forth; the King goes with the sacrificial offerings. They have been poured forth, the vigorous ones; O Soma, flow for nourishment with your stream toward the beloved [goal]. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"Agni kindles Agni"—these are the *ājya* verses. "Agni with Agni, I invoke Mitra; with Indra, I invoke them"—these are the *ājya* verses.

"Uccā te jātam andhasaḥ"—this is the Gāyatra, the Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha, the Aiḍa, and the Sauparṇa; "Abhi somāsa āyavaḥ"—this is the Gautama, the Antarikṣa, the Maidhātitha, and the Dvihikāra; and "Tisro vācaḥ"—this is the final Saṃkrośa of the Aṅgirases. || 3 ||
"Abhi tvā vṛṣabha" [is the Sāman] for the pressed juice; "Rathantara," "Ka stam indra tvā vasavaḥ," the Vāmadevya, the Śrāyantīya, and the Raurava. 4.
Thus [end] the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].
"Taraṇiritsiṣāsati" is the Raurava [Sāman]. The Gāyatrī is the metre of the Rathantara; the Bṛhatī is that of the Vāmadevya. || 4 ||

"Three voices arise" is the Gāyatra and the *arka* of Agni; "Press out, O friends, pour it around, sit down" is the *vācaḥsāma* and the *śaukta*; "The pressed juices, most full of honey"—these two are the *tvāṣṭrīsāmanī* in the *svāra* [melody] between the *andhīgava* and the *pavitra*; "That is your filter"—this is the final sixfold *iḍāpada-stobha*. || 5 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
Regarding the two *tvaṣṭrīsāman* chants in the *svāra* mode: "sutāsomāhā" is one, and "sutā somā" is the other; between these two is the *āndhīgava*. 5.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The hymns for Āyus. 7.
The Pramahiṣṭhīya, the Hārivarṇa, and the Udvaṃśīya.

Now, as for the Stomas: the Pavamāna chants are twenty-fourfold; the Ājya-lauds are seventeenfold; the Pṛṣṭha-lauds are twenty-onefold; and the Agniṣṭoma, together with its Ukthas, is twenty-ninefold. || 7 ||
Thus ends the third day. || 3 ||
The Pavamāna of the fourth day has brought forth the fourth day. This immortal god, he shall come with the wisdom of the Aṇvī; [bring] to you skill that is bliss-bestowing. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
The immortal god, the Hotṛ, whatever great Indra there is today at the rising of the sun for the sake of power—he whom [I invoke] with a beautiful hymn. 2.
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.

The *āmahīyava* and *satrāsāhīya* [sāmans] are based on the *gāyatra* verse beginning with "asya pratnāmanudyutam. The *pārśva*, *ātharvaṇa*, *abhīśava*, and *utsedha* [sāmans] are based on the verse beginning with "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam. The final [sāman], the *vāsiṣṭha*, is based on the verse beginning with "ayaṃ sāma. || 3 ||
Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
"When you were born, O unprecedented one," and "The great, most intoxicating [draught] of honey"—this is the Vāmadevya, the Traiśoka, and the Samanta.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].
The *anuṣṭubh* is the metre of the *bṛhat* [sāman]; the *uṣṇih* is that of the *vāmadevya*; the *atijagatī* is that of the *traiśoka*.
"yata indra" [is used] for all [the directions]. || 4 ||

"Pari svāno giriṣṭhā" (RV 9.61.12) is the Gāyatra and the Gauṣūkta; "sa sunve yo vasūnām... śiśurmahīnām" (RV 9.61.14) is the Dīrghavāravantīya; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" (RV 9.61.18) is the Niṣedha and the Śyāvāśva; "pari pra dhanva" (RV 9.61.22) is the Ṛk of Dīrghatamas; and "dhartā divaḥ" (RV 9.61.23) is the Aṣṭeḍa with the final *padastobha*.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna. The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. 5–6.
The Sākamaśva, the Traikakubha, and the Nārmedha. || 7 ||
Thus end the hymns.
The meter of the Traikakubha is the Uṣṇik. || 6 ||
The Gaurīvita is the Ṣoḍaśin-sāman; the night is the junction.

Now, the Stomas: the Pavamāna lauds are twenty-four-fold; the Ājya lauds are twenty-one-fold; the Pṛṣṭha lauds are twenty-seven-fold; the Agniṣṭoma is thirty-three-fold; the Uktha lauds, together with the Ṣoḍaśin, are twenty-one-fold; the night-chant is fifteen-fold; and the Sandhi is threefold.
The preceding days end with the consumption of curds; the final day ends with the Udavasānīyā offering. Thus concludes the fourth day. 4.
The three- or four-night rite is completed.

The *Jāmadagnya-caturrātra* is described by the section beginning with "The first day is the *Trivṛt-pañcadaśa* Agniṣṭoma; [this is] the first day. Regarding this, the Sūtra states: "On the thirteenth day of the dark fortnight, one should undergo initiation for the *Jāmadagnya*, etc. This is the ritual procedure (*kalpa*) for the first day.
"Upo ṣu jātam apturam" is the *anurūpa*; the *brahmasāman* is the *naudhasa*. In the world of Sujñāna, the *pauṣkala* is used. "Pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ" belongs to Audala-Gautama.
The rest is the same as the first day of the *abhiplava* period.
Thus: "Sing unto him, who has been born, the water-crosser; O Sage, [sing] of thee, the purifying one"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, come for the feast"—with these [verses] are the offerings of clarified butter.

"Forward, O Soma, for the inspired ones"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *aśva*. "Forward, O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—this is the *pajra*, the *yaudhājaya*, and the *auśana* as the final one. This *yaudhājaya* indeed has a two-syllable *nidhana*. The *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *naudhasa*, and the *kāleya*—these are the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"svādiṣṭhayā" and "gāyatrasaṃhite"; "ayā pavasva devayu" and "pavate haryato hariḥ" are the *sapha* and *pauṣkala* [stotras]; "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ" is the *audalagautama*; the last [verse] belongs to Kava; with the exception of the Kava verses, they consist of single stanzas. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
On this day, there is an alternating application of the *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* stomas.
Thus ends the first day. || 5 ||
The second day:
the ritual procedure for the second day. He extracts the Ājigarta and Krauñca [sāmans]; the Uṣṇih and Kakubh [metres] in their own places; the Yāma [sāman] in its own verses.
The rest is the same as the second day for the Caturvīra [rite]. || 2 ||

Thus [it is said]: "The two *uṣṇih* and *kakubh* meters are one's own. This means they belong to the second day of the *ābhiplavika* [six-day period]. The *bahispavamāna* chant consists of the verses: "Flow for speech," "Flow down, O Indu," "O Soma, you are a bull," "Soma, being purified, flows," and "Of you, the purifying sage."

The *ājya* offerings are with the verse: "We choose Agni as the messenger. The *gāyatra* chant is "Flow on, O bull, in your stream," which belongs to Haviṣmān and Suparṇa. The chant beginning with "O Soma, being purified, flow in your stream" consists of the *aiḍa*, the *āyāsya*, the *dairghaśravasa*, and the *triṇidhana* *āyāsya*. The final [chant] is "The red bull," belonging to Pārtha.
The Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita, and the Mādhucchandasa are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the Gāyatra and the Svāśira hymn by Arka; "pavasvendram accha"—this is the Śaṅkusujñāna; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayir bhagaḥ"—this is the Āsita and the Krauñca; "vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate"—this is the Yāma, which is the final [hymn]; the Krauñca is the extraction of the Svāra.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The Auśana, Saubhara, and Māṣṭādaṃṣṭra are the Ukthas; the Stomas are those declared in the Brāhmaṇa.
Thus ends the second day. || 6 ||

On the third day: then for the following day, the *bahiṣpavamāna* is the twenty-four-fold; the three *ājya* stotras are fifteen-fold; the *acchāvāka*’s [stotra] is seventeen-fold; the midday *pavamāna* is twenty-one-fold; two *pṛṣṭha* stotras are seventeen-fold; two [other *pṛṣṭha* stotras] are twenty-one-fold; and the third pressing (*savana*) is twenty-one-fold, consisting of the *uktha* stotras.
The ritual procedure for the third day:

he extracts [the verses] with the hymn "asṛkṣata pra vājinaḥ. Following the *arka* of Agni comes the *aiḍa* of Saindhukṣita, in the place of the *tvāṣṭrīsāman* which possesses repetition. The *tvāṣṭrīsāman* has three *nidhanas*; it is well-sounding and unimpaired.
The rest is the same as for the third day of the Caturvīra [rite]. || 2 ||

Thus: "With flashing luster, these drops have been poured forth; the King goes with the songs of wisdom. These Soma juices flow toward the beloved [goal]; for strength, flow with your stream across the *barhis* during the *pavamāna*."

The *ājya* verses are: "With Agni I invoke the enemy," and "With Indra I invoke them. The *gāyatra* hymn beginning with "High is thy birth from the soma-plant" belongs to Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha; it is in the *aiḍa* meter and is the *sauparṇa*. The hymn beginning with "Toward us, O Somas," belongs to Gautama; it comprises the *antarikṣa*, the *maidhātitha*, and the two *hiṃkāras*. The final verse, "Three voices," is the *saṃkrośa* of the Aṅgirases.
"Abhi tvā vṛṣabha sutaḥ"—this is the Rathantara; "Kaḥ tam indra tvā vasavaḥ"—this is the Vāmadevya and the Śrāyantīya; and the Raurava—these are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras.

"Three voices rise up"—this is the Gāyatra, the *arka* of Agni, and the *aiḍa* Saindhukṣita. "Press out, pour around, O friends, sit down"—this is the Vācasāma and the Śaukta. "The pressed juices, most sweet"—these are the Svāra and the two Triṇidhana Tvaṣṭrī-sāmans, with the Andhīgava in between. "This is your filter"—this is the Ariṣṭa, the final one. Here, the Svāra and the Tvaṣṭrī-sāman are the first of the two.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.
The *pramam̐hiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *udvaṃśīya* are the *uktha* chants.

On the third day, the *bahiṣpavamāna* is the twenty-onefold (*ekaviṃśa*); there are three *ājya* stotras; the *acchāvāka*’s [stotra] is the fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*); the midday *pavamāna* is the twenty-fourfold (*caturviṃśa*); the *pṛṣṭha* stotras are twenty-onefold; the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*) is the twenty-sevenfold (*triṇava*); and there are two *uktha* stotras; the *acchāvāka*’s [stotra] is twenty-onefold—such is the rule for the *stoma*s. || 2 ||
Thus ends the third day. || 7 ||
The Fourth Day:
The ritual procedure for the fourth day.
In the place of the Vāravantīya [sāman], one performs the Śrudhya in the Anuṣṭubh meter. The Vāravantīya is performed on the Dvipadā verses; the final hymn is the Arcika of Dīrghatamas. 1.
The rest is the same as for the fourth day of the Caturvīra sacrifice. || 2 ||

Thus: "Pavamāna has generated; this immortal god, he goes with subtle wisdom"—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "The immortal god, the Hotṛ; when today the sun has risen; the great Indra who by his might"—these are the *ājya* hymns. "This [is] of your thought, O Manman. Thus [the *ājya*s].

The Gāyatra, the Cāmahiya, and the Satrāsāhīya beginning with "asya pratnāmanudyutam"; the Pārṣṇi, the Ātharvaṇa, the Ābhīśava, and the Utsedha beginning with "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam"; and the final Vāsiṣṭha beginning with "ayaṃ soma" and containing the word "iha."
The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are: "yajjāyathā apūrvyā" for the Bṛhat; "edu madhormadintaram" for the Vāmadevya; and the Traiśoka and Samanta for the [remaining].

"parisvāno giriṣṭhā" consists of the *gāyatram* and the *gauṣūktam*. "sa sunve yo vasūnāṃ prāṇā śiśurmahīnām" consists of the *dīrghavāravantīye*. "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" consists of the *śyāvāśvam* and the *niṣedhaḥ*. "pari pra dhanva" is the *arka* of Dīrghatamas. "dhartā divaḥ" is the final *aṣṭeḍapadastobhaḥ*.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The Sākamaśva, Traikakubha, and Nārmedha are the Uktha hymns.
The Gaurīvita is the Ṣoḍaśin-stotra; the night is the junction.

On the fourth day, the Pavamāna stotras are twenty-four-fold; the Hotṛ’s Ājya-stotra is fifteen-fold; the three other Ājya-stotras are seventeen-fold; the Pṛṣṭha-stotras are twenty-one-fold; the Agniṣṭoma-sāman is thirty-three-fold; the Uktha-stotras are twenty-one-fold and include the Ṣoḍaśin; the Night-stotra is fifteen-fold; and the junction (sandhi) is nine-fold. Such is the rule for the Stomas.
Thus ends the fourth day. || 8 ||
Thus ends the four-night sacrifice of Jamadagnya.
The four-night Vāsiṣṭha sacrifice is either the Saṃsarpa;
by the section beginning with "The threefold is the morning pressing," the four-night Vāsiṣṭha is described, and that very same [sacrifice] is called the Saṃsarpa.
Regarding the first day: he states the arrangement for that first day;
that which is the first [day] of the Jamadagnya sacrifice is [the first day] of the Saṃsarpa.

Thus: the morning pressing has the *trivṛt* stoma; the midday pressing has the *pañcadaśa* stoma; the third pressing has the *saptadaśa* stoma. This is the arrangement of the *stomas*. The remaining *ṛc*-verses [are to be used] because of the *saptadaśa* nature [of the third pressing]. The remainder is equal to the first day of the *Jāmadagnya* [twelve-day rite]. || 1 ||
Thus ends the first day. || 9 ||
On the second day, he extracts nine verses from the Suparṇa hymns: "Pour out the pressed juice on all sides for Bṛhaduktha and Dīrghaśravas, both descendants of Ayasya. (1)
The rest is the same as the second day of the Jāmadagnya sacrifice.
Thus: "Flow on! Flow on with speech! O Indu, you are a bull, O Soma; you are resplendent, for you are indeed a bull. We [follow] you, the purifying one"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"We choose Agni as our messenger, Mitra, and Indra with songs of praise"—these are the *ājya* offerings for Indra and Agni.

"Flow as a bull in your stream," [is] the Gāyatra and the Hāviṣmat; "Pour out the pressed juice on all sides," [is] the Bārhaduktha and the Dairghaśravasa, addressed to Ayāsya; "The red bull," [is] the final [verse] of Pārtha; the Bṛhatī [meter] was composed by Śaśakarṇa.
The Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita, and the Mādhucchandasa are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the Gāyatra; "svāśirāmarkaḥ pavasvendramaccha"—these are the Śaṅkusujñāna; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"—this is the Āsita and the Krauñca as the last; "vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate"—this is the Yāma as the final one.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.

The *auśana*, *saubhara*, and *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* are the *uktha* chants. The morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*) consists of the fifteen-fold hymn (*pañcadaśa*). The midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina savana*) consists of the seventeen-fold hymn (*saptadaśa*). The third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*), together with the *uktha* chants, consists of the twenty-one-fold hymn (*ekaviṃśa*). || 2 ||
Thus ends the second day. 10.
The third day:

the ritual procedure for the third day of the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*) consists of the *ājya* and *bahiṣpavamāna* chants; the *gāyatrī* [meter] is also used. The rest is the same as on the third day of the *jāmadagnya* [twelve-day sacrifice].

"Thus: 'With flashing luster, these drops have been poured forth; the King goes with the hymns of wisdom. For the sake of nourishment, flow pure for us, O you who bear manly powers—thus maintain the stream,' [this is] the Bahiṣpavamāna."
"By Agni I invoke the enemy; by Indra I invoke them"—these are the *ājya* verses.

"High is the birth of your juice"—this is the Gāyatra and the Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha; "The Soma-drops, the active ones, [flow] toward [the filter]"—this is the Gautama, the Antarikṣa, the Maidhātitha, and the Dvihiṃkāra; "Three voices arise"—this is the final Saṃkrośa of the Aṅgirases.

*Abhi tvā vṛṣabhā sutaḥ* is the Rathantara; *kas tam indra tvā vasavā*, the Śrāyantīya, and the Raurava are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras. *Tisro vāca udīrate* is the Gāyatra and the *arka* of Agni; the Aiḍa and the Saindhukṣita; *ā sotā pari siñcata*, *sakhāya ā niṣīdata* are the Vācasāman and the Śaukta; *sutāso madhumattamāḥ* is the Svārādya and the Tvaṣṭrīsāman; the Āndhīgava and the Triṇidhana are also the Tvaṣṭrīsāman; *pavitraṃ te* is the Ariṣṭa as the final [stotra].
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The *pramahiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *udvaṃśīya* are the *uktha* hymns.
The morning pressing has seventeen [stotras]; the midday pressing has twenty-one; the third pressing, together with the *uktha*, has twenty-nine.
The Fourth Day.

Now he extracts the *paryāsa* for the fourth day: the *vrātyā gāyatrī*, "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā" (the *bṛhatī*), the *vāravantīya* following the *gauṣūkta*, and the *niṣedha* "Purojitī vo andhasaḥ"; he also brings the *dvipadā-aticchandas* verses as the *tvāṣṭra-sāman*. 1.
The rest is the same as the highest day of the Jāmadagnya [Sātra].
Thus: "The purifying one has brought [it] forth; this immortal god, he goes along with the subtle prayer"—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna*.
"The immortal god, the Hotṛ, that today at the rising of the sun, Indra who is great in might—this prayer of mine [is for] you both. These are the Ājya offerings.

For this [day], there are the Gāyatra, the Cāmahīyava, the Jarābodhīya, and the Satrāsāhīya, beginning with "asya pratnām. Then, following "punānaḥ soma dhārayā," there are the Pṛśni, the Ātharvaṇa, the Abhīśava, and the Utsedha. "ayaṃ somaḥ" is the final [verse] of the Vasiṣṭha family, containing the word "iha. "yajjāyathā apūrva" is the Bṛhat; "edu madhormadintara" is the Vāmadevya, along with the Traiśoka and the Samanta—these are the Pṛṣṭhas.

"parisvāno giriṣṭhāḥ" is the Gāyatra; "gauṣūktaṃ" and "vāravantīyam"; "sa sunveyo vasūnāṃ prāṇā śiśurmahīnām" is for the Dīrghaśrudhya; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Niṣedha and the Śyāvāśva; the Tvaṣṭrī-sāman is "yadūrdhveḍam"; "pari pra dhanve" is the Vājadāvarya; "ayā ruce" is the Nityavatsa; and "dhartā divaḥ" is the final Ārka of Dīrghatamas.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.
The Sākamaśva, Traikakubha, and Nārmedha are the Uktha hymns.

The Gaurīvita is the *ṣoḍaśin* chant; the night is the *saṃdhi*; the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*) is the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*); the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina-savana*) is the twenty-seven-fold (*triṇava*); the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*) is the thirty-three-fold (*trayastriṃśa*). The *uktha* chants descend in order: the first is twenty-seven-fold, the next two are twenty-one-fold with the *ṣoḍaśin*, and the night is fifteen-fold; the *saṃdhi* is threefold. Regarding this, the Sūtra states: "On the fourth day of the *saṃsarpa*, etc. (2).
Thus ends the fourth day. 12.
Thus ends the four-night rite of Vasiṣṭha.

The four-night sacrifice of Viśvāmitra consists of an Agniṣṭoma with the Trivṛt stoma, an Uktha with the Pañcadaśa stoma, an Uktha with the Saptadaśa stoma, and an Atirātra with the Ekaviṃśa stoma; thus the four-night sacrifice of Viśvāmitra, known as the Saṃjaya, is described by this Anuvāka.

The first day: regarding its first day, [the verses are]: "pra somāso vipaścitaḥ" on one verse in the *gāyatrī* meter; "āśvam" on one verse; and "jarābodhīyam" on one verse; and "pra soma devavītaye" [which is] the *yaudhājaya* chant on three verses. (1) The rest is the same as the first day of the *saṃsarpa*. (2)
Thus: "Upāsmai," "Upoṣu jātam," and "Pavamānasya te kave" constitute the Bahiṣpavamāna.

The *ājya* verses are "agna ā no mitrāvaruṇā," "indrāgnī," and so forth; the *gāyatra* triplet is "pra somāso vipaścitaḥ"; the triplet for the *āśva-jarābodhīya* melody is "pra soma devavītaye" (the *yaudhājaya* triplet) in three verses, with the final one being the *auśana*.
The Rathantara, Vāmadevya, Naudhasa, and Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha chants.

The two verses beginning with *svādiṣṭhayā* are the Gāyatra-saṃhitā; *ayā pavasva devayuḥ* and *pavate haryato hariḥ* are the Sapha and Pauṣkala; *pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ* is the Audala-Gautama; the last [verse] belongs to Kava; and those consisting of single verses are [to be used] excluding the Kava.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.
Everything is threefold.
Thus ends the first day. 13.
The second day:
regarding the second day, [he says] "O Soma, being purified, flow with thy stream," etc., as the Āyāsya [stotra].
The rest of the *saṃsarpa* sacrifice is the same as the third day.
"Thus: 'Flow on through speech; flow on, O Soma, as a bull, for you are indeed a bull. 'Of you, the purifying one, we...'—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna."
"We choose Agni as the messenger"—with these words, the *ājya* offerings are made.
"Flow as a bull in a stream," this is the Gāyatra and the Hāviṣmat; "Being purified, O Soma, flow in a stream," this belongs to Āyāsya; "The red bull," this is the final [verse] of Pārtha.
The Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita, and the Mādhucchandasa are the Pṛṣṭha stotras.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the Gāyatra; "svāśirāmarkaḥ pavasvendramaccha"—these are the Śaṅkusujñāna; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"—these are the Āsita and the Krauñca; "vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate"—this is the Yāma, which is the last. The Śaṅkusujñāna and Āsita consist of single verses each.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The Auśana, Saubhara, and Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra are the Ukthas; everything is fifteenfold.
Thus ends the second day. 14.
The third day: regarding the third day, he extracts the *saindhukṣita* and *āndhīgava* [verses]. || 1 ||
The rest of the procedure for the Saṃsarpa is the same as that of the third day.
Thus: "With flashing luster these drops have been poured forth; the King moves with the songs of wisdom. "O you who bear manly powers, flow thus in this stream"—this is the *bahis-pavamāna*.
"By Agni Agni is kindled"—these are the *ājya* verses.

"Uccā te jātamandhasaḥ" consists of the Gāyatra and the Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha. "Abhi somāsa āyavaḥ" consists of the Gautama, the Antarikṣa, the Maidhātitha, and the Dvihiṃkāra. "Tisro vācaḥ" is the final call of the Aṅgirases. The Gautama [Sāman] is used for the first verse; the Dvihiṃkāra is used for the middle verse.
"Abhi tvā vṛṣabha suta" is the Rathantara; "Kaṣ tam indra tvā vasu," "Śrāyantīya," and "Raurava" are the Pṛṣṭha stotras.

"Three voices arise"—this is the *gāyatra* chant and the *arka* of Agni. "O friends, pour [the soma] around; sit down"—these two verses constitute the *vācasāma* and the *śaukta*. "The pressed juices, most rich in honey"—this is the *svāra* chant, the first *tvāṣṭrīsāma*, and the *triṇidhana*. "This is your filter"—this is the *ariṣṭa*, the final [chant].
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The *pramam̐hiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *udvaṃśīya* are the *uktha* hymns; everything is seventeenfold.
Thus ends the third day. 15.
The Fourth Day:

On the fourth day, he extracts the *jarābodhīya* and *vāravantīya* [sāmans], as well as the *dvipadā* and *aticchandas* [verses]. "Pour out the pressed juice all around"—this is the *pṛśni*, the *ābhīśava*, the *ātharvaṇa*, and the *jyotiṣṭoma-anuṣṭubh*.
The rest of the Saṃsarpa sacrifice is the same as the final day. || 2 ||
Thus: "The purifying one has brought [them] forth; this immortal god, by means of his wisdom, goes along the narrow path"—this refers to the *bahiṣpavamāna*.
The immortal divine Hotṛ, that Indra who today at the rising of the sun is great in power—“This [hymn] of yours, from my mind”—these are the Ājya offerings.

The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are as follows: "asya pratnāmanudyutam" is the Gāyatra; "āmahīyavaṃ satrāsāhīyam"; "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam" is the Pṛśnyābhīśava; "ātharvaṇam"; "ayaṃ soma" is the Vāsiṣṭha ending with "ihavat";
"yajjāyathā apūrvya", "ehi bṛhat", and "edu madhormadintaram" are the Vāmadevya and Traiśoka; and "samanta" is the final one.

"Pari svāno giriṣṭhā" is the Gāyatra [Sāman] and the Gauṣūkta; "sa sunve yo vasūnām prāṇā śiśurmahīnām" is for Dīrghaśrudhi; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Śyāvāśva Āndhīgava; and "dhartā divaḥ" is the final Arcika of Dīrghatamas.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The Sākamaśva, Traikakubha, and Nārmedha are the Ukthas.

The Gaurīvita is the *ṣoḍaśin* chant; the night is the junction (*saṃdhi*). Everything is twenty-onefold (*ekaviṃśa*). For a junction consisting of a single *stoma*, there is either an insertion (*āvāpa*) or a repetition (*abhyāsa*).
Thus ends the fourth day. || 16 ||
Thus ends the four-night sacrifice, either according to the Jāhnavas or the Vaiśvāmitras.
Thus end the four-night rites.

Now, regarding the five-night [sacrifices], the *devapañcarātra*—the *abhyāsaṅgya*—is followed by three five-night [sacrifices]. The five-night sacrifice of the gods (*devānām pañcarātra*) is described in the section beginning with the verse: "The two threefold pressings."

On the first and second days, there is the two-day rite belonging to Viśvāmitra. In the place of the *jarābodhīya* [stotra], there is the *somasāman*; for the *marka*, the *svāśira*; and for the *saubhara*, the *aupagava*.
Thus [are the rites for] the first and second days. || 17 ||
The third day is the third day of the twelve-day rite. The Rathantara is in the world of Vairūpa; the Arka of Agni Pāṣṭhauhī; the Trivṛt-sāman of Gaurīvita.

The sequence for this three-day period is as follows: *svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā* is the two triplets of the *gāyatra-saṃhita*; the *gautama* [Sāman] is on a triplet; the *āsita* [Sāman] is on a triplet; and the *vācaḥ sāma* and the *śaukta* [Sāman] are on two triplets each.

He describes the arrangement of those three days with the section beginning, "The two-day period of Viśvāmitra. Two days are mentioned as the "two-day period of Viśvāmitra. Regarding these two, the specific feature of the first is that the *soma-sāman* is placed in the world of the *jarābodhīya*. For the second day, the *svāśira* is the *maukṣa* of Marka and the *aupagava* of Saubhara. The third day is said to be that of the twelve-day sacrifice; in the world of the *vairūpa*, the *rathantara* is used, the *arka* of Agni for the *pāṣṭhauha*, and the *tvāṣṭrī-sāman* for the *gaurīvita*.

Its specific feature is as follows: regarding this three-day period (*tryaha*), there is the "re-attachment" (*abhyāsaṅga*). Whatever *stoma* belongs to the third pressing (*tārtīyasavanīya*) of the preceding day is [the same] for the following day. That which is attached to the first two pressings is the "re-attachment. Because of its connection with this, this five-night rite (*pañcarātra*) is called "possessing re-attachment" (*abhyāsaṅgya*). And although that [re-attachment] exists for all five days, it is specifically prescribed here because of the extended application (*atideśa*) of the three-day period that lacks re-attachment.

The specific feature of the first day is the *gāyatra-saṃhita* consisting of two triplets beginning with "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā," and the *gautama* triplet. For the second day, it is the *āsita* triplet. For the third day, it consists of the *vācaḥsāma* and the *śaukta* in two triplets. Regarding the arrangement for the first day: the *bahiṣpavamāna* consists of [the verses] beginning with "upāsmai" and "upoṣu pavamānasya te kave."

The *ājya* stotras are: "agna ā no mitrāvaruṇā" and "indrāgnī. The *gāyatra-sāman* is "pra somāso vipaścitaḥ"; the triplet for the *āśva-sāman* is "somasāma. The *yaudhājaya-sāman* is "pra soma devavītaye"; in the three verses, the final one is the *auśana*. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are: the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *naudhasa*, and the *kāleya*. The *gāyatra-saṃhitā* is "svādiṣṭhayā. The *sapha-pauṣkala* are "ayā pavasva devayuḥ" and "pavate haryato hariḥ. The *audala-gautama* is "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ."

The *kāvamantya* [is the final verse]. The *sapha*, *pauṣkala*, and *audala* are each single-verse hymns (*ekarcas*). The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. There are two *trivṛt* pressings (*savanas*) and one *pañcadaśa*; such is the rule for the *stomas*.
For the second day: "Flow on for speech, flow on, O Indu; thou art a bull, O Soma, for thou art indeed a bull; we [follow] thee, the purifying one"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna chant.

The *ājya* verses are "We choose Agni as the messenger" (*agnim dūtam vṛṇīmahe*). The *gāyatra* and *hāviṣmat* chants are "Flow on, O bull, in your stream" (*vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā*). The *āyāsya* chants are "Being purified, O Soma, in your stream" (*punānaḥ soma dhārayā*), and the final *pārtha* chant is "The bull, the red one" (*vṛṣā śoṇaḥ*). The *pṛṣṭha* chants are the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *mādhucchandasa*. The *gāyatra* for the *aukṣa* chant is "That exhilaration of yours which is most excellent" (*yas te mado vareṇyaḥ*). The *śaṅkusujñāna* chant is "Flow on toward Indra" (*pavasvendram accha*). The *āsita* and *krauñca* chants are "This is Pūṣan" (*ayaṃ pūṣā*).

"Vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate" is the final *yāman*. There are two *kakubh* and *uṣṇih* verses consisting of single stanzas. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. "Preṣṭhaṃ vaḥ" is the *auśana*. "Tvaṃ na indra" is the *aupagava*. "Āṣṭādaṃṣṭraṃ pūrvam" are the *ukthas*. In the fifteenth pressing, there is one [verse] consisting of seventeen [syllables].

For the third day: *davidyutatyā rucā*, *ete asṛgram indavaḥ*, *rājā medhābhir īyate*, and *taṃ tvā nṛmṇāni bibhrataṃ iṣe pavasva dhārā*—these constitute the Bahiṣpavamāna. For the Ājya-stotras: *agnināgniḥ samidhyate*, *ā mitre varuṇe vayam*, and *indreṇa saha dūtyā*. For the Gāyatra-sāman: *uccā te jātam andhasaḥ*; for the Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha-sāman: *abhi somāsa āyavaḥ*. The Paurumadga-sāman is chanted on the first verse; the Gautama-sāman on three verses; and the Āṣkāraṇidhana-sāman on the middle verse.

The final [portion] is the cry of the Aṅgirases: "tisro vācaḥ. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Mahāvaiṣṭambha, and the Raurava. "tisro vāca udīrata" is the Gāyatra and the Agner-arka. "ā sotā pari siñcata sakhāya ā niṣīdata" is the Vācaḥ-sāman and the Śaukta. "sutāso madhumattamā" is the Svāra and the two Tvaṣṭrī-sāmans with three nidhanas. "pavitraṃ te" is the Ariṣṭa, which is the last.

The *svāra* is the *tvāṣṭrīsāman*, which is the first of the two [sāmans] in the second [turn]; however, according to the statement in the *Upagrantha*, the first of the two *svāra*s is the latter in the third [turn]. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. The *pramam̐hiṣṭhīya*, *hārivarṇa*, and *tairaścyam* are the *ukthas*. There are two *saptadaśa* stomas at the pressing; one is *ekaviṃśa*.
Thus ends the third day. || 18 ||
The Fourth Day:

He states the arrangement for the fourth day— "Pavamāna has procreated; purifying himself, he has stepped forth. When, like restless cows, [the waters] have flowed, O thou of lofty thought, run swiftly! The dawns impel the Sun. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"Agni shall strike down the Vṛtras"—this is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ;
his own [verses] follow next.
"O Mitra and Varuṇa, this Indra [has acted] with the bones of Dadhyañc; this is for you from my thought"—these are the *ājya* verses. 2.

"Pavasva dakṣasādhana" is the Gāyatra; "adārasṛt satrāsāhīyam"; "tavāhaṃ soma rāraṇa" is the Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra, the Ābhīśava, the Svaḥpṛṣṭha, and the Āṅgirasa; "uhuvā asya" is the final [verse] of the Vāsiṣṭha. 3.
[Thus ends] the midday Pavamāna.
And the Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Traiśoka, and the Pṛśni. ||4||
Thus end the *pṛṣṭhas*.

"Pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ" is the Gāyatra; "Svāśirā marko bṛhat" is the Bhāradvāja; "Tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya somaḥ punāna ūrmiṇā" is the Bṛhatkakrośa; "Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Nānada, the Tvaṣṭrīsāman, and the Ātharvaṇa; and "Pro ayāsīt" is the Lauśa as the final one. 5.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. 6.
The Saindhukṣita, the Saubhara, and the Udvaṃśīya. || 7 ||
Thus end the *ukthas*.
There are two *savana*s of twenty-one [verses] each; one of twenty-seven.
Thus ends the fourth day. 19.
The fifth day of the fifth day:
[of] Pavamāna—“They have let flow the all-knowing, the prize-winning; this immortal god, he goes with subtle wisdom. [I seek] thy skill that brings bliss. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
The immortal god, the Hotṛ, indeed exists even through many wide spaces; arising with vigor, for you two are the officiating priests of the sacrifice. 2.
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.

The Gāyatra [stotra] consists of "asya pratnāmanudyutam," the Cāmahīyava, the Jarābodhīya, and the Pavamāna Ṛṣabha; the Vāmra, the Mānava, the Anūpa, and the Utsedha consist of "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam"; and the final one, the Vāsiṣṭha, consists of "ayaṃ soma" with the word "iha. ||3||
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Śrāyantīya, and the Vaiyaśva. 3.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"parisvāno giriṣṭhāḥ" is the Gāyatra [Sāman], the Gauṣūkta, and the Vāravantīya; "sa sunve yo vasūnāṃ prāṇā śiśurmahīnām" is for Dīrghaśrudhi; "somāḥ pavanta indavaḥ" is the Niṣedha for Śyāvāśva and Andhīgava; "pari pra dhanva" is for Vājadāvari; "ayā ruce" is for Nityavatsa; and "dhartā divaḥ" is the final Ārka for Dīrghatamas. || 4 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. 5.
The Atirātra sacrifice with the Ṣoḍaśin cup has four heroes.

Thus: the Sākamaśva, Traikakubha, and Nārmedha are the Ukthas; the Gaurīvita is the Ṣoḍaśin-Sāman; the Āhīnikī is the night; and the Saṃdhi [Stoma] is the [Trivṛt]. There are two Triṇavas at the pressings; one is the Trayastriṃśa; the Ukthas descend in order, with the Triṇava first; two are Ekaviṃśas together with the Ṣoḍaśin; the night is Pañcadaśa; and the Saṃdhi is Trivṛt. Thus are the Stomas. || 6 ||
Thus ends the fifth day. ||20||
Thus ends the Devapañcarātra.

The *Pañcaśāradīya* sacrifice is described by the following *anuvāka*: "The *Agniṣṭoma* is the *Trivṛt*, the *Uktha* is the *Pañcadaśa*, the *Uktha* is the *Saptadaśa*, the *Uktha* is the *Pañcadaśa*, and the *Atirātra* is the *Saptadaśa*. Its *sūtra* begins: "In the *Pañcaśāradīya*, one should sacrifice with animal offerings (*paśubandha*)," and so forth.
He states the arrangement of the Stomas:
"This very same four-day rite is that which is not attached to the five-night rite of the gods. (1)
Thus it is said. Regarding that, he states the specific feature of the first day:
"The *punarjarābodhīya* [sāman] goes to its own world. (2)

Thus: that *Jarābodhīya* which was obtained for the gods in the *Pañcarātra* by extension from the *Vaiśvāmitra*, and which was set aside by the statement "the *Soma-sāman* is in the world of the *Jarābodhīya*," returns here once again to its own proper place; this is the meaning. || 2 ||
He states the distinction for the fourth [day]:
after the fourth day, one extracts the six verses of the *Satrāsāhīya*, the *Ābhīśava*, the *Bṛhat*, the *Bhāradvāja*, and the *Ātharvaṇa*. || 3 ||
"The subsequent six-verse hymn" means the latter of these two six-verse hymns, namely "prayad gāvaḥ" and "āśur arṣa."

In this regard, the arrangement for the first [day] is as follows: the *bahiṣpavamāna* is "upāsmai," "upo ṣu pavamānasya te kave"; the *ājya* hymns are "agna āyāhi"; the *gāyatra*, *āśva*, and *jarābodhīya* triplets of *sāmans* are "pra somāso vipaścitaḥ"; the *yaudhājaya* on three verses is "pra soma devavītaye"; the *auśana* is the final one; and the *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *rathantara*, *vāmadevya*, *naudhasa*, and *kāleya*; the *gāyatra-saṃhita* is "svādiṣṭhayā."

"Flow onward with this [hymn], seeking the gods"—this is for the Sapha and Pauṣkala chants. "The beloved tawny one flows," thus [it is said] in the Audala-Gautama. The final [hymn] belongs to Kava. Those other than the Kava consist of single verses. The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. Everything is threefold (trivṛt).
Thus ends the first day.

For the second day: "Flow on for speech, flow on, O Indu; O Soma, you are a bull, for you are indeed a bull. With "Of you, the purifying one," they perform the *bahiṣpavamāna*. For the *ājya* stotras: "Agni, the messenger," "We [worship] Mitra," "Indra, him the singers," and "In Indra and Agni"—these are the *ājya* hymns. For the *gāyatrahāriṣmat*: "Flow on as a bull, in your stream. For the *āyāsya*: "Being purified, O Soma, in your stream. For the final *pārtha*: "The red bull. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *Bṛhat*, the *Vāmadevya*, the *Śyaita*, and the *Mādhucchandasa*.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this *gāyatra* hymn belongs to Aukṣa; "pavasvendramaccha"—these belong to Śaṅkusujñāna; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"—these belong to Āsita Kautsa and Caiḍa; "vṛṣā matīnām"—this final hymn belongs to Yāma. The hymns of Śaṅkusujñāna and Āsita consist of single verses each.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*; the *auśana*, *aupagava*, and *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* are the *uktha*s; everything is fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*).
Thus ends the second day.

For the third day: "With the flashing luster" (*davidyutatyā rucā*), "These [Somas] have been poured forth, the kings of the Indu," "He approaches with the sacred hymns," "Thee, who bearest manly powers, flow for nourishment"—with these verses, the *bahispavamāna* chant is performed. For the *ājya* stotras: "With Agni I invoke the enemy," "With Indra I invoke them. For the *gāyatra* and the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*: "High is the birth of thy juice. On the first day, the *paurumadga* hymn begins with "The Soma-drops, the Āyus. The two triplets of the *Gautama-antarikṣa* are used. The *āṣkāraṇidhana* is used on the middle day.

The final [part] of the *saṃkrośa* of the Aṅgirases is "tisro vācaḥ"; the *pṛṣṭhas* are the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *mahāvaiṣṭambha* with "vayaṃ gha tvā," and the *raurava* with "taraṇir hi siṣāsati. The *gāyatra* is "tisro vāca udīrata" and the *arka* of Agni; the *sakhāya ā niṣīdata* is the *vācaḥ sāma* and the *śaukta* on two single-verse [hymns]; and the *tvāṣṭrīsāmanī* are "sutāso madhumattamā" with the *svāra* and other *atriṇidhana* chants.

"Pavitraṃ te" is the final [verse], which is unharmed. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*, *hārivarṇa*, and *tairaśca* are the *uktha*s. Everything is seventeenfold (*saptadaśa*).
Thus ends the third day.

The *pavamāna* of the fourth day: "Purifying himself, he has been born; purifying himself, he has stepped forth toward the offerings. Like eager cows, the dawns urge on the Sun. This is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. The *ājya* stotras: "May Agni strike down the Vṛtras"; "O Mitra and Varuṇa, this [soma] is for you two"; "O Indra, with the bones of Dadhyañc"; and "This [song] of yours from my mind. The *gāyatra* and *ādārasṛt* chants: "Flow on, O Soma, the accomplisher of strength. And the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* and the *svaḥpṛṣṭha* of Aṅgiras: "In thee, O Soma, I have taken delight."

The final [laud] belongs to Vasiṣṭha, beginning with *ūhuvāha asya*. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras consist of the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *traiśoka*, and the *pṛśni*. The *gāyatra* is *pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ*; the *svāśira* hymn is *arkaḥ*. The *bṛhat* is *tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya somaḥ punānaḥ ūrmiṇā*; the *krośa* is *purojitī vo andhasaḥ*; the *nānada* and the *tvāṣṭrīsāman* are *yadūrve padam*. The final [laud] is the *lauśa*, beginning with *pro ayāsīt*. The *bṛhat*, *krośana*, and *nānada* are each based on single verses (*ekarca*). The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The Saindhukṣita, the Saubhara, and the Udvaṃśīya are the Uktha-stotras; everything is fifteenfold.
Thus ends the fourth day. || 21 ||
The fifth day:
the ritual procedure for the fifth day.
Of the purifying Soma, the all-knowing, which they have released as a wondrous hymn of praise—forward rush the prize-winners! Your vital energies rise up; [we invoke] your skill that brings bliss. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

The *aindrāgna* [stotra] is with the verse, "O Indra and Agni, you two... He extracts the *ṛṣabha* and *jarābodhīya* [sāmans]. In the world of elevation (*utsedha*), he [extracts] the *triṇidhana* of Agni; the *gāyatra* and *gauṣūkta* with the verses, "This stalk for exhilaration... and "Flow on for the winning of booty...". The *śyāvāśva* and *āndhīgava* [sāmans] are with the verse, "Flow on for the winning of booty...". He extracts the *dvipadā* and *aticchandas* [verses]. 1.
The rest is the same as on the final day of the five-night rite of the gods. ||2||

Thus: the *bahiṣpavamāna* ends with "ā te dakṣaṃ mayobhuvam. The *ājya* stotras consist of "hotā devo amartyaḥ," "purūruṇā ciddhyasti," "uttiṣṭhannojasā saha," and "indrāgnī yuvāmime. The *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* [stomas] are used for "asya pratnām. For the first [verse] of the *vāmra*, one uses "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam. For the two triplets of the *mānava* and *anūpa* [sāmans], one uses [the respective verses]. For the *triṇidhana* of Agni, one uses the middle [verse] of the *asyā*. The final [verse] is the *vāsiṣṭha* beginning with "ayaṃ soma" which contains the word "iha."

The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śrāyantīya*, and the *vaiyaśva*. The *gāyatra* and the *goṣūkta* are [performed] with the verses beginning "asāvyaṃśurmadāya. The *dīrghaśrudhya* is performed with the verses beginning "sa sunve yo vasūnām" and "prāṇā śiśurmahīnām. The *śyāvāśvāndhīgava* is performed with the verses beginning "pavasva vājasātaye. The final *arka* of Dīrghatamas begins with "dhartā divaḥ. The *kakubh* and *anuṣṭubh* consist of single verses each. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.

The *sākamaśva*, *traikakubha*, and *nārmedha* are the *uktha* chants; the *gaurīvita* is the *ṣoḍaśin* chant; the *rātri* is the *saṃdhi*. Everything is seventeenfold (*saptadaśa*). According to the principle of a single *stoma*, there is either an insertion (*āvāpa*) or a repetition (*abhyāsa*) for the *saṃdhi*.
Thus ends the fifth day. || 22 ||
Thus ends the Pañcaśāradīya.

The five-night sacrifice consisting of observances (*vratavat-pañcarātra*) is stated by this Anuvāka: "The Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma, the Gaurukthya, the Mahāvrata, the Gaurukthya, and the Āyu Atirātra. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
the Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma, the Gaurukthya, the Mahāvrata, the Gaurukthya, and the Āyu Atirātra. ||1||
They are prescribed for a single day. ||2||

Thus: "The Jyotiṣṭoma is prepared as the world of Gaurivīti-Jambha. By this section, these [sacrifices] are established through the Jyotiṣṭoma and others mentioned in the context of the one-day sacrifices (ekāha): the Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma is the first day; the Gaur Ukthya is the second; the Mahāvrata is the third; the Gaur Ukthya is the fourth; and the Āyu Atirātra is the fifth. Its night is performed in a single day. Except for the first day, the Bahiṣpavamāna chant is performed in the Sadas.

Having gone out before the arrangement of the hearths (dhiṣṇya), the ritual concludes with the scattering of grass and so forth. There are four days ending with the consumption of curds; the fifth day ends with the Udavasānīyā offering. Thus [ends the second section].
Thus ends the five-night period within the vow. || 23 ||

There is a six-day period for the seasons, and then three six-day periods. The first is the *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period. The *ṛtu-ṣaḍaha* (six-day period of the seasons) is described by the section beginning with "The seasons did not find firm footing. Its ritual procedure is that of the *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period, whether in its condensed (*samūḍha*) or expanded (*vyūḍha*) form.

Thus [it is said]. In the *Brāhmaṇa*, the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha* is described as being arranged (*vyūḍha*) over ten nights. According to the opinion of some, this [ten-night rite] should be an unbroken (*avacchinna*) *samūḍha* (arranged in sequence); according to others, it is *vyūḍha* (intercalated). || 1 ||
He states his own view: "But the one who is completely deluded [is indeed subject to rebirth]. (2)
Thus [it is said]. The sense is that in this position there exists a multitude of very strong supporting arguments.

And so the *Nidāna* states: "One should arrange the *pṛṣṭhya* [stoma] when it is cut off; one should group it together; thus it becomes *vyūḍha*," says Śāṇḍilyāyana, and so forth. And since it was his own view that was to be stated therein, this alternative arrangement (*nyāsa*) is presented for the purpose of demonstrating that even the *vyūha*-position is not to be rejected, as it is also the opinion of the Teacher. ||2||
Therefore he says:
"Sing to him, O men, for his sake; sing to him who has been born, the swift one; of you, O sage, as you are being purified"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna stotra for the first day. || 2 ||

The *audala* is the *āsita* and the *tvāṣṭrīsāman*. The unmodified fourth day has the *tvāṣṭrīsāman* and the *krauñca*; these are the *svaras* of the *pṛṣṭhya*. "They approach the night from the son of Udvaṃśa in the world of the Gaurīvita," so it is said if [the arrangement] is expanded (*vyūḍha*). Because of the absence of the nine-day connection, there is a replacement of the *pratnavat* *bahiṣpavamāna* on the first day. "These are the *svaras*" means that these are the *svāra* chants.

This statement was made for the purpose of selecting these [notes] alone by means of the forthcoming declaration, "these are the svaras. Since the Gaurīvita [sāman] is released from the sacrificial session (satra) every day, various svaras have been prescribed here; however, the fourth day is unmodified (*avikṛta*). For in that case, because the Gaurīvita is prescribed as being with the *ṣoḍaśin* [stotra], a previously unknown svara was specifically established to prevent its displacement.

The arrangement for the first day is as follows: the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant is "upāsmai," "upoṣu pavamānasya te kave. The *ājya* hymns are "agna ā no mitrāvaruṇā" and "indrāgnī. The *gāyatra* is "pra somāso vipaścitaḥ"; the triplet of Sāmans is "somasāma. The *yaudhājaya* is "pra soma devavītaye," with the "auśana" as the final [verse] in all three [stotras]. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras consist of the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *naudhasa*, and the *kāleya*.

The duties of the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] are those stated in the passage beginning with "they should carry the chariot on their backs. The *gāyatra-saṃhitā* is "pra somāso madacyutaḥ. The *saphākṣāra* is "ayā pavasva devayuḥ" and "pavate haryato hariḥ. The *audalagautama* is "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ. The last [verse] belongs to the *kāva* [family]. With the exception of the last, they consist of single verses (*ekarcāḥ*). The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. Everything is *trivṛt*. In all cases, the *pathyā* *viṣṭutis* are used.

For the second day: "Flow for the sake of speech, flow for the sake of the cow, O Soma; you are indeed a bull, O Soma. With "We [choose] thee, the purifying one," they perform the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant. [They recite] "Agni, the messenger... and "Mitra..."

The *vayam indram id* section consists of four verses. The *ājya* stotras are *indre agnī*. In this four-verse section, the last verse is omitted. The *gāyatra* and *yauktāśva* are *vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā*. The *āyāsya* is *punānaḥ soma dhārayā*. The final *vāsiṣṭha* is *vṛṣā śoṇaḥ*. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *bṛhat*, *vāmadevya*, *śyaita*, and *mādhucchandasa*. The *gāyatra* and *hāviṣmat* are *yaste madaḥ*.

"Pavasva indram accha" and "Śaṅku sujñāne" consist of single verses each. "Ayaṃ pūṣā rayir bhagaḥ" is the *āsita* for the first [verse]. "Vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate" is the *yāma* for the last three verses. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *sākamaśva*, *āmahīyava*, and *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* are the *ukthas*. Everything is fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*).

For the third day: *davidyutatyā rucā*, *ete asṛgramindavaḥ*, *rājā medhābhirīyate*, *taṃ tvā nṛmṇāni bibhratam*, and *iṣe pavasva dhāraya* constitute the *bahispavamāna*. *agnināmitraṃ huve*, *indreṇa tā huve* are the *ājya* hymns. *uccā te jātamandhasaḥ* is the *gāyatra* and the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*. *abhi somāsa āyavaḥ* is for the first [turn] of the *paurumadga*. The two triplets of the *gautama* and *antarikṣa* are used. The *āṣkāraṇidhana* is for the middle *stotriya*.

The final [verse], "tisro vācaḥ," is the collective cry of the Aṅgirases. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras consist of the Vairūpa, the Vāmadevya, the Mahāvaiṣṭambha, and the Raurava. With the verse "tisro vāca udīrata," there are the Gāyatra and the Pāṣṭhauha. With the verses "ā sotā pari ṣiñcata" and "sakhāya ā niṣīdata," there are the Vācaḥ Sāman and the Śaukta, belonging to two single-verse hymns. With the verse "sutāso madhumattamāḥ," there are the two Tvaṣṭrī Sāmans, beginning with the Svāra and ending with the Atriṇidhana. With the verse "pavitraṃ te," the Ariṣṭa is the final [Sāman].
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *pramam̐hiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *tairaścya* are the *uktha* chants. Everything is seventeenfold (*saptadaśa*).

For the fourth day: *prata āśvinīḥ pavamāno ajījanat* (the purifying one has generated the Āśvina verses at dawn), *prayadgāvo na ṣaḍṛcam* (like cows setting forth, the six-versed hymn); *āśuḥ ṣaḍṛcam* (the swift one, the six-versed hymn); *hinvanti* (they urge on) is the Bahiṣpavamāna chant; *janasya ayaṃ vām indro dadhīcaṃ vāmasya* are the Ājya stotras; *pavasva dakṣa sādhanaḥ* is the Gāyatra, the Atharvaṇa, and the Nidhanakāma; *tavāhaṃ soma rāraṇa* is the Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra, the Ābhīśava, the Svarpṛṣṭha, and the Āṅgirasa; *punāno akramīd abhi* is the Satrāsāhīya as the final [verse].

The *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] are the Vairāja, the Vāmadevya, the Traiśoka, and the Pārśva. The *gāyatra* [stotra] consists of "pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ" and the Aurṇāyava. The Bṛhat [stotra] consists of "tvaṃ hyaṅga somaḥ punāna ūrmiṇā" according to the Kātīṣādīya. The Nānada [stotra] consists of "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" and the Āndhīgava. The Vātsapra [stotra] consists of "somaḥ pavate janitā matīnām" as the final one. The Yajñāyajñīya is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. The Ukthas consist of the Saindhukṣita, the Saubhara, and "vasiṣṭhasya priyam.
The Gaurīvita is the *ṣoḍaśisāman*. Everything is [performed] on the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*) stoma.

For the fifth day: "O winner of cattle, flow on, O Pavamāna, winner of all" (*govit pavastra pavamānasya viśvavit*); "The Soma-streams have flowed forth" (*pra somāso adhanviṣuḥ*)—these constitute the *saptarca*. "The Seer has gone forth" (*pra kaviḥ*)—this is the *saptarca*. "Yavam-yavam" (*yavaṃ yavaṃ*)—this is the four-verse hymn. "Those which are yours" (*yāste*) is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "Thy glory is wide" (*tava śri purūruṇo*), "Arising" (*uttiṣṭhan*), and "O Indra and Agni, you two" (*indrāgnī yuvām*) are the *ājya* offerings.

"Flow on, O Soma, most brilliant!"—this is the *Gāyatra* and the *Yāṇva*, both belonging to Śākala and Arśa. "Soma, being pressed by the pressers"—this is the *Mānava*, the *Ānūpa*, and the *Vāmra*, along with Agni’s *Triṇidhana*. "When, O Soma, [you are] wonderful and worthy of praise"—this is the final *Śaiśava*. The *Pṛṣṭha* chants are the *Mahānāmnīs*, the *Vāmadevya*, the *Bārhadgira*, and the *Rāyovājīya*. "This stalk is intoxicating"—this is the *Gāyatra* and the *Santani*. "Toward splendor, great fame, the vital breaths, the child of the great ones"—this is the *Cyāvana* and the *Krośa*.

"Pavasva vājasātaye" is the Tvaṣṭrī Sāman; and that which has repetition (sābhyāsa). Also the Ṛṣabha Śākvara, the Pārtha, the Aṣṭeḍa, and the Padastobha. "Indur vājī pavate gonyoghā" is the final Dāśaspatya. The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma Sāman. And the Saṃjaya, the Saumitra, and the Mahāvaiṣṭambha are the Ukthas.
Everything is twenty-sevenfold.

For the sixth day: *Jyotir yajñasya asṛkṣata*, *pra vājinaḥ pavasva devavīḥ*—these ten verses; *sanād aśoci*—these ten verses; *taratsamandī*—this group of four verses; *ete somāsaḥ* is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. *Imam pratibhindhi yajñasya* are the *ājyās*. *Indrāyendo marutvate* is the *gāyatram*, the *iṣovṛdhīyam*, the *gāyatrīkrauñcam*, the *vājadāvaram*, and the *revatīs*. *Mṛjyamānaḥ suhastya* are the *aukṣṇorandhra* and the *svāraiḍa*.

The *vājajit*, the *varuṇasāman*, and the *goṣṭha*; "etamu tyaṃ dakṣa kṣipaḥ"—this is the *vāmadevya* with the particle *iva* at the end; the *vāravantīya* on the *revatī* verses, the *vāmadevya*, the *ṛṣabha*, the *raivata*, and the *śyena*—these are the *pṛṣṭhas*. The *parisvāna*, the *gāyatra*, and the three *vaidanvatas*; "sa sunve yo vasūnām" and "taṃ vaḥ sakhāyo madāya"—these are the *dīrgha* and the *kārṇaśravasa*.

"Let the Soma drops flow clear"—this is the *svāra* [sāman], the *krauñca*, and the *madhuścunnidhana*; and in the *krauñca*, there are the *vāṅnidhana* and *aiḍa* [sāmans]. "Flow on with this"—the final [verse] is the *śnauṣṭa*. "O Soma drops, flow"—this is the *svāra* and *krauñca*. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. The *gūrda*, the *bhadra*, and "the son of Udaṃśa"—these are the *uktha* [sāmans]. Everything is the *trayastriṃśa*.

The night belongs to the *āhīnika* [type] and consists of fifteen [stotras]. The *saṃdhi* is *trivṛt*. There is no *ṣoḍaśin*, because of the statement: "They undertake the night from the *udvaṃśaputra*."
Thus the expanded array is completed.

He states the arrangement for the *samūḍha* [rite]: "Now, if it is the *samūḍha*: this very same [stotra] is the *bahiṣpavamāna* of the first day; these are the *svaras*. For the second day, 'vṛṣā śoṇa' is the final [stotra] of Pārtha. For the fifth day, the *loka* of Pārtha is the *ākūpāra*, as it was on the ninth day. (2)
The annual [Soma sacrifice] is performed with the Samūḍha arrangement; the Bṛhatī verses of the subsequent [period] are unmodified throughout the entire six-day period.

Thus: for the Samūḍha [Soma sacrifice], the first three days are entirely like those of the Vyūḍha. On the second day, in place of the Vāsiṣṭha [sūkta] beginning with "vṛṣā śoṇaḥ," the Pārtha [sūkta] is used; this is the distinction.

For the fourth day—the *samūḍha* [arrangement] of the Gavāmayana prescribed in the section beginning with "Pavamāno ajījanat" is to be performed for the subsequent three-day period (*tryaha*). Because the adaptation of the *abhīvarta* and *kāleya* [sāmans] is employed for the Gavāmayana, the *mādhyaṃdina-bṛhatīs* for this entire six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*) are those belonging to the ten-night rite (*dāśarātrika*). In that regard, this is the arrangement for the fourth day.

"Pavamāna has brought [beings] forth; purifying himself, he has stepped forward, as swift as eager cows. Flow quickly, O you of lofty thought! The dawns urge the Sun onward"—this is the *Bahispavamāna*. "May Agni strike down the Vṛtras; this Indra [has done so] with the bones of Dadhyañc. This [is the song] for you two from my mind, O Mitra and Varuṇa"—these are the *Ājyas*. "Flow on, accomplishing strength"—this is the *Gāyatra*, the *Atharvaṇa*, and the *Nidhanakāma* hymns.

"O Soma, I have rejoiced in thee"—this is the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* [stotra] belonging to Ābhīśu, whose back is the sky, and which belongs to Aṅgiras. "Soma flows, the progenitor of hymns"—this is the final *janitra*. The *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] are the *vairūpa*, the *vāmadevya*, the *traiśoka*, and the *pṛśni*. "The sage of heaven around the dear [drops]"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *aurṇāyava*. "For thou, O divine Soma, being purified, with thy wave"—these are the *bṛhat* and the *kātīṣādīya*. "With the conquest of your food"—this is the *nānada* and the *āndhīgava*.

The *lauśa* chant, ending with "pra ta āśvinīr," is the *yajñāyajñīya*, the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *ukthas* are the *saindhukṣita*, the *saubhara*, and the "dear to Vasiṣṭha. The *ṣoḍaśin-sāman* is the *gaurīvita*. Everything is in the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*) stoma.

For the fifth day: the *pavamāna* [laud] consists of the verses "O Soma, knower of all," "The wonderful hymn," "The Somas have flowed forth," "The sage for the feast of the gods," "Like barley, O you who are like barley," and "Those streams dripping with honey. The *ājya* [stotras] consist of "O Agni, we meditate on the hymn," "Even by the wide [path]," "Indeed, there is," "Rising up with vigor," and "O Indra and Agni, these two of yours. The *gāyatra*, *yaṇva*, *śākala*, and *vārśa* [sāmans] are used with the verse "Flow forth, O Soma, most brilliant."

The *soma uṣvāṇaḥ sotṛbhiḥ* [verses] constitute the *mānava*, the *ānūpa*, the *vāmra*, and the *triṇidhana* of Agni; the *indurvājī* [verse] is the final *sampātya*. The *pṛṣṭhas* are the *mahānāmnīs*, the *vāmadevya*, the *bārhadgira*, and the *rāyovājīya*. The *gāyatra* and the *saṃtani* are [the sāmans] for "this soma-stalk, intoxicating"; the *cyāvana* and *krośa* are for "toward splendor, great fame, the vital breaths, the child of the great ones. The *tvāṣṭrīsāman* and the *ṛṣabha* [sāman] of the *śākvara* family, along with the *ākūpāra*, are for "purify yourself for the winning of booty."

And *cāṣṭeḍa* is the *padastobha*. With the two verses beginning "govit pavasva," the final [laud] is the *lauśa* with double repetition. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. The *ukthas* are the *saṃjaya*, the *saumitra*, and the *mahāvaiśvāmitra*. Everything is the *triṇava* stoma.

For the sixth day: *asṛkṣata pra vājinaḥ*, *etamu tyaṃ daśa kṣipaḥ*, *pavasva devavīrati*, *sanā ca soma jeṣi ca*, *taratsamandī dhāvati*, *ete somā asṛkṣata*—these are the Bahiṣpavamāna chants. *yamagne pṛtsu martyam*, *prati vāṃ sūra udite*, *bhindhi viśvā abhi dviṣaḥ*, *yajñasya hi stha ṛtvijā*—these are the Ājya offerings.

"O Indu, for Indra accompanied by the Maruts"—this [section] contains the Gāyatra, the Ceṣovṛdhīya, the Gāyatrīkrauñca, the Vājadāvarya, and the Revatīs. "Being cleansed by the skillful hand"—this is the Auksnorandhra, the Vājajit, the Varuṇasāman, and the Goṣṭha of the Aṅgirases. "Flow on with this"—the final [verse] is the Īhavat of the Vasiṣṭhas. Upon the Revatī verses are the Vāravantīya, the Vāmadevya, the Ṛṣabha Śākvara, and the Śyena; these are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras. "Being purified, he who dwells on the mountains"—this is the Gāyatra and the three Vaidanvatas.

"sa sunve yo vasūnām" and "tam vaḥ sakhāyo madāya" [are the nidhanas] for the Dīrgha and Kārṇaśravasa [Sāmans]. "Somāḥ pavante" is the Krauñca [Sāman], and the first of the three [is the same]. In the Krauñca, there is the Madhu-cit nidhana; and in the Vāṅnidhana-Īḍa, there is the Jyotis [Sāman]. The Yajñasya [Sāman] belongs to the Maruts, and the Dhenu is the last. The Agniṣṭoma-sāman is the Yajñāyajñīya. The Gūrda [Sāman] is for Bhadra, and the Ukthas are for Uvaṃśaputra. The entire Trayastriṃśa [Sāman] is used. Regarding the statement "they proceed to the Rātri from the Uvaṃśaputra," this is the same here as well.

Regarding the question of how the night is to be treated during the six-day period of the *ṛtu*, Gautama states that it "should be performed" without distinction, based on the statement in the *Nidāna*. In that context, the night belongs to the preceding day; the fifteenth [lunar day] is the junction (*saṃdhi*).
Thus it is summarized.
Thus ends the six-day period of the seasons. || 24 ||

The six-day period for one desiring long life consists of a *trivṛt* *agniṣṭoma*, a *pañcadaśa* *ukthya*, a *saptadaśa* *ukthya*, and a *jyotir-gaur-āyuḥ* *atirātra*; thus the six-day period for one desiring long life is stated in this section. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
this is the same three-day period as that which occurs in the expanded form (*vyūḍha*) of the seasons.

On the third day, in the world of the Vairūpa [stoma], there is the Rathantara; "sutāso madhumattama" (the pressed juices, most sweet) are three Tvaṣṭṛ-sāmans; the Aiḍa is in the middle, flanked on both sides by the Svara and Bṛhat [sāmans] in three verses.
The Jyotis, Gaurāyus, and Atirātra; these are arranged as one-day sacrifices (ekāha). || 3 ||

Thus [it is said]. Its first three-day period is like the *ṛtu-ṣaḍaha*. For the second day, the final *vāsiṣṭha* [sāman] belongs to the midday pressing, because of the specific statement, "as in the *vyūḍha*. For the third day, the *rathantara* is in the place of the *vairūpa*; however, for the *ārbhava* [laud], there are the three verses beginning with "the voices rise up," which are the *gāyatra* and the *pāṣṭhauha*. [The verses] "O pressers, pour it around" and "O friends, sit down" contain the *śaukta* *sāman* and the *aikarcika* *sāman*.

The *Tvaṣṭrī* sāman, beginning with "sutāso madhumattamā," is performed on the first of the two *svāra* verses in the first [verse]; the *aiḍa* [sāman] is on the middle one; and the second of the two *svāra* verses is on the last one. The *bṛhat* [sāman] is on all three. The final [sāman], beginning with "pavitraṃ te," is the *ariṣṭa*.

The Jyotiṣṭoma is the Agniṣṭoma, which is the fourth day. Here, since both the third and fourth days would have the Rathantara as their *pṛṣṭha* stotra, there would be monotony (*jāmitā*); therefore, to avoid this, the Bṛhat is prescribed for the third day during the *ārbhava* pavamāna. The Gaurukthya is the fifth day. The Āyur-atirātra is the sixth. The Jyotis and others are arranged according to the rules of the one-day sacrifices (*ekāha*). || 3 ||
Thus ends the six-day rite for those desiring long life. 25.

The *pṛṣṭhyāvalamba* six-day period, the *abhyāsaṅgya* five-day period, and the *viśvajit* *atirātra*—by this [introductory] section, the *pṛṣṭhyāvalamba* six-day period is described. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
This very same five-day period is that which is combined with the seasons, joined by repetition, and characterized by the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* *pṛṣṭha* chants. || 1 ||

Thus: like the *ṛtu-ṣaḍaha*, it is arranged in a condensed form (*samūḍha*); like the *deva-pañcarātra*, it is characterized by the repetition of the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* *pṛṣṭha* chants; this is the five-day rite (*pañcāha*). ||1||
The *svādiṣṭhayā* verse belongs to the *Arbhava-pavamāna* of the first day.
For the second day, the Vāsiṣṭha is the last; the Pārtha is in its own place.
On the fourth day, after the Aurṇāyava, he extracts the Bṛhadbhāradvāja from the Āndhīgava; [he extracts] the Śuddhāśuddhīya for the Ṣoḍaśin.
On the fifth day, following the *santani* chants, there are the *aiḍa*, the *saindhukṣita*, and the *gauṣūkta*.

Thus: "Sing for him, O men; sing unto him who has been born from his mother," and "O Sage, of you, the purifying one"—these are the *bahiṣpavamāna* stotras. "O Agni, come for the feast"—these are the *ājya* stotras. "The wise Soma juices flow forth"—this is the *gāyatra* *āśva* *sāman*. "O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—these are the three verses of the *sāman* called *saumasa*. "O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—in these three verses is the *yaudhājaya*; the *auśana* is the final [verse]. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *naudhasa*, and the *kāleya*. "With the sweetest [hymn]"—these are the *gāyatra-saṃhitā* verses.

"Flow on with this [hymn]," "the beloved one flows, the tawny one," and "with the hoof-strike"—these are for Saphākṣāra. "For the pressed juice," [is for] Audala-Gautama. The last [verse] is for Kava. The verses of Saphākṣāra and Audala consist of single stanzas each. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. There are two *trivṛt* libations; one is *pañcadaśa*.

For the second day: "Flow for speech, flow for the waters, O Soma, bull; for you are indeed a bull," [is the beginning of] the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant, with the verses "Of you, the purifying one" and so forth. The *ājya* chants begin with "Agni, the messenger. For the *gāyatra* chant, there are the hymns of Ayāsya, "Purifying yourself, O Soma, in your stream" and "Yoked-horse. The final hymn is the Vāsiṣṭha, "The bull, the red one," which is like that of the *iha-vat* days. Because the Vāsiṣṭha hymn is not employed on the sixth day, there is no occasion for its transference (*saṃcāra*). Thus, the Vāsiṣṭha hymn remains as it was on the *iha-vat* days, and the Pārtha hymn remains as it was on the fifth day, following the pattern of the ten-night rite (*daśarātra*).

The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *mādhucchandasa*. The *gāyatra* and *hāviṣmata* are [performed] with the verse "yaste mado vareṇyaḥ. The *śaṅkusujñāna* [stotras] are [performed] with the verse "pavasvendramaccha. The *āsitakrauñca* [stotras] are [performed] with the verse "ayaṃ pūṣā. The final *yāma* [stotra] is [performed] with the verse "vṛṣā matīnām. In the *śaṅkusujñāna*, there are two single-verse [stotras]. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *uktha* stotras are the *sākamaśva*, the *āmahīyava*, and the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*. There are two *pañcadaśa* chants at the [midday] pressing; one is *saptadaśa*.

For the third day: "With flashing brilliance" (*davidyutatyā rucā*), "These drops have been poured forth" (*ete asṛgram indavaḥ*), "The King goes with the sacrifices" (*rājā medhābhir īyate*), and "Flow for our nourishment, O you who bear manly powers" (*taṃ tvā nṛmṇāni bibhrataṃ iṣe pavasva dhāraya*)—these are the *Bahiṣpavamāna* chants. "By Agni Agni is kindled" (*agnināgniḥ samidhyate*)—these are the *Ājya* chants. "High is your Gāyatra" (*uccā te gāyatram*) and the *Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*. "The Soma-drops, seeking men" (*abhi somāsa āyavaḥ*) is the first [verse] of the *Paurumadga*. The two triplets beginning with "Gautama in the atmosphere" (*gautamāntarikṣe*) are used. The *Āṣkāraṇidhana* is used for the *Adhyāsya*. "Three voices" (*tisro vācaḥ*) is the final *Saṃkrośa* of the Aṅgirases.

The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *mahāvaiṣṭambha*, and the *raurava*. The *gāyatra* and *pāṣṭhauha* are [chanted] with the verse "tisro vāca udīrate. The *vācaḥstoma* and *śaukta* *sāmans* are [chanted] with the verses "ā sotā pari ṣiñcata" and "sakhāya ā niṣīdata. The two *tvāṣṭrī* *sāmans*, *svāra* and *triṇidhana*, are [chanted] with the verse "sutāso madhumattamāḥ. The *ariṣṭa* is the final [verse], "pavitraṃ te. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The *uktha* stotras are the *pramam̐hiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *tairaścya*. There are two *saptadaśa* chants at the pressing; one is *ekaviṃśa*.

For the fourth day: *pavamāno ajījanat*, *punāno akramīd abhi*, *prayad gāvo na bhūrṇayaḥ*, *āśur arṣa bṛhanmate*, and *hinvanti sūram usrāḥ*—these are the *bahiṣpavamāna* chants. *agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanat*, *ayaṃ vāṃ mitrāvaruṇā*, *indro dadhīco asthabhiḥ*, and *iyaṃ vāmasya manmanaḥ*—these are the *ājya* chants. *pavasva dakṣasādhanaḥ*—this is the *gāyatra*, the *ātharvaṇa*, and the *nidhanakāma*.

"O Soma, I have rejoiced in thee"—this is the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*, the *ābhīśava*, the *svaḥpṛṣṭha*, and the *āṅgirasa*. "Soma flows, the progenitor of hymns"—this is the final *janitra*. The *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *traiśoka*, and the *pṛśni* are the *pṛṣṭhas*. "The sage of heaven [sings] the dear [verses]"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *aurṇāyava*, and the *bṛhadbhāradvāja*. "For thou, O divine Soma, art indeed... and "Purifying thyself with waves"—these are the *bṛhat* and the *kātīṣādīya*.

"Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" [is the first triplet], consisting of the Nānada, the Āndhīgava, and the Śuddhāśuddhīya. "Pra ta āśvinīḥ" [is the second triplet], with the Lauśa as the final [verse]. The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. The Saindhukṣita, the Saubhara, and "Vāsiṣṭhasya priyam" are the Ukthas. One extracts the Ṣoḍaśin from the Vairāja-apāya. Thus says the Sūtra: "And it departs upon the departure of the Virāj. And the Nidāna states: "Upon the departure of the Virāj-stanzas, they should shave the hair of the Svarāj. There are two Ekaviṃśa stotras at the pressing; one is Triṇava.

For the fifth day: the *pavamāna* [laud] consists of "O Soma, all-knowing," "That which is bright and praiseworthy," "The Somas have flowed forth," "The sage for the feast of the gods," "Grain after grain for us with your juice," and "Those streams of yours dripping with honey. The *ājya* [lauds] consist of "O Agni, we meditate on the hymn," "For even by the wide path there is indeed," "Arising with vigor," and "O Indra and Agni, you two. And the *gāyatra*, *yaṇva*, *śākala*, and *vārśa* [sāmans] begin with "Flow forth, O Soma, most brilliant."

"Soma, pressed by the pressers"—this is both the Mānava and the Ānūpa [Sāmans]. For Agni, there is the Triṇidhana. "Indu, the prize-winner"—this is the final Sampāntya. The Pṛṣṭha [Stotras] are the Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Bārhadgira, and the Rāyovājīya. "This Soma-stalk, for intoxication"—these are the Gāyatra, the Saṃtani, the Eḍa, the Saindhukṣita, and the Gauṣūkta.

"Abhi dyumnam bṛhad yaśaḥ," "prāṇā śiśur mahīnām"—these are for the *cyāvana* and *krośa* chants; "pavasva vājasātaye" is the *tvāṣṭrīsāman* and the *ṛṣabha-śākvara*. The *pārtha*, *cāṣṭeḍa*, and *padastobha* follow. "Govit pavasva" is the *dvayabhyāghāta*; the *lauśa* is the final [chant]. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. The *saṃjaya*, *saumitra*, and *mahāvaiśvāmitra* are the *ukthas*. There are two *triṇava* pressings (*savanas*). One is *trayastriṃśa*.
Because they belong to the remainder of the pressing, the *ukthas* should indeed be *trayastriṃśa*—so says the Sūtra. (25)
Regarding the sixth day, it says: the Viśvajit Atirātra. || 6 ||
And that [chanting] is established by the rule: "For the Viśvajit, [one should chant] 'pavasvendramaccha' for the Satrāsāhīya-śrudhya, if it is an Atirātra," and so forth. || 6 ||
Thus concludes the six-day period supported by the *pṛṣṭhya* chant. || 26 ||

The *Saptarṣisaptarātra* consists of seven *saptarātras*. Now, there are seven *saptarātras*: the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, the *mahāvrata*, and the *atirātra*; this is stated in the Anuvāka. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
This very same six-day period is that which is either condensed or expanded according to the seasons.
But he is indeed deluded. ||2||
This has been explained. || 12 ||
The vow lasts for one day. Its [sacrificial form] is the Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra accompanied by the Ṣoḍaśin cup. ||3||

Thus: "The *śyaita* is the *brahmasāman*, [with the verse] 'O Vrata, we invoke you among all'. In the place of the *gaurīvita*, there is the *audala*. The rest is the same; the one-day (*aikāhika*) vow has been stated by Maśaka as being part of the twelve-night rite (*sāṃvatsarika*). Regarding that, at the end of the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*, the *sūtra*—referring to the *ukthas* as the *sākamaśva*, *saubhara*, and *nārmedha*—states: "In the *atirātra* of the first of the seven-night rites, because the day is a *pañcaviṃśa-stoma*, they are *ekaviṃśa-stomas*, according to the extension from the *jyotiṣṭoma*."
Therefore, there are exactly twenty-one *ukthas*. The *gaurīvita* is the *ṣoḍaśin* chant; it is the twenty-first. The night consists of fifteen [stotras], while the *saṃdhi* consists of nine.
Thus ends the seven-night rite of the Seven Sages. ||27||

The Prājāpatya seven-night rite consists of a *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period, a seventeen-fold *mahāvrata*, and an *atirātra*. Its head is the *trivṛt*, its two wings are the fifteen-fold stomas, its body is the seventeen-fold stoma, and its tail is the twenty-one-fold stoma; thus the Prājāpatya seven-night rite is described by this section.
Its ritual procedure is as follows:
this very six-day rite is performed either in the condensed (samūḍha) or the expanded (vyūḍha) form. ||1||
But he is indeed deluded. ||2||

The seventeenth vow: its [chant] is "Sing forth to him, O men" (*upāsmai gāyata naraḥ*), "Flow on, foremost of speech" (*pavasva vāco agriyaḥ*), "With flashing luster" (*davidyutatyā rucā*), and "Thy powers rise up, O Sage, as thou art being purified" (*utte śuṣmāsa īrate pavamānasya te kave*); this is the Bahiṣpavamāna.
This is clear. || 1 ||
He draws out the Gāyatrīs in the north and the Anuṣṭubhs in the east; the rest is the same as with the previous vow. ||2||
Its hymns follow the sequence of the Stomas; the Ṣoḍaśin is the twenty-one-fold. ||3||

Thus: there are seventeen *ājya* stotras. For this [sacrifice], the *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* are set to "Asya pratnāmanudyutam. The *samanta* is set to "Parīto ṣiñcatā sutam" on the first verse; the *dairghaśravasa* on three verses; the *yaudhājaya* on the *adhyāsya*; and the final *pārtha* is set to "Ayaṃ somaḥ. The midday service (*mādhyaṃdina*) consists of seventeen [stomas]. The *vrata* is the *hotṛ*'s *pṛṣṭha*. Its specific features are: the head is the *trivṛt*, the two wings are the *pañcadaśa*, the body is the *saptadaśa*, and the tail is the *ekaviṃśa*.

The other *pṛṣṭha* stotras consist of seventeen verses each. "Pari svāno giriṣṭhā" is the *gāyatra*; "svāśirāmarkaḥ" is the *arka*. For the two single-verse hymns used for the *śrudhya* rite, "pavasvendramaccha" is the *sapha*. "Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the *śyāvāśva*; "andhīgave" is the *sūryavatīṣu kāvamantyam*. The *ārbhava* consists of seventeen verses. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*, or alternatively the *ilānda*. In the *ilānda* version, the *yajñāyajñīya* takes the place of the *śyāvāśva*. From the beginning of the *uktha* until the end of the *saṃdhi-stotra*, it is like the previous *mahāvrata*.

The *ukthas* are connected to its *stomas*: the seventeen-fold (*saptadaśa*) *stoma* of the day, and the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*) *stoma* which is the archetype (*prakṛti*). Or, for the *vrata*, it is the twenty-five-fold (*pañcaviṃśa*) *stoma* which is the archetype. Here, however, the meaning is that the *ukthas* follow the *stoma* of the day. Thus it has been stated: "They are connected to the *stomas," and they should be seventeen-fold because of the governing context, and so forth. ||3||
Thus concludes the seven-night rite dedicated to Prajāpati. || 28 ||

"For one desiring cattle, there is a seven-night sacrifice consisting of a *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period, a *chandoma-pavamāna*, and an *atirātra* with the *mahāvrata*. By this *anuvāka*, the seven-night sacrifice for one desiring cattle is prescribed. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
"This very same six-day period which belongs to the seasons, whether arranged in a condensed form (*samūḍha*) or an expanded form (*vyūḍha*). (1)
But he is indeed deluded. || 2 ||
The Chandoma Pavamāna is the vow. In the place of the four-verse hymn beginning with "Of that Pavamāna, we [are]," there is a triplet.

He exchanges [the verses] for the *satrāsāhīya*, the *jarābodhīya*, and those following the *yaudhājaya*: the *āśu*, the *bhārgava*, the *mārgīya*, the *saumitra*, and the *aiṭata*; as well as the *bārhaduktha*, the *dvaigata*, and the *pauruhanmana*. He exchanges [the verses] following the *svāśira* and the *arka* for the four beginning with the *śāmmada*; and those following the *āndhīgava* for the *ākūpāra*, the *sādhra*, and the *svāsu dharma*. 4.

The rest is the same as the first seven-night rite. Thus [ends the section]. "Sing forth to him, O men; sing unto him who is born, the impeller of waters; flow on as the foremost of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the bull, pressed with a flashing luster. "These drops have been released; we [partake] of thee, the purifying one; of thee, the purifying one, O Sage"—with these [verses], they perform the Bahiṣpavamāna chant. It is the Caturviṃśa [stoma]; the Ājya-stotras are fifteenfold.

The Gāyatra-stotra consists of "asya pratnāmanudyutim," the Cāmahīyava, the Satrāsāhīya, the Jarābodhīya, the Āśubhārgava, the Mārgīyava, the Saumitra, and the Caiṭata. The Samanta-stotra consists of "parīto ṣiñcata" along with the Dairghaśravasa, the Raurava, the Yaudhājaya, the Bārhaduktha, the Dvaigata, and the Pauruhanmana. "Ayaṃ somaḥ" is the final [verse] of the Pārtha-stotra. Thus, the forty-four-versed Mādhyandina Pavamāna has the Samanta at the first [turn].

In the *pauruhanmana* [chanting], the *vrata* and other *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] are as in the archetype (*prakṛti*). The *gāyatra* [sāman] is "parisvāno giriṣṭhā"; the *svāśira*, *arka*, *śāmmada*, *dāvasunidhana*, *pratīcīneḍa*, *kāśīta*, and *hāviṣkṛta* [are also included]. "pavasvendramaccha" is the *sapha* and *śrudhya*.

"Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Audala; "madhuścinnidhanam" is the Śvāvāśva; "andhīgavam" is the Ākūpāra; and "sādhram" is the Sūryavatī, the last of the Kava hymns. Thus, there are forty-eight verses for the Ārbhava Pavamāna. From the Agniṣṭoma-sāman up to the end of the Sandhi-stotra, it is like the first Vrata.
Thus is the seven-night rite for one desiring cattle. || 29 ||
