The *Kṣullakajāmadagnya* consists of seven nights:

an *abhyāsaṅgya* five-day period, then a thirty-three-night day, of which the thirty-fourth is an *agniṣṭoma*; the *mahāvrata* is seventeen-fold, followed by an *atirātra*. For this, the *bahiṣpavamāna* is twenty-four-fold, the "head" (*śiras*) is nine-fold, the two "wings" (*pakṣau*) are fifteen-fold, the "body" (*ātman*) is seventeen-fold, and the "tail" (*puccha*) is twenty-one-fold; thus the seven-night rite called *Kṣullakajāmadagnya* is described by this section. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
"This very same six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*) is that of the seasons, whether arranged in a condensed form (*samūḍha*) or an expanded form (*vyūḍha*). (1)
But he is indeed deluded. || 2 ||

He is attached to that for five days, just as one relies on the *pṛṣṭhya* [stoma]. On the fourth day, there is the twenty-one-fold *ṣoḍaśī*. On the fifth day, in the world of Pārtha, there is either the *ākūpāra* or the *vātreya*, if it is the *samūḍha* [arrangement].

Now, if the arrangement is expanded (*vyūḍha*), for the fourth day, which is the *Śuddhāśuddhīya*, there is the *Lokākūpāra*. For the fifth day, which is the *Pārtha*, there is the *Ātreya* or indeed the *Pārtha*. The *Bahiṣpavamāna* belongs to the *Chandomavat* vow; the vow is seventeen-fold (*saptadaśa*).
Everything else is the same.

Thus: like the *ṛtu-ṣaḍaha*, there is a five-day period (*pañcāha*) attached to the *pṛṣṭhya* [ṣaḍaha] with various *pṛṣṭhas*, like a hanging ornament. For the fourth day, the *gaurīvita* is the *ṣoḍaśin-sāman* on the twenty-one-fold chant (*ekaviṃśa*), employed with the *vairāja* [tune]. In that regard, in the case of the *samūḍha* arrangement, for the fifth day there is an option between the *ākūpāra* of Pārtha and that of Vātreya; in the case of the *vyūḍha* arrangement, it is the *ākūpāra* of Śuddhāśuddhīya for the fourth day and [the same] for the fifth day.

The Ātreya [chant] belongs to Pārtha; it is indeed for Pārtha. The distinction lies in its suspension from the *pṛṣṭhya* [stotra]. On the sixth day, there is a thirty-third [stoma], ending with the lineage and the son like the six-day rite (*ṛtuṣaḍaha*). The Agniṣṭoma has a thirty-fourth [stoma]. He utters the *hiṃ* sound eleven times.

He [chants] with three, he with seven, he with one; he utters *hiṃ* for eleven verses. He with one, he with three, he with seven; he utters *hiṃ* for twelve verses; he with eight, he with one, he with three. This is the *viṣṭuti* (arrangement) of the thirty-four-versed hymn, because of the statement beginning with "from those of the ten-night rite, it is greater by one," and so forth. The Mahāvrata is seventeen-fold; its *bahiṣpavamāna* is twenty-four-fold; its head is threefold; its two wings are fifteen-fold; its trunk is seventeen-fold.

The twenty-first day is said to be the tail; this refers to the seventh day. Its *bahiṣpavamāna* chant belongs to the *chandoma* vow: "Up to him," "Up to the one born," "O swift one," "Flow pure, the leader of speech," "Flow pure, O Indu, the bull, pressed," "Flashing with light," "These drops have been released," "Of thee, the purifying one," "We [worship] thee, the purifying one," and "Of thee, O sage"—these are for the twenty-fourth day. Everything else is like the seventeen-fold vow and the *atirātra*.
Thus ends the Kṣullakajāmadagnya rite lasting seven nights. 30.
The *Indrasaptarātra* sacrifice is described by the section beginning with "The *Jyotiṣṭoma* is an *Agniṣṭoma*, the *Gauḥ* is an *Ukthya*," and so forth.
Its ritual procedure is as follows:

the Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma, the Gaura Ukthya, the Āyus Ukthya, the Abhijit Agniṣṭoma, the Viśvajit Agniṣṭoma, the Sarvajit Agniṣṭoma, and the Sarvastoma Atirātra. These are the arrangements for the one-day sacrifices (ekāha). ||1||
Thus: "The Sarvajit" refers to the Mahāvrata. The mention of the "Ekāha" (one-day sacrifice) is for the purpose of excluding the [Mahāvrata] that occurs within the year-long cycle. || 1 ||
Thus ends the Indra-saptarātra sacrifice. 31.

The Janaka-saptarātra consists of four days with the *trivṛt* stoma, beginning with the *agniṣṭoma* form; [the remaining] the *viśvajit*, the *mahāvrata*, and the *jyotiṣṭoma-atirātra*. Thus the Janaka-saptarātra is described by this section of the text. Regarding the phrase "beginning with the *agniṣṭoma*," the meaning is that among the four days, the first day has the *agniṣṭoma* as its concluding form (*saṃsthā*), while the others have the *uktha* as their concluding form. [Now] he states the arrangement of the stotras:

"That which is the first [sacrifice] of the *pañcarātra* for the gods, that is unattached to the *janakasaptarātra*" (7.14.1). "Sing forth to him, O men; sing unto the one born, the swift one"—with these verses, [they perform] the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "O Agni, come to us; O Mitra; O Indra and Agni"—these are the *ājya* [stotras]. "The wise Soma juices"—this is the *gāyatra* [stotra]. "The Soma, the horse"—these are the *sāman*-verses. "Forward, O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—this is the *yaudhājaya* [sāman] on three verses. The *auśana* is the final [sāman].

The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *naudhasa*, and the *kāleya*. The *gāyatra-saṃhita* is [performed] with the verses beginning "svādiṣṭhayā. The *sapha* and *pauṣkala* are [performed] with the verses "ayā pavasva devayuḥ" and "pavate haryato hariḥ. The *audala-gautama* is [performed] with the verse "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ. The final [stotra] is the *kāva*; the *kāva* itself is performed on a triplet (*tṛca*). The others are performed on the initial [verses]. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. Everything is in the *trivṛt* stoma. || 1 ||

The *stotrīya*, *anurūpa*, and *paryāsa* of the second day [are as follows]: "vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā" is the *gāyatra* chant; "hāviṣmatam" and "ājigam" are single-verse chants (*ekarcāḥ*). "punānaḥ soma dhārayā" is the "triṇidhana" *āyāsya* chant performed on three verses; in the place of the *maukṣa* [chant], there is the *svāśira* *arka*; and for the *aupagava*, there is the *saubhara*.
The rest is the same as the second day of the five-night rite of the gods.

Thus: "Flow forth," "Flow forth, O Indu," and "Of thee, the purifying one"—these are the *bahiṣpavamāna* chants. "Agni, the messenger"—these are the *ājya* chants. "Flow forth as a bull," "The Gāyatra," "Possessing oblations," and "Come hither"—these are the *sāman*-verses. "Being purified, O Soma, in thy stream"—this is the *triṇidhana* *āyāsya* chant performed upon three verses. "The bull, the red one"—this is the final *pārtha* chant. The *pṛṣṭha* chants are the *Bṛhat*, the *Vāmadevya*, the *Śyaita*, and the *Mādhucchandasa*. "That exhilaration of thine which is most excellent"—this is the *Gāyatra* and the *Svāśira-arka*.

"Pavasva indram accha" is for the Śaṅkusujñāna; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayir bhagaḥ" is for the Āsitakrauñca; "vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate" is for the final Yāma-stotra. The Yāma-stotra itself consists of three verses. The Agniṣṭoma-sāman is the Yajñāyajñīya; the Ukthas are the Auśana, the Saubhara, and the Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra. Everything is in the Trivṛt stoma. ||3||

The *stotrīya*, *anurūpa*, and *paryāsa* of the third day are as follows: "uccā te jātam andhasaḥ" is the *gāyatra* *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*; these are the single-verse (*ekarca*) *svāra* hymns of Suparṇa. "abhi somāsa āyavaḥ" is the *antarikṣa* [sāman] performed on three verses. The *śrāyantīya* is in the world of the *mahāvaiṣṭambha*.
The rest is the same as the third day of the five-night rite of the gods.

Thus: "With flashing luster these drops have been poured forth; flow for nourishment, O stream!"—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "By Agni Agni is kindled"—these are the *ājya* verses. "High is thy birth from the soma-plant"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*, the *svāra*, and the *sauparṇa*; these are the *sāman*-verses. "The Āyu-somas [flow] toward [the goal]"—this is the *antarikṣa* performed on three verses. "Three voices"—this is the final *saṃkrośa* of the Aṅgirases.

The *pṛṣṭha* chants are the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śrāyantīya*, and the *raurava*. The *gāyatra* chant is "tisro vāca udīrate" and "agneścārkaḥ. The *sāman* of the *vāc* is the *śaukta*: "ā sotā pari ṣiñcata," "sakhāya," and "ā niṣīdata. The two *tvāṣṭrī* *sāmans* are "sutāso madhumattamā," which are the *svāra* and *triṇidhana*. "pavitraṃ te" is the final *ariṣṭa*. This same [last] one is used for the triplet (*tṛca*). The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *uktha* chants are the *pramam̐hiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *tairaścyam*. Everything is in the *trivṛt* stoma. 4.

The *stotrīya*, *anurūpa*, and *paryāsa* of the fourth day are as follows: "Pavasva dakṣasādhana" is the *gāyatra*; "adārasṛt satrāsāhīyam" consists of three single-verse hymns (*ekarcāḥ*). "Tavāhaṃ soma rāraṇa" is the *svaḥpṛṣṭha* and *āṅgirasa* performed on three verses. The *gauṣūkta* belongs to the world of Arka, the *svāśira*. The *arka* belongs to Lauśa Dīrghatamas; the *traikakubha* belongs to Saubhara. || 5 ||
The rest of the Pañcaśāradīya sacrifice is the same as the fourth day.

Thus: "Pavamāna has generated [the light]; purifying himself, he has stepped forth; the rays urge on the Sun"—this is for the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "May Agni strike down the Vṛtras; this [Soma] for you, O Mitra and Varuṇa; Indra with the bones of Dadhyañc; this [hymn] of yours from my mind"—these are the *ājya* stotras. "Flow on, accomplishing strength"—this is the *gāyatra*; "unassailable, conquering by the thousands"—this is the triplet of *sāmans*. "In thee, O Soma, I have rejoiced"—this is the *svaḥpṛṣṭha* belonging to the Aṅgirases, performed on three verses. "O, indeed, of him"—this is the final *vāsiṣṭha*.

The *Bṛhat* and the *Vāmadevya*, the *Traiśoka* and the *Pṛśni*—these are the *pṛṣṭha* chants. "The sage of heaven [sings] the dear [verses]" (*pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ*)—this is the *Gāyatra* and the *Gauṣūkta*. "For you indeed, O divine Soma, being purified with your wave" (*tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya somaḥ punāna ūrmiṇā*)—this is the *Bṛhat* and the *Kakrośa*. "With the conquest of your juice" (*purojitī vo andhasaḥ*)—this is the *Nānada* and the *Tvaṣṭrīsāman*. "The supporter of heaven" (*dhartā divaḥ*)—this is the final *arka* of Dīrghatamas. With the exception of the final one, these consist of single verses. The *Yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*.
The *Saindhukṣita*, the *Traikakubha*, and the *Udvaṃśīya* are the *uktha* chants. Everything is in the *trivṛt* stoma. 6.
The Viśvajit, the Mahāvrata, the Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra with the Ṣoḍaśin cup—these are the arrangements for one-day sacrifices (ekāha). ||7||
Thus: the Viśvajit, which lasts for one day, is the fifth day; the Mahāvrata, a Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra accompanied by the Ṣoḍaśin cup, is the seventh day; its night is that of the Ahīna sacrifice. ||7||
Thus concludes the Janaka-saptarātra sacrifice. ||32||
The *pṛṣṭhyastoma* seven-night sacrifice is described by the section beginning:

"The *pṛṣṭhya-stoma* six-day period, the *viśvajit-ati-rātra*. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows: this very six-day period is that which is combined for the seasons, without repetition, having the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* as its *pṛṣṭha* chants. For the fourth day, the *gaurīvita* is the *ṣoḍaśin* chant, with the verse "pratyasmai pipīṣate. For the sixth day, the *dārḍhacyuta* is in the place of the *revatī* verses. One exchanges the *aukṣṇorandhra* chants.
The Viśvajit Atirātra. || 1 ||

Thus, because there is no conjunction with the six *pṛṣṭha* days, there is an extraction (*uddhāra*) of the *revatī* verses. The transposition of the two *aukṣṇorandhra* verses is for the purpose of beginning the *iḍā* chant with the *bṛhatī*. However, in the case of the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, since the *revatīs* and the *aiḍokṣṇorandhra* would coincide, the status of being the commencement of the *iḍā* was disregarded due to the risk of redundancy (*jāmi*).
The Viśvajit Atirātra is the seventh day. ||1||
Thus ends the seven-night Pṛṣṭhya-stoma sacrifice. || 33 ||
The eight-night *pṛṣṭhya* six-day rite, the *mahāvrata*, and the *jyotiṣṭoma* *atirātra*—the eight-night sacrifice is described by this section. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
"This very same six-day rite, whether arranged in the seasonal order (*samūḍha*) or in the expanded order (*vyūḍha*). (1)
But he is indeed deluded. || 2 ||
The one-day vow: the Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra without the Ṣoḍaśin cup. ||3||

Thus [it is said]. Like the six seasons: either in the *samūḍha* (contracted) or *vyūḍha* (expanded) form, with various *pṛṣṭha* chants; this is the first six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*). On the sixth day, there is a night. The vow is that of a one-day sacrifice (*aikāhika*). The seventh day [is as before]. The eighth day is a *jyotiṣṭoma* *atirātra* without the *ṣoḍaśin* cup. Its night is that of the daily performance (*āhīnikī*). ||3||
Thus ends the eight-night sacrifice. 34.

The Navarātra of the gods; now, there are two Navarātras. Of these two, the first is described in the Anuvāka as consisting of a Pṛṣṭhya Ṣaḍaha followed by a Jyotis, a Go, an Āyus, and an Atirātra. Its ritual procedure (kalpa) is as follows: "This very same Ṣaḍaha is that which is either condensed (samūḍha) or expanded (vyūḍha) according to the seasons. (1)
But he is indeed deluded. ||2||
The Jyotis, Gaurāyus, and Atirātra; these are arranged as one-day sacrifices (ekāha). || 3 ||

Thus: like the Ṛtu-ṣaḍaha, the first six-day period has various *pṛṣṭha* chants; the Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma is the seventh day; the Gaur Ukthya is the eighth; and the Āyu Atirātra is the ninth. These, beginning with Jyotis, are arranged as one-day sacrifices (*ekāhas*). ||3||
Thus ends the nine-night rite for the gods. || 35 ||

The second nine-night sacrifice (*navarātra*) is described by this *anuvāka*: "For one desiring cattle, there is the Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma, the Gaur Ukthya, the Āyus Ukthya, the Abhyāsaṅgya Pañcāha, and the Viśvajit Atirātra. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows: the Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma, the Gaur Ukthya, and the Āyus Ukthya. For that Āyus [sacrifice], the Śyāvāśva [tune] is used for one verse; the Āndhīgava for one verse; the Ākūpāra for one verse; the Bṛhat for three verses; and the Vārkajaṃbha with the Bṛhat as its *nidhana*. ||1||
The Pṛṣṭhyāvalamba consists of a five-day period, a Viśvajit Atirātra, and a Viśvajit Atirātra. || 2 ||

Thus: the Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma is the first day; the Gaur Ukthya is the second; the Āyus Ukthya is the third. For that Āyus [day], the *sāman*-triplets are "purojitī vo andhasaḥ," "śyāvāśvam," "āndhīgavam," and "ākūpāram. The Bṛhat [Sāman] is performed on three verses; the specific difference is that it is the Vārkajaṃbha with the Bṛhat as its *nidhana*. These belong to the one-day (*aikāhika*) [sacrifices]. The five-day period is the *pṛṣṭhyāvalamba*; this very five-day period is that which is described starting with "of the seasons" (*ṛtūnām*). The ninth day is the Viśvajit Atirātra. ||2||
Thus ends the nine-night rite for one desiring cattle. ||36||
Thus ends the seventh chapter in the commentary on the Ārṣeyakalpa composed by Varadarāja, son of the venerable Vāmanārya. ||7||

"O Agni, purify our lives"—this is the *anurūpa* [verse]. "Be gracious to us, O Lord of Power"—this is the *abhīvarta*. The *brahmasāman* is "for the one who presses the soma-juice. The *audala* for the son of Divodāsa is "toward the dear things. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the final [stotra], with "homage to you, O Agni, by your might" as the *jarābodhīya*, the *agniṣṭomasāman*. Or, in its own verses, the rest is the same as on the first day of Janaka’s seven-night rite (811). "Like a bull, he purifies himself through our prayers"—this is the *yajñāyajñīya* as the final [stotra]. The *saubhara* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. In its own verses, the rest is the same as on the second day of the five-night rite of the Gods (812).

"O radiant one, for your splendor, the drops have been poured forth; flow for nourishment with your stream. "By Agni, Agni is kindled"—these are the *ājya* verses. "High is your birth from the plant"—this is the *gāyatra* on one verse, the *vairūpa* on one, and the *saumitra* on one. "O Soma, pressed by the stones"—this refers to the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*) in three verses. "The three voices"—this is the *saṃkrośa* of the Aṅgirases. The final [verses] are the *rathaṃtara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *naudhasa*, and the *raurava*. "The three voices arise"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*.

"O friends, sprinkle the Soma; sit down!"—this is the *vāk-sāman* and the *śaukta*. "The pressed juices, most rich in honey"—this is the *tvāṣṭrī-sāman* and the *āndhīgava*. "A filter for thee"—this is the *yajñāyajñīya*, the final *śrudhya*, the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* in its own verses. 82.

Pavamāna has brought [the world] forth; being purified, he has stepped across; as king, he moves with inspired thoughts. You, the hero, bearing manly powers, the sun, the dawns impel you. "May Agni strike down the Vṛtras"—this is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ. His own subsequent [verses]: "Flow on, accomplishing skill," which is the *gāyatra* and the *tvāṣṭrī-sāman*; "When they move about," "The Soma-drops, the Āyus"; "The eighteen-fold" is the *ātharvaṇa*, the *abhīśava*, and the *svaḥ-pṛṣṭha* of the Aṅgirases; "Truly, indeed, of him" is the final *vāsiṣṭha*, and the *bṛhat*.

The *vāmadevya* is "vayamenamidā hyaḥ"; the *vāsiṣṭha* is "svāsu pṛśni pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ"; the *gāyatra* is "caurṇāyavaṃ ca" and "tvam hyaṅga daivya somaḥ punāna ūrmiṇā"; the *bṛhatkrośa* is "purojitī vo andhasaḥ"; the *yajñāyajñīya* is "kṣullakakāleyaṃ ca"; the *lauśa* is "pra ta āśvinīḥ pavamāna dhenavaḥ"; and the *viśoviśīya*, the *agniṣṭomasāman*, is on its own verses. 83.

"Of Pavamāna, the all-knowing Soma, the wonderful hymn worthy of praise—when, like eager cows, O thou of lofty mind, thou flowest swiftly; those streams of thine dripping with honey—to thee, O Agni, we meditate upon this hymn. This is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ. His own [verses] follow. "Flow on, O Soma, most resplendent"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *yaṇva*, the *śākala*. "Soma, being pressed by the pressers"—this is the *vāmra*, the *anūpa*, the *triṇidhana* of Agni. "Toward the three-backed one"—with the concluding verse, the *rathantara* and the *vāmadevya* [are chanted]. "This Indra for the host of gods"—"Thou, O Indra... [and so forth].

"Thou art glory"—this is the *yauktasruc*; the two *hiṃkāras* and the *āsāvyam̐śuḥ madāya*; the *gāyatra* and the *gauṣūkta*; "Toward splendor, toward great glory, the breaths, the child of the great ones"—this is the *cyāvana* and the *vārśa*; "Flow for the winning of booty"—this is the *yajñāyajñīya* and the *rayiṣṭha*; "Flow, finding cattle"—this is the *lauśa* with a double *abhyāghāta* at the end; "The men [kindle] Agni"—this is the *bṛhadāgneya*, the *agniṣṭomasāman*. These are the *ukthas* of the third day. 84.

The six-verse hymn beginning with "They have been poured forth, the vigorous ones" (*asṛkṣata pra vājinaḥ*), followed by the triplet "Hitherward those ten fingers [have sent] him, the brown one, truly self-strong" (*etamu tyaṃ daśa kṣipo babhrave nu svatavase*); the *ājya* of the Hotṛ-priest beginning with "O Agni, the strength of that mortal in battles" (*yamagne pṛtsu martyam*); the subsequent verses of Pavamāna beginning with "As he strikes down" (*pavamānasya jighnataḥ*); the *gāyatra* and *adārasṛt* hymns; the *śaukta* hymn beginning with "Pour out the pressed juice on every side" (*parīto ṣiñcatā sutam*); the *yaśas*, *abhīśu*, and *pratoda* hymns; the *sākamukṣa* hymn; the final hymn of Vasiṣṭha which contains the word "here" (*iha*); the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, and the *śrāyantīya* chants.

And the *pṛṣṭha* [stotra], and you, O Soma, are the sustainer—thus the *gāyatra* and the *aśvasūkta*; "He is pressed who [is the lord] of the Vasus; him, O friends, do ye rejoice in"—thus the *dīrgha* and the *kārṇaśravasa*; "The Soma drops flow clear, the Indus"—thus the *krauñca*; "To him the seven milch-cows have yielded milk thrice"—thus the *marutāṃ dhenvantya*, the *yajñāyajñīya* as the *agniṣṭomasāman*. 85.

The Soma drops, which are slayers of enemies, far-reaching and all-seeing, have been let loose like rattling chariots; they have flowed along their path. May the immortal divine Hotṛ bring you skill that is bliss-bestowing. "Come hither, O Indra of wondrous luster," "O Indra and Agni, [come from] the luminous realms of heaven," "O Adhvaryu, [the Soma] pressed with stones"—thus [are the verses]. And the Gāyatra, the Mārgīyava, the Eḍa, the Sauparṇa, the Rohitakūlīya, the Pauruhanmana beginning with "I have rejoiced in thee, O Soma," the Dvaigata, and the Gauṅgava.

The *dviniṣedha* and *āyasya*; "pro kavyam uśanāiva bruvāṇaḥ"—the *vārāha* as the final [verse], the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *vāśa*, and the *vaiyaśva*; "pavasva deva āyuṣak"—the *gāyatra*; the *svāśira*, the *arka*, the *aiḍa*, and the *saindhukṣita*; "eṣa sya dhārayā suto gomanna indra aśvavat"—the *śārkara*; "traite purojitī vo andhasaḥ"—the *krauñca*, the *gautama*, and the *yajñāyajñīya*; "pro ayāsīt"—the *aiḍa*; the *yajñasārathi* as the final; and "ā te agne idhīmahi"—the *sraugmata*, which is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. 86.

Pavamāna has been let loose; driving away the adversaries, he flows on. Flow for the sake of the gods, O Soma; win and conquer! He, the exhilarating one, rushes forward to this feast; flow around with all thy fires, O Agni. When the sun has risen, I invoke the great Indra who is mighty in strength, the two impetuous Vṛtra-slayers. "O Indu, for Indra accompanied by the Maruts"—these are the verses beginning with the fifth of Dārḍhacyuta. "Being cleansed by the skillful hand"—these are the verses beginning with the fifth of Goṣṭha. "Hā u hu vā i śiśum" is the final verse of the Vasiṣṭha family, along with the Bṛhat and the Vāmadevya chants.

The *Traiśoka*, the *Vaikhānasa*, and "Pari svāno giriṣṭhāḥ"—these are the *Gāyatra* and the three *Vaidanvata* hymns; "Tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya pavasva devavītaye"—this is the *Sauparṇa* and the *Vaiśvamanasa*; "Pari tyam haryataṃ hariṃ"—this is the *Ākūpāra* and the *Tvāṣṭrīsāman*; the *Yajñāyajñīya*, the *Yadvāhiṣṭhīya*, and "Dhartā divaḥ"—this is the *Ṛc* of Dīrghatamas; the final [verse] "Agniṃ vo devaṃ agnibhiḥ sajoṣāḥ"—this is the *Rāyovājīya*, the *Agniṣṭomasāman*, the *Saindhukṣita*, the *Traikakubha*, and the *Udvamśīya*. 87.

"Upa ṣu jātam apturam," "Eṣa devaḥ amartyaḥ," "Eṣa dhiyā yāty aṇvyā," "Eṣa kaviḥ abhiṣṭutaḥ"; "Upa tvā raṇvasaṃdṛśam," "Ā no mitrāvaruṇā," "Tam indraṃ vājayāmasi," "Indrāgnī ā gatam sutam," "Uccā te jātam andhasaḥ"—these are the Gāyatra and the Āmahīyava. Also "Jigam" and "Abhīkam. "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā" is the Paurumadga; the Aṣkāraṇidhana and the Kāṇva; the Maidhātitha; the Utsedha and the Auśana as the final; the Rathantara and the Vāmadevya.

The *ca-naipātitha*, the *kāleya*, the *gāyatra* beginning with "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā," the *arka* of Agni, "bhidyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśaḥ," "indramaccha sutā ime," the *aiśira*, the *rohitakūlīya*, the *śyāvāśva* beginning with "abhī no vājasātamam," the *niṣedha*, the *sādhra*, the *yajñāyajñīya*, and the final *kāva* hymn beginning with "imam̐ stomamarhate jātavedase"—these constitute the *samanta-agniṣṭoma-sāman*. (881) The *viśvajit-atirātra* sacrifice.
(882) That which belongs to the *bṛhaspatisava* belongs to Kusurubinda; its first [part] consists of two single-verse hymns (*ekarcas*) concerning his birth. (891)

In the world of the *Hāviṣmat*, there are the *Yauktāśva* and *Svāśira*; for the *Arka*, the *Hāviṣmat*; for *Śaṅku* and *Sujñāna*, the *Satrāsāhīya* and *Śrudhya*; he extracts the *Ukthas*. The rest is the same as on the second day of the *Janakasaptarātra* sacrifice. 892. That which was the former [day] is now the latter. 89 3. "Flow clear, go toward Indra"—this is the *Satrāsāhīya* and *Śrudhya*; "The bull of prayers flows clear"—this is the *Yāma*; the final *Yajñāyajñīya* is the *Agniṣṭoma-sāman*; the *Ukthas* are the *Sākamaśva*, *Saubhara*, and *Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*. The rest is the same as on the second day of the *Trikakubha* sacrifice. 894.

"Eté asṛgram indavaḥ," "rājā medhābhir īyate"—these two triplets are used before the *paryāsa*; for the third day, there are the *januṣ* and *ekarca* verses, as well as the *sapha* and *pauṣkala* chants; the rest is the same as in the *Jyotiṣṭoma*. That which was the former [day] is now the latter.

For the *Tīvrasut*, the *ājya* and *bahiṣpavamāna* chants and the midday pressing are performed; in the place of the *saṃhita* hymn, there is the *agna raka*; the rest is the same as that [day], using the *Rathantara* *pañcadaśa* stoma.

For the second [day], characterized by its own natural *sāman*, the *ājya* and *bahiṣpavamāna* chants are in the *bṛhatī* meter; for the *pavamāna*, "te vayam" is the *paryāsa*. For the *maukṣa* [day], the *arka* hymn is in the *svāśira* meter. The rest is the same as that which belongs to the fifteen-fold *bārhatā* [stoma]. That which was the former becomes the latter; for the *arka* of Agni, the *saṃhita* hymn of Kava Dīrghatamas is used. The *ukthas* end with the *udvaṃśīyā* verses. The *ekaviṃśa* is the *atirātra*; the *ṣoḍaśin* follows the *stomas* of that which is the last among the single *stomas*.

For the first day of the five-day *pṛṣṭhya-avalamba* [period], the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant is like that of the ancient [days]; for the fifth day, the *anurūpa* is "They have pressed" (*asṛkṣata*). The *pratipad* is "Those Soma-draughts which are in the distance" (*ye somāsaḥ parāvati*). The *hotṛ*'s *ājya* is "The one who carries the seasons, Vaiśvānara. In the place of the *Kaṇvarathantara*, the *soma-sāman* is "Proclaiming wisdom like Uśanas. The final [laud] is the *vārāha*. The *ātreyam* is the *svara-sāman*. The *aiḍa* is "He has gone forth" (*pro ayāsīt*). The final [laud] is the *yajñasārathi*. Everything else is the same as on the seventh day of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*).

"Driving forth the hero with the rays," is the opening verse; "O Agni, with all thy fires," is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ; "Verily they urge the infant," is the final [verse] of Vasiṣṭha; "The tone, O, the sustainer," is the final [verse] of Kutsa, belonging to the *aiḍa* and *śārṅga* meters; the rest is the same as on the eighth day of the twelve-day rite. 8103.

The *pratipad* is "upōṣu jātamapturam"; the *ājya* of the Hotṛ is "upa tvā raṇvasaṃdṛśam"; the final [verse] of the Vasiṣṭha family is "hā u hu vā akrān"; the Gaurīvita-locus is "pari tyaṃ haryataṃ harim"; one [verse] is "āsitaṃ dīrghatamasaḥ"; one is "arkaḥ"; one is "ākūpāram"; one is "yatsvayonyasāvi somo aruṣo vṛṣā hariḥ"; the *aiḍa* is "yāmaṃ samānam"—this is the other [portion] by means of the ninth day of the twelve-day rite.

The *antarotsedha* and *niṣedha* [stotras] belong to Medhātithi; the final one belongs to Uśanas, beginning with "jāgṛvir. Among its own verses, the *rathaṃtara* and *vāmadevya* [stotras] are used. The *kāva* [stotra], the final one, is among those containing the word "sūrya," beginning with "pari pra dhanva. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. Everything else is the same as on the tenth day of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*). (8105) The *viśvajit* is an *atirātra*. (8106) It is a *triṣṭoma-agniṣṭoma*. Its *stoma* divisions share in the *savana*s, or they share equally. (8111)

The Jyotirukthya sacrifice has a thousand-fold *bahiṣpavamāna* chant, just as in the first *saṃhita*. In the world of Maukṣa, he extracts the Nārmedha hymn consisting of eighteen verses; the night is the same as that of the second [sacrifice] with a single-stoma. That which was the former is now the latter. The Gaurukthya follows.

The Abhijit is an Agniṣṭoma. For that Abhijit, [the verses] are: "O Soma, purifying yourself with the stream" (punaḥ soma dhārayā), "The Abhīvarta" on three verses, the Raurava on one verse, the Kaṇvarathantara on one verse, the Medhātitha on one verse, and the Yaudhājaya on three verses. If, however, one wishes to perform the Kaṇvarathantara as a triplet, one should transpose the places of the Abhīvarta and the Kaṇvarathantara; or alternatively, the Kaṇvarathantara and the Yaudhājaya may be transposed. The rest is the same. That which was the first [verse] becomes the last. The Viśvajit is an Agniṣṭoma, the Āyus is an Ukthya, and the Viśvajit is an Agniṣṭoma. The Sarvastoma is an Atirātra; these are the arrangements for the one-day sacrifices (ekāhas).

The five-day *pṛṣṭhya-avalamba* [is performed]; the sixth day is the *pṛṣṭhya-stoma*; following the *vaidanvata* days is the milk-offering; the third pressing is the thirty-six-fold (*ṣaṭtriṃśa*) *soktha*; there are three *chandomas*; thus they are combined. Again, the *kaṇvarathantara* [is performed], and he goes to his own world. Of the two fourfold stomas, the first is the *viśvajit-atirātra*, the *viśvajit-atirātra*. Chapter Eight: The Expansion (*vivṛti*).
The *Trikakud-daśarātra* (the ten-night rite with three peaks).

Now, there are four ten-night rites: the *Trivṛt-agniṣṭoma*, the *Pañcadaśa-ukthya*, the *Trivṛt-agniṣṭoma*, the *Saptadaśa-agniṣṭoma*, the *Ekaviṃśa-ukthya*, the *Saptadaśa-agniṣṭoma*, the *Triṇava-agniṣṭoma*, the *Trayastriṃśa-ukthya*, the *Triṇava-agniṣṭoma*, and the *Viśvajit-atirātra*. Thus the *Trikakud-daśarātra* is described by this section of the text (*anuvāka*). Regarding that, the ritual rule (*kalpa*) for the first day is as follows:

"O Agni, you purify our lives"—this is the *anurūpa* [verse]. "Be gracious among us, O Lord of Power"—this is the *abhīvarta* *brahmasāman*. "For the one who presses the soma-juice"—this is the *audala* for the son of Divodāsa. "Toward the dear things"—this is the final *yajñāyajñīya* [sāman]. || 1 ||
"Salutations to you, O Agni, by your vigor"—this is the *jarābodhīya* Agniṣṭoma-sāman, or it may be performed on its own verses.
The rest is the same as the first day of Janaka’s seven-night sacrifice.

"Thus: *Upāsmai gāyatā nara agne āyūṃṣi pavase pavamānasya te kave*—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna. *Agnā ā yāhi vītaye*—these are the Ājyas. *Pra somāso vipaścitaḥ*—this is the Gāyatra; *somasāma*—these are the Sāman-trikas. *Pra soma devavītaye*—the Yaudhājaya on three verses; the Auśana is the last. The Rathantara and Vāmadevya; *śagdhyūṣu śacīpate*—the Abhīvarta; *svāsu kāleyam*—these are the Pṛṣṭhas."

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" [is] the Gāyatra-saṃhita; "ayā pavasva devayuḥ" and "pavate haryato hariḥ" [are] the Sapha and Pauṣkala; "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ" [is] the Audala-Devodāsa; "abhi priyāṇi" [is] the Yajñāyajñīya as the final [stotra]. The final [part] of the Arjama consists of single verses. "namaste agne ojasaḥ" [is] the Jarābodhīya Agniṣṭoma-sāman, or [it may be] in its own [verses]. Its metre is the Gāyatrī. Everything is Trivṛt. 3.
Thus ends the first day. ||1||
The second day:

the ritual procedure for the second day is as follows—the *Yajñāyajñīya* chant, beginning with "The bull of prayers flows pure," is the final one; the *Saubhara* is the *Agniṣṭoma-sāman* performed upon its own verses. ||1||
The rest is the same as the second day of the five-night rite. || 2 ||

"Thus: 'Flow on through speech; flow on, O Soma, as a bull, for you are indeed a bull'—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. 'We choose Agni as the messenger'—these are the *ājya* hymns. 'Flow on, O bull, in your stream'—this is both the *gāyatra* and the *hāviṣmat*. 'Being purified, O Soma, in your stream'—this is the *āyāsya*. 'The red bull'—this is the final *pārtha*. The *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *mādhucchandasa*—these are the *pṛṣṭha* hymns. 'That exhilaration of yours which is most excellent'—this is the *gāyatra* at the *aukṣa*."

"Pavasva indram accha" is for the Śaṅkusujñāna; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayir bhagaḥ" is for the Āsitakrauñca; "vṛṣā matīnām" is the final Yajñāyajñīya. The Śaṅkusujñāna, Āsita, and Krauñca consist of single verses each. The Saubhara is the Agniṣṭoma-chant in its own meters; its metre is the Kakubh. The Auśana, Aupagava, and Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra are the Uktha chants. Everything is fifteenfold. 2.
Thus ends the second day. ||2||
The third day:

for the third day—“With flashing luster,” “These drops have been poured forth,” “Flow for the sake of nourishment, O stream,” and “By means of fire, fire is kindled”—these are the Ājya offerings. || 1 ||
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

"High is the birth of your juice"—on one [verse] is the Gāyatra, on one the Vairūpa, and on one the Saumitra. "O Soma, pressed by the stones"—this is the intermediate [chant] on three verses. "The three voices"—this is the final call of the Aṅgirases. || 2 ||
[Thus ends] the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Naudhasa, and the Raurava. ||3||
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].

"Three voices have arisen"—this is the Gāyatra and the Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha; "O friends, pour out the soma, sit down"—these are the Vācaḥsāman and the Śaukta; "The pressed juices, most rich in honey"—these are the Tvāṣṭrīsāman and the Āndhīgava; "Your filter"—this is the Yajñāyajñīya as the final one. 4.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
All the verses, with the exception of the last one, consist of single stanzas (ekarca). 4.
The Agniṣṭoma-sāman is to be chanted on its own verses.
Its metre is the uṣṇih; everything is threefold. || 5 ||
Thus ends the third day. ||3||
The Fourth Day:

Of the fourth day—Pavamāna has brought forth; purifying himself, he has stepped forth; as King, he moves with sacrificial wisdom. Thee, who bearest manly powers, the rays of light impel like a hero. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"Agni shall strike down the Vṛtras"—this is the *ājya* [verse] for the Hotṛ; his own [verses] follow thereafter.
"O Mitra and Varuṇa, this Indra [has acted] with the bones of Dadhyañc; this [is the song] of your thought"—these are the *ājya* verses. 2.

Flow on, you who accomplish skill! [Recite] the Gāyatra and the Tvaṣṭrīsāman. [Recite] "When they move about" (yadīṅkhantīḥ), and for the Soma verses, "The Āyus" (somāsa āyavaḥ). [Recite] the Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra, the Ārthavaṇa, the Ābhīśava, and the Svaḥpṛṣṭha of the Aṅgirases. The final [verse] is the Uhuvā of Vasiṣṭha. //3//
[Thus concludes the midday Pavamāna.
One should place the *aṣṭādaṃṣṭra* on the first [stotra], and the *svaḥpṛṣṭha āṅgirasa* on the middle one. 3.
The *Bṛhat* and the *Vāmadevya*, and "We have kindled this [fire]"—this is the *Vāsiṣṭha*; on its own verses, the *Pṛśni*. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].

"pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ" is the Gāyatra and the Caurṇāyava; "tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya somaḥ punāna ūrmiṇā" is the Bṛhatkakrauśa; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Yajñāyajñīya and the Kṣullakakāleya; and "pra ta āśvinīḥ" is the final Lauśa. || 5 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
In the Bṛhat-kakubha [stoma], there are two single-verse [hymns]. 5.
The *viśoviśīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* on its own verses.
Its metre is Anuṣṭubh; everything is seventeenfold. 6.
Thus ends the fourth day. 4.

The fifth day of the fifth day—the Pavamāna hymn for the All-knowing Soma: "That which is bright and worthy of praise, when, like eager cows, O thou of lofty mind, thou flowest swiftly; those streams of thine that drip with honey. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

"O Agni, we meditate upon the hymn"—this is the *ājya* (offering verse) for the Hotṛ; his own [verses] follow. "Truly, even through the wide [space]," "Arising with vigor," and "O Indra and Agni, these two of you"—these are the *ājya* verses.

"Flow on, O Soma, most brilliant!"—this is the Gāyatra, Yaṇva, and Śākala. "Soma, being pressed by the pressers"—this is the Vāmra, Ānūpa, and Agni’s Triṇidhana. "Toward the three-backed one"—with this they conclude.
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, "Indram id devatātaye," "Tvam indra yaśā asi," the *yuktasruc*, and the double *hiṃkāra*. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"asāvyaṃśurmadāya" is the *gāyatra* and the *goṣūkta*; "abhidyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśaḥ prāṇā śiśurmahīnām" is the *cyāvana-vārṣa*. "pavasva vājasātaye" is the *yajñāyajñīya* and the *rayiṣṭha*; "govitpavasva" is the *lauśa*, which is the final *dvyabhyāghāta*. || 5 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
"Agniṃ naraḥ" is the Bṛhat Āgneya Agniṣṭoma Sāman. Its metre is Virāj.
The Ukthas of the third day.
The *pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *tairaścya* are the *ukthas*; everything is the twenty-one-fold chant (*ekaviṃśa*).
Thus ends the fifth day. || 5 ||
The sixth day of the sixth day:

"They have been let loose, the prize-winners," "This very one, the ten fingers [have pressed]," and "For the brown one, indeed, for the self-strong"—these three verses from the six-verse hymn; "Your vital powers rise up," and "These Soma juices have been let loose. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, the mortal whom you [protect] in battles"—this is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ; his own [verses] follow.
At the rising of the sun, overcome all those who are hostile to you; for you two are the officiating priests of the sacrifice—thus [are] the *ājya* offerings. 2.
"Pavamānasya jighnataḥ" is the Gāyatra, consisting of the Ādārasṛt; "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam" is the Śaukta, consisting of Yaśas, Abhīśu, and Pratoda; and "sākamukṣa" is the final Ihavat of Vasiṣṭha.
[Thus ends the Mādhyamdina Pavamāna.
The Śaukta hymn is for the first [stotra], and the Pratoda for the second. 3.
And the Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śrayantīya, and the Pṛṣṭha. ||4||
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"Thou, O Soma, art the sustainer"—this is the Gāyatra and the Aśvasūkta. "He is pressed for the sake of the Vasus; him, O friends, do ye rejoice in"—this is the Dīrgha and the Kārṇaśravasa. "The Soma drops, the Indus, flow clear"—this is the Krauñca. "For him, thrice seven milch-cows have yielded milk"—this is the Marutāṃ Dhenu, which is the final [section]. || 5 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
For Dīrghatamas Kārṣṇaśravasa, there is one verse. 5.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. 6.
Everything is seventeenfold. ||6||
Thus ends the sixth day. || 6 ||
The seventh day of the seventh day:
"Those Somas which are in the distance, the slayers of enemies, the far-seeing; the drops have been poured forth like chariots on their path—[bring] thy skill that brings bliss. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

Of the six-verse hymn beginning with *babhrave nu svatavase*, the first triplet is employed on the preceding day; the last verse, *amitrahā vicarṣaṇiḥ*, is employed on the following day. Thus says the *Nidāna*: "The six-verse hymn beginning with *babhrave nu svatavase* is distributed across the sixth and seventh days for the sake of continuity," and so forth.
The immortal god, the Hotṛ, has been invoked for you; sing forth to Mitra and to Indra. O Indra of brilliant luster, come hither! Indra and Agni, [you who dwell in] the luminous realms of heaven. 2.
Thus end the offerings of clarified butter.

"O Adhvaryu, [the Soma] pressed with stones"—this consists of the Gāyatra, the Mārgīyava, the Aiḍa, the Sauparṇa, and the Rohitakūlīya. "For thee, O Soma, I have rejoiced"—this consists of the Pauruhanmana, the Dvaigata, the Gauṅgava, and the Dvinidhana-Āyāsya. "Proclaiming wisdom like Uśanas"—this is the Vārāha, which is the final [hymn]. (3)
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Vāśa, and the Vaiyaśva. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"Pavasva deva āyuṣak" is the Gāyatra; "svāśirāmarkaḥ" is the Aiḍa; "saindhukṣita" is the Śārkararava; "eṣa sya dhārayā suto gomanna indra aśvavat" is the Krauñca; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Gautama; "yajñāyajñīya" is the Yajñasārathi; "pro ayāsīt" is the final Aiḍa. (5)
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna. "O Agni, we kindle thee" (ā te agne idhīmahi) is the Sraugmata Agniṣṭoma-sāman. Its metre is Paṅkti; everything is the Triṇava stoma.
Thus ends the seventh day. ||7||
The Eighth Day: Of the eighth day— The purifying ones have been let loose;

driving away the adversaries, he flows pure. Flow for the sake of the gods and heroes; O God, win both ancient wealth and victory. Crossing over, the exhilarating one runs; flow around us with this food-offering. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
O Agni, with all your fires, as the sun rises today, I invoke the great Indra and the two Vṛtra-slayers, the bounteous ones, who are mighty in their power. 2.
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.
"O Indu, for Indra accompanied by the Maruts"—these are the verses beginning with the fifth [verse] of Dārḍhacyuta.
The *gāyatram*, the *iṣovṛdhīyam*, the *krauñcam*, the *vājadāvarya*, and the *dārḍhacyutam*;
"mṛjyamānaḥ suhastya" and the five [verses] beginning with "goṣṭha"; the *aukṣṇorandhra*, the *vājajit*, the *varuṇasāman*, and the *goṣṭha*.
"Hā u hvāyi śiśum" is the final [hymn] belonging to Vasiṣṭha. ||3||
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
And the Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Traiśoka, and the Vaikhānasa. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭhas*.

"Pari svāno giriṣṭhā"—this is the Gāyatra; the three Vaidanvatas; "Tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya pavasva devavītaye"—the Sauparṇa and the Vaiśvamanasa; "Pari tyaṃ haryataṃ harim"—the Ākūpāra, the Tvāṣṭrīsāman, the Yajñāyajñīya, and the Yadvāhiṣṭhīya; and finally, the hymn of Dīrghatamas beginning with "Dhartā divaḥ. || 5 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
"Agni, the god, with the Agnis, in harmony" (RV 8.43.14)—this is the Rāyovājīya, the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.
The Saindhukṣita, the Traikakubha, and the Udvaṃśīya. ||7||
Thus end the hymns.
The entire [chapter] on the Thirty-three [Devas]. || 7 ||
Thus ends the eighth day. || 8 ||
The Ninth Day:
Of the ninth day— "Born near the waters, the swift one; this immortal god; he goes with subtle wisdom; this seer is praised. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
We approach you, whose appearance is delightful; O Mitra and Varuṇa, we impel Indra for us. O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed juice! 2.
Thus end the clarified butter offerings.

"High is the birth of your juice"—the Gāyatra, the Cāmahīyava, the Ājiga, and the Abhīka; "being purified, O Soma, in your stream"—the Paurumadga, the Cākṣāraṇidhana, the Kāṇva, the Maidhātitha, the Utsedha, and the Auśana as the last. ||3||
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna:
the Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Naipātitha, and the Kāleya. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā," the Gāyatra, and the Ārka of Agni; "abhi dyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśaḥ," "indram acchā sutā ime," the Aiṣira, and the Rohitakūlīya; "abhī no vājasātamam," the Śyāvāśva, the Niṣedha, the Sādhra, the Yajñāyajñīya, and the Kāva as the final [hymn]. 5.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
"This hymn for the worthy Jātavedas"—this is the Samantam Agniṣṭoma Sāman. 6.
Its metre is Jagatī; everything is the Triṇava. 6.
Thus ends the ninth day. ||6||
The tenth day:
regarding the tenth day, he says—the Viśvajit Atirātra. ||1||
Thus [ends the first section]. ||1||
Thus ends the tenth day. 10.
Thus ends the Trikakud Daśarātra.

The *Kusurubinda-daśarātra* is described by the following *anuvāka*: "The first day consists of three *trivṛt* *agniṣṭomas*; three *pañcadaśa* *ukthyas*; three *saptadaśa* *ukthyas*; and an *ekaviṃśa atirātra*. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows: "That which belongs to the *Bṛhaspatisava* is the first [day] of the *Kusurubinda*. For that [first day], there are two verses concerning its birth (*januṣa*). The *bahiṣpavamāna* chant is "upa drava piba" (etc.). The *ājya* stotras are "agna ā yāhi", "no mitrāya", and "indrāgnī". The *sāman*-verses are "uccā te", "gāyatram", "cāmahīyavam", and "jarābodhīyam".

"Purifying, O Soma, in your stream" (*punaḥ soma dhārayā*)—these three [verses] are the *tiyudhājaya*. The last is the *auśana*. The *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] consist of the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *naudhasa*, and the *kāleya*. "With the sweetest [hymn]" (*svādiṣṭhayā*) is the *gāyatrasaṃhita*. "Flow on, seeking the gods" (*ayā pavasva devayuḥ*) and "The lovely, tawny one flows" (*pavate haryato hariḥ*) are the *sapha* and *pauṣkala*. "For your sake, with the conquest of the soma-juice" (*purojitī vo andhasaḥ*) is the *śyāvāśva* and *āndhīgava*. The last is the *kāva*. With the exception of the last, these are single-verse [stotras]. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. Everything is in the *trivṛt* [stoma].
Thus ends the first day. || 11 ||
The second day:

He speaks of the second day—[the hymn] of Hāviṣmanta in the world, [the hymn] of Svaśira for Marka, the Hāviṣmata [hymn] of Śaṅku and Sujñāna, and the Satrāsāhīya and Śrudhya; he extracts the Ukthas. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as the second day of the Janaka-saptarātra sacrifice.
"Thus: 'Flow on, flow on through speech; flow on, O Indu! We [are yours], O Pavamāna'—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna."

The *ājya* stotras are: "We choose Agni as the messenger" (*agnim dūtam vṛṇīmahe*). The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are: the *gāyatra* and the *hāviṣmat*, with the verses "Flow on, O bull, in your stream" (*vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā*) and "O Soma, being purified, flow in your stream" (*punānaḥ soma dhārayā*); the *āyāsya*; and the final *pārtha* with the verse "The red bull" (*vṛṣā śoṇaḥ*). Also, the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *mādhucchandasa*. The *gāyatra* for the *aukṣa* is "That exhilaration of yours which is most excellent" (*yaste mado vareṇyaḥ*); the *satrāsāhīya* and *śrudhya* are "Flow toward Indra" (*pavasvendramaccha*). The *āsita* and the *krauñca* are "This Pūṣan, this wealth, this Bhaga" (*ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ*).
The final *yāma* is "vṛṣāmatīnām"; the *agniṣṭomasāman* is the *yajñāyajñīya*; everything is *trivṛt*.
Thus ends the second day. 12.
The third day:
he speaks of the third day—“that which was the former is the latter. ||1||
The meaning is that the arrangement which belongs to the first day is the very same as that of the third day. ||1||
Thus ends the third day. 13.

Regarding the fourth day, he says: "Flow on, go toward Indra"—this is the *Satrāsāhīya* for the sake of hearing. "The bull of prayers flows on"—this is the final *yāma*. The *Yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *Sākamaśva*, the *Saubhara*, and the *Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* are the *ukthas*. 1.
The rest is the same as on the second day; [this applies] to the Trikakubh [stomas]. || 2 ||

Thus: "Flow forth with speech; flow forth, O Indu, as a bull; O Soma, for you are a bull"—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "Agni, the messenger"—these are the *ājya* hymns. "Flow forth as a bull"—this is both the *gāyatra* and the *hāviṣmat*. "Being purified, O Soma, in your stream"—this is the *āyāsya*. "The red bull"—this is the final *pārtha*. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *mādhucchandasa*. "That exhilaration of yours which is most excellent"—this is the *gāyatra* at the *aukṣa* [stotra].

"Pavasva indram accha" (Pavamāna, flow toward Indra) is for the *Satrāsāhīya* and the *Śrudhya*, each consisting of a single verse. "Ayaṃ pūṣā rayir bhagaḥ" (This is Pūṣan, wealth, Bhaga) is for one [verse]. The *krauñca* melody is for three [verses]. "Vṛṣā matīnām" (The bull of prayers) is the final *yāma*. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *sākamaśva*, *saubhara*, and *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* are the *uktha* chants. Everything is fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*).
Thus ends the fourth day. 14.

The fifth day: regarding the fifth day—it says, "These drops have been poured forth; the King goes with the insights," [this is] for the triplet preceding the *paryāsa*. For the two single-verse hymns, there are the *sapha* and *pauṣkala* chants. These are the *ukthas* of the third day.
The rest is the same as the Jyotiṣṭoma. ||2||

Thus: "Upāsmai āyudhatyā rucā," "ete asṛgram indavaḥ," "rājā medhābhir īyate," and "pavamānasya te kave"—these are for the *bahispavamāna*. "Agnā ā yāhi vītaye" and so forth are the *ājya* hymns. "Uccā te gāyatram" and "cāmahīyavam" [are the stotras]; "punānaḥ soma dhārayā" [is the *stotra*] for the *raurava* and *yaudhājaya*. The *auśana* is the final one. "Rathantaram ca," "vāmadevyam ca," "naudhasam ca," and "kāleyam ca" are the *pṛṣṭha* stotras. "Svādiṣṭhayā" [is the *stotra*] for the *gāyatrasaṃhita*.

"Flow with this [hymn], seeking the gods"—this is for the *sapha* and *pauṣkala* chants. "With the conquest of your soma-juice"—this is for the *śyāvāśva* and *āndhīgava* chants; the last [verse] belongs to the *kāva* chant. The *sapha*, *pauṣkala*, and *śyāvāśva* chants are used in single-verse strophes (*ekarcas*). The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *pramahiṣṭhīya*, *hārivarṇa*, and *tairaśca* are the *uktha* chants. Everything is fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*).
Thus ends the fifth day. 15.
The sixth day:
the arrangement of the fourth day is extended to the sixth—whatever was the former [day], that is the latter. 1.
Thus ends the sixth day. 16.

Regarding the seventh day, he says: "The seventh day"—the *ājya* and *bahiṣpavamāna* chants are in the *tīvrasuta* meter, and the *mādhyaṃdina* [stotra] is likewise; the *arka* belongs to Agni in the world of the *saṃhita*. ||1||
The rest is the same as that of this very [rite] with the Rathantara [Sāman] and the Pañcadaśa [Stoma].
Thus: "Sing forth to him, O men, with a flashing luster; these drops have been poured out; thee, who art bearing manly powers, O Sage, while thou art being purified"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna.

The *ājya* [stotras] are: "agna ā yāhi," "mitrāvaruṇā," and "indrāgnī. The *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* are performed with the verse "uccā te jātam andhasaḥ. The *dvihiṃkāra*, *maidhātitha*, *raurava*, *yaudhājaya*, and finally the *auśana* are performed with the verse "abhi somāsa āyavaḥ"; there is a *dvihiṃkāra* on the first [verse], and the *yaudhājaya* on the middle [verse]. The *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] are: the *rathantara*, *vāmadevya*, *naudhasa*, and *kāleya*. The *gāyatra* and the *arka* of Agni are performed with the verse "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā."

"Pavasva indram accha" and "iti sapha pauṣkala" are the two single-verse [stotras]. "Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Śyāvāśva and Āndhīgava. The final [stotra] belongs to Kava. The Agniṣṭoma-sāman is the Yajñāyajñīya. The Ukthas are the Pramahiṣṭhīya, the Svāra, the Hārivarṇa, and the Tairaśca. Everything is seventeenfold.
Thus ends the seventh day. || 17 ||
The eighth day:

regarding the eighth day—it is said that for the second *svarasāman*, the *ājya* and *bahiṣpavamāna* chants are in the *bṛhatī* meter; the *paryāsa* of the *pavamāna* is "pavamānasya te vayam"; and in the world of the *maukṣa* [sāman], there is the *svāśira* *arka*.
The rest is the same as that of this very [chant] with the fifteenfold Bṛhatī. ||2||

Thus: "Flow on with speech; flow on, O Soma, thou art a bull, radiant. "Thy powers rise up, we [sing] of thee, the purifying one"—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "Agni, the messenger"—these are the *ājya* hymns. "Flow on as a bull, in thy stream"—this is both the *gāyatra* and the *hāviṣmat*. "Pour out the pressed juice on every side"—this is the *samanta*, the *dairghaśravasa*, and the *āyāsya*. "The red bull"—this is the final *pārtha*. There are two single-verse hymns in the *kakubh* and *uṣṇih* meters. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *sākamaśva*, *saubhara*, and *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* are the *uktha* chants. Everything is in the seventeen-fold (*saptadaśa*) stoma.
Thus ends the eighth day. ||18||
Regarding the ninth day, he says: "The arrangement of the seventh day is the same as that of the ninth; that which is prior is [identical to] that which is subsequent. (1)
Thus it is said. Regarding this, he states the specific detail:
"In the world of that Agni-Arka, the *saṃhita* belongs to Kava Dīrghatamas; the *ukthas* end with the *udvaṃśīya*. (2)

The *svādiṣṭhayā* [verse] and the *gāyatra-saṃhitā*; the *pavasva indram accha* [verse] and the *sapha-pauṣkala*, which consist of single verses; the *purojitī vo andhasaḥ* [verse] and the *śyāvāśva-andhīgava*; and among the *kāva-ṛks*, the final *arka* of Dīrghatamas—these constitute the Ārbhava [Śastra]. The *pramahiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *tairaśca* are the Ukthas. The rest is the same as on the seventh day.
Thus ends the ninth day. 16.
Regarding the tenth day, he says:
"The tenth day is an Atirātra with the twenty-one-fold [stoma]. It follows the stomas of that which is the highest among the single-stoma rites.
The Sixteenth [Chapter]. || 1 ||
Thus [it is said]. Herein is the underlying cause: that the *ṣoḍaśī* is connected to its *stoma*, while the *ekaviṃśa* is not subject to such deliberation. ||1||
Thus ends the tenth day. || 20 ||
Thus ends the Kusurubinda Daśarātra.
The ten-night sacrifice (*daśarātra*) consisting of the *chandomas*— namely, the days from the first to the fifth,
followed by the five-day period (*pañcāha*), the four *chandomas*, and the *viśvajit* *atirātra*— is described in this liturgical section (*anuvāka*). This is its ritual procedure (*kalpa*).
The Pṛṣṭhya [Saṃsthā] lasts for five days. For the first day, the Bahiṣpavamāna is "like the ancient" (pratnavat).
For the fifth day, there is also an Anurūpa for the verse beginning with "asṛkṣata."

Thus it is said. Here, because the *chandomas* have been substituted by the *viśvajit*, there is an omission of the sixth day; consequently, although there is no connection with the nine-day period (*navāha*), since the tenth day still exists, the *anurūpa* verse belonging to the sixth day is prescribed in the fifth [day] for the sake of the tenth day, specifically for the purpose of enjoining the nine-verse hymn of *pratnavat*. For it has been stated: "The *bahiṣpavamāna* of the tenth day; the *anurūpas* of the five days beginning with the second; and the *bahiṣpavamāna* from the first; that consists of nine verses," and so forth.

For this first day, the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant is "Asya pratnām" (1.46). The *ājya* stotras are "Agnā ā naḥ," "Mitrāya," and "Indrāgnī. The *gāyatra* is "Pra somāso vipaścitaḥ"; the triplet for the *āśva* *sāman* is "Somasāma. The *yaudhājaya* is "Pra soma devavītaye" performed on three verses; the final one is the *auśana*. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *naudhasa*, and the *kāleya*. The *saṃhitā* is the *gāyatra* "Svādiṣṭhayā."

"Flow with this [hymn], O seeker of the gods"—thus flows the beloved, golden-hued one, with the *saphākṣāra* verses. "Forward for the one who presses the soma-juice"—this belongs to Audala Gautama; the last [verse] is in the *kāva* meter. The *saphākṣāra* and *audala* verses consist of single stanzas each. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. There are two *trivṛt* libations; one is *pañcadaśa*.

For the second day: "Flow for speech, flow for the voice, O Indu, for you are a bull"—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "I invoke Agni the messenger, Mitra; Indra indeed with songs; Indra and Agni"—these are the *ājya* hymns. "Flow as a bull in your stream"—this is both the *gāyatram* and the *yauktāśvam*. "O Soma, being purified, in your stream"—this is the *āyāsyam*. "The red bull"—this is the final *ihavat-vāsiṣṭham*. And the *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevyam*, the *śyaitam*, and the *mādhucchandasam*.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this consists of the *gāyatram* and the *hāviṣmatam*. "pavasvendramaccha"—in these two single verses, there is the *śaṅku* at *sujñāna*. "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"—this consists of the *āsita* and the *krauñca*. "vṛṣā matīnām"—this is the final *yāma*. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *sākamaśva*, *āmahīyava*, and *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* are the *ukthas*. There are two *pañcadaśa* chants at the pressing; one is *saptadaśa*.

For the third day: *davidyutatyā rucā*, *ete asṛgram indavaḥ*, *rājā medhābhir īyate*, *taṃ tvā nṛmṇāni bibhratam iṣe pavasva dhārā*—these are for the Bahiṣpavamāna. *agnināgniṃ huve*, *indreṇa gnā huve*—these are the Ājya hymns. *uccā te jātam andhasaḥ* is the Gāyatra and the Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha. *abhi somāsa āyavaḥ* is the Paurumadga for the first [Ājya]. The two triplets of the Gautama and Antarikṣa [Sāmans] are used; the Āṣkāraṇidhana is for the middle Ājya.

"Tisro vācaḥ" is the final *saṃkrośa* of the Aṅgirases. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the Rathantara, Vāmadevya, Mahāvaiṣṭambha, and Raurava. "Tisro vāca udīrata" consists of the Gāyatra and Pāṣṭhauha. "Ā sotā pari ṣiñcata sakhāya ā niṣīdata" consists of the Vācaḥsāman and Śaukta. "Sutāso madhumattamā" consists of the two Tvaṣṭrī-sāmans, the Svāra, and the Atriṇidhana; "Pavitraṃ te" is the final Ariṣṭa. The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.
The *pramam̐hiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *tairaśca* are the *uktha* chants; there are two *saptadaśa* stomas at the pressing, and one *ekaviṃśa*.

The *pavamāna* of the fourth day: "He who purifies has been born; being purified, he has stepped forth toward the offering like eager cows. Flow on, O one of lofty thought; the dawns impel the sun. This is the *bahis-pavamāna*. "May Agni strike down the Vṛtras; this Indra [has come] with the bones of Dadhyañc; this [is the song] for you two, Mitra and Varuṇa, from my mind. These are the *ājya* hymns. "Flow on, accomplishing skill"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *ātharvaṇa*, and the *nidhanakāma* chant.

"O Soma, I have rejoiced in thee"—this is the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* [stotra] with the *ābhīśava* chant, having *svaḥpṛṣṭha* as its back-chant, belonging to the lineage of Aṅgiras. "Soma flows, the progenitor of hymns"—this is the final *janitra*. The *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *traiśoka*, and the *pṛśni* are the *pṛṣṭha* chants. "The sage of heaven, beloved on all sides"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *aurṇāyava*. The *bṛhat* and the *bhāradvāja* [are also included]. "For thou indeed, O divine Soma"—[and] "Purifying thyself, O wave-like one"—these belong to the *vṛhat-kātīṣādīya*.

"Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" includes the Nānada, the Āndhīgava, and the Śuddhāśuddhīya; "pra ta āśvinīḥ" is the Lauśa as the final [stotra]. The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. The Saindhukṣita, the Saubhara, and "vasiṣṭhasya priyam" are the Ukthas. There is an extraction for the Ṣoḍaśin; there are two Ekaviṃśa stotras at the pressing, and one Triṇava.

For the *pavamāna* of the fifth day: "The all-knowing ones have been let loose; the prize-winning Soma juices have flowed forth; the sage has gone forth for the feast of the gods. With the words "Each grain by our means, those streams of yours dripping with honey," they perform the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "The hymn we meditate upon, O Agni, for you are indeed far-reaching"—with these words, and "Arising with power," and "O Indra and Agni, you two," are the *ājya* hymns. "Flow on, O Soma, most brilliant!"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *yāṇva*, the *śākala*, and the *vārśa* hymns.

"Soma, having been pressed by the pressers"—this is the *triṇidhana* for Agni, comprising the Mānava, the Ānūpa, and the Vāmra. "Indu, the steed"—this is the final *sampātya*. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Bārhadgira, and the Rāyovājīya. "This Soma-stalk, the exhilarating one"—these are the Gāyatra, the Saṃtani, the Aiḍa, the Saindhukṣita, and the Gauṣūkta. "Abhidyumna, Bṛhat, Yaśas, Prāṇās, Śiśur mahīnām"—these are the Cyāvana and Krośa.

The sixth day; then follow the four Chandomas. In the ten-night rite (*daśarātra*), there are four days beginning with the seventh; these are here the sixth and subsequent days. Regarding the first of these, he states the arrangement for the *samūḍha* (combined) form: "Those Somas in the far distance" (*ye somāsaḥ parāvati*) is the opening verse (*pratipad*). "In the cosmic order, the Vaiśvānara" (*ṛtāvānaṃ vaiśvānaram*) is the *ājya* chant of the Hotṛ. In the place of the Kaṇvarathantara, the *somasāman* is "Proclaiming wisdom like Uśanas" (*pra kāvyamuśaneva bruvāṇaḥ*); the Vārāha is the final [stotra]. The Svara is the Ātreya. "He has gone forth" (*pro ayāsīt*) is the Aiḍa; "O charioteer of the sacrifice" (*yajñasārathi*) is the final [stotra]. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as the seventh day of the twelve-day rite.

Thus: "The Soma-drops which, like chariots, have been let loose on their course from afar, resounding—O Indu, [bring] to thee skill that is bliss-bestowing. This is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. [Then follow]: "To the one who upholds the *ṛta*, Vaiśvānara"; "Sing forth to Mitra and Indra"; "Come hither, O you of radiant luster"; "Praise him who is the flame"; "The offerings of clarified butter"; "Flow on as a bull in your stream"—these are the *gāyatra*, the *santani*, the *svāra*, the *sauparṇa*, and the *rohitakūlīya*.

The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are: the *soma-sāman* "punānaḥ soma dhārayā" and the two-fold finale (*dvinidhana*) *gauṅgava* and *āyāsya*; the *vārāha* with the final verse "pra kāvyamuśaneva bruvāṇaḥ"; and the *kāṇva* and *vaikhānasa*, both having the *abhinidhana* finale. The *sāman*-verses are: the *gāyatra* "yaste mado vareṇyaḥ," the *maukṣa*, the *adhyardheḍa*, and the *soma-sāman*. The *arka* of Agni is on three verses. The *śārka* and *plava* are "eṣa sya dhārayā sutaḥ" and "sakhāya ā niṣīdata."

"Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" belongs to Atri and Kṛtayaja; "pra vājyakṣāḥ" belongs to Suhuviṣa; "pro ayāsīt" belongs to Iḍa, the son of Yajñasārathi. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. The *ukthas* are "vātsaṃ," "sauśravasaṃ," and "vīṅkaṃ. The entire twenty-four-fold [stoma] is used. Thus ends the sixth day.
Now he describes the arrangement of the combined [stomas] for the second *chandoma*, the seventh day.

“Hinvanti sūram usrāḥ” is the opening verse; “viśvebhir agner agnibhiḥ” is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ; “uhuvāi śiśum” is the final [verse] for Vasiṣṭha. (1) The *svāra* [melody] belongs to Kautsa; “hāu dharte” is the final [verse] for Aiḍa Śārṅga. (2)
The rest is the same as the eighth day of the twelve-day rite.

Thus: "The rays impel the Sun; these Soma-drops flow toward the beloved [Soma]. "The Soma, being purified, flows on. "The Soma-drops, the Indus, have been released. "Your vital strengths rise up. "He has flowed through; flow around. "Driving away the adversaries, he purifies himself. "Flow with this stream!"—these are for the *barhiṣpavamāna*. "O Agni, with all fires, we invoke Mitra. "We incite that Indra for strength. "To Indra and Agni be great homage"—these are the *ājya* verses.

"O Adhvaryu, [the Soma] pressed with stones"—this includes the Gāyatra, the Vairūpa, the Āśubhārgava, the Mārgīyava, the Saumitra, the Aiṭata, the Sākamaśva, and the Vilambasauparṇa. "The Soma-drops, the active ones..."—this includes the Dvihiṅkāra, the Vāmadevya, the Gāyatrapārśva, the Pauruhanmana, the Dvaigata, the Hārāyaṇa, the Acchidra, and the Bārhaduktha. "Hāi uhu vāi śiśum"—this is the final Vāsiṣṭha. There is a double *hiṅ* at the beginning.

In the Bārhaduktha-adhyāsyā, the *pṛṣṭha* chants are the Rathantara, Vāmadevya, Naipātitha, and Vaiyaśva. The Gāyatra chants are "Pavasva deva āyuṣak," the Svāśira, the Marka, the Surūpa, the Bhāsa, the Kākṣīvata, and the Āsita. The Aiṣira chants are "Abhidyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśaḥ," "Prāṇāḥ," "Śiśuḥ," and "Mahīnām. The Svara chants are "Abhī no vājasātamam," the Kautsa, and the Aiḍa—or the Kautsa.

The *Śuddhāśuddhīya*, the *Krauñca*, the *Rayiṣṭha*, and the *Audala*; "Pavasva soma mahān samudra" is the *Dharma* [stotra]. "Hāu dharta" is the final *Aiḍa* and *Śārṅga*. These are the *Aiṣira* and *Atra* as single-verse hymns (*ekarca*). The *Yajñāyajñīya* is the *Agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *Gāyatruśana*, *Sāṃvarta*, and *Māruta* are the *Uktha* [sāmans]. Everything is in the forty-four-fold (*catuścatvāriṃśa*) stoma. In that regard, the two applications of the *Samīṣantī* have been stated.
Thus ends the seventh day. || 23 ||

Regarding the eighth day of the third Chandoma, he describes the arrangement of the *samūḍha* (combined) form: The opening verse (*pratipad*) is "Born near the waters, the swift one" (*upoṣu jātam apturam*). The *ājya* of the Hotṛ is "Near you, who are beautiful to behold" (*upa tvā raṇvasaṃdṛśam*). The final hymn of the Vasiṣṭhas is "Hau hu vā akrān. In the section belonging to Gaurīviti, there is one verse: "Around him, the desirable, the golden-hued" (*pari tyaṃ haryataṃ harim*). There is one verse of Dīrghatamas’s *arka*: "To the limit of the earth" (*ākūpāram*). And one verse beginning with "That which is his own source" (*yat svayonim*). The *aiḍa-yāma* hymn is "Soma has been pressed, the ruddy, the bull, the golden-hued" (*asāvi somo aruṣo vṛṣā hariḥ*). || 1 ||
The rest is the same as the ninth day of the twelve-day rite.

Thus: "Near him who was born, the swift one; this immortal god, he who is to be approached with prayer through the paths; he indeed is that bull, the chariot; he is the steed urged on by men; he is the seer praised aloud; he, the bull, has been pressed for drinking. "O Seer, of you, the purifying one..."—this is the *Bahiṣpavamāna*. "I invoke you, whose seat is delightful, as a friend of purified will; great is Indra who [rules] by his might; I invoke those two by whom this..."—these are the *Ājya* offerings.

"Pavamānasya jighnataḥ" is the Gāyatra; the Ādārasṛt, Surūpa, Hariśrīnidhana, Saindhukṣita, Bābhrava, and the Saṃkṣāra of the Iḍās, as well as the Pavamāna-Ṛṣabha. "Parīto siñcatā sutam" is the Pṛṣṭha on three verses; the Kaulmalabarhiṣa, Arkapuṣpa, and Dairghaśravasa are the Sāman-trikas. The Devasthāna is on three verses; the Saṃkṛti is on a triplet; the Vaiyaśva is on one verse; the Bharga is on three verses; the Ābhīśava is on one verse; and the Yaśas is on three verses.

In the Vāsiṣṭha-madhyāsyā: *hāu uhu vā akrān* is the final [verse] of the Vāsiṣṭha. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śrāyantīya, and the Samanta. The Gāyatra, the Aśvasūkta, the Śāmmada, the Dāvasunidhana, the Pratīcīneḍa, the Kāśīta, the Hāviṣkṛta, and the Sauparṇa and Vaiśvamanasa [are recited] with the verse: *tvaṃ soma asi dhārayus* and *tvaṃ hy aṅga daivya pavasva devavītaye*.

The *paritya*, the *haryata*, the *hari*, the *icī*, the *asitottara*, the *arka* of Dīrghatamas, the *svayoni*, and the *ākūpāra*—these are the *sāman*s for the triplet of verses. The *nihava* is performed upon three verses. The *yadvāhiṣṭhīya*, the *asita*, the *sādhraka*, and the *ākūpāra* [are also included]. "Flow, O Soma, for great skill" (*pavasva soma mahe dakṣāya*) is the *vidharma*. "Soma has been pressed, the ruddy, the bull, the tawny one" (*asāvi somo aruṣo vṛṣā hariḥ*) is the final *aiḍa-yāma*. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *aidhmavāha*, the *traikakubha*, and the *udvaṃśīya* are the *uktha*s. All [of these] consist of forty-eight verses. 2.
Thus ends the eighth day. || 24 ||

He states the arrangement for the ninth day of the fourth Chandoma: the *maidhātitha* [stotra] has the *antarotsedha-niṣedha* [metres]; the final [stotra] is the *auśana* beginning with "ā jāgṛviḥ"; the *rathantara* and *vāmadevya* [sāmans] are on their own [verses]; the *vājajit* [stotra] begins with "pari pra dhanva"; the final [stotra] is the *kāva* on verses containing the word "sūrya. (1) The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. (2) The rest is the same as the tenth day of the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*). (3) Thus.

The vigorous ones have been let loose; Pavamāna, the all-conquering, has brought them forth. These drops have been let loose; flow, O pressed bull! "His ancient [hymns], nine new [verses]"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna.

The *ājya* stotras are: "O well-kindled one, bring [the gods] hither; whatever today at the rising of the sun... and "May the Soma-drops moisten you; O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed juice. The *gāyatra* chants are: "High is the birth of your plant," the *cāmahīyava*, the *ājiga*, and the *abhīka*. The *utsedha* is "O Soma, being purified, flow in a stream," the *maidhātitha*, and the *niṣedha*; the final one is the *auśana* chant beginning with "The watchful one. Then follow the *rathantara* and the *vāmadevya*. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are: "Up those most honey-sweet ones," the *abhīvarta*, and the *kāleya* among its own verses.

"svādiṣṭhayā" [is used] for the Gāyatra-saṃhitā; "pavasvendram accha" for the Sapharohitakūlīya; "pary ū ṣu" for the Śyāvāśvāndhīgava; "pari pra dhanva" for the Vājajit; and the final [laud] for the Kāva [is performed] with verses containing the word "sūrya. The entire Caturviṃśa [stoma] is used. The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. The Trayastriṃśa [stoma] follows. Here, the duties of the tenth day and the Mānasa [rite] must be performed. Because of the statement, "In all cases, one should be accompanied by the duties, even in the tenth vrata," it should be performed together with those duties.

Some declare that the mental cup (mānasa) on the tenth day is not an integral part [of the sacrifice], because it is introduced with the words "some say" and because of the statement: "It would be an adventitious element, since it is prescribed as a subject of discussion."
Thus ends the ninth day. || 25 ||
The tenth day;
he says the tenth day is the Viśvajit Atirātra.
Thus [ends the first].
Thus ends the tenth day. || 26 ||
Thus ends the ten-night rite consisting of the Chandomas.
The *devapur* ten-night sacrifice (*daśarātra*) consists of:

the first day is a *triṣṭomāgniṣṭoma*; [the second] is a *jyotirukthya-triṣṭomāgniṣṭoma*; [the third] is a *gaurukthya*; [the fourth] is an *abhijidagniṣṭoma*; [the fifth] is a *gaurukthya*; [the sixth] is a *viśvajidagniṣṭoma*; [the seventh] is an *āyurukthya*; [the eighth] is a *viśvajidagniṣṭoma*; and [the ninth] is an *atirātra* with all the *stomas*. This ten-night sacrifice, beginning with the *devapura*, has been described by this section of the text. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) follows.
This very [sacrifice] is the *triṣṭoma* *agniṣṭoma*. (1) By the word "this," the *jyotiṣṭoma*, which serves as the archetype (*prakṛti*) for all [sacrifices], is referred to. (1)
He shows how its nature as a *triṣṭubh* comes about: "Its stomas are sharers in the *savana*s, or they have equal shares. (2)

The *trivṛt*, *pañcadaśa*, and *saptadaśa* *stomas* partake of the three *savanas* respectively; thus they are "partakers of the *savanas*. Alternatively, they may be "partakers of equal shares," meaning that they partake of equal *stotras*: four *stotras* consisting of the *trivṛt*, four consisting of the *pañcadaśa*, and four consisting of the *saptadaśa*. The word *samāvat* is a synonym for *samāna* (equal). Thus the first day has been described. ||2||
Thus ends the first day. ||27||
The second day:

he speaks of the second day—the Jyotis Ukthya. Its Bahiṣpavamāna consists of one thousand verses, as in the first [day]. In the place of the Saṃhita [stotra], there is the Maukṣa; for the Nārmedha, the Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra. He omits the night [stotra]. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as the second [rite] with a single-stoma.

"Thus: 'Flow on as the leader of speech, with flashing luster'—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. 'Agni, the messenger; we [worship] Mitra; Indra, the singers [worship] Indra; Indra and Agni'—these are the *ājya* hymns. 'High is the birth of your juice'—this is the *gāyatra* and the *cāmahīyava*. 'Being purified, O Soma, in your stream'—this is the *samanta* and the *yaudhājaya*. 'The red bull'—this is the final *pārtha*. And the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *kāleya*—these are the *pṛṣṭha* stotras."

The *gāyatra* [stotra] is performed with the verse "svādiṣṭhayā" at the *aukṣa* [offering]; the *saphaśrudhya* with "pavasvendramaccha"; the *śyāvāśva* and *āndhīgava* with "purojitī vo andhasaḥ"; and the final [stotra] belongs to Kava on verses containing the word "sūrya. In the *saphaśrudhya*, there are two single-verse [stotras]. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *ukthas* are the *sākamaśva*, the *saubhara*, and the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*. By the designation "Jyotis," these are the *jyotiṣṭoma-stomas*. Because of the mention of "ukthya," there is the exclusion of the *rātri* and the *ṣoḍaśin*. Regarding this, the *nidāna* states: "The *jyotis* sacrifice has the *ukthya* as its conclusion, the *bṛhat* as its *pṛṣṭha*, and the *bārhata* as its *tantra*," and so forth. 2.
Thus ends the second day. || 28 ||
Regarding the third day,
he says: "Whatever is the arrangement of the first, that same is for the third"— that which was prior is the subsequent.
Thus ends [the first section]. ||1||
Thus ends the third day. ||29||
Regarding the fourth day, he says:
"The Gaur Ukthya is the fourth day. || 1 ||
Thus [it is said]. This [rite] lasts for one day. || 1 ||
Thus ends the fourth day. || 30 ||

The fifth day: he says "the fifth day. It is the *Abhijit* *Agniṣṭoma*. For that *Abhijit*, [the verses] "O Soma, being purified, flow with thy stream" (*punānaḥ soma dhārayā*) are used for three verses as the *Abhīvarta*; the *Raurava* for one verse; the *Kaṇvarathantara* for one verse; the *Maidhātitha* for one verse; and the *Yaudhājaya* for three verses. Now, if one should wish to perform the *Kaṇvarathantara* as a triplet, one should transpose the places of the *Abhīvarta* and the *Kaṇvarathantara*, or those of the *Kaṇvarathantara* and the *Yaudhājaya*. 1.

Thus it is said. It was previously stated that for the *pavamāna* [laud], one should use "Punānaḥ soma dhāraya" as the *abhīvarta*, and the *raurava* and *yaudhājaya* as the *sāman*s. However, in this case, in place of the *raurava*, one should employ the three *sāman*-verses consisting of the *raurava*, the *kaṇvarathantara*, and the *maidhātitha*. But if, because the *kaṇvarathantara* is considered inferior due to its being a remote form of the *rathantara*, its application to the triplet of verses is desired, then the *kaṇvarathantara* is to be performed on the three verses beginning with "Punānaḥ soma dhāraya."

The *raurava*, the *abhīvarta*, and the *maidhātitha*—these are the triple-verse *sāmans*; the *yaudhājaya* is [performed] on three verses. Or rather: the *abhīvarta* on three verses, the *raurava*, the *yaudhājaya*, and the *maidhātitha*—these are the triple-verse *sāmans*. Or: the *kaṇvarathantara* on three verses. The rest is the same.

Everything else is the same as the *Abhijit* performed in a single day (*aikāhika*). Here, because both the *Gauḥ* and the *Abhijit* have the *Bṛhat* as their *pṛṣṛtha*, they say there is a lack of variety (*jāmitā*); therefore, the *Kaṇvarathantara* is prescribed for the midday pressing of the two *Abhijits*. And so says the *Nidāna*: "They resort to the *Kaṇvarathantara*; [these] end with the *Rathantara*; they are the means of avoiding monotony (*ajāmi*) in the cases where the *Bṛhat* is combined. (2)
Thus ends the fifth day.
The sixth day;
he says "the sixth day"—that which is the former is the latter. ||1||
Thus; the meaning is that the Gaurukthya one-day sacrifice (ekāha) is thus established. || 1 ||
Thus ends the sixth day. || 32 ||
The days from the seventh to the tenth are the four days beginning with the seventh:
the Viśvajit Agniṣṭoma, the Āyus Ukthya, the Viśvajit Agniṣṭoma, and the Sarvastoma Atirātra.
They are prescribed for a single day. || 1 ||
Thus [ends the first section]. || 1 ||
Thus end the days beginning with the seventh. || 33 ||
Thus ends the *Devapūrvadaśarātra*.

The Pauṇḍarīka is an eleven-night sacrifice consisting of an Abhyāsaṅgya ṣaḍaha, three Chandomas, a Catuṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma, and a Viśvajit Atirātra; thus it is described by the [following] Anuvāka. Regarding its alternative mode of having twelve Upasad days like the Dvādaśāha, the procedure for the Sutyā days and so forth is the same as that of the Dvādaśāha.

In the case of the six-day rite with six *upasad* days, there is the *sutyā* [pressing] on the sixth day, and so forth. During the *sutyās*, the singing of the *yajñasārathi* [hymn] takes place. The *lokadvāra* and the *subrahmaṇyā* are exactly as in the archetype (*prakṛti*). He states the arrangement of the *stomas*: the first through the fifth days constitute the five-day period (*pañcāha*) based on the *pṛṣṭhya* [ṣaḍaha].

Thus: this very five-day period (*pañcāha*) is that which is described as "of the seasons" (*ṛtūnām*) and so forth; it is the five-day period based on the *pṛṣṭhya* [stoma]. The arrangement for its first day is as follows: the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant is "Sing to him, O men," "Toward the newborn, the swift one," and "Of you, O Sage, who purifies. There is the cessation of the *viśvarūpa*, the *jyotis*, the *gāna*, and the *dhūr-gānas*. The *ahiṃkāra*, the *visṛṣṭahiṃkāra*, and the *bhakāra* proceed. The *ājya* chants are "O Agni, come to us," "To Mitra," and "Indra and Agni."

"O Soma, [songs] for the inspired ones"—this *gāyatra* [sāman] is for the first day; the *āśva* for the second; the *somasāman* for the third. "O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—this *yaudhājaya* is for all three days; the *auśana* is the final one. The *rathantara*, *vāmadevya*, *naudhasa*, and *kāleya* are the *pṛṣṭha* [sāmans]. Regarding this six-day period, the sounds of chariots and drums mentioned in the rule "they should drive chariots over the *pṛṣṭhya* stotras of the *bṛhat* and *rathantara*" are not to be performed, because the sounds of chariots and so forth have already been prescribed in connection with the employment of the six *pṛṣṭha* sāmans beginning with the *rathantara*.

This has been stated in the *Upagrantha*: "How [are the rites] performed for those that are dissociated (*viprayukta*)? Some say: "Because they are prescribed for those that are associated (*saṃprayukta*). "How [is it] for those that are dissociated? For instance, when the *Bṛhat* and *Rathantara* [sāmans] are indeed associated, then on their *pṛṣṭha* day there occurs the maneuvering of the chariot and the beating of the drum; this does not happen when they are dissociated. And since this six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*) is characterized by the *Bṛhat* and *Rathantara* as its *pṛṣṭha*, there is no association with the six *pṛṣṭha* [sāmans] here.

Now follows the *Arbhava* [Pavamāna-stotra]. "With the sweetest" (*svādiṣṭhayā*) and "With this [Soma], flow, seeking the gods" (*ayā pavasva devayuḥ*) are the two *Gāyatra-saṃhitās*. "The beloved, tawny one flows" (*pavate haryato hariḥ*)—these two single verses are with the *sapha*-accentuation. "To the pressed juice" (*pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ*) is the *Audala* hymn; it is used in the first verse. The *Gautama* hymn is used for three verses. The *Kāva* hymn is the final one. The *Yajñāyajñīya* is the *Agniṣṭoma-sāman*. There are two *Trivṛt* pressings and one *Pañcadaśa* pressing. All the days prior to the *Udayanīya Atirātra* conclude with the consumption of the curd-portion (*dadhi-bhakṣa*).

During the time of carrying around the *vasatīvarī* waters while the *ahīna* rites are being performed, the *subrahmaṇyā* formula—containing the announcement of the sacrifice for the following day (*śvaḥsutyā*) and the names of the officiants (*pravacanī-sanāmagraha*)—must be recited. Some authorities also desire that the *subrahmaṇyā* announcing the sacrifice for the following day be recited at the time of the *hāriyojana* and *atipraiṣa*. However, it has already been established previously that this is not the intention of the author of the Sūtra. On the second day, the rites beginning with the *yajñasārathi* and ending with the *subrahmaṇyā* are to be performed as before.

"Flow forth with speech; flow forth, O Soma, as the bull, for you are indeed the bull"—with these words they perform the *bahiṣpavamāna*. For the second and subsequent days, they should chant the *bahiṣpavamāna* in the *sadas*. Having gone out before the distribution of the *dhiṣṇya* hearths, they should complete the rite at the *cātvāla* pit, beginning from the throwing away of the grass. The *ājya* stotras are "Agni, the messenger," "Mitra we [worship]," "Indra, him," and "Indra and Agni"; in the four-verse hymn, one should omit the final verse.
