"Flow on, O bull, in a stream"—this is the *gāyatra* [stotra] of Yauktāśva, which is the first. "Being purified, O Soma, in a stream"—this is the *aiḍa* with three *nidhanas*, belonging to Āyāsya. "The red bull"—this is the final [stotra] of Vasiṣṭha. Some desire the final [stotra] to be that of Pṛthu; however, that is not desired by the *ārṣeyakalpa*. For there is a statement in the *pṛṣṭhyāvalamba* that for the second day, the final [stotra] is that of Vasiṣṭha, and because this [sacrifice] follows that as its archetype (*prakṛti*). The *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] are the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *mādhucchandasa*.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this constitutes the *gāyatram* and the *hāviṣmatam*. "pavasvendramaccha"—these two single-verse hymns are for the *śaṅkusujñāna*. "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"—this consists of the *āsita* and the *krauñca*, with the latter being the subsequent one. "vṛṣā matīnām"—this is the final *yāma*. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. "ehyū ṣu"—this is the *sākamaśva*. "evā hyā mahīyavaḥ"—this is the *mahīyava*. "indraṃ viśvāḥ"—this is the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*; these are the *ukthas*. There are two *pañcadaśa* chants at the pressing. One is *saptadaśa*.
From the *stomavimocana* until the end of the *dadhi-bhakṣa*, and including the *subrahmaṇyā*, it is as before.

For the third day: the *bahispavamāna* [stotra] consists of the verses "davidyutatyā rucā," "ete asrgramindavaḥ," "rājā medhābhirīyate," "taṃ tvā nṛmṇāni bibhratam," and "iṣe pavasva dhārayā. The *ājya* stotras consist of "agnināgniṃ huvema" and "indreṇa nū sajoṣāḥ. For the first [turn], the *gāyatra* is "uccā te jātamandhasaḥ" and the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*; for the second, the *paurumadga* is "abhi somāsa āyavaḥ"; and the *gautama* is used for three verses; and the *antarikṣa* is used for three verses.

On the *adhyāsya* [day], there is the *āṣkāra-nidhana* [sāman] beginning with *pra hinvāna*. The last [part] is the *aṅgirasāṃ saṃkrośa* beginning with *tisro vācaḥ*. The *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] consist of the *rathantara* and the *vāmadevya*; the *mahāvaiṣṭambha* beginning with *vayaṃ ghatva*; and the *raurava* beginning with *taraṇir hiṣāsatī*. The *gāyatra* and the *pāṣṭhauha* [are used for] the [verse] beginning with *tisro vāca udīrate*. And the *vācaḥ sāman* and the *śaukta* [are used for] the [verse] beginning with *ā sotā pari ṣiñcata sakhāya ā niṣīdata*.

"Sutāsaḥ madhumattamāḥ" are the two *tvāṣṭrī* *sāmans*, beginning with *svāra* and having the *triṇidhana*. "Pavitraṃ te" is the final *ariṣṭa*. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *pramam̐hiṣṭhīya*, *hārivarṇa*, and *tairaścya* are the *ukthas*. There are two *saptadaśa* chants at the pressing; one is *ekaviṃśa*. The *stomavimocana* and so forth are as before.

The *pavamāna* of the fourth day: "Purifying himself, he has been born; flowing on, he has stepped forth like eager cattle. O thou of lofty thought, flow swiftly! The dawns impel the Sun. This is the *bahispavamāna*. "May Agni strike down the Vṛtras; this Indra [has acted] for you, O Mitra and Varuṇa, with the bones of Dadhyañc. This [is the song] of yours from my mind. These are the *ājya* hymns. "Flow on, accomplishing strength"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *ātharvaṇa*, and the *nidhanakāma*.

"O Soma, I have rejoiced in thee"—this is the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*, the *ābhīśava*, the *svaḥpṛṣṭha*, and the *āṅgirasa*. "Soma flows, the progenitor of hymns"—this is the *janitra* as the final [stotra]. The *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *traiśoka*, and the *pṛśni* are the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras]. "The sage of heaven, around the dear [ones]"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *aurṇāyava*, and the *bṛhadbhāradvāja*. "For thou indeed, O divine Soma, being purified, with thy wave"—these are the *bṛhat* and the *kātīṣādīya*.

"Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the *Nānada*, the *Āndhīgava*, and the *Śuddhāśuddhīya* with the *padanidhana*. "Pra ta āśvinīḥ" is the *Lauśa* as the final [stotra]. The *Yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. "Agniṃ vaḥ" is the *Saindhukṣita*. "Vayamu tvā" is the *Saubhara*. "Imam indra" is the *priya* of Vasiṣṭha. These are the *ukthas*. He extracts the *ṣoḍaśin*. This is established in the Sūtra as well by the conclusion: "In the Pauṇḍarīka, the *ṣoḍaśin* occurs on the fourth day because of the absence of the sixth," and so forth. There are two *ekaviṃśa* [stomas] at the pressing; one *triṇava*.

The *bahispavamāna* chant is: "O Soma, all-knowing, that which is bright and worthy of praise"; "The Somas have flowed forth"; "The sage [has flowed] forth for the feast of the gods"; "Grain after grain for us with your juice"; and "Those streams of yours dripping with honey. The *ājya* chants are: "O Agni, we meditate upon the hymn"; "For even by the wide [space], there exists [the light]"; "Rising up with vigor"; and "O Indra and Agni, you two indeed. And the *gāyatra*, *yaṇva*, *śākala*, and *vārśa* chants begin with: "Flow on, O Soma, most brilliant!"

"Soma has been pressed" (Soma uṣvāṇa) is the Mānava; "Vāma" is the Ānūpa; "Of Agni" (Agnestriṇidhanam) is the Triṇidhana; "Indu, the steed" (Indurvājī) is the Saṃpātya—these constitute the midday [pressing]. The Rathantara and Vāmadevya [are the Prastāvas]; "Indra for exhilaration" (Indro madāya) is the Bārhadgira; "From the sweet" (Svādoḥ) and "Come hither" (Āyāti) and "The prize-winning" (Rāyovājīyam) are the Pṛṣṭhas. "This stalk is for exhilaration" (Asāvyaṃśurmadāya) is the Gāyatra, the Santani, the Eḍa, the Saindhukṣita, the Gauṣūkta, the Abhidyumna, the Bṛhadyaśas, the Prāṇas, and the "Child of the great ones" (Śiśurmahīnām)—these are the Cyāvana and Krośa [Stomas].

"Pavasva vājasātaye" is the Tvaṣṭrī-sāman; "svārayoḥ uttaram" (the higher of the two *svāra* chants), the Ṛṣabha-śākvara, the Pārtha, and the Aṣṭeḍa with the *padastobha*. "Govit pavasva" is the Dvyabhyāghāta; the Lauśa is the final [sāman]. The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. "Ā te agne idhīmahi" is the Saṃjaya; "indrāya sāma gāyata" is the Saumitra; and "asāvi soma indra te" is the Mahāvaiśvāmitra—these are the Ukthas. There are two Triṇava-stomas at the two pressings; there is one Trayastriṃśa-stoma. 1.
Thus [are the rites] on the days beginning with the first and ending with the fifth.

The sixth day is the sixth day of the *pṛṣṭhya-stoma*. For the descendants of Vidanvat, there is milk as the subsequent offering; the third pressing consists of the twenty-sixfold stoma and includes the *uktha* chants. 2.

Thus the sixth day has been described. Its two pressings consist of the *trayastrimśa* stoma, while one [pressing] consists of the *ṣaṭtrimśa*; such is the arrangement of the stomas. This is because of the rule regarding the *abhyāsaṅga* six-day rite (*ṣaḍaha*), which prescribes the *abhyāsaṅga*, and because of the statement in the ritual manual (*kalpa*) that "the third pressing of the *ṣaṭtrimśa* is accompanied by *ukthas*."

For the sixth day: *asṛkṣata pra vājinaḥ*, *etamu tyaṃ daśa kṣipaḥ*, *pavasva devavīrati*, *sanā ca soma jeṣi ca*, *taratsamandī dhāvati*, *ete somā asṛkṣata*—these are for the *bahiṣpavamāna*. *yamagne pṛtsu martyam*, *prati vāṃ sūra udite*, *bhindhi viśvā apa dviṣaḥ*, *yajñasya hi stha ṛtvijaḥ*—these are the *ājya* offerings.

"O Indu, for Indra accompanied by the Maruts"—this is the Gāyatra, the Ceṣovṛdhīya, the Krauñca, the Vājadāvarya, and the Dārḍhyacyuta. "Being cleansed by the skillful hand"—this is the Aiḍasvāra in the Aukṣṇorandhra. The Vājajit and the Varuṇasāman; and the Goṣṭha. "By this purification, let him purify"—this is the final Vāsiṣṭha, which contains the word "here. The Bṛhat and the Vāmadevya; "the fair-formed doer for our aid"—this is the Ṛṣabha and the Raivata. "When both worlds, O Indra"—this is the Araṇyegeya; and the Śyena—these are the Pṛṣṭhas.

"parisvāno giriṣṭhāḥ"—this is the Gāyatra; the three Vaidanvata hymns, beginning with the third and ending with the fourth; and the *payaḥ* (milk) chant. "sa sunve yo vasūnām," "taṃ vai sakhāyo madāya"—these are the Dīrgha and the Kārṇaśravasa chants. "somāḥ pavanta indavaḥ"—this is the Krauñca chant, specifically the first of the three; the Madhuścut nidhana, and within the Krauñca, the Vāṅnidhana and the Aiḍa. "jyotir yajñasya"—this is the Marutāṃ Dhenu, the final [chant]. The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.

He utters *hiṃ* for twelve verses: three times with three verses, once with eight, and once with one. He utters *hiṃ* for twelve verses: once with one verse, three times with three, and once with eight. He utters *hiṃ* for twelve verses: once with eight, once with one, and three times with three. This is the *viṣṭuti* (recitation method) of the thirty-six-fold hymn (*ṣaṭtriṃśastoma*), according to the statement, "From the twenty-seven-fold up to the equal [stomas]. The hymns are: *agne tvam naḥ* as the *gūrda*; *imā nu kam* as the *bhadra*; and *pra va indra* and *udvaṃśaputra* as the *ukthas*. The ritual for the dismissal of the *stoma* and so forth is as before.

On this day, once it has concluded, until the preparation for the following day, they should avoid excessive speech and the private recitation of the Veda. He should feed the officiating priests with clarified butter and honey; thus the six-day period is completed.
Thus ends the sixth day.
The seventh, eighth, and ninth days are the three Chandomas arranged in exactly the same manner; then again, the Kaṇvarathantara goes to its own world. || 3 ||

"Now, the three *chandomas* are likewise combined (*samūḍha*). This means that it is just as in the ten-night sacrifice (*daśarātra*) which contains the *chandomas*. Furthermore, regarding the statement "the *kaṇvarathantara* goes to its own world," in the twelve-night sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*), because of the risk of redundancy (*jāmi*) between the two *bārhata* days—the sixth and the seventh—the *kaṇvarathantara* was prescribed for the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina*) of the seventh day. As the Śruti says: "There is redundancy in the twelve-night sacrifice; O Ugradeva, the seventh [day] belongs to the *rājana* [sāman], being *bārhata*," and so forth.

In the *daśarātra* sacrifice characterized by the *chandoma*, it is stated that because of the omission of the sixth day, there is an absence of *jāmi* (monotony), and thus the *kaṇvarathantara* is prescribed in the place of the *somasāman* so that the *bṛhatī* meter may be maintained from the beginning. However, in this case, since the sixth day does exist, there would be *jāmitā*; therefore, to prevent that, the meaning is that the *kaṇvarathantara* should be performed in its own proper place. In that regard, concerning the seventh day—

The *bahis-pavamāna* [stotra] consists of the verses: "Those Soma-drops which, in a distant place, have been let loose like chariots being urged on," and "O Indu, flow along the path toward your skill that brings bliss"—these are for the *ṛtāvan* Vaiśvānara. The *ājya* [stotras] consist of: "Sing forth to Mitra," "Come to Indra, O you of brilliant luster," and "Praise him who with his flame... The *viṣṭuti* is that which begins, "He utters *hiṃ* for eight [verses]. The [stotras] are the *gāyatram*, the *saṃtani*, the *aiḍam*, the *sauparṇam*, and the *rohitakūlīyam*, beginning with "Flow on as a bull, O drop, in your stream."

"O Soma, being purified, flow in a stream"—this is the Kaṇvarathantara, the Gauṅgava, and the Ayāsya with two finales (*dvinidhana*). "Proclaiming wisdom like Uśanas"—this is the Vārāha as the final [stotra]. The Bṛhat and the Vāmadevya; "We indeed [sing] to thee"—this is the Abhinidhana Kāṇva; and "Nothing indeed [overcomes it]"—this is the Vaikhānasa. These are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras. "That exhilaration of thine which is most excellent"—this is the Gāyatra on three verses. The Agnerarka, the Adhyardheḍa, the Somasāman, and the Maukṣa—these are the Sāmatṛcas.

Alternatively, there are the *sāman*-verses: the *gāyatram*, the *maukṣam*, and the *somasāma*; the *agni-arka* on three verses; the *śārkaraplavau* with "eṣa sya dhārayā sutaḥ" and "sakhāya ā niṣīdata"; the *ātreya* and *kārtayaśa* with "purojitī vo andhasaḥ"; the *sauhaviṣam* with "pra vājyakṣāḥ"; the *aiḍam* with "pro ayāsīt," ending with the *yajñasārathi*; the *agniṣṭomasāman* is the *yajñāyajñīya*; the *vātsam* with "ā te vatsa"; the *aupagavam* with "tvaṃ na indra";
and the *vīṅka* with "yad indra citra ma iha"—these are the *ukthas*. The entire *caturviṃśa* [stoma] is thus completed.

On the eighth day: "The rays urge on the Sun; these Soma juices flow toward the beloved [Soma]. "The Soma, being purified, flows; the Soma drops have been released. "Your vital energies rise up; he has flowed through the filter. "Driving away the adversaries, he purifies himself. "Flow with this stream, O Pavamāna!"—these are the *Bahispavamāna* verses. "O Agni, with all your fires, we invoke Mitra; we incite that Indra for strength. "To Indra and Agni be great homage"—these are the *Ājya* verses.

"O Adhvaryu, [the Soma] pressed with stones"—this consists of the Gāyatra, the Vairūpa, the Āśurbhāgava, the Mārgīyava, the Saumitra, the Aiṭata, the Sākamaśva, and the Vilambasauparṇa. "The Soma-drops, the Āyavas..."—this consists of the Dvihiṅkāra, the Gāyatrapārśva, the Pauruhanmana, the Dvaigata, the Hārāyaṇa, the Ācchindra, and the Bārhaduktha. "Lo, they have carried the Child..."—this is the final Vāsiṣṭha. There is a double *hiṅkāra* in the first [verse].

In the *bārhaduktha* [stoma] on the middle day: the *rathantara* and the *vāmadevya*; the *naipātitha* with "O Indra, from the east and from the north"; and the *vaiyaśva* with "May he hear both"—these are the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras]. "Flow, O God, for the sake of long life" is the *gāyatra*; and the *svāśira*, the *arka*, the *surūpa*, the *bhāsa*, the *kākṣīvata*, and the *āsita*—these are the *gāyatrīsāman*s. "Toward splendor, great fame," "The breaths," and "The child of the great ones"—these are the *aiṣira* single-verse hymns (*ekarca*).

"Abhī no vājasātamam" is the *svāra* [chanting]; "śuddhāśuddhīyaṃ ca krauñcaṃ ca" and "rayiṣṭhaudale ca"; "pavasva soma mahāntsamudraḥ" is the *dharma*; "hāu dharta" is the final *aiḍa* and *śārṅga*; the *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*; "preṣṭhaṃ vaḥ" is the *auśana*; "endra no gadhi priyā" is the *sāṃvarta*; "purāṃ bhinduryuvā kaviḥ" is the *māruta*—these are the *ukthas*. The entire [rite] has the forty-four-fold (*catuścatvāriṃśa*) *stoma*.

For this forty-four-fold stoma, three *viṣṭuti*s (modes of chanting) are prescribed. Among them, one view is that the first belongs to the *ājya* chants, the second to the *pṛṣṭha* chants, and the third to the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*s. An alternative view is also shown in the context of the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*).

For the ninth day: "Born near the waters, the swift one... "This immortal god... "He goes with the subtle prayer... "And he is that bull, the chariot... "He is the steed urged on by men... "He is the seer, highly praised... "That pressed [Soma] for drinking, O Pavamāna, you, the sage..."—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna. "I call upon you, the delightful to behold, the friend of pure strength... "Great is Indra who [rules] by his might... "I call those two by whom this [world exists]..."—these are the Ājya offerings.

"Pavamānasya jighnataḥ"—this is the Gāyatra, the Ādārasṛt, the Surūpa, the Hariśrī-nidhana, the Saindhukṣita, the Gatanidhana Bābhrava, the Saṃkṣāra of the Eḍas, and the Ṛṣabha Pavamāna. "Parīto ṣiñcatā sutam"—this is the Pṛṣṭha [stotra] performed on three verses.

The *Kauṇmalabarhiṣa* hymn is for the first [day]; the *Arkapuṣpa* for the second; the *Dairghaśravasa* for the third; the *Devasthāna* for three [days]; the *Saṃkṛti* for three [days]; the *Vaiyaśva* for the first; the *Bharga* for three [days]; the *Ābhīśava* for the first; the *Yaśas* for three [days]; the *Vāsiṣṭha* for the middlemost [day]; and the final *Vāsiṣṭha*, beginning with "Hāi uhu vāi akrān," [is for the last day]. This arrangement is established precisely by such statements as: "Its *bṛhatī* verses are to be sung in the forest (*araṇyegeyāni*) upon triplets (*tṛceṣu*)," and so forth.

The *Bṛhat*, the *Vāmadevya*, and the *Śrāyantīya*; the *Pṛṣṭha* chants beginning with "yata indra bhayāmahe" and ending with "samanta"; the *Gāyatra*, the *Aśvasūkta*, the *Śāmmada*, the one with the *Dāvasu* finale, the *Pratīcīneḍa*, the *Kāśīta*, and the *Hāviṣkṛta*; and the *Sauparṇa* and *Vaiśvamanasa* beginning with "tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya pavasva devavītaye"; and the *Āsitottara* beginning with "pari tyaṃ haryataṃ hariṃ"—these are for the first [day].

The *Dīrghatamasarkas* are on the second day; the *Ākūpāra*, *Yatsvayoni*, *Nihavayad*, *Vāhiṣṭhīya*, *Asitāt*, *Sādhrākūpāra*, and others are in the triplets (*tṛcas*). "Pavasva soma mahe dakṣāya" is the *vidharma*; "Asāvi somo aruṣo vṛṣā hariḥ" is the *aiḍa-yāma*, which is the last [stotra]. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. "Ā ghā yaḥ" is the *aidhmavāha*.

They chant the *traikakubha* with "He who alone," the *udvaṃśīya* with "They sing to thee," and these are the *ukthas*. The entire [sacrifice] consists of forty-eight [verses]. One should prescribe the *ājya* of the Maitrāvaruṇa with the final verse of the forty-eight-fold [stoma], and the final *stotras* with the very first verse. 3.
Thus end the seventh, eighth, and ninth days.
Of the two fourfold-stoma days, the first is the tenth day.

In the Catuṣṭoma sacrifices, the tenth day comes first. Its arrangement is as follows: there are three *anuṣṭubh* verses beginning with "This Pūṣan is wealth, he is Bhaga. He makes four *gāyatrī* verses: the *retasyā* verse "This Pūṣan is wealth, he is Bhaga" is used for the first three quarters; the second *stotrīyā* verse is "He has revealed both heaven and earth"; the third is "O Kaṇvas, the Soma-drops [have cleared] your paths"; and the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant is performed with the four verses beginning with "O Pavamāna, [grant] fame and inspired thoughts," which contain the characteristics of the *rathantara*.

The *ājya* hymns are "agna ā no mitrāvaruṇā" and "indrāgnī. For these, an eightfold *stoma* (*aṣṭistoma*) consisting of four rounds (*catuḥparyāya*) should be performed. The method of chanting (*viṣṭuti*) is as follows: he chants with two [verses] using the first [verse]; he chants with two using the first; he chants with two using the middle [verse]; he chants with two using the last [verse]. In the two *catuṣṭomas*, there are four rounds.

In that regard, there are four [sections]; beginning with the statement that there would be two sequences (*paryāya*) in the first [section], and so on up to the statement that for the eighth there are two sequences. Therein, having established the first and second [sequences] in the locations of the *ṛc*-portions, one should establish the third sequence to the north of the second *ṛc*-portion location using two blades of *kuśa* grass with their tips pointing westward. To the north of that, in the location of the *ṛc*-portion, one should establish the fourth.

Now follows the midday [service]: "High is the birth of thy juice" (*uccā te jātamandhasaḥ*)—the *gāyatra* and the *cāmahīyava*. "Being purified, O Soma, in thy stream" (*punānaḥ soma dhārayā*)—the *raurava*, the *maidhātitha*, and the *yaudhājaya*; these are the triple-verse *sāmans*. "Run forth" (*pra tu drava*)—the *auśana* as the final one; this constitutes the twelve-fold [stotra]. The *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śrāyantīya*, and the *kāleya* are the *pṛṣṭha* chants of the sixteen-fold [stotra]. This is the *viṣṭuti* (arrangement) of the sixteen-fold *stoma*: he utters the *hiṃ* call four times—once with two verses, once with one, and once with one.

He utters *hiṃ* four times: once with one [verse], once with two, and once with one; he utters *hiṃ* four times: once with one, once with one, once with one, and once with two. In the sixteenth [stotra], there are four twelve-fold cycles (*paryāya*); according to the statement that "among them, the middle ones are similar," the subsequent cycles follow. "With the sweetest [hymn]" (*svādiṣṭhayā*) is the *gāyatra-saṃhitā*; "Flow for Indra" (*pavasvendram accha*) is the *sapha-pauṣkala*, consisting of single verses; and "For you, the conquerors of the soma-juice" (*purojitī vo andhasaḥ*) is the *śyāvāśva-andhīgava*.

The *yajñāyajñīya* and the *kāva* as the final [stotra] constitute the Ārbhava Pavamāna with twenty verses. The *vāravantīya* is performed upon four triplets (*ṛcaḥ*) with six *stotrīyā* verses each, beginning with "yajñā eṣa," "taṃ te śrudhī," and "havam. The Agniṣṭoma-sāman is the Caturviṃśa. The *viṣṭuti* (recitation method) for the Caturviṃśa is as follows: "He utters *hiṃ* three times; he [sings] two [verses], he two, he two"—this is the first round (*paryāya*). The same applies to the three subsequent rounds.

Because of the statement, "In the twenty-fourth [day], there are four sets of six variations," and so forth; it is established in the *Nidāna* that on this day, the ten duties (*daśadharma*) other than those connected with the *mānasa* [chanting] are to be performed. What, then, are the ten duties? They are: the repetition of the final quarters of the two [verses] *ṛcam* and *sāma dadhikrāvṇaḥ*; and in the mantra *āyur me prāṇāḥ*, the repetition of the words *punar asmāsu dadhmaḥ*. Other duties also—such as those stated in the passage beginning, "On this day, having made the *anuṣṭubh* the measure, they should diminish [the syllables]," and so forth—are to be understood as being other than those connected with the *mānasa*. || 1 ||
Thus ends the tenth day. || 37 ||
The eleventh day is the Viśvajit Atirātra; the Viśvajit Atirātra. || 1 ||

The eleventh day is the Viśvajit Atirātra. Its Bahiṣpavamāna stotra consists of verses in the Trivṛt (nine-verse) stoma: "upa tvā jāmayo giraḥ," "janīyanto nvagravaḥ," "uta naḥ priyāḥ priyāsu," "tat savitur vareṇyam," "somānāṃ svaraṇam," and "agna āyūṃṣi pavase pavamānasya te kave. These constitute the Bahiṣpavamāna; they are all in the final triplet (tṛca). The others consist of single verses (ekarca), with the distinction of deities according to their respective characteristics (liṅga).

"Suṣamiddho na āvaha" (O well-kindled one, bring hither for us...), "tā naḥ śaktam" (those [powers] of ours, O capable one...), "pārthivasya" (of the earthly one...), "yuñjanti bradhnamaruṣam carantam" (they yoke the ruddy, moving sun...), and "tamīḍiṣva yo arciṣā" (praise him who with his flame...)—these are the *ājya* verses. "Suṣamidh" is used for the four-verse hymn. The extraction is according to the *gotra*. The *ājya* of the Hotṛ consists of fifteen verses; that of the Maitrāvaruṇa, seventeen; that of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, twenty-one; and that of the Acchāvāka, fifteen. "Asya pratnām" contains both the *gāyatram* and the *cāmahīyavam*; "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam" is the *kāleyam*, used in the first [turn].

The *Rathantara* is [chanted] on three verses; the *Yaudhājaya* on the *adhyāsya*; and "This Soma" (*ayaṃ soma*) is the final *Pārtha*. Thus, the Mādhyandina [savana] consists of seventeen [stotras]. At the time of the praise of the *Rathantara*, the sound of chariots should be produced, as stated in the passage beginning, "On the *pṛṣṭhya* day, they should drive chariots over the chariot," because of the existence of the performance of the six *pṛṣṭha* stotras. Furthermore, there is the statement: "One should perform the *Vairāja* duties in the Viśvajit sacrifice, and likewise in the other *pṛṣṭha* stotras"—this is the opinion of the Teacher (Ācārya).

The *pṛṣṭha* chants are the Vairāja, the Mahānāmnīs, the Vairūpa, and the Revatīs. The twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*) is the *pṛṣṭha* of the Hotṛ; the twenty-seven-fold (*triṇava*) is that of the Maitrāvaruṇa; the seventeen-fold (*saptadaśa*) is that of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin; and the twenty-one-fold is that of the Acchāvāka. The ritual rules for the Vairāja are stated in the passage beginning with "When the chant of the Vairāja has been commenced" (*vairājasya stotre upākṛte*). Those for the Mahānāmnīs are stated in the passage beginning with "Having placed the water-jars nearby" (*apassāvakā upanidhāya*). Those for the Vairūpa are stated in the passage beginning with "Approaching while seeking vigor" (*upa vājayamānāḥ*).

In the *vāravantīya* hymn, [the verse] beginning with "The milch-cow" (*dhenuḥ*) is for the *revatī*s; "Enveloping, dwelling on the mountain" (*parisvāno giriṣṭhā*) is for the *gāyatra-saṃhitā*; "Flow pure toward Indra" (*pavasvendramaccha*) is for the *sapha-śrudhya*; "Around you" (*paryūṣva*) is the *vāmadevya*; "For victory through your juice" (*purojitī vo andhasaḥ*) is the *āndhīgava* in the *yajñāyajñīya*. In the *triṇava* *ārbhava-stotra*, the *vāravantīya* is used in the two-footed verses (*dvipadā*), and the *kāva* is the final [verse] among those containing the word "sun" (*sūryavatī*). "O Agni, you are the invoker of sacrifices" (*tvamagne yajñānāṃ hotā*) is the *bṛhat* *agniṣṭoma-sāman* in the *trayastrimśa*.

They should strike the drum during the *bṛhat* hymn. The *sākamaśva*, *saubhara*, and *nārmedha* are the *uktha* chants; the first is the *triṇava*, and two are the *ekaviṃśa*. The *gaurīvita* is the *ṣoḍaśin* chant with the *indra juṣasva* verse as its *sāman* on the *ekaviṃśa* stoma. The night is the regular (*āhīnikī*) fifteen-fold (*pañcadaśī*). The junction (*saṃdhi*) is the nine-fold (*trivṛt*). From the dismissal of the *stomas* until the concluding oblation (*udavasānīyā*), the *subrahmaṇyā* call should not be performed here, because it is stated that the *āharantikī* (concluding) *subrahmaṇyā* is for the sake of what follows.

Now, Āpastamba has stated another method for the arrangement of the days of the Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice: "The Abhyāsaṅgya, five five-day periods, four Chandomas, the Mahāvrata, and the Viśvajit Atirātra with all the Pṛṣṭhas. In this context, everything except the Mahāvrata should be performed as in the Daśarātra (the ten-night sacrifice) which includes the Chandomas; however, the Mahāvrata itself follows the procedure of a one-day sacrifice (*aikāhika*). Regarding this, some say that the mental rites (*mānasa-dharma*) should take place here, as they do in the tenth day of the Daśarātra. To this, we state our own conclusion: the vow (*vrata*) that occurs after the tenth day until the end of the vow is always to be performed mentally.
According to the Sūtra, they are called the Gautamas who conquered Saṃvara. || 1 ||
At the conclusion of the vow, according to the school of Sāṃvargajita, it should be mental;
as for the other duties belonging to the tenth day, they are to be performed on the preceding day.
According to another view, the preceding rites should indeed be performed with identical mantras;
however, in this vow, the performance of those other rites—such as the *sarparājñī* hymns—is not required.
Even in the case of a sacrificial session (*pakṣa*), it should be determined that [these qualities] are not seen in any [other sacrifice];
for in the other, the Pauṇḍarīka, neither the ritual properties (*dharma*) nor the mental [concentration] exist.

Thus [it is said]. Now, the Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice as described by Āśvalāyana consists of an expanded nine-night rite (*vyūḍha-navarātra*), the Mahāvrata, and the Vaiśvānara [offering]. In that context, the expanded nine-night rite is to be performed like the expanded twelve-day rite (*vyūḍha-dvādaśāha*). The specific details are stated as follows: the Audala, the Māsita, the Tvaṣṭṛ-sāman, the Avikṛta, and the fourth day’s Tvaṣṭṛ-sāman; the Krauñca—these are the *svaras* [melodies] for the Pṛṣṭhya [ṣaḍaha], along with the Gaurīvita in the Loka [stotra]. The Ātreya is the *svāra* [melody] for the seventh day, and the Kautsa for the eighth.

On the ninth day, the verses "pari tyam haryatam hari" and "gaurīviti" are placed in the Gaurīvita-stotra; one [verse] is used for the *āsita*, and one for Dīrghatamas’s *arka*. One [verse] is used for Ākūpāra, which is to be performed in its own place (*svayoni*). Thus, the final *sāmarāja* of the midday pressing is fixed; however, Dīrghatamas’s *arka* is not [fixed]. Furthermore, that [Dīrghatamas’s *arka*] should not be substituted with a *bṛhatī* verse in order to avoid transposition (*asaṃcāra*). The *mahāvrata* is a one-day rite (*aikāhika*); by the word *vaiśvānara*, the *jyotiṣṭoma* *atirātra* is meant. Its night belongs to the multi-day (*ahīna*) sacrifice. || 4 ||
Thus ends the eleventh day. 37.
Thus concludes the eleven-night Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice.
Thus has Govinda, whose ritual procedures are not deficient, been explained by Varadarāja, the son of Vāmanārya; may he be pleased.
Thus ends the eighth chapter in this commentary on the Ārṣeyakalpa, composed by Varadarāja, the son of the venerable Vāmanārya.
The two Atirātras of the twelve-day rite are those containing the *ṣoḍaśin* cup. 911.
In the thirteen-night rite, in the place of the first *Chandoma*, which is the *Kaṇvarathantara*, there is the *Somasāman*: "O Soma, being purified, flow with thy stream... 912.
The vow pertaining to the year-long session applies to the sacrificial sessions (*sattras*). 913.

Where they proceed from the Atirātra to the Pṛṣṭhya [period], there the *anurūpa* for the first day is *asyapratnā*; or where [it follows] the Trikadrukas; or where the three-day period consists of Jyotis, Go, and Āyus, those [stomas] are Gaurīvita and Svara; these same [stomas] are reversed where [the sequence is] Āyus, Go, and Jyotis, ending with the Atirātra. These same [stomas] are used for the Go and Āyus [sacrifices] in Rātrisattras, except for those [Rātrisattras] which have an Atirātra and those measured by a year.
The first fifteen-night rite is established [as described].

For the second fifteen-night rite, there is an Atirātra, followed by an Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma in which the Agniṣṭoma-sāman is chanted on verses addressed to Vāyu; for that [rite], the Hotṛ’s Ājya-stotra is "Agniḥ pratnena janmanā" (with the Gaurīvita melody) in Anuṣṭubh meters.
This very same [structure] applies to the subsequent [rites]; its own Ājya-stotras [are as follows].
The arrangement [of the Sāmans] is established up to the seventeen-night rite (saptadaśarātra).

In the seventeen-night rite, there are four *ābhiplavika* days with the *śyaita*, *naudhasa*, *pauṣkala*, *śrudhya*, and *auṣṇiha* Sāmans. For the first day, this is the *eṣa pratna* *anurūpa*. For the fifth day, there are two pressings (*savanas*). For the sixth day, there is the third pressing; its *brahmasāman* is the *naudhasa*, and the *śrudhya* is on the *uṣṇih* verse. [The verses are]: "yajiṣṭhaṃ tvā vavṛmaha" for the *aidhmavāha*; the *traikakubha* and *nārmedha* for the *aidhmavāha*; or alternatively, the *sauśravasa* and *māruta* for the *aidhmavāha*. 921.

Where they proceed from the Atirātra to the Abhiplava, this is the *anurūpa* for the first day: "This ancient one... Where [the Abhiplava follows] the Trikadrukas, where the Abhiplava occurs in the Rātrisattras, the *brahmasāman* consists of the Śyaita and Naudhasa; the Pauṣkala, Śrudhya, and Auṣṇiha [are used], except in cases measured by the year-long sessions, up to the Vimśatirātra.
In the Vimśatirātra, the two year-long [sacrifices], the Viśvajit and Abhijit, are placed on both sides, just as in the Pūrdasharātra; thus it is the Bṛhatī.

In the first twenty-one-night rite, there are two Atirātras without the *ṣoḍaśin* on both sides, with the *ṣoḍaśin* in the middle; or all [the days] may be without the *ṣoḍaśin*, or indeed all may possess the *ṣoḍaśin*. (932) In the second twenty-one-night rite, the days are arranged according to the model of the year: the *Abhīvarta*, the *Kāleya*, the *Pṛṣṭhya*, those having the *Śyaita* and *Naudhasa* as *Brahmasāmans*, the *Svarasāmans*, the *Pauṣkala*, the *Śrudhya*, the *Auṣṇiha*, the *Viśuvat*, the *Sāmatṛca*, the *Loka*, the *Ābhīśava*, and the *Śrāyantiva-sūrya*; the *Vikarṇa* is the same [as the other]. (933) The arrangement extends up to the *Saṃsad* days. (934)

The *sam̐sad* is an *atirātra* with the *pṛṣṭhya-stoma* six-day period; for the first day, this *eṣapratna* is the *anurūpa*; the *gaurīvita* is on the *anuṣṭubh* [verse]; the fourth day is unmodified (*avikḷpta*) every day; on the fifth day, in the world of Ākūpāra, there is the *tvāṣṭrīsāman* which has two *anutoda*s. 935

Flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull; these drops have been let loose. And may they [grant] our prayer for the acquisition of cattle, for the man who exerts himself, O heroes. Like chariots that resound, the sons [of the gods] have been let loose toward our songs—the Indu-drops. On the path of thee, the purifying one, we [follow]; of thee, the purifying one, O Sage, [we offer] our own oblations. Of the purifying one who strikes [the foe], [there is the hymn]: "The Gāyatra and the Āmahīyava, the Ḍa and the Sauparṇa, the Rohitakūlīya and the Saṃtani. "O Soma, being purified, flow with thy stream"—[this is] the Samanta and the Kanvarathaṃtara.

The *Dairghaśravasa*, the *Bārhaduktha*, and the *Yaudhājaya*—these are his own final [stotras]; Pavamāna produced his own *pṛṣṭha* [stotras]. Thus, the *Gāyatra-saṃhita*, the *Jarābodhīya*, and the *Sauśravasa* are his own *uṣṇih* and *kakubh* [stotras]. "Abhi no vājasātamam" is the *Gaurīvita*; "Kārtayaśa" and "Śyāvāśva" are his own; "Andhīgave añjate" is the *Kava* as the final [stotra], and the *Yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. 94.

"Sing forth to him, O men; sing well to him who is born, the overcomer of waters, for the tawny one who possesses his own strength. These Soma-pressings flow toward the beloved; the Soma, being purified, flows on. O Agni, you wise one, come to the feast of the purifying Pavamāna. These are the *ājya* verses. "The inspired Soma-pressings... is the *gāyatra*, the *aśva*, and the *somasāman*; the *āśu*, the *bhārgava*, the *mārgīyava*, the *pajra*, the *dvaigata*, the *pauruhanmana*, the *hārāyaṇa*, the *yaudhājaya*, the *auśana* as the last, and the *rathantara*.

The Vāmadevya, the Naudhasa, the Kāleya, and [the hymns] "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā," which are Gāyatra-saṃhitas; the Kākṣīvata and the Bhāsa; "pavasvendramaccha"; the Saphākṣāra; "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ"; the Gaurīvita, the Padanidhana, and the Śuddhāśuddhīya; the Audala, the Gautama, the Kava, and the final Yajñāyajñīya as the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. 95

"eṣa u sya vṛṣā rathaḥ," "eṣa vāji hito nṛbhiḥ"—these two [verses] are placed before the six-verse *paryāsa* section; following the *yauktāśva* hymn, there are the *surūpa* and *carṣabha* hymns, and the two *āyāsya* hymns are the first among the *pṛṣṭha-kaulmalabarhiṣa* hymns; "vṛṣā śoṇaḥ" is the final *pārtha* hymn; "eṣa sya dhārayā sutaḥ pavasva devavītaye" is the *śaṅkusujñāna* hymn; following the *gaurīvita* hymn, there is the *yadvāhiṣṭhīya*; the rest is the same as on the second day of the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*). 961.

"Ut te śuṣmāso asthuḥ"—this four-verse hymn is recited before the *paryāsa* chant; thus this very third day is arranged as a *triṛca* (three-verse) sequence with the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*) stoma, and the subsequent three-day period is well-known.

Then he brings this very thirty-three-fold (*trayastrim̐śa*) day which is "unexpressed" (*anirukta*). For it, there is the *loka-vāśa* for the *Kaṇvarathaṃtara*, the *auśana* for the *Pārtha*, the *rathaṃtara* for the *Bṛhat*, the *naudhasa* for the *Śyaita*, and the *pauṣkala* for the *Śrudhya*.
The six-day period has its *pṛṣṭhya-stoma* reversed.

The *bahispavamāna* [stotra] consists of the *trivṛt* [stoma], the *aharana*, and the *nirukta*. For it, [the verses are]: "Pavasva inda vṛṣā suta" (one verse); "uta no goṣaṇiṃ dhiyam" (one verse); "śaśamānasya vā naraḥ" (one verse); "upa naḥ sūnavo giraḥ" (one verse); "pavamānasya te kave" (one verse). The *gāyatra* [sāman] is on one verse; the *āmahīyava* is on one verse; the *aiḍa sauparṇa* is on one verse; the *yaudhājaya* is on three verses with the words "punānaḥ soma dhārayā. The *gaurīvita* is in the place of Śyāvāśva. Everything else is the same as the *upahavya*. The entire [rite] is the *trivṛt*. This is the *jyotiṣṭoma agniṣṭoma*; its [stoma] is the *anuṣṭubh*, like that of Ṛṣabha.
The Jyotiṣṭoma is an Atirātra; everything else is the same as previously prescribed (967), up to the various Brahmasāmans (968).

There are three Atirātras with various Brahmasāmans, five Pañcāhas whose arrangements are like those of the Pañcāha, and which have various Brahmasāmans. For the first Pañcāha, according to the respective worlds, there are the Bṛhat and Rathantara, the Naudhasa, the Śyaita, and the Mahāvaiṣṭambha. (18)

"May he hear both [the *triśoka*]," or "he does not hear"—these are the *brahmasāmans*. For the second five-day period (*pañcāha*), they are the *anyonya*, the *loka*, and the *bṛhadrathantara*; the *abhīvarta* is "O Indra, in the races"; the *mānava* is "Thee indeed, O hero, yesterday"; that which is on the *pṛṣṭhya* day is the *chandasya* for the fifth day; the *āṣkāraṇidhana* is "Who knows him at the pressed [juice]"; the *kāṇva* is "Yoked with the ladle" upon its own verses; the *śrāyantīya* is upon its own verses—these are the *brahmasāmans* of the third five-day period, according to their respective places.

The *Bṛhat* and *Rathantara* [stotras] are performed with the Mānava hymn beginning "śagdhy ū ṣu śacipate," which belongs to the *yacchandas* class and is fixed for the fifth day; the Vāsiṣṭha hymn is "vayamenamidā hya"; the Bhāradvāja hymn is "ā tvā sahasram ā śatam"; and the Janitra is "yo rājā carṣaṇīnām. The hymn "tvam indra yaśa āsīḥ" belongs to Indra's glory (*indrasya yaśas*). These are the *brahmasāman*s. (971) The Viśvajit Atirātra sacrifice: in the place of the Gaurīvita [Sāman], one performs the Nānada; the Satrāsāhīya is the Traikakubha; the Nārmedha is the Gaurīvita, serving as the *ṣoḍaśin-sāman*. The night is the *saṃdhi* (junction). (972)

Now, this very five-day period is reversed; for the reversed five-day period, the *Bṛhat* and *Rathantara* [Sāmans] are for each other's world. "Drink of the pressed, flavorful [juice]" is the *Jāmadagna*; "When, O Indra, eastward, westward, northward... is the *Naipātitha*; "With the delightful bay horses, O Indra... is the *Abhinidhana* of Kaṇva; "As a wild bull [goes] to the place where he was driven away" is the *Manājya* of Gautama; "O friend, you have indeed praised... is the *Paurumīḍha*. These are the *Brahmasāman*s. The twelve-day rite consists of ten days of the ten-day period and an *Atirātra*.

In the middle thirty-three-night rite, all the *atirātras* include the *ṣoḍaśin*. In the final thirty-three-night rite, there is an *atirātra*, three five-day periods (*pañcāha*) arranged as five-day rites, with the *śyaita* and *naudhasa* as the *brahmasāman*s, and the *bṛhat* and *rathaṃtara* according to their respective positions; or alternatively, as arranged when the *brahmasāman*s are varied, there is a *viśvajit* with varied *brahmasāman*s. Then these same five-day periods are repeated. For the first day of the first of these repeated five-day periods, the *mānava* verse "ā soma āyavaḥ" is used once, and on that very same [verse], the *bṛhat* is used as the *nidhana*.

In one [verse] the *vārkajambha*, in another the *maidhātitha*, in three [verses] the *vāmra*; the *triṇidhana* of Agni is placed in the *adhyāsya*; the rest is the same as the established [form] up to the *vidhṛtis*. The *vidhṛtis* are the *jyotiṣṭoma* *atirātra* without the *ṣoḍaśin* cup; the *udvaṃśīya* is in the world of Kautsa. In these verses—"Come hither, O drops," "Enter thee," "O Jarābodha, do thou perform that"—the *jarābodhīya* is in the *gāyatrī* verses: "The noble lady, the maiden of the people," "This dawn is unprecedented. The *sandhi-sāman* is the *jarābodhīya*.

Now, that which was the *rāthaṃtara* and *trivṛt* of Kusurubinda, this is the *gaurīvita* for him in the *anuṣṭubh*; that which was the *bārhata* and *trivṛt*, that is the subsequent *pavamāna* with the *paryāsa* "te kava. In the world of Yuktaśva is the *hāviṣmata* of Mādhucchandasa; the *kāleya* of Hāviṣmanta is the *maukṣa*; the *sākamaśva* is the *saubhara* in the *gaurīvita-anuṣṭubh*; the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*—these are the *ukthas*. The rest is the same. That which was the former [verse] is the latter; its *ukthas* are the *pramam̐hiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, the *udvam̐śīya*, and the *tairaścya*. 982.

The Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra with the Ṣoḍaśin cup belongs to Kautsa. In the Uṣṇih verses beginning with "May the drops enter thee," "O Agni, bring us that wonderful wealth consisting of cattle," and "O Aśvins, come to our dwelling," he should perform the *śrudhya* at the junctions. 983.

Now, that which was Kusurubinda’s Rāthaṃtara fifteen-day rite is this very [rite] of his; the Gaurīvita is in the Anuṣṭubh meter; that which is the Bārhata fifteen-day rite is the "uttara" [part] of the Pavamāna, with the verse "te kava" as the *paryāsa* in the place of the Mādhucchandasa; the Kāleya is in the Anuṣṭubh meter in the place of the Gaurīvita—by these two [verses], there is a reversal up to the tenth day. On the tenth day, in the place of the Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra, the Nārmedha is used, with the verse "pratyasmai pipīṣate" as the *nānada*; the *Ṣoḍaśin* Sāman is the Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra, unmodified.

Now, that which belongs to Kusurubinda—the *rāthaṃtara* [sāman] with seventeen verses on the day—is this very [sāman] for him [Kusurubinda] in the world of Medhātithi: the *bṛhannidhana*, the *vārka-jambha*, the *raurava* of Medhātithi, the *saṃhita* of Agni, the *arka*, and the *gaurīvita* on an *anuṣṭubh*; that which is *bārhata* with seventeen verses is the subsequent [part] of the *pavamāna* chant, with "te kava" as the concluding verse (*paryāsa*) in the world of Mādhucchandasa; the *kāleya*, the *svāśira* of Arka, the *maukṣa*, and the *gaurīvita* on an *anuṣṭubh*—by means of these two, there is a reversal.

On the twelfth day, he extracts [the stotras] for the subsequent days: the Vārkañjabha according to the available space, the Raurava of Medhātithi, and the Ukthas ending with the Udvaṃśīya on the twelfth day.

(986) It is a Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra with the Ṣoḍaśin cup, in the world of Kautsa; the Udvaṃśīya is performed on these verses: "May the drops enter thee," "I think of that Agni who is a Vasu," "Awaken us today for our great [need]," and "The most beloved chariot"—on these Paṅkti verses is the Rāyovājīya Sandhisāman.
(987) The Pṛṣṭhya Ṣaḍaha is either contracted or expanded; however, it is indeed the expanded one. (991)

The Jyotiṣṭoma is an Atirātra with the Ṣoḍaśin cup. In the verses of Uśanas, the Vaiśvajyotis is the last; [the verses] beginning with "pra gāyata," "abodhy agniḥ samidhā janānām," "idam śreṣṭham jyotiṣām jyotir āgāt," and "abhāty agnir uṣasām anīkam"—in these Triṣṭubhs, the Auśana is the Sandhisāman. 992.

The six-verse hymn beginning with *babhrave nu svatavase* follows the *paryāsa*; the following [hymn] is the *āmahīyava*. Between the *āśu-bhārgava* and the *raurava-yaudhājaya*, there is the *maidhātitha* among its own verses, along with the *sapha* and *pauṣkala*. The rest is the same as that of the *rāthaṃtara* with the *pañcadaśa* stoma. The six-verse hymn beginning with *pra yad gāvo na bhūrṇayaḥ* follows the *paryāsa*; the following [hymn] is the *hāviṣmata*. The *svāra-sauparṇa* is between the *āyāsya* and the *dairghaśravasa*. [Recite] *tvam hy aṅga daivya pavasva*.

"devavītaye" is the *satrāsāhīya*; "śrudhye" is the same as the other [of that day], with its greatness (*barhas*) being fifteen-fold; by means of these two, there is an alternation up to the twelfth day. For the ninth day, "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" is the *gāyatra* and the *arkas* of Agni. For the tenth day, "yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" is the *gāyatra* and the *svāśiras* *arkas*. For the eleventh day, "abhi priyāṇi" is the *dīrghatamas* *arkas*. For the final [twelfth] day, the *utsedha* and *niṣedha* are the *dairghaśravasa* verses; the *ukthas* of that very day end with the *udvaṃśīya*. 993.

The Jyotiṣṭoma is an Atirātra without the Ṣoḍaśin cup; the Kāva [Sāman] is on the verses of Kaśyapa, with the Vasiṣṭha [Sāman] as the final one, beginning with "When he, the guardian of the people, was born, the watchful one... and ending with "These very Dawns have made their signal; Agni has been awakened; the Sun rises from the earth. Upon these Jagatī verses, the Kāva is the Sandhi-sāman.

In the *yamātirātra*s, there is the *kaṇvarathaṃtara* in the world of the *goṣṭoma* of Dairghaśravasa; the *bārhaduktha* [rathaṃtara] and the *dairghaśravasa* [sāman] in the world of the *gaurīvitamanuṣṭubh*; the *atirātra* with the *ṣoḍaśin* [stotra]. In the world of the *āyuṣṭoma* of Medhātithi, there is the *vārkajambha* with the *bṛhannidhana*; the *maidhātitha* and the *gaurīvitamanuṣṭubh* in the world of the *raurava*; the *saubhara* in the verses of Hāri-varṇa; the *atirātra* without the *ṣoḍaśin*. As the ten-night sacrifice (*daśarātra*) of the *abhijit* is, so is the *bṛhatī* in the *gaurīvitamanuṣṭubh*.

For Hārivarṇa, the *Ṣoḍaśin* Atirātra with the *Saubhara* is prescribed; the *Viśvajit* is prescribed; the *Sarvastoma*; the *Abhi somāsa āyavaḥ* [is the *Janitra*]; the *Raurava* on three verses, the *Bṛhannidhana* on one, the *Vārkajaṃbha* on one, the *Maidhātitha* on one, the *Yaudhājaya* on the middle verse, and the *Gaurīvita* on the *Anuṣṭubh*—this is the *Ṣoḍaśin* Atirātra. (9101) The ointments and unguents are prescribed. (9102) They are prescribed for the year, measured by the year, and include the sixty-one-night sacrifice. (9103)

The quarters of Savitṛ are fashioned by the *vidhṛtis*. One begins with the *trivṛt* stoma using the *rāthaṃtara* day; one reaches the *pañcadaśa* stoma with the *bārhatas*, the *saptadaśa* with the *rāthaṃtara*, and the *ekaviṃśa* with the *bārhatas*. Where there is an *agniṣṭoma*, the day is *bārhatas*; at midday, the *yauktāśva* [laud] is performed, and the *ārbhava* [laud] is *hāviṣmat*. He extracts the *arka* from among the *vidhṛtis*; the rest is the same as that which is fashioned up to the middle of the *pṛṣṭhya* period—up to the middle of the *pṛṣṭhya* period.
The *vivṛti*.
The Ninth Chapter: Sattras;
the twelve-night sacrificial session (dvādaśarātra-sattra).
Now, the sacrificial sessions (satras) have been described here in three Brāhmaṇas consisting of twenty-three chapters;
these [sessions] are [also treated] at the end of the Kalpa by means of the ninth and subsequent [chapters].

The author of the Sūtras has stated the time for initiation (*dīkṣā*) and so forth for those [sacrifices] by saying, "In all *satra*s, they should perform the initiation, purchase, pressing, and rising during the bright fortnight," and so on. But the *Nidāna* says: "Now, therefore, the *satra*s; of these, the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*) is the first," and so forth. Regarding that, relying upon the arrangement (*klpti*) of the twelve-day sacrifice as declared in the Brāhmaṇa, he states a specific rule:
"The two *atirātra*s of the twelve-day sacrifice are accompanied by the *ṣoḍaśin* cup. (1)

Thus it is said. That [sacrifice], being of two kinds—namely *vyūḍha* (expanded) and *samūḍha* (contracted)—is further divided into two types as *satra* (session) and *ahīna* (non-session), making four varieties in total. Among these, the *vyūḍha* form as a *satra* has been explained previously. Regarding the *ahīna* form, there are two positions: that it possesses the *gaurīvita* accent or that it possesses various (*nānā*) accents. Since the *gaurīvita* accent is possible, there is no distinction in the *Sāmakalpa*; however, the distinction regarding the *Karmakalpaka* has already been stated.

However, for the *nānāsvara* [sacrifice], the arrangement of the tones is like that of the *pauṇḍarīka*, the *vyūḍha-navarātra*, and so forth. Everything else follows the rule of the *ahīna* sacrifices, like the *satra*-type *vyūḍha-dvādaśāha*. Furthermore, since the *samūḍha-dvādaśāha* was not mentioned by the author of the ritual manual (*kalpakāra*), it must be inferred according to the established principle. In that regard, the arrangement of the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha* as a *samūḍha* is stated in the *gavām ayana*. The arrangement of the *chandomas* is stated in the *chandomavat-daśarātra*. For the first day of this [sacrifice], the verse begins with *pratnā*.

The *bahiṣpavamāna* consists of nine verses, because the application of the nine-day cycle (*navāha*) exists [here]. For the second day, the final [stotra] of the midday pressing is the *pārtha* hymn beginning with "vṛṣā śoṇaḥ. On the third day, there is no distinction. For the fourth day, the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses are "pavamāno ajījanat" and "punāno akramīd abhi," respectively. The *ājya* of the Hotṛ priest is "agnir vṛtrāṇi. The final [stotra] of the midday pressing is the *janitra* hymn beginning with "somaḥ pavate. The final [stotra] of the third pressing is the *lauśa* hymn beginning with "pra ta āśvinīḥ."

For the *pavamāna* of the fifth day, the *viśvajit*, the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses are "O Soma, [sing] the bright hymn" (*soma citram ukthyam*). The *ājya* of the Hotṛ is "O Agni, we meditate upon the hymn" (*agne stomam manāmahe*). The final verse of the midday pressing is concluded with "Indu, the prize-winner" (*indurvājī*). In the world of Pārtha, if there is the *tvaṣṭrīsāman*, the final *ārbhava* chant is the *lauśa* with the double repetition of "Flow on, finding cattle" (*govitpavasva*). For the sixth day, the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses are "The prize-winners have been let loose" (*asṛkṣata pra vājinaḥ*) and "This one, the ten fingers... (*etamu tyaṃ daśa kṣipaḥ*).

"O Agni, the mortal in battles..."—this is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ. "With this purification, purify these treasures..."—this is the final [stotra] of the Vasiṣṭhas at the midday pressing. "The light of the sacrifice..."—this is the final [stotra] of the Maruts at the third pressing. For the seventh day, "Those Soma-draughts which are in the distance... is the opening verse (*pratipad*). "O upholder of Truth, Vaiśvānara..."—this is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ. "Proclaiming wisdom like Uśanas..."—this is the final [stotra] of the Pārthas at the midday pressing. "He has gone forth..."—this is the final [stotra] of the Yajñasārathis at the third pressing.

The *Kaṇvarathantara* remains in its own place, because the arrangement of the *Soma-sāmans* is occasioned by the *jāmi*-defect, and here such a *jāmi*-defect exists; furthermore, the arrangement ending with the *svarasāman* is occasioned by the *ahīna* sacrifice, according to Ātreya, and thus the twelve-night rite (*dvādaśarātra*) is not a *satra*.

The performance [of the rite] is as follows: for the eighth day, the opening verse (*pratipad*) is "The rays impel the Sun" (*hinvanti sūram usrāḥ*). The *ājya* chant of the Hotṛ is "O Agni, with all thy fires" (*viśvebhir agne agnibhiḥ*). The final *mādhyaṃdina* chant belongs to the Vasiṣṭha family and begins with "Hither, indeed, the child" (*ūhu vāi śiśum*). The final *ārbhava* chant belongs to the Śārṅga family and begins with "Hāu, the sustainer" (*hāu dharta*). For the ninth day: the opening verse (*pratipad*) is "Near the born, the swift one" (*upoṣu jātam apturam*). The *ājya* chant of the Hotṛ is "Near thee, whose appearance is delightful" (*upa tvā raṇvasadṛśam*). For the *pṛṣṭha* stotra, the three-verse chants (*sāmatṛcas*) should be performed using the *arka* of Dīrghatamas and the *aiḍa* of Māṇḍava.

In the final section of the *sāman*-king, for the sake of favoring Dīrghatamas, the *arka* is prescribed; the final [verse] of the Vasiṣṭha family is "hāu uhu vāi akrān"; the final *yāma* of the Ārbhava [laud] belongs to Iḍā, beginning with "asāvi somo aruṣo vṛṣā hariḥ"; between the *utsedha* and *niṣedha* of the tenth day, there is the *maidhātitha*; the final [stotra] of the Mādhyandina [pavamāna] belongs to Uśanas, beginning with "ājāgṛviḥ"; the *rathantara* and *vāmadevya* [sāmans] are on their own verses; the *gaurīvitam* is on one verse, beginning with "paryū ṣu"; the *śyāvāśvam* is on one verse; and the *āndhīgavam* is on three verses.

Such is the arrangement of the *anuṣṭubh* verses. For, as he will state later, since the tenth day of the ten-day sacrifice (*daśarātra*) is extended by analogy (*atideśa*) from that which possesses the *chandoma* meters, one should not construct a *gaurīvita* based on what is employed in its similar [context]. Some, desiring the *gaurīvita* called *ājāgṛvi* to be the final [verse] of the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina*), do not desire a modification in the *anuṣṭubh*. That is incorrect; because even the construction of the *gaurīvita* at the midday pressing is prompted by adaptation (*ūha*), and because it would follow that the *auśana*, which is prompted by the whole collection, would be omitted.

And likewise, the *Nidāna* regarding the twelve-day sacrifice states: "The *yajñāyajñīya*, *gaurīvita*, *rathantara*, and *vāmadevya* [chants], when thus arranged, they call 'the arrangement of the Sāmans' (*sāmavyūha*). Thus, they conclude with the *chandomas* in the ten-night rite. It is said: "On the tenth day, one should collect the Sāmans. Therefore, the aforementioned arrangement of the *anuṣṭubh* verses must be performed. The *vājajit* [verse] beginning with "pari pra dhanva" takes the place of the *sauhaviṣa*. The final [verse] belongs to the *kāva* hymns and contains the word "sūrya. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.

All else is like the *vyūḍha* twelve-day sacrifice performed as a *sattra*. Thus, the *samūḍha* [twelve-day sacrifice] performed as a *sattra* has been described. For the *samūḍha* performed as an *ahīna*, the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha* should be performed according to the model of the seasonal *ṣaḍaha*. The *bahiṣpavamāna* for its first day is "The ancient song... (*pratnāmanvarkam*). As for the *chandomas*, they are to be modified exactly as they are in the ten-night sacrifice (*daśarātra*) that includes the *chandomas*; thus the rules for the twelve-day sacrifice have been stated.
Thus ends the twelve-night sacrificial session. ||1||
There are two sacrificial sessions (*sattra*) of thirteen nights each;

therein, first, regarding the two sessions of thirteen nights: an *atirātra*, a *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period, an *atirātra* consisting of all the *stomas*, four *chandomas*, and an *atirātra*—thus the first thirteen-night session has been stated by means of this recitation (*anuvāka*). Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
The sacrificial sessions (*satra*) consist of fourteen nights;
on the thirteenth night, in the place of the first *Chandoma*, namely the *Kaṇvarathantara*, the *Somasāman* is "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā" (O Soma, being purified, flow with your stream). || 1 ||

Thus [it is said]. For the first *chandoma* of the sixth day, because it is separated by an *atirātra* with all-stomas (*sarvastoma*), the *somasāman* is prescribed to avoid monotony (*jāmi*). Everything else is like the expanded twelve-day sacrifice (*vyūḍhadvādaśāha*) which has the nature of a *satra*. However, the *sarvastoma-atirātra* is mentioned as belonging to the [ordinary] sacrificial days (*ahīna*). Regarding its *satra*-type night: in the *satras*, at the *prāyaṇīya* and *udayanīya* *atirātras* where the *ṣoḍaśin* cup is neither enjoined nor prohibited, one may act according to one's desire as in the archetype (*prakṛti*).
But where an injunction or a prohibition exists, there those two serve for the purpose of restriction; such is the determination in the Sūtra. ||1||
Thus ends the first thirteen-night rite. || 2 ||

The second thirteen-night rite consists of an Atirātra, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra; thus the second thirteen-night rite is described. Regarding it, everything is like the expanded (vyūḍha) Dvādaśāha performed as a Satra. He states the distinction:
"In the Satras, the vow is that of the year-long [rite]. (1)
Thus [ends the first section]. || 1 ||
Thus ends the second thirteen-night rite. ||3||

There are fourteen-night sessions; indeed, there are three fourteen-night sessions. An *atirātra*, a *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period, a *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period, and an *atirātra* with the thirty-three-fold hymn as the opening—this is the first fourteen-night session according to the [relevant] section of the text. The two *pṛṣṭhya* periods proceed in direct and reverse order, combined as in the *Gavāmayana*. Regarding that, he states the specific rule for the first *pṛṣṭhya*:
"Where they enter the *pṛṣṭhya* after the *atirātra*, the *anurūpa* verse for this first day is *yatra vā trikakud rukmebhyaḥ*. (ŚB 12.2.3.2)

Thus [it is said]. The second triplet for the *bahiṣpavamāna* is appropriate: "Sing forth to him, O men; according to his ancient splendor, O sage, for you who are purifying"—this is the meaning of the *bahiṣpavamāna*. Because the *rāthantara* [sāman] is used for the *atirātra*, the *pṛṣṭhya*, and the first two days of the *trikadruka* sacrifice, the employment of this verse containing the word *pratna* ("ancient")—namely, "his ancient"—is for the sake of avoiding monotony (*ajāmi*). Since the previous thirteen-night sacrifice contains the application of nine days, it is established that the avoidance of monotony is achieved through the presence of both the "ancient" and the "new" verses.

And so says the Sūtra: "The *bahiṣpavamāna* [stotra] is like the *pratna* [hymn]; but beyond this, he says that this has the *pratna* as its *anurūpa* (corresponding verse). And it is observed even for the purpose of the tenth day in the case of a division. And because of the connection with the nine-day period. Here, even when the two days of the thirty-three-fold hymns meet, the absence of monotony (*ajāmitva*) has been explained in the Nidāna. Now, indeed, when these two thirty-three-fold days meet, by what means is there no monotony? One should either arrange the *kaṇvarathantara* because of the commonality of the day itself, or [place it] in the *ārbhava* [laud] of the preceding day, or in the midday [laud] of the succeeding day.
Thus ends the first fourteen-night rite. 4.

The second fourteen-night sacrifice consists of an Atirātra, the three-day sequence of Jyotis, Go, and Āyuḥ, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, and an Atirātra of Āyuḥ, Go, and Jyotis; thus the second fourteen-night sacrifice has been described. Regarding that, the ritual rule for the sacrificial sessions (satras) is as follows: "In those fourteen-night sessions where the three-day sequences of Jyotis, Go, and Āyuḥ occur, they are performed according to the one-day sacrifices, with the Gaurīvita and Svara chants."

Thus [it is said]. Here, the mention of "three-day" (*tryaha*) is for the purpose that this statement should apply only where the *jyotis*, *go*, and *āyus* are prescribed in that very arrangement—namely, as the *jyotir-gaur-āyus* three-day sacrifice—and so that it should not apply where they are arranged differently within another context, such as *jyotis-go-āyus*, *go-āyus*, *pañcāha*, and so forth. ||1||
For this very reason, regarding the injunction "The *Ayus*, the *Go*, and the *Jyotis* [sacrifices] are *Atirātras*," he says:
"These same [sacrifices], when repeated, are where the *Ayus*, the *Go*, and the *Jyotis* are *Atirātras*. (2)

Thus [it is said]. Here too, the mention of the *atirātra* is for the purpose of demonstrating the intended arrangement. Although here they proceed from the *atirātra* to the *rāthaṃtara*, and from the *rāthaṃtara* to the *jyotis*, nevertheless, after the *jyotis*, the verse "punaḥ soma dhāraya" (O Soma, flow again with your stream) and the *bṛhatī* verse beginning with "pratnavat" (as of old) are not a repetition (*ajāmi*). The six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*) is arranged as a *pṛṣṭhya* according to the model of the *gavāmayana*. For its first day, the verse "asya pratnāmanu dyutam" (according to his ancient splendor) serves as the *anurūpa* (corresponding verse), because it has been stated that [the sequence] begins with "yatra vā trikadrukebhyaḥ. || 2 ||
Thus ends the second fourteen-night rite. ||5||

The third fourteen-night sacrifice consists of an *atirātra*, the *go* and *āyus* two days, the ten days of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*), and an *atirātra*; thus the third fourteen-night sacrifice has been described. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
these same *go* and *āyus* days are used in other night-sessions (*rātrisatra*) except for those involving the *yamātirātra*.
And [the same applies] to those [penances] measured by a year. || 1 ||

"Thus. "These very [notes]" means that they are used in the *gaurīvita* accentuation of the one-day (*aikāhika*) sacrifice. Sacrifices lasting from thirteen nights up to a hundred nights are called *rātrisatra*s (night-sessions), because they are enjoined by the word "night" (*rātri*). Everything else is like the *vyūḍha-dvādaśāha* (the expanded twelve-day sacrifice). || 1 ||
Thus ends the third fourteen-night rite.

The fourteen-night rite is completed. Now follow the fifteen-night rites; there are four of them. The first fifteen-night rite consists of: an *atirātra*, a *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, a *mahāvrata*, a *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, and an *atirātra* beginning with the *trayastrimśa* stoma. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
The first fifteen-night rite is prescribed.

Thus: the two *pṛṣṭhya* six-day periods (*ṣaḍaha*) are combined in direct and reverse order, as in the *gavāmayana*. For the first day of the first six-day period, the *anurūpa* chant is "asya pratnām" (RV 8.47.18); this is the vow pertaining to the year-long sacrifice (*sāṃvatsarika-vrata*).
Thus ends the first fifteen-night rite.

The second fifteen-night sacrifice consists of an *atirātra*, a *trivṛt* *agniṣṭoma*, and the three-day sequence of *jyotis*, *go*, and *āyuḥ*; followed by a *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, and the *āyus*, *go*, and *jyotis* [again], concluding with an *atirātra*. Thus, there are two fifteen-night sacrifices; [along with] the ten-night sacrifice, these constitute the five sacrificial sessions (*satra*). Regarding the *subrahmaṇyā* formula, a specific distinction is stated: "After the *atirātra*, one [recitation] belongs to the *āgneyī* [day]; in the second fifteen-night sacrifice, there are two. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:

The second fifteen-night rite consists of an Atirātra, followed by an Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma in which the Agniṣṭoma-sāman is chanted on verses addressed to Vāyu. For this sacrifice, the Ājya-stotra of the Hotṛ is "Agnis pratnena janmanā" (RV 8.43.13), and the Gaurīvita-sāman is applied to an Anuṣṭubh verse.

Thus: for the sake of non-identity (*ajāmi*) between the two *rāthaṃtara* [sāmans] of the *atirātra* and the *agniṣṭoma*, the verse "Agni with the ancient... is prescribed. The *trikadruka* [stotras] are in direct order and repeated; they belong to the one-day sacrifices (*ekāha*) and possess the *gaurīvita* melody. The *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period is combined (*samūḍha*). For the first day of this [period], "The ancient, shining forth... is the *anurūpa* [verse]. || 1 ||
Thus ends the second fifteen-night rite. 8.

The third fifteen-night rite (*pañcadaśarātra*) is described by the section beginning with *trivṛd agniṣṭomo jyotir gaur āyuḥ* and ending with *dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ*. Prior to the *trikadruka* days, all *subrahmaṇyā* invocations are addressed to Agni, because of the rule stating that "all [invocations] prior to the *trikadrukās* are [for Agni] on the third day. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows: this same [procedure] applies to the subsequent [rites]; its own [specific] *ājya* chants are used. || 1 ||

In the subsequent nights, this third [night] of the fifteen-night period consists of the previously mentioned *trivṛd-agniṣṭut-agniṣṭoma*. Its *ājya* stotras are indeed those beginning with "O Agni, come hither" (*agna āyāhi*), because there is no first *atirātra* [in this sequence]; the meaning is that this avoids the fault of repetition (*jāmi*). ||1||
Thus ends the third fifteen-night rite. || 9 ||
The fourth [sacrificial session] is prescribed as fifteen nights, up to seventeen nights.

Thus: the *jyotis*, *go*, and *āyus* [sacrifices] are one-day (*aikāhika*) rites with the *gaurīvita* and *svarasāman* chants. The expanded (*vyūḍha*) twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*) includes the *atirātra*. The fourth fifteen-night rite (*pañcadaśarātra*) consists of an *atirātra*, the *jyotis*, *go*, and *āyus* three-day rite, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, and an *atirātra*. It is like the expanded twelve-day rite. The *jyotis*, *go*, and *āyus* are one-day rites with the *gaurīvita* and *svarasāman* chants. || 1 ||
Thus ends the fourth fifteen-night rite. 10.

The sixteen-night rite is described by the section beginning with "these very [days], together with the Mahāvrata. It consists of an Atirātra, the Jyotis, Go, and Āyu [one-day sacrifices], a three-day period, the ten days of the twelve-day rite (dvādaśāha), the Mahāvrata, and another Atirātra—thus making sixteen nights. The distinction from the previous sacrificial session (sattra) is that this is the vow lasting for a year.
Thus ends the sixteen-night rite.

The seventeen-night sacrifice consists of an Atirātra, a Jyotis, a Gauḥ, an Āyus, a Gauḥ, an Āyus, a Pañcāha, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, and an Atirātra; thus is the seventeen-night sacrifice described. Its ritual procedure is as follows:

in the seventeen-night sacrifice, there are four Ābhiplavika days with the Śyaita, Naudhasa, and Brahma-sāmans, and the Pauṣkala, Śrudhya, and Auṣṇiha-sāmans. For the first day, this is the *anurūpa* verse: *eṣa pratnaḥ*. 1.

Regarding the *satras*—specifically the "seventeen-night" (*saptadaśarātra*) sacrifice—it should be performed like the five-day *abhiplava* period of the *gavāmayana*, beginning with the *jyotis* day. Among these, the specific rule for the first four days has been stated as follows. For the first day: the triplet "eṣa pratnena janmanā" is the *anurūpa*. On this point, the *nidāna* states: "For the first day, 'eṣa pratnā' is the *anurūpa*; this is for the sake of non-repetition (*ajāmi*) and for the distinction between the *pṛṣṭhya* and *abhiplava* periods. The *naudhasa* is the *brahmasāman*; the *pauṣkala* is on the *uṣṇih* meter.

On the second day, the Śyaita is the Brahman-sāman; the Śrudhya is on the Uṣṇih verse. On the third day, the Naudhasa is the Brahman-sāman; the Pauṣkala is on the Uṣṇih verse. On the fourth day, the Śyaita is the Brahman-sāman; the Śrudhya is on the Auṣṇiha verse. In all cases, the Śyaita and Naudhasa are [performed] on their own respective verses, because of the statement: "But they recur on their own verses."
He states the specific feature of the fifth day:

there are two *savana*s of the fifth day; the third *savana* belongs to the sixth day. For that [third *savana*], the *brahmasāman* is the Naudhasa; on an *uṣṇih* verse, the Śrudhya. "We have chosen thee, the most worthy of sacrifice" (*yajiṣṭhaṃ tvā vavṛmahe*) is the Aitdhmavāha, the Traikakubha, and the Nārmedha. Or alternatively, the Aitdhmavāha is the Sauśravasa and the Māruta. 2.
Thus end the hymns.

There are two *savana*s of the *Āyuṣ* [Stoma]; the third *savana* of the fifth day belongs to the *Jyotis*. Its *brahmasāman* is the *naudhasa*; the *śrudhya* is on the *uṣṇih* [meter]. The *ukthas* are: "yajiṣṭhaṃ tvā vavṛmaha" (the *aidhmavāha*), the *traikakubha*, and the *nārmedha*. Or alternatively, the *aidhmavāha*, the *sauśravasa*, and the *māruta*. Regarding this, there is the *nidāna*: on the fifth day, one brings forward the third *savana* of the sixth day, in order to avoid the interruption of the six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*).

"That which is the *pañcama* [fifth day] is indeed the *stoma*, and that is the *saṃsthā*. Thus the five-day period (*pañcāha*) has been described. Everything else is like the expanded twelve-day sacrifice (*vyūḍha-dvādaśāha*). There are two *atirātras*, with or without the *ṣoḍaśin* cup.
Thus ends the seventeen-night rite. 11.

The eighteen-night sacrifice consists of an *atirātra*, an *abhiplava* six-day period, the ten days of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*), and an *atirātra*; thus the eighteen-night sacrifice has been described. In this sacrifice, they proceed from the *atirātra* to the *abhiplava*; for the first day, this is the *anurūpa* verse beginning with *eṣa pratnā*.

Or [it may be performed] for the Trikadrukās; where, in the Rātrisattras, there is the Abhiplava [ṣaḍaha], the Śyaita and Naudhasa as the Brahma-sāmans, the Pauṣkala, the Śrudhī, and the Auṣṇiha—[this applies] except in the case of those [sacrifices] measured by a year, and it is prescribed up to the twenty-night sacrifice.

Thus, for the first day of the *abhiplava* period, this is the *pratnānurūpa*. These two, the *naudhasa* and the *brahmasāman*, alternate; likewise the *pauṣkala* and the *śrudhya* in the *auṣṇiha* meters. Everything else is as in the *gavām ayana*.
Thus ends the eighteen-night rite. 12.

The nineteen-night sacrifice consists of these very [days] together with the Mahāvrata; by this Anuvāka beginning with "By these indeed Vāyu," the nineteen-night sacrifice has been described. It includes an Atirātra, an Abhiplava ṣaḍaha, and the sacrificial sessions (satrāṇi)—thus the twenty-night sacrifice.
The arrangement of the days for the twelve-day rite consists of ten days, the Mahāvrata, and the Atirātra; the specific distinction from the preceding [rite] is the annual vow.
Thus ends the nineteenth night. 13.

The twenty-night sacrifice consists of an *atirātra*, an *abhiplava* six-day period, the *abhijit* and *viśvajit* days, twelve days of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*), and an *atirātra*; thus it is twenty nights. The two *atirātras* have been described. For the *abhiplava*, the *sāmans* for the first day are the *aitana*, *audhasa*, *brahmasāman*, *pauṣkala*, *śrudhya*, and *auṣṇiha*; the distinction is that "this ancient one" (*eṣa pratna*) is the *anurūpa*.
In the twenty-night sacrifice, the Viśvajit and Abhijit, lasting one year each, are on both sides; as it is with the ten-night sacrifice, so it is with the Bṛhatī.

Thus it is said. For it was stated in the *Pūrvadaśarātra*: "For that *Abhijit*, [the Sāmans are] ‘punaḥ soma dhāraya’ on three verses, the *Abhīvarta* on three verses, the *Raurava* on one verse, the *Kaṇvarathantara* on one verse, the *Maidhātitha* on one verse, and the *Yaudhājaya* on three verses," and so forth. Here, because the sixth day of the *Abhiplava* and the *Abhijit* both consist of *Bṛhatī* verses, there would be a lack of variety (*jāmitā*); therefore, the *Kaṇvarathantara* is prescribed as an alternative for the midday pressing of the *Abhijit*. Everything else follows the procedure of the *Gavāmayana*. 1.
Thus [ends] the twenty-night [rite]. 14.

The first twenty-one-night period consists of an *atirātra*, an *abhiplava* six-day period, an *atirātra*, an *abhiplava* six-day period, an *abhiplava* six-day period, and an *atirātra*; thus the first twenty-one-night period has been described. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:

Of the preceding twenty-one-night sacrifice, there are two *atirātra*s without the *ṣoḍaśin* on both sides, while the one in the middle possesses the *ṣoḍaśin*. Alternatively, all may possess the *ṣoḍaśin*; indeed, all should possess the *ṣoḍaśin*.

Thus the distinction has been stated. The *abhiplava* periods consist of the *śyaita*, *naudhasa*, and *brahmasāman*, as well as the *pauṣkala*, *śrudhya*, and *auṣṇiha* chants, in the first two *abhiplavas*. This [chant] is the *anurūpa* for the first day. According to the opinion of some, the final *abhiplava* is in direct order (*anuloma*); according to others, it is in reverse order (*pratiloma*). Regarding this, it is said: "In the previous twenty-one-night period, Śaucivṛkṣi held that the third *abhiplava* was in direct order, for no reversal is known [therein]. Śāṇḍilya held it to be in reverse order, because of the statement that there are two *abhiplavas*. (1)
Thus ends the first twenty-one-night period. 15.
Then follows another twenty-one-night period:
an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, three Svarasāman days, a Divākīrtya day,
three Svarasāman days, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, and an Atirātra beginning with the Trayastriṃśa stoma.
Thus ends the subsequent twenty-one-night rite. Its ritual procedure is as follows:
for the subsequent twenty-one-night rite, the days are arranged according to the pattern of the year.
Regarding the sacrificial sessions (*satrāṇi*): there is one lasting twenty-two nights. Concerning that, he states the specific rule:
"The *pṛṣṭhya* [ṣaḍaha] consists of the *anuklṛpta*, the *abhīvarta*, and the *kāleya*. (2)

Thus [it is said]. All the *bṛhatī* verses of the *pṛṣṭhya* [ṣaḍaha] should be performed according to the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*), and not according to the year-long rite (*saṃvatsara*); this is the meaning. He states the specific rule for the *svarasāmans*:
"The *śyaita*, *naudhasa*, and *brahmasāman* are the *svarasāmans*; the *paupkala*, *śrudhya*, and *auṣṇiha* [are the others]. (3)
Thus [ends the third section].
He states the distinction for the equinox (viṣuvat):
at the world of the equinox, which consists of three Sāman verses, is the Ābhīśava; "śrāyanta iva sūryam" is the Vikarṇa. || 4 ||
The rest is the same.
Thus [ends the fifth].
Thus ends the twenty-first night of the Uttarā. 16.
When the twenty-one nights have been completed.

The twenty-two-night sacrifice consists of an Atirātra, the Jyotis, Go, and Āyus [Sāmans], the three-day Abhiplava Ṣaḍaha, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra; thus it is the twenty-two-night sacrifice. Its ritual procedure (kalpa) is as follows:
it is prepared up to the Sadas sessions. || 1 ||

Thus: the two *atirātras* belong to the *sātrika* [series]; the *trikadrukāḥ* belong to the *aikāhika* [series]; the *gaurīvita-svara* is the *abhiplava*; the *śyaita* and *naudhasa* are the *brahmasāman*. The *pauṣkala*, *śrudhya*, and *auṣṇiha* [are the *stotras*] of the first day; this is the *pratnānurūpa* of the first day, because it is stated that they proceed from the *atirātra* to the *abhiplava*, or because it is said "from the *trikadrukāḥ*. Everything else belongs to the [ritual] of the twelve-year cycle (*sāṃvatsarika*). || 1 ||
Thus [ends] the twenty-two-night [rite]. 17.

The twenty-three-night sacrifice consists of an *atirātra*, a *jyotis* day, a *go* day, an *āyus* day, another *go* day, another *āyus* day, a five-day *abhiplava*, a six-day period, the ten days of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*), and an *atirātra*; thus it is the twenty-three-night sacrifice. The seventeen-night sacrifice should be performed with a five-day period as in the [preceding] five-day [sacrifice]. Everything else is to be performed as before.
Thus [ends] the twenty-three-night [rite].
The first twenty-four nights are the *saṃsat* sacrifice called *āmayana*, consisting of days from the first through the seventh.

Now, regarding that twenty-four-night rite: there is an *atirātra*, the *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period with its *stomas*, and the thirty-third day which is *anirukta* (unspecified); this is established in the framework of the *upahavya*. For that, the *kaṇvarathantara* is used at the midday pressing. Then follows the thirty-third day which is *nirukta* (specified), two *triṇava* days, two *ekaviṃśa* days, a *triṇava* day, and the thirty-third day which is *nirukta*; then the thirty-third day which is *anirukta*, the *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period with its *stomas* in reverse order, a *trivṛt* day which is *anirukta*, a *jyotiṣṭoma-agniṣṭoma*, and an *atirātra*.
By this section [of the Veda], the twenty-four-night sacrifice known as the *saṃsad* has been described. Regarding this, the ritual manual (*kalpa*) states:
"The *saṃsad* consists of an *atirātra*, followed by a six-day period with the *pṛṣṭhya-stoma*. (1)

Thus [it is said]. The plural number in "of the assemblies" (*saṃsadām*) is due to the nights being the subject. The *atirātra* is the first day; then follows the six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*) of the *pṛṣṭhya-stoma*, which has not been mentioned in the section on the *anahīna*. ||1||

Regarding this, he states the specific rule: "For the first day, this [chant] has the *pratnānurūpa* and the *gaurīvita* on the *anuṣṭubh* meters every day; the *satra*s are unmodified—the eighth day is the fourth day. For the fifth day, in the world of Ākūpāra, there is the *tvāṣṭrīsāman*, which is a double *anutoda*. (2) The meaning is that the fourth day is unmodified; thus, the *gaurīvita* should not be performed in place of the *nānada*. The thirty-third day is the *anirukta* (unexpressed), established in the ritual procedure (*tantra*) of the *upahavya*. It has been stated that its *kaṇvarathantara* occurs at the midday libation (*mādhyandina*). (2)
Thus end the days from the first to the seventh. 18.
The eighth day:

regarding the eighth day, [the verses are] "Flow on, O Indu, as a bull, being pressed," "These drops have been let loose," and "And our prayer that wins cattle, O heroes. Or, "O men, toward us, like chariots resounding, the sons [of the gods] have let loose our songs; the drops have been let loose. "On the path of thee, the purifying one, we [follow]; of thee, the purifying one, O sage... 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
Their own *ājya* verses. ||2||

Thus [it is said]. Because of the statement, "It is prescribed in the ritual procedure (*tantra*) of the Upahavya," the word *svāni* means "those belonging to the Upahavya. The *ājya* offerings are: "The immortal god, the Hotṛ," "O great Heaven and Earth," "This one of yours," "Thou art united," "The cows lowed," and "We two have entered the pit. ||2||

"Pavamānasya jighnataḥ"—this is the Gāyatra, the Cāmahīyava, the Aiḍa, the Sauparṇa, the Rohitakūlīya, and the Santani; "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā"—this is the Samanta, the Kaṇvarathantara, the Dairghaśravasa, the Bārhaduktha, and the Yaudhājaya as the final [Sāman]. || 3 ||
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
"Sākamukṣa" is the final [stotra] of the Mādhyandina [Pavamāna] belonging to the Pārtha [śākhā]. 3.
One's own backsides. ||4||
"Mā bhema mā śramiṣma" is the Bṛhat; "svāsu" is the Vāmadevya; and "imā u tvā purūvaso" and "yasyāyaṃ viśva āryaḥ" are the Śyaita and Kāleya respectively—these are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras. 4.

With "Pavamāno ajījanat," one should perform the *jarābodhīya* and the *sauśravasa*, both set to the *gāyatrī* meter; the *uṣṇih* and *kakubh* meters are used for their respective [verses]. With "Abhī no vājasātamam," one should perform the *gaurīvita* and the *kārtayaśa*, and the *śyāvāśva* and *āndhīgava*. The final [laud] is the *kāva* with the verse beginning "Añjate. 5.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. 6.

All the hymns consist of thirty-three verses. Here, because the Upahavya [sacrifice] has seventeen verses and this day has thirty-three, the insertion (*āvāpa*) is made in its proper place within the *pavamāna* chants of the Upahavya-type sacrifices.

Regarding the sacrificial sessions (*satra*): the ninth day of the twenty-four-night session is arranged exactly like the Upahavya; all else is likewise prepared. Thus, the days that lead to the completion of the hymn-recitations (*viṣṭuti*) are to be repeated. 6.
Thus ends the eighth day of the twenty-four-night sacrifice. || 16 ||
The ninth day of the twenty-four-night rite;
now he recites the explicit [Nirukta] hymn for the thirty-third day:
