"Sing forth to him, O men! To him who has been born, the swift one, for the sake of the tawny one who possesses his own power—these Soma juices flow toward the beloved one. Purifying himself, Soma flows; of you, O Sage, who are being purified... (RV 9.61.1–2).
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
The *ājya* offerings are [performed] with the verse beginning "O Agni, come hither" (*agna āyāhi*).

"Forward, O Soma-stones, for the wise one"—this is the Gāyatra, the Aśva, the Soma-sāman, the Āśu, the Bhārgava, and the Mārgīyava. "Forward, O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—this is the Pajra, the Dvaigata, the Pauruhanmana, the Hārāyaṇa, the Yaudhājaya, the Auśana, and the final [sāman]. || 3 ||
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Naudhasa, and the Kāleya. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

With the verses "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" [SV 2.1–3], the *gāyatra-saṃhita* and the *kākṣīvata* and *bhāsa* [are performed]. With "pavasvendram accha" [SV 2.4–6], the *sapha* and the *akṣāra* [are performed]. With "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ" [SV 2.7–9], the *gaurīvita*, the *padanidhana*, the *śuddhāśuddhīya*, the *audala-gautama*, the *kāva*, and the final [hymn] [are performed]. 5.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. 6.
The entire [chapter] on the Thirty-three [Devas]. || 6 ||
Thus ends the ninth day of the twenty-four-night sacrifice. || 20 ||
On the tenth day of the twenty-four-night sacrifice, it is said that there is a Triṇava-stoma day.

[The verses] beginning with "This indeed is the bull-chariot, this is the steed urged by men" (RV 9.86.1–6) are placed before the Paryāsa hymn, following the six-verse section beginning with "yauktāśva. The *surūpa* and *carṣabha* hymns, as well as the *pāvamāna*, precede the two *āyāsya* hymns; these are the *pṛṣṭha* and *kaulmalabarhiṣa*. The final [hymn] is the *pārtha* hymn beginning with "vṛṣā śoṇaḥ. 1.
"Flow on with this stream, being pressed, for the feast of the gods"—this [verse] is at Śaṅkusujñāna, north of Gaurīvita, or at Yadvāhiṣṭhīya-āsita.
Regarding the sacrificial sessions (*satrāṇi*): in the twenty-four-night session, the twelfth day is the same as the second day of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*). || 3 ||
Thus [ends section] 3.
Thus ends the tenth day. || 21 ||
The eleventh day:

now follow two days consisting of the twenty-one-fold stoma. Of these, he prescribes for the first the four-verse hymn beginning with "ut te śuṣmāso asthuḥ" as the *paryāsa* (concluding verse). Now, this very third day is arranged in triplets (*tr̥ca*) and possesses the twenty-one-fold stoma.

"Thus," [it is said]. "This very thing" means the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*). Since the third day of the twelve-day rite consists of seventeen verses, it is stated that the arrangement of triplets (*tṛca*) is made for the purpose of bringing about its twenty-one-fold nature. Consequently, all four Sāmans—the Paurumadga and the others—must be performed upon a triplet in the *bṛhatī* meter; thus, the *adhyāsyā* verses are omitted. Likewise, we learn from the *āṣkāra-nidhana* of the Kāṇva school that in the sacrificial sessions (*satra*), the Vācaḥsāman and the Śaukta Sāman must be performed upon a triplet in the *ārbhava* laud. || 1 ||
Thus ends the eleventh day. 22.
The days from the twelfth up to the fourteenth are [as previously established]; thereafter, beginning with the twenty-first day, he describes the arrangement of three days:
"The subsequent three-day period is well-known. (1)

Thus: the twenty-one-fold, the twenty-seven-fold, and the thirty-three-fold—this three-day period is well-known; the twelve-day period is indeed established [as standard]. The meaning is that there is no distinction whatsoever therein. This aforementioned six-day period is called the "Broad Pṛṣṭhya. And so says the *Nidāna*: "This [six-day period] has its stomas reversed in the first three days and their stomas in natural order in the latter [three]; they call this the 'Broad Pṛṣṭhya'. Fourteen days have been arranged. It has been stated that the thirty-three-fold day is "unexpressed" (*anirukta*).
The days from the twelfth to the fourteenth [are the *pūrṇāhuti*s]. ||23||
Regarding the fifteenth day, he says:
"Now, he brings this very thirty-third day, which is unexpressed. || 1 ||
The meaning is that this very [hymn], beginning with "pavasvendo vṛṣā sutaḥ," is designated as the eighth immediately following [the previous one]. He states its specific details:
in the place of that Kaṇvarathantara, there is the Vāśa for the Pārtha; the Bṛhat for the Auśana; the Rathantara for the Śyaita; the Naudhasa for the Śrudhya; and the Pauṣkala [for the same]. || 2 ||
Thus [ends the second section].
Thus ends the fifteenth day. 24.

Regarding the six-day period consisting of the Pṛṣṭhya Stomas, which begins with the sixteen-fold chant and ends with the twenty-one-fold chant, and which is said to be directed westward (*pratyaṅ*), he speaks of that six-day period:
"The six-day period consists of the Pṛṣṭhya Stomas," thus it is repeated. || 1 ||
Thus [ends the first section].
Thus end the days beginning with sixteen and ending with twenty-one. || 25 ||
The twenty-second day:
regarding the twenty-second day, it is said—the day is threefold and its nature is undefined.

Its [Sāman] is: "Flow on, O Indu, as a bull when pressed; and [grant] our prayer that wins cattle, O heroes, for him who exerts himself. Or: "O sons, [listen] to our songs; O sage, to you, the purifying one... (1).
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
The *satra*s—first, the twenty-four-night sacrifice:

for the *pavamāna* chant of the slayer, the *gāyatra* is on one verse; the *āmahīyava* on one verse; the *aiḍa sauparṇa* on one verse; the *yaudhājaya* with "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā" on three verses; and the *gaurīvita* in the world of Śyāvāśva. || 1 ||
The rest is the same as the Upahavya sacrifice.
Everything is threefold. ||3||

Thus: at the Bahiṣpavamāna, the first and last [stotriya] triplets consist of three verses each, while the others consist of single verses; in the other two Pavamānas, only the last [stotriya] consists of a triplet.
Thus ends the twenty-second day. 26.
The twenty-third day:
regarding the twenty-third day, he says—the Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma; its [metre] is the Anuṣṭubh, just as that of the Ṛṣabha.

Thus: "Just as in the case of the Ṛṣabha-kratu, [the verses] 'purojitī vo andhasaḥ' are used—one Gaurīvita on one verse, one Āndhīgava on one verse, one Śyāvāśva on one verse, and the Bṛhat on three verses"—the meaning is that it is the same for this [sacrifice] as well. || 1 ||
Thus ends the twenty-third day. || 27 ||

On the twenty-fourth day, the Bṛhat-sāman is performed in the Anuṣṭubh metre for the sake of the following day, because that day is a Jyotir-atirātra; this is done to avoid monotony (ajāmi). He states that very point:
it is a Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra. Everything else is the same.
Thus [ends the first section]. || 1 ||
Thus ends the twenty-fourth day. 28.
Thus ends the preceding twenty-four-night rite.
The second twenty-four-night sacrifice consists of the sacrificial sessions (satras) beginning with twenty-five nights and ending with thirty-two nights;
it includes an Atirātra, two Abhiplava six-day periods, the ten days of the twelve-day rite (dvādaśāha), and an Atirātra. Thus is the second twenty-four-night sacrifice.
It is prepared for various *brahmasāman* chants. ||1||

Thus [it is said]. The *śyaita* and *naudhasa* are the *brahmasāman*s of the two *abhiplava*s; the *pauṣkala*, *śrudhya*, and *auṣṇiha* belong to the first day of the first *abhiplava*. Regarding this, there is a *sūtra*: "Gautama says that because of the injunction for the year-long sacrifice (*saṃvatsara*), the repetition of the *abhiplava*s in the *rātrisatra*s should be exactly like that. The meaning of this is: since the *abhiplava* is prescribed in the *gavāmayana*, and because the *rātrisatra*s have that as their archetype (*prakṛti*), the repetition [of the *abhiplava*s] is like the repetition of the *gavāmayana*.

And thereafter, as far as possible, in the second and subsequent *abhiplava* periods, on the second day at the midday pressing (*mādhyandina*), the *yauktāśva* hymn takes the place of the *hāviṣmat*; however, in the *viṣuvat* sacrifice of the *sattra* for Bharga and Yaśas, the arrangement is as stated in the Sūtra. In other cases, there is simply an option. At the Ārbhava pressing, the *hāviṣmat* takes the place of the *maukṣa*. On the fourth day, the *vīṅkaśuddha* and *aśuddhīya* are also explained by [the rules for] Bharga and Yaśas.

On the fifth day, in the place of the *yaṇva*, there is the *apatya*, the *santani*, and the *śākvaravarṇa* according to the sequence beginning with the second *abhiplava*. In that context, when the *santani* is to be sung by the village-singers (*grāmegeya*), then the *vāmra* should be performed before the *mānava* for the sake of avoiding monotony (*ājāmyārtha*). On the sixth day, following immediately after the *pṛṣya*, comes the *āśvasūkta*. In place of the two [verses] beginning with *triṇi dhanā*, there are the *iṣaḥ satrāṇi* in their respective order—the twenty-four-night rite (*caturviṃśatirātra*) and the subsequent longer one (*vṛdhīyasamanta*); this is the distinction. The ten-day period and the *atirātra* have been described.

"These very [rites] are accompanied by the Mahāvrata," thus it is for twenty-five nights. The vow lasting one year is the distinction from the previous [rite]. Its location is the same as that of the [rite] lasting one year.

An Atirātra, the Go and Āyus two days, two Abhiplava Ṣaḍahas, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, and an Atirātra—this constitutes the twenty-six-night sacrifice (*ṣaḍviṃśatirātra*). The Go and Āyus are one-day sacrifices (*aikāhika*) with the Gaurīvita-svara. The two Abhiplavas have the Śyaita and Naudhasa as their *brahmasāman*, and the Pauṣkala, Śrudhya, and Auṣṇiha [as their other sāmans]. The Dvādaśāha is arranged in its expanded form (*vyūḍha*). The two Atirātras have been described.

The *saptaviṃśatirātra* consists of an *atirātra*, two six-day periods (*ṣaḍaha*) each containing the *jyotis*, *go*, and *āyuṣ* days as the *abhilava* forms, the ten days of the twelve-day period (*dvādaśāha*), and an *atirātra*. The *jyotis* and other [days] are those used for one-day sacrifices (*aikāhika*), following the *gaurīvita-svara* pattern. The two *abhilavas* are as previously described. For the first day of the first *abhilava*, this is the *pratnānurūpa*; the rest is according to the expanded twelve-day period (*vyūḍha-dvādaśāha*).

These very [rites], together with the Mahāvrata, constitute the annual vow (*sāṃvatsarika-vrata*) performed for twenty-eight nights prior to the Udayanīya Atirātra; this is the distinction from the previous [rite].

The *ekānnatriṃśadrātra* (twenty-nine-night rite) consists of: an *atirātra*, a *jyotis*, a *gauḥ*, an *āyus*, a *gauḥ*, an *āyus*, two *pañcāhas*, two *ṣaḍahas*, the ten days of the *dvādaśāha*, and an *atirātra*. Regarding the *saptadaśarātra-sad-abhiplava*, he says: the *abhiplavas* are as before; this [rite] should not be performed as the *pratnā*; the others are like the *vyūḍha-dvādaśāha*.

An Atirātra, three Abhiplava six-day periods, ten days of the twelve-day rite (dvādaśāha), and an Atirātra—this constitutes a thirty-night sacrifice. The Abhiplavas have the Śyaita, Naudhasa, and Brahma-sāmans, as well as the Pauṣkala, Śrudhya, and Auṣṇiha. For the first day of the first Abhiplava, this is the *anurūpa* verse beginning with "eṣa pratnānu"; the rest has been explained.
"These very [rites] are accompanied by the Mahāvrata," thus it is for thirty-one nights; the one-year vow is the distinction from the previous [rite].

The Atirātra, the Go- and Āyus-days (two days), three Abhiplava six-day periods, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, and the Atirātra—this constitutes the thirty-two-night sacrifice. The Go- and Āyus-days are one-day rites with the Gaurīvita-sāman as the chant. The Abhiplavas have the Śyaita, Naudhasa, and Brahma-sāmans, as well as the Pauṣkala, Śrudhya, and Auṣṇiha-sāmans. The others are like those of the expanded twelve-day rite.
Thus end the sacrificial sessions (satra) lasting from twenty-five nights up to thirty-two nights. || 29 ||
Thus ends the subsequent twenty-four-night period.

The first *trayastriṃśadrātra* consists of the days beginning with the first and ending with the sixteenth; then there are three *trayastriṃśadrātras*: three *atirātras*, five five-day periods (*pañcāhas*), one *viśvajit-ati-rātra*, another five five-day periods, the ten days of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*), and an *atirātra*. This is the first *trayastriṃśadrātra*. These nights are said to have various *brahmasāmans*, because the five five-day periods possess various *brahmasāmans*. Thus he says:
The Atirātra with various Brahman-sāmans, three Pañcāhas, and the Pañcāha-kḷptas. ||1||

Thus: "Those with various *brahmasāmans*"; following the *atirātra*, three five-day periods (*pañcāha*) are prescribed for the seventeen-night sacrifice (*saptadaśarātra*) by means of the five-day period. || 1 ||
The Sattras—the first is the thirty-three-night sacrifice; therein the distinction is that there are various *Brahmasāmans*. 2.
Thus [ends the second section].
In the first five-day period, the Bṛhat and Rathantara [Sāmans] are used according to the light.

Thus: "according to the world" means according to their respective positions. This has been stated here in such a manner for the sake of clear demonstration, because it will be explained later by reversing this order. ||3||
The Naudhasa, the Śyaita, the Mahāviṣṭambha, the Traiśoka, and the Vāśa with the refrain "And may he hear both"—these are the Brahman-sāmans. 4.
Thus: for the first five-day period, the Naudhasa and other [stotras] are, in sequence, the Brahmasāmans. || 4 ||

For the second five-day period, the *loka* and *bṛhadrathantara* [stotras] are for each other. "O Indra, in the onsets" (*tvam indra pratūrtiṣu*) is the *abhīvarta*. "Thee indeed, O hero, for help" (*tvām id dhyo naraḥ*) is the *mānava*, which is used when there is a *pṛṣṭhya* [stoma]. On the fifth day, the *chandasya* [is used]. "Who knows him when the juice is pressed? (*ka īm veda sute sacā*) is the *āṣkāraṇidhana* of the *kāṇva* [school]. "In his own [verses], he has yoked the ladle" (*svāsu yukta-srucam*). "In his own [verses], the *śrāyantīya* [is used]. These are the *brahmasāmans*. 5.

Thus [it is said]. "The world of one another" means that it attains [the other], such is the ellipsis. For it is heard in scripture: "That which is the world of the *rathantara* is attained by the *bṛhat*, and that of the *bṛhat* by the *rathantara*. Here, the mutual attainment of the worlds of the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* is for the sake of non-identity (*ājāmyārtham*). "That which is prescribed for the *pṛṣṭhya*" means that which is ordained for the *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period; "that which follows is the *mānava*" is the meaning.

Now, if on this second day the *uttara-mānava* is prescribed as the *brahmasāman*, then there would be the undesirable consequence (*prasaṅga*) of the *mānava* being displaced to the *pavamāna-stotra* on the fifth day; therefore, it is said: "The *chandasīya* [is used] on the fifth day. This means the previous *mānava*. Those *sāmans* which have been assigned to the *jyotiṣṭoma* and the *atirātra* are called *chandasya* because they are other than those [specifically mentioned].

And likewise, the *nidāna* regarding the *prāyaṇīya* and the *caturviṃśa* [stomas] states: "Now, indeed, as for those sacrificial rites (*yajñakratu*) which follow after the *jyotiṣṭoma* and the ten-day period (*daśāha*), in them there occurs the introduction of the materials (*dravya*) belonging both to the *jyotiṣṭomas* and to the ten-day periods. Endowed with *stomas*, endowed with positions (*sthāna*), endowed with *pṛṣṭhas*, endowed with ritual frameworks (*tantra*), endowed with portions (*bhāga*), and endowed with terminuses (*saṃsthā*), they proceed according to their forms and according to the rules of the Vedic meters (*chandas*), accompanied by prayers for blessings (*āśis*)."

And in the *tri-kakub-daśarātra*, there are various *madhyenidhana* [chants], not those belonging to the ten-night sacrifice (*daśarātrika*). They experience the *madhyenidhana* [chants]; therefore, one employs those that belong to the Vedic meters (*chandas*). ||5||

On the third five-day period, the *Bṛhat* and *Rathantara* [Sāmans] are used according to the light [of the day]. The *Mānava* [Sāman], beginning with "śagdhyūṣu śacīpate," is always [used] on the fifth day; the *Vāsiṣṭha*, beginning with "vayamenamidāhya"; and the *Bhāradvāja*, beginning with "ā tvā sahasramā śatam. The *Janitra* [Sāman], beginning with "yo rājā carṣaṇīnām," and the *Indrasya Yaśaḥ*, beginning with "tvamindra yaśā asi"—these are the *Brahmasāmans*. 6.

Thus, because it is prescribed that "on the fifth day [the *chandasya* hymn] belongs to Mānava" on the second day, and since there is no possibility of its being displaced, the meaning is that the subsequent *mānava* hymn alone remains as the obligatory one for the fifth day. ||6||
Thus end the days from the first to the sixteenth.

The sacrificial sessions (*satrāṇi*): first, the thirty-three-night session; the seventeenth day is the *viśvajit*; the final day is the *atirātra*. In the world of Gaurīviti, there is the *nānada*. "Agni is the head of heaven, the summit" (*agnirmūrdhā divaḥ kakud*) is the *satrāsāhīya*, the *traikakubha*, the *nārmedha*, the *gaurīvita*, and the *ṣoḍaśisāman*. 5.1.
The night is the junction. || 1 ||

Thus [it is said]. This specific description of the Viśvajit performed annually is as follows: this day occupies the position of the Viṣuvat. Here, because of the conjunction of the Rathantara Sāman—belonging to the last day of the third Pañcāha—with the Vaiśvajita Pavamāna-stotra set in the Bṛhatī metre, the resulting monotony (*jāmitva*) is avoided by means of the Gāyatrī verse beginning with *pratna*, which is likewise situated there. ||1||
Thus ends the seventeenth day.
[31] Now follow the days from the eighteenth to the twenty-second; this is the same five-day period repeated in reverse order. [1]

The meaning is that [the sequence] should be performed in reverse order, beginning from the fifth day. Its repetitive nature has been established in the *Nidāna*: "The last five-day period becomes repeated," which is explained as "not being non-repeated. This refers to the twenty-one-night sacrifice mentioned previously. ||1||

For the *āvṛtta* five-day period, the *loka* is for each other [day], the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* [sāmans]; "Drink of the pressed, flavorful [juice]" (*pibā sutasya rasina*) is that of Jamadagni; "When, O Indra, eastward, westward, northward" (*yad indra prāgapāg udak*) is the *naipātitha*; "With the exhilarating bay steeds, O Indra" (*ā mandrair indra haribhiḥ*) is the *abhinidhana* of Kaṇva; "As a wild bull [goes] to the unreleased [water]" (*yathā gaura apākṛtam*) is the *manādya* of Gautama; "Thou indeed, O friend, hast praised" (*tvam aṅga praśaṃsiṣam*) is the *paurumīḍha*. These are the *brahmasāmans*. 2.

Thus: here, in place of the *rathantara* of the first *sat* of the fifth day, there is the *bṛhat*; and in place of the *bṛhat* of the second *sat* of the fourth day, there is the *rathantara*. Such is the alternation. 2.
Thus are the days from the eighteenth up to the twenty-second. 32.
The days from the twenty-third up to the thirty-third constitute the twelve-day rite (dvādaśāha), and the final day is the Atirātra. || 1 ||
Thus; the meaning is "like the expanded twelve-day sacrifice" (vyūḍha-dvādaśāha). || 1 ||
Thus end the days from the twenty-third up to the thirty-third.
Thus ends the first month consisting of thirty-three nights.

The middle thirty-three-night period consists of: an Atirātra, an Abhiplava six-day period, an Atirātra, an Abhiplava six-day period, an Atirātra, an Abhiplava six-day period, the ten days of the twelve-day rite (dvādaśāha), the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra. The Abhiplavas have the Śyaita, Naudhasa, and Brahma-sāmans; the Pauṣkala, Śrudhya, and Auṣṇiha-sāmans. For all of them, on the first day, this is the *anurūpa* verse beginning with "eṣa pratnā."
In the middle [set] of thirty-three nights, all the Atirātras are accompanied by the Ṣoḍaśin cup. || 1 ||
Thus is the distinction. || 1 ||
Thus ends the second thirty-three-night period. || 34 ||
The sacrificial sessions (*satrāṇi*): the third is a thirty-three-night rite; the thirty-three-night rite is the third;
[then] three five-day periods, a *viśvajit* *atirātra*, three five-day periods, and an *atirātra*—this is the final thirty-three-night rite. Its ritual procedure (*kalpa*) is as follows:
for the final thirty-three-night rite, there is an *atirātra*; then three five-day periods arranged according to the five-day pattern. ||1||
Thus [it is said]. He states its specific detail:
"The Śyaita, Naudhasa, and Brahma-sāmans, as well as the Bṛhat and Rathantara, are according to the world [usage]. (2)
Thus; the sense here is that because various *brahmasāman*s are heard [to be prescribed].
He states another alternative: "Or as in the case of various Brahman-sāmans. (3)

Thus, the meaning is that this is according to the opinion of one who holds the view that "this five-day rite is indeed the same as that which was taught in the first *Trayastriṃśa*. And so says the *Nidāna*: "But for him who might think, 'This is that very same five-day rite,' for him it is likewise the *Bṛhat* and *Rathantara*, and likewise the *Brahmasāmans*. (3)
The Viśvajit sacrifice has been arranged for those [cases] where there are various Brahman-sāmans. || 4 ||
Thus; here too, the seventeenth day stands in the place of the equinox. ||4||
Now, these same five-day periods are performed in reverse order. || 5 ||

Thus it is said. In this regard, the proponents of the prima facie view (pūrvapakṣa) maintain that there are five days; if they are like the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* [sāmans] as found in common worldly practice, then even when reversed they remain so; and if they are unlike the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* as found in common worldly practice, then these too are exactly the same—such is the established rule.

For the first day of the first five-day period among the recurring five-day periods, the *mānava* [sāman] "abhi somāsa āyavaḥ" is performed on one verse; the *anūpa* [sāman] is on that same verse; the *bṛhannidhana vārkajambha* [sāman] is on one verse; the *maidhātitha* [sāman] is on one verse; the *vāmra* [sāman] is on three verses; and the *triṇidhana* of Agni is on the *adhyāsya* [verse]. || 6 ||
The rest is the same.

Thus [it is said]. Here, since there would be *jāmi* (repetition/defect) upon the conjunction of the *vaiśvajita* *rāthantara* [sāman] on the former wing with the first day of the five-day periods on the latter wing—which has become the first by means of the *rāthantara* day—the *vārkajaṃbha* [sāman] with the *bṛhat* finale is prescribed to avoid that. This being established, the performance of that same [sāman] with the *mānava* finale both before and after the one possessing the [original] finale is improper precisely because of the risk of *jāmi*; therefore, it [the *mānava*] follows immediately after the *anūpa*.

This is a construction for the sake of establishing the *stoma*. For the purpose of achieving the *stoma*, there is the formation of a single verse (*ekarca*) from the *āgantu* [verse] of Medhātithi and the others. According to the principle that "of the four, two are in the first [verse], and the other two are in the subsequent ones," the sequence—where the *mānava* [verse] is in one [verse], and in that very same [verse] the *anūpama* and so forth—is to be understood. In the *vāma* and *āgneya* [sections], it is exactly as before.

The *tṛca* and the *adhyāsya* being established [as the subject], an objection is raised: since the five-day rite (*pañcāha*) has the *abhiplava* as its archetype, according to the principle stated in the rule "In the night-sessions (*rātrisatra*), because of the instruction for the year," the *santani* chants are performed on the fifth day of the third five-day period of the first half of the year. Consequently, on this day—which is the first day of the repeated cycle—there would be a collision (*jāmi*) between the *santani* and the *māna* chants, both of which possess the *nidhana*. As it has been said: "Of the repeated five-day periods, regarding the first day of the first five-day period..."

Regarding the *satras*: in the thirty-four-night sacrifice, there is the rule that "the *mānava* and others [should be] in the *bṛhatī*; it would be a repetition (*tajjāmi*) if [they were] in the *saṃtani*. It cannot be said here that on the fifth day, the day which is to be sung in the *grāma* [style] should be the *saṃtani*, and that the *vāmra* should come first. For indeed, when the *vāmra*, *mānava*, *ānūpa*, *vārka*, and *jambha* have been performed as single-verse hymns (*ekarca*) as before, the *maidhātitha* would have to be performed on a three-verse hymn (*tṛca*). And the performance of an adventitious [hymn] on a *tṛca* is never observed anywhere.

In that case, because they are modified forms (*vaikṛta*), the repetition (*abhyāsa*) that occurs in the case of the year-long sacrifice does not apply to those five-day periods (*pañcāha*). Rather, by virtue of the authority of the first [day] alone, one should not extend the *abhiplava* days; such repetition belongs to the year-long sacrifice. As it has been said: "But due to their being modified forms, there is cessation; one should not extend the *abhiplavas* in the five-day periods."

And here, according to worldly custom, since both wings possess the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* [sāmans], there would be a repetition (*jāmi*) because the first and last days of the two wings—the first day of the five-day period and the final day—possess the *rathantara*. To avoid this, on the first day of the preceding wing, this *pratna-anurūpa* should be performed; on the first day of the five-day period in the subsequent wing, which is a recurring day, the *vārka-jambha* should be performed as before.

As it has been said: "This [chant] is on the *pratnā* [verse], while the *vārkajaṃbha* is on the *pratipad*; just as the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* [sāmans] are on the two sides of the world, so this *pratnā* is on the first fortnight (*pūrvapakṣa*) and the *vārkajaṃbha* is on the latter. (7)
Thus ends the third [section], consisting of thirty-three nights. 35.

The thirty-four-night sacrifice consists of an Atirātra, the Jyotis, Go, and Āyu three-day periods, three Abhiplava six-day periods, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra; thus it is the thirty-four-night sacrifice.
It is prepared up to the *vidhṛti*s. || 1 ||

Thus: the two Atirātras are those of the Sātrika; the Trikadrukas are those of the Aikāhika; the Gaurīvita-svaras; the Abhiplavas have the Śyaita, Naudhasa, and Brahma-sāmans, as well as the Pauṣkala, Śrudhya, and Auṣṇiha. The specific distinction for the first day of the first Abhiplava is that its *anurūpa* is "eṣa pratna" (RV 8.64.4). Everything else follows the pattern of the year-long sacrifice (*sāṃvatsarika*). || 1 ||
Thus ends the thirty-four-night rite. 36.

The thirty-five-night rite consists of an *atirātra*, a *jyotis* day, a *go* day, an *āyus* day, a *go* day, an *āyus* day, five five-day periods (*pañcāha*), three six-day periods (*abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*), the ten days of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*), and an *atirātra*. This is according to the section [of the Sūtra]; the thirty-five-night rite is like the seventeen-night rite. The five-day *abhiplava* is as previously described; this [five-day period] should not be performed as the "ancient" one. The rest has been stated. Thus ends the thirty-five-night rite.
The thirty-six-night rite is described by the following section:

an *atirātra*, four six-day periods (*ṣaḍaha*) consisting of *abhiplava* days, the ten days of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*), and an *atirātra*. For the first day of the first *abhiplava*, this is the *anurūpa* verse: "This ancient... The *abhiplavas* have the *śyaita* and *naudhasa* as their *brahmasāmans*; the *pauṣkala*, *śrudhya*, and *auṣṇiha* [are used]. The rest is according to the annual cycle.
Thus ends the thirty-six-night rite.
The sacrificial sessions (*satra*)—the forty-night session and the thirty-seven-night session;
these same [sessions] include the *mahāvrata*, thus [there is] the thirty-seven-night session. The annual vow (*sāṃvatsarikaṃ vrataṃ*) is the distinction from the previous sacrificial session.
Thus [ends] the thirty-seven-night [rite].

The thirty-eight-night sacrifice consists of an *atirātra*, the *go* and *āyus* days (two *ahan*s), four *abhiplava* six-day periods, the ten days of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*), and an *atirātra*; thus the thirty-eight-night sacrifice is described. The *go* and *āyus* are one-day rites (*aikāhika*) performed with the *gaurīvita* chant. The *abhiplavas* have the *śyaita*, *naudhasa*, and *brahmasāman* chants, as well as the *pauṣkala*, *śrudhya*, and *auṣṇiha* chants. The twelve-day rite is in its expanded form (*vyūḍha*). The two *atirātras* are those belonging to the *sātrika* [twelve-day] rite.
Thus ends the forty-eight-night rite.

The forty-nine-night sacrifice consists of an Atirātra, the Jyotis-Gau-Āyu three-day period, four six-day periods (Abhiplavas), the ten days of the twelve-day rite (Dvādaśāha), and an Atirātra; thus it is the forty-nine-night sacrifice. Everything regarding it has been explained.
Thus ends the forty-nine-night rite.

For forty nights, these same [rites] are performed together with the Mahāvrata; thus it is for forty nights. This is the annual vow (*sāṃvatsarika-vrata*). There is the penultimate day. Everything else is as before.
Thus [ends] the forty-night [rite].
The first [period] consists of forty-nine nights,
beginning with the Prāyaṇīya Atirātra.

Now, there is a forty-nine-night sacrifice consisting of seven parts: an *atirātra*, three *trivṛt* days beginning with an *agniṣṭoma*, an *atirātra*, ten *pañcadaśa* *ukthya* days, a tenth day with a *ṣoḍaśin*, an *atirātra*, twelve *saptadaśa* *ukthya* days, an *atirātra*, a *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*), an *atirātra*, and twelve *ekaviṃśa* *ukthya* days followed by an *atirātra*. This is the twenty-nine-night sacrifice known as the *vidhṛti*. Regarding its opening *atirātra* (*prāyaṇīya-atirātra*), he states the specific rule:

The *vidhṛtis* consist of the *jyotiṣṭoma* *atirātra* without the *ṣoḍaśin* cup, performed in the world of Kautsa; the *udvaṃśīya* chant is performed upon these verses: "ā tvā viśantvindavaḥ," "jarābodha tadviviḍḍhi," "pratiṣyā sūnarī jani," and "eṣo uṣā apūrvyā"—these being in the *gāyatrī* meter; this is the *jarābodhīya* *sandhisāman*.

Thus [it is said]. The plural number in *vidhṛtīnām* (of the *vidhṛtis*) refers to the multiplicity of nights, as in the case of the *saṃsad* and other [terms]. Regarding this, the *Nidāna* states: "If the *sandhi-sāman* were the *aiḍa*, then the *udvaṃśīya* would belong to Kautsa; by this, one who desires the *iḍā* succeeds, as does one who follows the *ajāmi*-rule. Thus, because these [verses], beginning with *ā tvā viśantvindavaḥ*, are seen in the modification (*vikṛti*) of these nights—or because of the prescription of the *adhyardheḍā* in place of the word *nityāsu*—one who desires the *iḍā* [should perform them].

Regarding the *satra* sacrifices: the three-day periods are accomplished through their inherent nature (*svāratvāt*), as is the *ajāmilaka* arrangement. Others maintain that the *udvaṃśīya* chant should be performed only upon these [verses] beginning with "indra suteṣu. As it is said: "Or [it may be] on the obligatory verses (*nityāsu*)," they deliberate thus: "The *udvaṃśīya* is performed for a specific purpose; what would be the point of inserting it into the obligatory verses? Accordingly, in the Sūtras, we study the *udvaṃśīya* on both of the *ṛc*-triplets beginning with "ā tvendra suteṣu."

In accordance with the Brāhmaṇa passage beginning "The Jarābodhīya [is to be sung] on Gāyatrīs," the Sandhi-sāman is prescribed for the Gāyatrī verses. For the very purpose of indicating that this is its source, the meter is mentioned as "Gāyatrīs" in the Kalpa-sūtra. The same should be understood regarding the Uṣṇih verses, such as in the case of the Śrudhya-sāman and others. || 1 ||
Thus concludes the Prāyaṇīya Atirātra. || 38 ||

There are three *trivṛt* days. Of these, the first is one concluded with the *agniṣṭoma* form, and two are concluded with the *uktha* form; thus there are three *trivṛt* days. Regarding their first day, he says:
"Now, that which belongs to Kusurubinda, the *trivṛt* day connected with the *rathantara* [sāman], that is this very one. Of that—
The Gaurīvita [Sāman] is in the Anuṣṭubh [meter]. || 1 ||

Thus: the *bahiṣpavamāna* consists of the [verses] beginning with *upa drava pavasva*. The *ājya* hymns consist of [the verses] beginning with *agna ā no mitrāvaruṇā* and *indrāgnī*. The *sāmatṛcas* consist of the *gāyatra*, the *āmahīyava*, and the *jarābodhīya*, beginning with *uccā te jātam andhasaḥ*. The *yaudhājaya* is on three verses, beginning with *punānaḥ soma dhārayā*; the *auśana* is the final one. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras consist of the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *naudhasa*, and the *kāleya*. The *gāyatrasaṃhitā* begins with *svādiṣṭhayā*.

"Flow onward with this [hymn], seeking the gods," "The beloved, golden-hued one flows,"—these two are for the *sapha* and *pauṣkala* chants. "With your juice, victorious from of old"—this is for the *gaurīvita* and *andhīgava* chants. The final [verse] belongs to Kavaṣa; it remains the final [verse] in the triplet. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. Everything is in the *trivṛt* (nine-versed) arrangement. || 1 ||
The second [day] is a Trivṛt Ahargaṇa; that which is Bārhatam Trivṛt is the subsequent one. ||2||
Thus [it is said]. [The rule applies] specifically to Kusurubinda. || 2 ||
Regarding this, he states the specific details:

"O Sage, of thee who purifiest" (*pavamānasya te kave*) is the *paryāsa*. In the world of Yauktāśva, there is the *kāleya* of Mādhucchandasa for Hāviṣmanta; the *maukṣa* for Hāviṣmanta; the *gaurīvitam* in the *anuṣṭubh* meter; and the *sākamaśva*, *saubhara*, and *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* as the *ukthas*. || 3 ||
The rest is the same.

Thus: "Flow on, flow on through speech; flow on, O Indu," and "O Sage, of you who are being purified"—these are the Bahiṣpavamāna stotras. "Agni, the messenger," and so forth are the Ājya stotras. "Flow on as a bull, in your stream," and "The Gāyatra, rich in oblation, has come hither" are the verses.

The *satra*s—beginning with the *atirātra*—consist of *sāman*s set upon triplets (*tṛca*s). "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā" is the *triṇidhana* *āyāsya* on three verses; "vṛṣā śoṇaḥ" is the final *pārtha*. The *pṛṣṭha* *sāmans* are the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *kāleya*. "Yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" is the *gāyatra* on the *aukṣa* verse; "pavasvendramaccha" is the *satrāsāhīya* on the *śrudhya* verse; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ" is the *gaurīvitakrauñca*; "vṛṣā matīnām" is the final *yāma*. With the exception of the *yāma*s, these are [performed] on single verses (*ekarca*).
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*; the *sākamaśva*, *saubhara*, and *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* are the *uktha* chants.
By stating that "the arrangement of the first Trivṛt is the same as that of the third," he extends the rule; therein he states the specific distinction:
"That which was the former is the latter. For that [third], the *pramahiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, the *udvaṃśīya*, and the *tairaścya* are the *uktha* hymns.
Thus are the three days consisting of the *trivṛt* stoma. || 38 ||
The Atirātra follows after the Trivṛt;

he prescribes the Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra with the Ṣoḍaśin cup. [It is performed] upon these verses: "In the world of Kautsa," "The Udvaṃśīya," and "Into thee may the drops enter. Upon these Uṣṇih verses: "O Agni, of the booty consisting of cattle," "O Dawn, bring that wondrous wealth," and "O Aśvins, come to our dwelling"—[these constitute] the Śrudhya Saṃdhi-sāman. Thus [it is said]. 1.
Thus ends the Atirātra sacrifice. || 39 ||
There are ten fifteen-fold *ukthya* days;
he recites the first of the ten fifteen-fold [days]—namely, that which is Kusurubinda’s *rāthaṃtara* fifteen-fold day. Of that...
The Gaurīvita [is chanted] in the Anuṣṭubh meter. || 1 ||

Thus: "Sing for him, O men, with a flash of lightning; these drops of Soma have been poured forth; the King is approached with hymns; O Sage, you are the purifying one"—this is the *Bahiṣpavamāna*. "O Agni, come to us; O Mitra; O Indra and Agni"—these are the *Ājya* hymns. "High is the birth of your juice"—this is the *Gāyatra* and the *Cāmahīyava*. "Being purified, O Soma, in your stream"—this is the *Raurava* and the *Yaudhājaya*. The *Auśana* is the last. The *Pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *Rathantara*, the *Vāmadevya*, the *Naudhasa*, and the *Kāleya*.

The *gāyatra-saṃhita* consists of "svādiṣṭhayā" and "ayā pavasva devayuḥ"; the *sapha-pauṣkala* consists of "pavate haryato hariḥ"; the *gaurīvitāndhīgava* consists of "purojitī vo andhasaḥ"; the last is the *kāva*. The *uṣṇih* and *kakubh* meters, the *gaurīvita*, and the single verses [are used]. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *pramam̐hiṣṭhīya*, *hārivarṇa*, and *tairaścya* are the *uktha*s. Everything is fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*). || 1 ||

The *satra*s—there are fifteen *ukthya*s. He says that the second [day] has the fifteen-fold [stoma]; that which is the Bārhata fifteen-fold is the latter. "Of thee, O sage, as thou purifiest" (*pavamānasya te kave*) is the *paryāsa* in the domain of Mādhucchandasa; the Kāleya [sāman] is in the *anuṣṭubh* meter of Gaurīvita. || 2 ||

Thus: "Flow on with speech; flow on, O Soma, as a bull, for you are indeed a bull"—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant, using the verses beginning with "Of you, the purifying one, O sage. The *ājya* chants are those beginning with "Agni, the messenger. The *gāyatra* and *hāviṣmat* chants are those beginning with "Flow on as a bull, in your stream. The *āyāsya* chant is that beginning with "Being purified, O Soma, in your stream. The final *pārtha* chant is that beginning with "The red bull. The *pṛṣṭha* chants are the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *kāleya*. The *gāyatra* chant used at the *ukṣa* (sprinkling) is that beginning with "That exhilaration of yours which is most excellent."

"Flow on, go to Indra"—this is the *Satrāsāhīya* for the sake of hearing; "This Pūṣan, this wealth, this Bhaga"—these are the *Gaurīvita* and the *Krauñca*. "The bull of prayers"—this is the final *Yāma*. The *Kakubh*, the *Uṣṇih*, the *Gaurīvita*, and the single-verse hymns [are used]. The *Yajñāyajñīya* is the *Agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *Sākamaśva*, the *Saubhara*, and the *Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* are the *Uktha* chants. Everything is fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*). He states that the subsequent [days] are fifteenfold: by means of these very [chants], there is a reversal up to the tenth day.

Thus: with the *rāthaṃtara* [sāman] on the fifteen-fold [stoma], the third [day]; with the *bārhatasāman*, the fourth; and so on by alternation until the tenth day, which is equal to the fifteen-fold [stoma]. This is the arrangement. 3.
Regarding that, he states the distinction for the tenth day: on the tenth day, the *nārmedha* belongs to the world of Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra; "pratyasmai pipīṣate" is the *nānada*, the *ṣoḍaśin* chant. 4.

Thus [it is said]. This day is established as having the *ṣoḍaśin* [stotra]. Having prescribed the state of being an *ukthya*, it is because of the statement: "The tenth [day] possesses the *ṣoḍaśin*. On this day, among the *anuṣṭubh* verses, there is the [verse] beginning with "nānadat" (RV 10.94.1). ||4||
Thus there are ten fifteen-versed Ukthya sacrifices. || 40 ||
The *uttara* is an *atirātra*.
Regarding the *atirātra* following the fifteen-fold [stomas], he says:
"The *jyotiṣṭoma* is an *atirātra* provided with the *ṣoḍaśin* cup, not otherwise arranged. (1)
Thus; here, with reference to the *saṃdhi-sāman*, it is stated in the Śruti: "The *Rathantara* [is sung] upon the *Bṛhatī* verses."
Thus ends the Atirātra of the second day. 41.
There are twelve Ukthya days with seventeen stomas;
regarding the first day among those with seventeen stomas, he says:

"Now, that which was Kusurubinda’s Rathantara-day consisting of seventeen stomas, this very one is it. For that [day], in the world of Medhātithi, there is the Bṛhat-sāman with the Vārkañjabha nidhana; the Raurava-sāman belongs to Medhātithi; the Saṃhita-sāman belongs to Agni Arka; and the Gaurīvita-sāman is in the Anuṣṭubh metre. (1)

The *satra* sacrifices consist of seventeen *ukthya* rites. [The stotras are performed with the following verses: "Sing forth to him, O men, with a flashing luster"; "These drops have been poured out"; "Thee, who art bearing manly powers"—[these are] for the *bahispavamāna*, [using] "O Sage" as the refrain for the *pavamāna*.

The *ājya* stotras are: "O Agni, come for the feast" (*agna ā yāhi vītaye*); the *gāyatra* and *cāmahīyava* chants with the verse "High is the birth of thy juice" (*uccā te jātamandhasaḥ*); and the *dvihiṃkāra*, *vārkajambha*, *yaudhājaya*, and the final *auśana* chant with the verse "Toward us, O Soma, the living ones" (*abhi somāsa āyavaḥ*). There is a *dvihiṃkāra* on the first [verse], and the *yaudhājaya* on the middle [verse]. The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are: the *rathantara* and *vāmadevya*; the *bṛhannidhana*, *maidhātitha*, *naudhasa*, and *kāleya*. The *svādiṣṭhayā* chant is combined with the *gāyatra*.

"Pavasva indram accha" and "sapha-pauṣkala" [are the stotras]. "Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" and "gaurīvita-andhīgava" [are the stotras]; the last belongs to Kava. The "sapha-pauṣkala" [is formed] from two single verses. The "yajñāyajñīya" is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. The "pramahiṣṭhīya," "hārivarṇa," and "tairaścya" are the Ukthas. Everything is seventeenfold (saptadaśa).

Lest there be a lack of variety (*jāmitā*) due to the conjunction of this *rathantara* day with the preceding *jyotiṣṭoma-ati-rātra* which has the *rathantara-saṃdhi*, the *vārka-jambha* is prescribed for the midday pressing. And by virtue of that, the *maidhātitha* belongs to the *raurava*. However, because the two *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* *rauravas* were used in the previous *jyotiṣṭoma-ati-rātra* where the *saubhara* was the *brahmasāman* of the *ukthas*, there is no lack of variety.
He states the seventeenth [stoma] as the second:

that which is the Bārhata seventeen is the uttara. "Pavamānasya te kave" is the paryāsa. The Kāleya is in the world of Mādhucchandasa; the Svāśira is the mark of the Arkas; the Gaurīvita is in the Anuṣṭubh. ||2||

Thus: "Flow on as the leader of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the bull, pressed; O Soma, the bull, your powers rise up; of you, the purifying sage"—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "Agni, the messenger"—these are the *ājya* hymns. "Flow on as a bull, in your stream"—this is both the *gāyatra* and the *hāviṣmat*. "Pour out the pressed juice all around"—this is both the *samanta* and the *dairghaśravasa*, belonging to Ayāsya. "The red bull"—this is the final *pārtha*. The *bṛhatī* is composed of the *śaśakarṇa*.

The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *kāleya*. The *gāyatra* [sāman] for the *aukṣa* [stotra] is "yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"; the *satrāsāhīya* for the *śrudhya* is "pavasvendramaccha"; the *gaurīvita* and the *krauñca* are for "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"; the final *yāma* is "vṛṣā matīnām". The *kakubh* and *uṣṇih* are each single-verse [stotriyas]. The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *uktha* stotras are the *sākamaśva*, the *saubhara*, and the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*. Everything is seventeenfold (*saptadaśa*). 2.
He speaks of another seventeen [verses]:

"By means of these very [verses], one extracts the reversal from the twelve-day rite, or the *arkajambha* from the subsequent [rites], or the *maidhātitha* and *raurava* according to the tradition. (3)

Regarding the sacrificial sessions (*satrāṇi*)—the *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period: in the third and subsequent days up to the seventeenth, because the preceding day consists of *bṛhatī* verses, there is an absence of monotony (*jāmi*); therefore, the *vārka-jambha* [chant] is to be omitted. Consequently, the *maidhātitha* and *raurava* [chants] are to be placed in their respective positions. In that regard, this is the arrangement for the *bṛhatī*: "The Soma-drops, the Āyus... (with two *hiṃkāras*), and the *maidhātitha*, as well as the *raurava* and *yaudhājaya*. The rest is the same. || 3 ||
He states the specific feature of the twelfth day:
"On the twelfth day, the Ukthas end with the Udvaṃśīya."
Thus [ends the fourth].
Thus there are twelve Ukthya sacrifices, each consisting of seventeen [stotras]. ||42||

The Atirātra follows after the Saptadaśas; he speaks of the Atirātra as the Jyotiṣṭoma accompanied by the Ṣoḍaśin. The Udvamśīya is the world of Kautsa. [One should recite] "May the drops enter thee," and these [verses]: "I think of that Agni who is the Vasu," "Awaken him today with great oblation," and "The most beloved chariot."
In these *paṅkti* verses, the *rāyovājīya* is the *saṃdhi-sāman*.
Thus, in this way, there are twenty-nine days consisting of the Uktha-stomas. ||1||
Thus ends the Atirātra sacrifice. ||43||
The Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha;
the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha is either arranged in the condensed form (samūḍha) or the expanded form (vyūḍha). It is indeed the condensed form that is used.

Thus [ends the section]. This text has been explained in the context of the six-day seasonal sacrifice (*ṛtu-ṣaḍaha*). Regarding this first day, some maintain that the *anurūpa* verse is "pratna" (ancient); we, however, say no. For the absence of monotony (*ajāmitā*) is already established by the *saubhara* chant performed during the preceding *atirātra*. || 1 ||
Thus ends the Pṛṣṭhya Ṣaḍaha. ||44||
Regarding the Atirātra following the Pṛṣṭhya, he says:

"The Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra with the Ṣoḍaśin [cup]; the Vaiśvajyotiṣa [Sāman] is the last among the Auśanasa Ṛks, that which begins 'pragāyata'. In these Triṣṭubh verses—"abodhy agniḥ samidhā janānām," "idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotir āgāt," and "abhīty agnir uṣasām anīkam"—the Auśana Saṃdhi-sāman is [performed]. (1) Thus, for the purpose of not displacing the Auśanasas, the Vaiśvajyotiṣa has been prescribed in their place. (1)
Thus ends the Atirātra. ||45||
There are twelve Ukthya-stotras consisting of twenty-one verses each.
Regarding these twelve sets of twenty-one, he states the first:

"For Babhru, who is self-strong" (*babhrave nu svatavase*)—this six-verse hymn is placed before the *paryāsa*; after the *āmahīyava* follows the *āśubhārgava*; between the *raurava* and the *yaudhājaya* is the *maidhātitha*; and within its own [verses] are the *sapha* and *pauṣkala*.
The rest is the same as that of this very [chant] with the *rathantara* [sāman] and the fifteenfold [stoma]. ||2||

Thus: "Sing forth for him, O men, with a flashing luster; these drops of Soma have been poured out; the King goes by means of the sacrifices; indeed, for the tawny one who possesses his own strength—O Sage, of you, the purifying one. This is the *bahispavamāna*. "O Agni, come hither for the feast"—these are the *ājya* hymns. "High is the birth of your plant"—this is the *gāyatra* and the *cāmahīyava*.

The *satra* sacrifices consist of the twenty-one-versed *ukthya* chants, the *cāśubhārgava*, and the following: the *raurava* with "punaḥ soma dhārayā," the *maidhātitha*, the *yaudhājaya*, and the *auśana* as the final; the *pṛṣṭha* chants are the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *naudhasa*, and the *kāleya*; the *gāyatrasaṃhita* is with "svādiṣṭhayā"; the *saphapauṣkala* is with "pavasvendram accha"; the *gaurīvitāndhīgava* is with "purojitī vaḥ"; the *kāva* is the final; and the *agniṣṭomasāman* is the *yajñāyajñīya*.
The *pramahiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *tairaścya* are the *ukthas*; everything is the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*).

He states the second [hymn], the twenty-first: "prayadgāvo na bhūrṇayaḥ" (1.84), a six-verse hymn placed before the *paryāsa*; following the *hāviṣmat* [hymn] is the *svāra-sauparṇa*, with the *dairghaśravasa* inserted within the *āyāsya*; and "tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya pavasva devavītaye" (9.65) is the *satrāsāhīya-śrudhya*. 3.
The rest is the same as that of this very [chant] with the fifteenfold Bṛhatī. || 4 ||

Thus: "Flow on with speech; flow on, O Indu; Soma, you are a bull, for you are indeed a bull," like eager cows setting forth—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant for the Seer (*kavi*). "Agni, the messenger"—these are the *ājya* chants. "Flow on as a bull, O stream"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *hāviṣmat*, the *svāra*, and the *sauparṇa*. "Being purified, O Soma, in a stream"—this is the *aiḍa*, the *āyāsya*, the *dairghaśravasa*, and the *triṇidhana āyāsya*. "The red bull"—this is the final *pārtha*.

The *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *kāleya*. The *gāyatra* [sāman] on the *aukṣa* [verse] is "yaste mado vareṇyaḥ. The *satrāsāhīya* on the *śrudhya* [verse] is "tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya pavasva devavītaye. The *gaurīvita* and the *krauñca* are on the verse "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ. The final *yāma* [sāman] is on the verse "vṛṣā matīnām. The *agniṣṭomasāman* is the *yajñāyajñīya*. The *uktha* stotras are the *sākamaśva*, the *saubhara*, and the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*. Everything is seventeenfold (*saptadaśa*). 4.
He states that the [days] beginning with the third up to the twenty-first are as follows:
"By means of these very two, there is a reversal from the twelfth day. (5)
Thus it is said. Regarding that, he states the specific details for the ninth day and others:

for the ninth day, the *gāyatra* hymn "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" and the *arka* of Agni; for the tenth day, the *gāyatra* hymn "yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" and the *arka* of Svāśira; for the eleventh day, the *arka* of Dīrghatamas beginning with "abhi priyāṇi"; and for the twelfth day, the final [hymn] "antarotsedhaniṣedhau," which belongs to Dairghaśravasa.
On that very day, the Ukthas end with the Udvamśīya.

The forty-ninth night is the second *satra*. On the ninth day, in place of the *saṃhita*, there is the *arka* of Agni; on the tenth day, in place of the *maukṣa*, there is the *svāśira-arka*; on the eleventh day, there is the *arka* of Dīrghatamas, son of Kavasa; on the twelfth day, in place of the two *āyāsya*s, there are the *utsedha* and *niṣedha* and the *u dvaṃśīya* of Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra. The rest is the same. || 7 ||
Thus, there are twelve Ukthya sacrifices, each consisting of twenty-one stotras.

Regarding the *udayanīya-atirātra*, he says: "The *jyotiṣṭoma* is an *atirātra* without the *ṣoḍaśin* cup. The *kāva* [sāman] is upon the *ṛks* of Vasiṣṭha; the last is 'When this one has shouted' (*yad eṣa prakrośaḥ*). 'The guardian of the people, the watchful, has been born; these have made the banner of that Dawn; Agni has been awakened; the Sun rises from the earth'—upon these *jagatī* verses is the *kāva* *saṃdhi-sāman*. (1)
Thus; here too, lest there be a transference of the Kāvasa, the arrangement for the Vāsiṣṭhas is made in its place. || 47 ||

The second [sacrificial session] lasts forty-nine nights: two *atirātras* called *yamātirātras*, two *abhiplava* six-day periods, the *go* and *āyu* [one-day sacrifices], two more *abhiplava* six-day periods, the *abhijit* and *viśvajit* [one-day sacrifices], two *atirātras*, one *abhiplava* six-day period, the *sarvastoma* [one-day sacrifice], nine seventeen-fold stomas, two *atirātras*, the ten days of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*), the *mahāvrata*, and an *atirātra*. Thus the *yamātirātras* have been described. There are also the *prāyaṇīya* and *udayanīya* *atirātras*, which may or may not include the *ṣoḍaśin* cup.

This [verse] is the *pratnānurūpa* for the first day of the *abhiplava* period; in that context, the *go* and *āyus* [stotras] are those belonging to the one-day sacrifice (*aikāhika*). For it has been stated that these same *go* and *āyus* stotras occur in night-sessions (*rātrasatra*) other than the *yamātirātra*s and those measured by the year-long sessions (*sāṃvatsarasaṃmita*).
Regarding that, he states the specific details of the Goṣṭoma:

for the Goṣṭoma, there is the Kaṇvarathantara in the world of Dīrghaśravas; the Dairghaśravasa [Sāman] belongs to Bṛhaduktha; the Gaurīvita is in the Anuṣṭubh meter; and the Atirātra is without the Ṣoḍaśin cup. || 1 ||

Thus, because the sixth day of the *ābhiplavika* period and the *go* [sāman] are both composed in the *bṛhatī* meter, the *kaṇvarathaṃtara* is arranged for the sake of avoiding monotony (*ājāmya*). || 1 ||

He states the specific details of the Āyuṣṭoma: In the world of the Āyuṣṭoma of Medhātithi, there is the Bṛhat- nidhana Vārkajaṃbha; the Raurava of Medhātithi is the Gaurīvita on an Anuṣṭubh verse; the Hārivarṇa is the Saubhara on Ṛk verses; and it is an Atirātra without the Ṣoḍaśin cup. ||2||

Thus, because the *saṃdhi* and the *āyuḥ* stotras connected with the *goṣṭoma* belong to the *rathantara* [sāman], the *vārkajaṃbha* is prescribed for the sake of avoiding *ajāmi* (repetition) precisely in the *āyuḥ* [stotra] of the *pṛṣṭhya-saṃdhi* which belongs to the *rathantara*. Furthermore, for the sake of avoiding *ajāmi*, the *saubhara* is ordained in its verses (*ṛk*) in place of the *hārivaṇa*. For it is heard in scripture: "If one should perform the *saubhara* with the *rathantara*-sāman, there will be freedom from *ajāmi*. || 2 ||
Regarding the forty-nine-night *satra*, he states the specific feature of the second *abhijit* *atirātra*:

"As the ten-night [sacrifice] is for the *abhijit*, so is the *bṛhatī* [stoma], the *gaurīvita* [sāman] upon the *anuṣṭubh* verses, and the *saubhara* upon the *hārivarṇa* verses; it is an *atirātra* accompanied by the *ṣoḍaśin* cup. (3)

Thus [it is said]. Here too, there is an arrangement for the Kaṇvarathantara and Saubhara chants for the sake of avoiding sameness (ajāmi). Regarding the Viśvajit and the Sarvastoma sacrifices, he states the arrangement:
"The Viśvajit is already arranged."
The Sarvastoma is prescribed. || 5 ||

Thus [it is said]. These two are established in the section on the one-day sacrifices (*ekāha*). Of those two, the night belongs to the *sattras*. He states the specific rule for the nine-seventeen-fold (*navasaptadaśa*) *atirātra*:

"For the nine-seventeen-fold [stoma], 'The Soma-drops, moving toward men' (*abhi somāsa āyavaḥ*): the *janitra* [sāman] is performed in three verses; the *raurava* with the *bṛhat* finale is in one verse; the *vārka-jambha* is in one verse; the *maidhātitha* is in one verse; the *yaudhājaya* is in the *adhyāsya*; the *gaurīvita* is in the *anuṣṭubh*. This *atirātra* is without the *ṣoḍaśin* cup. (6)

Thus [it is said]. Here too, for the sake of the *ajāmi* (non-repetition) principle, there is the *bṛhannidhana* [chant] of the *vārka-jambha*; by virtue of that, there is the arrangement of the *āguntuna* of the *maidhātitha*, as well as the formation of the *sāman*-triad. The rest has been explained. 6.
Thus ends the second [sacrificial session] of forty-nine nights, consisting of [the *yamātirātras*]. ||48||
The *āñjanābhyañjana* [sacrifice] consists of a third [period] of forty-nine nights:

an *atirātra*, four six-day periods (*ṣaḍaha*) with *abhiplava* days, an *atirātra* consisting of all the *stomas*, two six-day periods with *abhiplava* days, the ten days of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*), and an *atirātra*. Thus the *āñjanābhyañjana* sacrifices have been described. Regarding the *āñjanābhyañjana* sacrifices, the sūtra begins: "At the *upasads* of the *gārhapatya* fire," and so forth.
The ointments and unguents have been prepared. || 1 ||

Thus [it is said]. This is the *pratnānurūpa* for the first day of the first *abhiplava*. The last two *abhiplavas* are performed in reverse order (*pratiloma*), because of the statement regarding the *vidhṛti*s and so forth: "on the third and sixth. All *abhiplavas* have the *śyaita* and *naudhasa* as their *brahmasāman*s; they possess the *pauṣkala*, *śrudhya*, and *auṣṇiha* [stotras]. Everything else is well known. || 1 ||
Thus [are described] the collyriums and ointments.
The third [section], consisting of forty-nine nights, is completed. || 49 ||
Those measured by a year have been stated:

the forty-fourth [day], the forty-ninth night, the sixty-first night, the Atirātra, the twenty-fourfold Prāyaṇīya day, three six-day periods (Abhiplavas), the Abhijit, three Svarasāmans, the Divākīrtya day, three Svarasāmans, the Viśvajit, one six-day period (Abhiplava), the Āyu and Gau days—these two days—the ten days of the twelve-day rite (Dvādaśāha), the Mahāvrata, and the Atirātra; these constitute what is measured by a year.
Those arranged for a year, measured by a year, and those lasting sixty-one nights. || 1 ||

Thus, the meaning is that they are arranged according to the *gavāmayana* sacrifice. Therefore, the *abhilava* periods have the *abhīvarta* as their *brahmasāman*, and the *uṣṇih* meters are easy to recognize. And it has been said: "The *śyaita*, *naudhasa*, *pauṣkala*, *śrudhya*, and *uṣṇih* [sāmans] are used elsewhere than in those [periods] measured by the year."

Regarding the *satra*s: the forty-nine-night sacrifice is the fifth; and the *go* and *āyus* sacrifices are among the annual ones. And it is said: "These very *go* and *āyus* [sacrifices] are to be performed in other *rātrisatras*, except for those involving the *yamātirātra*s and those measured by a year. In the third *abhiplava* period, which is considered to be the *iṣovṛdhīya*, there is a deliberation as to whether one should perform it or not; the established conclusion (*siddhānta*) set forth in the *Nidāna* is that one must indeed perform it.

Regarding the *abhiplava* that occurs after the *viśvajit* and is repeated, there arises an inquiry as to which [of the following] one should perform on its first day: the *yaṇva*, the *apatyasaṃtani*, the *śākvara*, or the *varṇa*. The conclusion stated in the Sūtra is that it should indeed be the *yaṇva*. || 1 ||
Thus, those rites measured by a year are completed.
The forty-fourth [section], consisting of the forty-nine-night and sixty-one-night rites, is completed. || 50 ||
The fifth [sacrificial session] consists of forty-nine nights: an *atirātra* of the *kakubh* verses of Savitṛ;

nine days consisting of the *trivṛt* stoma with the *agniṣṭoma* as the opening; then three days—an *agniṣṭoma* on both sides and an *ukthya* in the middle; nine days consisting of the *pañcadaśa* stoma with the *agniṣṭoma* as the opening; then three days—an *agniṣṭoma* on both sides and an *ukthya* in the middle; nine days consisting of the *saptadaśa* stoma with the *agniṣṭoma* as the opening; then three days—an *agniṣṭoma* on both sides and an *ukthya* in the middle; nine days consisting of the *ekaviṃśa* stoma with the *agniṣṭoma* as the opening; then those which...

Three days consisting of *agniṣṭoma*s on both sides, an *ukthya* in the middle, ten days of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*), the *mahāvrata*, and the *atirātra*—these are declared to be the "peaks" (*kakubha*) of Savitṛ. Among these, there are nine threefold (*trivṛt*) days following the introductory *atirātra*. Of these, the first is concluded with the *agniṣṭoma* form; five are *ukthya*s; and of the remaining three days, the first and last are *agniṣṭoma*s while the middle one is an *ukthya*. The fifteen-fold (*pañcadaśa*) days should be understood in the same manner.
He states the arrangement of the hymns (*stotra*): "The peaks of Savitṛ are arranged by means of the *vidhṛti*s. (1)
Thus it is said. Regarding this, he states the specific rule:
"One enters upon the Trivṛt-stoma with a Rāthaṃtara-sāman; the Pañcadaśa-stoma with a Bārhata-sāman; the Saptadaśa-stoma with a Rāthaṃtara-sāman; and the Ekaviṃśa-stoma with a Bārhata-sāman. (2)

Thus [it is said]. "He undertakes" (pratipadyate) means he begins. This is what is being stated: in the *vidhṛti* sacrifices, there is an undertaking of all the *trivṛt* and other [stomas] with the *rāthantara* days; but here it is not so. Rather, that *trivṛt* day which is *rāthantara* in the *vaidhṛta* sacrifice should be made the first *trivṛt* here, and the second [day] should be *bārhata*; in this manner, one should proceed by alternation up to the ninth day. The ninth day is *rāthantara*.

Then, for the sake of the *ajāmi* (non-repetition), one should perform nine fifteen-versed hymns by alternating them: whatever *vaidhṛta* and *bārhata* fifteen-versed hymns there are, here the first of the fifteen-versed ones is *rāthantara*, the second [is *vaidhṛta*], and so on by alternation; the ninth becomes *bārhata*. Then, starting with the seventeen-versed *vaidhṛta-rāthantara*, one should perform them by alternation up to the ninth; [likewise] with the twenty-one-versed *bārhata*, one performs the twenty-one-versed [hymns]. || 2 ||
In this [rite], the Agniṣṭoma is characterized by the Bṛhat-sāman, the midday pressing has the Yauktāśva-stotra, and the Ārbhava-praüga is the Hāviṣmat.

Thus: in the manner described, when the *rāthaṃtara* and *bārhata* days are performed by alternation, wherever the *bārhata* day occurs as the *agniṣṭoma* conclusion—such as the first, seventh, and ninth days among the fifteen-verse and twenty-one-verse stomas—there, in the midday *pavamāna* of those [days], the *yauktāśva* should be performed in place of the *hāviṣmata*.

Regarding the *satra*s: in the forty-nine-night sacrifice (*ekānnapañcāśadrātra*), on the sixth and seventh days, at the *ārbhava* [laud], in place of the *maukṣa*, there is the *hāviṣmata*. Likewise, the *Nidāna* states regarding the ten-night sacrifice of Kusurubinda: "On the days consisting of *bṛhatī* verses, there is the *yauktāśva-hāviṣmata*; in the *agniṣṭoma*s, there is the *hāviṣmata*; in the *uktha*s, the *maukṣa*; and in the *uktha-sāman*s, the *maukṣa*. || 3 ||
He who draws up the sun during the ritual distributions.

Thus [it is said]. In the *vidhṛtis*, three *arkas* of the twenty-one-fold hymns are prescribed for the ninth and subsequent days; since those for the tenth and eleventh days are absent here, two *arkas* are omitted. Furthermore, having extracted the *arka* of Agni prescribed for the ninth day—namely, the *gāyatra* "svādiṣṭhayā" and the *arka* of Agni—one should place the *saṃhita* in its stead. This is because the *arkas* are to be performed in their entirety during the ten-night rite (*daśarātra*). And so says the *Nidāna*: "He extracts the *arka* from the *vidhṛtis*, for he is about to perform the *arkas* in the ten-night rite. (4)
The rest is the same. ||5||
Thus; the words "with the *vidhṛtis*" are to be supplied as the remainder. || 5 ||
Thus ends the forty-ninth night (the *Savituḥ Kakubhaḥ*), the fifth [section]. ||51||

In the sixth and seventh [fortnights], consisting of forty-nine nights, there is an *atirātra*, four *abhiplava* six-day periods, the *mahāvrata*, two *abhiplava* six-day periods, the ten days of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*), and an *atirātra*; thus the forty-nine-night sixth [fortnight] is described. It is arranged from the middle *pṛṣṭhya* up to the middle *pṛṣṭhya*. ||1||
Thus; in the repetition, the two *abhiplava* periods are the last; the rest is well known.
An Atirātra, six Abhiplava Ṣaḍahas, twelve days of the Dvādaśāha, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra—thus everything regarding the forty-nine-night rite has been stated in the seventh [section]. ||1||
Thus, the sixth and seventh [sections] conclude with the completion of the forty-nine nights. || 52 ||

The sixty-one-night sacrifice consists of an *atirātra*, a *caturviṃśa* opening day (*prāyaṇīya*), three six-day periods of *abhiplava* days, a six-day period of *pṛṣṭhya* days, the *abhijit*, three *svarasāman* days, a *divākīrtya* day, another three *svarasāman* days, the *viśvajit*, a six-day period of *pṛṣṭhya* days beginning with the thirty-three-fold hymn-form (*trayastrimśārambhaṇa*), one six-day period of *abhiplava* days, the *āyu* and *go* days (two days), the ten days of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*), the *mahāvrata*, and an *atirātra*. This constitutes the sixty-one-night sacrifice. Its days are to be performed according to the model of the *gavāmayana*.

Because it has been stated that they are "arranged according to the year" (*saṃvatsaraklṛptāḥ*), meaning they are "measured by the year" (*saṃvatsarasaṃmitāḥ*), and consist of sixty-one nights; and because this was also stated by [Baudhāyana] himself regarding the repeated *abhiplava* period, based on the statement "sixty-one nights."
Thus ends the sixty-one-night rite.
The Śatarātra consists of an Atirātra,

the Jyotis-Gau-Ayu three-day period, fourteen Abhiplava six-day periods, the ten days of the twelve-day rite (Dvādaśāha), the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra; these are the sacrificial sessions (satras)— the Saṃvatsararātra.

Thus the Śatarātra has been described. For the first day of the first Abhiplava, this is the *anurūpa* verse beginning with *pratna*. The Abhiplavas consist of the Śyaita, Naudhasa, and Brahma-sāmans, as well as the Pauṣkala, Śrudhya, and Auṣṇiha chants. The vow is that of the year-long sacrifice (*sāṃvatsarika-vrata*). Everything else is established by rule (*siddha*).
Thus ends the Śatarātra.

The *saṃvatsararātra* and then the six *saṃvatsarasattras*—beginning with "the *atirātra* and the twenty-fourth day, the *prāyaṇīya* day," and ending with the *saṃvatsarabrāhmaṇa* and the word "brāhmaṇa"—the *gavāmayana* has been described. Its ritual arrangement (*klṛpti*) has already been explained previously.
Thus ends the night of the year.

Thus ends the first chapter concerning the sacrificial sessions (*satra*), which is the ninth from the beginning, in this commentary on the *Ārṣeyakalpa* composed by Varadarāja, the son of the venerable Vāmanārya. 9.

The *atirātra* is prescribed for the middle *pṛṣṭhya*; the twenty-fourth day (*caturviṃśamahar*) is prescribed for the first day of the *ābhiplavika*. [The stotras are]: the *gāyatra* "pra somo vipaścitaḥ" for the *āśva* (Aśvin) chant; the *pajra*, *gauṅgava*, and *yaudhājaya* chants beginning with "pra soma devavītaye"—these are single-verse hymns (*ekarcāḥ*). The rest is the same. For the second day, there is the *trivṛt* [stoma]. [The stotras are]: the *mādhucchandasa* chant beginning with "punānaḥ soma dhārayā"; the *bharga* on one verse, the *aiḍa* on one verse, and the *āyāsya* with three *nidhanas* on three verses.

The rest is the same; for the third day, there is the *gāyatra* and the *vairūpa*, beginning with "sa na indrāya yajyavaḥ"; the rest is the same. For the fourth day, there is the *trivṛt*; [the verses] beginning with "tavāhaṃ soma rāraṇa" are recited: one on a *pṛśni*-verse, one on an *ātharvaṇa*-verse, one on an *ābhīśava*-verse, and three on *yaudhājaya*-verses; the rest is the same. For the fifth day, there is the *pañcadaśa*; [the verses] beginning with "apsā indrāya vāyava" are recited: one on a *gāyatra*-verse and one on a *mārgīyava*-verse; he begins the *bṛhatī* with the *vāmra* [verse]; the rest is the same. It is the *trivṛt*.

For the sixth day, the six-verse hymn beginning with "This steed, urged by men" (*eṣa vājī hito nṛbhiḥ*) is placed before the *paryāsa*; the other fifteen-fold stoma is arranged up to the *bṛhaspati-stoma*. For that [day], the *bhīvarta* is the *brahmasāman* on an *uṣṇih* verse; the *gaurīvita* is on an *anuṣṭubh* verse; the rest is arranged identically up to the *indra-stoma*. For that [day], the *śyaita* is on an *anuṣṭubh* verse in the *indrakratu* [stotra]; the rest is arranged identically up to the *vyūḍha agniṣṭomas*. Their arrangement for the first day is according to the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*).

For the second day, the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses, the *paryāsa*, and the *gāyatra* chant are "Flow on as a bull, O Soma, in thy stream"; the *svāra-sāman* is the *yauktāśva*; the *sauparṇa* is "Being purified, O Soma, in thy stream"; the *antarā-dairghaśravasa* is "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā"; these are single-verse hymns (*ekarcāḥ*), while the rest is the same; the *trivṛt* [stoma] belongs to the third day. For the fourth day, the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses and the *paryāsa* are "That [Soma], for Indra, the sacrificers... and so forth; the *gāyatra* is the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*, and the rest is the same; the *trivṛt* [stoma] belongs to the fourth day.

In the world of Nānada, the Gaurīvita is the same as the other. For the fifth day, the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses are in the *trivṛt* [meter]. The *paryāsa* is "Flow on, O Soma, most brilliant" (*arṣā soma dyumattama*). There is a *gāyatra* [sāman] on one verse, a *yaṇva* on three verses, and an *ānūpa* on one verse: "Soma pressed by the pressers" (*soma u ṣvānaḥ sotṛbhiḥ*). There is an *agni-triṇidhana* on a *viṣṭārapaṅkti*, and a *saṃtanya* on the verses of Bṛhadgiras: "The stalk, intoxicating" (*aṃśur madāya*). There is a *gāyatra* and a *gauṣūkta*; "Flow for the winning of booty" (*pavasva vājasātaye*) is the *gaurīvita*. And the *carṣabha* is the *śākvara*; the rest is the same.

The *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* of the sixth day consist of the *trivṛt*; the *paryāsa* is "indrāyendo marutvate," which is a *gāyatra* on one verse; "revatīs tisṛṣu"; "mṛjyamānaḥ suhastyā" is an *aiḍa* on one verse; "aukṣṇorandhram"; "goṣṭho viṣṭārapaṅktau"; and "pari svāno giriṣṭhā" is a *gāyatra* and a *vaidanvata*, both having the *nidhana* "yan. "somāḥ pavanta indavaḥ" is the *gaurīvita* and the *krauñca*. That which has its own source (*svayoni*) is the same as the other *trivṛt*. 102.

The *stotrīya* for the seventh day consists of a triplet from a hymn of nine verses; the *anurūpa* and *paryāsa* are the triplet beginning with "Flow on, O bull, in thy stream" (*vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā*). On one verse there is a *gāyatra*, on one a *mārgīyava*, on one an *aiḍa sauparṇa*, and on the verses of Kaṇva a *saṃtani*. From the triplet beginning with "That exhilaration of thine which is most excellent" (*ye te mado vareṇyaḥ*), he extracts the *gāyatra* and the *arka* of Agni, as well as the *dvipadās*. The *stotrīya* for the eighth day consists of a triplet from a hymn of nine verses; the *anurūpa* and *paryāsa* are the triplet beginning with "Thy [drop], O Indu, from the plant" (*tava tyo indo andhasaḥ*). There is a *gāyatra* and a slow-moving *sauparṇa*, and the verses beginning with "The Soma-drops, the Āyus... (*abhi somāsa āyavaḥ*).

Thus, [he sings] the *dvihiṅkāra*, the *gāyatrapārśva*, the *pauruhanmana*, and the *acchidra*; [then] "Pavasva deva āyuṣak," which is the *gāyatra* and the *svāśirā*; [then] "Arko bhī no vājasātamam," which is the *gaurīvita* and the *triṇidhana*. He extracts the *tvāṣṭrīṣāma*; they urge on the two-footed [verse]: "Hinvanti sūram usrāḥ. This is the final *saṃkṣāra* of the *iḍās*. The rest is the same. For the ninth day, the *stotrīya* of the *trivṛt* is a ten-verse hymn; the *anurūpa* is a triplet, and the *paryāsa* is "Pavamāno rathītamaḥ," which is a *gāyatra*.

"Pour out the pressed juice for him who is swift and eager"—this is the *pṛṣṭha* [stotra]; the *kaulmalabarhiṣa*, the *devasthāna*, and the *ārka* of Dīrghatamas; the *sāmarāja* is the last, beginning with "O Soma, you are the sustainer. The *gāyatra* and the *aśvasūkta*; "Him, the desirable, the golden"—this is the *gaurīvita*; and the *saṃkṛti*. He extracts the *dvipadās*: "The swift one has been born near," and the *pratīcīneḍa*; the *kāśīta* is the last; the rest is the same as the *trivṛt*. 103.

For the tenth day, there are three *anurūpas* corresponding to five days: one *ekarca* and two *tṛcas*. The *bahiṣpavamāna* consists of the *gāyatra* "uccā te jātam andhasaḥ," the *āmahīyava*, and the *ābhīka*; the *antarotsedha* and *niṣedha* consist of "punānaḥ soma dhārayā"; the *gaurīvita* consists of one *ekarca*; and the *yajñāyajñīya* is the last, beginning with "ā jāgṛviḥ. He extracts the *dvipadās*. The rest is the same. There are two days, the *udbhic* and the *valabhi*; the *udbhic* is in the place of the *maidhātitha*.

The *Bṛhannidhana* for the *Arkajañjabha*, the *Raurava* for the *Maidhātitha*, and the *Gaurīvita* for both; the rest is the same as the established [chanting] for the *Āvṛtta* *Abhiplavas*. For the first day of the first *Āvṛtta* *Abhiplava*: the *Aiḍa-aukṣṇorandhra* with the verse "mṛjyamānaḥ suhastya"; the *Kaṇvarathantara* on one [verse], the *Varuṇasāman* on one, and the *Triṇidhana-āyāsya* on three; the rest is the same. He omits [the chants] for the subsequent [days].

The Kaṇvarathantara and Varuṇasāman are arranged as triplets; the Bṛhatī [verses] belong to the Go and Āyus sacrifices of the twelve-year cycle, while the two Bṛhatīs belong to the one-day (aikāhika) sacrifice. 104.

"Following his ancient splendor, these Soma drops flow toward the beloved [Soma]; being purified, Soma flows; the Soma drops, the Indus, have been released. Purify yourself for us with rain! Your unceasing streams flow forth, O Sage Pavamāna. O Agni, come for the feast!"—these are the *ājya* verses. "The wise Soma drops," this is the *Gāyatra*, the *Aśva*, the *Somasāman*, the *Āśu*, the *Bhārgava*, the *Mārgīyava*, the *Abhīka*, the *Aiḍa*, the *Sauparṇa*, the *Rohitakūlīya*, and "O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—this is the *Pajra*.

The Dvaigata, the Pauruhanmana, the Hārāyaṇa, the Dvihiṃkāra, the Gauṅgava, the Yaudhājaya, and the Uśana at the end; the Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Naudhasa, and the Kāleya; [the hymns] with "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" are the Gāyatra-saṃhitā; the Śaiśava, the Bhāsa, the Kākṣīvata, and the Jarābodhīya; [the hymns] with "pavasvendramaccha" are the Saphākṣāra; and the Gaurīvita, the Vaiśvāmitra, and "asāvi soma indra ta."

Thus, for one whose source is *iti*, and who has *padanidhana*, *śuddhāśuddhīya*, *svāra*, *kautsa*, and *aurukṣaya*; and for those [verses] beginning with *adardarat* and *asṛjat*; for these two, the *uttaramaudala*, the *gautama*, and the *kāva* are the final [parts], while the *yajñayajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. 105

"Flow on as the leader of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. O Soma, you are brilliant; for you are indeed a bull by your luster. This god is immortal"—from this ten-verse hymn, he omits the final triplet. "This very one is the bull, the chariot; this is the steed urged on by men; this is the seer, highly praised. "Your vital powers have arisen, O Pavamāna; we choose Agni as our messenger"—these are the *ājya* verses. "Flow on as a bull in your stream," the *gāyatra*, the *yauktāśva*, the *surūpa*, the *hariśrīnidhana*, and the *ājiga*.

And the Svāra, the Sauparṇa, the Chāndasya, the Yauktāśva, and the Ṛṣabha; the Pāvamāna hymn beginning with "punaḥ soma dhāraya"; the Samanta, the Dairghaśravasa, the Pṛṣṭha, and the Yaśas; the Kaulmalabarhiṣa; the Āyāsya beginning with "vṛṣā śoṇaḥ"; the Pārtha as the final [Sāman]; the Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita, and the Mādhucchandasa; and the Gāyatra beginning with "yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"; the Hāviṣmat, the Śāṃmada, the Dāvasunidhana, the Asita, and the Aśvasūkta—this is it.

With the verse, "Flow with your stream, pressed for the feast of the gods," [he sings] the *śaṅku* at *sujñāna*; [he sings] the *pūṣā*, *rayiḥ*, and *bhagaḥ*; the *gaurīvita* and the *caiḍa*; the *kautsa*, the *bharga*, and the *āsita*; the *yadvāhiṣṭhīya*, and the two *krauñca*s. Of these, he uses the first and the last; [he sings] "The bull of prayers flows on" as the *yāma*; the final [verse] is the *yajñāyajñīya*, the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. These are his own *uktha*s. 106.

With flashing brilliance, the drops have been poured forth; the King is approached with sacred hymns. To you, who bear manly powers, this one goes with a slender prayer. The drops have been poured forth on their path; the purifying ones have flowed. Striking down adversaries, he flows for the sake of nourishment. Flow with a stream! "Agni is kindled by Agni"—with these [verses] and the *ājya* offerings; "High is the birth of your juice"—with the *gāyatra*, the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*, the *saumitra*, the *iṣṭata*, the *sākamaśva*, the *vilambasauparṇa*, and [the verse] beginning "The Soma-drops, seeking men..."

The *paurumadga*, the *sadoviśīya*, the *gautama*, the *antarikṣa*, the *acchidra*, the *maidhātitha*, the *aṣkāraṇidhana*, the *kāṇva*, and "the three voices"—this is the *saṃkrośa* of the Aṅgirases; the final [stotra] consists of the *rathaṃtara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *mahāvaiṣṭambha*, and the *raurava*. "The three voices arise"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *pāṣṭhauha*, the *aiḍa*, the *saindhukṣita*, the *auśana*, and the *vairūpa*; and "our own *uṣṇih* and *kakubh* stanzas, the most honey-sweet pressed juices"—this is the *gaurīvita* and the *sādhra*.

The Śyāvāśva [Sāman], the three Tvaṣṭṛ-sāmans, this Svāra [Sāman] with three nidhanas, the Pavitra beginning with "ta it," the Ariṣṭa as the final [Sāman], and the Yajñāyajñīya as the Agniṣṭoma-sāman—these are his own Ukthas. 107

Pavamāna has brought them forth; purifying himself, he has stepped forward like cattle toward their pastures. Flow swiftly, O one of lofty mind, for the sake of the tawny one who is self-strong. Like chariots, the rays urge the Sun forward. May Agni utterly destroy the Vṛtras—this is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ. His own subsequent [verses] are: "Flow on, O bestower of skill," which is both *gāyatra* and *ātharvaṇa*; the *nidhanakāma*, the *adārasṛt*, and the *satrāsāhīya*; "I have rejoiced in thee, O Soma," which is the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*, the *arkapuṣpa*, and the *bārhaduktha*.

And [the hymn] "Māṇḍavaṃ ca vidāvasu" has the *nidhana* "ābhīśavam"; "Svaḥpṛṣṭham" and "Aṅgirasam"; "Somaḥ pavate janitā matīnām" is the final [hymn] "Janitram"; "Bṛhat" and "Vāmadevyam"; "Traikrośam" and "Pṛśni"; "Pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ" is the "Gāyatram"; "Aurṇāyavam" and "Bṛhat"; "Bhāradvājam" and "Mārgīyavam"; "Yadīnidhanam"; "Sve uṣṇikkakubhau"; "Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the "Gaurivitam"; and "Vārkajambham" with the *nidhana* "Yadī".

If the *iḍā* verses are pure and impure, and if on the ninth day there is the *aiḍa*, the *ākūpara*, the *āndhīgava*, the *āśvinī* verses beginning with "pavamāna dhenavaḥ," the *lauśa* as the final verse, and the *yajñāyajñīya* as the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*, he omits his own *ukthas* and [performs] the *ṣoḍaśin*. 108.

"Ut te śuṣmāsa īrate"—this five-verse hymn is for the *paryāsa* at the beginning; "Agne stomam manāmahe" is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ. His own [verses] follow. His own *gāyatrī*: "Somā u ṣvāṇaḥ sotṛbhiḥ," the *mānava*, the *anūpa*, and the two *vaiṣṇava* verses: "Tavāham soma rāraṇa. Of these, on the first day, there is the *yauktasruc*, the *vāmra*, the *triṇidhana* of Agni, "Indur vājī pavate gonyoghā"; with the concluding verse, there are the *rathaṃtara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *bārhadgira*, and the *rāyovājīya*.
