The *cāsāvyam̐śu*, *madāya*—the *gāyatram*, the *saṃtani*, the *adhyardheḍam*, the *somasāma*, and the *gauṣūktam*; the *uṣṇih* and *kakubh* meters in their own place; "pavasva vājasātaye"—the *gaurīvitam*, the *carṣabha*, the *śākvara*, and the *tvāṣṭrīsāma*; the *dvyanutodam*, the *trāsadasyavam*, the *aṣṭeḍa*, and the *padastobha*; "govitpavasva"—the *dvyabhyāghātam*, the *lauśam*, and finally the *yajñāyajñīyam* as the *agniṣṭomasāma*; and for the ten-verse hymn beginning with "pavasva devavīratī," its own *ukthas*.

He extracts a triplet; he extracts the *aiḍa* of Aukṣṇorandhra as the last; he extracts the *svāra* of Vaidanvata; he extracts the *gaurīvita* in an *anuṣṭubh*. Now, that which is the sixth day of the *pṛṣṭhya-stoma*, this is the thirty-versed [stotra] arranged as a triplet.

The Soma-drops which, having been pressed, have flowed forth like chariots from afar—those drops, with their juice, [grant] us barley after barley; [the draught] that is skillful, joy-bestowing, and true to the cosmic order (ṛta). This is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ, beginning with "Vaiśvānara. His own subsequent [verses] are his own: the *gāyatrī* beginning with "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā," the *soma-sāman*, the *kaṇvarathaṃtara*, the *paurumadga*, the *gaugava*, and the *ayāsya* with its two finales. [The verse] beginning with "Pra kāvyamuśaneva bruvāṇaḥ" is the *vārāha*, the last of his own; [and the verse] beginning with "Yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" constitutes the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

The *gāyatra* [sāman] is on three verses; the *arka* of Agni is on one; the *jarābodhīya* is on one; the *dakṣanidhana* is on one; the *uṣṇih* and *kakubh* meters are on their own; the *gaurīvita*, the *kārtayaśa*, the *ātreya*, and the *gautama* are on the *dvipadā* verses; the *sauhaviṣa* is on the verse beginning with "pro ayāsīt"; the *aiḍa* is the final *yajñasārathi*; and the *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. These are his own *ukthas*. 1010.

"These dawns urge on the hero; these Soma-juices flow toward the beloved. While the Soma is being purified, it flows; its powers have stood up high. "Flow around for the feast with [the offering]," and "O Agni, with all thy fires"—these are the *ājya* verses of the Hotṛ. His own subsequent verses are: "O Adhvaryu, [the Soma] pressed by the stones," the *gāyatra*, the *vairūpa*, the *āśu* of Bhṛgu, the slow-moving *sauvarṇa*, "toward [us], O Soma, the Āyavas," the *dvihiṅkāra*, the *gāyatrapārśva*, the *pauruhanmana*, the *hārāyaṇa*, and the *acchidra*: "O, indeed, this child..."

The Vāsiṣṭha is the final [stotra]; one's own Pṛṣṭhas are with the verses "pavasva deva āyuṣak"; the Gāyatra is on three verses; the Svaśira Ārka is on one verse; the Kākṣīvata is on one verse; the Bhāsa is on one verse; one's own Uṣṇih and Kakubh are with "abhī no vājasātamam"; the Gaurīvita, the Aiḍa, the Kautsa, and the Audala are with "rayiṣṭham" on their own verses; the Dharma is with "hā u dharta" on an Aiḍa verse; the Śārṅga is the final [verse]; the Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman; and one's own Ukthas [are used]. 1011.

"Upa ṣu jātam apturam," "eṣa devaḥ amartyaḥ," "sa sutaḥ pītaye vṛṣā," "ayā pavasva dhārayā," "pavamānasya te kave," and "upa tvā raṇvasaṃdṛśam"—these are the *ājya* verses of the Hotṛ; the subsequent ones belong to Pavamāna. "Pavamānasya jighnataḥ" is the *gāyatra*; the *adārasṛc* and the *saṃkṣāra* of the *iḍās*. "Ṛṣabhaśca pāvamānaḥ," "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam," "devasthānam," "saṃkṛtim," "dairghaśravasam," and "dīrghatamasaśca arkaḥ"—and "hā u hu vā akrān."

The final [stotra] belongs to Vasiṣṭha; his own *pṛṣṭha* lauds are: the *gāyatra* on three verses beginning with "Thou art Soma, the sustainer"; the *āśvasūkta* on one verse; the *pratīcīneḍa* on one verse; the *kāśita* on one verse; the *hāviṣkṛta* on one verse; his own *uṣṇih* and *kakubh* meters; the *gaurīvita* on the verses beginning with "That desirable, golden one"; the *vāṅnidhana* and the *krauñca*; the *sādhra* on his own verses; the *aiḍa* on the verses beginning with "Soma has been pressed, the ruddy, virile, golden bull"; the *yāma* as the final [laud]; the *yajñāyajñīya* as the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*; and then his own *uktha* lauds. Now, as for that which...

Of the ten-night *chandoma* sacrifice, the ninth day is [the *mahāvrata*], and here the tenth is its supplement (*paryūṣ*). Therein, the *gaurīvita* is on one verse, the *auṣṇiha* with the *ekonidhana* on one verse, the *śyāvāśva* on one verse, and the *āndhīgava* on three verses; the rest is the same as the *mahāvrata*. Both the *mahāvrata* and the *atirātra* [are thus performed]. The tenth chapter, concerning the expansion (*vivṛti*).
The central sacrificial session is known by the alternative name *ādityānām ayana*.

It consists of an *atirātra*, a twenty-four-fold day (*caturviṃśa*), an opening day (*prāyaṇīya*), two six-day periods (*ṣaḍaha*) consisting of the *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* stomas, and two *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍahas*. This constitutes the first month; the second, third, fourth, and fifth months are likewise composed of three six-day periods each consisting of the *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* stomas, followed by a *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, a *trivṛt* day, the *bṛhaspatistoma*, three *svarasāman* days, a *divākīrtya* day, three more *svarasāman* days, and an *ukthya* day consisting of the *pañcadaśa* stoma dedicated to Indra.

The *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha* begins with the *trayastrimśa*; there is one *pañcadaśa* and one *trivṛt* *ṣaḍaha*; the ten days of the *dvādaśāha* in their expanded (*vyūḍha*) form; *agniṣṭoma*s consisting of *trivṛt*s; two days, the *udbhic* and the *balabhit*; two *ṣaḍaha*s consisting of *pañcadaśa* and *trivṛt*; a *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*; two *ṣaḍaha*s consisting of *pañcadaśa* and *trivṛt*—this is the first month. This is the second; this is the third; this is the fourth. A *ṣaḍaha* consisting of *pañcadaśa* and *trivṛt*; a *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*; a *ṣaḍaha* consisting of *pañcadaśa* and *trivṛt*; and two days, the *gauḥ* and the *āyus*.

The Chandomada ten-day period consists of the forty-eighth day first, then the forty-fourth, the fortieth, the thirty-sixth, the thirty-second, the thirtieth, two twenty-eighths, the twenty-fifth, and the twenty-fourth, followed by the Mahāvrata and the Atirātra. The Ādityānām Ayana has been described by the Anuvāka beginning with "ādityānāṃ madhyepṛṣṭhyam"; that very [sacrifice] is called "madhyepṛṣṭhya" because there is a six-day period with the Pṛṣṭha-stotras in the middle every month.
The Atirātra is prescribed in the middle of the Pṛṣṭhya; the Caturviṃśa day is prescribed. ||1||
Thus [it is said]. The Atirātra is the archetype. The Caturviṃśa belongs to the Gavāmayana. These two days are counted as completing the sixth month. || 1 ||

Of the first day of the *ābhiplava* [six-day period]: "Forward, the Soma-pressings of the wise" (*pra somāso vipaścitaḥ*) is the *gāyatra* hymn for the horse; it belongs to Āśu Bhārgava. "Forward, O Soma, for the feast of the gods" (*pra soma devavītaye*)—these are the *satrāṇi*:
the *madhyepṛṣṭhya*, the *ayanam*, the *pajram*, the *gauṅgavam*, and the *yaudhājayam*. These consist of single verses (*ekarcāḥ*). The rest is the same as the threefold (*trivṛt*) [stoma]. 2.

Thus: the Gāyatrī and Bṛhatī meters are prepared for the Sāman triplet; the last [verse] belongs to the Auśana [Sāman], according to the Mādhyandina school, while the Ārbhava [Śastra] consists of single verses excluding the last one. Everything else is the same as the first day of the Abhiplava [ṣaḍaha]; everything is the Trivṛt [stoma]. || 2 ||

On the second day, [the stotras are]: "punaḥ soma dhāraya" (Soma, purifying yourself, flow with your stream) on one verse; the *bharga* [sāman] on one verse; the *aiḍamāyāsya* [sāman] on one verse; and the *triṇidhana-āyāsya* [sāman] on three verses. The rest is the same as the fifteen-fold [stoma].

Thus: "Flow as a bull, O Soma, in your stream" (*vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā*)—this is the *gāyatra* and the *hāviṣmat*. "Being purified, O Soma, in your stream" (*punānaḥ soma dhārayā*)—this is the *mādhucchandasa*. "The splendor of Āyāsya, the descendant of Iḍā" (*bharga aiḍamāyāsyam*)—this is the *sāmatṛca*. The *triṇidhana* of Āyāsya is performed on three verses. "The red bull" (*vṛṣā śoṇaḥ*)—this is the final *pārtha*; this constitutes the midday pressing. In the subsequent *abhiplava* days, in place of the *hāviṣmat*, the *yauktāśva* comes next; in place of *bharga*, there is *yaśas*. On the latter wing, at the *ārbhava* [pressing], there are the *śaṅkusujñāna* and the *gaurīvitāni* on single-verse hymns.
The rest is equal to the second day of the Abhiplava of the Gavāmayana; everything is fifteen-fold.
On the third day, "sa na indrāya yajyave" is the Gāyatra and the Vairūpa [Sāmans].
The rest is the same as the Trivṛt.

Thus: in the two subsequent *pavamāna* chants, there are single-verse hymns (*ekarcas*), excluding the final one. The rest is the same as the third day of the *abhiplava* period. Everything is in the *trivṛt* stoma. || 5 ||

For the fourth day, he recites "O Soma, I have rejoiced in thee" (*soma rāraṇa*): one verse by Pṛśni, one by Ātharvaṇa, one by Ābhīśava, and three by Yaudhājaya. The rest is the same. It is the Pañcadaśa-stoma. 6.

Thus: "Flow on, O means of accomplishing skill" (*pavasva dakṣasādhana*) is the *gāyatra* [sāman]; "Adārasṛt"; "O Soma, in thee I have rejoiced" (*tavāhaṃ soma rāraṇa*) is the *pṛśni-ātharvaṇa*; "Ābhīśava"—these are the three *sāman*-verses; the *yaudhājaya* is on three verses; "O, indeed, of him" (*ūhu vā asya*) is the final *vāsiṣṭha*. This is the midday [pressing]. In the *ārbhava*, the *kakubh* and *uṣṇih* [verses] and the *gaurīvita* are each single-verse [sāmans]. The rest is the same as the fourth *abhiplava* [day]. Everything is fifteen-fold (*pañcadaśa*).
On the fifth day, [the stotras] for Indra and Vāyu are the *apsas*; the *gāyatra* and the *mārgīyava*. He begins the *bṛhatī* with the *vāma* [sāman]. The rest is the same. It is the *trivṛt*. 7.

Thus: "apsā indrāya" consists of the Gāyatra and the Mārgīyava; "abhi somāsa āyavaḥ" consists of the Vāmra, the Mānava, and the Ānūpa; and the Triṇidhana of Agni. "Abhi tripṛṣṭham" concludes the Mādhyandina [pressing]. With the exception of the last, these are single-verse (ekarca) hymns. Since the Yaṇv and other [hymns] must be performed as continuous triplets (tṛca), it is inappropriate to perform them as single verses; therefore, they are excluded here. Accordingly, there is a sūtra in the section on the Santani: "And in the case of single-verse hymns, the [exclusion] is established by rule."

The commencement with the Bṛhatī is for the sake of the Vāmadevya and for the sake of commencing the Iḍā; the last [verse] is in the Ārbhava [Pavamāna] triplet; [this is done] by means of the fifth day of the Abhiplava; the rest is the same.

The *satra*s—the central *pṛṣṭhya* arrangement of the sixth day: for the *paryāya*, the six-verse hymn beginning with "This steed, slain by the men" (*eṣa vājī hato nṛbhiḥ*) is used; the rest is the same. [It is] the *pañcadaśa* [stoma]. 8.

"Thus: *asṛkṣata pra vājinaḥ*, *etamu tyaṃ daśa kṣipaḥ*, *eṣa vājī hato nṛbhiḥ*, *pavamānasya te kave*—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna. In the Ārbhava [Stotra], the Kakubh, Uṣṇih, and Gaurīvita are each single-verse hymns (*ekarcāḥ*). In the second Abhiplava, the Iṣovṛdhīya is at the end because of its immediate succession to the Pṛṣṭhya. Everything else is the same as the sixth Abhiplava; all [the Stomas] are fifteen-fold (*pañcadaśa*)."

The first month consists of two Abhiplava periods, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, and again two Abhiplavas. The other four months are likewise arranged. In the sixth month, there are three Abhiplavas and a Pṛṣṭhya as before.
Regarding this, it is said:
"It is established from the Bṛhaspatistoma. (9)
Thus [ends the ninth].
He states the specific details of the Bṛhaspatisava:
"For that [sacrifice], the Abhīvarta is the Brahman-sāman; the Sujñāna on an Uṣṇih verse, and the Gaurīvita on an Anuṣṭubh verse; the rest is the same. 10.
Thus [ends the tenth].
Then, up to the point of the *svarasāman* chants, it is like the *gavāmayana*. Regarding this, he says:
"It is established from the *indrastoma*. (11)
Thus [ends the section]. ||11||
He states the specific feature of the Indrastoma:
"In that Indra-sacrifice, the Śyaita [Sāman] is on the Gāyatrī [verse], and the Gaurīvita [Sāman] is on the Anuṣṭubh; the rest is the same. 12.
Thus [ends the section]. 12.
Now, the *abhiplava* of the *gavāmayana*, which was mentioned immediately after the *pṛṣṭhya*, is reversed. Regarding that, he says: "It is established up to the *vyūḍha-agniṣṭomas*. (13)
Thus, ten days of the twelve-day sacrifice are arranged as Agniṣṭomas with the Trivṛt stoma; these are the ten arranged Agniṣṭomas mentioned in the Śruti. 13.
He states them in order:
"Of these, the first day is arranged just like the twelve-day sacrifice. (14)
The first great day is unmodified, like the twelve-day sacrifice.
Thus ends the first day. || 1 ||
The second day:

for the second day, the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* [verses] are "Flow on, O bull, with thy stream" (*vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā*), which is a *gāyatra* hymn; the *paryāsa* is "Yauktāśva," which is *svāra* and *sauparṇa*. "Being purified, O Soma, with thy stream" (*punānaḥ soma dhārayā*) is the *āyāsya*; between these two is the *dairghaśravasa*. These are single-verse [hymns]. The rest is the same. It is the *trivṛt* [stoma]. 1.

"Thus: 'Flow on through speech, flow on, O Indu; we [follow] thee, the purifying one'—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna. At midday, the Gāyatrī and Bṛhatī verses are arranged according to the Sāman-trichs; at the Ārbhava [Pavamāna], they consist of single verses, excluding the final one. The rest is the same as the second day of the twelve-day rite (dvādaśāha). Everything is threefold (trivṛt). In all the days, there is the extraction (uddhāra) of the hymns. || 1 ||
Thus ends the second day. ||2||
The third day:

the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses for the third day, the *paryāsa*, and the *gāyatra* and *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha* chants beginning with "sa na indrāya yajyave" are the same as the others. It is the *trivṛt* [stoma]. 1.

The *satras*—the *madhyepṛṣṭhya* sacrifice—is as follows: "With flashing brilliance, these drops have been poured forth; flow for nourishment, O Soma, in your stream"—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "He [flows] for Indra, the sacrificers"—these two single-verse hymns are the *gāyatra* and the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*. "The *āyava* Somas toward [Indra]"—these three-verse *sāmans* are the *paurumadga*, the *gautama*, and the *antarikṣa*; the *āṣkāraṇidhana* is placed in the middle of the *āsyāyā*. "Three voices"—this is the final *saṃkrośa* of the Aṅgirases; this constitutes the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina*). Only the first [of the three verses] is used for the three [verses]; the others are used for the initial [verses].
The rest is the same as the third day of the twelve-day rite; everything is *trivṛt*.
Thus ends the third day.
The fourth day:
for the fourth day, there are the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses; the *paryāsa* is the *Gaurīvita* in the place of the *Nānada*; the rest is the same. It is the *Trivṛt*. 17.

Thus: "Pavamāna has generated for you the Aśvinī [verses]; the dawns urge on the Sun"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna. At the midday [pressing], there are two Sāman triplets consisting of Gāyatrī and Bṛhatī verses; the last one is used in a triplet. At the Ārbhava [Pavamāna], they are used in the first verses, excluding the last one. There is an extraction of the Ukthas and the Ṣoḍaśin. The rest is the same as the fourth day of the twelve-day rite (dvādaśāha). Everything is Trivṛt. 17.
Thus ends the fourth day.

On the fifth day, for the Stotriya and Anurūpa verses of the fifth day, there is the *paryāsa* verse "O Soma, most brilliant one... (*arṣā soma dyumattamaḥ*) in the Gāyatra melody on a single verse; the Yaṇva melody on three verses; and the Ānūpa melody "Soma, being pressed by the pressers... (*soma uṣvāṇaḥ sotṛbhiḥ*) on a single verse. There is the Agni-triṇidhana in the Viṣṭārapaṅkti meter; the Saṃtani in the Bārhadgira verses; and the Gāyatra and Goṣūkta melodies on "This stalk, the exhilarating one... (*asāvyaṃśurmadāya*). There is the Gaurīvita melody on "Flow for the winning of booty... (*pavasva vājasātaye*), and the Ṛṣabha Śākvara.
The rest is the same; it is threefold. 18.

"Thus: *govit pavastra pavamānasya viśvajit yāste* is the Bahiṣpavamāna. *asāvyaṃśurbhadāya*, the Gāyatra and the Gauṣūkta; *abhidyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśaḥ prāṇā śiśurmahīnām* is the Cyāvana-krośa. *pavasva vājasātaye* is the Gaurīvita and the Ṛṣabha-Śākvara. *indurvājī* is the Dāśaspatya—this is the Ārbhava Pavamāna. With the exception of the last [verse], [the verses] are used in the first [positions]. The rest is the same as the fifth day of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*). Everything is threefold (*trivṛt*). (18)

The *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses for the sixth day, the *paryāsa*, and the *gāyatra* [sāman] "indrāyendo marutvate" on a single verse; the *revatī* verses on three verses, the *aiḍa* "mṛjyamānaḥ suhastyā," and the *aukṣṇorandhra* on a single verse; the *gāyatra* "goṣṭho viṣṭārapaṅktau" and the *vaidanvata* "parisvāno giriṣṭhāḥ," which has a *nidhana*; the *gaurīvita* "somāḥ pavanta indavaḥ" and the *satrāṇi* [verses]; the *krauñca* [sāman] at the middle of the *pṛṣṭhya* sacrifice, which has its own source (*svayoni*); the rest is the same. It is the *trivṛt* [stoma]. 16.

Thus: for the *jyotis* sacrifice, they have created these Soma-libations; this is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "O Indu, for Indra accompanied by the Maruts"—this is the *gāyatra* on a single verse; the *revatī* verses on three verses; "being cleansed by the skillful hand"—this is the *aiḍa* on the *aukṣṇorandhra* verse, on a single verse. Thus is the midday [pavamāna]. The *goṣṭha* is in the *viṣṭārapaṅkti* meter; and the *gāyatra* beginning with "surrounding thee, dwelling on the mountains"; and the *vaidanvata* which possesses the *nidhana*.

"Sasunveyo vasūnām" and "taṃ naḥ sakhāyo madāya"—these are the *dīrghakarṇa* and *śravasa* [verses]; "somāḥ pavanta indavaḥ" is the *svayoni*; and "krauñca" is the last. "Ayā pavā pavasva" is the *śnauṣṭa*; thus ends the *ārbhava* [śastra]. With the exception of the final [verse], the others consist of single verses (*ekarcāḥ*). The rest is the same as on the sixth day of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*). Everything is in the *trivṛt* stoma.
Thus ends the sixth day.

The seventh day: for the seventh day, the *stotrīya* is a triplet of nine verses, and the *anurūpa* and *paryāsa* are likewise triplets. "Flow as a bull, O drop" (*vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā*) is a *gāyatra* on one verse; a *mārgīyava* on one verse; an *aiḍa sauparṇa* on one verse; and the *saṃtani* among the verses of Kaṇva. "That exhilaration of yours which is most excellent" (*yaste mado vareṇyaḥ*) is a *gāyatra* and the hymn of Agni. He extracts the two-footed verses. The rest is the same as the *trivṛt*. 20.

Thus: *pra kāvyam*, *prasūnvānāya*, and *ā te dakṣam*—these three triplets constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna*. *Vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā* is the *gāyatram*; *mārgīyavam*, *aiḍam*, and *sauparṇam* are the triplets of *sāmans*. *Punānaḥ soma dhārayā* is the *kaṇvarathantaram*; *gauṅgavam* and *āyāsyam* are the triplets of *sāmans*. *Pro ayāsīt* is the final *pravad-bhārgava*. Thus concludes the midday [service]. *Vayaṃ gha tvā* is the *santani brahmasāman*. *Yaste mado vareṇyaḥ* is the *gāyatram* and the *arka* of Agni.

"eṣa sya dhārayā sutaḥ," "sakhāya ā niṣīdata," "iti śārkaraplavau," "purojitī," and "gaurīvitaṃ ca kārtayaśaṃ ca"; "ye somāsaḥ" is the *jarābodhīya*, which constitutes the *ārbhava* [stotra]; the final triplet alone [is used]. The rest is the same as on the seventh day of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*); thus everything is *trivṛt*. 20.
Thus ends the seventh day.

The eighth day: for the eighth day, the *stotrīya* is a triplet consisting of nine verses, and the *anurūpa* is the *paryāsa*. [These are] the *gāyatra* "tava tyā indo andhasaḥ" and the *vilambasauparṇa*; the *dvihiṅkāra* "abhisomāsa āyavaḥ" and the *gāyatrapārśva*; and the *pauruhanmana* and the *acchidra*. [Then there are] the *gāyatra* "pavasva deva āyuṣak" and the *svāśirāmarka*; the *gaurīvita* "abhī no vājasātamam" and the *triṇidhana* *tvāṣṭrīsāman*. He extracts the *dvipadās*.
"The rays urge on the Sun"—this is the final *saṃkṣāra* of the *iḍās*. The rest is the same. It is the *trivṛt*. 21.
The *satras*—the *ayanam* with the *pṛṣṭhya* in the middle:

"To the infant newly born," "These Soma juices [flow] toward the beloved one," and "Flow onward with your stream"—these three *ṛcs* constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "O Indu, of that juice of yours" is the *gāyatra* and the *vilambasauparṇa*, both as single verses. "The Soma juices, the Āyus... is the *dvihiṅkāra*; "the side of the *gāyatra*" and "the *pauruhanmana*" are the *sāmatṛca* for the *acchidramadhyāsyāyā*. "The upholder of heaven" is the *udvadbhārgava* in three verses. Thus ends the midday [service].

"Pavasva deva āyuṣak" is the Gāyatra; "svāśirāmarkaḥ," "abhi dyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśaḥ," and "prāṇā śiśurmahīnām" are the Ārbhava Pavamāna stotras. "ityaiṣira," "abhī no vājasātamam," the Gaurīvita, the Triṇidhana, and the Tvaṣṭrīsāman follow. "Hinvanti sūramusrayaḥ" is the Saṃkṣāra of the Iḍās, which is the last [stotra] of the Ārbhava Pavamāna. The rest is the same as with the eighth day. Everything is Trivṛt.
Thus ends the eighth day.

The ninth day: for the ninth day, the *stotrīya* is a triplet consisting of ten verses, and the *anurūpa* is the *paryāsa*. The *gāyatra* and the *ādārasṛt* are "pavamāno rathītamaḥ. The *pṛṣṭha-stotra* consists of the hymns of Kaulmalabarhiṣa, Devasthāna, and Dīrghatamas, with the *arka* of Dīrghatamas—the *sāmarāja*—as the final verse. The *gāyatra* and the *aśvasūkta* are "tvaṃ somāsi dhārayuḥ. The *gaurīvita* and the *saṃkṛti* are "pari tyaṃ haryataṃ harim. He recites the *dvipadās* aloud.
"Upo ṣu jātam apturam"—this is the last [verse] with the *pratīcīna-ṛca* and the *kāśīta*; the rest is the same. It is the *trivṛt*. 22.

Thus: "The ocean has stepped forth; this god is immortal" (*akrānt samudra eṣa devo amartyaḥ*), and "Of thee, O sage, who art being purified" (*pavamānasya te kave*)—these three triplets constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna*. "Pavamāna, the best of charioteers" (*pavamāno rathītamaḥ*) is the *gāyatra* triplet, along with the two single verses (*adārasṛt*). "Pour out the pressed juice on every side" (*parīto siñcatā sutam*) is the *pṛṣṭha* hymn of Kaulmalabarhiṣa. "The station of the gods" (*devasthānam*) is the triplet of Sāmans for the *adhyāsyā*. Dīrghatamas’s *arka*, "the king of Sāmans" (*sāmarāja*), is the *mādhyaṃdina*. "Thou, O Soma, art the sustainer" (*tvaṃ somāsi dhārayuḥ*) is the *gāyatra* and the *aśvasūkta*.

"O member, flow as a divine one for the feast of the gods"—this is the *sauparṇa* and the *vaiśvamanasa*. "Around that desirable, golden-hued one"—this is the *gaurīvita* and the *saṃkṛti*. "Near the born, the swift one"—this is the *pratīcīneḍa*; "Kāśīta is the last"—this is the *ārbhava*. With the exception of the last [verse], they consist of single verses. The rest is the same as on the ninth day of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*). Everything is in the *trivṛt* stoma. || 22 ||
Thus ends the ninth day.
The tenth day:

for the tenth day, the *bahiṣpavamāna* consists of five days' *anurūpas*: three single verses (*ekarcas*) and two triplets (*tṛcas*). [The first triplet begins: "High is the birth of your juice... (*uccā te jātam andhasaḥ*).

The *satra*s—consisting of the *madhyepṛṣṭhya* sacrifice, the *gāyatram*, the *āmahīyavam*, and the *ābhīkam*—have the *punānaḥ soma dhāraya* as their *antarotsedha* and *niṣedha*, and the *gaurīvitam*. These consist of single verses (*ekarca*). The *yajñāyajñīya* is the final [stotra] with the verse beginning "ā jāgṛviḥ. One extracts the *dvipadā*s. The rest is the same. It is a *trivṛt*. 23.

Thus: *asṛkṣata pravājinaḥ*, *pavamānasya viśvavit*, and *pavamāno ajījanat*—these three are single-verse hymns (*ekarcāḥ*). *ete asṛgram indavaḥ* and *pavasvendro vṛṣā sutaḥ* are two triplets (*tṛcau*) for the Bahiṣpavamāna. At the midday pressing, there are two triplets in Gāyatrī and Bṛhatī meters for the Sāman. In the Ārbhava Pavamāna, there is the extraction (*uddhāraḥ*) of the Sauhaviṣa triplet; the last one remains a triplet, while the others are placed upon the initial verses. The rest is the same as on the tenth day of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*). Everything is in the Trivṛt stoma;
the duties of the tenth day and the Mānasa cup are like those of the twelve-day rite.

The Udbhid and Balabhit [Sāmans] are for two days. For that Udbhid of Medhātithi, the Bṛhat is the Nidhana in the Vārkajambha [Sāman], the Raurava of Medhātithi, and the Gaurīvita for both; the rest is the same in the Anuṣṭubh.

Thus: because the tenth of the expanded Agniṣṭomas and the Udbhid are Rāthaṃtara, for the sake of avoiding sameness (ājāmya), there are twenty-eight days consisting of the Bṛhannidhana, Vārkañjabha, and Balabhit; in the seventh month, the two concluding Atirātras are the thirtieth. || 24 ||
The [stomas] are prescribed for the abhiplava days that have been turned back. || 25 ||
Thus; here, the prefix *pra* is attached for the purpose of denoting pervasion (*abhividhi*). || 25 ||
Regarding this, he states the specific detail:

for the first day of the first *abhiplava* among the repeated *abhiplavas*, [the verses] "mṛjyamānaḥ suhastya" and so on constitute an *aiḍa* hymn dedicated to the bull (*aukṣṇorandhra*) set to a single verse; the *kaṇvarathantara* is set to a single verse; the *varuṇasāman* is set to a single verse; and the *triṇidhana āyāsya* is set to three verses.
The rest is the same. 26.

Thus, because this day and the *balabhid* [stotra] belong to the *bṛhatī* metre, the *kaṇvarathantara* is employed for the sake of avoiding *ājāmya*; and on account of that, the *varuṇasāman* is prescribed here. || 26 ||
One extracts the Kaṇvarathantara, the Varuṇasāman, and the Bṛhatī from the subsequent [stotras], arranged in triplets. 27.

Thus: from the subsequent *abhiplava* periods, one should extract the *kaṇvarathantara*, *vāruṇa-sāman*, and [other] *sāmans*. This is because of the avoidance of *jāmi* (repetition of similar elements). Consequently, the meaning is that the *bṛhatī* is established by means of two triplets (*tṛca*) alone: "mṛjyamānaḥ suhastya" for the *aiḍa*, and "akṣṇorandhraṃ triṇidhanam" for the *āyāsya*. Therein, the eighth month consists of six-day periods (*ṣaḍaha*) repeated as two *abhiplavas*, a *pṛṣṭhya*, and again two *abhiplavas*. Likewise, there are three others. Even in the twelfth month, there are twenty days consisting of an *abhiplava*, a *pṛṣṭhya*, and an *abhiplava*. On the twentieth day, the *go-āyuṣī* [are performed]. || 27 ||
He states the arrangement for those two:
"The *go* and *āyus* [stomas] are for the one-year sacrifice; the two *bṛhatīs* are for the one-day sacrifice. (28)

Thus, the sequence for the Sāṃvatsara [sacrifices] is *āyus* and *gaur*. In that regard, it has been stated that the arrangement of *vārka-jambha* is for the sake of avoiding *jāmi* (monotony). Here, however, because of the transposition (*vyatihāra*) of those two, there is an absence of *jāmi*, and thus both are *bṛhatī* chants belonging to the one-day sacrifice (*aikāhika*). Within the *satra* sessions, there is the *pṛṣṭhya* [stoma]: namely, in the world of Gaur Vārka-jambha Dairghaśravasa, there is the Bārhaduktha; and in the world of Āyus Vārka-jambha, there is the Maidhātitha, and for him, the Raurava.
Thus ends the first section.
Section Two:
Now follows the Chandoma Daśāha. He states the arrangement for its first day:

These Soma juices flow toward their ancient, shining splendor, toward what is dear; being purified, Soma flows onward. The Soma drops have been released; purify for us rain like this. O Sage, your unceasing streams of Pavamāna flow forth.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, come for the feast"—with these [verses] are the offerings of clarified butter. ||2||

The Soma-hymns of the wise ones: the Gāyatra, the Aśva, the Somasāman, the Āśubhārgava, the Mārgīyava, the Ābhīka, the Aiḍa, the Sauparṇa, and the Rohitakūlīya. O Soma, for the banquet of the gods: the Pajra, the Dvaigata, the Pauruhanmana, the Hārāyaṇa, the Dvihiṃkāra, the Gauṅga, the Yaudhājaya, and the Auśana as the final one. 2.
[Thus is the Mādhyandina Pavamāna:
the Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Naudhasa, and the Kāleya. || 3 ||
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" consists of the Gāyatra-saṃhitā, the Śaiśava, the Kākṣīvata, and the Jarābodhīya; "pavasvendramaccha" is the Saphākṣāra; "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ" consists of the Gaurīvita and the Vaiśvāmitra; "asāvi soma indra te" is that which has its own womb (yoni); the Padanidhana, the Śuddhāśuddhīya, the Svāra, the Kautsa, and the Aurukṣaya; and the latter of these two, "adardar utsamasṛjaḥ," are the Audala and Gautama; and the final one is the Kāva.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. 5.
All [this] is the forty-eighth. || 5 ||
Thus ends the second section. || 2 ||
The third section of the second day:
Flow on as the leader of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull; O Soma, you are brilliant, the bull.

"Thou art indeed the back of the sacrificial sessions with thy light; this god is immortal"—from this ten-verse hymn, he extracts a triplet, omitting the last verse: "This very bull is the chariot; this is the steed urged by men; this is the seer praised aloud. Thy vital powers have arisen, O Pavamāna; we [belong] to thee. (1)
Thus concludes the Bahiṣpavamāna.

"Agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe"—with these [verses] are the Ājya[-stotras]. The Gāyatra, the Yauktāśva, the Surūpa, the Hariśrīnidhana, the Ājiga, the Svāra, the Sauparṇa, the Chandasya, the Yauktāśva, and the Carṣabha are the Pavamāna [stotras]. With "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā," the Samanta, the Dairghaśravasa, the Pṛṣṭha, the Yaśas, and the Kaulmalabarhiṣa are the Āyāsya [stotras]. "Vṛṣā śoṇaḥ"—this is the final Pārtha [stotra].
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.

The first [verse] is for Samanta Dīrghaśravas; the others are in the three [verses]. Because of the statement, "If there is one or two [verses] at the Mādhyandina [Pavamāna], they should be in the Bṛhatī [meter] alone," when performing them as single verses, one should place one at the beginning of the first [verse], and two in that same [verse]. || 3 ||
And the Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita, and the Mādhucchandasa. || 4 ||
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the *gāyatram*, the *hāviṣmatam*, the *śāmmadam*, the *dāvasunidhanam*, the *asitam*, and the *aśvasūktam*. "eṣa sya dhārayā sutaḥ pavasva devavītaye śaṅkusujñāne"; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"—this is the *gaurīvitam*, the *aiḍam*, the *kautsam*, the *bhargam*, the *asitam*, the *yadvāhiṣṭhīyam*, and the *krauñce*. Of these, the first and last [verses] are used. "vṛṣāmatīnāṃ pavate"—this is the final *yāma*. 5.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
At the Śaṅkusujñāna, there are two single-verse hymns.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
His own hymns. || 7 ||
"Sākamaśva," "evā hi asi," "vīrayuḥ," "ityāmahīyava," and "māṣṭādaṃṣṭra"—these are the Ukthas. All [of them] consist of forty-four verses. 7.
Thus ends the third section. ||3||

The Fourth Section of the Third Day: With brilliant luster, the gods have been poured forth; the King is led by the songs of wisdom. You, who bear manly powers, he goes with a subtle prayer. The drops have been poured forth along the path; the purifying Soma-streams have been let loose. Driving away adversaries, he flows for our nourishment; flow with your stream for our strength!
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
The *satra* offerings—namely, the *ājya* offerings beginning with "In the midst of the spine, fire is kindled by fire"—are performed. || 2 ||

"High is the birth of your juice"—this consists of the Gāyatra, the Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha, the Saumitra, the Aiṭata, the Sākamaśva, and the Vilambasauparṇa. "The Soma-drops, the Āyus"—this consists of the Paurumadga, the Sadoviśīya, the Gautama, the Antarikṣa, the Acchindra, the Maidhātitha, and the Aṣkāraṇidhana of Kaṇva. "Three voices"—this is the final *saṃkrośa* (shouting together) of the Āṅgirases. 3.
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The Paurumadga [hymn] is in the first [turn].
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Mahāviṣṭambha, and the Raurava. ||4||

Thus are the *pṛṣṭha* stotras. "Three voices arise" (*tisro vāca udīrate*) is the *gāyatra*, the *pāṣṭhauha*, the *aiḍa*, the *saindhukṣita*, the *auśana-vairūpa*, and the two *uṣṇih-kakubh* verses. "Press out, pour around, O friends, sit down" (*ā sotā pari ṣiñcata sakhāya ā niṣīdata*) is the *vācaḥsāman*, and the *śaukta*. "The pressed juices, most sweet" (*sutāso madhumattamāḥ*) is the *gaurīvita*, the *sādhra*, and the *śyāvāśva*; and the three *tvāṣṭrīsāmans*: the *aiḍa*, the *svāra*, and the *triṇidhana*. "This is your filter" (*pavitraṃ ta it*) is the *āriṣṭa*, which is the final one. || 5 ||
The Gaurīvita is in one verse; the Svāra is the first of two Tvaṣṭrī-sāmans.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
One's own hymns of praise. || 7 ||

The *pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *tairaścya* are the *ukthas*. The entire [chant] consists of forty [verses]. The rule states: "The *gautama* consists of forty. He utters the *hiṃ* call for thirteen [verses]: he with three, he with nine, he with one. He utters the *hiṃ* call for thirteen [verses]: he with one, he with three, he with nine. He utters the *hiṃ* call for thirteen [verses]: he with nine, he with one, he with three.

The *viṣṭuti* is arranged from the twenty-seven-fold up to the forty-nine-fold. Having chanted with the forty-nine-fold, one should introduce the middle verse of the triplet without the *ahiṃkāra*; that is called the *āskanda*. 7.
Thus ends the fourth section. || 4 ||
Fifth Section of the Fourth Day:

Pavamāna has brought forth; purifying himself, he has stepped forward. When, like restless cows, he rushes forth, flow swiftly, O thou of lofty thought! Toward the tawny one who possesses his own strength, let the sounding drops go forth like chariots.
The sacrificial offerings— the rays of light— send forth the Hero into the midst of the back-verse.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"Agni shall strike down the Vṛtras"—this is the *ājya* (offering verse) for the Hotṛ; his own [verses] follow next.
Thus end the offerings of clarified butter (ājya).
"May this Indra bestow upon you both that which is desirable"—these are the subsequent *ājya* offerings. ||2||

Flow on, O accomplisher of skill, with the *gāyatram* and the *ātharvaṇam*, ending with the desire for the *nidhana*; the *adārasṛt* and the *satrāsāhīyam*. "O Soma, in thee I have rejoiced"—this is the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭram*, the *ārkapuṣpam*, the *bārhaduktham*, and the *māṇḍavam*, ending with the *nidhana* "vidāvasu. The *ābhīśavam* and the *svaḥpṛṣṭham* belong to the *āṅgirasa*. "Soma flows, the progenitor of hymns"—this is the *janitra*, which is the final one. ||3||
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Traiśoka, and the Pṛśni. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.
"Pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ" is the Gāyatra, the Caurṇāyava, the Bṛhat Bhāradvāja, and the Mārgīyava with the *yadi* finale; its own [verses] are the *uṣṇih* and *kakubh*.
"O dear one, you indeed are the divine Soma, purifying yourself with your wave," [is said] according to the Bṛhat-kātīṣādīya.

The *gaurīvita* beginning with "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" and the *vārkajambha* with the *yadī* finale; the *śuddhāśuddhīya* and the *aiḍa* with the *iḍā*s; the *ākūpāra* and the *āndhīgava* on the ninth day; and the *lauśa* ending with "pra ta āśvinīḥ pavamāna dhenavaḥ. || 5 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. 6.
He recites his own hymns; he draws out the Ṣoḍaśin cup. ||7||
The Saindhukṣita, the Saubhara, and "the dear [hymn] of Vasiṣṭha" are the Ukthas; the whole [rite] consists of thirty-six [verses]. || 7 ||
Thus ends the fifth section. || 5 ||
The sixth section of the fifth day:
"utte śuṣmāsa īrate" is [the verse] before the Paryāsa.
The five-verse [hymn]. || 1 ||

Of Pavamāna, the knower of all, that wondrous and praiseworthy [glory], O Soma; the Soma-juices have flowed forth, and the Sage has flowed forth for the banquet of the gods. With our juice, [bring] barley after barley; and your powers, the sacrificial rites, rise up together toward the center of the back [of the altar].
Those streams of yours which drip with honey—thus [is] the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, we meditate upon the hymn"—this is the *ājya* (offering verse) of the Hotṛ;
his own [verses] follow thereafter.
"Even though there is much that is far away, arise together with vigor; O Indra and Agni, you two indeed [are here]"—these are the *ājya* verses. ||2||
The Gāyatrī [meter] belongs to itself. ||3||
"Flow on, O Soma, most resplendent"—this is the Gāyatra, the Yaṇva, the Śākala, and the Vārśa [hymns].

"Soma, pressed by the pressers" (Soma u ṣvāṇaḥ sotṛbhiḥ)—this is for the Mānava and Ānūpa [sāmans], and for the Vaiṣṇava [sāman]. "O Soma, with thee I have rejoiced" (tava ahaṃ soma rāraṇa)—of these, the first [is used]. The Yuktasruc, Vāma, Agneḥ triṇidhana, and "Indu, the steed, flows, rich in milk" (induḥ vājī pavate gonyoghāḥ)—these are the concluding verses (saṃpātyās).
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
In the first [verse] of the Mānava [school], because of the *bṛhatī* being first and following the Vaiṣṇava [hymn], there is the recitation of the modified (*ūha*) text. 4.
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Bārhadgira, and the Rāyovājīya. ||5||
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].

The *asāvyam̐śuḥ madāya* [verse], the *gāyatram*, the *saṃtani*, the *adhyardheḍam*, the *somasāma*, the *gauṣūktam*, the two *uṣṇih-kakubh*s in their own [proper places], and "abhi dyumnam bṛhad yaśaḥ prāṇāḥ śiśur mahīnām" [are used] in the *cyāvanakrośa*.

"Pavasva vājasātaye" is the Gaurīvita; "carṣabhaśca śākvaraḥ" and the Tvaṣṭrīsāman; and that which is the Dvyanutoda Trāsadasyava, the Aṣṭeḍa, and the Padastobha; "govit pavasva" is the Dvyabhyāghāta Lauśa as the final [Sāman]. || 6 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
Regarding the Cyāvana-krośa, there are two single-verse hymns. 6.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*;
[these are] one's own *ukthas*. 7.
The *ukthas* are "Saṃjaya," "Saumitra," and "Mahāvaiśvāmitra. The whole [section] consists of thirty-two [verses]. 7.

Of the ten-verse hymn for the sixth day beginning with "Pavasva devavīrati," he omits the final triplet. He omits the Aiḍa-aukṣṇorandhra; he omits the Svāra-vaidanvata; and the Gaurīvita in the Anuṣṭubh meter. Now, that which is the sixth day of the Pṛṣṭhya-stoma is thus arranged as a Triṃśa-stoma consisting of triplets.
Thus: "The vigorous ones have flowed forth; this very one, the ten fingers [have pressed]; flow on, O winner of the gods! This is the *triṃśastoma* *viṣṭuti*. 8.
Thus ends the sixth section. || 6 ||
The *satra*s— Section Seven, situated in the middle of the *pṛṣṭhya* period, belonging to the seventh day.

Those Soma drops which, having been pressed, have flowed forth like chariots from afar—the drops that, with their juice, bring us barley after barley—[bring] to you your skill that is bliss-bestowing. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna. "The righteous Vaiśvānara" is the Ājya-stotra for the Hotṛ;
his own [verses] follow. 2.
"Go forth to Mitra and Indra; O you of radiant luster, be most highly praised"—these are the *ājya* verses.
The Gāyatrī [meter] belongs to itself. ||3||
"Flow as a bull in a stream"—this is the Gāyatra, the Santani, the Aiḍa, the Sauparṇa, and the Rohitakūlīya.

The *punaḥsoma* with the *dhārā*, the *soma-sāman*, the *kaṇvarathantara*, the *paurumadga*, the *gauṅgava*, and the *dvinidhana āyāsya*; and the final [sāman] for the *vārāha* is "pra kāvyamuśaneva bruvāṇaḥ. 4.
In the case of the *soma-sāman* consisting of a single verse (*ekarca*), [the same applies]. ||4||
One's own backsides. || 5 ||
The *Bṛhat*, the *Vāmadevya*, the *Abhinidhana*, the *Kāṇva*, and the *Vaikhānasa* are the *pṛṣṭha* stotras.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is a *gāyatra* triplet; [it consists of] the *arkasāman* of Agni on three verses, the *jarābodhīya* on one verse, the *dakṣanidhana* on one verse, and two *uṣṇih* and *kakubh* verses on their own.
"This one, pressed with its stream, sits down for the friends"—thus [says] Śārkaraplava.

With the hymn beginning "purojitī vo andhasaḥ," one should recite the verses of Gaurīvita, Kārtayaśa, Ātreya, and Gautama, as well as the *dvipadā* verses of Sauhaviṣa; and with the hymn beginning "pro ayāsīt," the *aiḍa* verses of Yajñasārathin. 6.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna. The Gaurīvita [is chanted] on a single verse.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
His own hymns. ||7||
The Vātsapra, the Sauśravasa, and the Vīṅka are the Ukthas; the entire [rite] consists of twenty-eight [verses].
Thus ends the seventh section.
The eighth section of the eighth day:
"The rays urge on the Sun; these Soma juices flow toward the beloved [Soma]; being purified, Soma flows onward."
The sacrificial sessions—those whose vital strengths have arisen in the midst of the spine; flow around with this food-offering! 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, with all thy fires," is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ; his own [verses] follow next.
[Thus end the offerings of clarified butter.
Those belonging to the eighth day. 2.

"O Adhvaryu, [the Soma] pressed with stones"—this is the Gāyatra, the Vairūpa, the Āśu Bhārgava, the slow-paced Sauparṇa, and the Abhisomāsāyava; these include the Dvihiṅkāra, the Gāyatrapārśva, the Pauruhanmana, the Hārāyaṇa, and the Acchidra. "O, indeed, [I praise] the child"—this is the Vāsiṣṭha, which is the final [stotra]. 3.
Having sat upon a seat that is free from gaps. || 3 ||
One's own backsides. || 4 ||
The [qualities] belonging to the eighth stage.

"Pavasva deva āyuṣak" is the Gāyatra [sāman] on three verses; "svāśirāmarka" on one verse; "kakṣīvatama" on one verse; "bhāsama" on one verse; and the Uṣṇih and Kakubh [sāmans] on their respective [verses].
The two [sāmans] belonging to the eighth [day]:
"abhī no vājasātamam" is the Gaurīvita; and the Caḍa, the Kautsa, the Audala, and the Rayiṣṭha are their respective dharmas. "hā u dharta" is the Śārṅga, which is the last of the Aiḍas. 5.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Gaurīvita [Sāman] is on one verse. 6.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
His own hymns. || 6 ||
The eighth [categories] are all twenty-eight. 6.
Thus ends the eighth section. ||8||
The Ninth Section: Of the ninth day— Hither [I call] the one born near the waters, the swift one; this immortal god, the bull, has been pressed for drinking.

Flow with this stream, O Sage, as thou art being purified. 1. Hither [I call] the one born near the waters, the swift one; this immortal god, the bull, has been pressed for drinking. Flow with this stream, O Sage, as thou art being purified.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"Upa tvā raṇvasaṃdṛśam"—this is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ; his own [verses] follow next.
[Thus the offerings of clarified butter.
The sacrificial sessions (*satra*s)—the ninth-day rites in the middle of the *pṛṣṭhya* period. 2.

"Pavamānasya jighnataḥ" is a *gāyatra* hymn; "Adārasṛt," "Iḍānām saṃkṣāraḥ," and "Ṛṣabhaḥ pāvamānaḥ"; "Parīto siñcatā sutam" is a *devasthāna* hymn; "Saṃkṛtiḥ" and "Dairghaśravasam"; and "Hā u hu vā akrān" is the final hymn of Dīrghatamas, belonging to the Vasiṣṭha family. The hymn "Arkaḥ" of Dīrghatamas is for the *adhyāsya* [chanting].
One's own backsides. ||4||
The ninth [chapter]. ||4||

"O Soma, you are the sustainer"—this Gāyatra verse is recited over three verses; the hymn of the horse over one verse; the *pratīcīna-iḍa* over one verse; the *hāviṣkṛta* over one verse; and the *uṣṇih* and *kakubh* meters over their respective verses.
The two belonging to the ninth [chapter].
"Pari tyam haryatam harim" is the Gaurīvita and the Vāṅnidhana; "Krauñca" is the Sādhra in its own verses; "asāvi somo aruṣo vṛṣā hariḥ" is the Aiḍa-yāma at the end. 5.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
Gaurīvita is performed on a single verse. 5.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*;
[these are] their own *ukthas*.
The ninth [section] consists of all fifteen [verses]. 6.
Regarding the tenth day:

now, that which was the ninth day of the ten-night period consisting of the *chandomas* becomes here the tenth day. For it, [the *stotras* are]: the *Gaurīvita* on one verse; the *Auṣṇiha* with a single *nidhana* on one verse; the *Śyāvāśva* on one verse; and the *Āndhīgava* on three verses. ||7||
The rest is the same.

"Thus: 'The vigorous ones have been let loose; Pavamāna, the all-knower, has generated them. 'These drops have been let loose; flow, O Indu, as a bull, pressed according to his ancient splendor'—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna."

"Suṣamidhā na ā vaha," "yad adya sūra udite," "u tvā mandantu somāḥ," and "indrāgnī ā gatam sutam"—these are the *ājya* verses. "Suṣamidhā" consists of four *ṛc*s. The *uddhāra* (selection) is according to the *gotra*. "Uccā te jātam andhasaḥ" includes the *gāyatram*, the *cāmahīyavam*, the *ājigam*, and the *abhīkam*. "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā" includes the *utsedha*, the *maidhātitham*, the *niṣedha*, and the *ajāgṛvi*; the last one belongs to the *auśana* [family].
The Rathantara, Vāmadevya, Naudhasa, and Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras.

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" and "gāyatra" are the *saṃhita* chants; "pavasvendramaccha" and "sapha" are the *rohitakūlīya* chants; "paryū ṣu" and so forth are the *satrāṇi* chants—the *gaurīvitam* is placed in the middle of the *pṛṣṭhya* sequence, the *adhyāsyāyām*. The *auṣṇiha* with the *ekonidhana* is on the second day; the *śyāvāśva* is on the third day; the *āndhīgava* is on all three days. "para pra dhanva" and so forth is the *vājajit*; the *kāva* chant, containing the word "sūrya," is the final one.

The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *daśadharma* and the *mānasa* are like those of the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*). All the *stotras* are twenty-four-fold (*caturviṃśa*). In this case, only the *ṛks* and *sāmans* are extended from the tenth day; the *stoma* is not. Therefore, the determination in the *sūtra* is that both the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* and the *mānasa* are indeed twenty-four-fold.
The Mahāvrata and the Atirātra; the Mahāvrata and the Atirātra.
Thus concludes the annual vow; the Atirātra sacrifice is the archetypal form.
Thus ends the ninth section.
The Ādityānām Ayana is completed.
Thus ends the tenth chapter from the beginning—the second chapter on the *sattras*—in this commentary on the *Ārṣeyakalpa*, composed by Varadarāja, son of the venerable Vāmanārya.

The Atirātra is arranged before the Pṛṣṭhya; the Caturviṃśa day is arranged; the Pṛṣṭhya is arranged; the first day of the Abhiplava is arranged. Just as in the middle of the Pṛṣṭhya, for the second day there are the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa*, the *paryāsa* is "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam," and the *bṛhatī* [is used]; the rest is the same. The third day is arranged as the *trivṛt*. Just as in the middle of the Pṛṣṭhya, for the fourth day there are the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa*, the *paryāsa* is "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam," and the *bṛhatī* [is used]; the rest is the same.

The fifth day is arranged as the *trivṛt*; in the middle of the *pṛṣṭhya* [ṣaḍaha], for the sixth day, there is the *gaurīvita* on one verse, the *auṣṇiha* with a single *nidhana* on one verse, the *śyāvāśva* on one verse, and the *āndhīgava* on three verses; the rest is the same as the *mahāvrata* and the *atirātra*, the *mahāvrata* and the *atirātra*. 111.

The Atirātra is prepared before the Pṛṣṭhya; the Caturviṃśa day is prepared; the Pṛṣṭhya is prepared; the first day of the Abhiplava is prepared. Just as in the middle of the Pṛṣṭhya, for the second day there are the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa*, the *paryāsa* being "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam," and the *bṛhatī*; the rest is the same. The third day is prepared as the *trivṛt*. Just as in the middle of the Pṛṣṭhya, for the fourth day there are the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa*, the *paryāsa* being "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam," and the *bṛhatī*; the rest is the same.

The fifth day is prepared with the *trivṛt* stoma; in the middle of the *pṛṣṭhya* [ṣaḍaha], there is the *soma-sāman* for the sixth day, which is both swift (*āśu*) and the *bhārgava*. [The verses] "pra soma devavītaye" [are used for] the *pajra*, *gauṅgava*, *yaudhājaya*, and *auśana*; the last is the *rathaṃtara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *naudhasa*, and the *kāleya*. With the verse "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā," the *gāyatra* is combined; "pavasvendramaccha" is the *saphākṣāra*; "pra sunvānāyāndhasa" is the *gaurīvita*, the *gautama* with the *padanidhana*, the *śuddhāśuddhīya*, and the *kāva* as the final one; the *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. 112.

Flow on as the leader of speech; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. O Soma, you are brilliant; for you are indeed a bull by your radiance. This very one is the bull, the chariot; your vital strengths have stood up. Flow with your stream, O Pavamāna! "We choose Agni as our messenger"—with these [verses] are the *ājya* stotras. "Flow on as a bull, O stream"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *yauktāśva*, and the *surūpa*. "O bull," and "Pavamāna, being purified, O Soma, with your stream"—this is the *pṛṣṭha* and the *yaśas*. [These belong to] Kaulmalabarhiṣa. In the *āsyā* [stotra], [the verse begins] "The bull, the red one."

The *pārtha* is the final [stotra]; the *bṛhat*, the *vāmadevya*, the *śyaita*, and the *mādhucchandasa*; the *gāyatra* beginning with "yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"; the *hāviṣmat* and the *āsitatama*; the *śaṅkusujñāna* beginning with "eṣa sya dhārayā sutaḥ pavasva devavītaye"; the *gaurīvita* beginning with "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"; the *bharga* and the *āsitakrauñca*; the *yāma* beginning with "vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate"; the *yajñāyajñīya* as the final [stotra], which is the *agniṣṭomasāman*. These are one's own *ukthas*. 113.

The drops have been poured forth with glittering radiance; the King is approached with sacred hymns. To you, who bear manly powers, this [sacrificer] approaches with a subtle prayer. Striking down adversaries, he flows for the sake of nourishment. Flow with your stream; Agni is kindled by Agni—thus [are the verses]. The *ājya* offerings consist of the *gāyatra* "High is your birth from the plant," the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*, the *saumitra*, and the *aiṭata*; the *paurumadga* "The Soma-drops, the Āyus," the *gautama*, the *antarikṣa*, the *maidhātitha*, the *aṣkāraṇidhana*, and the *kāṇva*.

"Tisro vācaḥ" is the *saṃkrośa* of the Aṅgirases; the last [verses] are the *rathaṃtara*, the *vāmadevya*, the *mahāvaiṣṭambha*, and the *raurava*. "Tisro vāca udīrata" is the *gāyatra*, the *pāṣṭhauha*, the *aiḍa*, and the *saindhukṣita*; [the verses] "sve uṣṇikkakubhau" are the *sutāso madhumattamāḥ*; the *gaurīvita*, the three *tvāṣṭrīsāmans*, the *aiḍa*, the *svāra*, and the *triṇidhana*. "Pavitraṃ te" is the *ariṣṭa*; the last is the *yajñāyajñīya*, the *agniṣṭomasāman*; these are their own *ukthas*. 114

The six-verse hymn beginning with *babhrave nu svatavase*—the *Satrāsāhīya*, the *Māṇḍava*, the *Mārgīyava*, and the *Śuddhāśuddhīya*—these he extracts. Now, that which was the fourth day of the previous Chandoma-daśāha, that is here arranged as a triplet; the thirty-verse [hymn] is arranged as the fifth day, just as in the middle of the Pṛṣṭhya. For the sixth day, before the *Paryāsa*, there is the triplet beginning with *ayā vītī pari srava*; in the *Auksnorandhra* [day], there is the *Antarārkapuṣpa*; the *Yacchandasya* and the *Payas* are the four [hymns] belonging to Vaidanvata.
The Gaurīvita is in the Anuṣṭubh meter; now, that which is the sixth day of the Pṛṣṭhya-stoma, this is arranged as a triplet, consisting of thirty-six verses.

The Soma drops that have been pressed afar, like chariots, have been let loose upon their path—just as swift cattle rush forth. Flow quickly, O thou of lofty mind, for us, like grain after grain, with thy juice. [The verses beginning] "Thy skill, which brings bliss," "the Truth-abiding Vaiśvānara"—these are the *ājya* of the Hotṛ. His own [verses] follow. His own is the *gāyatrī*; in it are the *gauḥ-uktha*, the *śākala*, and the *somasāman* "O Soma, purifying, with thy stream," the *kaṇvarathaṃtara*, the *paurumadga*, the *gautama*, the *vāśa*, the *gauṅgava*, and the two-toned (*dvinidhana*) chant.

"Proclaiming his wisdom like Uśanas" (cāyāsyaṃ pra kāvyamuśaneva bruvāṇaḥ); "The boar's [hymn]" (vārāham) as the final [part]; his own *pṛṣṭha* chants; "That exhilaration of yours which is most excellent" (yaste mado vareṇyaḥ); the *gāyatra* chant; the *arka* of Agni; the *jarābodhīya*; the *dakṣiṇidhana*; his own *uṣṇih* and *kakubh* meters; "With the conquest of your soma-juice" (purojitī vo andhasaḥ); the *gaurīvita* and the *kārtayaśa*; the two *tvāṣṭrī-sāmans*; the *svāra* and the *akāraṇidhana*; the *ātreyasāman* and the *gautamasāman*; the *sauhaviṣa* among the *dvipadā* verses; "He has gone forth" (pro ayāsīt)—this is the *aiḍa* chant; the *yajñasārathi* as the final [part].

The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*; its own *ukthas* follow. Then, those two days of the *chandomavat* ten-night rite which are the forty-four-versed and the forty-eight-versed, these two are the *gaurīvita* on the *anuṣṭubh* verses. And that which was the tenth day of the former *chandomavat* ten-night rite, that here is the tenth day, consisting of both the *mahāvrata* and the *atirātra*. 116.

The passage for Dṛti and Vātava is prepared with the *vidhṛti* verses. He extracts the *ukthas* from the *trivṛt* stomas up to the twenty-seven-fold; the *ṣoḍaśin* from the fifteen-fold; the *vārṣāhara* and *vāmadevyas* from the seventeen-fold; and the *arkas*, the *utsedha*, the *niṣedha*, and the *udvāṃśīya* from the twenty-one-fold. He extracts these, including the fourth triplet beginning "pra svānāso rathā iva" before the *paryāsa*, the nine-verse hymn after the *āmahīyava*, and the *jarābodhīya* before the *raurava* and *yaudhājaya*.

The *Dvihiṅkāra* [is performed] for Medhātithi; the *Gaurīvita* follows after the *Uttara*; the *Śuddhāśuddhīya* for Śyāvāśva; everything else is the same. With the *Rathantara* [Sāman], with the twenty-one-fold [Stoma], and with the verse "āśur ṛṣabho bṛhanmataḥ," there is a six-verse hymn preceding the *Paryāsa*. The *Hāviṣmata* follows after the *Uttara*; the two [Sāmans] for Ājiga and Āyāsya come first; the *Samanta* and *Dairghaśravasa* follow after the *Gaurīvita*; the *Madhuścunnidhana* and *Asita* [follow]; everything else is the same. With this very [set of Sāmans], using the twenty-one-fold [Stoma] belonging to the *Bṛhat*, he performs the month in reverse order. This is the fourth [month].

The *tṛca* and both *paryāsa*s are as follows: after the *āśubhārgava*, the *mārgīyava*; the *dvaigata* is in the middle of the *bārhatas*; after the *saṃhitā*, the *kākṣīvatabhāsa*; the rest is the same. With the *rāthaṃtara* *triṇava* chant, [the priest] drives away the enemies with the verse, "O Pavamāna, drive away the adversaries. Before the *paryāsa* *tṛca*, after the *svārātsauparṇa*, comes the *harīśrinidhana*, the *arkapuṣpa*; it is in the middle of the *bārhatas*. After the *maukṣa*, there are the *śāṃmada* and the *dāvasunidhana*.

The rest is the same as that [of the Gavām Ayana], except for this: by means of the Bārhata Triṇava, there is a reversal of these two; there are twenty-nine days, the Mahāvrata, and the Viṣuvat. Then these very months are reversed; by those reversed months, one performs the six subsequent months. Of these, the first day is the Ekānnatriṃśa. The Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana is arranged according to the Dṛtivātavator Ayana up to the Daśarātra. The Daśarātra is well-known; the Vrata is well-known; the Atirātra is well-known. This is the Vivṛti.
The eleventh chapter:
the *pṛṣṭhya* [period] preceding [the sacrifice],
also known as the *Aṅgirasa-ayanam*.

The first section: the Atirātra; the twenty-four-fold Prāyaṇīya day; the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha; four Abhiplava-ṣaḍahas consisting of Trivṛt-stomas—this constitutes one month. This is the second, the third, the fourth, and the fifth month. [In the fifth month: three Abhiplava-ṣaḍahas consisting of Trivṛt-stomas; a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha; a Trivṛt Bṛhaspatisāman; three Svarasāmans; the Divākīrtya day; three Svarasāmans; an Ukthya consisting of Pañcadaśa-stomas and the Indra-stoma; a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha beginning with the Trayastriṃśa-stoma.

One *trivṛt* *abhiplava* six-day period; ten days of the twelve-day rite arranged as *agniṣṭomas* consisting of *trivṛt* stomas; two days for the *udbhicca* and *balamica*; four *trivṛt* *abhiplava* six-day periods; a *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period—this constitutes one month. That is the second, that the third, and that the fourth. Two *trivṛt* *abhiplava* six-day periods; a *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period; the *āyuḥ* and *go* days; the ten-day period of the *chandomas*; the twenty-four-fold stoma as the first day; two twenty-eight-fold stomas; the thirty-fold stoma; and the thirty-two-fold stoma.

The thirty-sixth, the fortieth, the forty-fourth, the forty-eighth, the twenty-fourth, the Mahāvrata, and the Atirātra—by means of this Anuvāka beginning with "the Pṛṣṭhya of the Aṅgirases," the Aṅgirasām Ayana is described; that very [sacrifice] is called the Purastāt-pṛṣṭhya.
The Atirātra is prepared before the Pṛṣṭhya; the Caturviṃśa day is prepared; the Pṛṣṭhya is prepared;
and the first day of the Abhiplava is prepared, just as [it is] in the middle of the Pṛṣṭhya.
The Atirātra is according to the archetype. The Caturviṃśa and the Pṛṣṭhya are as in the Saṃvatsara sacrifice. The first day of the Abhiplava is like that of the Madhyedvipṛṣṭha. ||1||
The *satra*s: before [the central] *pṛṣṭhya* [day], for the second day there are the *stotrīya* and *anurūpa* verses, and the *paryāsa* verse is "Parīto ṣiñcatā sutam" (Sing forth the pressed juice);
this is a *bṛhatī*. The rest is the same. It is the *trivṛt* [stoma]. 2.

Thus: "Parīto siñcatā sutam" (Pour out the pressed juice on all sides), which belongs to Mādhucchandas; "Bharga aiḍam āyāsyam," which consists of three Sāman verses; the *triṇidhana* [Sāman] is on the middle verse. It is in the *bṛhatī* meter. The rest is the same as the second day of the six-day period (*abhiplava*) of the year-long sacrifice. Everything is in the *trivṛt* stoma. || 2 ||

The third day is arranged as it is in the middle of the *pṛṣṭhya* [ṣaḍaha]. For the fourth day, there are the *stotrīya*, the *anurūpa*, and the *paryāsa*. The *bṛhatī* verse is "parīto ṣiñcatā sutam"; the rest is the same. It is the *trivṛt* [stoma]. 3.
Thus: "Pavamāna has been born; purifying himself, he has stepped forth"—with these [verses] for the *bahispavamāna*.

For the two subsequent *pavamānas*, there are single verses, excluding the final one. "Pour out the pressed juice on all sides"—this is the *pṛśni* of Ātharvaṇa; "the *ābhīśava*" refers to the triplet of Sāmans. The arrangement of the *bṛhatī* is according to the *yaudhājaya* and the *adhyāsya*. Everything else is equal to the fourth day of the *abhiplava* of the year-long sacrifice. All is *trivṛt*. 3.

The fifth day is arranged as in the *madhyepṛṣṭhya*. For the sixth day, there are the *stotrīya*, *anurūpa*, and *paryāsa* verses. "O Indu, for Indra accompanied by the Maruts" (*indrāyendo marutvate*) is the *gāyatra* hymn on one verse; the *āśvasūkta* on one verse; "O bestower of booty" (*vājadāvarya*) on one verse; "Being cleansed by the skillful-handed one" (*mṛjyamānaḥ suhastya*) is the *aiḍa aukṣṇorandhra* on one verse; the *varuṇasāman* on one verse; and the *triṇidhana āyāsya* on one verse. The rest is the same. It is the *trivṛt* [stoma]. 4.

"Thus they have been let loose, the prize-winners; ten fingers [have impelled] that one, O Sage, as you flow clear"—with these verses is the *bahispavamāna* performed. At the midday pressing, the two *sāman*-verses for the *gāyatrī* and *bṛhatī* meters are as previously stated. For the two subsequent *pavamāna* lauds, only the final triplet is used. The rest is the same as on the sixth day of the six-day period (*abhiplava*) of the year-long sacrifice.

The [stotras] are prepared for the recurring *abhiplava* days. For the first day of the first recurring *abhiplava*, there is the *gāyatra* [sāman] "indrāyendo marutvate" on a single verse; on that same verse is the *aśvasūkta*. There is the *aiḍa* [sāman] "mṛjyamānaḥ suhastya" on a single verse of the *aukṣṇorandhra*; on that same verse is the *kaṇvarathantara*. There is the *varuṇasāman* on a single verse; there is the *triṇidhana āyāsya* on a single verse.
The rest is the same. || 5 ||

Thus, for the sake of avoiding monotony (*ajāmitva*), the *Kaṇvarathantara* has been prescribed here in the *bṛhatī* [verse], as in the case of the *pṛṣṭha* [stotra]. And by virtue of that, the *vājadāvarya* [verses] have been extracted from the *gāyatrī* for the purpose of achieving the required *stoma*. || 5 ||
The Kaṇvarathantara [Sāman] rescues them from the higher worlds; the Vājadāvarya [Sāman] causes them to return to their own world.

It has been stated that because of the absence of *jāmi* (repetition) in the *abhiplava* days, the *kaṇvarathantara* should be extracted from them. Consequently, on the first fortnight (*pūrva-pakṣas*), the *vājadāvarya* verses return to their own proper place: the *gāyatra* on one verse, the *āśvasūkta* on one verse, and the *vājadāvarya* on one verse.
The annual [Soma sacrifice] and the Go-āyus [sacrifice] are not modified.

Thus it is said. For here the sequence is "life-span, cow, year. Consequently, for the sake of avoiding sameness (*ājāmya*), the sacrificial sessions (*satra*) have the *go* and *āyus* [stomas] at the very beginning of the *pṛṣṭhya* period in the one-year rite; however, unlike those in the middle of the *pṛṣṭhya*, these two do not have *bṛhatī*s in the one-day rites (*aikāhika*). This is the meaning. || 7 ||
Thus ends the first section. 2.
The second section:
[The text] states the first day of the Chandoma-daśāha:
"His ancient, shining splendor... "These Soma juices flow toward the beloved [splendor], O Agni; you purify the lifespans, O Sage, as Pavamāna. (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, come for the feast"—with these [verses] are the butter-offerings.

"O Soma juices, [inspire] the wise ones"—this is the Gāyatra, the Aśva, and the Soma-sāman Āśubhārgava; "O Soma, for the feast of the gods"—this is the Pajra, the Gauṅgava, the Yaudhājaya, the Auśana, and the final one. ||3||
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
The Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, the Naudhasa, and the Kāleya. 4.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" is the Gāyatra-saṃhitā; "pavasvendram accha" is the Sapha with the Akṣara [Nidhana]; "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ" is the Gaurīvita, the Gautama, the Padanidhana, the Śuddhāśuddhīya, and the Kava as the final [Sāman]. || 5 ||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman. 6.
And all [of this] consists of twenty-four. ||6||
Thus ends the second section. || 2 ||

The Third Section; the second day is described: Flow on, the foremost of speech! Flow on, O Indu, pressed as a bull! O Soma, you are brilliant; for you are indeed a bull by your radiance. This very one is a bull, a chariot; your vital strengths have stood up. Flow with this stream of yours, O Pavamāna; we [belong] to you, the purifying one.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.

"Agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe"—with these [verses] are the *ājya* lauds. "Vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā," the *gāyatra*, the *yauktāśva*, the *surūpa*, and the *carṣabha* are the *pavamāna*. "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā" is the *pṛṣṭha* and the *yaśas*; "kaulmalabarhiṣāyāsye" is the *pārtha*, with "vṛṣā śoṇaḥ" as the final [verse].
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna. The sacrificial sessions (*satra*s) — the *pṛṣṭhya* [period] is first; the *pṛṣṭha* [stotra] is on the first day. 3.
And the Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita, and the Mādhucchandasa. ||4||
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the *gāyatram*, rich in oblation, and dark; "eṣa sya dhārayā sutaḥ pavasva devavītaye"—this is at the *śaṅkusujñāna*; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"—this is the *gaurīvitam* and the *bharga*, both being dark and *krauñca*; "vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate"—this is the final *yāma*. 5.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
The Gaurīvita [is sung] on one verse; and the Krauñca is the last of three verses. || 5 ||
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
His own hymns. ||7||
The second [set of] verses. All [of them] are the twenty-eighth. 7.
Thus ends the third section. ||3||
