The *ājya* verses are "By fire fire is kindled" (*agnināgniḥ samidhyate*). Then follows the *gāyatra* hymn "High is thy birth from the plant" (*uccā te jātam andhasaḥ*), the *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*, the *saumitra*, the *aiṭata*, the *paurumadga* "Toward us, O Somas, the Āyus" (*abhi somāsa āyavaḥ*), the *gautama*, the *antarikṣa*, the *maidhātitha*, the *aṣkāraṇidhana*, and the *kāṇva*. Finally, there is the "Lament of the Aṅgirases" (*tisro vācaḥ*) as the concluding part.
Thus concludes the Mādhyandina Pavamāna.
In the case of the *adhyāsya* [chant], there is the *āṣkāra-nidhana*. || 3 ||
The Rathaṃtara, the Vāmadevya, the Mahāvaiṣṭambha, and the Raurava. || 4 ||
The hearts and backs.
"Three voices have arisen"—this is the Gāyatra, the Pāṣṭhauha, the Aiḍa, and the Saindhukṣita; the Uṣṇih and Kakubh are in their own [proper] places.
The sacrificial sessions (*satrāṇi*): first the *pṛṣṭhya*, then two *tārtīya* days.

The *sutāsaḥ* [hymn], which is most rich in sweetness; the *gaurīvita*; and the three *tvāṣṭrīsāmans*: the *aiḍa*, the *svāra*, and the *triṇidhana*. The *pavitraṃ te* [hymn] is the *ariṣṭa*; this is the final [set].
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
Gaurīvita is sung on a single verse. 5.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
One's own hymns.
The Tārtikas; all [these] are the twenty-eighth.
Thus ends the fourth section. || 4 ||
The fifth section describes the fourth day:
"To Babhru, indeed, the self-strong," this six-verse hymn; the Satrāsāhīya, the Māṇḍava, the Mārgīyava, and the Śuddhāśuddhīya—these he extracts. ||1||
Now, that which was the fourth day of the former Chandoma-daśāha is this very Tricaklṛpta Triṃśa.

Thus [it is said]. For the fourth [stotra] of the former [sacrifice] consists of thirty-six [verses]. Therein, for the sake of establishing its state of having thirty [verses], one should extract the six-verse hymn beginning with *babhrave nu svatavase* from the Bahiṣpavamāna; the *Satrāsāhīya* from the Mādhyandina; the *Māṇḍava*, the *Ārbhava*, and the *Mārgīyava-śuddha-aśuddhīya* from the Ārbhava-pavamāna. Three [of these] are to be repeated. The remainder is the same. 2.
The fifth day is arranged just as [the central day] is in the middle of the *pṛṣṭhya* [stoma].

For the sixth day, the triplet beginning with "ayāvītī pari srava" is placed before the *paryāsa*; the *aukṣṇorandhra* contains the *arkapuṣpa*, which belongs to the meters; the fourth [stotras] consist of the *vaidanvata* verses; and the *gaurīvita* is in the *anuṣṭubh* meter. 4.
Now, that which is the sixth day of the *pṛṣṭhya-stoma* is this arrangement of three-day periods (*tṛca*): the thirty-six-fold. 5.

"Thus they have been let loose; the vigorous ones [have flowed] forward. Ten fingers [urge] that one; flow for the sake of the gods, O Soma! Win both ancient [treasures] and conquer! The exhilarating one runs forth; flow around as a non-failing one. "These Somas have been let loose"—this is the *Bahispavamāna* chant.
O Agni, that mortal whom you protect in battles—when the sun has risen, shatter all our enemies. For you two are the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) of the sacrifice; thus [are] the *ājya* offerings.

"O Indu, for Indra accompanied by the Maruts"—this is the *gāyatra*, the *ceṣovṛdhīya*, the *gāyatrī*, the *krauñca*, the *vājadāvarya*, and the *dārḍhacyuta*. "Being cleansed by the skillful hand"—this is the *aiḍa*, the *aukṣṇorandhra*, and the *satrāṇi*. The *pṛṣṭhya* is preceded by these;

the latter is the *vārkapuṣpa*, the *svāra*, the *aukṣṇorandhra*, the *vājajit*, and the *varuṇasāma*. "The stall of the Aṅgirases"—"Flow on with this purification, bringing these riches"—this is the final *vāsiṣṭha* which contains the word "here."
The Bṛhat and Vāmadevya [Sāmans], the Ṛṣabha, Raivata, and Śyena [Sāmans] are the Pṛṣṭhas.

"Parisvāno giriṣṭhāḥ"—this is the Gāyatra, the three Vaidanvata hymns, and the *payaḥ* chant; "sasunve yo vasūnāṃ taṃ vaḥ sakhāyo madāya"—this is the Dīrgha Kārṇaśravasa; "somāḥ pavanta indavaḥ"—this is the Gaurīvita, the Madhuścunnidhana, and the Krauñca with the *vāṅnidhana* and *aiḍa* chants; and "jyotir yajñasya"—this is the Marutāṃ Dhenu as the final [chant].
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. The *ukthas* are "gūrdaṃ bhadram," "udvaṃśaputra," and so forth. Everything consists of thirty-six [verses]. 5.
Thus ends the fifth section. ||5||
The sixth section describes the seventh day:

Those Soma drops which, like chariots, have been let loose from afar, flowing forth like eager cattle upon their path—O thou of lofty mind, flow swiftly with thy juice toward our barley after barley; [bring] that skillful one who is the source of bliss. 1.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
The *ājya* for the Hotṛ priest is addressed to Vaiśvānara, the upholder of cosmic order (*ṛtāvan*). His own subsequent [verses] follow. These are the verses belonging to the seventh [day].
The Gāyatrī is its own [meter]. In it, there are the Gauḥ-sūkta and the Śākala.
"Flow on as a bull, O stream"—this is the Gāyatra, the Saṃtani, the Aiḍa, the Sauparṇa, the Rohitakūlīya, the Goṣūkta, and the Śākala.

The *punaḥsoma* with the *dhārā*, the *soma-sāman*, the *kaṇvarathantara*, the *paurumadga*, the *gautama*, the *vāśa*, the *gauṅgava*, the *dvinidhana*, the *āyāsya*, and the *vārāha* ending with "pra kāvyam uśanāiva bruvāṇaḥ. (3)
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna. The Soma-sāman is on a single verse. 3.
One's own backsides. 4.
The sacrificial sessions (*satra*s)— namely, those consisting of seven-day periods, beginning with the *pṛṣṭhya* day at the front.
"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the Gāyatra [Sāman] of Agni, as well as the Ārka, the Jarābodhīya, and the Dakṣiṇidhana; likewise, the two Uṣṇih and Kakubh [Sāmans] belonging to the seventh [day].

"Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Gaurīvita and the Kārtayaśa; the two Sāmans for Tvaṣṭṛ are the Svāra and the Akāraṇidhana; the Ātreya and the Gautama are in the Dvipadā verses; and the Sauhaviṣa is "pro ayāsīt"; the Aiḍa is "yajñasārathi," which is the final one. 5.
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.

The Gaurīvita is on one verse; the Svara-sāman, belonging to Tvaṣṭṛ’s daughter, is on the two following verses, according to the statement in the Upagrantha: "In the fifth or seventh day of the Chandoma-daśāha."
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*;
its own *ukthas*. 6.
The [sections] belonging to the seventh [book]; all [of them] consist of forty [stanzas]. 6.
For he arranges it in the eighth and ninth [days]:
"Now, those two days of the ten-night period consisting of meters which are the forty-fourth and the forty-eighth, these are they; in both cases, the Gaurīvita [Sāman] is on the Anuṣṭubh verses. (7)
Thus he speaks of the tenth day:
"Now, that which was the tenth day of the previous Chandoma-daśāha, that here is the tenth day."
Thus [ends the seventh verse].
The Mahāvrata and the Atirātra. 8.
Thus ends the Aṅgirasām Ayana, [chapter] 8.
Thus ends the sixth section. ||6||
The seventh section: The course of Dṛti and Vātāvati.

It consists of an Atirātra, a month with the Trivṛt-stoma, a month with the Pañcadaśa, a month with the Saptadaśa, a month with the Ekaviṃśa, a month with the Triṇava, a month with the Trayastriṃśa, a Mahāvrata, a month with the Trayastriṃśa, a month with the Triṇava, a month with the Ekaviṃśa, a month with the Saptadaśa, a month with the Pañcadaśa, a month with the Trivṛt, and an Atirātra; thus is the course of Dṛti and Vātāvati described.
The path of Dṛti and Vātāvata was prepared by means of the *vidhṛti* measures up to the twenty-sevenfold [stomas]. ||1||
Regarding this, he states the specific details:

from the *trivṛt* [stomas] he extracts the *ukthas*; from the *pañcadaśa*, the *ṣoḍaśin*; from the *saptadaśa*, the *vārka-jambha* and the *udvaṃśīya*; and from the *ekaviṃśa*, the *arkas*, the *utsedha*, and the *niṣedha*. These end with the *udvaṃśīya*. He extracts the fourth triplet of verses.

The *satra*s—beginning with the *pṛṣṭhya* day—are as follows: all the *agniṣṭoma*s are based on the *trivṛt*; the *ukthya*s are based on the *pañcadaśa*. There is no *ṣoḍaśin* here on the tenth day. On the first day of the *saptadaśa* stomas, there is the *vārkajaṃbha*; on the twelfth day, the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* alone, ending with the *ukthya*. There is no *udvaṃśīya*. On the ninth day of the *ekaviṃśa* stomas, there is the *saṃhita* alone; on the tenth day, the *maukṣa* alone. There is no *svāśira* hymn by Arka. On the eleventh day, the *kāva* alone; there is no hymn by Dīrghatamas. On the twelfth day, between the two *āyāsya*s, there is the *dairghaśravasa*.

Regarding the *notsedha* and *niṣedha* [chanting]: on that very day, the *uktha* hymns are those beginning with "aṣṭādaṃṣṭra," but they do not end with the *udvaṃśīya*. In that regard, all the months should be performed by alternating between the *rāthantara* and *bārhata* [stomas]. On the first day of the month consisting of twenty-seven verses (*triṇava*), he says:

The nine verses beginning with *pra svānāso rathā iva* form the *paryāsa*; following the *āmahīyava*, the *jarābodhīya* follows; the *raurava* and *yaudhājaya* precede it; the *dvihiṃkāra* follows the *aidhātithe*, and the *gaurīvitā* follows it; the *śuddhāśuddhīya* follows the *śyāvāśva*. The rest is the same as that of the *rāthantara* twenty-one-fold chant.

Thus: in the *Bahispavamāna*, there is the fourth triplet, "The King goes with the *medhātithi* verses"; its exclusion [from the sequence] is intended. The mention of both the *Raurava* and the *Yaudhājaya* is for the purpose of establishing their immediate succession. For in the twenty-one-fold chant (*ekaviṃśa*), the *Medhātitha* is prescribed between those two; but here, having placed both of them without any interval, the meaning is that the *Medhātitha* should be performed with two *hiṅkāras* by means of those two.

The arrangement of these two [stotras] is as follows: "Sing forth to him, O men, with a flash of light" (*upāsmai gāyata naro davidyutatyā rucā*); "These drops have been poured out for the brown one who is self-strong" (*ete asṛgram indavo babhrave nu svatavase*); and "Like chariots, they have been sent forth, the flowing ones of you, O Sage" (*pra svānāso rathā iva pavamānasya te kave*). This is the Bahiṣpavamāna [stotra]. || 3 ||
"O Agni, come for the feast"—with these [verses] are the Ājya offerings.

"Uccā te jātam andhasaḥ"—this consists of the Gāyatra, the Cāmahīyava, the Jarābodhīya, and the Āśubhārgava; and "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā"—this consists of the Dvihiṅkāra, the Maidhātitha, the Raurava, the Yaudhājaya, and the Auśana as the final [Sāman].
The Rathantara, Vāmadevya, Naudhasa, and Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha chants.

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" is the Gāyatra-saṃhitā; "pavasvendramaccha" is the Sapha and Pauṣkala; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Gaurīvita and Śuddhāśuddhīya; and the final [sections] are the Śyāvāśva, Āndhīgava, and Kava.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*; the *pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*, the *hārivarṇa*, and the *tairaścya* are the *uktha*s; everything is the *triṇava*. 4.

He states the second day: "O Āśura, O Ṛṣi, O Bṛhanmati"—this is the six-verse hymn before the *paryāsa*. From the *hāviṣmat* [tune] comes the next, the *ājiga*. From the two *āyāsya* [tunes] come the first two *samanta* [tunes], and from the *dairghaśravasa* the next two. From the *gaurīvita* come the next two, the *madhuścunnidhana* and the *asita*. The rest is the same; it is performed with this very twenty-one-fold *bārhata* [stoma]. ||5||

Thus it is said. Here, because of the instruction "from these two [verses] for the Ajigama" in terms of immediate succession, one should extract the Dairghaśravasa [verse] from between those two; prior to those two, the Samanta-dairghaśravasa should be performed. In that regard, the sacrificial sessions (*satra*) are as follows: the *Dṛtivātavatorayana* and its *klṛpti*. The *Bahiṣpavamāna* chant is: "Pavasva vācaḥ," "Pavasvendo," "Vṛṣā soma," "Vṛṣā hyasi," "Prayadgāvo na bhūrṇayaḥ," "Aśurarṣa bṛhanmate," and "Pavamānasya te kave."
"We choose Agni as the messenger"—with these words, the clarified butter offerings are made.

"Flow as a bull, O Soma, in a stream"—this is the Gāyatra, the Hāviṣmat, the Ājiga, and the Sauparṇa. "Being purified, O Soma, in a stream"—this is the Samanta, the Dairghaśravasa, and the Āyāsya. "The red bull"—this is the final Pārtha.
And the Bṛhat, the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita, and the Kāleya are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the Gāyatra for the Auksa; "tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya pavasva devavītaye"—this is the Satrāsāhīya for the Śrudhya; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"—this is the Gaurīvita, along with the Madhuścunnidhana, the Asita, and the Krauñca; "vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate"—this is the Yāma as the final [stotra]. The Agniṣṭoma-sāman is the Yajñāyajñīya; the Ukthas are the Sākamaśva, the Saubhara, and the Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra. Everything is the Triṇava.
One should practice the reversal by means of these two for one month.

Thus: the meaning is that one should complete the month with the two previously mentioned *triṇava* stomas, the *rāthantara* and *bār̥hata*, arranged in alternation. He describes the thirty-third month: he brings forward the fourth triplet; both [stomas] are *paryāsa*; after the *āśubhārgava* comes the *mārgīyava*; the *dvaigata* is in the middle of the *bār̥hata* verses; after the *saṃhitā* come the *kākṣīvatabhāsa*;
the rest is the same as this very [month] with the *rāthantara* *triṇava*. 6.

Thus: "Sing for him, O men, with a flashing luster; these drops have been poured forth; the King moves with the sacrificial offerings; like chariots, they have been sent forth for the tawny one who is self-strong—O Sage, of you, the purifying one! This is the Bahiṣpavamāna chant.
The *ājya* offerings [are made] with the verse: "O Agni, come hither for the feast."

"Uccā te jātam andhasaḥ"—this consists of the Gāyatra, the Cāmahīyava, the Jarābodhīya, the Āśubhārgava, and the Mārgīyava; "Punānaḥ soma dhārayā"—this consists of the Dvihiṅkāra, the Maidhātitha, the Dvaigata, the Raurava, the Yaudhājaya, and the Auśana as the last. This is the midday [pressing].

With the verses *svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā*, the *gāyatra-saṃhita* [is performed], as well as the *kākṣīvata*, the *bhāsa*, the *satrāṇi*, and the *dṛtivātavator-ayanam*; this is the *ārbhava-gāyatrī*. Everything else is the same as that very [day] with the *rāthaṃtara* [stoma] of twenty-seven. Everything is [performed] with the thirty-threefold [stoma]. Thus is one day. 6.

Now, another [form]: with the triplet "apaghnan pavate mṛdhaḥ" and "ayā pavasva dhārayā" at the beginning of the *paryāsa*; after the *svāra* [sāman], the *sauparṇa* [sāman] follows; in the middle of the *bārhata* [sāmans], there is the *hariśrīnidhana* and the *arkapuṣpa*; after the *maukṣa*, the *śāmmada* and the *dāvasunidhana*. Everything else is the same as this very [form] with the twenty-seven-fold *bārhata* [stoma]. 7.

Thus: "Flow on, flow on through the voice; flow on, O Soma, Indu, for you are a bull, yes, you are a bull. Like eager cows, rush forth, O swift one, flow toward the high-minded one. Striking down the adversaries, he flows; flow with your stream, O Sage, as you are being purified. This is the *bahiṣpavamāna*.
"We choose Agni as the messenger"—with these words, the clarified butter offerings are made.

"Flow as a bull, O Soma, in a stream"—this is the Gāyatra, the Hāviṣmat, the Ājiga, the Svāra, the Sauparṇa, and the Hariśrīnidhana. "Being purified, O Soma, in a stream"—this is the Samanta, the Dairghaśravasa, the Arkapuṣpa, and the Ayāsya; "the red bull"—this is the Pārtha as the final [stotra]; such is the midday pressing.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the Gāyatrī of the Ārbhava Pavamāna, consisting of the Aukṣa Śāmmada and the Dāvasunidhana; the rest is the same as that of the Bārhata Triṇava. All [the verses] are Trayastrimśa. 7.
By reversing these two alone, there are twenty-nine [possibilities]. (8)
Thus, the six months have been described. ||8||
The Viṣuvant day is the Mahāvrata.
The meaning is that the Mahāvrata [rite] takes place at the position of the Viṣuvat. ||9||
Now, these same months are reversed. By means of those reversed, [he enters] the six northern months; of these, the first is the twenty-ninth day.

Thus: a month whose measure consists of twenty-nine days is a "twenty-nine-day month" (*ekānnatriṃśī*). The suffix *ḍini* is applied according to the rule *śacaśanorḍiniḥ*. Here, the mention of twenty-nine days for the sixth and seventh months is intended so that they do not become part of the year-long [sacrificial session] along with the two *atirātra* days. However, in the Sūtra, the state of having thirty days for those two months is also stated as an alternative:

"In the *ayana* of Dṛti and Vātavat, they should press two twenty-nine-day months consisting of the *trivṛt* [stoma]," says Gautama; "They consist of thirty-three [days]," says Dhānañjayya; "Or both may consist of thirty days, according to this Brāhmaṇa. (10)
Thus ends the *Ayana* of Dṛti and Vātāvati.

They undergo initiation for the month-long Kuṇḍapāyinām-ayana. They purchase the Soma on the [full] moon day. For them, there are twelve Upasad days; having performed the Upasads and having bound the Soma, they offer the Agnihotra for a month. They sacrifice with the New and Full Moon sacrifices for a month; with the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice for a month; and with the Varuṇapraghāsa sacrifices for a month. These are the Satras—the Kuṇḍapāyinām-ayana.

One month with the Sākamedha sacrifices; one month with the Śunāsīrya sacrifice and the Trivṛt-stoma; one month with the Pañcadaśa-stoma; one month with the Saptadaśa-stoma; one month with the Ekaviṃśa-stoma; one month with the Triṇava-stoma; one month consisting of the eighteen and thirty-three-day periods; ten days of the Dvādaśāha; and finally the Mahāvrata and the Atirātra—this is the Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana. There are six months beginning with the Agnihotra and six months of Soma-pressings; this is the Saṃvatsara-sattra. The initiations (dīkṣā) begin on the full moon day.

The sūtra beginning with "of the Kauṇḍapāyina" states: after performing the *upasads* and the subsequent *upavasatha* rite, they should enter upon the *atirātra*. This is the opinion of Śāṇḍilya, because it is observed as such in other *satra*s. In that case, the *subrahmaṇyā* invocation should be performed just as in the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*). Even in the *agnihotra-māsa* and similar rites, the *subrahmaṇyā* must be invoked at the beginning and end of each day. Regarding the *kauṇḍapāyina* and *sārasvata* sacrifices within the *iṣṭyayana*s, Śāṇḍilya maintains this is so because of the scriptural statement: "the *agnihotra-māsa* is like a *sutyā*."

And in that case, for the days ending with the twelfth day, the instruction regarding the *sutyā* is simply, "Come to the *sutyā*," and not, "The *sutyā* is on this many days. Thereafter, it is like the *dvādaśāha*. As it has been stated: "Having understood that the *sutyā* for the Kauṇḍapāyina and Tāpaścita rites occurs on the *dvādaśāha*, Dhānañjayya [holds] that the invitation according to the measure [of days] should be: 'May they come to the *sutyā* during the intervening days'. Regarding the *sutyās*, however, Gautama’s opinion is that after performing the *upavasatha* rite prior to the *sutyās*, there should be an *atirātra* sacrifice, and other [details] likewise, because of the observation of such [in the texts].

In that regard, all the *subrahmaṇyā* invocations, ending with the *śaunāsīrya* and extending up to the eighteenth [day], must indeed be performed with the words "Come to the *sutyā*. According to the opinion of Dhānañjayya, there should be no *atirātra* because it is not mentioned in the *Brāhmaṇa*. However, let the other matter be determined from the *Sūtra* itself. ||1||
He states the arrangement of the hymns:
"The Dṛtivātavator-ayana is arranged; the Kuṇḍapāyinām-ayana up to the ten-night sacrifice. (1)

Thus: for one month with the *trivṛt* [stoma], for one month with the *pañcadaśa*, for one month with the *saptadaśa*, for one month with the *ekaviṃśa*, for one month with the *triṇava*; and eighteen and thirty-three days [make up] the end of the arrangement. || 1 ||
The ten-night rite is prescribed by tradition. ||2||
The twelve-day [sacrifice]. || 2 ||
The vow is well-known. ||3||
The annual [offering]. ||3||
The Atirātra sacrifice is prescribed by way of wisdom. ||4||
By means of the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice. ||4||
Thus ends the Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana.

The *Tapaścita-ayanam* is described by the section beginning, "They remain consecrated for a year; they perform the *upasad*s for a year; the [Soma] is pressed for a year. Here too, as in the case of the *vyūḍha* arrangement, during the final twelve *upasad* days of the year, the *subrahmaṇyā* invocation is performed with the measured formula: "May the others come to the pressing (*sutyā*). There is an option, as before, as to whether there should be an *atirātra* or not.
The *Caitrāyaṇa* sacrifice is prepared by means of the *Gavāmayana*, or by means of the *Jyotiṣṭoma* which has not been fully prepared. 1.

Thus [it is said]. Here, the phrase "by the unmodified" (*aviklṛptena*) is for the purpose of excluding the *gaurīvita* accent. And so, with reference to the deliberations on the *Tāpaścita-āmayana* mentioned in the Sūtra, the *Nidāna* states:

"Among those [rites], whichever are performed in a single day (*ekāha*) are without the *gaurīvita*; whichever are performed over multiple days (*nānāha*) are with the *gaurīvita*. The *gaurīvita* is for the sake of the continuity of multiple days. Six *saṃvatsara-satra*s have been described. ||1||
Thus ends the Tapaścita-ayanam.
The sacrificial sessions (satrāṇi)— the Agni-sahasrasāvya lasting twelve years, the thirty-six-year session, and the hundred-year session.

By the section beginning "Three Trivṛt years, three Saptadaśas, three Ekaviṃśas," the year of Prajāpati consisting of one hundred years is described. By the section beginning "Nine Trivṛt years, nine Pañcadaśas, nine Ekaviṃśas," the thirty-six-year cycle of the Śāktyas is described. By the section beginning "Twenty-five Trivṛt years, twenty-five Pañcadaśas, twenty-five Saptadaśas, twenty-five Ekaviṃśas," the hundred-year cycle of the Sādhyas is described.
By means of the movement of the skin-bag and the wind, the twelve-year, thirty-six-year, and hundred-year cycles of Prajāpati were fashioned. || 1 ||

In that [sacrifice], there are *agniṣṭoma* rites consisting of the *trivṛt* stoma, and *ukthya* rites beginning with the *pañcadaśa* and so forth. According to the opinion of Śāṇḍilya, the *atirātra* and the *viṣuvant* should not be present because they are not explicitly mentioned. According to the other view, following the rule for *satras*, there should be two *atirātras* on both sides, with the *viṣuvant* in the middle. It has the *bṛhat* as its *pṛṣṭha-stotra* and the *rathantara* at the midday pressing. Regarding this, the opinion of Dhānaṃjayya is that the *pañcadaśa* stoma of the first fortnight and the *saptadaśa* stoma of the second fortnight should alternate. Other alternative options, however, are to be found in the Sūtra itself.
Thus, the twelve-year, thirty-six-year, and hundred-year cycles are completed.
The *sahasrasāvyam* sacrifice has been described by the section beginning with "The *atirātra* of Agni, the thousand-day *atirātra*."
By means of the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice, when it is not yet fully arranged, the thousandfold attainment of Agni is accomplished, or rather by means of the Gaurīvita-svara.

On this point, the Sūtra states: "The teachers say that in the Sahasrasāvin there are one thousand days together with two Atirātras; for Śaucivṛkṣi says, 'It is called the Sahasrasāvin because it is between [the two Atirātras],' and he says that there are one thousand days between the two Atirātras. || 1 ||
Thus ends the thousandfold extraction of Agni.
Thus ends the seventh section.
The Eighth Section:
The First Sarasvata Sacrifice.

The first Sarasvata sacrifice has been described by the Anuvāka beginning with "They undergo initiation at the Vanashana of the Sarasvati. Its Sūtra states: "On the southern bank of the Sarasvati, at the Vanashana, they should undergo initiation for the sake of the Sarasvatas."
For the first Sārasvata [sattra], there are two Atirātras accompanied by the Ṣoḍaśin cup.
Thus; the dual number is intended with reference to the *udayanīya-atirātra* sacrifice which is to be described later.
The *iṣṭyayana* sacrifice is prescribed in the *Anubrāhmaṇa*.

Thus it is said: "When the Atirātra has been concluded, they sacrifice with the Sānnāyya. Therefore, they proceed toward that [lunar half] which is waxing by means of the Amāvāsyā sacrifice. On the full moon day (Paurṇamāsī), their Stoma is the Goṣṭoma; it is an Ukthya with the Bṛhat-sāman. When the Goṣṭoma has been concluded, they offer the Paurṇamāsa oblation. They proceed toward that [lunar half] which is waning by means of the Paurṇamāsa sacrifice. For them, on the new moon day (Amāvāsyā), there are the sacrificial sessions (*satrāṇi*)—the first being the Sārasvata-ayana.

The Āyuṣṭoma stoma is performed; it is an Ukthya sacrifice with the Rathantara Sāman—thus, according to the Brāhmaṇa, the seasonal course (ayanam) for the bright and dark fortnights is established by means of the New and Full Moon sacrifices respectively. Thereafter, the Go and Āyus sacrifices are prescribed respectively for the Full Moon and the New Moon. ||2||
He states the arrangement of those two:
"The Go and Āyus [sāmans] for the one-day sacrifice are not modified. (3)

Thus it is said. Now, regarding the conclusion of the *sattra*, four occasions for rising from it are heard in the tradition: "When a hundred cows have become a thousand; when they drive a bull among the hundred cows; when they reach a thousand; or when they suffer total loss—these are occasions for rising. Or when the householder dies—this is an occasion for rising. Or when they come to the *plakṣa* tree at Prasravaṇa—this is an occasion for rising."

In this regard, even though the *Udayanīyātirātra* is mentioned [in the context of the *Satra*], it is stated—"The rising from the *Atirātra*" (Sūtra 4)—with the intention that it should be performed according to the rule of the *Satra*. Furthermore, since no specific details are heard regarding all [the *Atirātras*] even though there are four feet [of the sacrifice], this *Atirātra* is indeed the *Prāyaṇīyātirātra*. However, in the Sūtra, the alternative view that "there is another *Atirātra* at every *parvan*" is also stated; that [view] should be examined in that very place.

This sacrificial session (*sattra*) is one that does not require the *pṛṣṭha* chants for its pacification; thus, the *iṣṭi* for Agni Kāma is not performed for the purpose of pacifying the *pṛṣṭhas*. In this regard, the *prāyaṇīyā* [offering] reaches the *sutyā* day, as do the others. After the *atirātra*, up until the call to the *subrahmaṇyā*, it proceeds like the *dvādaśāha*; thereafter, because of the performance of the *iṣṭis*, the call to the *subrahmaṇyā* occurs at the beginning and end of each day. In that context, prior to the *sutyā*, the instruction for the *sutyā* is simply "come to the *sutyā*."

As it has been said: "In the case of the Kauṇḍapāyina and the Sārasvata [sacrifices], regarding the *iṣṭi* and the *ayanāni*, according to Śāṇḍilya, one should attend the *sutyā*. The others [should attend] after the *atirātra* of the first Sārasvata, and before the *śvaḥsutyā*. (4)
Thus ends the first Sarasvata session (of Mitra and Varuna).
The second [Sārasvata] session belongs to Indra and Agni:

an Atirātra, a Trivṛt Pañcadaśa, the Indra-Agni session, the Go and Āyus [sacrifices], the two Indra-kukṣis, and an Atirātra—thus the second Sārasvata is described. Regarding that, the Sūtra states: "By this very [method], the subsequent ones are explained," and so forth. Herein is the ritual manual (kalpa):

For the second Sārasvata [sacrifice], there are two Atirātras including the Ṣoḍaśin. They are arranged according to the method of Dṛtivātava: a Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a Pañcadaśa Ukthya, a Trivṛt Rathantara-stotra, and a Pañcadaśa Bārhata-stotra. The Go and Āyus [one-day sacrifices] follow the one-day [sacrifices], with the Gaurīvita-svara.

Thus: as in the previous case with the *darśapūrṇamāsa* sacrifices, here too, by means of the aforementioned *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* days, both fortnights are performed in alternation; however, it is not that the *trivṛt* occurs in the first fortnight and the *pañcadaśa* in the latter fortnight. As it has been said: "In all cases, the *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* should indeed alternate. Regarding the *go* and *āyus* [sacrifices], the *satra*s are the second *sārasvata-ayana*.

As before. And it has been stated: "At the two solstices, [the rites are] in Indra’s belly. In this context, when the *ayana* (solar course) is performed according to the manner described by means of the *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* [stomas], if there is no increase or decrease of lunar days (*tithi*), the fourteenth day is joined with the fifteenth-day rite; thus, the northern wing (*pakṣa*) is commenced with the *trivṛt* alone, even though it is not formally joined. However, if there is an actual increase or decrease of lunar days, the fourteenth day is joined with the *trivṛt* rite; thus, the northern wing is commenced with the *pañcadaśa*, even though it is not formally joined.

As it has been said: "In whichever of these two [sāmans] one falls short, one should begin the subsequent fortnight with that. Regarding this, an objection is raised: "From the Atirātra with the Rathantara-sāman, they enter upon the Trivṛt day belonging to the Rathantara."
Thus; and consequently, the consequence of [producing] a sibling follows—this is the remainder [of the sentence]. || 2 ||
He avoids [the fault]—by means of the *pratnavatī* *bṛhatī* for the day of the *rathantara*, thereby it is not a repetition (*ajāmi*). || 3 ||

Thus, for the *rathantara* day which consists of the *trivṛt* stoma, there is the verse "purifying himself, O Soma, you hold [the waters] in the *bṛhatī*. And since the word "ancient" (*pratna*) occurs therein in the phrase "sit in the ancient dwelling place," the absence of repetition (*ajāmitva*) is established; this is the meaning. ||3||

Now, due to the waxing and waning of the lunar day (*tithi*), on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight (*pūrvapakṣa*) the fifteenth [day] is reached as the *bārhata* day; and on the full moon day (*paurṇamāsī*), there is the *goṣṭoma* consisting of *bṛhatī* verses. Since the conjunction of these two would be a repetition (*jāmi*), he says:
"Where they approach the *go* from the *bārhata* day, as the *go* is in the *yamātirātra*s, so is the *bṛhatī*. (4)

Thus it is said: "In the *yamātirātra* sacrifices, the *kaṇvarathantara* belongs to the world of the *goṣṭoma* of Dairghaśravasa, and the [sāman] of Bṛhaduktha belongs to the world of Dairghaśravasa. However, when they approach the *trivṛt* day on the fourteenth day due to the presence of increase and decrease, then, following the *bārhata* *goṣṭoma* which was approached on the full moon day, they would approach the fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*) *bārhata* on the first day of the subsequent fortnight; this would result in monotony (*jāmitva*), which he now avoids.

In this [rite], they employ the *gaurīvīta* as the *bṛhat* day. For the *bṛhat* day, [they chant]: "Purifying himself, O Soma, in thy stream" (*punānaḥ somadhārayā*) as the *āyāsya* *aiḍa* on one verse; the *kaṇvarathaṃtara* on one verse; the *dairghaśravasa* on one verse; and the *triṇidhana āyāsya* on three verses. || 5 ||
Thus it is said.

Now, when on the fourteenth day of the waning fortnight—due to the increase or decrease of the lunar day—they perform the *rathantara* [sāman] as the *trivṛt*, and on the new moon day they perform the *rāthantara-āyuṣṭoma*, there would be a ritual redundancy (*jāmi*). Therefore, he says:
"Where they perform the *āyuḥ* [stotra] from the day of the *rāthantara*, just as the *yamātirātra*s are from the *āyuḥ*, so too is the *bṛhatī*. 6.

Thus it is said: "In the case of the *yamātirātra*s," for it has been stated: "In the world of the *āyuṣṭoma* [performed] by Medhātithi, there is the *bṛhannidhana*; [the *vārkajambha*] belongs to Raurava, and the *medhātitha* [belongs to] Medhātithi. (6)

But when, due to the absence of increase or decrease, the fourteenth day is joined with the fifteenth, and on this new moon day the *rathaṃtara* is reached from the preceding [day], then on the first day of the waxing fortnight (*pūrvapakṣa*) the *rāyantaram* [sāman] and the *trivṛt* [stoma] would be reached again; thus there would be a tautology (*jāmi*). To this he says: "Where they reach the *rāthantara* day of life, and for that *rāthantara* day the *bṛhatī* verse beginning with *pratna*, by that it is not a tautology. (7)
Thus; this has already been explained. || 7 ||
Regarding the sacrificial sessions (*satrāṇi*):
here too, as before, the rising (*utthāna*) is to be performed after the *atirātra*; thus he says:
"The rising from the *atirātra*" (8).
Thus [ends the eighth].
Thus ends the second Sarasvata-ayana of Indra and Agni.
The third [Sārasvata sacrifice] is the Sārasvatamayanam: an Atirātra, a Jyotirāyuṣ-trirātra, the Viśvajit on both sides, two Indrakukṣis, and an Atirātra; thus the third Sārasvata is described.

For the third [sacrificial session] dedicated to Sarasvatī, there are two Atirātras accompanied by the Ṣoḍaśin cup; the one-day sacrifices are the Trikadrukas, the Viśvajit, and the Abhijit, as well as the Gaurīvita and Svara chants.

Thus: the Viśvajit and Abhijit are one-day (aikāhika) sacrifices; the Gaurīvita-svara and Jyotis and so forth [are also one-day sacrifices]. Here, the Trikadrukas take the place of the New and Full Moon sacrifices (darśapūrṇamāsa). The Abhijit occurs on the full moon day, and the Viśvajit on the new moon day. For it is said: "The two parvans are the belly of Indra. When the Abhijit-atirātra modifications are being performed in the course of the year by repetition on the full moon day, whichever parvan should arrive while they have not yet been completed, one should begin the subsequent fortnight with that [modification]. This has been stated: "By this, the [performance] of the northern [fortnight] among the Trikadrukas is explained. ||1||
In that context, he gradually avoids the defect of *jāmi* (monotony) arising from their being performed together:

"From the *Atirātra* with the *Rathantara*, they proceed to the *Jyotis* with the *Rathantara*; from the *Jyotis*, [they proceed] to the *Bṛhatī* with the *Pratnavatī*; therefore it is not *jāmi*. (2) This is the sixth [section]. Where, however, from the *Āyuṣ* with the *Rathantara*, they proceed to the *Jyotis* with the *Rathantara*, there the *jāmitva* has already been avoided. Where, from the *Āyuṣ* with the *Rathantara*, they proceed to the *Jyotis* with the *Pratnavatī Bṛhatī*, therefore it is not *jāmi*. (2)

Now, when there is equality of the lunar day (tithi), then on the fourteenth day the Gaur-sāman occurs, and on the full moon day the Abhijit. Since both are Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha, he speaks [as follows] due to the context of similarity (jāmi): "Where they employ the Gaur and the Abhijit, as the Abhijit is in the case of the Yamātirātras, so is the Bṛhatī. (3)

"Thus: *punaḥ soma dhāraya* [is used] in the *abhīvarta* chant across three verses; the *raurava* on one verse; the *rathantara* on one verse; the *maidhātitha* on one verse; and the *yaudhājaya* on three verses. This is stated regarding the *bṛhatī* in the *abhijit* sacrifice of the ten-night rite (*daśarātra*). That same rule is extended by analogy (*atideśa*) to the *yamātirātra* sacrifices. And here, just as it was in the ten-night rite, so too must the *bṛhatī* be performed because of their proximity as *satras*, as has been stated regarding the *yamātirātras*. 3.
Wherein they approach the light of Abhijit, with that Bṛhatī verse containing "pratna" from the Jyotis [Sāman], there is no kinship-conflict.

Thus: when there is an increase in the lunar day (*tithi*), the *Abhijit* sacrifice is performed on the fourteenth day; having performed the *Goṣṭoma*, the *Abhijit* occurs on the full moon day. Therein, the *Rathantara* is the *Agniṣṭoma-sāman*. And because of that, on the first day of the waning fortnight (*aparapakṣa*), the *Jyotis* becomes characterized by the *Rathantara*. Thus, there is repetition (*jāmi*) in the first [set]. || 5 ||
Just as the Vāyu [śastra] follows the sequence of the Āyus [stomas], so too does the Bṛhatī [metre] follow the sequence of the Yamātirātras.

Thus [it is said]. In the phrase "where [the Sāman] Vāyu," the words "they enter upon the Abhijit" are to be supplied as an ellipsis. The meaning is: "where they enter upon the Āyu after the Abhijit. For if there were equality of lunar days (*tithi-sāmya*), then when the *satra* sacrifices—the Dārṣadvata, Turāyaṇa, and Goṣṭoma—have been performed on the fourteenth day, the Abhijit-Rāthantara-Agniṣṭoma would fall on the full moon day; and since the Rāthantara-Āyu would then occur on the first day of the waning fortnight (*aparapakṣa-pratipad*), there would be a fault of monotony (*jāmitā*). || 5 ||
Where they perform the Viśvajit either from the Jyotis or from the Arāyi, its ancient [verse] is a Gāyatrī of the Viśvajit.

Thus: when, in one view, the *vṛddhi* (increase) applies to these two in the former case, namely regarding the *viśvajit*, and the *bṛhat* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* in the subsequent *bārhata goṣṭoma* being performed, it removes the resulting monotony (*jāmitā*). Where they employ the cow of the *viśvajit*, just as the *gaurīvat* occurs in the *atirātra*s, so too does the *bṛhatī*; by that, there is no monotony. || 7 ||
Rising from the Atirātra sacrifice. || 8 ||
Thus, as before, there are also four seasonal festivals for those [rites] belonging to the Atirātra here as well. || 8 ||
Thus ends the third [section], the Sārasvata-ayana of Aryaman.
Regarding the Dārṣadvatamayana and the Turāyaṇa:

the Dārṣadvata is described by the section beginning with "A Brāhmaṇa should guard cows for a year," and the Taura is described by the section beginning with "An offering to Agni on eight potsherds. These two, the Dārṣadvata and the Taura, are prepared through specific means.

The "means" (upāya) refers to the manner of performing what has been stated by the Brahmana. The meaning is that when [the ritual] is prepared by that very means, there is no restrictive rule regarding either of the two alternative options. And these have been clearly explained in this way in the Sutra as "the vrātas of the Dārṣadvata and Aurya. || 1 ||
Thus ends the Dārṣadvata-ayana and the Turāyaṇa.
Thus ends the eighth section.

The ninth section: The Sarpa-sattra consists of Atirātra sacrifices on both sides with Agniṣṭomas in the middle; the entire year is twelvefold, and the Viṣuvat day is the twelfth—thus the Sarpa-sattra has been described by this Anuvāka.
The Sarpasattra consists of two Atirātras accompanied by the Ṣoḍaśin cup.
Regarding the Agniṣṭomas, he first says:

"The Januṣa and Ekarca [stotras] consist of the Sapha and Pauṣkala; [then come] the Śyāvāśva, Loka, and Gaurīvita. One repeats the other with a pair of Virājs. All is Daśin. (2) Thus, what was called "this Virāj" refers to the entire Daśin by means of the pair of Virājs; the meaning is that this entire Agniṣṭoma is a Daśistoma. (2) He now describes the second Agniṣṭoma:
Flow on as the leader of the voice; your vital energies have risen up, O Sage, as you are being purified. 3.
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"Agni we choose as messenger"—with these [verses] are the ājya offerings.

The *satras*: the *sarpasattra*, the *vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā* with a *gāyatra* melody on one verse; the *yauktāśva* on one verse; the *ṛṣabhaḥ pavamānaḥ* on one verse; or the *svāra-sauparṇa*; the *punānaḥ soma dhārayā* with an *aiḍa-āyāsya* melody on one verse; the *triṇidhana-āyāsya* on three verses; and the final *pārtha* chant, "vṛṣā śoṇaḥ."
[Thus ends the Mādhyandina Pavamāna:
the Bṛhat and the Vāmadevya, the Śyaita and the Kāleya.
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"yaste mado vareṇyaḥ"—this is the *gāyatram* and the *hāviṣmatam*; "pavasvendramaccha"—this is the *satrāsāhīya* for the sake of hearing; "ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"—the *gaurīvitam* is on one [verse]; the *krauñcam* is on one; the *arkapuṣpam* is on one; and "yacchandasyam" is the *yāmam* ending with "vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate."
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
With the exception of the last verse, the others consist of single stanzas.
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*. Every [verse] consists of ten syllables. 9.
For these same two [periods], the reversal [of the penance] lasts for six months.
The words "they approach" are to be supplied as the remainder [of the sentence]. ||10||
Among them, the thirty-first is the best.
The other months consist of exactly thirty [days]. 11.
Thus ends the ninth section. 6.
The tenth section:
it has been stated that the twelfth is the Viṣuvat. He speaks of the Viṣuvat:
"Flow on as the foremost of speech; sing unto him, O men, with a flashing luster! Of you, O Sage, who are being purified... (1)
Thus ends the Bahiṣpavamāna.
"O Agni, come for the feast"—this is the *rāthaṃtara* [sāman]; there are three *bārhata* [sāmans]. "We choose Agni as the messenger"—thus they say, "the two types of *ājya* [stotras]. (2)

The position is that because the *bṛhat* [sāman] is predominant due to its being situated in the *pṛṣṭha* position, there are three *bārhatāni* [chants]. Alternatively, the position is that because the *rathantara* is also predominant due to its being situated in the *pavamāna*, both types of *ājyāni* [chants] are used; such is the intention. ||2||

The *satrāṇi* [verses], the *viṣuvān*, and "High is your birth from the pressed juice" (*uccā te jātam andhasaḥ*) are in the *gāyatrī* meter; one [verse] in the *gauṣūkta*; one in the *satrāsāhīya*; one in "Being purified, O Soma, in your stream" (*punānaḥ soma dhārayā*), which is the *samanta*; one in the *saṃsarpa*, which is the third; one in the *dairghaśravasa*; and the *rathantara* in three [verses]. The final [verse] is the *pārtha*: "A bull, red" (*vṛṣā śoṇa*). ||3||
The Bṛhat and the Vāmadevya [Sāmans], the Saṃsarpa among the verses of the Śyaita, and the Kāleya among its own [verses]—these are the first. || 4 ||
Thus end the *pṛṣṭha* chants.

"svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" is the Gāyatra and the Aśvasūkta; "pavasvendracchā" belongs to Sapha and Śrudhya; "purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is the Gaurīvita on a single verse, and on that same verse is the Āndhīgava; the Saṃsarpa is on three verses, as is the second [Gaurīvita]; the Kāva is the last, consisting of verses containing the word "sūrya. ||5||
[Thus ends the Ārbhava Pavamāna.
There are two triplets in the Kāvasa-saṃsarpa; the others are single verses (ekarcas).
The *yajñāyajñīya* is the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
The whole [is] twelvefold. || 7 ||
He states the alternative position:
"Now, these same two preceding days are reversed. From those two [reversed] subsequent days, [they proceed] through the six subsequent months. Of those, the twenty-ninth day is the first. (8)

"Thus. The phrase "these very two" refers to the two days in the *agniṣṭoma* arrangement mentioned immediately above; the meaning is that here too, the two months consist of twenty-nine days each, stated for the purpose of completing the year together with the two *atirātra*s. In this *satra*, the two days preceding the final one, which are designated as the *abhigara* and occupy the place of the *mahāvrata*, are those spoken of in the Brāhmaṇa. It should not be said that because only that much is heard, the *gavāmayana* is the model (*prakṛti*) and this *sarpasatra* is a modified form (*vikṛti*) with a different arrangement of *stomas*; for this is established by the authority of the words of the Kalpakāras. As he says: "Some say that the *sarpasatra* is the *gavāmayana* with a modified arrangement of *stomas*. (8)
Thus ends the Sarpa-satra.
The three-year sacrificial session, the Gavāmayana, consists of the first year, then that of the Ādityas, and then that of the Aṅgirases; thus the three-year session has been described.
The first year of the three-year cycle is arranged by means of the Gavāmayana; the second by the Ādityānām-ayanam; and the third by the Aṅgirasām-ayanam. || 1 ||
The sūtra for this is: "The full moon [marking] the commencement, the three-year [cycle]," and so forth. "Commencement" (prasava) refers to the first pressing (prathamasutyā). || 1 ||
Thus the three-year sacrificial session (sattra) is completed.
Prajāpati’s sacrificial session lasts for a thousand years:
a thousand Trivṛt days followed by an Atirātra; thus [it constitutes] Prajāpati’s thousand-year session.

The sacrificial sessions (*satrāṇi*)—the session of the creators of the universe (*viśvasṛjām ayana*), the *bṛhaspatisava* as arranged by Aviklṛpta, the thousand-year session of Prajāpati, or that performed with the *gaurīvita-svara*. ||1||
Thus concluded Prajāpati’s sacrificial session of a thousand years.

The Viśvasṛj-sahasrasaṃvatsara is described as follows: fifty-three-year periods consisting of the Trivṛt-stoma, fifty-five-year periods consisting of the Pañcadaśa-stoma, fifty-seven-year periods consisting of the Saptadaśa-stoma, and fifty-one-year periods consisting of the Ekaviṃśa-stoma. Thus the Viśvasṛj-sahasrasaṃvatsara is declared. The Viśvasṛj-sahasrasaṃvatsara is arranged according to the Dṛtivātavatorayana. || 1 ||
He states another alternative:
"Or by the Jyotiṣṭoma not arranged [according to the specific stomas]. That is, "or by the Jyotiṣṭoma as arranged according to its stomas" (yathāstomaklṛptena). || 2 ||

Thus, by the phrase "without modification," the *gaurīvita* accentuation is prohibited. By the phrase "according to the arrangement of the *stomas*," it means that in the first fifty-five years, all the *stotras* of the *jyotiṣṭoma* are *trivṛt*; then for fifty-five [years] they are *pañcadaśa*; then for fifty-five [years] they are *pañcadaśa*; then they are *saptadaśa*; and then they are *ekaviṃśa*. The meaning is that one proceeds according to this arrangement, without overstepping the *stomas* of the years as declared in the Brāhmaṇa.

In that regard, the arrangement of the *stomas* for the *pavamāna* chants among the substances must be established through insertion (*āvāpa*) and removal (*uddhāra*) by means of the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice itself. For example, for the threefold (*trivṛt*) Jyotiṣṭoma, there is the *gāyatra* chant beginning with "uccā te jātam andhasaḥ. Likewise, for the tenth day of the ten-night rite (*daśarātra*), this same [chant] is to be used as its introductory verse (*pratipad*). He states that even when one is initiated, no modification of the introductory verse should be made for the *udayanīya* *atirātra*: "Except for the *prāyaṇīya* and *udayanīya* *atirātras*."

The intention is that the *prāyaṇīya* and *udayanīya* *atirātra* rites must necessarily be performed for the sake of completion (*samādhi*). Thus, the underlying reason for establishing the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*) as a sacrificial session (*satra*) is stated: "It occurs with the *prāyaṇīya* and *udayanīya* days being common (*samāna*). This means that it is "common" (*samānam*) to whichever day the opening rite (*pratipad*) has been performed; that is, it is identical to that [opening] day. || 2 ||
Thus ends the pilgrimage of the creators of the universe.
Thus ends the tenth section. || 10 ||
Thus ends the third chapter concerning the Sattras, the eleventh from the beginning, in this commentary on the Ārṣeyakalpa composed by Varadarāja, the son of Śrī Vāmānārya. || 11 ||
The Ārṣeyakalpa is completed.
